events.title: Drive the walkthrough from the dictionary, and rein in the descent
events.message:
Drive the walkthrough from the dictionary, and rein in the descent

The walkthrough was typing 11 of the game's 53 verbs, so two thirds of the
command dispatcher was never entered -- and no amount of following branches
reaches it, because a dispatch table is exactly what recursive descent
cannot see through. verb_drill derives a command per verb from the decoded
dictionary instead, so the list comes out of the game and cannot go stale:
116 commands now, and 4763 addresses executed against 4406.

That wider drill promptly broke the code map, which is the useful part.

Three addresses the CPU executed turned up inside instructions the descent
had decoded, with nothing branching to them. The cause was not the length
table this time: a byte in the game's variables reads as CALL NZ,$7874, and
following that phantom call decoded everything after it one byte out. So
any decoded instruction that straddles an address the CPU executed is now
struck out and the walk done again without it -- those boundaries came from
a processor, these came from a table, and there is no contest.

Worse, the unbounded descent was claiming 60% of the region as code against
26% executed, with 8517 starts in pages the CPU never touched at all --
including $CCxx, the picture table, and $B6xx, the variables. It was
decoding the database. One wrong byte in data manufactures a whole
plausible routine, and the round-trip check cannot tell the difference,
which is the whole reason this has to be argued rather than measured.

So speculation is bounded twice. Branches are followed only out of
instructions a CPU really executed; past that the walk goes straight on and
stops at the first RET or unconditional jump. And a start in a 256-byte
page where nothing at all executed is dropped, which loses a genuinely
unreached routine in an untouched page and is worth it.

The gain came down from +9905 to +1024, and that number is worth more.

events.title: image: address the scroller's frame offset through a table
events.message:
image: address the scroller's frame offset through a table

The blit computed a frame's offset with mulu #kFrameStride,d2, but
kFrameStride is the whole frame's byte count across every block type: a
160x80 phase with masked, shifted-masked and eight pre-shifts comes to
86,400, and MULU has no long-immediate form. vasm rejects it (error
2037, immediate operand out of range), so the export reported success
and handed the user a .s that could not be built.

Emit a longword table (kFrameOffsets: dc.l kFrameStride*N) in the data
section and index it: lsl.w #2 then move.l 0(a0,d2.w),d2. The obvious
PC-relative form does not work — 68000 displacement is a byte and the
table is ~160 lines away, which vasm reports as error 2030 — so a base
register is required; a0 is free there because the block's own lea
reassigns it two lines later, which the generated comment now says.

The new test builds a phase whose stride is over 16 bits, asserts the
stride really is over 16 bits (otherwise it proves nothing), that no
mulu on the stride is emitted, and assembles the pair with real vasm
warning-free. kCopyStride is not exposed: it is one block's size,
bounded by the 320x200 screen.

events.title: build: do the floppy geometry math in 64 bits
events.message:
build: do the floppy geometry math in 64 bits

A crafted BPB pushes firstDataSector * sectorSize past INT_MAX, and the
wrapped — often negative — product sailed through the bounds check
written to contain it, so parseGeo accepted a geometry that describes
nothing. Signed overflow is UB regardless of what the wrap happens to
produce; UBSan flags it at FloppyImage.cpp:360 on the new test's image.

Validate the whole layout in 64-bit in parseGeo (data start inside the
image, at least one cluster of data area, total sectors inside the
image), keep geoClusterOffset 64-bit until the final mid(), and share
one rootDirBytes() between listRaw and readFileRaw — the latter had no
root-directory bounds check at all, resting on QByteArray::mid
tolerating an out-of-range offset.

Verified red under a UBSan build (signed integer overflow: 16711433 *
512), clean after: the whole parsers suite runs with no runtime errors
under -fsanitize=undefined.

events.title: Find code by following branches as well as by running it
events.message:
Find code by following branches as well as by running it

codemap.py decodes instructions and follows every call, jump and
fall-through out from addresses already known to be code. It never guesses:
an address is only marked because something already known to be code goes
there. That is the opposite failure mode to the execution map, which cannot
contain a false positive but only ever finds what the playthrough reached
-- so the two are combined rather than one replacing the other. It adds
1119 instruction starts to The Hobbit's 4406, a quarter as many again.

Seeding from the execution map is the point. Recursive descent stops dead
at an indirect jump, and descent from $6C00 by itself reaches only about
two thirds of what actually ran, so it cannot stand on its own; seeded, the
real targets of every dispatch a CPU ever took are already in hand.

A heuristic pass -- mark anything that decodes plausibly -- is what the
build scripts reject, and the round-trip check is no defence against it:
data disassembled as instructions reassembles to exactly the same bytes, so
the verify stays green while the listing fills with fiction. The safety has
to come from the method.

Which is why the hand-written length table is checked against the execution
map on every build: thousands of addresses a real CPU fetched as
instructions must all come out of this decoder as instruction starts too.
It failed the first time it ran, on 62 addresses, and the cause was real --
a DD or FD prefix on an opcode naming (HL) makes it (IX+d), which carries a
displacement byte, so it is two bytes longer than the plain form and not
one. Nothing downstream would have noticed.

It then failed once more, at $8113, which turned out not to be a bug: a JR
aims at the second byte of an ED 52, so falling in runs SBC HL,DE and
jumping in runs the $52 as a one-byte no-op that skips it. Both readings
are code. The check now separates the two cases by asking whether anything
deliberately branches to the address, and only the other kind is fatal.

events.title: Trace the inflection flags back to subject agreement
events.message:
Trace the inflection flags back to subject agreement

$B6EA holds who the sentence is about, and zero means the player, so the
test PRINT_WORD makes really is subject agreement: while the game narrates
you it is zero and no verb inflects, and while it narrates anybody else it
holds that character's identifier and the inflectable verbs take their -s.
$B6E8 is a second participant, and flag $10 is how a word is made to agree
with that one instead.

Watched rather than argued: a breakpoint on PRINT_WORD, reading DE and both
variables at every call, reconstructs each sentence word by word as it is
composed. The opening runs with $B6EA zero throughout; a turn of narration
about other characters walks it through a run of consecutive identifiers
while repeating the same verb, which is a group being described one after
another.

That the identifiers are character numbers rather than flags is what the
writers say: $FF at $79B6, loaded from tables at $7956 and $7942 elsewhere,
and compared against list entries with CP (HL) at $7A73.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Work out the word reference's inflection flags
events.message:
Work out the word reference's inflection flags

The top four bits of a word reference decide whether the word is inflected,
and that is all they do: $40 always adds the suffix, $50 never does, $10
adds it when $B6E8 is non-zero, and any other value adds it when $B6EA is.
The word has the final say either way -- the suffix only goes on if bit 7
of its second byte is set, which is what marks an entry as able to take it.

Measured rather than read off the listing. PRINT_WORD was called directly
with each of the sixteen flag values and the buffer read back, then the two
variables were toggled by hand to test the dispatch; the word at $6AC1
comes out inflected or not exactly as the rule predicts in all six cases.
Nothing in the indexed list inflects, which fits: that list is what the
parser matches against, and nothing is ever printed from it.

The first attempt at this reported that no flag did anything to any word,
which was the harness and not the game -- the register indices were guessed
rather than taken from skoolkit.simutils, so DE was never actually set and
every call expanded whatever was already there. Worth remembering that a
result identical across every input is a broken experiment, not a finding.

What sets $B6E8 and $B6EA is still open. Two variables deciding whether a
verb takes its -s reads like subject agreement, but that is an
interpretation of the mechanism rather than anything traced to a writer.

events.title: Nothing in Paradroid is multicolour: the sprites are hires too (KC)
events.message:
Nothing in Paradroid is multicolour: the sprites are hires too (KC)

KC, 2026-09-18, correcting two docs at once. This is the THIRD time a
colour-format model in this project has been believed, written down and
built on without being checked against the data, so both corrections
are recorded in place rather than quietly rewritten.

graphics.md section 3 said:

  "The game sprites are multicolour. The multicolour renderings show
   coherent droid shapes; the hires renderings look fragmented."

That is a reading of how a ripped render LOOKED, not a measurement, and
it is wrong. The game sprites are HIRES - 1 bit per pixel, 63 bytes + 1
pad, 24x21 mapping 1:1 onto MODE 1.

decisions.md's "Why MODE 1" was wrong in every particular. It claimed
"both the tiles and the sprites are C64 multicolour" and derived the
mode from one multicolour pixel being exactly two MODE 1 pixels, with
table rows for "Multicolour pixel | 2 screen px | exactly 2 px" and
"Colours per cell | 4 | 4". The deck has been known to be hires since
2026-08-18 (layer-1, after THREE successive wrong models), so that
section had been stale for a month and nobody re-read it.

Worse, its own correction note had the map backwards - it said an
earlier version "described the map as 1bpp hires ... both were wrong",
when 1bpp hires is the answer layer 1 arrived at. Deleted.

THE DECISION ITSELF IS UNAFFECTED. MODE 1 is still right and the 1:1
mapping still holds - only the reason changes, and the correct reason
is simpler: 320 pixels across either way, so a C64 pixel IS a MODE 1
pixel, a character is 8x8 either way, a tile 32x32, a sprite 24x21.
Nothing is scaled and no artwork is redrawn.

The rewritten section states what the cost actually is - per-cell
foreground out of a 12-slot palette collapsing to four global logical
colours - and the counting that makes it survivable: over the tiles a
deck PLACES, weighted by placement, every deck wants the background
plus three colours and the fourth-most-used appears 2 to 40 times
against the third's hundreds. Nothing is merged. Logical 1 is black on
all sixteen decks, which deckPalette confirms: every one of the sixteen
4-byte records has &00 in slot 1.

The standing lesson, which graphics.md now carries at the site:
do not state a colour format from how a rip renders.

events.title: ui: answer a refused build, and reset session state in one place
events.message:
ui: answer a refused build, and reset session state in one place

Three related gaps in MainWindow's state, each user-visible:

A build that refused to start (no source, failed save, missing linker)
emitted nothing, so a remote-control build sat out its full 120 s
timeout for an answer known in microseconds, and run() could leave
m_launchAfterBuild armed for a build that never started — the next
plain Build then launched an emulator nobody asked for. refuseBuild()
is now the single exit for every refusal: it drops the launch intent,
logs, and emits buildCompleted(false) before showing the dialog. run()
lost its duplicate no-source check and always delegates to build().
RemoteControl's run wait also quits on buildCompleted(false), and
starts the operation from a zero timer so the wait loop is running
when a synchronous refusal emits — a quit() before exec() is lost.

m_lastState was written on every state update and never reset, so the
remote state command answered with the previous session's registers:
a plausible, wrong register file rather than 'no session state'.
resetSessionState() now owns every per-session member (arming state,
resolved bases, cached state, pending remote command) and is called
from both ends of a session's life — launch and runningChanged(false).

build.assemblerPath was persisted, shown in the settings dialog and
recommended by the setup dialog, but never passed to findAssembler();
the emulator probe had the same gap. Both now take the project
override, and refreshToolchain() runs after the settings dialog and
when a loaded project names a tool path, so an override works without
a restart.

Each fix has a regression test verified red against the pre-fix
sources: the remote run wait measured 120,320 ms empty pre-fix and
549 ms with an error after; the refused build emitted nothing; the
assembler path resolved to discovery instead of the override; and
state summary returned a dead session's pc/d0-a7/sr.

events.title: build: bound the floppy listing walk and sanitize entry names
events.message:
build: bound the floppy listing walk and sanitize entry names

A crafted image can make many directory entries name the same cluster,
or make directories point at each other in a cycle: the listing walk
had only a depth cap, and readChain's cycle detection is per call, so
two self-referencing entries per level expanded without bound on the
GUI thread — mounting such an image, or copying onto it, hung the app
until the memory ran out.

The walk now carries a visited-cluster set across the whole recursion
(expand a directory cluster at most once) plus a total-entry budget, so
a degenerate tree lists its unique entries and stops.

The same walk produces the entry paths the copy-out destinations are
joined from, and the on-disk 8.3 bytes are untrusted: display83 now
drops control characters and both separators from each component, so a
crafted name like '../evil' lists as '__evil' and cannot smuggle a
traversal or an absolute path past the join. The extraction path in
FileBrowser additionally refuses any destination that resolves outside
the folder the user chose.

The cycle regression test was verified red under a 2 GB ulimit (the
walk dies of std::bad_alloc) and green after the fix; the name test
was red with F/../evil listed verbatim.

events.title: build: keep the floppy image recoverable when the replace fails
events.message:
build: keep the floppy image recoverable when the replace fails

updateImage removed the original image before renaming the staged one
into place, so a failed rename (an emulator holding the image open on
Windows, AV/ACL interference, a full directory) lost the user's disk
image outright — despite the API's promise that a failure never
truncates the original, and with QFile::remove's return discarded so
the failure was indistinguishable from success.

The replace is now a same-directory rename dance: the original is set
aside as a .bak beside it, the staged image is renamed into place, and
the backup is removed only on success. A failed final rename rolls the
backup forward again, leaving the image exactly as it was; a failed
set-aside fails loudly with the original untouched. The round-trip test
now also asserts no staged or backup file survives a successful update.

events.title: editor: make sprite undo address the phase it was made in
events.message:
editor: make sprite undo address the phase it was made in

PaintCommand and LayerPixelsCommand recorded the frame and layer but not
the phase, and their undo resolved both through whatever phase was
current at undo time — so painting on one phase, clicking another, and
pressing Ctrl+Z wrote the undo into the wrong phase: silent corruption
of the phase on screen (in range whenever cell sizes match, the common
case), and the actual edit kept. SnapshotCommand assigns the whole
document, which is why structural operations were immune.

ImageDocument::editFrame(phase, frame, fn) runs fn with the recorded
phase and frame current and restores the previous selection afterwards,
skipping a phase or frame deleted since the push; both commands wrap
their undo/redo in it. The stroke captures its phase at first paint, so
a phase switch mid-drag cannot misattribute it.

The regression test draws and flips on phase A, undoes from phase B,
and asserts both phases' pixels. Its first draft failed identically
before and after the fix: addPhase leaves the new phase current, so the
stroke landed on B and the assertion read a pristine A. The corrected
draft was verified red by stashing the fix and rebuilding.

events.title: build: refuse an AUTO-folder program that does not fit the floppy
events.message:
build: refuse an AUTO-folder program that does not fit the floppy

writeAutoFolderImage wrote the program's clusters and FAT chain with no
capacity check, unlike writeImage's allocateClusters guard on the generic
export path: anything over 729,088 bytes (712 clusters, after AUTO's
cluster 2) ran past the end of the 720 KiB image vector, and past ~1 MB
off the FAT copy as well. A game with incbin'd assets plus a pre-1.04
TOS ROM — the AUTO-folder fallback's exact audience — hit heap
corruption instead of an error.

The check mirrors allocateClusters' refusal, and the same bound keeps
the highest written cluster at 714, inside the 1024-entry FAT, so one
check closes both overflows. MainWindow's existing error path shows the
message.

The regression test pins both sides of the boundary: exactly 729,088
bytes succeeds, one byte more is refused with no partial image left
behind. Red under ASAN before the fix (one-byte heap-buffer-overflow).

events.title: control: fix remote-control use-after-free when a peer disconnects
events.message:
control: fix remote-control use-after-free when a peer disconnects

Blocking commands (build/run/cmd) spin nested event loops, and several
branches pump events before replying (modal dialogs from open and the
build refusal paths, screenshot's processEvents). A peer disconnecting
inside one of those loops is deleted by the disconnected -> deleteLater
in onNewConnection, and any later use of the raw socket pointer is a
use-after-free.

Two things were needed. Every reply in execute() now goes through a
QPointer, and commands execute one event-loop hop after readyRead via a
queued invocation rather than inside the socket's own dispatch: the
nested loop used to deliver the deferred delete while the socket
notifier frame that dispatched the readyRead was still suspended beneath
it, so Qt itself resumed into a destroyed socket (proven by a gdb
backtrace of the regression test crashing under both Debug and Release).

The regression test aborts the peer from a timer so the disconnect is
delivered inside the nested wait, the way a real peer's arrives; it was
red under ASAN before the fix (SIGSEGV in QIODevice::write through the
freed vtable).

the repository on purpose.

events.title: Find what reads The Hobbit's second word list
events.message:
Find what reads The Hobbit's second word list

It is the vocabulary the game's messages are composed from, as against the
one it searches when you type. PRINT_WORD takes a 12-bit offset from $6000
and expands whatever entry it lands on, so a word is only ever named by its
own offset and nothing holds the list's address at all -- which is why
searching the image for a pointer to $67AB, absolute or as an offset, finds
nothing, and why guessing from the bytes was going nowhere.

Found with a read watchpoint over the range while the game played, on a
second server so the one in use was left alone. The list stays untouched
through the opening, LOOK and INVENTORY, and is first read on a command
that composes a sentence about an object. A control watchpoint on the
indexed list was used first to show that a read watchpoint fires at all,
which it does: it stopped on the L bucket the moment a word beginning with
L was typed.

Both ends of the format are now the game's own account rather than mine.
MATCH_WORD turns typed ASCII into 5-bit codes with AND $1F -- the codes are
the low five bits of the letters' ASCII, which is why that works -- indexes
$6000 by the first letter doubled, and walks the bucket until an entry's
initial letter stops matching, confirming the linear scan the loose
ordering within a bucket implied. PRINT_WORD states the awkward rule
outright: it stops on a byte with bit 7 set unless only two letters have
been emitted, because the first two bytes carry the part of speech. A
decoder that stops at the first bit 7 splits ATTACK into AT and TACK.

events.title: menu: the PCMCIA slot names its card in its own list, and two categories move
events.message:
menu: the PCMCIA slot names its card in its own list, and two categories move

On an A600 or A1200 the main menu's PCMCIA Card row carried what was in
the slot as its value. A slot is empty most of the time, so nearly every
time the menu opened it said "Empty" -- and with a card in, the value was
the card's whole description, path and size included, which widened the
menu to fit it.

The row now carries no value. The list it opens starts with what is in
the slot, greyed and unpickable, in the shape of the MT-32's Control ROM
and PCM ROM lists: a dimmed None for an empty slot, the card's name for a
fitted one, then Insert CF Card Image... and Eject Card as before. A card
goes by the file name of the image behind it, as the MT-32's ROMs do; an
SRAM card with no file behind it by what it is. A level is as wide as its
widest row, so the name is cut to the width the two rows under it already
give the list, ending in the "~" the launcher's path rows use for a
clipped name.

Emulation Settings moves up to lead the settings categories, above Audio
Settings, and Warp Settings moves to close them, under Input Settings and
ahead of the ports a machine may or may not have. The player build
offers neither and is unchanged.

Three tests in menu.rs pin the list for an empty and a fitted slot, that
a long name leaves the list exactly as wide as an empty slot does, and
the order of the categories. The UI guide's menu sections follow the new
order and its PCMCIA entry is reworded; the menu picture is regenerated
from panels_render_into_their_rects, which also drops the Frame Analyzer

events.title: window: a native picker no longer runs under the winit callback on macOS
events.message:
window: a native picker no longer runs under the winit callback on macOS

On macOS 27, opening any native file picker and resizing it aborted the
emulator: "tried to handle event while another event is currently being
handled", raised in a frame that cannot unwind.

The blocking rfd picker was run from inside the winit event callback.
While a callback is on the stack winit does not deliver further events;
it queues them as blocks on the main run loop in kCFRunLoopDefaultMode,
on the reasoning that a modal panel runs in NSModalPanelRunLoopMode and
a panel resize in NSEventTrackingRunLoopMode, so the blocks wait until
the callback has returned. macOS 27 breaks that: a mouse-down on the
panel is routed through the new gesture environment, and
_NSGestureRecognizerSortAndSendDelayedEvents spins
-[NSRunLoop runMode:beforeDate:] from inside -[NSSavePanel runModal].
The queued block runs there, under our callback, and winit panics. A
minimal winit 0.30.13 + rfd 0.17.2 program reproduces it; the same
program with rfd's async dialog does not.

A picker is now asked for with a PickRequest and a continuation
(App::pick_path / App::pick_paths) rather than called for its return
value. On macOS the request opens as a sheet on the window and returns
at once; the window loop collects the answer on a later pass and runs
the continuation then, so no callback is on the stack while a panel is
up. Windows keeps the picker thread and message pump from 54b08b2f and
Linux the direct call, with the same continuation run as soon as the
picker returns. All 19 call sites are converted; the larger ones keep
their bodies in a helper that takes the chosen path.

While a sheet is up the machine is held, as it is for the life of a
blocking picker, a second picker is refused, and the pad does not walk
the panels. A netplay session runs on behind the sheet so the peer is
serviced. Live audio is suspended and the realtime clock re-anchored
around every picker now; the SoundFont, MT-32 ROM and cover art pickers
did neither before. load_state_from_dialog no longer sets the control
flow itself: about_to_wait settles it from the run state after every
pass.

Verified on macOS 27 (M5 Max): every launcher and menu picker opened
and resized, the two-sheet Kickstart sequence, cancel paths, pacing and
audio after the sheet closes. Verified unchanged on Windows 11 ARM64
and Ubuntu ARM64. cargo test --locked: 3,879 passed, 43 ignored; six
new tests in native_dialog cover the held machine, single delivery,
cancel, a chained sheet and the refused second picker. cargo fmt
--check, clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings, and the
--no-default-features and frontend,cpu-jit checks are clean. No
user-visible surface or documentation changes.

events.title: Disassemble The Hobbit from its tape, verified byte-for-byte
events.message:
Disassemble The Hobbit from its tape, verified byte-for-byte

The fifth game here, and the first adventure. One 40000-byte payload at
$6000 entered at $6C00, no tape protection, so the disassembly comes
straight off the tape -- but a large part of those bytes is the database
rather than code, and a heuristic pass reads much of it as plausible
instructions. So the code map is built the Atic Atac way, by running the
game and recording what executes; unlike Atic Atac, random keys get
nowhere, so a walkthrough is typed in through real port reads.

The dictionary is decoded rather than described: a 26-letter index at
$6000 and 355 words from $6040, one 5-bit letter per byte, part of speech
in the spare top bits of the first two, and a bit-6 terminator introducing
a 2-byte synonym link. Every bucket and every synonym is checked to land
on an entry start, which is what makes the format proved rather than
merely plausible -- GET -> TAKE, KILL -> ATTACK, I -> INVENTORY.

The annotations cover the picture pipeline: a vector opcode stream (move,
line, flood fill, paint attributes) over a 256x128 canvas, its table at
$CC00, and the routines that draw it. Timings there are measured, not
estimated -- a room costs about 6.9 seconds and PIXEL_ADDRESS is 52% of
it, recomputed per pixel by both the line drawer and the fill.

Two things are deliberately left undone and say so: the second word list
at $67AB, which nothing in the index reaches and which should be found
through its reader rather than guessed at, and the drawing speed itself.

check_annotations is ported from build_aticatac.py and extended to catch a
comment whose start address is mid-instruction, not just its length. That
is the mistake counting bytes down a listing actually produces, and it
shifts every address after it while the round-trip check reports only a
byte count slightly too large.

events.title: editor: find and replace, from a Search menu
events.message:
editor: find and replace, from a Search menu

Ctrl+F opens a find bar along the bottom of the editor (the viewport gains the
margin, so nothing is hidden behind it) and Ctrl+H opens the same bar with the
replace row. Searching is incremental: every hit is highlighted through the
extra selections as the needle is typed, and the bar's label counts them. Enter
or F3 goes on, Shift+Enter or Shift+F3 back, both wrapping; match-case and
whole-word options are toggles, and Escape closes the bar, drops the highlights
and returns the caret to the text.

Replace writes one hit at a time, stepping on to the next, and Replace All goes
back to front inside a single edit block so the whole lot undoes in one step —
which also means it does not walk over the positions it has yet to do.

The hits live in CodeEditor, and the Search menu in MainWindow acts on the
focused editor, so a session with an image tab has nothing for them to do and
they grey out with it. That needed the per-tab pass to run once at the end of
the window's construction: the pristine tab is added before the actions exist,
so Find was otherwise dead until the first tab switch.

tst_gui covers the incremental hits and their wrapping, both options, replace
one and replace-all-as-one-undo, Escape, Shift+Enter, the shortcut keys
themselves, and the actions following the tab type.

events.title: image: choose which palette colour the export masks out
events.message:
image: choose which palette colour the export masks out

The mask treated ST colour 0 as the background, hard-coded. Which colour a
sprite is cut against is the artist's call, so the export dialog now picks it
from the document's active palette — shown as its swatch — and starts on the
document's own background register. "None" leaves only the unpainted pixels
out, so every painted colour, colour 0 included, is opaque.

A colour left out is absent from the planes as well as the mask, so a blit
keeps the screen there and has nothing to OR over it; the generated scroller
says in its header which colour that is.

Also give the file map a fixed width and no wrapping: the columns were
breaking onto their own lines once a phase had frames to report.

events.title: image: export a phase's bitplanes as .dat, with an optional scroller
events.message:
image: export a phase's bitplanes as .dat, with an optional scroller

File → Export Bitplane Data… writes the blocks you tick — palette, sprite,
masked sprite, pre-shifted copies — for every frame of a chosen phase, as raw
ST screen-format bitplanes. `bitplaneLayout()` produces the byte map and the
encoder walks it, so the offsets the dialog prints are the ones the file has,
and the blocks are uniform: a pre-shift is `base + k*kCopyStride`, a frame is
`base + f*kFrameStride`.

The dialog picks the phase from the document's list, the blocks and the
pre-shift count, and prints that map (the full per-label `equ` list goes to the
console, and the map is a scrolled view since an 8-frame phase runs long).

"Also write a scroller (.s)" adds a ready-to-assemble `-Ftos` program beside
the `.dat` that `incbin`s it — vasm looks for an incbin beside the source it is
assembling, so the pair travels together and PiST's F7 build finds it — and
addresses each block through those same `equ`s. It takes supervisor mode (the
ST bus-errors user-mode access to the hardware), installs the palette, clears
the screen, then animates and scrolls across it until a key is pressed, when it
restores the palette and returns. On a screen that is not 320×200 with four
planes it says so and waits rather than drawing, and it asks before replacing
an existing `.s` (the path is derived, not chosen).

Verified against a real Hatari run: the sprite draws, animates and scrolls, a
keypress returns cleanly to GEM, and the non-low-res bail prints and waits.
tst_image covers the layout, the frame and copy strides, the phase plumbing and
a warning-free vasm assemble of the `.s`+`.dat` pair from two working
directories; tst_gui covers the dialog's phase list, map and gating.

events.title: Serialize the second RGA conflict pointer
events.message:
Serialize the second RGA conflict pointer

save_custom_slots()/restore_custom_slots() wrote only the p and
conflict pointers of each RGA slot, so a savestate captured during a
copper/blitter address-pointer conflict lost conflict2 on restore:
either the conflict vanished (slot had NULL) or a stale pointer from a
previous slot use survived. Serialize conflict2 through the previously
reserved slot field, encoded as the register index plus one so old
savestates, which hold a zero there, still restore a clean NULL.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Detect overlap on zero-pitch repeated lines in transparent blits
events.message:
Detect overlap on zero-pitch repeated lines in transparent blits

The transparent blit templates chose the backward branch with
src + h * srcpitch > dst, which is never true when BytesPerRow is zero
(the repeated-line RenderInfo that validatecoords2 explicitly allows),
so a rightward overlapping copy on that line ran forward and overwrote
source pixels before reading them, smearing the row. Use the row's
pixel width as the span when the pitch is zero, in both the 24-bit and
the generic template.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Print the exclusive end of the searched range
events.message:
Print the exclusive end of the searched range

The byte-search status line printed the user's endaddr as the last
searched address, but the loop stops before comparing at endaddr, so a
match there was never found despite being advertised. Print endaddr - 1,
matching the other search message in this file.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Resume immediate blits when DMA is re-enabled
events.message:
Resume immediate blits when DMA is re-enabled

When an immediate blit's event fired while blitter DMA was disabled,
blitter_handler() parked it with a positive blit_stuck countdown
(~3 frames of hsyncs). Re-enabling DMA calls blitter_check_start() from
DMACON(), but it only resumed negative (non-immediate) stuck states, so
the immediate blit and its completion interrupt stayed delayed until
the countdown expired. The DMACON call site already gates on
dmaen(DMA_BLITTER) and a nonzero blit_stuck, so resume any stuck state
there.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Mask unused pixel bits when matching the transparency key
events.message:
Mask unused pixel bits when matching the transparency key

The 16/32-bit transparent loops compared the source pixel against the
key at full width, so a pixel with the same visible color but a
different unused bit (the high bit of 15-bit formats, the alpha byte of
32-bit formats) was treated as opaque and overwrote the destination.
rgbmask exists exactly to exclude those bits and is already applied
throughout the logical blit macros; apply it to both sides of the
transparent comparison in both directions.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Compare against the actual positive int32 boundary
events.message:
Compare against the actual positive int32 boundary

fpu_precision_valid() rejected the negative int32 conversion endpoint
but the positive check compared against 0x7ffffffff (nine hex digits),
which no int can ever equal, so values that overflowed
floatx80_to_int32() to the positive endpoint passed validation in
precision-limited FPU tests. Compare against 0x7fffffff like the paired
0x80000000 check.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Apply suffix-based AROS detection to the MAPROM guard
events.message:
Apply suffix-based AROS detection to the MAPROM guard

load_kickstart() recognizes the built-in AROS replacement ROM both as
the exact path ":AROS" and as a path ending in ":AROS" (what a
relative-path expansion produces), but the MAPROM guard in
memory_map() still compared only the exact string. A relative-path
":AROS" therefore took the shadow-ROM mapping path that canonical
":AROS" explicitly skips, mapping AROS's split main/extended ROM
inconsistently. Both decisions now use one is_builtin_aros_rom()
predicate.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Keep long access for 24-bit transparent blits, special-case the last pixel
events.message:
Keep long access for 24-bit transparent blits, special-case the last pixel

Rework the 24-bit BLT_NAME_TRANS loops back to 32-bit long access for
the bulk of each row (read-modify-write that preserves the fourth byte,
as before) and use byte access only for the final pixel of the row,
whose 4-byte window would otherwise pass the row/buffer end. Direction
from the WinUAE upstream review of the same code. Both directions keep
the exact value composition of the previous byte-wise version, and no
access leaves the row's w*3 bytes.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Clear conflict2 when recycling RGA slots
events.message:
Clear conflict2 when recycling RGA slots

clear_rga() reset conflict but left conflict2 behind, so a recycled
slot kept the second pointer of an earlier DMA address conflict. When
the slot later took part in a sprite/blitter collision, which sets only
conflict, process_blitter() saw both pointers non-null, treated the
collision as a copper conflict, and wrote the derived copper address
through the stale pointer. Reset conflict2 alongside conflict.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Include demux hook 40 in the obsolete-hook guard
events.message:
Include demux hook 40 in the obsolete-hook guard

While the uaegfx card is installed, uaelib hooks 16-39 are rejected so
legacy callers cannot switch the emulator into uaegfx_old mode, but the
new transparent-blit hook 40 sat outside the guard: a legacy caller
invoking it set uaegfx_old = 1, silently disabling RTG hardware
interrupts and the built-in card allocation. Extend the guard through
hook 40; BlitRectTransparent is reachable through its BoardInfo
callback instead.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Fix zero random FPU divisor in cputest fpu_random
events.message:
Fix zero random FPU divisor in cputest fpu_random

With fpu_max_precision enabled, fpu_random() divided by
((rand8() + 1) & 7), which is zero whenever the low three bits of
rand8() are 7 — one draw in eight, compounded across the ten loop
iterations, so most values came back as infinities. fpuregchange()
filters those through fpu_precision_valid(), but the fill_memory_buffer()
path accepts fpu_random() results directly, so precision-limited FPU
tests filled their memory operands with infinities instead of finite
values. Form the divisor as (rand8() & 7) + 1, range 1-8.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Fix quoted argument splitting in the debugger command parser
events.message:
Fix quoted argument splitting in the debugger command parser

debug_line() swapped the active quote delimiter whenever it saw the
other quote character, so `s "don't";r` stayed quoted after the closing
double quote and swallowed the `;r` into the search arguments, while a
string with two apostrophes could be split on a semicolon still inside
double quotes. Only open a quote when none is active and only close on
the matching delimiter.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Fix BlitRectTransparent RenderInfo register and install its BoardInfo callback
events.message:
Fix BlitRectTransparent RenderInfo register and install its BoardInfo callback

The uaelib demux handler for BlitRectTransparent read the RenderInfo
from A0, which holds the BoardInfo in every Picasso96 callback
(FillRect, BlitRect, BlitRectNoMaskComplete all take it from A1), so
case 40 blitted from a BoardInfo structure misread as a render buffer.
The dead srcri/dstri register reads left over from the
BlitRectNoMaskComplete layout are removed with it.

inituaegfxfuncs() never installed PSSO_BoardInfo_BlitRectTransparent
in the live RTGCALL block (only inside the disabled #if 0 block), so
the BoardInfo function pointer stayed NULL and P96 could not reach the
accelerated transparent blit at all. Install it like its siblings.
events.author: midwan

events.title: Fix RTG transparent blits (BlitRectTransparent)
events.message:
Fix RTG transparent blits (BlitRectTransparent)

Four defects in the transparent blit path:

- do_blitrect_frame_buffer_transparent() had no BLIT_SRC case in any of
  its pixel-size switches, while picasso_BlitRectTransparent() always
  calls it with BLIT_SRC: the operation was a silent no-op. Add
  BLIT_SRC_{16,24,32} template instantiations (8-bit already existed)
  and dispatch BLIT_SRC in all four switches.
- The 8/16/32-bit forward branch of the BLT_NAME_TRANS template
  advanced src2/dst2 after the row loop instead of inside it, so every
  row re-processed row 0 and rows 1+ were left untouched. Move the
  pitch increments into the loop, matching the 24-bit variant.
- The 24-bit transparent loops loaded and stored 32-bit words at
  3-byte pixels, over-reading/writing one byte past the final pixel of
  a tightly packed region. Compose and store the three bytes instead.
- transparentcolor was compared against host-order pixel loads without
  the endianswap() used by every other pen-taking path, so 16/32-bit
  keys virtually never matched. Normalize with endianswap(Bpp).

Verified with a standalone harness instantiating the generated
BLIT_SRC_TRANS functions for all four depths: forward multi-row
copies, transparent-key skipping, overlapping blits in both
directions, and guard zones past tightly packed regions all pass
(failing before the template fixes).

events.title: release: 0.5.0
events.message:
release: 0.5.0

The sprite editor learns to select, and the pointers find their tips.

- Sprite editor: a select tool drags a marquee you can move (drag inside
  it or nudge with the arrows), then copy, cut, paste and delete; paste
  keeps transparent pixels see-through, and every edit rides the undo
  stack.
- Importing an ST image adopts the file's palette as the active set, so
  phases sliced from it no longer report their colours as overspill.
- Canvas pointers: the brush, fill and eyedropper cursors draw from the
  toolbar glyphs with hotspots on the paint tips, the select tool gets a
  marquee pointer with its click on the bottom-right corner, and cursors
  render at a flat 32px so X11 never clips them.
- Floppy images: fix a use-after-free in readFileRaw that corrupted
  reads and rewrites under allocators that reuse freed blocks quickly
  (behind the macOS CI failures).
- The dropper, undo/redo, and selection toolbar glyphs are traced from
  their SVG Repo sources for a consistent look.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: Keep the window alive past the present worker's join
events.message:
Keep the window alive past the present worker's join

Closing the window (the title-bar button or Cmd+Q) hung with a beach
ball since the present worker arrived. Render drops its fields in
order: the window Arc, the reclaimed GPU side, then the worker, whose
Drop joins the copperline-present thread. That thread's closure held
the last Arc<Window>, and on macOS winit drops a Window through a
synchronous dispatch to the main thread -- the thread blocked in
pthread_join on the worker. A sample of the hung process shows exactly
that pair: main in JoinInner::join, the worker in Arc<Window>::drop_slow
waiting on the main dispatch queue.

PresentWorker now keeps its own reference to the window, so the
thread's clone is never the last one; the window drops on the main
thread after the join, as it did before the worker existed. Verified by
clicking the close button on a windowed CD32 session: the fixed build
exits with status 0 where the previous one sat in the join.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Make the CD32 FMV module opt-in
events.message:
Make the CD32 FMV module opt-in

The CD32 profile has fitted the bundled open FMV cartridge by default
since the open ROM landed (6eb61d649, in 0.19.0). A stock CD32 has no
cartridge, and fitting one is not free for the guest: the module's
resident ROM moves the heap and shifts boot timing. Kang Fu's GREED
intro is the case that surfaced it. The game clears 36 words by 356
rows with the blitter from a buffer it allocated, and with the module
fitted the effect-slot table it renders its bouncing ball from sits 22
bytes inside the tail of that clear. The ball's sprite pointers are
then rebuilt through a NULL record, pick up the ROM vector at $108,
and the ball vanishes behind a frame of sprite streaks. The clear is
the game's own bug; the default decided what it hit. v0.18.0, which
never fitted the module, keeps the ball, and so does 0.20.0 with
fmv_rom = "".

The cartridge slot is now empty unless asked for. A new top-level
fmv = true fits the module with the bundled open ROM; fmv_rom = "path"
fits it with that image and implies the switch; fmv_rom = "" keeps its
older meaning of an empty slot, and the two keys must agree. The
machine profile no longer seeds the bundled ROM. In the launcher the
FMV row starts as an empty slot with a Fit action, fits the bundled ROM
on Fit (saved as fmv = true), takes a chosen file as before, and offers
Remove once fitted; clearing a chosen file keeps the module on the
bundled ROM. The configuration guide, UI guide, peripherals chapter,
example config and the FMV asset README describe the switch.

Verified from a cold boot of the Kang Fu CD on the CD32 profile: with
the stock config the boards and frames match the earlier fmv_rom = ""
run byte for byte and the ball keeps bouncing past 120 s; with
fmv = true the FMV board autoconfigures at $200000 and the frames match
the previous default byte for byte.

events.title: Revert the Microsoft Store packaging
events.message:
Revert the Microsoft Store packaging

The Store refused the submission under policy 10.13.10:

  Products that emulate a game system or game platform are not allowed on
  any device family.

There is no exception in that policy for emulators of general-purpose
computers, and Copperline emulates the CD32 and CDTV alongside the
machines, so the classification is not one a reworded listing would
change. Windows distribution stays the portable zip until a code-signing
certificate is in hand, at which point a signed package can be built and
distributed directly, with no Store involvement and none of the
constraints the Store imposed.

This reverts the merge of #696 in full: the MSIX manifest and builder, the
Store logos and listing text, the Partner Center identity, the packaging
job, the shared payload staging, and the install and release
documentation. packaging/windows, RELEASE.md and the Windows workflow are
byte-identical to before that work.

The console-window section added since is kept, less its mention of the
Store as a way to start Copperline.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Address the review: chrome under the GPU picture, launcher hidpi, bound staleness
events.message:
Address the review: chrome under the GPU picture, launcher hidpi, bound staleness

Five findings from review, all real.

The scaler's picture draw sampled only the picture through its map and
clamped rows past it to the last picture row. That was right for the
autocrop layout, whose display draw covers the picture alone, but the
classic layout -- autocrop off, which is the default -- is one draw
over the picture and the status-bar band together, so the band showed
the last picture row. The picture shader now samples the composed
texture itself for the rows below the picture (a textureLoad on the
sRGB-typed texture already yields linear light, like the sampler), and
the GPU comparison covers the classic single draw with a chrome band:
point sampling is bit-identical there too. The sharp filter's tolerance
is now stated in linear light, where the difference lives -- near black
the steep foot of the sRGB curve turns a 0.4/255 linear difference into
five encoded LSBs.

A machine started from the launcher applied the configured aspect,
scaling, vsync and autocrop but not hidpi_texture; App::apply_hidpi_
texture sets the global and replans the backing texture.

The Copper wake bound assumed the line and frame lengths it was
computed under. A frame that wraps earlier -- shortened by an ECS
VTOTAL/BEAMCON0 write or a LACE change -- left the bound standing over
the restarted Copper, and a shortened line made the position arrive
before it. The wrap itself now drops the bound, as does any write to
the beam-timing registers (HTOTAL through HCENTER).

The present worker gave the window's pre-present hint on the main
thread at hand-off, before the surface was acquired or the frame drawn,
which on Wayland arms a frame callback for a buffer that may never be
committed. The worker now passes the window to the presenter itself off
macOS, keeping the established order (after the draw, before the
present); on macOS, where every winit window method waits on the main
thread and the hint is a no-op, it passes none.

The clip ring's repeat key omitted the pixel aspect, though the built
picture's height follows it; an aspect change on a static screen kept
the old-sized frame. The key carries the capture's row count.

Same checks as before: save state and frame dumps identical, the
timing-test golden renders unchanged, and the headless core benchmark
unmoved by the extra invalidations.

release: 0.4.0

The sprite editor becomes a sprite-set editor, and the file bar learns

- File bar: copy, cut, paste and drag & drop within and across the hard

- Floppy round-trip: text documents open straight off a mounted disk

  documents whose exports recompose back into the disk image.
- Sprite editor: phases own their frames with per-phase cell sizes, a
  spritesheet mode composes, places, drags and slices phases against an
  imported sheet, cell sizes are editable, and Export Sprite Sheet and
  sprite-safe export write the results back out.
- demo.pim is refreshed to the v2 sprite-set format.

events.title: ui: imported sheets open as untitled documents; sheet source toggle
events.message:
ui: imported sheets open as untitled documents; sheet source toggle

Hitting Save after importing a .pi1 did not save: the import adopted
the file as the document path, so Save silently recomposed and
overwrote the imported file — no dialog, no .pim, and the source art
gone. Under the sheet model an imported image is a sheet target, not
the document: importing now leaves the document untitled, so Save asks
for a .pim name and reports it, and Export Sprite Sheet is the explicit
act of composing back to the sheet. Exporting a sheet that came off a
mounted floppy writes the recomposition back into the disk image
(exportSpriteSheetTo, with the floppy write-back hooked in).

The spritesheet view also gains a Sheet source toggle — show the
imported pixels as the slicing reference, or hide them and see only the
composed export.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: ui: placement auto-slices the sheet under a phase, moves re-slice
events.message:
ui: placement auto-slices the sheet under a phase, moves re-slice

The import journey users actually take never reached the slice dialog:
drag the staged phase onto the sheet, add frames by hand, attach the
sheet in the panel — and every frame stayed empty because nothing
sliced. Placement now slices the art under a phase automatically:

- dropping a staged strip on a sheet fills its empty frames from the
  cells under them;
- moving a placed strip re-slices frames that still match the cells
  they were cut from — the strip is a window onto the sheet until a
  frame is edited, and edited frames keep their pixels;
- adding a frame to a placed phase slices the next cell of the strip.

The explicit slice dialog remains for bulk cuts.
events.author: idontwantyourspamthanks

events.title: Skip a sleeping Copper's comparator until its WAIT can release
events.message:
Skip a sleeping Copper's comparator until its WAIT can release

The CPU-idle fast-forward already computes a sleeping WAIT's exact
wake deadline once and leaves the comparator dormant until then; the
ordinary CPU-driven path evaluated the comparator on every eligible
slot of every colour clock, 3.8% of the core in the Copper slot stepper
plus the WAIT release test and its free cycle, because its spans were
thought too short for the prediction to pay for itself.

The same invariant now rides along as a cached absolute bound
(CopperWakeBound on the bus, consulted by every bus quantum through
advance_one_chip_bus_quantum_limited). Once a WAIT is in its steady
comparator phase, the earliest clock at which it could release -- the
nearest of its position, a pending frame restart and the field wrap,
with the end-of-list WAIT bounded by the wrap alone, which the idle
deadline never covered -- is computed once. Quanta strictly before it
skip the comparator; at it, the comparator runs every eligible slot
again and wakes the Copper at the slot it always would. A WAIT already
at its position gets no bound, so the wake slot and the blitter-finished
condition stay with the per-clock path, and a running Copper gets none.

What can move the wake drops the bound: the COPJMP strobe, VPOSW and
VHPOSW, a DMACON write that changes the Copper's own DMA gate, a
sleep/wake transition in the slot stepper, reset, and a state load (the
field is not saved). The first cut invalidated on every DMACON write and
every Copper step and ran 30% slower than no bound at all: the position
scan walks the beam clock by clock, and games and lists write DMACON
constantly. A bound cache lives or dies by invalidation frequency times
recompute cost.

Exactness: a save state 12 s into the Kang Fu slide is byte-identical
apart from the header's save timestamp, frame dumps match, and the
timing-test golden renders pass unchanged. Headless core benchmark, 30 s
emulated: M5 7.78 s -> 7.16 s (-8%, -14% from the start of this
series); the 2020 Intel MacBook Pro ran 23.1-24.1 s against 24.9-26.3 s
for the branch before the core work, in a noisier session.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: ui: sheet pixels reload from disk, and the preview follows phase selection
events.message:
ui: sheet pixels reload from disk, and the preview follows phase selection

Testing the import flow end to end left sliced frames empty: a document
reopened from disk had no sheet pixels in memory, so Add phase silently
fell back to creating an empty phase, and hand-added frames stayed empty
with an empty animation preview. Sheets with a readable file now reload
their pixels (and underlays) whenever a document loads, so slicing works
across sessions; sheets with no path or a missing file say so in the
status line when Add phase cannot slice instead of falling back quietly.

Selecting a phase also retargets the animation preview — it kept playing
whatever phase was previewed before, which read as empty frames even
when the slice had landed.

events.title: ui: slice dialog with live preview boxes and empty-slice feedback
events.message:
ui: slice dialog with live preview boxes and empty-slice feedback

Slicing a phase out of an imported sheet asked for name, size, position
and count as bare number prompts with defaults — if the numbers missed
the art, six empty cells were cut in silence, and the dimmed underlay
made the empty strips read as markers over the sprite.

Add phase over an imported sheet now opens one dialog whose field
changes redraw the pending cells as yellow boxes on the sheet itself,
with the frame count pre-filled from how many whole cells fit. After a
slice, the editor status line reports the frame count — and warns
loudly when every cut cell came out empty, which almost always means

events.title: ui: editable phase cell size, sheet slicing on import, live sheet view
events.message:
ui: editable phase cell size, sheet slicing on import, live sheet view

Three gaps from testing a real 6-frame Degas import:

- Phase cell size is editable in the phases panel (w/h spinboxes).
  ImageDocument::setPhaseCellSize resizes every frame of the phase,
  content anchored top-left: cropped when shrinking, transparent when
  growing, layers and composites both.
- Over a freshly imported sheet, Add phase slices cells out of it —
  name, sprite size, first cell, and frame count — instead of only
  ever creating an empty phase, so a 6-sprite strip imports as a
  6-frame animation in one step.
- The sheet canvas repaints on frame and cell-size changes: adding a
  frame extends the strip immediately instead of the box sitting still.

A sliced six-frame import, cell resizing and strip growth are covered
by new tests in tst_image and tst_gui.

events.title: Settle the per-colour-clock early-outs before the register decodes
events.message:
Settle the per-colour-clock early-outs before the register decodes

Line-level profiling of the AGA workload (samply on a line-tables
release build, symbolicated with atos inline chains) put 17.6% of the
core's time on one line of the per-colour-clock bus quantum: the
inlined advance_beam(cck), whose callees re-derived per clock what only
changes on register writes -- the display start from the DIW registers
(twice per clock), the effective BPLCON0 with its write-landing delay
decoded into a display mode, the effective DMACON -- before reaching
the checks that reject the vast majority of clocks. The m68k crate
itself is 11% of the core; the chip bus arbitration and the beam
bookkeeping are where the time goes.

Four reorderings, each exact, each pure computation moved after a
cheaper test it was gating nothing for:

- advance_beam resolves the display start once per quantum; nothing
  between its two uses changes the DIW registers or the frame geometry.
- The DDF sequencer's bitplane capture consults the line's slot table
  before decoding BPLCON0 and the framebuffer row, so a clock with no
  plane slot -- most of them -- costs one table load.
- The sprite capture settles its vertical gate (vpos at or past the
  display start) before the effective BPLCON0/DMACON lookups and the
  timing probe it then never uses.
- fixed_dma_owner_at answers bitplane-or-nothing straight away for
  hpos >= 0x034 off the line-end refresh pair: refresh, audio, disk and
  sprite slots all sit below 0x034 or at 0x0E2/0x0E3, so their four
  tests can only fail there.

A save state written 12 s into the Kang Fu slide is byte-identical to
one from the previous binary apart from the header's save timestamp,
the frame dumps match, and the timing-test golden renders pass
unchanged. Headless core benchmark of that scene, 30 s emulated: M5
8.24 s -> 7.78 s (-5.3%); 2020 Intel MacBook Pro 24.9 s -> 23.3 s
(-6.3%).

image: phases own their frames — the sprite-set model, v2 .pim

A phase is now an animation with a home: it owns its frame stack outright
and carries a cell size (cellW x cellH), so one document can hold 32x32
characters next to a 64x64 boss — the thing the old shared-frame-list
model could not express. Phases additionally carry sheet placement
(sheet index + x/y), and a document holds sprite-sheet targets (path +
size). Frame and canvas accessors delegate to the current phase.

sliceSheetCells() cuts imported sheets back into phase frames. The
old range-based phase helpers and the region experiment (model, export,
tool, panel) are gone; the .pim format moves to version 2 and v1 files
are rejected outright, per decision — no users yet.

panel (name, cell size, placement); the full spritesheet mode follows.

events.title: Sample the presentation buffer on the GPU when nothing composes over it
events.message:
Sample the presentation buffer on the GPU when nothing composes over it

With the present worker in place, the largest frontend cost left on
the main thread was copy_window_present_frame: the CPU copy of the
presentation buffer into the 2x texture, resolving the TV glass column
blend and the row selection per texel, ~1.8 ms of a 27 ms frame on the
2020 Intel MacBook Pro, plus the 6 MB upload of the result. That copy
is a resample, which is what the scaler pass already does.

The scaler's display draw can now sample the presentation buffer itself
(ScalerDraw::picture, PresentScaler::upload_picture): the buffer goes up
at the canvas's own size, and the shader reproduces the CPU copy per
texel of the texture it stands in for -- the same row selection and the
same 8.8 two-column glass blend in the same integer arithmetic on the
encoded byte values (picture_texel, from the PictureMap that
present::picture_map builds from the copy's inputs), then the same
clamp-to-edge bilinear filter in linear light that the sampler applies
to the composed texture. Point sampling is bit-identical to the CPU
path; the sharp filter differs by the sampler's weight and sRGB-decode
precision, within two LSBs, which picture_draws_match_the_composed_
texture checks on the GPU against the CPU copy for the glass, a nudged
glass and full overscan, at an exact multiple and a fractional fit.

The redraw takes the GPU path when nothing has to be composed over the
picture on the CPU: no menu, panel, OSD, badge, guest overlay or drop
hint, no tint, and no CRT, bezel or RTG pass (those sample the composed
texture). Everything else composes the whole frame on the CPU as
before, and the chrome band below the picture always does, so the
status bar, keyboard and instrument panels are unchanged. The
presentation buffer is copied into a worker-recycled buffer for the
job, ~1.5 MB, in place of the texture copy.

Intel Mac, same save state, presenting live: 0.741x with the present
worker, 0.799x with the picture draw; 0.644x on main before this
series.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Hrany spritu: bez / Scale2x / vyhlazeno, a cache zvetsenych platen
events.message:
Hrany spritu: bez / Scale2x / vyhlazeno, a cache zvetsenych platen

Rozbalovatko v pruhu vylepseni. Obe upravy stoji na tomtez indexovem
Scale2x (AdvMAME2x), lisi se dotazenim na displej: Scale2x nejblizsim
sousedem (tvrde hrany), vyhlazeno bilinearne. Maskovane pozemni objekty
se nezvetsuji - maska se cte v souradnicich 1:1.

Zmereno na vyrezu 44x44 px pri zvetseni 6 (69 696 bodu): bez vs Scale2x
4 513 bodu, bez vs vyhlazeno 10 571, Scale2x vs vyhlazeno 6 821.

Dve pasti: prvni verze "vyhlazeno" byla BITOVE shodna s "bez" (sprite se
predzvetsuje nejblizsim sousedem a na displej se dotahuje 1:1, takze
bilinearka nema co michat) a `state.spriteScale` nemela vychozi hodnotu,
takze se Scale2x zapinal i tam, kde ma byt vypnuty - chytil to kontrakt
naklonu vrtulniku.

Pri hledani toho se zmerila cena podpixelove cesty: predzvetseni stoji
na zlomkove poloze 40,39 ms na snimek proti 6,18 ms bez nej. Zvetsena
platna se proto pamatuji, ale az od DRUHEHO vyskytu tehoz platna (jinak
by maskovane pohyblive sprity zakladaly nove platno kazdy snimek).
Obraz zustava BITOVE stejny, cela poloha klesla z 35,95 na 2,20 ms.

Kontrakt v uitest.py: vsechny tri rezimy musi dat tri ruzne obrazy
a vychozi hodnota musi byt "bez".

events.title: Present frames from a worker thread
events.message:
Present frames from a worker thread

The window's redraw ended at pixels' present: the texture upload, the
GPU passes and, with vsync on, the wait for the display's vblank, all on
the main thread that also turns the emulation loop. On a host that falls
short of real time that wait is a per-frame stall of the emulator; on
the 2020 Intel MacBook Pro it was ~1.5 ms of a 28 ms frame after the
copy-path fix.

Render now keeps only the window and its geometry, and the GPU side --
the pixels surface with the scaler, CRT, bezel, sticker and RTG passes,
Gpu in window.rs -- lives on a copperline-present thread while frames
are threaded. The redraw handler composes the texture image into a
buffer the worker recycles (two in flight; a third redraw marks the
presentation dirty and waits a pass) and hands off a PresentJob with
everything the passes need resolved on the main thread: scaler draws,
CRT and bezel uniforms and viewport, the RTG rect. present_job() is the
one draw path, run by the worker for the normal display and by the main
thread for a frame that carries something only it has: the RTG board's
texture upload, or the inspector's egui paint. Render::gpu_mut reclaims
the GPU side for those and for surface and texture resizes, present-mode
and shader changes and sticker loads, waiting out a frame in flight; the
next threaded redraw lends it again, and Drop reclaims it so the surface
is destroyed on the thread that made it.

The worker never calls winit: on macOS every Window method waits on the
main thread (pre_present_notify included, though it is a no-op there),
which would deadlock against a main thread waiting in reclaim. The main
thread gives the pre-present hint at hand-off instead, and
Presenter::render takes the window as an Option. Without a vsync wait in
the redraw, a polling loop with nothing running would spin; it now takes
the same 16 ms tick the vsync-off path already did.

COPPERLINE_THREADED_PRESENT=0 presents every frame from the main thread,
which is also the control for the measurement: on the Intel Mac, from
the same save state with presentation live, the committed binary runs
0.710x, the worker 0.752x, and the worker with the knob off 0.710x. The
presenter's profile line names its thread.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Resolve the TV glass column map once per frame and add [display] hidpi_texture
events.message:
Resolve the TV glass column map once per frame and add [display] hidpi_texture

On a 2020 Intel MacBook Pro (Ice Lake i5, Iris Plus, Retina) the 0.20.0
release runs AGA titles below real time. It is not GPU bound: the GPU
sits at 8%, the main thread is on-CPU 96% of the time, and the
emulation core alone takes 17 ms of the 20 ms PAL frame. The frontend
added a further ~8 ms per frame on the main thread, half of it in
copy_tv_aperture_to_window: the default "tv" overscan copy resolved the
glass column map through a per-pixel closure (tv_glass_sample, an 8.8
fixed-point two-column blend) for every one of the 769k pixels of the
2x Retina texture, every frame.

The map depends only on the column, so tv_glass_column() now yields the
(column, column, weight) triple, tv_glass_sample is one lookup of it,
and the live copy builds a frame's map once and applies it to every
row. The texture rows outnumber the aperture's, so runs of them show
one source row (the row map is monotone): a run's later rows copy the
row just built instead of resampling it, in both the TV and the
full-overscan copies. window_copies_match_a_per_pixel_reference pins
the rewrite bit-exact against the old per-pixel semantics at texture
scales 1-3, on both canvases, with the picture nudged off centre.
Measured against unmodified main on that Mac, presenting live from the
same save state: 0.644x -> 0.708x, no visual change.

[display] hidpi_texture (default true) is the knob for hosts that still
fall short: false pins the backing texture to canvas resolution and
leaves the upscale to the scaler pass, a quarter of the per-frame copy
and upload. The plan's integer multiple stands, so integer scaling
draws the same point-sampled blocks; only the smooth fit selects rows
at canvas resolution instead of the finer texture grid. Same Mac:
0.708x -> 0.741x.

Two smaller changes ride along, both correct and tested but measured as
noise on the scene above: begin_new_beam_frame swaps the promoted
capture buffers instead of taking them, so they keep their capacity
across frames; and the clip ring notes a slot whose presentation buffer
has not taken a new picture (present_fb_generation, kept per writer)
with ClipRing::repeat instead of rebuilding and comparing the frame,
which only pays on static pictures.

events.title: Volba palety: hardware vs dobovy monitor
events.message:
Volba palety: hardware vs dobovy monitor

Prevod ctyrbitove slozky na barvu byl roztrouseny na trinacti mistech
jako `n * 17`; svedeny do jedine funkce `rgb4()`, jinak by se volba
palety nekde roztrhla.

`hardware` je vychozi a presne `n * 17` - tak to delaji emulatory i nase
baseline snimky, takze na tom stoji vsechny kontrakty. Overeno na vsech
4096 kombinacich: zadna odchylka, compare dal 12/12.

`dobovy monitor` NENI mereni - zadny Commodore 1084 tu neni. Stoji na
dvou publikovanych cislech: gama 2,4 podle ITU-R BT.1886 proti 2,2
u sRGB (stredy byly na CRT tmavsi) a bily bod 9300 K misto D65, na ktery
spotrebni PAL monitory bezne jely (bila byla CHLADNEJSI, ne teplejsi).

Retezec je fyzikalne serazeny: dekodovat gamou CRT do linearniho svetla,
tam posunout bily bod, teprve pak zakodovat gamou sRGB. Prvni verze
posouvala bily bod az nad gamou, coz efekt prehanelo a bila se orezavala.
Pomery jsou normovane tak, aby nejvetsi byl 1.

Zmereno: meni 4094 ze 4096 kombinaci, nic mimo rozsah, cerna zustava
cerna, bila 224,234,255, stredni sed 136 -> 113,118,128.

Past, do ktere se slaplo: `setMonitorMode()` se vola pri definici, ale
`const state` vznika o pet set radku niz - prvni verze do nej zapisovala
a stranka padala na "Cannot access 'state' before initialization".
Stav volby proto zije v modulovych promennych.

also means an opened test.pi1 no longer titles itself untitled).

spriteSafeDocument(): colour 0 is reserved for the background (the
sheet's own background colour if free, else the first free word) and

- tlacitka byvaji na jinych cislech, takze palba (0/2/7) nesla vubec.
  Mimo `standard` mapovani ted bere jakekoli tlacitko mimo smerovy kriz.

Pribyla lista `ovladani`: kazdy slot ma rozbalovatko (automaticky / jen
klavesnice / konkretni ovladac) a vedle zivy vypis toho, co hra
z ovladace opravdu cte. Bez toho se vzdalena diagnostika "joystick
nefunguje" vest neda. Volba prezije reload.

a hatu v klidove poloze.

Use SERPER bit 15 to distinguish 9-bit transfers instead of treating

bit for framing, which caused 0xa9 markers before every byte on TCP
connections.

events.title: unix: process pending input actions while paused
events.message:
unix: process pending input actions while paused

pause_emulation is toggled from AKS_PAUSE, but like all AKS_* actions it
only takes effect via inputdevice_handle_inputcode() draining the
pending-action queue (inputdevice_do_keyboard() just queues it with
inputdevice_add_inputcode()). The first Pause press works because the
normal per-frame inputdevice_vsync() path drains the queue, but once
inside the while (handle_events()) pause-wait loop in custom.cpp,
nothing drains it again, so a second Pause press queues an unpause
that's never applied and the loop spins forever.

od-win32/win32.cpp's handle_events() already calls
inputdevice_handle_inputcode() on every iteration of its own pause wait
for this reason; mirror that here.
events.author: Graham Bates

events.title: build: share feature macros between winuae_core and Qt frontend
events.message:
build: share feature macros between winuae_core and Qt frontend

winuae_core and winuae_unix_qt_frontend both compile struct uae_prefs
through options.h, but only winuae_core gets the feature macros that
gate members of that struct. The frontend therefore compiles a different
layout for uae_prefs than the core code that initializes and writes into
it, so prefs objects allocated in the frontend and passed to core
functions overflow their allocation and corrupt the heap.

Move all of winuae_core's feature-macro definitions onto a new
winuae_unix_core_defs INTERFACE library and link both winuae_core and
winuae_unix_qt_frontend against it so both targets agree on the struct
layout.
events.author: Graham Bates

events.title: copperhf: confirm Kickstart 1.3 FFS-from-LSEG crash is a binary/OS
events.message:
copperhf: confirm Kickstart 1.3 FFS-from-LSEG crash is a binary/OS
version mismatch, not a bug

Traced the previous regression test's Guru Meditation to exec.library's
own jump table getting clobbered while the modern FastFileSystem 46.13
binary (which links utility.library, a Kickstart 2.0+/V36+ component
1.3/V34 never shipped) starts running as DH0's handler process --
entirely inside real, unmodified Kickstart ROM code, not
guest/copperhf/mounter.c.

Confirmed by A/B test: swapping in the genuinely period-correct V34.85
FastFileSystem already bundled for the lide device's own tests
(test-assets/lide/wb13/Workbench1.3/l/FastFileSystem) makes the exact
same mount sequence complete cleanly with no code changes. The test now
uses that binary and passes, turning it into a real regression proving
copperhf.device correctly mounts and boots FFS media under Kickstart
1.3, with the investigation kept as documentation for the next person
who hits this with a too-modern FastFileSystem on their own disk.

ui: file operations in the project panel, document tabs, appearance preferences

Three related workbench features:

  QSettings and settable from a new Appearance tab in the settings
  dialog. Dark uses a Fusion palette; the highlighter carries light and

events.title: toolchain: skip version probes of non-PE files on Windows
events.message:
toolchain: skip version probes of non-PE files on Windows

The toolfetch suite hung for 300 s on the Windows CI runner, killed by
QTest's watchdog with no captured output. Instrumented CI runs traced it
to probeVersion's QProcess::start on the suite's shell-script fixture
(named vasmm68k_mot.exe): starting a non-PE file stalls indefinitely
inside the OS under ctest, while the same start returns instantly under
file redirection and on Linux.

Probing such a file is meaningless on Windows — it can never execute, so
it can never answer --version — so read the MZ magic and skip the probe
instead of paying a process start. Real tools are PE and are unaffected.

Also gate vasmTarballBuildsAndInstalls on canBuildVasm(): the Windows
runner has make but no cc/gcc/clang, and the production build path
refuses to build without a compiler, so the test failed the refusal
rather than anything it exists to verify.

Admit browser spectators without a count and show one invitation at a time

The Spectators select in Advanced is gone: every hosted room game now opens
its watch room with all eight places when the host clicks Host game, and the
host keeps its confirmed history from frame zero, so spectators can arrive
whenever they like until the places are full. The resize machinery the select
drove goes with it, on the page, in the room client and in the service, whose
POST /watch/{id}/slots route is removed; the refuse route stays, since a host
whose places are all watching still has to turn surplus offers away.

The spectator invitation is its own block with its own QR code. Both
invitations show while the host waits for player 2; once player 2's
connection opens, the spent player invitation gives way and only the
spectator invitation stays for the rest of the game. The code field offers
the one button that fits what it holds, Watch game for a spectator link and
Join game for a player invitation, whether the link was opened or pasted.

The netplay guide, the service README and the worker, hub and room client
tests follow, and the rooms harness checks both invitations and QR codes
while waiting, the hidden player invitation once player 2 is in, the missing
Join button on a spectator link, and a second spectator pasting the same
invitation.

events.title: Voda je jen jezero v RIVERu; _ARCTIC je snih. Rezim prezije reload
events.message:
Voda je jen jezero v RIVERu; _ARCTIC je snih. Rezim prezije reload

Hrac zapnul vlnky ve hre a napsal: "to se vlni v ICE a je to snih a ne
voda". Mel pravdu - a bylo to uz tretí chybne urceni vodni plochy:

1. podle JMENA souboru - `_ARCTIC` jsem povazoval za snih a vynechal
2. podle PODILU indexu 13/14/15 - pribralo `_ARCTIC`, ale v GRASS
   oznacilo za vodu hneda pole
3. podle BARVY (modra > cervena) - opravilo GRASS, ale `_ARCTIC` proslo
   dal, protoze snih je taky modrejsi nez cervenejsi: (11,11,13)

Vykresleno se spravnou paletou je to okamzite videt:

    _ARCTIC#5 (ICE, SCIFI)  index 14 = (10,10,12) na VSECH 168
                            dlazdicich, svetle modrobila = SNIH
    _LAKE#0 (RIVER)         index 14 = (1,4,4), tmave tyrkysova = VODA

V ICE tedy zadna voda neni. `WATER_TILES` je ted obycejny seznam a
udrzuje se vizualnim overenim; automaticke pravidlo zadne. Vodni plocha
klesla z 919 617 na 126 404 bodu - jen jezero v RIVERu.

Kontrakt presmerovan z radku 13600 (to misto vybrala chybna maska) na
13505, nejsirsi misto jezera.

Pri tom se naslo, proc hrac efekty opakovane nevidel: rezim "vylepseno"
se po kazdem reloadu vracel na "original" a vsechny efekty byly potichu
vypnute (overeno: modeorig true, smooth false, localStorage prazdny).
Zvetseni si stranka pamatovala, rezim ne. Ted uz ano.

events.title: Vlnky posouvanim textury - cyklovani palety bylo neviditelne
events.message:
Vlnky posouvanim textury - cyklovani palety bylo neviditelne

Hrac vlnky porad nevidel. Cyklovani tri vodnich indexu bylo technicky
bez chyby (53 081 zmenenych indexu, 0 mimo masku), jenze ty tri odstiny
jsou v cele hre jen krok od sebe:

    RIVER   (1,5,6) (1,4,4) (1,3,3)    rozpeti 6 ze 45
    ICE     (11,11,13) (10,10,12) (9,9,11)
    SCIFI   totez

Jsou to sousedni odstiny jednoho prechodu, kterym je nakreslena vlnkova
textura. Prehazovat je nemuze byt videt nikdy, at je maska sebepresnejsi.
Tri kola se ladila maska, pritom sam efekt byl principialne neviditelny.

Ted se posouva TEXTURA: vlny v dlazdici uz nakreslene jsou, takze se jen

events.title: Refuse spectator place changes once the watch room has ended
events.message:
Refuse spectator place changes once the watch room has ended

A hub whose room had expired or closed with the game still answered a place
change with a fulfilled promise, so the panel announced places it never
asked for and kept showing a dead invitation. An ended hub now rejects every
change, a change overtaken by the room ending fails instead of resolving,
the count drops to zero, and the invitation is withdrawn from the panel.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Let a browser host keep playing until player 2 arrives and change spectator places at any time
events.message:
Let a browser host keep playing until player 2 arrives and change spectator places at any time

Clicking Host game used to snapshot the host's media at once and lock every
machine and disk control while the invitation waited, so a host could not set
up the game it meant to share. The page now only checks that a ROM and every
inserted disk are on hand when hosting starts, keeps running as an ordinary
local page, and captures the media, replaces the machine and locks the
controls when player 2's connection opens. Guests and spectators still lock at
Join game or Watch game.

The Spectators choice was also fixed at hosting time. The select now stays
live for a room host before and during play: the spectator hub opens the
watch room on the first non-zero count and resizes it afterwards, the host
always keeps its confirmed history in room mode so late admission works
whatever the count was at frame zero, and None admits nobody new while
keeping the room, its invitation and everyone already watching. The room
service gains two owner routes for this, POST /watch/{id}/slots (0 to 8) and
POST /watch/{id}/refuse. The service only counts places still in signaling,
so a host whose places are all watching now turns surplus offers away and the
spectator's answer poll reports the refusal instead of waiting for the offer
to expire. Spectator notices hold the status line for a few seconds against
the once-a-second frame report.

The rooms harness inserts DF1 and picks the spectator count only after
hosting, refuses a second spectator when the one place is taken, and goes
from None back to two places on the same invitation; its spectator condition
accepts under a second behind, since a live spectator always trails the
players by the input delay. The netplay guide, the service README and the
worker, room client and hub tests cover the new behaviour.
