events.title: assets: refresh the bundled AROS ROM to master 311afcc057 + PR 1179
events.message:
assets: refresh the bundled AROS ROM to master 311afcc057 + PR 1179

Rebuilt from upstream master at 311afcc057 (2026-09-11) with pull
request 1179 ("m68k: memory footprint reduction", head 2776346929, open
at the time of the build) merged on top. That series trims the resident
OS's own allocations: m68k CPU contexts sized to the detected processor,
ETasks without the scheduler bookkeeping m68k does not use, one sparse
exception-handler list instead of 256 empty ones, Exec pools that start
their first data puddle at the requested size and grow geometrically,
right-sized gameport and CDVDFS buffers, OOP objects allocated without
an AllocVec size prefix, HIDD method and interface tables coallocated,
Intuition class pools and helper tasks created on first use, Shell
buffers sized from the parsed arguments, and RunCommand's temporary
stacks taken from the high end of memory so the largest low-address
block stays contiguous.

Measured with a guest probe calling AvailMem at the instant a --run
staged program starts: total free memory 646,872 -> 741,936 bytes on a
1 MB chip-only A500 and 1,680,816 -> 1,777,232 on a 2 MB A1200, with the
largest contiguous chip block gaining slightly more (630,864 -> 735,632
and 1,664,768 -> 1,770,928). That matches the 96,600 bytes the pull
request reports at Startup-Sequence entry.

The local stack-floor patch is dropped: upstream commit 765871daef now
defines PROC_MINSTACKSIZE as PROC_STACKSIZE (8 KiB), exactly the floor
assets/aros/patches/0001-... restored after e9c4ecde99 lowered it to
4 KiB and broke every --run and copperhf autoboot. With the directory
gone, the libretro packaging step no longer copies it.

The ROM also picks up the cd.device CD32 startup-memory and audio fixes
(00d74535c5, e35256ca74), the revert of the m68k CIA timer one-shot
(93c01c8c78: CheckTimer already forces the microhz interrupt through
SetICR, so the extra 1-tick timer completed timer.device requests early
and hung device init), a Shell hardening series that propagates buffer
failures instead of truncating, console.device and console.handler
bounds and lifetime fixes, Run preserving redirected output handles and
the append position, ata.device ATAPI interrupt and abort fixes, and a
font-list semaphore in graphics/diskfont.

The timing-test golden is re-blessed for the new boot handoff phase, as
on every ROM refresh: 12 of its 32 rows move by 1 to 3 E-clock ticks
(read back over --serial stdout and compared row by row), and the other
44 probes are pixel-identical, bltprobe-pace included this time. The DAP
hello-one-frame cpuprofile golden is re-blessed for the same reason; it
was already stale before this refresh (151 nodes committed against 150
under the previous ROM, 93 commits since it was last blessed), so this
also absorbs that earlier drift.

The full unit and integration suites pass. Of the asset-gated --ignored
suite, only the hardware- and network-gated tests (fluxbridge, blockdev,
gamelib, the floppy-bridge capture probes) and the two pre-existing
failures (run_flag_boots_and_runs_a_guest_binary, mhi_m2_savestate_
resume) fail, as before the refresh.

events.title: Take the mix headroom from the kernel, and the mixer phase from the clock
events.message:
Take the mix headroom from the kernel, and the mixer phase from the clock

Two corrections to the band-limiting, both from review.

The headroom was justified by the shortest period a channel could be given,
quoted as AUDxPER 124. That is the NTSC figure -- this module already spells
both out, and PAL_AUDIO_MIN_PERIOD_CCK is 123 -- but the deeper problem is
that neither is a floor on anything. Both constants describe what audio DMA
can sustain, neither is referenced anywhere, aud_percntrld takes AUDxPER as
given, and a CPU feeding AUDxDAT in IRQ mode is not held to the period DMA
could keep up with. An argument from how fast the staircase may move
therefore cannot bound the overshoot at all.

Take the bound from the decimation kernel instead. The sum of its absolute
taps is the most it can make of input bounded by full scale, whatever that
input is, so scaling by it leaves nothing able to run off the end of the
host's range no matter what the guest plays. That is 1.5792 for this kernel
against 1.3241 for the period-derived figure, which costs a further 1.5 dB
and buys a guarantee that holds unconditionally instead of one resting on a
limit nothing enforces. the_mix_headroom_covers_the_decimation_kernel holds
the constant to the kernel it is claimed for, so the two cannot drift apart,
and the sweep over duty cycles now runs down past the period audio DMA can
sustain. Output is 10.0 dB below the old scaling rather than 8.5 dB.

The decimators also counted their own way to each mixer frame, which
duplicated what host_sample_acc already knew. During a run the two agreed, so
the duplication was invisible; restoring a state written before the
decimators existed broke it. Such a state carries an accumulator that can sit
anywhere within a mixer frame, and serde(default) builds decimators counting
from zero, so the frame boundaries came out one to three oversample slices
late -- and stayed there, since nothing resynchronises them.

Decimator now keeps tap history and nothing else: push records a sample,
output reads the band-limited value, and advance_audio decides when it wants
one. The phase of the mixer grid lives in the accumulator alone, so there is
no second copy to contradict it and no fix-up needed on load.
the_mixer_cadence_follows_the_accumulator_not_the_decimators resumes at each
oversample slice in turn and requires the frame in progress to still be
finished.

No change to the measured result: the worst in-band image stays at -51 dBc,
slice counts are unchanged, and emulation is now about 2% slower than before
the band-limiting rather than 4%, since push no longer branches on a counter
and the kernel is applied once per mixer frame instead of once per channel
per oversample slice.

events.title: Oprava me opravy: `armed` musi zustat shora otevreny; tlacitko zbran +
events.message:
Oprava me opravy: `armed` musi zustat shora otevreny; tlacitko zbran +

**Vcerejsi oprava byla spatne** a hrac to nahlasil hned: po nacteni
pozice byli nepratele jen na zacatku a pak uz zadni.

Pricina: `armed` NEZNAMENA "ted se narodi", ale "je zpusobily se narodit,
az na nej dojde rada". `startGame` ho nastavuje jednou pro celou mapu
dopredu - zmereno, ze hned po startu RIVERu je ozbrojeno 913 z 936
objektu, drtiva vetsina daleko pred hracem. Omezeni `esy >= -256` proto
odzbrojilo **864 objektu dal v mape** a zbytek urovne zustal prazdny.

Spravne je `esy <= 276`: shora otevrene, jen bez objektu, ktere uz jsou
za hracem. Overeno srovnanim MNOZIN objektu, ktere se probudi v useku
500..3000 tiku za bodem ulozeni, proti nepreruseneho behu: **35 = 35,
nula rozdilu v obou smerech**.

Past pri mereni, na kterou jsem naletel: `born` je sticky priznak, ktery
se po smrti objektu nenuluje. Prvni srovnani proto hlasilo 46 chybejicich
objektu, prestoze slo o objekty davno za hracem (esy 541 az 762) - meril
se stav priznaku, ne skutecne probuzeni. Spravne se pocita prechod
`!born -> born`. Kontrakt v uitest.py to ted meri takhle a hlida obe
strany chyby: ze na obrazovce nezustane objekt bez korutiny a ze objekty
dal v mape zustanou ozbrojene.

Pridano vyvojarske tlacitko **"zbran +"**: 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> plna sila
-> zpet na 1. Musi zvedat i `+102` (pocet sebranych bonusu), jinak by
`0x70c8` silu pri dalsim respawnu zase srazila - tabulka `0x70c0`
clampuje strop podle nej. Neni v originale, proto je v testovaci liste.

Vsech sedm kontraktu zelenych, compare 12 radku [OK] / 0 pod prahem.

Nacteni pozice nechavalo objekty na obrazovce bez korutiny

Snimek od hrace ukazal tank, ktery po nacteni ulozene pozice neslo
sestrelit. Prvni kolo hledani slo po tancich samotnych a nic nenaslo -
protoze chyba nebyla v nich, ale v ceste, kterou hra prochazi pri
nacteni.

**Zmereno:** po `loadFromSlot` mel KAZDY objekt na obrazovce
`born: false, armed: false` a zustal tak i po dalsich 60 ticich. Byl
videt, ale nemel korutinu: nehybal se, nestrilel, a sweep ho preskakoval
(`if (!s.born) continue`), takze do nej strely proletly.

Pricina byla v `jumpMap`, kterou `loadFromSlot` pouziva. Ozbrojovala
objekty pravidlem startu urovne (`armedAtStart`, `0x3728`): "zaznam pod
hornim okrajem se tise zahodi". To je spravne pro ZACATEK mapy, kde ctec
jeste nikde nebyl - ale po skoku nebo nacteni je to naopak: do takoveho
mista se v originale nelze dostat jinak nez tim, ze tudy ctec projel,
takze kazdy objekt, ktery uz minul prah -256 a jeste nebyl cullnuty,
svou korutinu dostal.

Byl to **muj vedomy kompromis, ktery se ukazal jako spatny**. Komentar u
nej tvrdil, ze nic dalsiho nastavovat nesmime, protoze objekt s `born`
bez rozpracovaneho stavu shodi `step()` (boss bez `parts`). To plati pro
primy zapis `born = true` - NE pro `armed = true`, kdy si objekt
inicializaci udela sam normalni cestou pres `startMapObjectTask`.

Opraveno na `esy >= -256 && esy <= 276`. Overeno 98 skoky pres vsech sedm
zon (pulzona po pulzone, 40 tiku po kazdem): zadny pad, zadna JS chyba.
Kontrakt v uitest.py hlida, ze po nacteni neni na obrazovce zadny objekt
bez korutiny a ze tank jde sestrelit.

Pravidlo startu urovne zustava beze zmeny: compare 11/11 (12 radku [OK],
0 pod prahem), spawncheck 980/981, lockstep i zbytek zelene.

events.title: MEDTANK ma tridu podle TYPU; vylepseny rezim zapne vsechny podvolby
events.message:
MEDTANK ma tridu podle TYPU; vylepseny rezim zapne vsechny podvolby

**Hlaseni "v RIVERu jsou tanky, ktere nejdou rozstrelit".** Sestrelitelne
jsou - zmereno tak, ze se hrac postavil pod kazdy druh a stridal palbu:
`tank` umira po 28 ticich, `flattank` po 115, `juntank` po 16 pri primem
zasahu. Dojem dela HP, ktere u `tank` a `flattank` NENI konstantni, ale
roste s obtiznosti (`0x9ee2`/`0x9e1a`: `fp@(182) + 1`, resp. `+ 5`);
v RIVERu po nekolika minutach vychazi obtiznost 6-7, takze flattank ma
11-12 HP a pri sile zbrane 1 jsou to dve sekundy palby. To prepis ma
spravne a vzorec obtiznosti `0x1cd4` sedi vcetne vsech tri posunu a klapu.

**Skutecna odchylka byla jinde.** `0x9ece` da MEDTANKu `d1 = 36`, ale
`0x9ed4` testuje **bit 3 v typu** a pri jeho nastaveni preda `a2c6` tridu
**32** - takovy tank zustane sestrelitelny, ale kontaktem nezabije ani
jeden stroj. V RIVERu jsou to typy 9 a 10, tri z devatenacti tanku.
Prepis mel tridu jen podle chovani, takze tyhle tri zabijely jeep.
Opraveno pres `a2c6Class(o)`. MEDTANK je **jedine** chovani z 73, kde
trida zavisi na typu - overeno skenem vsech rutin na vicenasobne plneni
`d1` pred `a2c6`; ostatni nalezy patri formacnimu `0xa2a2`.

**a2c6check.py u toho lhal**: HP zavisle na obtiznosti cetl jako
chybejici a hlasil `tank`/`flattank`/`yellow` jako neshodu, prestoze je
prepis ma spravne. Ted umi `fp@(182) + N` na obou stranach a vypisuje
`obtiznost+N`. Regex musi respektovat "prvni prirazeni do `s.hp` vyhrava",
jinak precte HP nasledujiciho chovani (blok pretece) - to docasne pridalo
falesne `goose7` a `popup`. Zbyva sest znamych a dokumentovanych hlaseni.

**Vylepseny rezim** ma ted vsechny tri podvolby (hloubka ostrosti, mekke
stiny, prolnuti pohybu) zaskrtnute uz od zacatku. Prepnuti zpet na
original je vsechny vypne bez ohledu na zaskrtnuti, at je "original"
opravdu original.

Vsech sedm kontraktu zelenych, compare 11/11.

events.title: Band-limit Paula's output onto the host mixer grid
events.message:
Band-limit Paula's output onto the host mixer grid

Paula's DAC output is a staircase: each channel holds its 8-bit sample for
AUDxPER colour clocks and steps at up to ~28.6 kHz, so the summed output only
ever changes on the 3.546895 MHz colour-clock grid. The mixer read that
staircase once per 44.1 kHz frame, which folds everything above the mixer's
Nyquist straight back into the audible band.

Amiga Test Kit's 10 kHz square -- two samples at AUDxPER 177, full volume on
all four channels -- shows it plainly. Its harmonics at 30, 50 and 70 kHz
arrived as tones at 14.0, 6.0 and 18.1 kHz, the worst of them only 10 dB under
the tone itself, alongside sideband pairs from the beat between Paula's
20038.95 Hz sample rate and 44.1 kHz. Being inharmonic, that is heard as
ringing rather than brightness.

The mix now runs on a grid four times the mixer's rate and filters down onto
it. advance_audio bounds each step so that neither an oversample instant nor a
channel period expiry falls strictly inside one, which holds each channel's
level constant across the step and lets channel_area accumulate
sample * volume * clocks exactly; dividing by the interval width at each
oversample instant is then a true box average of the staircase rather than a
sample of whichever step the instant landed on. One Decimator per channel, new
in src/audio/resample.rs and sharing the windowed-sinc kernel Resampler
already builds, takes that 4:1 to the mixer rate. Per channel rather than per
side because decimation is linear, so the per-channel stem taps stay exactly
consistent with the mix they sum to.

Four is where the two stages balance: the box average needs the oversample
rate well above Paula's own, and the kernel's transition band needs it low
enough to stay clear of the top of the audio band. The worst surviving image
in that test drops from -10 dBc to -51 dBc. Two leaves a -28 dBc spur, and
neither eight nor a longer kernel improves on four.

This is also what lets the LED filter sit where hardware puts it, after the
channel mixer's summation. Filtering a point-sampled mix attenuated the real
tone while leaving untouched the aliases that had already folded below the
cutoff: with the filter engaged, the same 10 kHz test came out as a 2 kHz buzz
nearly 6 dB louder than the tone it was meant to be attenuating. The tone is
now the loudest thing in the output, with everything else at least 43 dB down.

Genuine zero-order-hold images of Paula's own sample rate are kept, since they
are real output ahead of the hardware's analogue filter: the 500 Hz test still
carries its images at 19.5 and 20.5 kHz.

Set the level against what Paula can actually produce, too. Each side takes
two channels, so the mix divided one channel's DAC level by 128 * 64 and
summed, reaching +/-2.0 on a +/-1.0 scale. The comment there said the worst
case was essentially never real music, which the test kit's four channels of
full-volume square hit exactly, and nothing between the mix and the host
device clips: 97.7% of that capture sat outside +/-1.0. Full scale is now both
channels saturated at full volume plus the headroom the band-limited waveform
needs to overshoot them, since taking a square's harmonics away leaves
something taller than the square that carried them. The shortest legal period
bounds it: AUDxPER 124 holds a sample for a little over six oversample
intervals, and the most a run that long draws out of the kernel is 1.3241
times the staircase. PAULA_RECONSTRUCTION_HEADROOM rounds that to 1.33, so
nothing Paula can play leaves the host's range. Output is 8.5 dB quieter as a
result.

Sources line-mixed alongside Paula keep their level relative to a Paula
channel. Their sum with it is still not separately limited, so a CD32 playing
a full-scale CD track under a full-scale module can ask for more than full
scale, as it could before.

The emulated timeline is untouched: advance_audio runs the same channel state
machine over the same colour clocks either way, and the finer splitting only
changes how often it is re-entered. Slice counts are identical before and
after, and the golden probe renders are unchanged. Emulation is about 4%
slower with all four channels at AUDxPER 177 and about 2% on an ordinary boot.

host_sample_acc keeps the meaning and range it always had, with the oversample
grid read off it as a finer threshold, so the PAUL chunk needs no version
bump. channel_area, area_cck and the decimators' tap histories are
serde(default), and a state written before them resumes with silent histories.

events.title: Hra ve dvou po siti: lockstep bez serveru
events.message:
Hra ve dvou po siti: lockstep bez serveru

Po siti jdou JEN VSTUPY a obe strany pocitaji tutez simulaci. Herni kod
se kvuli tomu nezmenil ani o radek - nova vrstva jen rozhoduje, KDY smi
`step()` bezet a cim jsou naplnene `g.keys`/`g.keys2`. Lokalni umysl
hrace se drzi zvlast v `g.netLocal`, jinak by ho sitovy vstup prepsal.

- **Vstupni zpozdeni 3 tiky** (60 ms): vlastni vstup pro tik `t+3` vznika
  a odesila se v tiku `t`. Prvni tri tiky se predvyplni prazdnym vstupem.
- **Signalling je rucni** - kazda strana ukaze kod a vlozi ten druhy.
  Projekt tim zustava jeden staticky soubor bez serveru. SDP se zabali
  `CompressionStream('deflate-raw')`, takze kod ma ~700-800 znaku misto
  nekolika kilobajtu a da se poslat chatem.
- **Kontrolni soucet .adf** je primo v kodu: SWIVFIX a ciste SWIV se lisi
  uz startovni zbrani, takze bez teto kontroly by se hry rozesly hned a
  nebylo by poznat proc.
- **Detektor rozjezdu** porovnava otisk stavu kazdych 50 tiku.
- U kazdeho stroje sedi jeden hrac, takze obe sady klaves ovladaji jeho
  vlastni stroj. Hostitel ridi vrtulnik, host jeep (pripoji se palbou za
  kredit jako lokalne).

`tools/nettest.py` je sedmy kontrakt a bezi v REALNEM CASE s normalnim
rAF, tedy tou cestou, kterou pujde skutecny hrac: hostitel v Chromiu
(V8), host ve WebKitu (JavaScriptCore), spojeni pres skutecny WebRTC
datovy kanal. **400 spolecnych tiku, 0 neshod**, obe strany vidi dva
hrace. Zkouska detektoru: umely posun hrace o 3 px na jedne strane byl
zachycen do jedne periody porovnani - bez ni by prosel i detektor, ktery
nic nehlida.

Meze jsou v GAPS: symetricky NAT by potreboval relay (a ten uz je server;
prepis to pozna a rekne misto aby visel), zpozdeni je pevne, pauza neni
synchronizovana a rozjezd se jen hlasi, neresi.

Vsech sedm kontraktu zelenych, compare 11/11 beze zmeny.

events.title: tools/lockstep.py: simulace je bit po bitu stejna ve V8 i JavaScriptCore
events.message:
tools/lockstep.py: simulace je bit po bitu stejna ve V8 i JavaScriptCore

Sesty kontrakt. Pred jakoukoli sitovou hrou je potreba vedet, jestli dva
prohlizece spocitaji z tychz vstupu tentyz stav; tenhle skript to meri
primo misto aby se to odvozovalo. Tyz skriptovany beh v Chromiu (V8) a
WebKitu (JavaScriptCore), otisk celeho stavu po kazdem tiku.

**5600 tiku ve ctyrech scenarich bit po bitu shodnych**, vcetne dvou
hracu, palby, skoku jeepu a prechodu pres SWAP plosiny v RIVERu.

Kontrakt ma vlastni kontrolu citlivosti: posune hraci `x` o jediny ulp
(2,8e-14 px) a overi, ze se otisk zmeni. Bez toho by prosel i otisk,
ktery nic nemeri. Otisk porovnava BITY cisel pres Float64Array, ne
zaokrouhleny text, aby rozdil v posledni platne cifre nepropadl.

**OPRAVA drivejsiho tvrzeni.** Vcera jsem napsal, ze `SIN256` pocitana
pres `Math.sin` je riziko rozjezdu a chce ji predpocitat na konstanty.
Neni. Zmereno: hodnota nejblizsi hranici zaokrouhleni je index 229
(-157,499287), tedy 1,25e10 ulp od preklopeni, zatimco rozdily `Math.sin`
mezi enginy jsou radu jednotek ulp. Navic tatáz tabulka je v AMPROG.OBJ
na 0x6a82 a porovnani dalo **0 neshod ve vsech 256 polozkach** - prepis
uz ted pocita presne ta cisla, ktera ma hra v datech. Zadna zmena kodu
tedy nebyla potreba a lockstep je proveditelny bez zasahu do simulace.

Zbyva mimo simulaci: signalling server, vstupni zpozdeni, kontrolni
soucet ADF v handshake a periodicke porovnani otisku jako detektor
rozjezdu - k tomu uz staci `window.__hash` z tohoto kontraktu.

events.title: Camputers Lynx: 48K, 96K and 128K, with cassette, floppy and keyboard (#28)
events.message:
Camputers Lynx: 48K, 96K and 128K, with cassette, floppy and keyboard (#28)

* Camputers Lynx 48K, 96K and 128K support

An eighth machine: a Z80A at 4MHz with a Motorola 6845 sequencing the
raster over three one-bit colour planes. All three models boot their real
ROMs to the BASIC prompt and take keyboard input.

Banking is the unusual part, and there are two schemes. A write lands in
every enabled bank at once, and a read comes from whichever bank the
decode selects, as one of a handful of fixed eight-page layouts. The
48K/96K take that on port 0x7F with two bits of port 0x80 joining in; the
128K moves it to port 0x82 with both nibbles bit-reversed and swapped end
for end, adds a fourth RAM bank, and drops port 0x80 from the decode.
Their write paths differ too: the 48K/96K video banks leave A13 and A15
out of the decode, so one store lands at four addresses, while the 128K
decodes in full.

Video follows from that. Each board keeps its planes elsewhere and steps
rasters by its own stride, and the 128K programs the 6845 for 64 columns
rather than 32 - so it is 512 pixels across, with pixels half as wide.
Rows are counted from the CRTC display region rather than a fixed border,
and the frame takes its line count from the 6845 with the interrupt
driven off VSYNC.

The keyboard has no select register: the line number rides in A8-A11 of a
read at port 0x80, so the port decode takes the whole 16-bit address.

Tape and disk are not fitted yet - the media service says so rather than
mounting something that would not load - so the 96K and 128K do not claim
built-in drives, though their FD1793 answers the bus.

Verified headless against the hosted ROM sets: all three reach the prompt,
draw their sign-on, and echo typed keys.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01USAgYedo5mR5nC7pur8DQa

* Lynx cassette support, and put the Lynx in the model menu

Two things, one of which should never have shipped.

The Lynx was registered but had no entry in the model menu, so it could
not be selected at all - the machine booted, passed every test, and was
unreachable. MODEL_LABELS is exhaustive over MachineModel so the compiler
catches a missing label, but a missing menu entry was invisible. The menu
now lives in its own module beside the pane, held against the registry by
a test that fails if a registered model cannot be reached, or the menu
offers one the registry does not have.

Cassettes now load. Lynx .tap shares an extension with the ZX Spectrum's
and nothing else: no length prefixes and no checksums, just entries whose
size is implied by a type letter and a 16-bit field inside them, with the
leader tones left out of the file entirely. The parser puts the leader and
sync byte back and hands the shared pulse deck a pure-data block per entry,
because on the wire each byte is eight bits MSB first with no start or stop
bit, and a bit is one square-wave cycle whose width alone says which bit it
is. The 128K runs its tape at twice the speed, so its cells are half as
wide. Sizes and encoding are MAME's camplynx_cas.cpp, checked against the
TOSEC images.

The transport needs none of the CPC's cadence guessing: the Lynx has a
real motor relay on port 0x80, so the deck runs when the ROM spins it. The
deck is advanced on each cassette read rather than once a frame, since the
ROM measures the gap between edges and has to see the level at the T-state
of the read. A Spectrum .tap is refused by name rather than played as noise.

Verified by loading real software end to end on the 48K: Lynx Invaders,
3D Monster Craze, Gobble de Spook, Mazeman, Mined Out and Deathball all
load from tape and run, in colour, through to gameplay.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01USAgYedo5mR5nC7pur8DQa

* The Lynx Save menu offered saves it cannot produce

The Save menu was keyed to a coarse 'spectrum'/'cpc'/'vdp' family, so the
Lynx declared 'spectrum' and offered .szx/.z80 and .scr entries despite
having no snapshot or screen-dump service. Replace the family with a
per-machine list of entries (SaveMenuItem[]), so a machine names exactly
what it can write. The Lynx now lists Screenshot (.png) and RAM (.bin); the
raw .bin dump is universal, backed by LynxMemory.ramSnapshot() (256K on the
48K/96K, 320K on the 128K, matching MAME's RAM device). A capability test
holds every declared entry against the service that must honour it, and
requires every machine to offer .bin.

Non-square pixels (pixelAspectX < 1 — Lynx 128K, CPC, SAM, Einstein-256) are
squeezed by the CSS box. With image-rendering: pixelated, the compositor's
2:1 nearest-neighbour downscale dropped every other source pixel at 1x
(missing columns); 2x was unaffected because each source pixel is then two
backing pixels. Let the compositor filter that axis instead — vertical is
always 1:1, so nothing else changes.

* Lynx tape display, turbo loading, and reload restore

The Lynx's .tap name entry and typed data entry now carry their file
identity, so the tape pane lists them as a Spectrum-style load line
(BASIC / CODE) and pairs the name header with the data block that follows.

Turbo while loading now engages on the Lynx. The machine has a real motor
relay, so the loading signal is the motor plus cassette-port reads rather
than the CPC's read-cadence guess; a 25-frame cooldown rides out the gap
between blocks, and the frame probe drives the TURBO lamp.

A model switch rewinds a tape carried across to its first block.

The persisted-model whitelist is now derived from the registry. It had been
hand-listed and omitted lynx48/96/128, so an F5 reload rejected the saved
model, cleared it, and fell back to the Spectrum.

* The Lynx tape pane listed a file's data entry twice

Format-tagged tape blocks (the Lynx's quoted name entry and its typed data
entry) showed the same file line on both the name header and the data child,
so uncombining them produced two copies of `LOAD "NAME"`.

Uncombined, the data child now lists as the raw `Data N bytes` entry — the
same header/data split the Spectrum's TAP blocks use. Combined, it still
hides behind its name header.

* Lynx floppy disks: .ldf raw dumps on the 96K and 128K

The FD1793 and its DOS ROM were already wired, but the machine had no disk
service, so the Drive pane never appeared and .ldf images were refused. Add
the missing pieces:

- media/floppy/ldf-image.ts parses, serializes and blanks the headerless
  Lynx dump: 512-byte sectors, 10 a track, cylinder-major with heads
  interleaved. 200K is 40 tracks single sided, 800K 80 tracks double sided
  (MAME's camplynx_dsk.cpp).
- LynxDiskService drives the two internal units.
- LynxMediaService mounts .ldf into A: or B: on disk models and still refuses
  it on the 48K.
- The descriptor now claims builtinDisk (so the Drive pane and floppy sound
  appear), adds the dsk LED and persists disks; the Drive pane offers blank
  Lynx disks instead of the +3 DSK/HFE set.
- The frame probe ticks the FDC (format latch, latch decay) and feeds the
  drive-sound fields.
- The DOS ROM is exposed as the Memory pane's `rom-dos` region.

* Lynx: the DOS ROM gets its own socket, and an FD1793 toggle

The DOS ROM was the fourth entry of the concatenated system image, so the ROM
pane showed one combined "System + DOS ROMs" socket. Split it out: every Lynx
ROM socket is one 8K image — two system images on the 48K, three plus the DOS
ROM on the 96K/128K — and each is independently overridable through the shared
MTX-style multi-slot machinery (a Lynx branch in romPageSlotCount/romSlotSize).

Add a Hardware-pane "Disk interface (FD1793)" checkbox. Switching it off
rebuilds the machine with the interface removed: the DOS socket disappears
from the ROM pane, .ldf media is refused, the FDC ports and drive LEDs go
away, and the Drives pane hides. The Lynx 48K has no interface to toggle, so
the checkbox is not shown for it.

* The Lynx FD1793 addresses four drives (A-D)

The FDC was modelled with two units, so only A:/B: existed. The FD179x drives
two select lines and the Lynx DOS manual says up to four drives (A-D), so widen
it:

- WD179x core: four-wide disk/head/write-protect/dirty arrays and `& 3` unit
  indexing, plus `selectDrive` over 0-3. Transparent to the SAM/Beta/MTX, which
  use at most two.
- Lynx port 0x58 decodes both drive-select bits.
- LynxDiskService exposes A-D, and the descriptor declares `builtinDrives: 4`
  (the pane reads that capability, so the extra rows appear before the machine
  is built — the live service is not reactive at first render).
- The shell disk transport is generalized to four units through a DISK_UNITS
  table, and `restoreMedia` restores `ui.builtinDrives` of them.
- The Drive pane renders C:/D: rows for machines with more than two built-in
  drives, and the Hardware checkbox is relabelled "Floppy disks" to match the
  other optional-disk systems.

* The Lynx tape deck did not restart after running off the end

`cassetteInput` advances the deck by the CPU time since the last read, but it
returns early while the deck is not playing — so `tapeLastAdvanceT` froze once
the tape ran off the end. A later rewind + play then advanced by the whole idle
gap (hundreds of millions of T-states) and jumped straight back to the end.

Re-base the advance clock whenever the deck (re)starts — `resetTapeAdvance()`
on mount, play, resume and rewind. The motor-on path already did this via
`setTapeMotor`.

* A Camputers Lynx keyboard, traced from a 48K

The Lynx was the last machine with a key matrix and no on-screen keyboard.
The deck is 16u wide and every row is centred on it, which is what produces
the staircase: the SHIFT row runs the full 16u, the A row 15u, and the number
and Q rows 14.5u, so each row above starts a quarter unit further right than
the one below. Row widths, the 1.5u caps and the stagger are measured off a
photograph, where a cap top is 63px against a 94px pitch. Caps sit 2 units
apart and the wells clear them by the same 2, so every gap on the face is the
one measurement.

Two cells the host key map had wrong. SHIFT LOCK is [0,3], which MAME leaves
unnamed and the MiSTer Lynx48 core identifies; between them the matrix
accounts for every cap on the deck but BREAK, and every cell but [9,4], which
no cap reaches. The old map pointed the host End key at that phantom cell, so
it carries CapsLock instead.

BREAK gets no cell at all. It is not a matrix key: it pulls the CPU's
interrupt line, which this machine already asserts once a frame, so the cap
depresses under the pointer and reaches no switch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Each machine declares the drive it sounds like

Every probe published floppyProfile its own way. The Spectrum carried an
inline copy of the capacity test that profileForDisk already does, the SAM
and the Spectrum's +D path used a bare 1, and the machines with no drive a
bare -1, so whether a machine was fixed or adaptable was implicit in each
call site rather than stated anywhere.

A drive path now names itself once, at the top of its probe: fixedDrive for
the machines that only ever shipped the one kind of unit, byCapacity for the
+3 and the CPC, which shipped a 3" CF2 but were routinely fitted with a 720K
3.5". It is per interface, not per machine -- the Spectrum's +3 controller
adapts while its +D/Beta path is always 3.5" -- so the per-frame line becomes
one uniform call. fixedDrive closes over its code at module load, so sample()
still allocates nothing.

The Lynx moves to 5.25" with it. Camputers shipped the machine with 5.25"
drives, and its 800K format is 80 tracks double-sided: past the capacity
where the shared test would have called it a 3.5" had it been adaptable,
which is exactly why the choice belongs to the machine and not to the disk.

The two emulator tests that stub floppy-sound.ts now spread importOriginal
and stub only FloppySound, which reaches for Web Audio. Listing the pure
exports by hand is what broke them here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Boot: a filing system softloaded into sideways RAM can be the fourth bank (#18)
events.message:
Boot: a filing system softloaded into sideways RAM can be the fourth bank (#18)

hexwab's portability list (#18), item 9, reversed by KC: ZMMFS is
common on a model B. Its bootloader copies MMFS into the highest free
sideways RAM bank and marks it in the ROM table at &02A1, and PARSWR
skips every marked bank, so a B with four banks and ZMMFS found three
and refused.

PARSWR's SwrImage: only at exactly three clean banks, the highest bank
that has a ROM type AND is RAM (MMFS's own test - flip &8006, read back,
flip back, interrupts off) becomes the fourth slot, SWRAM_XFER, and the
report says so. Four clean banks and nothing changes; the intro borrows
only the first two slots.

.start loads PARXFER LAST, after the font, staged at XFER_STREAM = &4000;
then claims the NMI (the last call the image must answer), zeroes the
bank's ROM-table byte so the MOS never offers it a service call again,
and only then unpacks into it. BootBanks does three banks. make_disc.py
writes PARXFER's load address and puts it after PARAFNT on the disc.
Code image +9 (code_end &2FC9 -> &2FD2, 46 free).

Verified in jsbeeb with a fake ROM image planted in bank 7 of a Master
(exactly four banks): the old image refused with FOUND 3; the new one
detected 4 5 6 7 with the image line and played, and the image's last
service call was 12 (the NMI claim), its &02A8 byte 00, bank 7 holding
PARXFER, &0D00 = &40. The same through the -Intro build, where the image
survived the intro intact. B/DFS 1.20 and B/1770, with and without the
intro, still play. No real ZMMFS machine tried.

Refs #18

events.title: Zony mimo TOWN a DESERT: zoneshot.py a prvni checkpoint v GRASS
events.message:
Zony mimo TOWN a DESERT: zoneshot.py a prvni checkpoint v GRASS

MEGA TRAINER zadny level select nema - overeno snimkem jeho obrazovky
(F1 zivoty, F2 kredity, F3 zbrane, F4 spread, F5-F8 autofire). Do
dalsich zon se tedy hra sama nedostane: `0x3cbe` scrolluje jen pri
`fp@(166) == 0` a bit 3 drzi ziva instalace, kterou drzeny fire za 1200 s
nezniici (snimky t=600, t=900 i t=1200 stoji na tomtez radku).

`tools/survey/zoneshot.py` proto pousti original v harnessu ve
WebAssembly a **kazdy snimek mu zhasne jen bit 3** v `fp@(166)`. Bit 1
zustava: ten drzi scroll, dokud stavitel terennich pruhu (`0x3422`) neni
32 radku napred, a bez nej by se rolovalo do nepostavene mapy. Mapova
data, palety, Copper i blitter delaji dal svou praci, takze pro TEREN a
vykreslovani je snimek plnohodnotny; pro chovani objektu ne, protoze hra
bezi s trainerem a hrac strili.

Pozice se cte z `fp@(3530)` - 16.16, cela cast je HORNI slovo (prvni
pokus cetl cely long a vysly z toho nesmysly).

Novy typ checkpointu `zone` stavi prepis **bez jedineho objektu** (jen

events.title: JEEP davka 6: skore obou slotu pres attribuci +506 - plan hotovy
events.message:
JEEP davka 6: skore obou slotu pres attribuci +506 - plan hotovy

**Komu se skore pripise, rika `+506`** - tytez slovo, ve kterem sweep
sklada udalosti. Bity 0..5 vybiraji handler (`0x64b6`), **bit 6 = zasah
slotu 1, bit 7 = zasah slotu 2**, a `0xa36a` je cte v tomto poradi:

    a36e: d0 = +506
    a372: a0 = fp@(11176)     ; slot 1
    a376: btst #6,d0 / bne -> pripsat
    a37c: a0 = fp@(11356)     ; slot 2
    a380: btst #7,d0 / beq -> NIKDO
    a38c: a0@(76) += +362

Bit 6 ma prednost. `0x710c` po pripsani porovna `+76` s `+84`: pri
prekroceni prida 30000, ubere zivot z `+68` a pricte **6000 do `+110`** -
extra zivot tedy zvedne obtiznost. Kdyz `+68` dojde (`0x709a`), `0x70ac`
odlozi skore do `+80` a uloha slotu skonci.

V prepisu: `collectBulletEvent` vraci masku vlastniku misto booleanu,
cile si ji odkladaji do `creditMask`, `creditedSlot` z ni vybira slot.
Strely nesou `owner`. Zmereno: tataz strela da 12 bodu slotu 1, nebo
slotu 2, podle vlastnika. Slot 2 ma vlastni prah zivota (10000, pak po
30000) i rank bonus; po vycerpani zasoby se zavre, odlozi nejlepsi skore
a da se koupit za dalsi kredit.

**Vedoma odchylka:** `0xa36a` pri nulove masce nedava skore nikomu,
prepis ho da slotu 1. `+506` nese udalost i attribuci v jednom slove,
takze kdyz callback bezi, je bit 6 nebo 7 prakticky vzdy nastaveny;
nulova maska nastava jen u smrti mimo sweep. Chovat se tam jako driv
znamena, ze se jednohracska hra nikde nehnula - HUD je na vsech osmi
checkpointech dal 100 %. Zapsano v GAPS spolu se sdilenym poolem strel,
TOKENy jen pro slot 1 a continue oknem jen pro slot 1.

Tim je plan z docs/PLAN-JEEP.md cely hotovy. Vsech pet kontraktu
zelenych, compare 8/8.

events.title: JEEP davka 5: SWAP plosiny prepinaji cele vozidlo - pribyla lod 0x8e26
events.message:
JEEP davka 5: SWAP plosiny prepinaji cele vozidlo - pribyla lod 0x8e26

Rozpis rikal "SWAP plosiny a dopravnik, 0,5 dne". Byl spatne. Plosiny
nejsou dekorace, ktera by neco odemykala, ale **prepinac mezi dvema
podobami vozidla**: slot 2 ma vedle jeepu jeste lod `0x8e26`.

**Dvojice plosin.** `0xac6a` (SWAP#0, dvojice A) a `0xacb6` (SWAP#1, B)
zapisou po `0x9afa(32)` svou polohu do sve dvojice `fp@(3550..3557)` a
**vynuluji tu druhou** - plati vzdy jen pozdejsi. Pak cekaji, dokud
vozidlo nenastavi `fp@(3548)`, a teprve tehdy zapisou `fp@(3558)`, coz
je strop pro `0x94f0`.

**Prepnuti** dela `0x94c2` (z jeepu) a `0x94d0` (z lodi), volane kazdy
tik z hlavy smycky: `y - 64 <= y protejsi plosiny` -> `0x6160` zalozi
druhy tvar, `0x6db4` ukonci tenhle. Novy tvar jde pres spolecne `0x9046`
a `0x90a0`/`0x8e38` jej rovnou prenese na jeho vlastni plosinu.
Zmereno v RIVERu: lod vznikne na `x = 270`, jeep zpatky na `x = 303` -
presne souradnice obou plosin v mape.

**Lod** se od jeepu lisi: grafika `JEEPHELI#31`, za jizdy `#25`
(`0x8ee8`); rychlost `+356 = 768` = 3 px/t proti 2,5; pri pustene pace
`0x8f22` ubira z rychlosti osminu (`asrl #3`) misto nulovani, takze
dojizdi; brazda `0x9358` kazdy ctvrty tik za jizdy a kazdy sestnacty VBL
pri stani; houpani ma zlomek od `0x8000` a gravitaci `-3072` misto
`-4096`, takze se houpe vyrazneji. Vez `0x89e8`, skok i kolize s terenem
jsou spolecne.

**Stopy jeepu** (`0x9172` -> `0xad78` -> `0xad98`) jsou tentyz dekal
`JEEPHELI#40..#43` jako vez tanku, jen po trech ticich misto po dvaceti.

V prepisu jsou oba tvary jednim objektem s `form: "jeep" | "boat"`;
original ukonci jednu ulohu a zalozi druhou, ale stav, na kterem zalezi,
stejne zije v rodici `+276`.

Kontrakt v uitest.py projede RIVER, overi obe prepnuti na spravnych x,
vzajemne vylouceni dvojic plosin, nastaveni `fp@(3548)`/`fp@(3558)` a
rychlost i dojezd lodi. Vsech pet kontraktu zelenych, compare 8/8.

events.title: JEEP davka 4: skok 0x91e8 vcetne automatiky a prohozeni kolizni tridy
events.message:
JEEP davka 4: skok 0x91e8 vcetne automatiky a prohozeni kolizni tridy

Skok se ukazal bohatsi, nez rikal rozpis:

**Automaticky spoustec.** `+282` neni timeout. `0x91c4` ho drzi na 15,
dokud jeep NENI zablokovany; kdyz do prekazky tlaci, `0x9136` ho kazdy
tik ubira a po patnacti ticich jeep sam vyskoci a prehoupne se pres ni.
Stani na miste jej nastavi na 5 (`0x91a0`). Rucni skok je bit 6 vstupu.

**Kolizni trida se PROHAZUJE, nevypina.** `+504` bit 4 -> bit 3 vymeni
handler: `0x654c` da `+518` (udalost 1 = vzdusne objekty), `0x6558`
zpatky `+522` (udalost 2 = pozemni). Jeep tedy prehopne tank, ale ve
vzduchu ho muze srazit letec.

**Vyska `+328`** se integruje v `0x62d2` (`0x62fe`..`0x6336`): rychlost
se nejdriv zvysi o zrychleni, pak se pricte k poloze, a pri podteceni
pod nulu se vsechny tri longy vynuluji naraz - to je dopad. Zmereno:
skok trva **58 tiku** a ma vrchol **27,3 px**; `+356` je pritom 896
(3,5 px/t) a uhel veze se pres skok drzi (zasobnik 0x9228/0x9250).

**Chveni na zemi.** `0x9154` losuje jen DOLNI slovo `+340`, tedy zlomek
rychlosti (`(rnd & 0x7fff) + 0x4000`), a drzi gravitaci. Jeep se tim
chveje o 0 az ~4 px a cte PRNG kazdy tik - dvouhracska hra ma proto
v originale jiny tok RNG nez sam vrtulnik. Protoze `z` posouva jen STIN
(`0x6364`), je to videt jako poskakovani stinu pod vozem a ve skoku jako
jeho odpojeni.

Vedlejsi nalez: `0x4dc6` byla posledni zvukova rutina bez volajiciho a
patri prave sem (`0x920a`, panorama podle x). Doplnena i zastarala
poznamka v SOUND.md o AMHITUNE, ktera uz od 2026-09-07 neplati.

Klavesa skoku je `q`. Kontrakt v uitest.py meri delku skoku, vrchol,
stav po dopadu, rozsah chveni a to, ze pozemni objekt jeep ve vzduchu
nezabije. Vsech pet kontraktu zelenych.

events.title: Take the beam layout height from Agnus, not from field parity
events.message:
Take the beam layout height from Agnus, not from field parity

Inferring "interlaced short field" from an even line count was wrong for
programmable beam totals: VARBEAMEN drives the beam entirely and overrides
the interlace long/short selection, so a 200-line frame is 200 lines every
frame and was being laid out as 201, with picking shifted and clamped at the
bottom row.

Agnus already reckons the height a capture belongs to. `nominal_frame_lines`
returns the long field of an interlaced signal and a programmable total as it
stands, so carry that on the trace and lay out against it, rather than
deriving a field mode from parity.

Also restore the widget metadata the replaced standard widgets carried. The
tabs, sub-tabs, mode segments and close boxes are drawn controls, so they
report their label, role and selected state; the close box is painted rather
than typed and names the inspector it closes. AccessKit is not compiled into
this build, so nothing consumes this yet, but the controls no longer describe
themselves less than the widgets they replaced.

Darken the muted tab colour. A closed tab is dimmed to read as inactive, but
it is still an actionable control, and 139,146,158 on the panel background
was 2.74:1 -- below the 4.5:1 needed to stay legible. 98,105,117 is 4.84:1
and still clearly apart from the ink used by an open tab.

events.title: Show what each inspector tab holds, and close from the tab
events.message:
Show what each inspector tab holds, and close from the tab

The Debug workspace drew an inspector open behind the current one exactly
like one that had never been opened, so "open" was not a visible state. That
is what made the strip's single "Close inspector" button read as doing
nothing: with no way to see that an inspector was open, closing it showed no
change. The button also sat at the far end of the strip from the tab it
acted on, and could only ever reach the selected inspector.

Each tab now says which of the three states it is in -- not open, open
behind, open and shown -- and carries its own close box, which closes the
inspector it is drawn on, background ones included. A dot reports whether
that inspector's capture is armed on the machine in front of you, which is
the only indication of the cost an inspector keeps paying once you are back
in Play.

The title bar's "Return to Play" button becomes a Play/Debug switch. Leaving
Debug is a change of view, not a dismissal: the inspectors stay open and keep
capturing, and a two-state switch reads that way where a button did not. The
tabs within an inspector are underlined rather than filled so the two levels
of the header cannot be mistaken for each other.

Also lay the beam diagram out against the long field. An interlaced signal
alternates a long field and a short field one line shorter, and the captured
trace reports the field it took, so the diagram grew and shrank on every
frame with everything below it moving, and a held pointer read alternating
rows. Size, pick and overlay against the long field, clamping the row to the
field actually captured.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Re-arm the open inspectors when the machine is replaced
events.message:
Re-arm the open inspectors when the machine is replaced

The inspectors are host state and outlive the machine they were opened on,
but everything they capture with is armed on the bus and the CPU: the frame
analyzer's slot trace, its heat map, the CPU's recent-PC ring, and the
reverse-debug ring. A machine built by the launcher's Run comes up with none
of it, and the panels stay open across the swap, so their open guards skip
the arming they only do on first open.

The analyzer then sat dead on the new machine until its own Run happened to
re-arm it -- a pause and a run, which reads as the pane having stopped rather
than the capture -- while Recent PCs, the reverse controls and the heat map
stayed dead with it.

Re-arm what is still open against the machine that has just been built,
under the same ownership rule the Memory tab applies, so the pane does not
claim a heat map on the new machine that it would not have armed on the old
one.

docs: the intro's *TAPE, investigated and tested (#18)

hexwab's portability list (#18), KC's ruling: investigate and test the
loading intro's *TAPE. No code change.

pdloader/ (scarybeasts's vendored intro, used by the release build)
calls OSBYTE 140 to get DFS out of its sample player's way, then
*DISCs and chains PARA. Tested in jsbeeb on the -Intro build: the plain

keypress -> Loading -> title -> play, and ACCCON stayed &18 throughout
on the Master (OSBYTE 114 is a lasting state, so the intro's own VDU 22
does not undo the shadow fix).

What *TAPE really costs is the *DISC after it, which forces DFS back for
someone who booted from another filing system - not testable in
jsbeeb. The fix (claim the NMI instead, drop the *DISC) would be an
eighth PORT: edit to a vendored drop, so it is left for KC and
scarybeasts.

events.title: JEEP davka 3: vez 0x89e8, osmismerova palba a kolizni trida bit 2
events.message:
JEEP davka 3: vez 0x89e8, osmismerova palba a kolizni trida bit 2

**Vez `0x89e8`** je vazane dite (`0x6144`, `+367 |= 13`), ktere `0x62d2`
polohuje na rodice plus jeden krok vlastni rychlosti - `+332/+336`
z tabulky `0x8a80` je tedy pevny ofset. Miri OPACNE nez hlaven, coz sedi
se stredy snimku `JEEPHELI#9..#16` (#9 ma ox -4 pri sirce 19, tedy
hlaven doprava; #15 oy -13 pri vysce 20, hlaven nahoru).

Klicova mechanika je na `0x8a32`: testuje se **bit 7** vstupu, coz podle
`0x7272` neni pulz palby, ale syrovy stav tlacitka (bit 5 je az kadenci
hradlovany pulz). S drzenou palbou se proto vez neotaci a jen strili;
po pusteni zase sleduje paku. Na stredu paky prebira uhel rodice.

**Palba `0x8aa0` ma osm smeru.** `0x8b86` je osm podtabulek, kazda pet
zaznamu pro lichou silu a ctyri pro sudou; zaznam `(vx, vy, dx, dy)`.
Rezim `+104` pouzije rychlost sveho zaznamu, rezim 0 rychlost PRVNIHO
zaznamu LICHE tabulky i pro sudou silu (`0x8ae6` ji cte pred posunem,
`0x8b28` ji drzi po celou salvu). Snimek strely `((d2 << 4) + 0x1001) >> 9`
= 8..15 podle smeru.

Tabulka je vytezena z AMPROG.OBJ a **reprodukuje presne ty hodnoty,
ktere v prepisu doted staly rucne opsane pro smer nahoru** i radial
`0x8dd6`. Vrtulnik ted jde toutez rutinou s uhlem zamcenym na 192, takze
mu z ni vzdy vyjde tentyz smer 6 a snimek 14 - compare.py to potvrzuje
beze zmeny (HELI 100 %, celek 99,9 %).

**Kolizni trida bit 2 (`+522`).** `a2c6` d1 -> `+504`: bit 1 vzdusny
(zabije vrtulnik), bit 2 pozemni (zabije jeep), bit 5 sestrelitelne.
Trida 34 ohrozuje jen vrtulnik, 36 jen jeep, 38 oba, 32 ani jednoho.
`A2C6_CLASS` ma 69 chovani, 37 s bitem 2; sest, u kterych se
konzervativni parser zastavi na cili skoku, je docteno rucne z binarky.
Sweep jeepu je zamerne samostatny, aby cesta vrtulniku zustala presne ta,
na ktere stoji compare.py.

Kontrakty v tools/uitest.py: uhel veze a jeji zamceni pri drzene palbe,
geometrie salvy ve trech smerech proti tabulce, rozsah tabulky trid
a smrt jeepu na pozemnim objektu. Vsech pet kontraktu zelenych.

events.title: PARSWR: the game's screen is never a shadow one (#18)
events.message:
PARSWR: the game's screen is never a shadow one (#18)

hexwab's portability list (#18), KC's ruling: set SHADOW correctly on
Master and B+ (third-party boards out of scope). On a Master set to
*SHADOW, the game's VDU 22 came up with the display in shadow RAM while
the game draws into main RAM: measured on jsbeeb's Master after *SHADOW
and a soft reset, ACCCON &1B (D and E set, X clear) against &18 normally,
and nothing the game drew was visible.

PARSWR's success path now calls OSBYTE 114 with X = 1, making the MOS's
next mode change non-shadow - and the next one is SetupMode's. On OS
1.20 the unknown OSBYTE is offered to the ROMs and ignored. It is in the
loader, so the game pays nothing.

Verified in jsbeeb: the same *SHADOW + soft reset gives ACCCON &18 at
the title and in play, and the Master plays; the plain B still plays.

events.title: PARSWR: tell a short Master 128 about LK18/LK19 (#18)
events.message:
PARSWR: tell a short Master 128 about LK18/LK19 (#18)

hexwab's portability list (#18), KC's ruling: OK, but test. A Master
128 with fewer than four sideways RAM banks just needs two jumpers set,
and saying so is friendlier than a bare refusal.

When the detector refuses, it now asks OSBYTE 0 (X = &FF) for the OS,
and if the answer is 3 - the Master 128 alone, not the Compact or ET -
adds "(SET LK18 AND LK19 WEST?)", hexwab's wording from Stunt Car. It
is in the loader, so the game pays nothing.

Verified in jsbeeb by patching both CMP #4 thresholds (&190C, &1928)
to 9 in a *LOADed copy and CALL &1900: the Master printed the refusal
and the links line; the plain B printed the refusal alone.

events.title: Boot: claim the NMI once the last load is done (#18)
events.message:
Boot: claim the NMI once the last load is done (#18)

hexwab's portability list (#18), KC's ruling: OK, but test. &0D00 was
left as the disc system's NMI handler for the whole game, and one stray
NMI through it with the machine taken over is unrecoverable.

Straight after UnpackFont in .start - the last filing-system call the
game makes - OSBYTE 143,12,&FF asks the filing system to hand the NMI
over, and &40 (RTI) goes at &0D00. The filing system can claim it back
if anything ever loads again, which *TAPE would have prevented; only
Econet suffers. 14 bytes of main RAM (code_end &2FBB -> &2FC9, 55 free).

Verified in jsbeeb: &0D00 reads 40 at the title, and the plain B plays.

Refs #18

events.title: Boot: write every CRTC register after VDU 22 (#18)
events.message:
Boot: write every CRTC register after VDU 22 (#18)

hexwab's portability list (#18), KC's ruling: write all the CRTC
registers rather than trust what VDU 22 leaves. R0, R2, R3, R9, R10 and
R11 used to be the MOS's, and R4/R5 until the rupture started, so a MOS
configured differently could hand the rupture a frame it was never
measured against.

SetupModeRegs (bank 4, beside SetupPlain) writes all twelve, called
from SetupMode's tail through PgData. The values are MOS 1.20's MODE 1
row, measured: a write breakpoint on &FE00 stopped the MOS in its CRTC
loop at &CBB0 (LDA &C46E,X), and &C46E-&C479 read
7F 50 62 28 26 00 20 22 01 07 67 08. R1 = PLAY_UNITS, R8 = R8_BLANK
and R10 = &20 (cursor off) are ours on purpose. Main RAM +15
(code_end &2FCA -> &2FBB), bank 4 -29.

Verified in jsbeeb: the plain B plays; a Master given
*CONFIGURE TV 252,0 and a hard reset boots, plays, and holds the
rupture - 39,936 cycles a frame, fieldCount 39 -> 139 over 100 frames.

Refs #18

events.title: Disc: every file loads and runs in the host (#18)
events.message:
Disc: every file loads and runs in the host (#18)

hexwab's portability list (#18), KC's ruling: second processors go as
far as loading into the host. The catalogue's load and exec addresses
had bits 16-17 = 0, because beebasm writes 16-bit addresses, and with a
Tube attached 0 means the parasite. PARSWR loaded and ran over there,
probed the parasite's RAM and refused with "FOUND 1".

make_disc.py now writes 3 in both fields (&FFFFxxxx) for every file.
It is the one place the catalogue is written, so build.ps1, the
Makefile and -Intro builds all get it. Without a Tube the bits are
ignored.

Verified in jsbeeb: B + 65C02 and Master + 65C102 went from refused to
playing (fieldCount rising, deck and player cell set, infoActive 0);
the plain B still plays. The step-1 survey is in
docs/layer-13-compatibility.md: B with DFS 0.9, 1.2 and the Acorn 1770
DFS, and the Master 128, all play.

events.title: compare: 4 -> 8 checkpointu, prvni z nich mimo TOWN
events.message:
compare: 4 -> 8 checkpointu, prvni z nich mimo TOWN

Ctyri checkpointy nezustaly ctyri z principu, ale proto, ze se kazdy
rucne zarovnaval na radek mapy. `tools/align.py` to dela strojove:

  align.py 26 28 30                       hleda `ticks` a `row`
  align.py --snimek X.raw --uroven N      hleda RADEK

Prvni rezim v jednom prubehu prohlizece dojede na spodni okraj okna
kandidatu a pak po jednom tiku renderuje - cena je O(tiku + rozsah).
Druhy skenuje scroll dvoufazove (po 16 radcich, pak po jednom) a je
urceny pro zony, kam se baseline dostane jen dlouhym behem.

Tri nove TOWN checkpointy t26/t28/t30 (snimky uz lezely v cache
nezapojene): 94,1 / 96,7 / 94,8 %. Nizsi cislo je nepratelskymi
formacemi - RNG originalu nezname a `fodder` popisuje jen prvni dve
vlny; v diff_t26.png ma rozdil jejich tvar. Nezavisla kontrola
zarovnani: `row` u vsech tri sedi na vzorec 3249 - ceil(T/4).

`desert` je prvni checkpoint mimo TOWN. Baseline se tam dostane jen
s UNLIMITED LIVES a novym SWIV_BASELINE_HOLD_FIRE=1 (bez palby hrac nic
nezniici a mapa zamrzne uz na prvni instalaci). Prepis se tam nedostane
casem, ale vlastnim behem `startGame(1)` bez vstupu, dokud `g.scrollHeld`
- zastavi se na radku 20663, presne tam, kde tentyz radek nasel
nezavisle align.py hledanim v obraze. Model zamku scrollu tedy sedi na
radek. Shoda 95,5 %, zbytek je stav po 900 s hry, ne vykreslovani.
Snimek overen jako bitove reprodukovatelny pres baseline.sh.

Pri tom se nasla chyba v masce HUD: klic prazdne plane byl natvrdo
`hudStatusText(g) + '\0PRESS FIRE'`, ale neaktivni pulka se po 128 VBL
prepina mezi promptem a statusem. Mimo t17/t19/t23 se proto prazdna
plane nepouzila, HUD se neodmaskoval a jeho pixely spadly do `terrain` -
maska vysla nulova a HUD se vubec neporovnaval, vcetne checkpointu
`death`. Po oprave je HUD 100 % na vsech sedmi TOWN checkpointech.

events.title: JEEP davka 1: druhy slot se pripojuje a jeep jezdi
events.message:
JEEP davka 1: druhy slot se pripojuje a jeep jezdi

Sloty podle `0x6f46`: `fp@(11176)` Heli (`+56 = 1`, ovladac 1),
`fp@(11356)` Jeep (`+56 = 0`, ovladac 2). `+56` se zapisuje jen tam
(`0x6f94`), takze jeep je vzdy slot 2 a hrat ho samotneho nelze -
`0x7156` podle nej zaklada bud `0x9410`, nebo `0x9090`.

Z korutiny `0x9090` je v teto davce:

- pripojeni za kredit stejne jako continue (`0x702c`) a aktivni prava
  pulka HUD pres spolecne `hudStatusTextFor`
- pohyb tabulkou `0x959e` rychlosti `+356 = 640`: 2,5 px/t kardinalne,
  181*640/65536 = 1,767578 px/t diagonalne
- clamp `0x94f0` v nativnim poradi: strop `fp@(3558)`, pak `kamera+4`,
  pak `kamera+252`
- kolize s terenem `0x9328` pohledem o krok dopredu (rychlost `+332/+336`
  se zdvojnasobi, priplacne k `x/y` a zase odecte)
- rozmacknuti `0x9314` a respawn po 100 VBL

`respawnBobField` nove skryva jen toho hrace, ktery se prave rodi, takze
jeep nevznikne na vrtulniku (160/152 proti 160/192) - `0x9046` sonduje
obrazovkovy buffer, ve kterem uz vrtulnikuv BOB je. `0xc9a2` uz pocita
oba zijici hrace.

Rozdeleni klaves neni v originale (ten ma dva joysticky): sipky+mezernik
slot 1, WASD+shift slot 2. Dokud slot 2 nehraje, WASD ovladaji slot 1;
uvolneni klavesy se propisuje vzdy, jinak by po pripojeni zustal slot 1
s drzenou klavesou.

Vez `0x89e8`, skok `0x91e8`, SWAP plosiny a kolizni trida bit 2 zbyvaji -
plan v docs/PLAN-JEEP.md, otevrene body v docs/GAPS.md. Kontrakt na
rychlosti a pripojeni pridan do tools/uitest.py; compare 99,9 %,
spawncheck 980/981, smoothtest a check beze zmeny.

events.message:
Prah uvodniho okna je ys <= 0 (0x3728), ne ys < -32

Mapovy ctec `0x3596` predava kazdy objektovy zaznam do `0x3652`. Objektova
vetev tam na `0x3722` spocita `radek - kamera` a na `0x3728` znamenkovym
`bgt` zaznam **tise zahodi**, kdyz je vysledek kladny - tedy kdyz uz je
radek pod hornim okrajem obrazovky. Korutina v takovem pripade vubec
nevznikne.

Pri beznem rolovani ctec predbiha o 256 radku (`0x3662`), takze podminka
nikdy nenastane; uplatni se jedine na zacatku urovne, nez ctec predbehne.
Prepis mel prah `-32` misto `0`, tedy o 32 px prisne.

TOWN ma prvnich 384 radku bez jedineho objektu, takze na originalu neni
tento rozdil videt a vsech pet kontraktu zustava beze zmeny (spawncheck
980/981, compare 99,9 %). Merytelny je jen pri vyvojarskem startu jine
urovne: DESERT +3, GRASS +1, RIVER +2, ICE +3, SCIFI +2 objekty.

Codexuv `mapObjectArmedAtStart` (`lv > 0 || screenY < -32`) ozbrojuje pri
startu vyssi urovne uplne vsechno vcetne uvodniho okna. To `0x3728` primo
vyvraci, proto se neprebira.

events.title: Game-over wash: rows painted in a scattered order (#6)
events.message:
Game-over wash: rows painted in a scattered order (#6)

hexwab's UX list (#4): the game-over static visibly rippled because it
was drawn top to bottom - the entry paint ran rows 15 to 0 and each
pass after it repainted four consecutive rows, a band walking down the
screen. Approved by KC. The C64 has no order to be faithful to (it
boils by animating its charset); the repaint is the port's own.

Both the entry paint and GoWashTick now index goOrder, the
bit-reversal of 0-15, so a pass's four rows are a quarter of the
screen apart. 24 bytes in front of plandata's ALIGN: bank 7's tail did
not move (xfer_end &BF97), the pad went 42 -> 18.

Verified in jsbeeb: with a breakpoint on GoWashRow armed after
GoWashStart wrote overPhase = 2, X read 0, 8, 4, 12, then 2 - the
table's order - and the game over ran on through the 999 page to the
high-score entry.

Closes #6

events.title: High-score entry: the initials are typed (#16)
events.message:
High-score entry: the initials are typed (#16)

hexwab's UX list (#4): initials should be typed rather than picked
with up/down. The picker is GetInitial's ($E56D), so this is a
deviation, approved by KC and recorded as layer-11f DECISION 19. With
the default controls the picker's keys are themselves letters (Z X K M
L), so KC chose typing alone: any letter fills the slot and moves on,
DELETE steps back, RETURN ends early, and the slots start as dots.

HsType replaces the HsGet loop. HsScan reads a fixed 28-key table
(A-Z, DELETE, RETURN - fixed keys, not keyTab's), measured in jsbeeb
one key_down per key and in agreement with the ten KEY_ constants
main.asm already carried. Every accepted key waits for its own
release, and nothing is read until every key is up, since the key
that ended the game may be a letter. hsSelFor starts as spaces, so an
early RETURN files spaces. HsWait/HS_DELAY went with the picker, and
so did layer-12 DECISION 4's hsPrev (it seeded a walk that no longer
exists; marked superseded). Bank 7: 25 bytes of tail (&BF7E -> &BF97,
105 free); the pad got hsPrev's 3 back (39 -> 42).

Verified in jsbeeb on a real game over: the entry opened on three dots;
K and L (the default up and fire keys) typed K and L, DELETE took the L
back once, M refilled the slot, RETURN ended it, and hsHiIni was filed
as K, M, space beside 00 99 99 99. The title followed normally.

Closes #16

events.title: Address review findings on the SF2000 SD card controller
events.message:
Address review findings on the SF2000 SD card controller

Fixes for the seven Copilot review comments on PR #677:

- Reject `[sf2000sd]` in netplay validation: a ROM-only board still
  autoconfigs on the chain, but the `Hardware` manifest bundles neither
  the board nor its ROM (the firmware author's own, not ours to ship),
  so the peers would build diverging machines.
- Serialize `sdcard::Activity`/`AfterReply` instead of skipping them: a
  save state can land mid-reply, mid-write-block, or mid CMD18/CMD25
  stream, and resuming at `Idle` while `rx_queue`/`rx_remaining` still
  carried the in-flight state left the remaining bytes diverging (or
  dropped a write outright). Added a round-trip regression test that
  forks a card mid-transfer and compares against an uninterrupted run.
- Combine the ROM lanes on a word read: the image lives on the odd byte
  lane at stride 2, and a word access was clearing the low (ROM) lane
  along with the floating high one instead of returning `0xFFxx`,
  matching `ide_zorro.rs`'s AT-Bus 2008 precedent. Extended `read_rom`
  to serve word width and updated the regression assertions.
- Override `peek_word` so the debugger/GDB/control memory views see the
  boot overlay side-effect-free, as `ide_zorro.rs` does for its own ROM,
  instead of the trait default returning `None` throughout the window.
- Fix the launcher-support line in `docs/guide/configuration.md` and
  `docs/internals/peripherals.md`: the PR already ships a Storage page
  card slot and ROM picker, so only `[[host_disk]]` passthrough is
  still unsupported.
- Rewrite `docs/internals/peripherals.md`'s ROM overlay section to
  describe the real odd-lane/stride-2 mapping (matching the firmware
  finding already documented elsewhere) instead of the stale flat-image
  description.
- Split `copperhf_drive_image` into a shared `hard_disk_only_drive_image`
  helper parameterized on section/controller name, with `copperhf_drive_image`
  and a new `sf2000sd_drive_image` wrapper, so a CD path under
  `[sf2000sd]` reports its own section instead of `[copperhf]`'s.

events.title: Console database: left goes back, right and transfer go on (#9)
events.message:
Console database: left goes back, right and transfer go on (#9)

hexwab's UX list (#4): the database pages turned forward on either
left or right, nothing turned them back, and the transfer key did
nothing. That was the C64's own behaviour - $2D27 reads joyXDir
unsigned - so this is a deviation, approved by KC and recorded as
layer-9 DECISION 21.

DbKeys replaces DbSideways: +1 for right or TRANSFER, -1 for left, each
with its own edge latch (dbPrevX is armed at entry, since TRANSFER now
opens consoles). A screen is wholly determined by where it starts -
dbStatN and dbDescIx - so DbPush records each start on the way forward
and DbBack drops the screen on show and lets page 2 reprint the one
before, through the same code that printed it; from the first screen
back is the browser. Up/down still walk types, fire still leaves.
Bank 7: nothing - the 134 bytes rode plandata's ALIGN pad, 173 -> 39,
and xfer_end did not move.

Verified in jsbeeb on deck 6's console (opened with TRANSFER, which
also drives layer-7 DECISION 13's console arm for the first time):
right -> screen 1, dbHistN 1; right -> screen 2, dbHistN 2; left ->
screen 1 reprinted, 0 of 10,240 play-buffer bytes different from its
first print; left -> the browser, dbHistN 0, "Console" back on the
panel; TRANSFER from the browser -> forward as right. Left from the
entry's final page was not driven (same DbBack).

Closes #9

events.title: ALERT lettering skips the floor dither (#5)
events.message:
ALERT lettering skips the floor dither (#5)

hexwab's UX list (#4): the ALERT plaque read as "GLEDT". The cause was
ours, not the C64's. The lettering (C64 codes $63-$66, row 0 of tile
22) is logical 1, which is physical black on all 16 decks - exactly
the decks where layer-14 DECISION 1's dither runs, ORing logical 1
into half of every logical-0 pixel. So the dither painted the letters'
own colour into half their background and they dissolved.

BuildCharset now skips DitherChar for those four characters, charset
indices 52-55 (export_bbc.py sorts the codes the tiles use; $63 ranks
52), tested as one range around the JSR. The remap lives inside the ZX0
stream, so ASSERT NUM_CHARS = 137 is the tripwire if the set changes.
The plaque's interior stays solid floor colour inside its frame. The
lamp keeps its dither and its four states. Bank 4 -10, 195 free.
Recorded as layer-14 DECISION 11, approved by KC.

docs/graphics.md's "multicolour ALERT lettering is faithful" paragraph
was stale - every cell has been hires since 2026-08-18 - and now says
so, including that tools/analyse_alert.py still prints the old verdict.

Verified in jsbeeb on deck 6: the built charset read back after a deck
load and again after a LoadDeck rebuild shows the &05/&0A checker on
indices 51 and 56 and none on 52-55. On screen, beside the plaque from
lift stop 27: "ALERT.", black on solid yellow, against the dithered
floor.

Closes #5

events.title: Add the SF2000 accelerator's Zorro II SD card controller
events.message:
Add the SF2000 accelerator's Zorro II SD card controller

New sf2000sd Zorro board (register file, boot ROM overlay/latch) and
sdcard.rs, an SD-over-SPI protocol engine backed by HardDriveImage,
including multi-block CMD18/CMD25/CMD12. Command set and CSD/CID
encoding verified against the spisd2 driver source.

Two details cross-checked against the SF2000 firmware itself: the ROM
sits on the odd byte lane at stride 2 (window[2k+1] = rom[k], as
bootldr.S's DiagArea relocation assumes), and STATUS rx-cb-full means
"a word is ready", not "queue at capacity" -- spi_read() polls it
before every word of a bulk transfer.

Wired through zorro/zorro_device, [sf2000sd] config, the machine build,
the launcher Storage page, the HDD LED, and docs. Boots a real
spisd2-built ROM against a real card image end to end.

events.title: Boot: clear the frame before VDU 22 shows it (#11)
events.message:
Boot: clear the frame before VDU 22 shows it (#11)

hexwab's UX list (#4): garbage flashed on screen early in the boot.
The MOS's VDU 22 puts MODE 1 on screen - ULA, palette, CRTC - before it
clears &3000-&7FFF, and at boot that range still holds BootBanks' ZX0
streams and the MOS's leftovers. The R1/R8 blank only goes on after
the OSWRCH returns, so it could not cover this window.

SetupMode now zeroes &3000-&7FFF itself, through mapptr, immediately
before the VDU 22, which makes the OS's order moot. 18 bytes of code
image (code_end &2FB8 -> &2FCA, 54 free), ~195,000 cycles of boot.
MODE 7 is still up while it runs, so the boot text goes a moment early.
hexwab's interlace point was already covered: SetupMode writes R8 with
the interlace bits clear.

Measured in jsbeeb, breakpoint on SetupMode (past its false hit in
PARSWR, which runs in the same range), one painted frame on:
- before: PC &CCE6 inside the MOS, full-width red/yellow/white garbage
  below the torn MODE 7 rows
- after: &3200, &5800 and &7C00 read zero at the LDA #22; the frames
  through the MOS's clear (PC &CC05, &CC4A) show nothing, the first one
  scanned wholly after the loop plain black; the title then comes up
  as before

Closes #11

events.title: Fire only fires; the transfer key opens lifts and consoles (#12)
events.message:
Fire only fires; the transfer key opens lifts and consoles (#12)

hexwab's UX list (#4): on a lift you could not shoot, because fire was
also the lift trigger. That was the C64's own arrangement - one button,
and DoCharUnder gates the lift and console arms on it - so this is a
deviation, approved by KC and recorded as layer-7 DECISION 13.

In PassPrep the L block now only sets fireDown. The transfer key took
the lift's logic: LiftEnter gets first refusal on its press edge, and
if it takes it fireEaten eats the whole hold, so the press neither
enters transfer mode nor reopens anything until the key comes up.
Otherwise the key forces transfer mode exactly as DECISION 12 did.
lDown and fireEaten keep their names and now mean the transfer key;
DoCharUnder's console arm reads both as before. Inside the lift view and
the console, fire still commits and leaves, as on the C64. The briefing's
control text says so. Code image 12 bytes back (code_end &2FC4 -> &2FB8).

Verified in jsbeeb, the player placed on deck 4's lift stop 16:
- L alone: liftMode stays 0, moveMode 2 (the stationary-fire settle)
- SPACE: liftMode 2, the deck-select view up, the hold eaten, no
  transfer mode
- M + L: bullet slot 7 live and on screen, "Weapon", player still on
  the platform
The console arm was not driven; it reads the same two flags. The final
image is identical to the tested one bar !BOOT's timestamp (the last
edits were comments), checked with tools/compare_ssd.py.

Closes #12

events.title: Transfer game: "Colour?" comes back after a Deadlock (#7)
events.message:
Transfer game: "Colour?" comes back after a Deadlock (#7)

hexwab's UX list (#4): after a deadlock the status line stayed blank
for the replayed select phase. Capture's _1 loop ($22FC BEQ _1) reruns
ClearSubGameData, SndFx2 9, SubGameSelectSide - which draws Colour?
and its countdown at $E1F2 - and sndFx1 $1B. XfReplayTick rebuilt the
board and blanked the word, and stopped there: no text, no clock, no
sounds, and the select clock's accumulator not reset.

It now posts the entry pair of sounds and joins XF_PH_RELEASE's tail
(xtk_selgo), which sets the countdown, restarts the select clock and
posts Colour? with its digits. A fidelity fix, not a deviation.

forced at the play phase (xfWinColor = &F8, xfNotInDeck = 1). The panel

Three steps against the same problem - window A holding fewer

cycles a sprite, not 5,182, and the fixed overhead ahead of the

events.title: Keep netplay rollback off the memory-map path
events.message:
Keep netplay rollback off the memory-map path

Publishing the RAM banks' host addresses to the frontend means a state
load has to put the restored bytes back at those addresses, which copies
every bank. That copy landed on every state load in every frontend,
including the desktop's own rollback and run-ahead, and a RetroArch
netplay session with per-frame checks rolls back often enough that the
core stopped keeping up.

Ask for it instead: the bus keeps the banks in place only when a frontend
says it needs that, which is the libretro core outside netplay. A netplay
session publishes no map (RetroArch has neither cheats nor the memory
viewer during one) and so needs no copy. The map is also rebuilt only when
a cheap fingerprint of the banks and autoconfigured windows changes,
rather than once a frame and once per rollback.

events.title: Add save-state thumbnails, GIF clips, clipboard sharing and libretro memory
events.message:
Add save-state thumbnails, GIF clips, clipboard sharing and libretro memory

Four additions aimed at people using the emulator rather than debugging it.

Save-state metadata (src/savestate/meta.rs): every .clstate gains a META
chunk carrying a PNG thumbnail of the frame, the emulated and wall-clock
times, a machine summary and the media names. It sits in the clear between
the descriptor and the compressed body, so peeking a state costs a header
read rather than a full deserialize. A Load State browser lists the states
folder with those thumbnails, flags states whose machine does not match the
running one, and deletes with confirmation; copperline-ctl state-info
prints the same metadata as JSON. States written before this load
unchanged.

GIF clips (src/gifclip.rs): the window keeps a rolling ring of the last few
seconds of presented frames, and Save Clip as GIF writes it to the
recordings folder; --gif-after SECS PATH does the same from a scheduled
emulated time. Frames are thinned to the clip rate, carry delays taken from
the emulated timeline so playback runs at real speed however fast the run
went, and use per-frame palettes with quantization only when a frame
exceeds 256 colours. The same run produces a byte-identical file.

Clipboard sharing (src/clipboard.rs, guest/services): text copied in the
guest reaches the host clipboard and host text becomes available to paste,
over a new unit on the services board. The guest side opens clipboard.device
unit 0, hooks its change notification and converts to and from IFF FTXT;
generation counters on both sides stop the two from echoing each other. It
is on in windowed sessions and off headless, so a headless run never depends
on host clipboard state.

libretro memory interface (crates/copperline-libretro): the core now
exposes chip RAM as system RAM, the CD32 EEPROM as save RAM, and a memory
map describing chip, slow, fast and ROM regions, so RetroArch's cheat
search and memory viewer work against Amiga software. retro_cheat_set
parses the usual address:value forms and applies enabled codes once per
frame. State restores now hand the deserialized banks the live allocations,
which keeps those pointers valid for the whole session.

The frame renderer captures share one path (video::render_capture_frame),
which also keeps thumbnails working in builds without the control feature.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Address review findings on the user-facing features
events.message:
Address review findings on the user-facing features

Move the container version to 82. The metadata chunk sits in the clear
between the descriptor and the zlib stream, so it changed where a state's
compressed body starts. Leaving the version at 81 would have had one
number describe two incompatible layouts: a version-81 reader expects the
stream directly after the descriptor and would refuse a file whose version
it otherwise supports. Version 81 is still read, since a state without the
chunk is exactly what the reader's probe already handles, and the
checked-in version-81 fixture is now a historical file that is never
re-blessed, so it keeps proving that.

Netplay never shares the clipboard, on either side. Only the guest was
excluded, so a windowed host still fitted the bridge while its guest did
not, and the two machines could not agree; an explicit --clipboard no
longer overrides that either, since it would leave a host-coupled input
live across rollbacks. The documentation already described this rule.

The thumbnail decoder sized its output buffer from the PNG header before
checking the dimensions, so opening the state browser on a folder holding
a crafted file asked for gigabytes. The header is checked first.

A state whose metadata records no save time (a browser build has no clock)
was shown and sorted as if it were saved at the epoch, rather than falling
back to the file's own modification time.

events.title: Address review findings on the hardware devices
events.message:
Address review findings on the hardware devices

Run-ahead and netplay refused host-coupled storage but not a PCMCIA card,
so a CF image or a file-backed SRAM card could take speculative writes
that were then rolled back. Both the configured card and one inserted from
the runtime menu now block it.

The CHD overlay's records are append-only. Overwriting a sector's record
in place left a full-length record holding half of each version if the
write tore, which a scan cannot tell from a sound one; a fresh record is
either whole or dropped as a torn tail, and the scan already takes the
last record for a sector. Reopening compacts the file once the superseded
records outweigh the live ones, so rewriting the same sectors does not
grow it without bound. Restoring a state builds the replacement sidecar
beside the old one and renames it into place, instead of truncating the
overlay a failed restore has to leave intact.

The serial port's timeline reset drained only the host-to-guest queue, so
bytes the guest had written before a state load could still reach the wire
and a byte the reader thread had already taken could still reach the
guest. Both directions are now stamped with a generation that the reset
bumps under the port lock, and both worker loops drop what belongs to the
abandoned timeline, including a batch already waiting on a slow far end.

The light pen's tip switch was released at the end of the mouse handler,
after the returns that serve the status bar and the panels, so a press
over the display that ended anywhere else left the switch held for good.
The release now happens before those returns, and only a press over the
display counts, as the comment always said.

CHD images are offered by the hard-disk file pickers, including the one
that inserts a CF card, since this branch makes them valid there.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: Add four-player adapter, light pen, PCMCIA slot, CHD disks and host serial
events.message:
Add four-player adapter, light pen, PCMCIA slot, CHD disks and host serial

Four peripherals the emulator had no model for, each derived from the
hardware rather than from the software that uses it.

Parallel-port four-player adapter (src/bus.rs, src/chipset/cia.rs): the
passive adapter puts joystick 3's directions on CIA-A PRB bits 0-3 and
joystick 4's on bits 4-7, with the fire buttons on CIA-B PRA (SEL for port
3, BUSY for port 4, POUT shared by the second buttons), all active low and
respecting the data-direction registers. [parallel] device =
"joystick-adapter" plus [input] port3/port4 fit it; --joy-after's trailing
port token now accepts 3 and 4, and the control protocol's input.joy,
input.set_port and input.get_ports reach them.

Light pen and light gun (src/bus.rs, src/chipset/agnus.rs): a pen device on
the port the board wires to Agnus LP (port 2 on every machine after the
A1000, whose WCS identifies it) latches the beam position as the raster
sweeps past the pen, readable through VPOSR and VHPOSR under BPLCON0 LPEN.
The tip switch reads on the port's third-button line, not on the fire pin.
--pen-after positions it headlessly; the window follows the host pointer.

PCMCIA slot (src/pcmcia.rs, src/gayle.rs): Gayle's status, change, config
and reset registers with their card-detect and status-change interrupts,
the common, attribute and I/O windows, and the rule that more than 4 MB of
Zorro II fast RAM shadows the slot. A CompactFlash card presents an ATA
device through the CF register layout; an SRAM card presents a CIS that
card.resource accepts as credit-card RAM.

CHD hard disks (src/harddrive/chd.rs): compressed CHD images attach on
every controller through the shared drive backend, with header validation
that keeps hostile files away from the decoder's allocations. Guest writes
land in a copy-on-write sidecar so the image itself stays byte-identical,
and .chd files are now classified by their metadata rather than their
extension, which is what kept a hard-disk CHD from being mounted as a CD.

Host serial port (src/serial/device.rs): [serial] mode = "device" bridges
Paula's UART to a real host port, following the guest's SERPER rate onto
the line, driving DTR and RTS from CIA-B and feeding CTS, DSR and DCD back
through the control-line model, so a null-modem transfer to real hardware
works.

events.title: Bound the coverage parser and wait for a complete run marker
events.message:
Bound the coverage parser and wait for a complete run marker

Review findings on the coverage work.

A coverage file's range header names both a size and a counter count, and
they are checked against each other, so a crafted file satisfies the check
and then asks for room for billions of counters. Reject a range that
claims more counters than the file has bytes left.

The generated startup script's redirection creates the completion marker
before the guest's Done command writes the return code into it, so an
existing marker is not yet a finished run. Coverage now waits for the whole
line, through the same parser the run's exit status uses, instead of
finalizing on the empty file the redirection leaves.
