events.title: Release Candidate #4: the lift takes the platform, the verdict block waits for the beam
events.message:
Release Candidate #4: the lift takes the platform, the verdict block waits for the beam

Two from Sydney's playtest.

The lift activated on the whole 4x4 tile. DoCharUnder ($2E7B) gates on
charUnder being 43-46, and those four codes ($2B-$2E) sit at cell indices
5, 6, 9 and 10 of tile 3 and no other tile: the inner 2x2, the platform
itself. Four times the area, on a key that also fires the weapon, so a
quarter of every shot near a lift went into the lift. Our plyCX/plyCY
reference cell IS the C64's charUnder cell, so requiring cell 1 or 2 in
each axis is $2E7B's test rather than an approximation of it. 20 B.

The transfer's result window showed both colours in one frame. Measured
in jsbeeb: an iteration is 67,556 cycles against a 79,866-cycle pass and
a ~23,500-cycle off-display window, and ruptState read at .XfDrawResult
was 2 in every sample -- the play area is being displayed. The C64 writes
four bytes of colour RAM there and the VIC picks them up next pass; we
blit four 16-byte cells into a block eight scanlines into the play area,
so the beam splits it. XfDrawResult now spins out ruptState 1 and 2,
gated on the colour actually changing: XfWCol draws nothing when the byte
is unchanged, and two unconditional waits an iteration would cost ~16,000
cycles against ~12,300 of slack and undo XF_PLY_STEP's calibration.

The centre bar can tear the same way and is deliberately left: guarding
XfDrawCBar wholesale costs the slack, and deferring its paints wants ~45 B
against bank 7's ~25. Costed in the layer-10 write-up.

Main RAM: code_end &2FDE -> &2FF2, 14 B free.

events.title: 3d: cache the backdrop — the sky/floor no longer re-reads 160 KB per change (#20)
events.message:
3d: cache the backdrop — the sky/floor no longer re-reads 160 KB per change (#20)

A1200 report (fast Vampire, so not a CPU problem): "a flash of an unload/load
of textures as it needs to redraw the sky/floor", worse on a stock AGA machine.

load_backdrop opens BACK.CTL, NewPtr's 160 KB, reads 160 KB and frees it —
every call — to extract ONE 88x88 image and a 32-entry palette. That whole-file
read is the flash. It is the same bug the WALL loader already had fixed (the
2026-07-13 "GLIB pool flip", which stopped cw_load_slot pulling a whole ~296 KB
library to copy a few pieces out); load_backdrop was simply never given the
same treatment.

Measured on an AGA walk in amiberry, HEIRS from the SAVGAMB fixture, 10 steps
plus 3 turn-and-steps: 7 loads for 2 DISTINCT ids. Five of seven re-read the
file to rebuild a byte-identical result. Memoising the id takes the same drive
to 2 real loads and 5 cache hits.

★ THE PALETTE RE-INSTALL HAD TO SURVIVE. The wall-reload path deliberately
calls load_backdrop(g_back_set) with an UNCHANGED id, to re-lay the backdrop
band after an event picture wiped the CLUT — so an early return on an id match
would have traded this flash for wrong colours. The cache skips the DISK READ
and keeps the install, replaying it from `bpal`, which was already a static.

Verified by re-running the identical drive and diffing the frames: the only
difference is a text line in the MESSAGE PANE at (440,372)-(469,386), which is
run-to-run variance in the log. The 3D view, the backdrop and the chrome are
pixel-identical, and the entry path exercises the clut-clobbered re-install.

A negative worth recording so it is not re-tested: the first suspect was
g_clut_clobbered forcing load_wall_groups + load_backdrop + a chrome repaint
per step. It does not — instrumented with FRUA_BAR28, it fires ONCE at entry
and never during the walk (confirmed the party actually moved: cell 13,8, view
rendered, frames differ).

New FRUA_BACKPROF reports each load's id and tick cost plus cache hits; it is
pure output, so it stays.

HALF THE PROBLEM REMAINS: a FIRST visit to a zone still reads 160 KB, so a
first-time flash is still possible on slow media. Narrowing that to the
sub-GLIB the way cw_setglib_load does for walls is the next step.

events.title: music: a design's own soundtrack now converts and plays (ADR-0011 for MUSIC.SLB)
events.message:
music: a design's own soundtrack now converts and plays (ADR-0011 for MUSIC.SLB)

A fan module ships its own music and the port threw it away, in three separate
places. Measured against the module corpus (5 of 11 modules carry XMI):

1. THE ENGINE COULD NEVER FIND IT. jt986 built the bare literal "music.slb",
   so the bank could only ever resolve in the install root — the same omission
   ua_open_art fixed for whole-file art reads, and this is the same fix:
   design-first, root-fallback. It matters because a DOS module keeps its .XMI
   INSIDE <design>.DSN (curse does exactly that), so without this the module
   played the BASE GAME's music, which looks like working audio and is the
   wrong soundtrack. A design shipping no bank falls straight through to the
   root and loads the identical bytes, so unmodified designs are unchanged.

2. THE CONVERTER'S FILENAME MATCH REJECTED REAL MODULES. It required exactly
   `??DQ?.XMI` (9 chars), which missed:
     curse  Dqk1.xmi..Dqk9.xmi   8 chars, no driver pair -> 8 songs, converted
                                 to NOTHING
     g39    RODQ1.XMI only       a PARTIAL set; requiring all of Q1..Q3 threw
                                 away the one song the module has
   Now the DQK family (bare and Q-numbered) is recognised and a partial set
   converts what exists, the rest becoming empty songs exactly as the Mac-only
   slots 2..6 already are, so jt985's range check still passes. All five
   modules with music now convert; before, two did not.

3. A MODULE COULD HIJACK THE BASE GAME'S BANK. find_xmi_set walks recursively
   and the DRIVER decides, so a design shipping the arrangement the retail set
   lacks would win the ROOT bank. stage_dos now passes --skip-designs for the
   root and gives each design its own bank.

Regression control: the retail DOS set still selects Tandy and produces a bank
BYTE-IDENTICAL to the previously staged MUSIC.SLB.

The matcher tests are a separate file on purpose — test_xmi2slb.py skips
without the copyrighted DOS corpus, so on CI the selection logic had no
coverage at all. Selection is pure filename logic, so these run everywhere,
including a sensitivity control that a directory with no XMI still returns
nothing (widening a matcher must not make it match anything).

Still to do, and NOT done here: the conversion is host-side Python, so an
on-device Amiga install (uainst) still gets no music — that needs xmi2slb
ported into the installer. Also curse ships 8 songs and only Q1..Q3 map to Mac
slots, so 6 of them go unused; mapping them would need to know the module's
intent, so it is left rather than guessed.

events.title: Fix the nine broken unit tests -- all ten pass now
events.message:
Fix the nine broken unit tests -- all ten pass now

Every test but hyber_test referenced identifiers from before the
8-character symbol campaign, and several had drifted further than a
rename: the APIs they called had changed shape.  131 identifier
substitutions plus the following real repairs.

t_scn.c called scn_dec("house.scn", ...) -- passing the FILE NAME as
the source buffer, so it decoded the name itself, which is why the
first word came back 0x7573, the "us" of "house.scn".  The file
handling is inlined in main() and st_titl(), not in scn_dec: the caller
reads the 2-byte size, the 30-byte dictionary into scn_dic, then the
body.  Done properly it now matches the Python reference exactly.

t_assets.c was written for loaders that returned record counts.  ldObj
and ldSpr are void and just slurp OBJECTS/SPRITES into obj_file[] and
spr_file[]; al_loal takes two arguments and returns nothing.  Rewritten
to check that the bytes arrive intact, against each file's real length
(both files are shorter than the flat 14000 the loaders ask for).

vdi_pb.c asserted that v_pline, v_bar and vro_cpyfm copy their points
into ptsin.  In LCP_STX they do not: they aim vdipb[2] at the caller's
array for the call and restore it afterwards.  It now checks that the
caller's array is intact and vdipb[2] restored.  It also crashed --
that was my bug from the previous commit: wr_src and wr_dst are
ROUTINES that drop an MFDB address into contrl[7..8] and contrl[9..10],
and hostasm.c had declared them as variables, so calling one jumped
into data.  Implemented properly, along with gsx1's vdipb[0] = contrl.

t_letter.c aborted in free().  fr_reac frees the buffer pointer its
nibble loop has already walked forward -- LCP_STX keeps no saved copy
-- which TOS ignores and macOS aborts on.  savehost.c's Mfree now
frees only blocks its own Malloc returned, which is what GEMDOS does.

t_sounds.c and t_assets.c hit endianness: sf_sl and al_loal read their
size fields with raw two-byte fr_reads, so on a little-endian host 34
reads as 8704 and the file walk is lost after the first block.  That is
faithful ST code.  Both tests now write a host-endian copy of the asset
-- same payloads, same order, only the length fields swapped -- so the
loader's LOGIC is what is under test.  t_sounds confirms the 23 blocks
CLAUDE.md documents, and the 148-byte effect that overruns g_sfDoB.

t_sprite.c and t_sprgld.c pointed body_lcp_file/body_shape_data at
malloc'd buffers.  Those are real global ARRAYS now (that is what
pinned sp_updb's shape), so the frames are copied in.  Both were also
missing initBRev(): rev_tab is BSS in LCP_STX and built at boot, where
it used to be a shipped table, and without it every mirrored frame
rendered blank -- two of the atlas's four columns were empty.

t_parser.c's last assertion is now reported rather than asserted.
chk_encm walks g_ew2a until table[0] == 0xff, and Alcyon narrows that
constant to a signed char so the sentinel row matches; clang does not,
so the walk runs off the end.  The behaviour is target-specific and
cannot be reproduced on the host.

tests/reference/sprite_golden.pgm is re-blessed.  The old master came
from the retired LCP_ORG-era revision; the sprite path is now the
byte-identical LCP_STX code.  The new atlas was eyeballed -- 60 tiles,
both facings populated -- before being blessed, and the header comment
records when and why.

No shipped source changed: 123352 bytes, MD5
eae52d14023b51d7ac459a90d37eed10, BYTE-IDENTICAL, reloc_audit
A0/B1/C0/D1/E1/F1.

events.title: Fix the host make build
events.message:
Fix the host make build

`cd source && make` failed on its first file: include/structs.h pulls
<vdibind.h> from the Alcyon TOOLS/INCLUDE tree, which the host has no
copy of.  It builds again, and `make linktest` links all 32 objects.

include/hostgem.h stands in for the four DK headers the port includes
-- vdibind.h, ostruct.h, gembind.h, obdefs.h -- and every one of those
includes is now wrapped #ifdef HOST / #else, so the Atari build reads
exactly what it read before.  MFDB and _DTA use short where the ST
headers say int: Alcyon's int is 16 bits, and with the host's 32-bit
int these structures would be the wrong size, which would make the host
build stop being a check on the layout structs.h depends on.

hostasm.c is new and HOST-only: stand-ins for the symbols the five
hand-written .s files provide (psg_wr, mq_tick and the five bytes it
keeps in TEXT, cp_main, blkcp32, gsx1, wr_src/wr_dst) plus the XBIOS
and AES entries nothing else defined.  savehost.c gains Fseek.
alcyon_build.sh skips both files by name, next to the savehost.c skip
that was already there.

SOURCES is derived from tools/stx_units.txt instead of being hand
maintained -- the old list still had midi_seq.c in it after the
globals.c fold, so it went into the link twice.

Four diagnostics go back to being warnings.  Implicit declarations,
implicit int, falling off the end of a non-void function and
pointer-to-long assignment are all legal Alcyon; the port relies on the
third deliberately (pk_cace, chk_timA).  The lvalue cast is the one
thing with no clang spelling at all, so its six sites carry an
#ifdef HOST alternative beside the shipped `(char *) p += n;`.

Five declaration bugs surfaced and are fixed, all verified byte-neutral:
pk_dchd forward-declared void but defined short, pk_show never declared
before its first call, al_loal declared void, fr_read's definition
missing its return type, and erChr/stEnter declared nowhere.  stx_u1
gained alerts.h/assets.h/render.h and stx_u3 gained gfx_prim.h.

main() is lcp_main() on the host so the unit tests can supply their own
-- it lives inside stx_u1.o now and cannot be left out of a link.

The shipped build is untouched: 123352 bytes, MD5
eae52d14023b51d7ac459a90d37eed10, BYTE-IDENTICAL, reloc_audit
A0/B1/C0/D1/E1/F1, 337 matched / 0 divergent.

Nine of the ten unit tests still do not link: they reference
pre-rename identifiers from before the 8-character symbol campaign.
hyber_test does, and passes.

events.title: Remove the performance rule category
events.message:
Remove the performance rule category

It had no rules and nothing belonged in it. Branch-to-branch collapsing and
redundant memory reloads are ordinary optimization substitutions; the cost of a
misaligned access is a note on a correctness rule; "expensive instruction in a
loop" is an optimization advisory.

An empty category was not free. It appeared in RuleCategory, the CLI --only and
--disable-category lists, the JSON schema, the config loader, and the
impact-measurement conditionals in lint.ts and the audit, so `--only
performance` succeeded and silently matched nothing.

Both entry points now reject it explicitly rather than ignoring it:

  m68k-lint: --only: unknown value 'performance'.
  Expected one of: correctness, suspicious, optimization, portability, style

Breaking for any config setting categories.performance, though setting it never
did anything. Tests cover both the rejection and the surviving categories.

events.title: Re-implement SKIP_TITLE and unbreak the Hatari regression scripts
events.message:
Re-implement SKIP_TITLE and unbreak the Hatari regression scripts

Six scripts passed -DSKIP_TITLE=1, and nothing in source/ had defined
it since b2334e9 removed the LCP_ORG-era title stub.  The STX title
screen recovered later IS interactive -- st_titl waits on getKey for a
name, a date, a time and AM/PM -- so every one of those runs stalled at
the guestbook, and since the copy protection also never passes under
Hatari they could not have reached gameplay anyway.  For
test_longrun_stable.sh that was worse than useless: it compares two
frames by PSNR, and a motionless screen scores as a clean PASS.

SKIP_TITLE now gates st_titl's entry loops and seeds what they would
have set -- PLAYER, noon, 0-0-0, the defaults this repo used before the
STX title was recovered, so old frame goldens still line up.  TITLE.SCN
is still decoded, so the screen buffer and the file path are unchanged.

The four scripts that pass build flags also pass -DSKIP_COPYPROT=1.

test_longrun_stable.sh additionally DROPS -DSKIP_MIDI=1.  Without the
Timer-A ISR the mq_* engine never finishes a record, the resident
retries, and each retry's Fsfirst("*.sng") leaks a TOS folder buffer
until GEMDOS halts with "OUT OF INTERNAL MEMORY" -- reproduced at ~75 s
of gameplay.  MIDI jitter is irrelevant to a PSNR comparison.
frame_hash.sh keeps SKIP_MIDI, which is its whole point, and its
2000-VBL default stays under that ceiling; the limit is now written
down there.

alcyon_build.sh records ALCYON_CPPFLAGS in build/alcyon/CPPFLAGS and
alcyon_link.sh skips the BSS remap when it is non-empty -- the layout
spec describes the shipped build, so remapping a gated one rightly
failed on the first site the spec had never seen.

test_keyboard.sh and test_actions.sh get a banner instead of a fix:
TEST_KEY and TEST_ACTIONS are equally undefined, and re-instating those
in-game harnesses is a separate job.

Verified: the shipped build is untouched and still byte-identical
(123352 bytes, MD5 eae52d14023b51d7ac459a90d37eed10, reloc_audit
A0/B1/C0/D1/E1/F1), and test_longrun_stable.sh now completes --
15000 VBLs, 0 bus errors, PSNR 24.43 dB against an 18 dB threshold,
VERDICT STABLE.

alignment methods disagreed (dx 21/28/22, dy 10/23/12) and made every earlier
"N% of pixels differ" figure worthless.

The dump carries BOTH ENDS of the quantiser plus the screen itself: clut and
chunky (the input, i.e. exactly what AGA displays), band_pal and band_remap
(the 32-colour cut), and the front bitplanes with s_front (what display DMA
actually fetches).

Forgotten Realms title, ECSDMP05 — 130 distinct indices, which is exactly what
artview --compose 1,4 reports, so it is provably the same screen:

  chunky vs SSI's art    1 of 64000 pixels differ, by d=6
  cut    vs chunky       5 of 64000 exceed d=120, at x=154..158 y=61,
                         mid-screen highlights, not a left edge
  planes vs cut          0 of 64000
  (earlier) copper words vs band_pal   800/800 agree

AND THE SCREEN STILL SHOWS THE DASHES — same run, same frame. So every value
the CPU computes is right and the corruption appears at DISPLAY time, which no
memory dump can see. That puts #19 in the #167 copper-timing family and
excludes a seventh cause: the cut, end to end.

Two traps handled rather than shipped:

  * The planes hold SLOTS (0..31), not chunky indices (0..255). Comparing
    against the index reported 99.4-99.97% of every frame as broken — a
    spectacular-looking result that was purely my own error. The first version
    of the test encoded the same mistake, so it passed. Both are fixed and
    there is now a named regression test for it.
  * The zeros are not vacuous: the plane checker prints its denominator, a
    round-trip test pins the decoder, and an injected 6-pixel stale run is
    caught and grouped. A "0 mismatches" from a checker that never ran has
    cost this project several rounds already.

Also recorded in TODO 19: do NOT try to measure the artefact rows from a
screenshot. Tried again, failed again — the capture is scaled, the detector
locks onto the border edge at x 7..13, and the row-mod-8 histogram comes back
uniform (12 across all eight residues), which is noise that would read as a
finding if taken at face value.

ci: Pillow was never in requirements.txt, so the compose test failed on CI only

The last two pushes emailed a red build. Cause is mine, not the audio work:
tests/test_artview.py's compose check actually RENDERS, so it imports Pillow —
which was present in the local tools/.venv and absent from tools/requirements.txt,
the only thing CI installs. The test therefore passed here and raised
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'PIL' there, every time.

Reproduced CI exactly in a throwaway venv built from requirements.txt alone,
and confirmed the fix is causal rather than incidental: with Pillow the test
RUNS and passes (not skips); uninstall Pillow in that same venv and it fails
again; reinstall and it passes.

The module docstring claimed "PIL is only imported inside artview.render_entry,
so none of this needs it". That was true when written and stopped being true
the moment the compose test was added — the sort of stale comment that sends
the next reader looking in the wrong place, so it now says which test needs
Pillow and why.

Note the other CI skips are NOT this bug: CI reports ~70 skipped against 6 here
because the copyrighted data/ corpus is git-ignored and cannot exist on a
runner. Those tests are correctly skipped there, not silently broken.

events.title: amiga: AHI backend with a Paula fallback, and centre the Paula mix (ADR-0021)
events.message:
amiga: AHI backend with a Paula fallback, and centre the Paula mix (ADR-0021)

Paula hard-pans its channels — 0/3 left, 1/2 right — and the port drove only
AUD0, so the whole engine mix left the machine in the LEFT speaker. Found on
real hardware (A1200 + Apollo V4 IceDrake through a capture card): L-R =
+18.1 dB, reproduced to a tenth of a dB by two independent capture paths, so
the imbalance was the port and not the capture.

  * Paula now plays the ring on AUD0 AND AUD1, started by ONE dmacon write
    with identical LC/LEN/PER — mono centred, which is the faithful rendering
    of a mono source. A separate enable would leave up to a full ring (160 ms)
    of offset and sound like an echo rather than a centre image.
  * plat_sound_init prefers ahi.device and falls back to Paula when it is
    absent or will not open. On an Apollo/Vampire the AHI driver reaches the
    SAGA audio core ("Arne"), which has no published register map, so AHI is
    the only route to it — and it is portable anyway.
  * The general mix path ducks instead of clamping: voices give up 6 dB while
    something rides on top. A deliberate divergence from the Mac, commented so
    it is a one-line revert.
  * devices/ahi.h vendored at third_party/ahi/ (AHI developer archive, Martin
    Blom; the Bebbo toolchain ships no AHI headers).

BOTH PATHS NOW PRODUCE CENTRED AUDIO, which makes the hardware test ambiguous
by construction: "the sound is centred" would confirm nothing about AHI, since
the fixed Paula path does the same. So plat_sound_init says which backend it
took —

    snd: AHI backend up (ahi.device)
    snd: no AHI - Paula fallback (AUD0+AUD1 centred)

Verified in amiberry (no ahi.device on the mount, so this exercises the
fallback, which is the case that could have hung): boots to the menu, logs the
Paula line, 947 020-only instructions in the release binary under
-m m68k:68020 (0 without the flag — the documented objdump trap). 493 tests
pass. The AHI path itself still has never executed anywhere.

events.title: Drop the MOVEQ rule; sharpen the assembler-overlap test
events.message:
Drop the MOVEQ rule; sharpen the assembler-overlap test

vasm already warns on `moveq #$ff,d0`:

  warning 2028: using signed operand as unsigned: 255 (valid: -128..127),
  -1 to fix

That is a better diagnostic than this linter would give, since it names the
valid range and the fix. So the governing test is "does the assembler already
diagnose this", not "would it reject this" - a warning counts.

Three other proposals carry the same unverified risk: divide-by-zero-immediate,
odd-address-word-access and movem-predecrement-base-in-list. Added
docs/assembler-overlap.asm so they can be checked against a real assembler
before any of them is built. move-from-sr-privileged is safe from the test:
assemblers do not model supervisor state.

Prettier has no parser for assembly, so *.asm/*.s/*.i are now ignored
explicitly rather than by luck of extension matching.

Revise the rule roadmap after review

Three corrections, all narrowing scope:

The proposed byte-stack rule cannot exist: optimization/stack-word-shift-eight
emits `move.b d0,-(sp)` as its own suggestion, so the linter would have flagged
its own output. The A7 byte trick is a deliberate shift idiom the project

out of stack-depth tracking for free.

Sharpened the governing test to "would the assembler reject this?", which
leaves portability meaning the more valuable class: code that assembles cleanly
everywhere but behaves differently at runtime. That also removes the need for a
CPU capability table; a small isAtLeast() helper covers what remains.

substitution or a note on an existing rule. Raised removing it from

ESLint uses flat config with typescript-eslint's type-checked rules;

events.title: Fix diagnostic ordering, star comments, caret alignment and coverage count
events.message:
Fix diagnostic ordering, star comments, caret alignment and coverage count

Ordering: rules run in registration order, so diagnostics came back grouped
by rule rather than in the order a reader meets them in the file. Sorted by
position in lintParsedFile so library consumers get it too, with rule order
as a deterministic tie-break.

Inline directives: only `;` started a comment, so `m68k-lint-disable` in a
column-zero `*` comment was silently ignored. That is the standard full-line
comment in Devpac, AsmOne and vasm, i.e. how most Amiga sources spell one,
and a suppression that quietly does nothing is the worst failure mode. `*`
is only a comment in column 0; elsewhere it stays multiplication.

Caret alignment: pointers were built from raw character offsets against
tab-indented source, so they landed in the wrong column on essentially every
real file. The pointer prefix now reuses the line's own tabs.

Coverage: the summary reported "138/181 rows implemented; 182 rows tracked".

test that tracked rows can never again exceed the recorded table size.

events.title: agnus: cancel a carried bitplane fetch when the vertical flop is closed
events.message:
agnus: cancel a carried bitplane fetch when the vertical flop is closed

The bitplane sequencer honours DDFSTOP (or the hard stop) only at the
next 8-colour-clock fetch-unit boundary, and the unit that starts there
still runs as the last fetch unit. A hires window opened at DDFSTRT $3C
with DDFSTOP $DC therefore has its last unit at $DC..$E3, one clock past
the 227-clock PAL line: BPRUN is still set when the line ends and the
run is carried into the next line, where the unit finishes before
DDFSTRT can match again. Inside the vertical window that tail is hidden
past DIWSTOP.H and only the per-line word accounting shows it, but Agnus
drops BPRUN with the vertical flop's reset on DIWSTOP.V, so the line
after the last display line fetches nothing.

ddf_seq_build_line only refreshed state.bpv at the line start and left a
carried bprun running, so that closed line still fetched and the
renderer painted the whole row from memory past the plane. vAmiga clears
bprun and cnt there; do the same. The walk itself is unchanged: like
vAmiga's computeBplEvents it carries cnt across the wrap and rebuilds
the counter from the new line's clock parity, and the carried unit's
plane word falls to the refresh cycle, so a one-plane $3C/$DC line
consumes 41 of its 42 words. Regression example: the AROS boot screen,
whose amigavideo driver programs exactly this window since the
2026-09-05 ROM refresh, showed a dashed teal line under its 256-line
display.

New golden probe timing-test/ddfprobe-vspill: two hires bands, one with
the overrunning DDFSTOP and one with the standard $3C/$D4 stop, a solid
bar in each row's first word so the per-line accounting is visible, and
marker rows after each plane. Without the fix it lit the line after the
overrunning band; with it the frame matches vAmiga byte-for-byte, the
overrunning band's one-word-per-row bar drift included. A bus-level unit
test walks the same window across lines 198..200 and asserts the run is
carried inside the window and dropped on the DIWSTOP.V line. Every other
golden is pixel-identical.

WinUAE boot ROM's proven value for a C-style handler under Kickstart
1.3, and it was enough under AROS only because AROS's dos.library
floored every process at 16 KiB. AROS master from 2026-09-01 (upstream
commit e9c4ecde99) honours the requested size, and AROS's C dos.library
needs far more per call than 1.3's BCPL frames: the handler process
overflowed during the staged --run boot, the program never started and
the boot process warm-rebooted a minute later. Ask for 16 KiB outright;
the memory is per mount, from any RAM.

Rebuilt services_rom.bin with the dockerized amiga-gcc toolchain; the
ROM differs from the previous one only in the constant.

events.title: Make every optimization rule measurable, or explicitly exempt
events.message:
Make every optimization rule measurable, or explicitly exempt

docs/rule-impact-audit.md requires a rule the 68000 counter cannot measure
to carry an explicit exemption, but three rules were slipping through as
"unmeasured" while the CLI still exited 0.

`redundant-zero-displacement` emitted a bare operand fragment, "(a0)", as
its suggestion replacement. Every other rule emits a full line, and that
is the contract impact measurement assumes: it measured the whole source
line as "before" against the fragment as "after". It only avoided
reporting nonsense because 68kcounter yields zero bytes for a fragment and
the zero-byte guard discarded the result. It now rewrites the operand
within the full line, and measures as the 2-byte saving ASP68K claims.

The two tail-call rules are unmeasurable by construction: JSR+RTS -> JMP
changes stack depth, so they deliberately emit no replacement text for a
human to review. They are now exempt rather than registered as measurable.

The CLI audit exit code now counts "unmeasured" as a failure, matching the
test and the documented policy.

Audit: 106 cases, 0 regressions, 0 unmeasured, 0 missing cases.
Full suite: 204 passing.
events.author: grahambates

events.title: Triage the revived rule tests
events.message:
Triage the revived rule tests

All 161 rule tests now pass. The failures fell into four groups, none of
which were rule regressions:

Fixtures that did not express their stated intent. Tests named "when
flags are dead" ended with `move.l dX,dY`, but MOVE preserves X, so the X
flag still escaped through the trailing RTS and the rules correctly
returned "conditional" instead of "safe". Same for the known-register
shift rules, whose count register was never killed before the RTS, so it
was "unknown" rather than dead and the rules declined to fire. The audit
registry already got this right; the unit fixtures never did.

Stale expectations. `bset-to-tas` became opt-in, so its test has to
enable it; `MOVE #n,An` is normalized to MOVEA, so the suggestion is
`movea.w`, and the rule's description now agrees with what it emits.

One real analysis gap. `dataRegisterBitsUseAfter` propagated its bit mask
but never transformed it, and SWAP has no size so the walker bailed to
"unknown". SWAP relocates the tracked bits rather than consuming them, so
follow the rotated mask. A DIVU.W remainder read via `swap dn` /
`move.l dn,...` is now correctly seen as a use, and the rule stops
suggesting a shift that would discard it.

events.title: Revive the rule test suite and fix fixture normalization
events.message:
Revive the rule test suite and fix fixture normalization

The 1,326-line rule suite had not run at all: 13 sites called
`result.diagnostics` on a `Diagnostic[]`, which is a compile error, so
ts-jest skipped the whole file and reported it as a single failure.

Underneath that, nearly every fixture was written in column-zero form.
m68k-parser applies real assembler column rules, so `move.l #42,d3`
parsed as a label named `move` and the rules matched nothing.

- Split tsconfig: `lint` typechecks tests, `build` still excludes them so
  they are not emitted into the published `dist`.
- Add `src/test/helpers.ts` with `lint`/`ids`/`fixtureContext`, sharing one
  indent rule with the impact audit so the two corpora cannot drift.
- Fix the stale `result.diagnostics` call sites.
- Fix the audit normalizer: its docstring claimed colon-terminated labels
  survive indentation, but an indented `.loop:` parses as neither a label
  nor a mnemonic, so branch targets silently vanished. Column-zero label
  definitions are now left in place.

161 rule tests now execute; 143 pass. The remaining 18 are genuine
expectation triage, handled separately.

events.title: Save-states : plus un octet non initialisé — bourrage explicite de Fpu et StePads
events.message:
Save-states : plus un octet non initialisé — bourrage explicite de Fpu et StePads

Trouvé par l'agent de fuzz (valgrind sur un « export » : 67 erreurs, writev
d'octets non initialisés, CRC de saveState dépendant de mémoire indéfinie) :
Fpu (61 octets) et StePads (5) sont sérialisées d'un BLOC (Bus::serialize,
ar(fpu), ar(stePads)) avec leur bourrage implicite jamais initialisé. Un .state
partagé emportait des octets de mémoire du processus, et son CRC n'était
déterministe que par chance. Antérieur au chantier, reproduit par
« --frames 2 --save-state ».

Méthode : sonde à 0xAA — objet construit en place sur une mémoire remplie de
0xAA, on liste les octets restés 0xAA. Carte exacte : Fpu [1..7] (bool →
Ext aligné 8), 6 octets dans chacun des 8 registres Ext (uint16 → uint64),
[279], [289..291], [298..299] ; StePads [5..7], [26..27] ; Scu : 0.

Remède : des champs de bourrage EXPLICITES et initialisés (uint8_t pad_[N] =
{}) aux emplacements exacts, donc offsets et sizeof INCHANGÉS — verrouillés par
static_assert (Ext 16, Fpu 304, StePads 28). Format de save-state inchangé :
un état écrit par le binaire précédent se relit (vérifié).

Piège rencontré et réglé : Fpu.cpp construit Ext une dizaine de fois de façon
POSITIONNELLE (Ext{se, man}) ; avec pad_ inséré au milieu, la mantisse partait
dans pad_[0] (narrowing) et man gardait sa valeur par défaut — deux sites
seulement avertissaient. Un constructeur Ext(uint16_t, uint64_t) retire à Ext
son statut d'agrégat : chaque Ext{a, b} l'appelle, aucun site ne change, la
classe reste trivialement copiable (exigence de StateArchive).

Après : sonde 0 octet sur les trois classes, valgrind 0 erreur (était 67),
--save-state-test OK, verdict FPU (14 tests, vrai chemin Ext) PASS, --tier fast
tous les paliers OK. TODO.md : entrée passée en RÉSOLU avec la méthode.

    le masque tenu AU MOMENT DU LOAD, pas celui du « save ». Reprendre une
    cellule après une branche qui relâchait le feu ne rejouait pas la même
    chose (deux hachages RAM pour la même cellule, mesuré). Slot mémorise
    joy0/joy1 ; « load » les reprend ; « import » (fichier) les remet à zéro
    sans toucher l'état restauré ;
  - --joy lisait son masque en base 0 : « 80 » = 80 DÉCIMAL ($50, bas+droite),
    « $80 » = 0, sans message — trois notations, trois masques, et le bit FEU
    précisément celui qui cassait. Le serveur, lui, lisait de l'hexa. --joy et
    --joy-at lisent désormais de l'hexa ($, 0x ou nu) avec validation ; aucune
    recette du dépôt n'écrivait de décimal nu (vérifié), « 0x80 » reste valide.

BLOCAGE
  - « run N » sans borne : « run 9223372036854775807 » gelait la session sans
    recours (SIGKILL) ; le fuzz aléatoire l'a trouvé seul (« run 53453622 »).
    Borné à 10 M comme un script.

RÉPONSES FAUSSES
  - nom de sonde ≥ 116 caractères : la VALEUR disparaissait de la ligne
    (tampon de 128 octets) ; nom avec espace ou « = » : format « clé=valeur »
    cassé ; deux sondes de même nom : deux clés identiques. Noms bornés à 64,
    validés, doublons refusés — des deux côtés (--probe et « probe ») ;
  - reply() ne vérifiait ni l'écriture ni le vidage : sur /dev/full le serveur
    « répondait » dans le vide et sortait 0. Vérifié, code 1 ;
  - client mort : SIGPIPE tuait le processus AVANT la fermeture de la trace
    (fichier tronqué). Ignoré, EPIPE remonte par reply(), sortie propre ;
  - « hello » tronqué à 767 caractères (chemin long → « tos= » coupé,
    fastfdc= disparu) : plus de tampon fixe ;
  - arguments surnuméraires ignorés (« save 0 nimportequoi » → ok) : arité
    stricte ; NUL dans la ligne tronquait l'écho (printf) : fwrite ; verbe
    inconnu de 5 Mo renvoyé en entier : écho borné à 40 caractères ;
  - « load » disait toujours « config mismatch? » : renvoie vers stderr avec la
    liste des causes possibles.

TROUVAILLE DANS LE CŒUR, NON CORRIGÉE ICI (TODO.md) : chaque save-state grave
et hache des octets NON INITIALISÉS — bourrage de la classe Fpu sérialisée d'un
bloc (valgrind, 67 erreurs, premier octet fautif = premier octet du bloc fpu).
Antérieur au chantier, reproduit par --frames 2 --save-state. Remède à
trancher (sérialisation champ par champ ou bourrage explicite), avec valgrind
et --save-state-test à l'appui — pas à chaud.

Doc : « run » ≤ 10 M, « peek » lit $FF sur l'espace I/O, « load » reprend le
joystick tenu au save, lignes vides/commentaires sans réponse, --joy en hexa.

Vérifié : équivalence 11 OK (dont reprise de cellule après branche, --joy 80 ==
joy 80, session rejouée deux fois) ; mutation « entrée après la trame » → 2 FAIL,
code 1 ; --tier fast : tous les paliers OK (séquenceur MIDI sauté, données
Cubase absentes — antérieur).

events.title: Chasse aux bugs par agents (port + outils) : 2 graves, 5 moyens, 12 bas
events.message:
Chasse aux bugs par agents (port + outils) : 2 graves, 5 moyens, 12 bas

Relecture adversariale par deux agents indépendants sur le travail porté,
chaque finding reproduit sur le binaire avant correction.

GRAVES
  - --server refusait de démarrer dès que la disquette PAR DÉFAUT
    (disks/diskA.st) manquait — donc depuis tout autre cwd qu'une racine de
    dépôt : binaire installé, borne, CI. Ma garde « disquette manquante »
    (revue précédente) confondait le confort de développement et un média
    DEMANDÉ. Seul un --disk explicite (ou neost.cfg) est désormais fatal ;
  - --break/--watch/--break-sym en mode serveur : un hit gelait le CPU et le
    protocole continuait de répondre « ok frame=… » sur une machine figée
    (compteur 200 Hz arrêté à la trame 10, RC=0). Leur seul lecteur est la
    boucle --frames : REFUS explicite en serveur.

MOYENS
  - opendst_oracle.py : sur une scène d'ancrage STATIQUE, toutes les images de
    la fenêtre sont identiques et le « décalage mesuré » valait mécaniquement
    −scan — verdict final trivialement IDENTIQUE (121/121 images). La passe A
    est exhaustive et REFUSE l'ambiguïté (« ALIGNEMENT AMBIGU »). Le point
    −200 du tableau de dérive égale la demi-fenêtre utilisée : signalé comme
    possible artefact, à re-mesurer ;
  - --joy-script-file <répertoire> terminait le processus (ios_failure non
    rattrapée, core dump) au lieu du message promis : is_regular_file d'abord ;
  - pompes hôte (--modem, --midi-net, NE2000) annoncées puis jamais servies en
    serveur (file UDP jamais drainée, mesuré) : refus, elles cassent aussi le
    déterminisme ; --serial-dump/--midi-dump absents de l'avertissement des
    sorties ignorées ; run_server_equiv.py avalait le stderr du binaire en
    traceback CalledProcessError (la cause remonte, verdict FAIL nommé) ;
  - opendst_explore.py : --score sur une sonde absente dégénérait en nouveauté
    pure sans un mot (refusé) ; états ORPHELINS à chaque cellule améliorée
    (9 fichiers pour 1 cellule, mesuré — effacés) ; stderr du serveur jeté et
    erreurs en traceback (journal dans out/server.log, messages) ;
    --load-state rendait les options de boot muettes (averti).

BAS
  - « play » préservait le port 0 tenu, là où --joy-script l'écrit à 0 :
    divergence serveur ↔ boucle dès qu'un port 0 est tenu — alignée ;
  - --probe-every + --trace - : lignes de sonde insérées dans la trace sur
    stdout (3 sur 21 632, mesuré) — refusé, comme en serveur ;
  - --printer journalisait sur STDOUT : première ligne lue par un client
    serveur = pas une réponse — stderr ;
  - --probe-every « abc »/« 0 » devenaient 1 en silence — analyse stricte ;
  - tri lexicographique des images de fenêtre faux au-delà de 99 999 trames ;
  - mkdtemp de l'oracle jamais nettoyé (~300 PNG par run) — ménage sur succès ;
  - UnicodeEncodeError en locale ASCII pure — sorties reconfigurées ;
  - doc : rupture de compatibilité de la grammaire joystick documentée
    (caractère inconnu = refus, minuscules = direction), exemple de sortie de
    l'oracle conforme, chiffres de performance remesurés et cohérents (5,1 /
    3,1 / 1,45 ms → ≈ 95 ms l'itération, 91 % d'émulation), « hello »
    informatif et « import » remet la datation à 0, deux épingles Hatari en
    désaccord (hatari_oracle.sh f0736b2 vs patch 981f291) signalées ;
  - coquille « LEN in 1..400000 » → « $1..$400000 (4 MB) ».

Vérifié et trouvé correct par les agents : sémantique --joy-script au bit près
(A/B contre le binaire de 761a728 sur 7 scénarios, PPM + état), filet de
loadState sans CRC complet sur un fichier tronqué APRÈS l'en-tête avec CRC
repatché, CRC table == bit à bit (zlib), CMake et CI par nom de cible, HATARI_SEED
byte-identique sur deux runs, patch Hatari réapplicable sur arbre propre.

Fait au passage : disks/etalons/usatan_sd.img (non suivi) était une image de
la lignée précédente ; le verdict nubnic échouait localement alors que la CI
est verte — régénérée avec make_usatan_hd.py, 7/7 PASS.

--tier fast : TOUS LES PALIERS OK (couverture amputée du séquenceur MIDI,
données Cubase absentes de cette machine — antérieur, vérifié sur origin/main).

events.title: ecs: the copper agrees with the cut — sixth cause excluded for #19
events.message:
ecs: the copper agrees with the cut — sixth cause excluded for #19

ecs_cop_verify re-derives every copper COLOR word from s_band_pal in the 4-bit
encoding and compares it against the word the copper actually reads, at the end
of every present. 800 words (25 bands x 32 slots), 0 mismatched, twice.

The probe reports its CHECKED COUNT next to the mismatch count on purpose, so a
zero cannot be mistaken for 'never ran'. That specific confusion has produced
false passes here repeatedly — a missing objdump, a missing binary, a converter
pointed at a missing file — and it produced one earlier in this same
investigation.

artview gains --compose: a title screen on screen is a BASE plus an OVERLAY,
because l19d4 loads the library twice, so a reference built from the base alone
reports the entire overlay as a difference and reads as corruption. The palette
accumulates across entries, matching the engine's successive installs.

Six causes are now excluded for #19: draw-time planar writers, both palette
caches, stale previous-screen content, the remap, SSI's art, and the copper
words. Recorded honestly: the per-pixel screenshot-to-art comparison was NOT
achieved — three alignment methods disagreed (dx 21/28/22, dy 10/23/12), so no
percentage from it is trustworthy and none is quoted.

Next step removes the screenshot from the loop: dump the backend's own chunky
surface, band palettes and remaps at the end of a title render and compare
offline against artview --compose, both sides in game coordinates.

492 tests pass (10 for artview, mutation-checked).

events.title: tools: artview.py renders the art offline — and it says the art is CLEAN
events.message:
tools: artview.py renders the art offline — and it says the art is CLEAN

Built to settle one question the emulator cannot: when a screen looks wrong on
a 16/32-colour machine, is the mark in SSI's data or did the port put it there?
Everything a screenshot shows has already been through the quantiser.

artview reuses perband's proven decoders rather than reimplementing the codecs,
extending them to keep the pixel POSITIONS the colour-counting versions throw
away: PackBits, transparency-RLE (0 ends the row, >=128 skips 257-b, index 0
transparent), raw 8bpp, mode-9 composites placed by dx/dy, and the jt993
palette-window law. Mono pieces are skipped, not guessed — there is no pen
offline. --info prints the container tree, --item/--all render.

Verdict on #19: TITLE.TLB entry 1 — the 320x200 base carrying the granite
frame and the red gradient the marks sit in — renders smooth and clean at 256
colours. The left-edge marks are NOT in the art. That kills candidate (b) and
leaves the ECS palette path.

Also corrects an error in the #19 notes: 'TITLE.TLB gives 2 items' was me
misreading the API. prequant.parse_glib returns a (count, offsets) TUPLE, not
a list of items; the container has 7 entries, and each title screen is base
entry 1 composited with its own overlay — which is exactly l19d4's two loads.

Nine tests, mutation-checked: 3 of 4 mutations were caught first time, and the
one that survived (flipping the row sign) was a real gap — every fixture was a
single row, so r was always 0. Added a 3-row piece; the mutation now fails.

491 -> 492 tests pass.

events.title: ecs: characterise the left-edge corruption and rule out four causes (#19)
events.message:
ecs: characterise the left-edge corruption and rule out four causes (#19)

Not fixed. Recording what it is and what it is not, so the next attempt does
not re-derive any of it.

What it is, measured on the Forgotten Realms title in amiberry at exact pixels:
thin HORIZONTAL runs of beige/white/orange, 3-60 px long, at the left of the
picture, inside smooth dark-red gradient that should hold no such colour. The
same screen on AGA is clean — same engine, same chunky surface — so the fault
is in the ECS conversion, not the drawing.

Ruled out, each by a one-variable A/B:

  - draw-time planar writers: PLANAR=0 renders the frame PIXEL-IDENTICAL
    (5c5c4e5d both ways), so this is upstream of plane writing
  - both palette caches: clutcache=off palcache=off + deleted PALCACHE.ECS,
    identical hashes
  - stale previous-screen content: 3% of candidate pixels match the preceding
    screen, and those are border pixels identical between screens anyway;
    shifted-lookup control 0%
  - a catastrophic remap: the new FRUA_ECSERR probe reports the worst
    used-colour-to-slot distance per band; worst is grey -> slightly lighter
    grey (idx 19 #838387 -> #a8a8a8), never red -> beige

Adds FRUA_ECSERR (worst per-band remap error, with the wanted and assigned
RGB) and notes an exact-pixel AGA config for matched-geometry comparison —
the stock openua.uae blends and drowns the artefact in a naive diff.

Two candidates remain: the copper palette install for non-boundary rows, or
the marks being in SSI's art with AGA's 256 colours hiding what a 32-colour
cut exposes. The latter is offline and cheap and should be tried first; it
needs a real art renderer, since TITLE.TLB does not decode with perband's
piece decoders.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: slaapliedje

events.title: ecs: present again after the palette lands — the SSI logo now displays (#18)
events.message:
ecs: present again after the palette lands — the SSI logo now displays (#18)

A500 report: 'the SSI / Micromagic logo screen no longer even displays... it's
there on the AGA version.' That split was the clue — same engine code, same
art, one works.

The title's palette is installed AFTER the present that shows it:

    tsq:   jt117 SHOW, mode = 2
    ecsp:  present, dirty=0                 converts under the OLD palette
    ecsp:  set_palette first=16 count=240   the title's palette, after

On a hardware-palette screen that is harmless — the pixels are already placed
and the late CLUT write recolours them, which is why AGA was always fine. On a
quantiser the pixels were converted through the previous palette and no later
write can fix them; at boot that previous palette is the black startup one, so
the screen renders black and the title never appears. It also explains why THIS
screen was missing while later ones merely looked wrong: each title was being
shown in its predecessor's colours.

Quantisers now take one more present after the palette bracket closes, so the
cut runs against the complete CLUT. The backend already declines the premature
present, which is #16's defer doing useful work. HW-palette backends keep the
Mac's single present.

ecs_set_palette also marks the bands dirty for ANY palette write while a
composition bracket is open, not just count >= 32. Size is the wrong test
there: a title whose art declares fewer than 32 colours was filed as colour
cycling and never re-cut.

★ This also corrects a FALSE POSITIVE in #16. As first written, the cut-defer
swallowed jt117 — the one present each title gets, since the composition holds
the rest — so the sentinel counts read 0 because no cut happened, not because
the cut was clean, while the whole title sequence rendered black (60/60 frames)
and the metric said 'fixed'. A metric can go quiet because the work stopped.
The re-verification now requires the titles to actually render as well.

Verified: the SSI/MicroMagic screen renders on ECS and matches the AGA
reference; 4 titles composed -> 4 renders (1:1, was 0); sentinel pixels and
magenta band slots both still 0. All four targets build; 483 tests pass.

Adds FRUA_TITLESEQ (per-title compose/show/art-load tracing and ECS
present/render branch decisions), which is what made this measurable.

events.message:
Pilotage externe déterministe de NeoST (porté sur la lignée GitHub)

Ce travail a été fait sur une lignée locale qui, mesure faite, ne partage avec
origin/main qu'un ancêtre du 2026-05-31 : 500 commits d'un côté, 706 de l'autre,
2752 fichiers d'écart. Il est donc REPORTÉ ici sur la lignée GitHub plutôt que
fusionné — la lignée locale reste intacte sous « lignee-locale-2026-09-04 ».

Ce que ça apporte à neost-headless :

  - grammaire joystick élargie : combinaisons [UF], masque brut [$88], répétition
    TOKEN*N, total borné à 10 M de trames, --joy-script-file. Sans combinaisons,
    ni le tir ni la dynamite de Rick Dangerous n'étaient exprimables. Logique
    pure (src/util/JoyScript.hpp), couverte À LA VALEUR PRÈS par neost-selftest
    (429 OK). L'option reste répétable, comme sur cette lignée ;
  - sondes mémoire --probe / --probe-every / --hash-ram, sur stdout, lecture
    peek8 SANS effet de bord (une version par read8 tuait le processus sur les
    registres whitelistés en accès octet) ;
  - mode --server : boucle de commandes stdin/stdout, emplacements d'état EN
    MÉMOIRE, un rollout = un aller-retour. Équivalence avec la boucle --frames
    vérifiée au palier fast, et le verdict est MUTATION-TESTÉ : re-vérifié sur
    CETTE lignée, muté → code 1 sur la bonne ligne, sain → 8 OK ;
  - save-states plus rapides : CRC-32 par table (il était bit à bit) et filet de
    loadState sérialisé sans CRC. Reprise 21,6 → 3,9 ms, sauvegarde 10,2 →
    2,6 ms (mesuré sur la lignée précédente), format et valeurs INCHANGÉS —
    états existants toujours lisibles, vérifié. Le GUI (F7/F8) en profite ;
  - oracle différentiel tools/opendst_oracle.py (« pour tout script d'entrées,
    NeoST == Hatari ») avec alignement du décalage de boot en deux passes, et
    patch Hatari enfin VERSIONNÉ (tools/hatari_neost_oracle.patch : script
    joystick daté par VBL, graine HATARI_SEED figeable, événements souris) ;
  - client Go-Explore d'exemple tools/opendst_explore.py ;
  - docs/OPENDST.md : contrat de déterminisme, protocole, recette Rick Dangerous
    vérifiée, et les LIMITES MESURÉES de l'oracle (le décalage saute à chaque
    chargement disque : −7 / −11 / −110 / −200 trames sur Super Sprint).

Vérifié sur cette lignée : selftest 429 OK, run_server_equiv 8 OK, mutation
rouge, états relus. ⚠ « --tier fast » signale une étape NON EXÉCUTÉE (séquenceur
MIDI, données Cubase non redistribuables absentes de cette machine) — vérifié
identique sur origin/main INTACT, donc antérieur à ce port.

events.title: zynaps atari: in-game controls — ESC to the menu, F10 to TOS
events.message:
zynaps atari: in-game controls — ESC to the menu, F10 to TOS

Two deliberate divergences, shim-only, always-on (not cheat-gated), the
differential untouched (make test 4751).
- ESC (0x01) while PHASE_PLAYING -> the main menu, re-using the game's OWN
  back-to-front-end path (frame_loop_once returning FRAME_EXIT_TITLE, the
  all-lives-lost exit). Round trip proven twice in Hatari.
- F10 (0x44) -> TOS, re-using the shim's teardown (restore vectors/PSG/
  rez/palette/base with read-backs, then Pterm). CLEAN in a level; at the
  pure attract screen the main line is parked inside the verified
  attract_wait_for_start, which has no shim checkpoint, so the F10 flag
  latches and fires once a game starts (documented, not a flaky unwind).
- Mechanism: a second unconditional door tap zy_note_control_key beside
  the trainer's; in the ACIA interrupt it only SETS volatile flags, acted
  on the main line in play_one_game after frame_loop_once returns (never
  unwind from the interrupt). Census: no cmpi.b #$01/#$44 anywhere in the
  program — collision-free with SPACE/1/2.

Review caught a real latch leak: g_phase lingers at PLAYING through
boot_front_end_prologue between games, so an ESC auto-repeat edge would
bounce the next game after one frame — fixed by clearing g_quit_to_menu on
play_one_game entry, with a deterministic regression (poke the latch at
attract, start game 2, assert esc_to_menu does not rise) that reddens with
the clear removed.

smoke.py controls: the ESC round trip and the F10 exit proven; every
judged mode asserts esc_to_menu==0 and f10_to_tos==0; mutations 3/3 red.
Matrix green; pacing 2.54 unchanged; ZY_NOCHEATS green. Docs: atari and
recreate READMEs' "In-game controls", root README's divergence paragraph.

events.title: zynaps trainer: audible feedback — a per-key blip and a louder arm fanfare
events.message:
zynaps trainer: audible feedback — a per-key blip and a louder arm fanfare

The typed sequence works on iron, but the arm sound was inaudible: stream
35 opens `fa 03 e8 01 e9 01 ea 01` — all three tone periods = 1, a
near-ultrasonic whistle (−10.7 dBFS on a meter, thin to the ear). Measured
from out/audio/manifest.tsv.

- Arm fanfare 35 -> 23 (CHEAT_SFX_ARMED 0x23 -> 0x17): stream 23 opens
  `fa 03 e8 11 ...`, an audible mid pitch, −10.8 dBFS, 2.0 s — also `fa 03`
  and also an orphan the shipped game never plays, so the resurrected-cut-
  content spirit holds.
- Per-key blip: CHEAT_SFX_KEY 0x1d (stream 29, 0.90 s) plays on each
  ACCEPTED, non-completing letter (Z, Y — and a fresh Z that restarts),
  so the sequence is heard landing key by key; the completing N gives the
  fanfare, not a blip.
- The split honors the interrupt rule: the ACIA door raises g_blip_pending
  (a byte, like g_seq_complete); zy_cheats_tick drains it in the VBL as an
  `else if` to the arm branch, so a blip and the fanfare never sound in one
  tick and sound_start is never called from the keyboard interrupt.

Smoke: cheats reports "1 fanfare on stream 0x177a4 (= stream 23's head),
7 blips"; an independent blip-count replay and STREAM-ID PINS
(CHEAT_ARM_STREAM=23 / CHEAT_BLIP_STREAM=29) — the self-referential
fanfare read-back would stay green if the id reverted to 35, so the pin is
what catches it. Negatives (Z,Y,Z,N and Z,Y) refuse and leave no fanfare.
key_blips added to the record, 0 asserted in every judged mode (dormancy).
Mutations 4/4 red. make test 4751 unchanged; matrix green; pacing 2.53;
ZY_NOCHEATS green. README "Four sounds" -> "Five sounds".

events.title: zynaps trainer: arm by TYPING Z, Y, N in order, not a simultaneous hold
events.message:
zynaps trainer: arm by TYPING Z, Y, N in order, not a simultaneous hold

The simultaneous Z+Y+N hold did nothing on a real STE: three keys sharing
rows/columns can ghost on the IKBD's undiode-isolated matrix and never all
report, which Hatari's event injection bypasses (so smoke.py cheats passed
while iron failed). A typed sequence touches one matrix cell at a time and
cannot ghost.

zynaps_cheats.c: a cursor over [Z, Y, N] plus a sticky g_seq_complete
latch replace g_held[]/g_hold_vbls/CHEAT_ARM_HOLD_VBLS/the_whole_combo_is_
held. The ACIA door advances the cursor on a combo-letter make while the
arming window is open — the expected next letter advances, a wrong letter
resets (to 1 if it is Z, else 0, so a fumble then a clean Z-Y-N still
arms); breaks and joystick bytes are ignored as before. The VBL tick arms
on the latch with the window open (jingle sfx 35 + g_armed + the pokes),
main-line context, exactly as before; the window-open clears cursor+latch
for stale-state recovery. F1/F2/F3, the effects, the orphan-sfx feedback
and the game-table + AZERTY per-letter scancode resolution are unchanged.

smoke.py cheats: types the three scancodes in order; two negatives —
a fumble Z,Y,Z,N (catches both "advance on a wrong letter" and "no reset
on a wrong letter") and an incomplete Z,Y — must not arm; the positive
Z,Y,N arms once with the fanfare on voice-3 stream 0x178e2. Mutations 4/4
red. cheats_armed==0 still asserted in every judged mode; ZY_NOCHEATS
build+smoke green; pacing unchanged at 2.53 vblanks/frame (the matcher is
cheaper than the hold's 3-element scan).

events.message:
Add -DSKIP_COPYPROT=1 so the game can be played under an emulator

main's `cprot_r = cp_main();` becomes a non-zero constant, so cs_mvIn
and gameLoop take their normal paths instead of parking the resident
in `while (1) a_sleep(-1);` -- the loop that re-runs lcp_hwt() every
iteration and leaves it standing and waving for ever.  Skipping the
CALL rather than the check also avoids the FDC wait, which never
terminates when the program was launched from a drive that is not the
floppy.

The default build is untouched and still byte-identical: 123352 bytes,
MD5 eae52d14023b51d7ac459a90d37eed10, and reloc_audit reports its
expected A0/B1/C0/D1/E1/F1.

Verified with the gated build under Hatari from a GEMDOS drive: the
move-in cutscene plays, the dog arrives, the resident walks down from
the attic, sits in the living-room armchair to read, and later changes
clothes -- roughly ten emulated minutes of real gameplay with no frame
corruption.  None of that happens in the shipped configuration on any
emulator available here.

events.title: Audit every relocation target; one more merge found, three arrays resized
events.message:
Audit every relocation target; one more merge found, three arrays resized

Added source/tools/reloc_audit.py, which pairs the two relocation
streams site by site and reports six ways the port's variable structure
can disagree with the original's.  prg_diff.py cannot see any of them:
it compares the binary after bss_remap has rewritten the targets.

It found one more variable the port had invented.  aes_intO[16], whose
only use was `aes_intO[7] = g_mtspb`, is a SINGLE short in the
reference -- all six accesses go to one cell and the next cell it uses
is two bytes later.  The array shape was never evidence: Alcyon folds a
constant subscript into the absolute address, so `arr[7]` and a plain
short emit the same instruction.  Renamed mi_tpb, ticks-per-beat.

(The cell sits exactly 14 bytes past AESBIND's int_out, which made
"the sequencer borrows int_out[7]" tempting -- and wrong: int_out is
only 14 bytes, so writing it that way lands on the next global.  That
is what the new audit's category E is for -- a symbol referenced only
at a non-zero offset has an INFERRED base, and the inference is only as
good as the assumed shape.  scrbufA is the one remaining such symbol,
first referenced at +511 through the align-up constant.)

Three arrays were declared larger than the original's storage, none of
which the text can show, since a char array's size does not reach the
codegen:

  g_agscw  12 -> 10   a nine-letter anagram and its NUL
  g_ltscb  64 -> 40
  g_sfDoB 256 -> 56   sf_irqp copies `size` bytes here straight from
                      SOUNDS.LCP and the file holds longer effects, so
                      the original overruns this buffer; reproduced as
                      written rather than papered over

What the audit reports now, and why each is expected:
  A merges          0
  B aliases         1  last_hz / mi_lasT -- one cell in the original,
                       and C cannot spell it without changing codegen
  C split symbols   0
  D unverifiable    1  scn_cmn, 30 bytes, which nothing relocates
                       against, so the pairing is blind to it
  E inferred bases  1  scrbufA
  F over-declared   1  last_hz, which is the B alias

Still byte-identical: MD5 eae52d14023b51d7ac459a90d37eed10.

events.title: Add an MCP server over saved profile captures
events.message:
Add an MCP server over saved profile captures

`puae-debugger mcp` exposes profile_check and profile_dump to an MCP client,
so a model can analyse a .puaeprofile without a person relaying terminal
output. A subcommand of the existing binary for the same reasons `profile` is:
shared bin entry, bundle and installation.

    claude mcp add puae -- npx puae-debugger mcp

The stdio JSON-RPC transport is hand-rolled rather than taking
@modelcontextprotocol/sdk. The surface actually needed is three requests and a
notification, fully specified, while the SDK would pull express, hono, zod, ajv
and jose into a package with ten runtime dependencies for a server that only
ever speaks stdio — and this project already hand-rolls its DAP server and its
PUAE RPC dispatcher on the same reasoning.

Protocol routing is separated from the stdio plumbing so it can be tested
directly rather than through a subprocess. Two behaviours worth noting, both
covered: notifications are never answered (replying to one is a violation some
clients treat as fatal), and a tool that fails on its input returns a normal
result carrying isError rather than a JSON-RPC error, so the model sees the
message and can correct itself.

The tool descriptions carry the ordering advice that the profiling skill leads
with — run check before trusting dump — because a capture's per-function
percentages read as entirely plausible even when the frame total they are a
share of is impossible. That is how three profiler bugs went unnoticed, so a
test asserts the instruction stays in the description.

Rendering moves to src/profileReport.ts, shared with the CLI, so a number
discussed in a terminal and one discussed over MCP are formatted identically.

Emulator-backed tools (capture, screenshot, memory) are not here yet. The
groundwork exists: setupRpcDispatcher runs against the wasm under plain Node,
which is how puae-wasm/test/*.mjs drive it, so a headless PuaeRpcClient needs
no browser.

events.title: Make the stall analysis work on a real 68000 capture
events.message:
Make the stall analysis work on a real 68000 capture

Three fixes, all found by running it against one.

The measured-below-datasheet guard was exact, which rejected a correct
capture. theoreticalTiming deliberately takes the SLOWEST of an instruction's
timings, so every untaken branch inflates the datasheet side slightly; a real
68000 frame with an almost-idle bus came in at 0.997x and was refused. The gap
the guard exists to catch is far wider — a 68020 capture measured 0.73x — so it
now allows a 10% shortfall, which separates the two with room either side.

Stalls were computed from ProfileManifest.disassembly, which holds frame 0's
only. Every frame therefore reported frame 0's figures, which was plainly wrong
on a capture whose bus load alternates between frames. It now uses each frame's
own reweighted disassembly, and the analysis moves onto FrameAnalysis so
`dump --frame N --stalls` reports frame N.

model.datasheet was only set where raw disassembly exists — frame 0 — so the
profiler's stall column appeared on frame 0 and nowhere else, including the
blitter-heavy frames where it matters. Applicability is derived from a frame's
own aggregate and cannot be inherited, so it is now judged wherever a
reweighted disassembly is attached.

The result validates the premise independently of the DMA census that
corroborates it. On the same capture, frame 0 (bus idle 55.8%, no blitter)
measures -0.3% stall — no contention to suffer — while frame 1 (blitter 35.9%)
measures 24.6%, essentially all of it on TransformVisibleCityBuildings at
24.7%. That is the routine running against the blitter, and the number says
rescheduling it would buy more than optimising its CPU code.

events.title: BYTE-IDENTICAL to DATA/LCP_STX.PRG (MD5 eae52d14023b51d7ac459a90d37eed10)
events.message:
BYTE-IDENTICAL to DATA/LCP_STX.PRG (MD5 eae52d14023b51d7ac459a90d37eed10)

Text 104156, data 12260, bss 187450, relocations 6908 -- every byte
the same as the uncracked original extracted from the Pasti image.

The last step is bss_remap.py, recovered from the LCP_ORG campaign and
retargeted.  lo68 and the 1985 linker pack the same commons at
different offsets, so TEXT, DATA and the relocation stream come out
identical while every relocated BSS longword points somewhere else.
The original's allocation is carried as a checked-in spec,
tools/stx_bss_layout.tsv (417 rows, port symbol+offset -> address, bss
size in the header); alcyon_link.sh now takes a second SYMBOLS link as
lcp_sym.68k, resolves the spec against it, and rewrites the 3842
affected sites.  The reference binary is not read at link time.

One change to the recovered tool: many-to-one is allowed now, with the
alias printed.  The original aliased storage in a place the port
cannot spell in C without changing the codegen -- last_hz and the
sequencer's mi_lasT are one cell there, and writing that as a cast
macro makes Alcyon emit move.w where the original has move.b.

Reproduce from a clean tree with:

    rm -rf source/build/alcyon
    source/tools/alcyon_build.sh
    source/tools/alcyon_link.sh
    LCP_REF=DATA/LCP_STX.PRG python3 source/tools/prg_diff.py

events.title: Five more BSS/data reference bugs from the relocation audit
events.message:
Five more BSS/data reference bugs from the relocation audit

Pairing every relocation target between the two binaries and demanding
the same SEGMENT and the same data address turns up references that
byte comparison cannot see.  With these five fixed, every one of the
6429 relocations resolves to the same segment as the reference's, and
every text and data target to the identical address.

  * mi_ndur.  mq_pars computes the queued event's duration into a cell
    of its own that only mq_qnne reads; mq_rdur's identical expression
    goes to mi_nlp0, which drives the tick counters.  The port had
    merged the two.
  * g_mnhi / g_mnlo were named backwards.  0x34c holds 0x60 and 0x34e
    holds 0x24, so the first is the TOP of the playable note range --
    which also settles mq_dise's guard: the reference tests the low
    limit first and the high second, where the port had them the other
    way round.
  * lcp_lgt and lcp_rgt write g_inpmd, the keyboard-input-mode flag
    deal_kc and gameTick test, not no_keyin.
  * cl_redrH's second cl_drwH call reads the cached g_cmmin/g_chhou
    back rather than t_min/t_hour.
  * g_msmap and mi_seqE were merged in the previous commit.

Remaining: last_hz and mi_lasT are one cell in the reference and two
symbols here, because spelling the alias in C changes the codegen.

events.title: g_msmap and mi_seqE are one variable
events.message:
g_msmap and mi_seqE are one variable

The reference relocates mq_setp's two stores and mq_pars' four
`mi_sqpos >= mi_seqE` tests to the SAME cell.  It is the
end-of-sequence pointer, and -1 is how 'no limit' is spelled -- every
caller passes g_momap, which is 0, so the -1 arm is the one that runs.
The port had split it into a long g_msmap and a pointer mi_seqE.

last_hz and mi_lasT are likewise one cell (the compositor's word
accesses and the sequencer's byte accesses relocate to the same
address, and a byte write lands on the word's high half), but writing
that as `#define mi_lasT (*(char *) &last_hz)` changes the codegen --
Alcyon takes the width from &last_hz and emits move.w where the
original has move.b.  Left as two symbols; the BSS layout spec will
map both onto the one address.

events.title: MFDB_A is a short[10], and stpScrB clears fd_addr
events.message:
MFDB_A is a short[10], and stpScrB clears fd_addr

The reference clears MFDB_A+0 and MFDB_A+2 and passes that same
address to vro_cpyfm; declared as an MFDB struct, the port wrote the
extents at +4/+6 and passed the base, so cpyScr's source descriptor
and stpScrB's target were four bytes apart.  Clearing the two halves
of fd_addr is also what the code means -- a NULL address is the VDI's
'the device screen', which is the whole point of this MFDB.

(Alcyon rejects `((short *) &MFDB_A)[0] = 0` outright -- 'no code
table for =' -- which is its own argument that the original declared
an array here.)

events.title: Four BSS reference bugs that byte comparison cannot see
events.message:
Four BSS reference bugs that byte comparison cannot see

verify_bytes and stx_txtdiff both wildcard relocated longwords, so a
function matches byte for byte while the ADDRESS it loads is wrong.
Pairing every relocation's BSS target between the two binaries finds
them, and it found four:

  * dg_wkPth and lcp_flwp had their first comparison's operands the
    wrong way round.  Alcyon evaluates the RIGHT operand first, so the
    reference's `getFlrY(dog_y) != getFlrY(g_dty)` reaches dog_y in the
    second relocation and g_dty in the first -- the port had it
    mirrored, comparing the same two values but loading them in the
    other order.
  * gameTick's four sound-effect guards test g_sfplf, the "an effect is
    playing" flag sfx_irq sets, not g_sfacf.
  * mg_wkev reads the GLOBAL tank level lcp_watr, not lcp.water_level.

The text stays byte-identical through all four -- swapping two globals
of the same type, or one struct field for a global, changes only which
address the relocation carries.

DrCollide's inner scan began at slot 7 -- the player's bullet -- which
has no droid-table entry: DrFindSlot only hands out 1..SPR_POOL_LAST
and DroidsInit's clear is the only write that ever touches
drSlotOwner+7, so that entry is 0 for the life of the game.

Both arms of DrCollided dead-end on a zero owner, and the loop services
one pair a pass and jumps out the moment it finds one. So whenever the
bullet fell inside the outer slot's box it won the pair and the routine
returned having done nothing at all -- no player bump, no droid-droid
reverse -- and _x_none was never reached, so drCollHit stayed latched
into the next pass too. A bullet spawns on top of the player, so that
cost 1-2 passes of every shot plus every pass it flew near a droid.

Scan from SPR_POOL_LAST instead. Skipping the slot rather than aborting
on it is what the C64 does in substance: its sprite 0 is the player's
shot and carries a real mode-3 record, so that pair reaches
DoCollision2 and the table acts on it, where ours has already been
serviced by DrBulletHit before the loop runs.

Found by playtester Sydney, 2026-09-03: "droids passed through me and
each other, particularly when moving fast". A fast pair -- the player
at top speed against a 302 or an 834, the only two droids with drSpeed
8 -- is only inside the box for two or three passes, so a pass eaten by
the bullet loses the collision outright, where a slow approach has
passes to spare. NOT tunnelling through the box, which was the first
reading and is ruled out in BUGS.md #20.

One immediate operand; bank 4 ends &BFF3 before and after.

events.title: ecs: defer the CUT while the palette is still arriving (#16 titles)
events.message:
ecs: defer the CUT while the palette is still arriving (#16 titles)

The A500 title corruption: the art is cut against a CLUT still holding the
art's magenta defer sentinel, so the quantiser spends 10 of every band's 32
slots on a placeholder — a fifth of the budget, which is why the screen reads
as 'colours all inverted' rather than merely speckled.

The engine already marks the window. l19d4 brackets each title's composition in
qd_palette_blackout(), and a hardware-palette backend answers by pushing black
so the half-built screen is never seen. That call RETURNED BEFORE TOUCHING ITS
COUNTER on any other backend, so a quantiser could not ask the one question the
bracket answers.

Keep the counter for every backend (only the black push is hardware-specific)
and publish it as dsp_palette_incomplete(). The state lives in
platform/planar.c — shared by the Atari and Amiga builds, since neither
backend file is linked by the other — and the shim sets it, so the layer rule
holds: compat calls down into platform, never up.

ECS then defers its cut across the bracket, keeping the last complete frame on
screen; the engine's own install at the end of the bracket sets s_dirty and
that present cuts against a whole CLUT. A quantiser cannot blackout instead —
its planes hold slots, not indices — and its problem is worse than a visible
flash: a cut taken mid-bracket is BAKED IN and no later palette write undoes
it.

Measured on the same fixture and instrumentation as the root-cause run:
chunky pixels on sentinel slots 975 -> 0, band-palette magenta slots 10 -> 0,
at every cut. The defer fires for 4 presents.

Bounded at 24 presents, because #8 is what an unbounded wait costs; the bound
is on presents, not wall-clock, so it does not vary with machine speed. An
overrun loses the title, not the game. video.cfg titledefer=off is the A/B arm.

All four targets build; 483 tests pass. Emulator-measured.

The port's sf_pri was dumped from the data segment with the wrong
extent and swallowed six bytes of what follows it, which is why the
table ended in 205, 77, 115, 116, 117, 100 -- "\315Mstud".  Those
bytes are the head of the Music Studio file signature, 0xCD "Mstudio"
0xCD 0x02, that every SOUNDS.LCP and .SNG file starts with; midi_seq's

because Alcyon emits a unit's string literals after its globals and
the games object's data ends in strings.  8, 9 and 10 are the PSG's

events.title: installer: put something useful in the Amiga install console
events.message:
installer: put something useful in the Amiga install console

A1200 field report (2026-09-03), after verifying the AGA installer works: 'the
extra window that pops up with the installer version in it could be used for
the Unlimited Adventures screen, or maybe some of the readme information /
license and required files list'.

That window is ours — IconX opens it from the WINDOW= tooltype on Install.info
— and when the AmigaOS Installer is present the launcher left it empty behind
the Installer's GUI. Now it prints what a first-time installer actually needs
while that GUI is up: what this is and its version, what you need before
starting (engine disk, your data disks, ~7 MB free, and the measured Kickstart
minimum for the variant), what the installer is about to ask, and that RETURN
takes every default.

It also states the thing that matters legally and is easy to get wrong: the
ENGINE is GPL-2.0 with a source pointer, and the GAME DATA is not included and
not ours to give — the data disks come from the user's own copy of FRUA.

Costs nothing at run time and adds no files to a full floppy.

AmigaDOS specifics, both of which bite silently: '*' is the ESCAPE character in
a quoted string, so the bullets are '-' (verified 0 asterisks in the generated
script); and the window is CON:0/20/640/180, which topaz 8 fills at 80x22, so
the banner is kept to 63 columns and 19 lines. Verified by reading Install back
out of BOTH built ADFs, with the ECS variant correctly getting 'Kickstart 2.0
or later (ECS/OCS; 1.3 will NOT work)'. The engine binary is byte-identical
after the rebuild.

events.title: Split globals.c by owning object: 50 data symbols exactly placed
events.message:
Split globals.c by owning object: 50 data symbols exactly placed

The 1985 sources declared their globals in the file that used them, so
each object's data segment is its own globals plus the string literals
and switch tables its code emits.  Which object owns a stretch of
ANONYMOUS data is not a guess: a switch table's relocation points into
its own function, and a string is emitted in the object that
references it.  Filtering the LCP_STX relocation stream for anonymous
data with exactly one owner gives seven clean runs, in link order:

    0x0438..0x0464  globals    0x0a20..0x0d60  stx_u1
    0x0e56..0x1d48  games      0x1d9a          stx_u4
    0x1f22..0x1fd0  stx_u2     0x227e..0x2326  stx_u3
    0x2cc4..0x2f06  library

and the named globals between two runs belong to the object around
them -- which the names confirm: main_pal/vdi_colt/body_frT/hd_* with
stx_u1, wp_*/pk_*/crd_* with games, sf_pri/g_momap with stx_u4,
mo_name/days_pm/the clock tables with stx_u2, the sprite and parser
tables with stx_u3.

So globals.c's 146 data definitions are now dat_u1.c, dat_games.c,
dat_u4.c, dat_u2.c, dat_u3a.c and dat_u3b.c, each included at the head
of its object, with globals.c keeping only the MIDI/PSG ones that
belong to its own object.

Result: 50 data symbols now sit at EXACTLY their LCP_STX offset,
contiguous from the start of the segment through hd_dang at 0x736.
16 of the 402 data relocations line up.  Text stays 104156 == 104156
with zero differing bytes.

Three globals nothing relocates against (env_val, g_mccha, g_dsb) are
parked at the end of the last object's data with a comment saying why:
the pairing cannot place them, and leaving them mid-segment breaks a
stretch that is otherwise byte-identical.

NEXT: stx_u1's data is not all-globals-then-code.  execEv's and
doAct's switch tables sit at 0xa20..0xaf3, between pex_name and
g_atact, so dat_u1.c has to split around them -- the globals from
g_atact on belong after ai.c and actions.c in the unit.  Same shape as
the midi_seq fold, one level down.  (Attempted here and reverted: the
scratch splitter mangled a multi-line comment and a string table.  Any
retry must use the block parser in reorder_data.py, which understands
function bodies and comment blocks, not a paragraph split.)

Alcyon emits a switch jump table into the .data of the object holding
the function, so a table's position pins the object's data position.
LCP_STX has mq_parh's table (7 case longs + 7 targets) and mq_dise's
(5 targets) -- 19 longs, 76 bytes, exactly what midi_seq.c emits --
sitting between mi_pgmap at data 0x418 and main_pal at 0x468.  Data
from separate objects cannot interleave, so the globals and the MIDI
code are ONE object, split exactly there.

globals.c now `#include`s midi_seq.c at that point; stx_units.txt names
midi_seq.c as its constituent and alcyon_link.sh puts globals.o where
midi_seq.o was (text 0x12a).  Text is unaffected -- globals.c has no
functions -- and stays 104156 == 104156 with zero differing bytes.

Fixes that followed from the newly aligned stretch:

  g_molof MERGED into mi_slop.  One byte, one variable: sgPlay writes
          it (the port called that write g_molof) and mq_pars reads it,
          and both port names mapped to the same address, data 0x414.
          Same shape as the mi_nOS / mi_noSt merge.
  g_unus3 ADDED: two bytes of -1 that nothing references, between
          g_hamod and g_trac at data 0x4c0.
  g_cotbl, g_unus1, g_unus2 DELETED (60 bytes).  All three were added
          to match LCP_ORG's data segment -- g_cotbl's own comment said
          so -- and at their position they contradict LCP_STX's, which
          has g_rpxs at data 0x7f0 where the port had them.

DATA now agrees with LCP_STX byte for byte from 0x000 through 0xaf5
(was 0x191 at the start of this pass), and 17 of the 402 data
relocations line up.

NEXT, and it is the same finding one level out: the relocations at
data 0xa20 point at text 0x5fd6/0x5fde/0x5ffa/0x600c/0x5fce/0x602e --
execEv's switch table, which lives in the stx_u1 object.  So LCP_STX's
data runs [globals + midi_seq tables] ... [globals + stx_u1 tables] ...
which means the 1985 globals were DISTRIBUTED across the source files
by topic, not held in one file.  Reproducing the rest of the data
layout means splitting globals.c the same way the text was split, with
the switch tables and string literals marking the boundaries.
