events.title: hrtmon: build the HRTMon 2.39 cartridge image from source and bundle it
events.message:
hrtmon: build the HRTMon 2.39 cartridge image from source and bundle it

HRTMon is Alain Malek's Action Replay-style system monitor, maintained
by Bert Jahn (wepl) and contributors under the GPL, version 2 or later.
hrtmon-rom/build.sh assembles the pinned upstream source (commit
3af8d5105f1e01ecc7961475568826e564995068, HRTMon 2.39) with vasm in its
UAE cartridge configuration -- UAE=1 (ORG $A10000), CARTRIDGE=1 (the
cartridge header: RTE address, "HRT!" at +4, bra.w mon_install at +8,
bra.w monitor at +12) and SAVE_CUSTOM=1 (the custom-register snapshot
read from $A9F000) -- and bundles the result as assets/hrtmon/hrtmon.rom
beside its README and license text.

Two assembler fixes ride on the patched copy in build/: vasm's automatic
absolute-to-PC-relative optimisation is switched off with OPT a-, since
the source opens its vasm block with MC68030 and the optimiser rewrites
TST's absolute operands as (d16,PC), a 68020+ form on which a 68000 or
68010 takes an illegal-instruction exception at the first freeze; and
HRTMon's own AFB_68060 BITDEF is guarded for NDK 3.2 includes, which
already define it. The $VER date is pinned to the commit's so the image
is reproducible (199,300 bytes, SHA-256 184c9b12...).

romsearch::find_bundled_hrtmon locates the image the way the other
bundled ROMs are found (COPPERLINE_HRTMON_DIR, next to the binary,
Resources/ and share/copperline/ under the install prefix, assets/),
and the Homebrew formula, the Flatpak manifest and the AppImage and DMG
builds ship it with its notice and license.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: cartridge: HRTMon freezer bank at $A10000, register shadows and the level-7 freeze
events.message:
cartridge: HRTMon freezer bank at $A10000, register shadows and the level-7 freeze

A freezer cartridge takes the machine over whatever the running program
is doing: its button drives the 68000's IPL lines to 7, the one level
the SR mask cannot hold off, and the CPU vectors through the level-7
autovector into the cartridge's own monitor. This models the cartridge
as HRTMon's UAE build expects its host to behave (which is also how
WinUAE hosts it); nothing here is Amiga hardware -- a real Action
Replay sits on the expansion bus and snoops the chip-register writes
itself.

- Bank: 1 MiB at $A10000 (the image at its start, $FF beyond it),
  plain read/write memory on the CPU side decoded after RAM, ROM and
  the extended ROM at external-bus cost like Zorro RAM, cacheable, and
  present at all times: the monitor keeps its variables, stack and
  screen buffers there.
- Configuration block: the header fields at +20..+72 (screen colours,
  ide/a1200/aga/cd32, screenmode, novbr, entered, hexmode, max_chip)
  tell the monitor what it is running on. Bus::attach_cartridge writes
  them from the boards fitted (Gayle or A4000 IDE, Akiko, the chipset
  revision, the video standard, the chip RAM size), and a keyboard
  reset writes them again and clears the "entered" flag the monitor
  sets while it is active, as WinUAE's hrtmon_configure does.
- Register shadows: the monitor cannot read the write-only custom
  registers back, so the bus keeps the last value written to (or driven
  on a read of) every custom register, CPU and Copper alike, and the
  last byte written to each CIA register. A freeze copies them into the
  bank where the SAVE_CUSTOM build reads them: PTR_CUSTOM ($A9F000),
  and the CIA bytes at $A9E000 (CIA-A, odd lane) and $A9D000 (CIA-B,
  even lane) on the chips' $100 register stride.
- Entry: Cartridge::freeze writes the level-7 autovector (VBR + $7C,
  through the RAM-only writer DMA masters use, so a VBR in fast RAM
  works and a VBR in ROM refuses the press) to the bra.w monitor at
  +12 and arms the interrupt. pending_irq_level and the IPL sample
  report 7 while it is armed, the core takes level 7 regardless of the
  mask, and interrupt_acknowledge(7) consumes it: entered exactly once
  per press, as a 68000 recognises level 7 on its transition and not
  its level, so the RTE the monitor exits through does not re-enter it.
  The data cache is dropped at the acknowledge in case the vector slot
  sat under a stale line.
- State: the bank, the shadows, the pending interrupt and the press
  count are machine state inside Bus (STATE_VERSION 74), so run-ahead,
  rewind and save states restore a monitor session with the guest.

Tests: the cartridge module's own (loader tags, decode, the config
block, the shadow copy and the one-shot arm); a CPU test with a stub
handler at +12 that proves the NMI is taken under an SR mask of 7,
runs the handler from the bank, returns through RTE with the mask
intact and is not re-taken until the next press; bus tests for the
block on an AGA/NTSC/Gayle/Akiko machine and its rewrite on reset, and
for CPU, Copper and CIA writes reaching the bank on a freeze; a
save-state round trip keeping the bank, the shadows and a pending
press.

events.title: campaign2: recover the STX object partition wholesale (stx_objmap.py)
events.message:
campaign2: recover the STX object partition wholesale (stx_objmap.py)

New tool exploits two facts -- as68 only shortens SAME-OBJECT calls
to bsr, and the linker lays each object down contiguously -- so a
bsr from A to B proves all of [A,B] is one object.  Merging the
intervals spanned by all 1098 bsr instructions bounds the objects.

Result: 20 clusters with ZERO of the 1426 jsr edges falling inside
any of them.  Independent validation: the library clusters reproduce
real DRI libc source files (_access/_chmod/_chown, _free/_realloc,
_lseek/_tell, __creat/_opena/_openb).

The finding that matters: the STX build's game code is only ~7
objects, all huge (26-27 KB each), where the port has 55 small ones.
One 27 KB STX object holds functions the port spreads across nine
.c files; the 26 KB minigame object maps 1:1 onto games.c already.

Strategy shift documented in CLAUDE.md: stop moving functions
between .c files one at a time (each move was hand-replicating a
single edge of this partition) and instead build the default
configuration as ~7 unity translation units matching the recovered
boundaries, leaving the individual sources and the FAITHFUL build
untouched.

events.title: debugger: pin headless observation as timeline-transparent, drop the crash alarm from save states
events.message:
debugger: pin headless observation as timeline-transparent, drop the crash alarm from save states

The COPPERLINE_DBG_* debugger is a pure observer: its hooks read machine
state through side-effect-free peeks, never bill chip-bus or CPU time, and
write only to the host log. Measured knob by knob on three workloads (KS1.3
A500 with a disk-loading game, KS3.1 A1200/68020 with an AGA loader, the
bundled AROS ROM), every knob leaves the save-state and screenshot hashes
byte-identical. Two things did differ and are handled here:

- A [cpu] jit machine drops to the precise per-instruction loop while any
  debug or diagnostic hook is armed (jit_fast_path_ok), so a debugged run
  is the precise-timing run rather than the JIT run. note_jit_debug_fallback
  logs a warning at set_jit_enabled and arm_headless_debugger so this is no
  longer silent.
- Bus::diag_lowmem_blit, the COPPERLINE_DIAG_CRASH-only alarm latched by a
  blit whose D destination lands in low memory (KS3.1 AGA loaders do
  this), was serialized but cleared by the loader. On an undiagnosed run it
  stays latched for good, so a resumed run's state file, and the reverse
  watch's snapshot/restore bracket, differed from the uninterrupted run by
  that one byte. It is host diagnostics, so it is skipped from the layout
  (state version 74).

Debugger::new and M68kMachine::arm_headless_debugger arm the debugger
programmatically. tests/debugger_transparency.rs boots the bundled ROM on
two machines, one with a watch, a breakpoint, the VERTB catch, Alert()
catching, a dump and an unbounded trace armed, and compares colour clock,
frame, PC, rendered frame and chip RAM after every frame.
tests/savestate_roundtrip.rs now also compares the resumed run's final
state file byte for byte with the uninterrupted run's. docs/debugger/
headless.md gains a "Timeline transparency" section.

events.title: zynaps atari M2: the whole game composed — frame-differential ZERO bytes
events.message:
zynaps atari M2: the whole game composed — frame-differential ZERO bytes

The composition (atari/zynaps_main.c, build.sh game/gamefault/play):
boot slices in the original's order (the four $fffa21 read-back spins done
for real between the slices that stop on either side), vector DISPATCH on
the image's own vector page ($70/$120/$118 -> the eight C handlers; an
unknown address halts with the value in the record), the attract loop, the
section chain, frame_loop_once with its five exits wired to the chain, and
game over / high scores reached from inside the frame stage by playing.
build.sh play floppy -> ZYNAPS.ST boots from drive A through TOS's AUTO
scan to PLAYER 1 / PREPARE FOR COMBAT; the GEMDOS build plays a section
with ship, starfield, scrolling terrain, enemies and HUD.

Checks (clean builds, rc=0): title 14 green (two new: the game fork not
taken, Timer B never fired at M1); titlefault inverts (172,356 colour
bytes); game 7 green with the FRAME DIFFERENTIAL at frames 1/30/60/120/240
— framebuffer, twenty entity records and sixteen pens all IDENTICAL to the
shipped binary (300 frames, 3 lives, 917 ACIA interrupts, 9444 RMWs, 0
unknown-vector halts); gamefault (a mis-dispatched exit) reds the
framebuffer at every frame (748/32000) with pens/exit green; floppy 12
green on TOS 1.04 and 1.02.

Backend: hw_bset8/hw_bclr8/hw_and8 as real byte RMWs (2db68f6's contract
discharged); the video-base translation in the hardware door; the floppy
medium a flag, not a mode. Input: keyboard real end-to-end (IKBD -> $118
-> ikbd_acia_isr -> the polled byte); the joystick cannot be pressed
headless (Hatari swallows keys bound to its own joystick emulation), so
the frame differential pokes the ISR's byte on BOTH sides from inside a
wait; run.sh --joystick 1 is the human discharge.

Chief residual: the C attract raster ISR is too slow for its own interrupt
— Timer B every ~2 scanlines, 79 of 156 arrivals served, the colour bars
at half density. Open, recorded. Also unpinned: frame_loop_once's two
register parameters passed as 0 (D1's high byte indexes the fire-chance
table; derivation = the scroll blit's movem leftovers, STATUS has the
table); the entity table zeroed at the loop head on both sides (front-end
scratch — our attract loop exits early, ACIA starved by the raster ISR);
in-game tunes uncompared; the floppy game photographed, not diffed; the
RMW doors non-atomic; nothing on real hardware yet.

Review fixes: a zip-truncation false green in the frame sampler, the fatal
path restarting instead of stopping, a wedged MFP on an unknown vector, an
M1-only Timer B assertion reddening the game modes, artifact-name
collisions, two cross-language pins now read from the C.

events.title: control: MCP server mode for copperline-ctl
events.message:
control: MCP server mode for copperline-ctl

`copperline-ctl --mcp [--info FILE | --connect ADDR --token TOKEN]`
serves the control protocol as MCP tools over stdio, so an agent in
Claude Code, Cursor or any other MCP client drives a live machine
without a REPL. The protocol subset (initialize, ping, tools/list,
tools/call; newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, MCP 2025-06-18 with earlier
revisions echoed) is hand-rolled in control::mcp on std + serde_json,
no async runtime; the bin stays a shim.

control::bridge is the client behind it: one authenticated connection,
a reader thread that owns the receive side and routes replies by id,
and a bounded queue (1024, drops counted) for the event.* notifications
that arrive while a resume verb's reply is outstanding. It also
launches a headless emulator (`--control :0 --control-info TMP
--noaudio` plus the caller's flags) for the session_launch tool, waits
for the endpoint, and sends the process's output to a log file.

Bridge-owned tools: session_launch, session_attach, session_status,
session_close (one session at a time; an emulator this server launched
is shut down on close and on stdin EOF), events_next and events_drain.
The resume verbs take an extra wait_ms: a control-protocol resume
replies with the eventual stop event and MCP handles one request at a
time, so on expiry the bridge sends pause and returns the stop that
produces, marked bridge.paused_after_ms. capture_screenshot attaches
the PNG as an image content block so the model can look at the screen;
with no path the file is temporary. A control-protocol error is a tool
result with isError, never a transport error.

The ctl-bin feature now depends on control, since the bin links the
library's mcp module. headless.rs gains a test helper that serves one
session on a background thread, for the bridge tests that live on the
test thread.

One entry per control-protocol method, with a one-paragraph description,

call the protocol without reading the reference: the table the MCP

underscores (warp.get -> warp_get); the reverse mapping is a table
lookup, since method names such as run_until carry underscores of their

The tests pin the catalogue to exec::parse_method both ways: every
string-literal arm of the parser has an entry, every entry is a method
the parser or a driver answers, and every example parses without a
method-not-found or invalid-params error.

events.title: refactor(debug): decouple the MCP and UI debug surfaces from the Z80
events.message:
refactor(debug): decouple the MCP and UI debug surfaces from the Z80

The MCP server and the debugger's register panel reached past DebugService
into src/debug/z80 — z80Cpu() for port I/O and every trap, the Z80
disassembler for the disassemble/step/reset-trap output, and a register
panel hardcoded to AF/BC/DE/HL/IX/IY/IR/IM. Adding a second CPU family
(src/debug/m6502/ for a 6502 machine) would have meant editing hosts that
are supposed to be family-blind.

Grow DebugService the seams that were missing: getReg (mirroring setReg),
the family's own text formatting (stepLine/regsText/regsSummary),
returnStack/returnFromCall for the RET chain, and ports — null on a CPU
that memory-maps its hardware instead of having an I/O port space. Contract
DisasmRow.text as marker-free and add isTerminal so listings can still stop
at the end of a routine. The Z80 formatting bodies move verbatim out of
mcp/format.ts into debug/z80/service.ts, so every MCP output string is
byte-identical to before.

mcp/ now touches no Z80 module: traps run on getReg/setReg/returnFromCall,
port_in/port_out on debug.ports (reporting cleanly when a machine has
none), disassemble on debug.disasm. Trap.condC generalises to
cond {reg,value}; the cond_c tool input is unchanged. The BDOS decode keys
off getReg('C') !== null rather than a family check, so it self-disables on
a CPU without those registers. The lone remaining Z80 import is
frame_trace, which is Spectrum contention forensics behind activeSpectrum()
— commented as such.

The register panel becomes a Dynamic over Record<CpuFamily, Component>:
Z80Registers keeps the hand-laid-out layout, and a new GenericRegisters
renders whatever RegisterSnapshot reports, so a new family is debuggable in
the UI the day its DebugService lands.

tests/mcp/cpu-family-decoupling.test.ts drives the trap system and the
shared formatters with a fabricated non-Z80 service, so a Z80 assumption
creeping back into a host fails there rather than at porting time.

transport concerns in gdbstub::headless: RSP framing, ack mode, interrupt
polling, continue/step driving, and console delivery as O packets.
Monitor and loadseg output accumulates as console data on the core for
whichever driver delivers it.

The wire-test fixtures (the LoadSeg ROM program and the minimal RSP
client) move to gdbstub::testkit so a windowed driver's tests can reuse
them. No behaviour change: all existing wire tests are unchanged, plus a
new unit test that the core buffers monitor output as data.

events.title: La 0.6.1 ne se publiait pas : un apt-get install sans update dans linux-bionic
events.message:
La 0.6.1 ne se publiait pas : un apt-get install sans update dans linux-bionic

Le tag 0.6.1 a été posé mais la release n'est pas sortie : linux-bionic a échoué deux
fois de suite (donc pas un aléa), et publish dépendant des huit paquets, il a été
skipped.

Cause : l'index apt de l'image runner est figé à sa date de construction. Quand Ubuntu
publie une révision d'un paquet, l'ancienne SORT du pool et l'index périmé la demande
encore — libssh-gcrypt-4 0.10.6-2ubuntu0.4, dépendance transitive de ffmpeg, ignorée
par les trois miroirs puis 404. L'étape échouait avant d'avoir rien construit.

C'était le SEUL apt-get install du dépôt sans apt-get update devant lui : les six
autres (tests.yml ×4, oracle.yml, et le job linux-arm64 quinze lignes plus bas dans le
même fichier) l'ont toujours eu. Omission isolée, pas une pratique.

Le tag sera REPOSITIONNÉ sur ce commit : gh run rerun rejoue le workflow tel qu'il
existe AU TAG, donc relancer sans déplacer le tag rejouerait le même échec. Aucune
release n'avait été publiée depuis ce tag et aucun asset diffusé — le numéro n'est pas
brûlé, rien ne change sous les pieds d'un utilisateur. Consigné au CHANGELOG.

events.title: control: per-frame profile export (profile.start/stop/status)
events.message:
control: per-frame profile export (profile.start/stop/status)

A profiler view outside the emulator (the VS Code integration this
serves, a notebook, a script) needs what WinUAE's monitor-profile dump
carries, in an open format. profile.start brackets a capture the way
trace.start and waveform.start do: every committed emulated frame
appends one JSON object to profile.jsonl -- chip-bus ownership totals,
blitter busy/starve and blit records from the frame analyzer's trace,
the guest's uaelib idle colour clocks, the retired-instruction delta,
optionally one frame-boundary PC sample (no precise-loop cost), the
per-colour-clock owner grid RLE'd over the vAmiga-compatible codes, and
optionally a screenshot per frame through the same side-effect-free
renderer capture.screenshot uses. profile.stop writes a profile.json
summary (machine descriptor, options, owner names, the registered
uaelib resources); the streamed file survives a crash without it. The
capture self-stops at its frame budget (default 500, capped).

The collector is host-side state on the Emulator, polled from
step_frame's committed path, so both drivers feed it and run-ahead's
speculative frames never do; a reverse step or state load appears as a
reposition marker rather than a corrupt delta. The frame analyzer is
armed for the session (which suspends run-ahead, its existing rule) and
shared with the pane the way the heat map is: closing the pane hands
the arming to the capture, profile.stop re-arms for a pane still open,
and disarms otherwise only what the capture armed.

New chapter docs/debugger/profiling.md documents both file formats
field by field.

events.title: SCANSTEP defers the page carry into the crossing tail
events.message:
SCANSTEP defers the page carry into the crossing tail

INC bufp needed its carry propagating into bufp+1 on every step. It
does not: THE SCANLINE IS IN bufp, so a low byte that has just wrapped
to zero has `bufp AND 7` = 0 as well, and that step always takes the
crossing branch. The carry can be handled once in SprScanRow instead
of tested 335 times. bufp+1 is stale for the four instructions in
between and nothing there reads it.

3 cycles and 4 bytes off every step, against 2 cycles back on one step
in eight -- so the blit gets cheaper as well as smaller:

  bank 5       &BFFA -> &BD5E     668 B     (6 B free -> 674)
  bank 6       &BEF3 -> &BC63     656 B     (269 B free -> 925)
  code image   &2FFD -> &2FF1      12 B     (3 B free -> 15)

Bank 5 was down to six bytes and the code image to three, so this
lands on both of the binding constraints. The shorter macro also
compresses better: PARASPR and PARSPR2 lose ~90 B each on disc.

Orthogonal to the SCANSTEP tail folding held in reserve in
docs/ram-pass.md, which buys bytes by SPENDING cycles; the two compose.

Verified three ways, since this is not a mechanical change and the
listing-stream check cannot validate it on its own:

  - exhaustive: both sequences modelled at 6502 semantics over all
    65536 values of bufp (8192 row crossings, all 256 page wraps),
    comparing svp, bufp, A, carry and control flow. Zero mismatches.
  - structural: the patched 23187-instruction stream re-expands to the
    baseline 23855 exactly, so nothing else in any bank moved.
  - runtime: headless jsbeeb A/B over 400 frames of eight-way movement,
    both mapHX parities and all eight line values, deck and drSeed
    pinned -- final play buffer identical, 0 of 10240 bytes.

That pinning matters: TiBootPal seeds the starting deck from
USR_VIA_T1CL, so boot duration picks the deck, and any size change
moves it. Unpinned, the same baseline binary differs from itself by up
to 4799 buffer bytes.

events.title: Chasse round 5 : le save-state acceptait une AUTRE ROM, et le harnais annonçait des écritures tronquées comme réussies
events.message:
Chasse round 5 : le save-state acceptait une AUTRE ROM, et le harnais annonçait des écritures tronquées comme réussies

7 soumises, 3 retenues, 4 ÉCARTÉES (57 % de rejet). Et la lentille de régression n'a
RIEN trouvé contre le round 4 : la seule trouvaille visant la réécriture tactile et le
bornage du zoom borne a été réfutée. Premier lot de correctifs de la journée à
survivre intact à un passage adverse.

- Machine : loadState affirmait refuser tout état pris dans une autre config, mais
  identifiait la ROM par ses 2 SEULS octets de version TOS. Or tos104us/uk/fr/de/es
  portent toutes $0104, tos106* toutes $0106, etos192us et etos192fr aussi. La ROM
  étant le composant HORS-snapshot par excellence, un état repris sous une autre
  localisation passait tous les contrôles, et la RAM restaurée — vecteurs, piles,
  adresses de retour — désignait des adresses d'une AUTRE image : CPU figé, sans un
  mot. L'en-tête porte désormais un CRC32 de l'image ROM (v18 → v19). Vérifié : même
  ROM acceptée, etos192fr sur un état pris avec etos192us rejeté en nommant la cause.
- main_headless + Tracer : cinq écrivains annonçaient « réussi » sur une écriture
  tronquée. Seul writePpm contrôlait fwrite ET fclose ; --dump-at, la trace, le WAV,
  --midi-dump et --serial-dump jetaient leurs retours, contre l'invariant que le
  harnais s'est donné (« une SORTIE fichier a échoué → exit ≠ 0, jamais silencieux »).
  Reproduit sur un disque RAM de 2 Mo : avant, exit 0 et ligne de succès pour
  1 949 696 octets écrits sur 4 000 000 ; après, exit 1 et le compte exact. Idem pour
  la trace, Tracer::close() rendant maintenant un verdict.
  ⚠ Gravité RÉTROGRADÉE par le contradicteur, à juste titre : aucun runner du dépôt
  n'appelle --dump-at, et les consommateurs réels échouent du bon côté.
- InputCallbacks : le filtre borne F9/F10 était le SEUL filtre à condition volatile
  placé AVANT le bloc de relâchement, alors que F9/F10 ont un scancode ST ($43/$44)
  et que A.kiosk change au clavier. Un BREAK pouvait donc être avalé — touche collée
  côté ST. Filtre déplacé après le bloc ; F12, sans scancode ST, reste en amont.

Écartés : rétrécissement du zoom borne (prémisse fausse), --loopback hors fenêtre
(impact nul), aliasing RTC (garde amont ; le harnais testait Rtc.cpp compilé SEUL),
std::terminate du navigateur borne (site immunisé, prouvé). Quatre mécanismes exacts,
quatre impacts qui ne tiennent pas.

Scheduler et Bus rendent ZÉRO — deux sous-systèmes lourds jamais balayés, rien à en
tirer. Deux trouvailles de l'axe « outillage de test » écartées par le contradicteur :
mécanisme exact, impact démenti par une garde amont. Bon tri.

- main_web : le bundle PUBLIC démarrait le profil STE sur tos162uk.img, ROM que la
  purge du 2026-08-30 a sortie du bundle. adjustMachineForTos ne pouvant pas OUVRIR le
  fichier rendait la machine demandée telle quelle, loadTos échouait, et le repli
  chargeait EmuTOS 192 Ko — ROM ST-only — SANS rejouer la garde. Le défaut pointe
  désormais etos256us.img, réellement préchargée.
- StScreenView : le zoom de la borne ne se calculait que sur la HAUTEUR et AMPUTAIT
  l'image sur tout écran sous 16:10. Le chemin bureau posait pourtant la règle (« on
  préfère une bande haut/bas à une image amputée ») en supposant le cas absent en
  borne. La fonction reçoit cW et applique la même borne.
- Android : le déballage purge aussi les RELIQUES de la racine. Le sous-dossier data/
  déplaçait la destination, mais c'est le nom SOURCE qui est relatif : une relique
  masquait l'asset, et un fichier de 0 octet rendait l'app définitivement sans TOS, en

au même endroit — compteur lu après décrément ; mouvement d'un 2e doigt diffé contre la
position du 1er (l'écart ENTRE LES DOIGTS) ; id primaire jamais réarmé, figeant la

tap → clic gauche ; glissé → 179 px ; deux doigts sous trois formes → clic droit ;
pilote levé en premier → souris VIVANTE ; id recyclé → aucun saut (594 px avant) ;

Blitter+FDC, GEMDOS (handles/Pexec/DTA) et couverture du save-state : ZÉRO
trouvaille. La consigne « zéro est une excellente réponse » a été prise au mot, et

produit une trouvaille, correctement écartée (fidélité Hatari, catégorie exclue, et
impact démenti par la mesure du contradicteur).

Les deux seules trouvailles sont des RÉGRESSIONS SUR MES PROPRES CORRECTIFS du round
2, posés moins d'une heure plus tôt. Toutes deux prouvées par exécution, toutes deux
dans le frontend Android — celui que le build par défaut ne compile pas et que je
n'avais vérifié qu'au -fsyntax-only.

- Le clic droit à deux doigts était TOUJOURS inatteignable. J'avais levé un verrou
  (compteur de doigts lu après décrément) ; il y en avait un SECOND, indépendant :
  SDL_FINGERMOTION ne filtre pas fingerId et diffe contre un lastX/lastY UNIQUE, si
  bien que le premier mouvement d'un 2e doigt calculait l'ÉCART ENTRE LES DOIGTS —
  0,40 de travel pour un seuil de tap à 0,02, et 360 px de souris parasites. Le tap
  gauche tombait aussi dès qu'une paume touchait la dalle. Seul le doigt PRIMAIRE
  pilote désormais le mouvement.
- La réparation du déballage était un NO-OP. Sous Android, SDL_RWFromFile avec un nom
  RELATIF cherche d'abord dans le stockage interne et ne retombe sur l'AssetManager
  qu'en cas d'échec (SDL 2.30.9, le tag qu'épingle fetch_sdl.sh). Comme je déballais à
  la racine du stockage interne, la garde comparait le fichier à LUI-MÊME. Pire pour
  le cas que mon commit nommait — fichier de 0 octet — : want=0 rendait la condition
  fausse et sautait la branche en silence, message d'erreur compris. Le déballage vit
  dans un sous-dossier data/, ce qui rend au nom relatif son sens.

Vérifié par EXÉCUTION cette fois, après deux correctifs Android faux d'affilée : le
corps de handleTouch est EXTRAIT du fichier par script, pas retapé, et rejoué sur six
scénarios. Clic droit dans les quatre cas à deux doigts (travel 0,0004 au lieu de
0,400), glissé toujours à 179 px, tap simple toujours clic gauche.

⚠ Le correctif du déballage n'est PAS vérifié par exécution : il repose sur la
sémantique de résolution de chemin de SDL sous Android, qu'aucune machine ici ne peut
exécuter. Établi par lecture du SDL épinglé et par construction.

L'affirmation « le déballage se répare tout seul au lancement suivant », écrite dans
l'entrée du round 2, était fausse : elle est rectifiée là où elle a été écrite plutôt
qu'effacée.

faithful: BYTE-IDENTICAL to LCP_ORG.PRG (MD5 02900cfd)

Phase 2/3 complete -- the -DFAITHFUL build now reproduces the 1985
binary bit-for-bit (87832 bytes, text/data/bss/reloc all identical).

Data layout (globals.c and friends reordered to ROM declaration
order):
- mi_evi/mi_evcn(=9)/mi_nlp0(=100) are initialized data at 0x120fa;
  g_msmk block follows g_msmsa; env_val block follows psg_ntAc.
- Kept-engine sequencer state (mi_*/psg_* tables) gated out of
  FAITHFUL: none of it exists in the ROM's data segment.
- Minigame window at 0x12484: g_agwgm before g_agorw; g_aggpr and
  poker/wordpuzzle strings/tables are kept-only; g_pcbet/g_ppbet
  precede g_pcmon at 0x124a0 (pk_main's clears reference them).
- g_ptdsi is 12 shorts at 0x1358a (ping-pong + 0 terminator),
  g_obdea is [3]; g_cotbl is 19 shorts of {id, 0} pairs.
- g_dsb statically points at dsb_stor (reloc'd data 0x1214e).
- cs_mvIn sets lcp_face, not g_lcyof (ROM 0x8106 truth).

BSS layout:
- Kept-only commons gated (#ifndef FAITHFUL); ROM sizes restored
  under FAITHFUL: SPRITE_HW_SLOTS_ALLOC=8, pst_arr[4],
  dsb_stor[16256], pk_ch/pk_ph[26] (war hands), assets
  body_buf[20000]/pex_buf[12000].
- The ROM stores the loaded PEx frame pointer over pex_name's first
  4 bytes; FAITHFUL aliases pex_ptr onto _pex_nam via Alcyon's
  8-char symbol truncation (extern short *pex_namP).
- The 1985 linker's .comm allocation order matches no surviving
  linker (lo68/link68 hash-group, ALN.PRG sorts alphabetically,
  and it is neither first- nor last-mention order).  New
  tools/bss_remap.py pairs the byte-identical relocation streams

events.title: control: warp.get/warp.set, event.warp, the debug event family, debug.resources and debug.idle
events.message:
control: warp.get/warp.set, event.warp, the debug event family, debug.resources and debug.idle

A control-protocol client can now switch warp at runtime, and the guest
can through the uaelib trap. App::set_warp is the one place warp changes
for any reason other than a boot gate's own engage/finish: the hotkey and
menu, a client's warp.set, and the guest's warpmode() all land there.
Warp off is a complete action whoever asks (it drops a pending --run /
--warp-boot phase, releases any programmatic hold, and re-paces). Warp
on from a client or the guest records a hold that mutes live audio like
the boot gates do and keeps a gate's finish from re-pacing underneath
it; the manual toggle records no hold and keeps its audible behaviour.
One press of Cmd/Alt+W, power off, or the client disconnecting releases
a hold. A capture run is never re-paced, and a bridged physical drive
keeps the machine paced, which the reply's note reports.

The guest's request is drained once per committed frame in the burst
loop (breaking the burst so the new pacing applies at that frame) and
after frames retired outside it. The headless server, unpaced end to
end, accepts warp.set as a no-op with a note and reports the guest's
request as an event.

New surface: warp.get / warp.set {"on"} (source: none, manual, control,
guest, launch, boot, headless); `paced` and `warp` on status; event.warp,
sent without a subscription whenever warp changes for a reason other
than the client's own warp.set, delivered best effort so a full outbound
queue never disconnects the client; the `debug` event family
(event.debug, kind log or resource, with the device's drop count);
debug.resources and debug.idle (read-only, collectable); guest_idle_cck
on event.frame.
events.author: LinuxJedi

events.title: uaelib: WinUAE-compatible trap at $F0FF60 for guest warp, debug log and resources
events.message:
uaelib: WinUAE-compatible trap at $F0FF60 for guest warp, debug log and resources

WinUAE's boot ROM carries a service trap at rtarea+0xFF60 that guest
tools and cross-compiler templates call: uae-configuration, and the
vscode-amiga-debug template's warpmode(), KPrintF() and debug_*()
helpers, which test the first word at $F0FF60 for a JSR (0x4EB9) or the
A-line form (0xA00E) and call the address as a C function with the
function number first, result in D0. Copperline answers the same ABI at
the same address so that code works unchanged.

Copperline has no CPU trap hook, so the stub is 32 bytes of real 68k
code decoded by the CPU bus adapter next to Gayle: JSR to an inner
routine, MOVE.L A7 to a doorbell longword, MOVE.L of the host-latched
result into D0, RTS. The call is serviced inside the write that
completes the doorbell (a 68000 lands the high word first; the services
board's completes_long_reg rule), reading the arguments from the guest
stack at A7+8+4n through the CPU's own address mask. Only the function
number must be readable: trailing arguments beyond RAM read as 0, as a
caller with a short frame expects, rather than losing the call. A CDTV
extended ROM at $F00000 decodes first and hides the trap, as WinUAE's
rtarea relocation does there; $F00000 itself stays open bus.

Function 82 parses the "key value" line cfgfile_uaelib_modify would
(pairs, index -1, size 0 = NUL-terminated, out cleared) and latches only
`warp`; the template's cpu_speed and *_cycle_exact keys are accepted and
ignored, the core being always cycle-exact. Function 86 echoes the text
on stdout as a DBG: line (withheld while a run-ahead frame is
speculative, like Paula's serial sink) and queues it for the control
protocol. Function 88 keeps the template's resource registry (bitmaps,
palettes, copper lists from the 50-byte debug_resource struct) and turns
its idle markers into per-frame colour-clock accounting closed at
begin_new_beam_frame; overlay drawing and load/save are accepted no-ops.
Everything else returns 0.

The latches, pending warp request, bounded event queue, registry and
idle accounting are machine state in Bus (state version 73) so run-ahead
and rewind restore them with the guest that made them. `[emulation]
uaelib = false` leaves $F0FF60 floating; the launcher carries the key
across its round trip.

Cinq axes NEUFS — frontend GUI, frontends non-desktop, vidéo, IKBD, et une lentille
de RÉGRESSION braquée sur les correctifs du jour même. Réfutation à barre haute :
reproduire d'abord, déclarer ce qui a été exécuté, réfuter dans le doute. 8 soumises
→ 7 prouvées PAR EXÉCUTION, 0 par raisonnement seul, 1 écartée (catégorie « fidélité
Hatari », exclue d'office). Le round 1 avait laissé passer 9 sur 9 : le tri fonctionne.

Le plus important : la lentille de régression a trouvé un trou dans le correctif posé
ce matin. fixBools() avait été appliqué aux TROIS SITES NOMMÉS au lieu d'auditer, et
il en manquait un — le plus lourd : ar(reg) copie en bloc moira::Registers, qui porte
StatusRegister sr avec NEUF booléens, dont le bit SUPERVISEUR. L'audit est refait PAR
LE COMPILATEUR (static_assert temporaire) : 7 agrégats non-tableaux dans le dépôt, 4
avec booléens (tous traités), 3 sans. Liste écrite dans StateArchive.hpp.

- ConfigWindow/AppLoop : la case MT-32 de la page MIDI était un CONTRÔLE MORT — sa
  requête n'était consommée nulle part, la case se recochait seule. Prouvé par
  compilation (membre supprimé d'un en-tête hors dépôt → AppLoop compile encore).
- AppConfig : couper tous les canaux d'un appareil MIDI le rouvrait EN GRAND au
  redémarrage (masque vide écrit « 1-16 »). Jeton « none » ajouté ; la ligne illisible
  vaut toujours « tous les canaux », comme prévu à l'origine. 8 assertions neuves.
- Android : déballage des assets sans vérifier l'écriture, gardé par la seule
  existence du fichier — un TOS tronqué le restait POUR TOUJOURS. Lectures et
  écritures vérifiées, fichier partiel supprimé, garde sur la TAILLE.
- Android : un tap n'envoyait AUCUN clic (appui et relâchement dans la même trame ;
  le paquet souris n'est construit qu'à la VBL). Le remède existait deux fonctions
  plus haut — g_injectHold, le clic maintenu 4 trames — il n'était pas câblé.
- Android : le clic droit à deux doigts était structurellement inatteignable (le
  compteur lu valait toujours 1 après la garde). Remplacé par un maximum de geste.

Le contrôle syntaxique du frontend Android (SDL2 Homebrew + bouchon GLES2 généré) a
attrapé une erreur DE MOI : `std::vector<uint8_t> buf(size_t(sz));` est le most
vexing parse — déclaré comme une FONCTION. Le build par défaut ne compile pas ce
fichier ; sans ce contrôle, du code non compilable serait parti sur la branche.

  RELOC32/RELOC32SHORT legally targeting a LATER hunk always found
  segs[idx] NULL and failed the load. Every hunk is now allocated up
  front from the HUNK_HEADER size table, like real LoadSeg.
- The volume-name BSTR was not longword-padded, so any even-length
  partition name left the FileSysStartupMsg/DosEnvec that follow it
  odd-aligned -- an Address Error on 68000. M3's "DH0" dodged it by
  luck.
- ADNF_STARTPROC and the ConfigDev were passed for every partition;
  per expansion.doc both belong only to bootable ones (a non-bootable
  partition's handler starts on first reference).

guest/copperhf-test/gen_lsegfix.py generates lsegfix, a hand-crafted
248-byte three-hunk executable pinning the loader's edge cases byte-for-
byte: cross-hunk RELOC32 and a two-group RELOC32SHORT with its odd-word
pad, a DATA hunk whose header size exceeds its body (trailing-zero
truncation), and a BSS round trip -- its entry point folds three
relocated reads into magic 0x88911FD5 that only survives a fully correct
load. Because AmigaDOS starts a mounted DeviceNode's dn_SegList as a
real handler process on first reference, the fixture implements a
minimal DOS-packet loop and hands the magic back as a packet's Res2;
chftest_m6 verifies the FileSystem.resource entry, the seglist chain,
the magic via Lock("CHFM6:")'s IoErr(), and the DeviceNode patch, one
marker block each (blocks 512-515 of unit 0).

events.title: Chasse aux bugs : 9 défauts corrigés, dont un hors bornes qui ne visait que Windows
events.message:
Chasse aux bugs : 9 défauts corrigés, dont un hors bornes qui ne visait que Windows

Cinq axes de recherche en parallèle, puis un contradicteur par trouvaille chargé
de la RÉFUTER. Périmètre exclu d'emblée : une divergence de fidélité avec Hatari
n'est pas un bug, sauf plantage ou UB.

⚠ Zéro trouvaille sur neuf n'a été écartée — un étage adversarial qui ne rejette
jamais rien n'a pas fait son travail. HostPath et Fdc ont donc été re-vérifiées à
la main avant d'être crues ; toutes deux confirmées.

MAJEURS

- GemdosHd : le champ `slen` d'un .PRG n'était validé NULLE PART. Avec `long` sur
  32 bits (MinGW-w64, le paquet Windows livré depuis 0.5.1), un slen >= 0x80000000
  rendait l'index de relocation NÉGATIF — lecture à ~2 Gio sous le tampon, puis
  application d'une table de relocation fantaisiste à la RAM invitée. Sur LP64 la
  branche n'était jamais prise : le défaut ne se voyait que sur la plateforme qu'on
  ne lance jamais à la main. Arithmétique passée en int64_t.
- Acsi : un paquet UltraSatan 'USWr…' resté en vol détournait le WRITE(6) suivant —
  le secteur destiné à la carte SD écrasait les réglages, et l'écriture perdue était
  annoncée RÉUSSIE au pilote. Désarmé par emulateCommand() et clearData(). Vérifié
  que le chemin normal n'est pas touché.
- Acsi : unmountAll() gardait `path`, donc mountedPath() annonçait une carte montée
  sur un descripteur fermé et usatanApply() sautait le remontage.
- Machine : les gardes d'horloge ne contraignaient que l'ÉCART entre frameStart_ et
  frameEnd_ ; un couple décalé de façon COHÉRENTE les passait toutes et figeait
  l'émulateur. La fenêtre est ancrée sur l'horloge maître restaurée. Prouvé par
  forge : offsets retrouvés en diffant deux états, CRC recalculé, décalage 2^58 →
  état rejeté par nom, état légitime toujours accepté.
- MidiOutHost : panic() réinitialisait le décodeur depuis le thread principal
  pendant que le worker l'alimentait. parser_ n'appartient plus qu'au thread de
  livraison ; panic() pose une demande atomique honorée entre deux octets. Pas de
  verrou : en prendre un ferait attendre l'émulation sur un pilote MIDI.

MINEURS

- HostPath : le clamp de « .. » était le corps purement Unix d'Hatari — sous Windows
  il jetait la lettre de lecteur. Borné à la racine réelle.
- StateArchive : la normalisation des booléens ne couvrait que les bool passés SEULS,
  alors que son commentaire affirmait couvrir tout le projet. fixBools() rattrape les
  trois sites en bloc (Scc::Chn, Fpu, StePads) ; la portée réelle est écrite.
- DriveSound : init(), appelé deux fois, fuyait un ma_engine, son thread et deux
  ma_sound décodés.
- Fdc : conversion flottant→uint16_t hors domaine (UB) sur toute piste STX de moins
  de 25 octets d'image.

10 assertions neuves au palier fast. Palier full vert. Le dépôt n'a pas été modifié
par les agents (lecture seule imposée, git status vérifié vide).

events.title: copperhf: M5 -- asynchronous worker-thread I/O
events.message:
copperhf: M5 -- asynchronous worker-thread I/O

CHF_DOORBELL no longer executes a request inline. Doorbell time (emulation
thread) reads the IOStdReq, validates against board-cached unit state, and
copies write/SCSI payloads out of guest memory; a single FIFO worker
thread owning the backing files (Arc<Mutex<units>>, locked only per job)
does the real sector/CDB work; drain time (tick, emulation thread) copies
read data back in, writes io_Error/io_Actual, applies TD_EJECT's
media/counter bookkeeping, and pushes the completion.

Determinism is the invariant the whole shape hangs on: a request is due at
the first tick after its own doorbell write, and tick blocks on the
worker's result channel until everything already in flight has delivered
-- host disk speed costs wall-clock inside that block and can never move
which emulated tick a completion surfaces at. next_event_cck reports
in-flight work as immediately due so the sparse-wake scheduler always
reaches that tick. The doorbell-to-worker channel is bounded
(backpressure); deadlock-free because the worker never needs the emulation
thread to make progress.

Save states quiesce first: Emulator::save_state/save_state_bytes (now
&mut self, mirrored in the web crate's wrapper) drain the pipeline via
Bus::copperhf_quiesce before serializing, as do the CCP
copperhf.attach/copperhf.eject handlers before touching a unit -- a state
is always captured with nothing in flight (STATE_VERSION 71: the board
also gained a cached per-unit total_sectors). The browser build, which
has no threads, gets an inline-execution Worker variant with the same
FIFO contract.

events.title: review: redraw on the element's size, keep captures smooth, name the config file
events.message:
review: redraw on the element's size, keep captures smooth, name the config file

Copilot's review of the browser integer scaling (#614), three findings.

The layout redraw was keyed to the window's resize alone, but the
element changes size without one -- the CSS fullscreen fallback pinning
it to the viewport, the on-screen keyboard strip taking its share, the
shell's sidebar opening beside it -- and a paused or exactly reused
frame then left the backing store at its old size, CSS-stretched, so an
integer draw was no longer pixel-exact. A ResizeObserver on the canvas
now drives the same redraw, and the page's own fullscreen and keyboard
paths call it directly so they redraw at once rather than a frame later.

Screenshots were documented as untouched by the settings, but under
integer scaling a 60 Hz aperture presents at its own 428 woven rows and
the capture read that buffer. The capture wrapper that already drops a
drawn bezel around the buffer read drops integer scaling the same way,
so a capture keeps the smooth presentation's shape whatever the page
draws, as the desktop's captures keep the aspect's own shape whatever
its window draws.

The page fetches ./copperline.json; the guide called it config.json.
The shell hooks are also un-hidden explicitly on a capable bundle, so a
shell can ship #scaling and #autocrop hidden (the #devkeyboard pattern)
and never show a dead control ahead of the glue.

events.title: web: integer scaling and autocrop for the browser frontend
events.message:
web: integer scaling and autocrop for the browser frontend

The browser build stretched the presentation buffer over its 4:3
element and carried neither `[display] scaling = "integer"` nor the
autocrop presentation (#608). Both port onto the desktop's own
machinery rather than a JavaScript re-derivation.

The pure pieces move from window/present.rs into present_common.rs,
which the wasm build compiles: AutocropLatch, per_axis_fit and the
smooth fallback (now exact integer arithmetic, so a rect of the
viewport's own shape fills it to the pixel), and a new sub_rect_fit
holding the factors/destination core of display_src_layout. Two maps
follow the renderer's content envelope into the buffer the page draws:
FieldPlacement::content_rect onto the woven field, then
region_present_content_rect, the inverse of the deinterlacer's aperture
copy. buffer_layout answers a page's viewport with the rect to draw and
the whole-number factors, at the glass pixel shape read off the buffer
itself (buffer_glass_par: the page shows the buffer in a 4:3 element,
so a 668 x 540 PAL aperture states the desktop's 1.078 and an NTSC one
0.854). render_reusing_previous reports the fresh render's envelope
(ReuseRender) so the wrapper can latch it.

WebEmu gains set_scaling, set_autocrop, present_content_rect and
present_layout. The envelope is latched per frame in buffer pixels,
re-fed on an exactly reused frame so a static screen still lets a
smaller crop prove itself stable, and reset across a scan-geometry
change. Under integer scaling a 60 Hz aperture is presented at its own
woven rows rather than resampled onto the 50 Hz row count -- the
browser's equivalent of the desktop drawing its unresampled canvas --
so the factors carry every scan line as one exact block; a drawn bezel
suspends both modes, as on the desktop.

try.js draws the answer: the monitor passes take the picture sub-rect
through a u_src uniform mirroring crt.wgsl's src_rect (half-texel
clamp, whole texture by default), the 2D fallback scales a staging
canvas into a device-resolution store, pointer scaling follows the
layout, and fullscreen lets the element span the viewport while a mode
is on so a cropped picture can take a 16:9 screen's full height.
#scaling and #autocrop controls, remembered per browser and seeded from
copperline.json, hide on a bundle without present_layout.

Le smoke de paquet cesse de tester une copie inscriptible : 5e phase en lecture seule

Les quatre phases de smoke_package.sh ÉCRIVENT dans le paquet (captures, journaux,
dossier GEMDOS) : elles exigent donc un dossier EXTRAIT, et c'est ce qui les rendait
structurellement incapables d'exercer le support que l'utilisateur lance vraiment —
un .dmg monté ou un AppImage, tous deux en LECTURE SEULE. Le paquet qui
n'enregistrait aucun réglage (5 paquets sur 8, corrigé en ebd6a32) est passé
exactement par là : aucun palier ne pouvait le voir.

5e phase : retirer le droit d'écriture sur le paquet, relancer le binaire livré
depuis un répertoire EXTÉRIEUR, vérifier qu'il démarre en rendant une image et
qu'il n'a RIEN déposé dans son paquet. Elle ne prouve pas le réglage lui-même —
l'écriture de neost.cfg est le fait du binaire GUI, qu'aucune CI ne peut lancer
faute d'affichage, et c'est la garde unitaire de neost-selftest — mais la PROPRIÉTÉ
dont ce défaut n'était qu'un cas.

Vérifiée par mutation : une écriture délibérée dans le paquet est détectée. Les
permissions sont rendues même sur échec (le trap les rétablit AVANT de nettoyer,
sinon un arbre non supprimable resterait). Éprouvée sur le paquet fabriqué par la
CI — artefact NeoST-macOS-universal2-dmg du run de a500bd6, monté puis recopié :
les cinq phases passent.

chmod et non un vrai montage : celui-ci dépend de la plateforme (hdiutil, FUSE,
root) quand le retrait du droit d'écriture capture la même propriété partout. Sous
MSYS2 il est largement inopérant — la phase y est faible, et le script le DIT
plutôt que de le sous-entendre.

Trouvé en la posant : neost-headless résout disks/diskA.st par rapport au
RÉPERTOIRE COURANT, là où le frontend GUI résout par rapport au binaire. Lancé
d'ailleurs que du paquet, le headless perd la disquette et la capture sort uniforme
— la phase passe donc ses chemins en absolu, et le piège est écrit.

events.title: copperhf: M4 -- guest-side NSD/change-interrupt stub and end-to-end probe
events.message:
copperhf: M4 -- guest-side NSD/change-interrupt stub and end-to-end probe

BeginIO now answers three commands entirely from the ROM stub, since
they need guest pointers or guest state the host cannot provide:
NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY (NSDeviceQueryResult filled from a ROM-resident
supported-command table), TD_ADDCHANGEINT (request held on a per-device
pending list under Disable()), and TD_REMCHANGEINT (removes the pending
add, matched by io_Data, and replies it exactly once -- also when a
caller reuses the very same request block). The INT2 server drains
CHF_IRQ_STATUS bit 1 by calling device.c's chf_drain_changes(), which
acks CHF_CHANGED_MASK at the board and Cause()s each pending change
interrupt whose unit the mask names; is_Data now carries the device
pointer, with dev_BoardBase's offset shared to the asm via
device_layout.h and a _Static_assert.

Two more hard-won toolchain findings documented in-source: recovering a
struct pointer by subtracting a field offset from the field's VALUE
(not its address) is nonsense arithmetic that only crashed the path
that needed it, and this GCC target silently ignores an __asm("a5")
parameter binding on an ordinary internal function (callee-saved
register), falling back to stack-passing -- so chf_drain_changes takes
its argument on the stack, pushed explicitly by int_handler.s.

guest/copperhf-test/chftest_m4 exercises the full surface over an AROS
autoboot (tests/copperhf_m4_guest.rs, marker block per subtest):
NSCMD_DEVICEQUERY, TD_CHANGENUM/CHANGESTATE/PROTSTATUS, TD_READ64,
HD_SCSICMD INQUIRY and READ CAPACITY(10), and the ADDCHANGEINT ->
TD_EJECT -> software-interrupt -> REMCHANGEINT story end to end.

Protocol version 2 (copperhf_board.h): CHF_CHANGED_MASK/CHF_CHANGED_ACK
(per-unit media-change bits), CHF_UNIT_MEDIA (media present, distinct
from the now slot-configured CHF_UNIT_PRESENT so eject behaves like
pulling a disk from a still-attached drive), and CHF_IRQ_STATUS bit 1
gating INT2 alongside completions.

New host-side commands: TD_CHANGENUM/CHANGESTATE/PROTSTATUS/EJECT, the
TD64 family and its NSCMD twins (io_Actual is io_HighOffset on entry, no
4 GiB ceiling), and HD_SCSICMD answering CDBs against the unit's image
through src/scsi.rs::ScsiDisk (extended with READ/WRITE 12/16, READ
CAPACITY 16, MODE SENSE/SELECT 10, and a from_disk/sense_bytes reuse
surface), with SCSIF_AUTOSENSE sense fill and HFERR_BadStatus reported
in io_Error on a non-GOOD scsi_Status per scsi.device's contract. Plain
32-bit CMD_READ/WRITE/TD_FORMAT past 4 GiB now fail IOERR_BADADDRESS
(no wrap); I/O against a media-absent unit fails TDERR_DiskChanged.

Hot attach/detach: CCP methods copperhf.attach/copperhf.eject
(docs/debugger/control.md), sharing one path with the guest's TD_EJECT.
Boot-time config attach deliberately bumps neither the change counter
nor the changed mask -- an M1-M3 guest never acks the mask, so flagging
the initial attach latched CHF_IRQ_STATUS bit 1 forever and INT2-stormed
the whole boot; a unit that never changed also must read TD_CHANGENUM 0.

events.title: autocrop: crop programmable multisync scans through their own sync-anchored window
events.message:
autocrop: crop programmable multisync scans through their own sync-anchored window

Autocrop derived its envelope from the standard 15 kHz presentation and
suspended itself for programmable (VARBEAMEN) scans, so a DblPAL or
Multiscan Workbench, or a 31 kHz console, never got the crop-and-refit
(#607). The renderer's per-line display-window envelope was already
computed for those frames; only the presentation threw it away.

post_process_rendered_field now returns the FieldPlacement it applied --
a standard field's centring and recentring shifts, or a programmable
scan's sync-anchored column resample and the vertical window's skipped
and padded rows -- and FieldPlacement::content_rect follows the envelope
through it onto the presentation buffer. The programmable columns are
found by scanning the glass against the resamplers' own taps
(screenshot::stretch_rows_x_source, stretch_rows_x_window_source,
factored out of the resamplers), so a partly blended edge column counts
and the crop cannot disagree with the pixels; the deinterlacer's row
count says whether the placed rows were woven (LACE) or passed through at
native height. The renderer trims the envelope's edges by the
programmable blanking windows (VBSTRT/VBSTOP, HBSTRT/HBSTOP) and the
frame end, with the predicates apply_programmable_blanking paints with:
Kickstart leaves the display window open across the blank on these
modes, and those rows are black to the eye. canvas_content_rect folds a
35 ns canvas onto the canvas columns, so super-hi-res programmable scans
crop too.

App::display_canvas_src drops the programmable and canvas-width
suspensions (display_canvas_src_for is the same decision pure of the
live globals); a programmable scan keeps the uniform multiple under
per-axis integer scaling, since its rows are not woven pairs for a
per-line factor to step by, and a bezel or RTG scanout still suspends.
The autocrop latch resets across a scan-geometry change (programmable
flag, rows, width), the way the deinterlacer drops its weave history.
COPPERLINE_DIAG_AUTOCROP's layout line names the scan instead of the
two suspensions.

events.title: Make the whole WERNER.PRG byte-identical to the original
events.message:
Make the whole WERNER.PRG byte-identical to the original

`make link` now produces a WERNER.PRG that is byte-for-byte identical
to Disk_1/WERNER.PRG -- all 103577 bytes, header through relocation
table -- and verifies it.  Getting there required reconstructing the
entire link, not just the C code:

Toolchain forensics
- The game was NOT built with the Atari Developer's Kit: the startup
  code, vdibind, aesbind, gemlib and osbind come from the May 1985
  Alcyon distribution (Compiler/Alcyon/alcyon2), with the DK's LIBF.
  These are vendored in werner-c/vendor/.
- The original link order is werner, joystick, meiern, meiern2, nebel,
  bau, auto, panik, sound -- with no data.o: the palettes and prompt
  strings are initialized globals inside werner.c (data.c is gone).
- lo68's common-symbol allocator hashes NAMES: the era behavior is
  bucket = (byte-sum >> 1) & 31, which the modern port changed to
  sum & 31.  tools/lo68era.c is the port with the era hash restored;
  the link script builds and uses it.

Reconstruction fixes surfaced by full-relocation comparison (cmpfn's
bsr/operand masking had hidden these):
- pbobj calls pc2ini2/pc3set2 and pc5set calls pc3set2 (wrong callees).
- ps0done plays sfxp12, not sfxd12.
- The original's VDI attribute calls are vsl_color/vst_color in many
  places our code said vsf_interior/vsf_style/vsm_color.
- The car position is a struct (rcar.x/.y) and the sprite size two
  plain WORDs (rsprw/rsprh) -- c168 canonicalizes struct-member
  operands in sums, which fixes dozens of operand orders; same story
  for pu5/pzc0 size pairs, plus a handful of genuine operand swaps.
- Variables the original SHARES across games are now shared again:
  a0st/pvc1st, a0x/pvc1x, paxy/ahxy, papalsv/purgb.
- Reproduced original latent bugs: auto.c's score writes clobber the
  first word of svrobot() (symbol collision the era linker resolved
  silently), and the acarfi[6..8] init runs into palnini[].
- joytime/joyscan/ahfdt and sbtprev are zero-initialized DATA, several
  arrays get their original sizes, "auto0 .pc1"/"000000.  km" string
  fixes, and menuscr's Knopf prompt has three leading blanks.

BSS layout: all commons are declared in one ordered block in werner.c,
and ~200 globals carry hash-tuned names (NAMES.md maps them to their
descriptive forms).  gap* entries are original variables nothing
references.

Verified: make -> make link reports byte-identical from a clean tree;
cmpfn.py still shows 238/238 EXACT.

events.title: scaling: draw the tv aspect per axis from the square canvas under integer scaling
events.message:
scaling: draw the tv aspect per axis from the square canvas under integer scaling

Integer scaling of the default tv aspect scaled a canvas already resampled
onto 537 rows for the 4:3 shape: crisp blocks of a resampled picture, with
square + integer the only pixel-exact pairing (#606). Integer scaling now
presents from the unresampled canvas under either aspect
(video::square_canvas), and under the tv aspect the scaler pass draws it
with a separate whole-number factor per axis -- surface pixels per hi-res
column and per field line -- chosen to approximate the shape of a
square-canvas pixel on the 4:3 glass, read back from the tv canvas's own
resample (glass_par: PAL 1.078, NTSC 0.854; the whole field over the glass
for full overscan). per_axis_fit takes the tallest fit whose shape is
within 11/10 of the glass's, then the closest, and the closest shape at
the largest size when none is inside the tolerance. Counting per field
line rather than per woven row is what reaches 4:5 on a 1080p display:
a non-interlaced line's two woven rows are identical, so an odd count per
line still lands as one exact block, and every display rect starts on a
woven pair, so the scaler's sample centres never sit on a line boundary.
Square + integer keeps its uniform multiple.

The window canvas (present_height) follows the rule; captures take the
aspect's own height (capture_height), so screenshots, recordings and
headless shots never change shape with a window setting. A bezel keeps
the tv canvas -- its opening resamples the whole glass -- and the bezel,
scaling and pixel-aspect toggles share one canvas-change path
(resync_canvas_geometry); the launcher adopts the bezel before the
scaling so the canvas moves at most once. DisplaySrc generalises the
autocrop sub-rect and the two modes compose: autocrop supplies the rect,
the fit the factors. COPPERLINE_DIAG_AUTOCROP names the mode, the factors
and the shape.

elle n'exécute pas. Et l'outil qui aurait pu répondre ne le pouvait pas — le
perfbench garde des RATIOS, machine-indépendants par construction.

`run_perfbench.py --budget` rend le facteur temps réel ABSOLU (trames/s ÷
balayage lu sur la sortie, jamais supposé) ; `NEOST_HEADLESS=` le pointe sur le
binaire LIVRÉ ; la charge de la machine entre dans la config relevée.
`docs/HW_VALIDATION.md` tient le registre par cible, protocole en cinq pas.

Passe macOS arm64 sur le .dmg 0.6 PUBLIÉ : somme conforme, contenu 100 % libre
vérifié sur le paquet servi, palier 0 de signature confirmé (syspolicy_check ne
relève plus que « Notary Ticket Missing »), binaire livré à ×26,9 temps réel au
pire — l'universal2 ne coûte rien de mesurable.

Ce qu'elle a trouvé : le paquet ne pouvait JAMAIS enregistrer sa configuration.
Support en lecture seule → la règle A36 retombe correctement sur
~/.config/neost/, mais RIEN ne créait ce dossier. Prouvé par expérience (sans le
dossier → échec ; dossier créé à la main, rien d'autre changé → config écrite).
Portée réelle : 5 paquets sur 8 — aucun ne livre de neost.cfg portable, donc le
.dmg ET les quatre AppImage. Le message d'erreur nomme désormais le chemin VOULU,
son écrasement par le repli le rendait illisible.

La CI ne pouvait pas l'attraper : les six smoke-tests tournent sur un dossier
EXTRAIT, donc inscriptible — le support de livraison réel n'est jamais exercé.
Garde posée dans neost-selftest (AppConfig.cpp y entre, aucune dépendance ImGui)
et vérifiée par mutation : correctif retiré → 2 FAIL. Le test d'A36 était PUR, il
prouvait quel chemin la règle retient, jamais qu'on sache y écrire.

Pas 1 et 2 soldés sur les HUIT paquets (aucun matériel requis) : sommes 8/8,
aucune ROM Atari nulle part — la promesse « 100 % libre » passe du script qui
fabrique aux artefacts servis. tools/appimage_ls.py rend les AppImage
inspectables sans unsquashfs.

Non-conformité GPL trouvée et corrigée : le paquet web ne portait AUCUNE licence,
alors qu'il est distribué deux fois (zip de release + GitHub Pages). Le job wasm
était l'un des deux sans garde ; il pose et vérifie désormais les trois textes.
Huit jobs distincts gardent les licences — ce que RELEASE.md affirmait déjà alors
qu'ils n'étaient que sept. Le job android est sain (set -euo pipefail), rien ajouté.

Vérifié statiquement sans les cibles : Windows n'a aucune DLL manquante (table
d'importation PE = DLL système seulement), et le plancher glibc du Pi était déjà
gardé en CI.

Palier full vert, poste au repos.

events.title: copperhf: M3 -- boot-ROM RDSK/PART mounter with FSHD/LSEG loading
events.message:
copperhf: M3 -- boot-ROM RDSK/PART mounter with FSHD/LSEG loading

guest/copperhf/mounter.c walks each present unit's RDB at rt_Init time
over a polled doorbell/completion protocol (IRQ still disabled, so the
INT2 server never sees the mounter's portless requests), hand-builds a
DeviceNode + FileSysStartupMsg + DosEnvec per PART block (honoring
PBFF_NOMOUNT/PBFF_BOOTABLE), and adds it via AddBootNode on V36+ or the
hand-built eb_MountList BootNode / AddDosNode fallback on V34, mirroring
guest/services/handler.c's proven recipe. rdb_FileSysHeaderList is
walked too: a matching FSHD's LSEG chain is loaded through a minimal
streaming hunk loader (CODE/DATA/BSS, RELOC32 long and short forms,
SYMBOL/DEBUG skipped) into FileSystem.resource, created if absent, and
DeviceNodes are patched per fse_PatchFlags. entry.s's da_BootPoint now
boots dos.library on V34 instead of declining, same recipe as
guest/services/entry.s.

Two new hard-won toolchain pitfalls documented at the site: GCC's loop
idiom recognition emits memset/memcpy calls -nostdlib cannot link
(-fno-builtin-* / -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns), and strict
aliasing let -Os dead-store-eliminate the IORequest field writes behind
recast byte pointers outright -- the doorbell rang with io_Command
never written, verified by disassembly -- so those stores are volatile
now and the ROM builds with -fno-strict-aliasing.

events.title: A scrolling pass never puts the player in tranche B
events.message:
A scrolling pass never puts the player in tranche B

KC: the player judders when the screen scrolls. The trace showed the
position data clean - plyX, posX and slot 0's unit advancing in
lockstep - so it was temporal: the window-B repaint classes could
force the player's component into tranche B, and a tranche-B image is
one field behind the scroll. World-anchored, that is invisible on a
droid; the player is held against the screen frame by the view-follow,
so he oscillated centre-minus-a-step / centre at 25 Hz. The old "the
player is always in the window drawn first" line was this exact
guarantee, and the forcing had broken it - constantly, because the
tile tests ignored rows, so any door in the same columns forced him.

Both fixes live in the banks, no code-image cost. SprTileHit now
tests the tile's four char rows against the slot's padded row span
(row-blindness was harmless when all forcing went to tranche A; it
is not now). And SprScanCls flags a view-moved pass (mapHX/posY vs
oldHX/oldPosY, valid since ApplyMove has run) as bit 2 of sprCls[0];
SprAssignTr masks the class bits off satForce and refuses the split
when the forced-B component is the player's and the view moved.
Standing still keeps the split - recharging on a pad, the case the
window-B repaint was built for, lags no scroll.

Verified in jsbeeb: sprTr[0] never 1 while the view moves; 120 of
128 passes still split on a heavy diagonal leg through doors (5
refusals, drawn whole); timing histograms unchanged from step 4.
The branch-range fix in sat_asg is the player-refuse block pushing
sat_asgnext past 127.

events.title: review: WORDEQUAL is the comparator's live level, not a latch held until read
events.message:
review: WORDEQUAL is the comparator's live level, not a latch held until read

Paula's DSKBYTR bit 12 is the DSKSYNC comparator output itself: true for
the one cell in which the shift register equals DSKSYNC and gone once the
next cell shifts in, so a polling loop can miss a match and wait a
revolution for the next, as Copylock's does on real hardware. Only DSKBYT
is reset by a read; the DSKSYNC interrupt is the latched edge of the same
comparator and stays separate. Drop the event latch the register still
carried, and make the tests and the internals documentation say so,
including a match that has shifted out before the first read.

events.title: Plus aucune référence oracle non re-dérivable : spec512_bands s'ancre sur la VBL par `stop`
events.message:
Plus aucune référence oracle non re-dérivable : spec512_bands s'ancre sur la VBL par `stop`

Dernière astérisque d'A11. Hatari ne se reproduisait pas lui-même sur ce disque
(deux runs → deux jeux de phases disjoints, 2 460 px de la référence au mieux) :
son RNG de boot décale le démarrage du programme de quelques cycles, et une
resynchro par scrutation de $FF8207 ne se recale qu'à ~20 cycles près — sur
l'étalon dont TOUT l'objet est de rendre un cycle CPU visible. oracle_scan n'y
pouvait rien, le décalage est sous-trame.

Le remède est dans le PROGRAMME. La séquence vit dans le handler de VBL et le
programme attend en `stop #$2300` : latence d'exception FIXE, là où un `bra.s`
d'attente (l'ancrage de freq_switch, suffisant là-bas) prend l'interruption à une
frontière d'instruction, jusqu'à 10 cycles de jitter. Mesuré : 2 runs Hatari →
mêmes 3 phases ; NeoST rend ces mêmes 3 images (matrice 3×3, zéro sur la
diagonale). L'image cycle sur 5 trames — le handler démarre 4 cycles plus tard à
chaque trame (première écriture à cyc 138, 142, 146…) — identiquement chez
Hatari : c'est le programme, et oracle_scan retient la trame identique.

Référence régénérée (trame nominale, décalage 0, une image comparée) ; un run
Hatari FRAIS la retrouve à l'identique (--oracle-check). L'exclusion
oracle_check: false est levée, le mécanisme reste. Le job hebdomadaire confronte
désormais 7 étalons, tous les oracles sur ROM libre — et le run CI précédent,
avec nocooper dans le périmètre, est passé (11 min 38).

Règle retenue pour tout étalon généré dont la mesure est sous-ligne : ancrer sur
la VBL par `stop`, jamais sur le compteur vidéo (docs/HATARI_AUTOMATION.md).

Paliers fast et full verts, aucune étape sautée.

events.title: L'oracle Hatari se pilote au clavier à la VBL près, perd sa LED, et ffmpeg cesse de renuméroter ses trames
events.message:
L'oracle Hatari se pilote au clavier à la VBL près, perd sa LED, et ffmpeg cesse de renuméroter ses trames

Trois verrous d'outillage réglés à la source, dans le mécanisme d'Hatari lui-même.

APPUI TOUCHE, PRÉCIS À LA VBL. HATARI_ORACLE_KEYS="down:up:scancode …" (manifeste :
oracle_keys). `--parse` pose un point d'arrêt `b VBL = N :once` par événement ; Hatari
s'y GÈLE sur le prompt de son débogueur, dont stdin est une fifo tenue par le script ;
on pousse `hatari-event keydown|keyup <scancode>` dans la fifo de contrôle puis « c »
— l'événement est lu par la boucle SDL au tour suivant (sdl/gui_event.c:133 →
Control_CheckUpdates), appliqué à la VBL N+1, déterministe, sans une seule attente
horloge. Tout prompt reçoit un « c », même inattendu.

Deux affirmations de docs/HATARI_AUTOMATION.md étaient FAUSSES et coûtaient cher :
`--cmd-fifo` ne désactive PAS le fast-forward (562,9 VBL/s avec, 565,0 sans, mesuré) —
la chorégraphie « temps réel + sleep 30 s » n'avait pas lieu d'être ; et la fifo ne
bloque pas à l'ouverture (O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK, control.c:553). En revanche un writer
laissé connecté fait rendre EAGAIN à chaque lecture, que Hatari journalise à chaque
trame : le writer n'est ouvert que le temps d'un message.

Vérifié sur No Cooper, l'oracle « posé à la main » du premier jour d'A11 : espace
tenue VBL 900→960, oracle_fastfdc ajouté (il manquait, timelines désalignées), trame
6929 retenue (+139), IDENTIQUE à la capture NeoST et à la référence commise.
nocooper sort de la liste des non re-dérivables ; le job hebdomadaire confronte
6 étalons.

LA LED DISQUETTE n'est pas une fatalité : --drive-led off, zone vérifiée entièrement
noire. Le masque buffer_noled reste tant que des références commises la portent (note
posée dans compare_screenshot.py).

FFMPEG RENUMÉROTAIT LES TRAMES. Hatari encode chaque image PNG en pal8 dès qu'elle
tient en 256 couleurs, rgb24 sinon — le format change sans arrêt le long de l'AVI
(nocooper : 0-2 pal8, 3 rgb24, 4-408 pal8, 409 rgb24…). À chaque changement ffmpeg
reconstruit son graphe et le `n` de select REPART DE ZÉRO : « frame 1000 hors de
l'AVI » alors que ffprobe en compte 1 100, et une fenêtre de scan silencieusement
décalée. -reinit_filter 0 (+ -pix_fmt rgb24) sur les deux extractions ; vérifié
trame seule ≡ trame de fenêtre au même n.

Aussi : HATARI_ORACLE_KEEP=1 conserve AVI et journal (c'est ce qui a permis de voir
les deux points précédents) ; le script est écrit pour le bash 3.2 de macOS (pas de
mapfile), celui que run_etalons.py invoque.

Ce commit porte aussi le manifeste, le TODO et le CHANGELOG du chantier V3 qui le
précède (freq_switch posé, glue_selftest_attr passé à =0, décompte 18 étalons).

Paliers fast et full verts, aucune étape sautée.

events.title: V3 : l'attribution de ligne à la grille réelle devient le défaut — le verrou ne faisait rien
events.message:
V3 : l'attribution de ligne à la grille réelle devient le défaut — le verrou ne faisait rien

Dernier reste à valeur élevée du front « précision cycle ». NEOST_LINELEN_ATTR
(attribution des écritures freq/res à la grille RÉELLE des débuts de ligne) était
OFF depuis toujours faute d'étalon qui bascule la fréquence en cours de trame ;
« le palier full est vert avec le verrou armé » se lisait comme une non-régression.
C'était pire : le verrou n'avait aucun effet.

L'EXHIBITEUR — tools/make_freqswitch_test.py → étalon `freq_switch` (généré, ROM
libre). Une ligne 60 Hz fait 508 cycles, pas 512 : la grille réelle dérive de 4
cycles par ligne, et il faut PLUS D'UNE LIGNE ENTIÈRE de dérive (≥ 128 lignes) pour
que grille fixe et grille réelle désignent des lignes différentes — c'est pourquoi
aucune démo du dépôt ne l'exhibait (bascules ponctuelles). Plage de 140 lignes 60 Hz
puis 8 bascules alternées, écran à l'index 1 pour lire la largeur de chaque ligne.
Ancré sur la VBL : se resynchroniser sur le compteur vidéo (le bon choix de
make_spec512_test.py) est faux ici — le compteur dépend de la fréquence, donc de ce
qu'on mesure ; dès 2 lignes de 60 Hz l'image changeait de trame en trame. Dans le
handler de VBL, 12 trames NeoST et 17 trames Hatari sortent md5-identiques.

CE QU'IL A MONTRÉ D'ABORD : image bit-identique dans les deux positions du verrou,
alors que l'instrumentation [varline] annonçait 17 écritures sur 18 mal attribuées.
Le diagnostic [attr] (gardé, gated NEOST_VARLINE_TRACE) a dit lequel des deux modèles
tournait : sous le verrou, seul le CYCLE bougeait (+4), jamais la LIGNE. Cause : la
longueur de ligne retombait à cpl à CHAQUE ligne du replay et n'était corrigée que par
un Freq_match tombant SUR la ligne — 140 lignes de 60 Hz sans écriture restaient à 512.

LE CORRECTIF : la longueur de base de chaque ligne est celle qu'implique l'état
freq/res au début de ligne (glueLineLenFor ≙ Video_StartHBL → nCyclesPerLine chez
Hatari), les Freq_match la raffinent ensuite comme avant — replay et chemin live.

LA PREUVE, AU NIVEAU DE LA GLUE : trace `video_sync` d'Hatari contre [attr]. Même
cycle-trame des deux côtés, et les 18 écritures de la trame attribuées à la même
ligne ET au même cycle — 169/336 174/268 179/224 184/156 189/112 194/44 199/4
203/444 208/400 213/332 218/288 223/220 228/176 233/108 238/64 242/508 247/468. La
grille fixe en manque 17 sur 18, d'une à deux lignes. Le pixel n'était pas juge :
Hatari rend les lignes 60 Hz d'une trame 50 Hz avec l'artefact « left+2 » tranché en
A40 (ligne entière à l'index 8) — 56 % d'écart image sans rapport avec
l'attribution ; d'où ref_kind: snapshot, preuve consignée au ref_note.

PROMOTION : défaut ON (ShifterInternal.hpp, env_locks.json, bandeaux). Palier pixel
entier à 0 px avec le canal armé — rien d'existant ne bouge, seul l'exhibiteur le
voit. NEOST_LINELEN_ATTR=0 fait rougir freq_switch à 16 408 px (garde vérifiée par
mutation). Banc de débit dans la tolérance après avoir hissé un getenv par écriture
que le premier jet du diagnostic laissait dans la boucle (+53,6 % sur blitter/boot,
revenu à +0,0 / +4,2 %).

Le manifeste (entrée freq_switch, glue_selftest_attr passé à =0 pour garder l'A/B
exécutable), le TODO et le CHANGELOG suivent dans le commit d'outillage oracle, qui
partage ces fichiers.

events.title: The movement pipeline: keys and walls compute for the NEXT pass
events.message:
The movement pipeline: keys and walls compute for the NEXT pass

Step 4 of the audit, the shape raster-timing.md already sketched:
ReadKeys/CalcSpeed/CheckWalls - and the ESCAPE test with them - leave
window A for the display period, sharing DroidsUpdate's overPhase
gate, and compute the speeds the NEXT pass's ApplyMove applies.
ApplyMove alone stays above the erase (the scroll depends on it), and
since it has already run when CheckWalls executes, the clip is taken
against exactly the position the next move starts from. Cost: one
pass (40 ms) of input latency, the pipeline the droid AI already
rides.

ReframeView zeroes xSpd/ySpd: every way back to the deck passes
through it, and the pipelined speeds were clipped at a position a
transfer, a lift or a deck load may have moved the player away from.
The 001 screen's held-back reframe means the zeroing also runs before
the first ApplyMove of a game, so uninitialised speeds can never
apply on real hardware.

Measured in jsbeeb: DoRedraws entered 4,727 cycles into the pass
against ~13,100 - the level draw's latch budget nearly doubles to
~17,300 cycles - and on a fast diagonal leg 75% of passes now enter
it inside the first 8,192 cycles. The band remains the one tenant
that can overrun window A (~23% of band-crossing passes, by ~3k
where it was ~11k), and it is latch-bound like the columns.
Verified: movement/walls/doors unchanged in play, ESCAPE runs the
full death-wash-highscore-title chain from its new home, split
127/129, all pass starts aligned, 25.0 Hz. Net +1 byte of code
image; code_end &2FFD.

events.title: floppy: frame DSKBYTR from the read shifter and model IPF cell-density profiles
events.message:
floppy: frame DSKBYTR from the read shifter and model IPF cell-density profiles

Rob Northen Copylock reads its key sector byte by byte through DSKBYTR:
it waits for WORDEQUAL, collects the bytes while counting how often it
polled between them, rejects the read unless the first two bytes are the
MFM of the sector's first data byte, then times a second sector against
the first and demands the few-per-cent difference the master put between
them. On an IPF both halves of that went wrong (issue #610, Lemmings
freezing black before the disk 2 prompt):

- DSKBYTR served bytes from the track's own byte grid, but Paula frames
  them with the bit counter a WORDSYNC match resets. Syncs on an IPF or
  flux track sit at any bit phase (this one at phase 1), so the bytes came
  out shifted and Copylock retried every revolution forever. Synthesised
  AmigaDOS tracks hid it because their syncs are word-aligned. DSKBYTR's
  byte, DSKBYT and WORDEQUAL now come from the read shifter, which also
  reframes on every WORDSYNC match with no transfer running: Copylock arms
  a zero-length read, which completes on arming, and relies on the
  free-running comparator from then on.

- The density models of an IPF track (IMGE density 3..9) decoded with
  uniform 2 us cells, so the timing check computed 0% and handed the game
  a wrong key: the disk 2 prompt appeared and the game crashed to garbage
  once disk 2 loaded. The decoder now emits the CAPS library's own
  profiles as per-mille cell-time spans (Copylock Amiga slows and speeds
  blocks 4-6 by -5.5/-0.5/+4.5% from the preceding gap through the block,
  the newer scheme blocks 0-2; Copylock ST, Speedlock and the Brierley
  models weight single blocks; the Brierley density-key model takes a bit
  per block from block 0's gap value), RawMfm carries them, and TrackRev
  scales each cell's clock by its run's weight. Uniform tracks keep the
  exact old arithmetic. Weak bits remain the one IPF modelling gap.

The DSKBYTR grid-position fields leave the floppy state and TrackRev gains
the profile, so the save-state version is bumped. Tests that pinned the
grid model move to hardware semantics; new ones cover off-grid sync
framing, Copylock's zero-length-arm idiom, the TrackRev density
arithmetic and the IPF profile generation.

Fixes #610.

events.title: Door repaints join the animated tiles in window B
events.message:
Door repaints join the animated tiles in window B

The second half of getting the level draw's tenants out of window A:
a moving door's tile repaint is a single-tile write exactly like the
recharge pad's, so it takes the same class-B path. DoorsUpdate's
STATE half stays in window A - it writes doorDef, which the same
pass's band and column draws read, and no buffer - and the repaint
half (du_draw, now DoorAnimPaint) runs from the window-B block on a
split pass, between tranche B's restore and its draw, with AnimPaint
as its tail so one call serves doors and tiles in both windows. On a
whole pass du_gate falls straight through and the old window-A order
holds. SprHitsDraw classes doors as bit 1 now; a sprite standing in
a moving doorway is forced into tranche B.

Columns do NOT move to window B, and the raster-timing step-3 sketch
that said they could is withdrawn in the docs: the CRTC start latched
at fire 1 shows the new viewport in the SAME field's display, so a
column drawn in window B would display one field of stale buffer at
the exposed edge - and deferring the latch instead makes the player
oscillate against the viewport by the scroll delta at 25 Hz. The
band and columns stay latch-bound in window A.

Verified in jsbeeb: the buffer oracle reads 0 of 10,240 against
RedrawAll (diagonal scroll, line=7, mapHX=21 odd, deck cleared by
CTRL+C, draws and restores NOPed per the docs/ram-pass.md recipe);
sprCls reads 2 for droids standing at moving doors and the split is
kept; doors and the pad animate cleanly. Walking diagonally through
a droid crowd, 128-pass histograms: tranche-A draws ending over the
display fall from the audit's 59% to 27%, tranche-B from 30% to
5.5%, split taken 127/128, exactly 25.0 Hz. What remains late is the
band + pass preamble against the fire-1 latch - the movement
pipeline (audit recommendation 4), not the repaint classes.
