events.title: Layer 15: the ship reset was missing the alert and the player's energy
events.message:
Layer 15: the ship reset was missing the alert and the player's energy

KC found a new ship starting on red alert. $1293 STA Alert is part of
_entership, and the port only zeroed alertLvl in CombatInit - which sits
ABOVE the T5 split, precisely because it also wipes the score. So a ship
transition inherited the last deck's alert, which after clearing a ship
is red by definition.

Auditing $1289-$12CD store by store, at KC's request, turned up a second
miss with the same cause: $12A7 sets the player's energy to 7 on entering
a new ship and the port carried the old ship's energy over. KC confirmed
porting it as it stands. droidType is NOT reset, on the C64 or here, so
the droid captured on the last ship comes with you - at 7 energy, against
whatever ceiling that droid has, because maxEnergy is genuinely untouched
at $12A5.

The other twelve stores were already right. Two needed checking rather
than trusting the annotated names: droidSprNum looked like it might be
maxEnergy, since $12A5 sets it and droidEnergy to 7 together, and $158F
shows it is not - it is the sprite number, which has no port meaning
because the player is slot 0 and drSprNum[0] is unused. And
ClearSubGameData sounds like it clears transfer state; $377E shows it
only zeroes the FindStrings index, which the port has no equivalent of.
The full table is in the layer doc as DECISION 7.

The alert reset joined EnterShip4's existing A = 0 run in bank 4; the
energy went into InfoHigh's ih_ship in main RAM, because bank 4 had three
bytes left and it needed five. DroidsInit deliberately leaves entry 0
alone, so after the call is as correct as inside it.

Paid for by two rewrites that are provable rather than clever, each a
LDA #n : STA where the branch immediately above has just tested the
flag's value: dbgdeck.asm's two latch sets became INC (+4 bank 4) and the
main loop's shipClear clear became DEC (+2 main RAM).

Verified in jsbeeb: alertLvl forced to &C0 reads 0 on the new ship;
energy 62 before and 7 after, with maxEnergy unchanged at 58; shipLevel 2
and a fresh 119-droid roster.

Bank 4 has 3 bytes free, main RAM 2.

events.title: nova: gate the direct-LUT probe on the xVDI cookie — classic 1MB cards bus-errored
events.message:
nova: gate the direct-LUT probe on the xVDI cookie — classic 1MB cards bus-errored

The memory-mapped RGB565 LUT at Logbase()+0x1FF000 is an ATW800/2 FPGA
feature, not an ET4000 one: on a classic Nova/ET4000 card the probe
write lands past the 1MB memory window and bus-errors (found by running
the classic NOVA-VDI driver on the hatari-et4000 emulated card, where
FRUA needed novalut=off to boot). The ATW800/2 always ships with xVDI,
so its cookie now gates the probe; classic cards fall back to vs_color
cleanly (verified: menu up on the emulated card with no video.cfg).
novalut=on forces the probe without the cookie; off/4mb as before.

events.title: Introduce RTL builds
events.message:
Introduce RTL builds

In general, individual dialog controls are flipped rather than the
overall dialog layout, so e.g. an OK button on the right in LTR builds
remains on the right in RTL builds. This is not the modern approach
to RTL UI, but this was good enough for MacOS 7.1.

`kBuildIsRTL` is now defined, 0 if LTR and 1 if RTL.

* The MGTK `DrawStringForward`, `DrawStringBackward` (etc) aliases are
  reversed so that strings are drawn in the correct direction.

* The `DEFINE_LABEL` macro takes an optional width parameter. In RTL
  builds, the label's X position is defined as left + width, so that
  after a `MoveTo` call, drawing the label with `DrawStringForward`
  works as expected. The constants `kLabelCentered` and
  `kLabelManualAlignment` (both 0) can be used to improve code
  readability in those cases.

* BTK draws button labels on the right and shortcuts on the left in
  RTL builds.

* BTL draws radio buttons and checkboxes on the right side of the
  passed rect, and the label on the left. Passing a width to the
  `DEFINE_BUTTON` macro for these control types is now recommended.

For most dialogs it is then sufficient to just add widths to labels
and buttons, and direction-aware toolkit calls take care of
everything.

Dialogs with more complex layout or where a control and its label need
to be swapped have RTL-specific build-time logic added.

In a small number of cases, modified runtime code is added:
* Reverse the order of calls for some draws
* For runtime layout, change add to subtract and vice-versa.
* Add RTL-aware code for wrapping alert strings.

Not everything is updated; some strings are definitely still wonky,
and there is no actual BiDi support so e.g. naming shortcuts is always
LTR, and menus and list boxes remain LTR.

events.message: Merge branch 'claude/blitter-b3-b4' : base de temps unifiée blitter↔ordonnanceur (B3) + dispatch par accès (B4), Lethal Xcess joue sur megast/ste/megaste
events.author: habib256

events.title: Blitter : les cycles volés avancent l'horloge de l'ordonnanceur (B3 + B4)
events.message:
Blitter : les cycles volés avancent l'horloge de l'ordonnanceur (B3 + B4)

Lethal Xcess se bloquait en `machine=megast` alors qu'il allait en jeu en
`machine=st`, mêmes ROM, mêmes disques, mêmes entrées. Le symptôme FDC noté au
TODO le 2026-08-19 (`cmd=d0` puis silence) était un LEURRE : il est identique à
la milliseconde près en `machine=st`, où le jeu démarre.

B3 — deux bases de temps. `Blitter::onSlice` (tranche non-hog) est le callback de
l'échéance `Scheduler::BLITTER` : il tourne dans `Scheduler::runTo`, donc ENTRE
deux `cpu.run()`. Ses cycles de stall n'entraient ni dans `ran` (mesuré depuis un
`quantumStartBus_` réancré sur l'horloge CPU à chaque entrée de `Cpu68k::run`) ni
dans `sched.now()` : perdus pour l'ordonnanceur. Mesuré (`NEOST_QDELTA_DIAG`) :
escalier de 136 en 136 sur les 21 derniers quanta, soit 8 tranches × 136 = 1088
cycles bus de dette, résorbée d'un coup par le `syncTo` du hook d'IACK juste avant
le handler Timer A. Ce saut mangeait 2 tics de prescaler : `Mfp::readTimerData`
rendait TADR = $3C au lieu de $3D/$3E et la garde $14C2E du jeu tombait dans son
ILLEGAL. Chez Hatari il n'y a qu'UN compteur : `Blitter_AddCycles`
(blitter.c:351-352) écrit dans `nCyclesMainCounter` / `CyclesGlobalClockCounter`,
ceux-là mêmes que lit CycInt.

B4 — dispatch par accès. La facturation est passée du lot de fin de tranche à
l'accès : `Blitter::billCycles` (port de `Blitter_AddCycles` + `Blitter_FlushCycles`)
est appelé par `readWord`/`writeWord` pour leurs 4 cycles et à chaque arbitration,
à sa position réelle — prise du bus AVANT le transfert, restitution APRÈS. Et
`Scheduler::addStolenCycles` DISPATCHE (`syncTo`) au lieu d'avancer `now_` en
silence : une échéance tombant au milieu d'une tranche est servie au cycle où elle
tombe. L'obstacle supposé — `runTo` non ré-entrant — n'en était pas un : `fired` et
`minAll` étaient déjà des locales et `nextDue_` est rebalayé à chaque sortie ; seul
`firingDue_`, l'ancre anti-dérive de l'événement en cours, manquait, et une trame
imbriquée l'écrasait (bug déjà latent sur le chemin runTo → callback → syncTo →
runTo). Garde RAII `FiringGuard`. C'est le modèle d'Hatari, dont `CycInt_Process`
(cycInt.h:85-88) est un simple `while (due <= now)` sans masque anti-relance, lui
aussi ré-entré depuis le handler `INTERRUPT_BLITTER`. Le membre `inDispatch_`
introduit par B3 devient inutile : B4 RETIRE de l'état au lieu d'en ajouter.

Le bug frappait les TROIS machines à blitter, pas seulement Mega ST : `megast`
cassait trame 5552, `ste` et `megaste` trame 5523 (écran noir, 1 couleur).

Halt du 68000 observable. NeoST arrêtait le CPU en SILENCE sur une double faute :
écran figé, aucune explication — c'est ce qui avait fait ouvrir le faux bug
« Stardust sur ST : NeoST reste noir là où Hatari halte ». Vérification : NeoST
HALTE déjà, sur la MÊME instruction que Hatari ($FC5082, A7=$4E7340E7 impair).
`cpuDidHalt()` était disponible côté Moira mais non surchargé. Aucun changement de
comportement émulé. Pas de PC affiché (le prefetch a déjà avancé `reg.pc0`, il ne
désigne pas la faute — Hatari n'en affiche pas non plus) : vecteur et SSP, latchés
par les délégués d'exception de groupe 0.

Validation (arbre fusionné, pas les prototypes) :
- Lethal Xcess : aucun BREAK $14C2E sur `megast`/`ste`/`megaste` ; 29 couleurs à
  26000 trames, écran de jeu inspecté visuellement.
- `timer IRQ max lateness` : 265 → 132 sur les trois machines à blitter (= la
  valeur ST, mais sans plus masquer le saut de 1088) ; boot EmuTOS `megast` nu
  3334 → 161.
- `machine=st` : capture 26000 trames BIT-IDENTIQUE (patch inerte, pas de blitter).
- `run_all.py --tier full` : TOUS LES PALIERS OK.
- Ré-entrance testée assertions ACTIVES (⚠ `RelWithDebInfo` réinjecte `-DNDEBUG`
  APRÈS `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS`, passer par `CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO`) : 26000
  trames, ~1,6 M préemptions, aucune assertion de `runTo` déclenchée.
- Aucun état persistant ajouté, format de save-state inchangé.

Limites assumées, écrites dans TODO.md : aucun étalon n'exerce le blitter
(`NEOST_BLIT_TRACE=1` rend 0 blit sur tout le corpus pixel) — un `--tier full` vert
prouve la non-régression de la base de temps, pas la correction ; le chemin HOG
n'est exercé par aucun titre (5764 blits de LX, tous ctrl=$80) ; et le cross-check
oracle est structurellement impossible sur ce titre (`control.c:87-140` ne route
`hatari-event key*` que vers le clavier, or le tir joystick est load-bearing).

Sonde de non-régression conservée : `NEOST_QDELTA_DIAG=1` (le delta d'entrée de
quantum doit rester PLAT à 40, jamais d'escalier), documentée dans DEV.md.

events.title: Layer 15: the endgame - clearing a ship, and the next one
events.message:
Layer 15: the endgame - clearing a ship, and the next one

The port had no win condition and no ship progression at all: shipNumDroids
was maintained and never read, and GameStart fused the C64's two entry
points so its second half could not be reached. All five tasks land here.

T1/T3, the payouts. 500 for a deck (two AddScore 250, $17DF and $17E4, not
one call of 500 - AddScore takes a byte) with sndFx1 = $17, and 2,000 for a
ship as ten calls of 200, $1274-$127D. Both at DroidsUpdate's clear hook,
which is now all of $17DC rather than Layer 14's colour alone.

T2, leaving the deck. The C64 raises notInDeck, a shared "leave this loop"
flag the port has no equivalent of - it reaches the lift, the console and
the transfer by other means - so this is a dedicated shipClear byte, tested
in the main loop beside them and below the sprites, where the transfer's own
screens are and for the same reason: the page takes the play buffer over.

T4, ShowShipClear. $3816 is GotoHires, ClearGameScreen, ShowRobotType,
BuildIntroSprites, PrintTokenString - which is IsStart's is_st_norm path
instruction for instruction. So the screen is five table entries and a token
list and no drawing code. The list is SIXTEEN bytes, not the ten the scoping
note claimed: $6DCE is two sentences and the $FF is at $6DDD.

T5, the split. GameStart now writes shipLevel = 0 - $1255's own value, where
the port wrote 1 - and falls through into EnterShip4, whose first act is
NextLevel's INC at $129E. The split point is not a judgement call: above it
is what a new game needs and a new ship must not have, and the decisive
member of that set is CombatInit, which zeroes the score. Call it on a ship
transition and the 2,000 just awarded goes with everything else earned.
$1289 also falls into NewShipInfo at $12C7, so a new ship announces itself
on the screen the port already had.

Two pre-existing bugs fell out of building it.

export_strings.py stopped one string short, on the stated reasoning that
the C64 never prints its last. It does: string 248 is "awarded", the last
word of ShipClear_txt, and this screen is the first thing in the port to
ask for it. Token $F8 was landing on the sentinel. 248 -> 249 strings,
1542 -> 1549 bytes. Re-run export_strings.main() - the script has no
__main__ block and build.ps1 does not run the exporters.

And walking back onto a cleared deck re-ran the whole event - sound, colour
and another 500 points, every time. The C64 does not: $1388 tests what
InitDeckDroids placed and skips RunDroids outright when it placed nothing,
while $1395 runs InitColors regardless, which is why an already-clear deck
still shows the cleared floor. DroidsInit now assumes clear and lets the
first placement say otherwise, so a count of 1 makes DroidsUpdate's guard
return and the arm is never reached. It moved above ReframeView for that:
RedrawAll builds the palette and DroidsInit is what now decides the floor.

DEBUG_DECK's arm moved to bank 4 (src/dbgdeck.asm) to pay for the main-RAM
arm above - the trade dbgkill.asm made, one size up, and NOT in colourMap's
padding, where 69 more bytes would push the ALIGN past the page.

Verified in jsbeeb: the deck payout (score 0 -> 975 on a deck whose roster
predicts exactly 475 in kills plus 500); the screen in the C64's own words
with the player's droid; shipLevel 1 -> 2 with a fresh 119-droid roster and
the score carried, not reset; re-entry to a cleared deck leaving the score
at 975 with the floor still blue and no effect; and the relocated deck hop.

Main RAM and bank 4 both end with 2 bytes free.

order as the D= RGB diffs -- while the D= render itself is unchanged (0-byte diff

events.title: Reconstruct the 1987 SSG renderer from the Amiga binary; add .dat support
events.message:
Reconstruct the 1987 SSG renderer from the Amiga binary; add .dat support

Recover the lost SSG (Scene Simulation Generator) renderer as C source in
ssg-src-authentic/, reverse-engineered from the original 1987 Amiga 68000
executable with Ghidra and validated byte-for-byte against the binary's
output under vamos. The reconstruction reproduces the binary's actual
behaviour rather than merely its images: bare rt-style names, single-
precision (FFP) math, an fscanf .dat reader built on the executable's own
recovered scanf grammar, a fixed up-front sphere allocation, and the
scanline-coherent screen-space-culling renderer (per-sphere projected
bounding boxes, per-scanline active lists, per-pixel column cull). Builds
as the ssg_authentic target with a ctest that checks it against the
captured original-binary renders.

Also add the runtime .dat parser for the modernized rt pipeline
(src/datparse.c) and PNG output (src/png.c); reverse-engineering notes;
blog posts (parts 3 and 4); Ghidra export scripts and validation tooling;

events.title: RI (GPIP6) : active basse et au repos assertée, comme CTS et DCD
events.message:
RI (GPIP6) : active basse et au repos assertée, comme CTS et DCD

Fin de l'enquête sur le test S des cartouches Field Service. En désassemblant la
routine de détection ($FA2880-$FA2916 de ST_Diagnostic_v4.4), le protocole est
sans ambiguïté : elle arme un canal MFP, bascule DTR, attend, puis vérifie qu'un
drapeau a été effacé par le gestionnaire d'interruption. Elle le fait TROIS fois,
pour les canaux 14 (RI), 1 (DCD) et 2 (CTS) — et sa table de chaînes nomme les
échecs « S9 RS232 RI-DTR not connected » et « SA RS232 DCD-DTR not connected » :
RI et DCD y sont deux contrôles du MÊME signal DTR.

Or NeoST modélisait RI à l'envers de ses deux jumelles : DCD et CTS sont actives
BASSES (assertées → bit GPIP à 0), RI était active haute. L'assertion produisait
donc un front MONTANT, alors que l'AER du diagnostic vaut 0 et réclame un front
DESCENDANT : le canal 14 ne se levait jamais.

Mesuré par les instructions d'échec réellement exécutées (bset dans $049B),
témoin $FA28C6 vu à chaque fois pour prouver la méthode :

  avant tout          RI, DCD, CTS  -> les trois echouent
  apres la polarite   RI echoue seul (DCD et CTS passent)
  apres ce correctif  aucune des trois n'est atteinte

Le repos ASSERTÉ préserve l'oracle : le GPIP pristine vaut toujours $B1 (bit6 à
0), simplement obtenu autrement — riLine_ vrai au repos au lieu d'un bit figé.

Le bouton Ultimate Ripper suit : il tire désormais RI HORS du repos et la rend au
relâchement, au lieu de l'inverse. Vérifié qu'il fonctionne toujours (--button-at).

Auto-test --serloop-selftest étendu à RI (6 assertions), mfpSelfTest recalé sur le
nouveau modèle. run_all.py --tier full : TOUS LES PALIERS OK, dont les verdicts
série P1 ; déterminisme save-state intact ; neost-selftest 157 OK / 0 FAIL.

events.title: Bouclage RS-232 : la polarité des lignes de contrôle était inversée
events.message:
Bouclage RS-232 : la polarité des lignes de contrôle était inversée

Le port A du PSG est ACTIF BAS. La convention est établie sans ambiguïté sur CE
registre chez Hatari : psg.c:223 le met à $ff au reset (« no drive selected +
side 0 »), et la sélection lecteur s'y teste par « (PORTA & (1<<1)) == 0 »
(psg.c:400). NeoST lisait au contraire « bit != 0 » pour RTS (bit3) et DTR
(bit4) :

    const bool rts = (a & 0x08) != 0;
    const bool dtr = (a & 0x10) != 0;

Conséquence : au repos ($ff, toutes lignes inactives) le connecteur de bouclage
assertait CTS et DCD, et toute bascule les faisait bouger À L'ENVERS. Le
commentaire juste au-dessus de ce code disait pourtant déjà « Le port A est
actif BAS (bit=0 → ligne assertée) » — code et commentaire se contredisaient.

Mesuré (GPIP, CTS=bit2, DCD=bit1, 0 = assertée) :
  portA=$ff repos              -> CTS inactive, DCD inactive   (avant : les DEUX assertées)
  portA=$f7 bit3=0, RTS        -> CTS ASSERTEE, DCD inactive
  portA=$ef bit4=0, DTR        -> CTS inactive, DCD ASSERTEE
  portA=$e7 les deux           -> les deux ASSERTEES

Trouvé en faisant tourner les deux cartouches Atari « Field Service » (ST v4.4
et STE v1.9) sur leur test S, qui concluaient « No loopback connector » alors
que DEV.md annonce que --loopback sert justement « les tests diagnostic serial S
/ MIDI M ». ⚠ Le test S ne passe PAS pour autant : la détection du connecteur
exige encore autre chose que je n'ai pas identifié. La polarité est corrigée sur
ses propres mérites (source de vérité + commentaire du dépôt), pas au prétexte
de faire passer le test — je ne prétends pas l'inverse.

Nouvel auto-test --serloop-selftest, déclaré dans etalons.json (donc joué par
run_all.py) : le câblage vit dans une lambda de Machine, il n'est donc pas
atteignable depuis neost-selftest. Vérifié en réinversant : 4 assertions tombent.

run_all.py --tier full : TOUS LES PALIERS OK — dont les verdicts série P1, qui
utilisent --loopback et étaient le vrai risque de régression ici.

events.title: wonderboy: blit register window — no libgcc modulo (4.75 → 9.45 fps)
events.message:
wonderboy: blit register window — no libgcc modulo (4.75 → 9.45 fps)

Reconstruction
- src/blit.c: mask_reg/plane_reg wrapped the 68000 register window with a
  `% WB_BLIT_SCRATCH_REGS`; -m68000 has no 32-bit divide, so each was a
  ~900-cycle __umodsi3 (→ __udivsi3 + __mulsi3) call — 856 per frame, 47%
  of the frame, from nine sites inlined into blit_row. Both now wrap with
  one conditional subtract (bit-identical for every reachable cell/plane);
  the cross-header bound the argument relies on is pinned by a
  _Static_assert (WB_BLIT_CELL_WORDS == WB_PLANES + 1).
- Measured with Hatari's CPU profiler: 1,646 K → 838 K cycles per frame,
  blit_row 42,000 → 8,807 cycles per call; the original runs 320 K/frame
  at a locked 25 fps.

Verification
- make test 6,417 green on a clean build; blit.o references no `si3`
  helper; mutations (swap the wrap comparison) go RED in test_blit.py.

Docs
- STATUS.md: "Performance" section with the measurement and the change.

events.title: Layer 14: a cleared deck's floor turns blue, and C to clear one
events.message:
Layer 14: a cleared deck's floor turns blue, and C to clear one

KC, 2026-08-24. When the deck holds nothing but the player, its
background goes blue.

The C64 does the same thing at a coarser grain: RunDroids ends its
compaction with STY numDeckDroids and, at a count of 1, runs a whole
deck-cleared event - InitColors, AddScore twice with 250, sndFx1 = $17,
and INC notInDeck when the ship is clear too. InitColors forces the
whole 12-slot record to ColorSets entry 7, which the listing itself
labels "7 - deck cleared", and its floor is C64 colour $B, dark grey.
MODE 1 has no grey, so blue is KC's substitution, and only the
background changes rather than all four logicals. Only the colour is
ported; the score, the sound and the ship-clear arm are Layer 15's, and
layer-14 DECISION 6 lists them as open.

deckClear is the test, not drCount, and that is a bug KC found rather
than a preference. LoadDeck runs ReframeView - which ends in RedrawAll,
which calls SetPalette - BEFORE DroidsInit, so arriving from a cleared
deck the palette was built while drCount was still 1 and the new deck
stayed blue with droids on it. LoadDeck now clears the flag first and
the compaction sets it, so the state cannot depend on the load order.
The C64 reads numDeckDroids directly and gets away with it because
InitColors is called from RunDroids, after the count is right.

The text palettes are exempt: palBase >= 64 is deckTextPal, whose
logical 0 is a legibility choice of its own (DECISION 4), not a floor.

DEBUG_KILL, ON, is the fourth debug flag that changes what the game
does: C kills every droid on the deck one at a time through
DrKillDroid, so the cleared floor can be reached without shooting a
deck empty. It drives the REAL kill path - explosion, sound, score,
alert, DrRemoveShip, sprite slot - so what it tests is the mechanism
and not a shortcut past it. It lives in src/dbgkill.asm, in bank 4
because DroidsUpdate calls it, and included before colours.asm so
colourMap's ALIGN padding absorbs it and the bank does not grow.

events.title: Layer 15: bank 4 gets 97 bytes back, from tables nothing read
events.message:
Layer 15: bank 4 gets 97 bytes back, from tables nothing read

The Layer 15 space pass. Bank 4 was 8 bytes on the fuel gauge and the
endgame's five tasks want about 50; it is now 105, with colourMap's 17
bytes of alignment padding untouched on top.

The saving is 112 bytes of per-deck tables that no longer had a reader.
Of the C64's eight tables at $F120 only deckDroids is read anywhere in
src/: deckOffsetLo/Hi indexed the RLE stream Layer 13d deleted;
deckY/deckX/deckHeight/deckWidth are the deck-plan geometry, of which
bank 7 has its own copy in sideview.asm because only one bank is visible
at a time; deckColour predates colours.asm's per-deck scheme table.
src/data/ is generated, so the change is in export_bbc.py, which carries
a comment saying how to put any of them back.

15 bytes went straight back out, and that is the part to remember.
Shifting bank 4 down by 112 pushed sound.asm's 38-byte voice-state block
across a page and broke ASSERT HI(snFreqLo) == HI(snPhase+1) - SndCopy's
stride-2 self-modified store steps the low byte only. That assert had no
padding behind it, so any bank-4 edit of the wrong size could break it.
It now has a conditional pad, at most 37 bytes and often none, so it
heals itself; the cost in this build is 15. A future bank-4 change can
therefore move the gauge by up to 37 bytes on its own - read it.

Verified as purely mechanical: both builds' listings reduced to a stream
of (mnemonic, addressing class) and diffed - 22,954 instructions, zero
differences. Main RAM, banks 5, 6 and 7 all end where they did.

In jsbeeb: boot, title, briefing, play; a diagonal scroll with the play
buffer diffed against a forced RedrawAll (SprDrawAll/SprDrawTr poked to
RTS), 0 diffs of 10,240; C clearing the deck; a deck hop; the console
opened from a console tile with all three pages drawn and closed through
entry 0; a lift ride to another deck; ESCAPE to game over, the high-score
entry, and round through the title to the briefing.

DEBUG_KILL was not turned off - the room was found elsewhere and its ~45
bytes stay in reserve. DEBUG_MAPGUARD no longer blows the one-page assert
but is still 19 bytes over bank 4; recorded, not chased.

events.title: RTC : TIMER EN honoré — la batterie Z du diagnostic passe entière sur Mega ST
events.message:
RTC : TIMER EN honoré — la batterie Z du diagnostic passe entière sur Mega ST

Reprise du premier des deux écarts laissés ouverts. Hier je refusais de livrer ce
changement parce qu'il ne corrigeait pas le symptôme et que je le croyais
spéculatif sur une horloge persistée. Les deux objections tombent :

 · le symptôme (« C1 clock increment error ») a été corrigé depuis, par la
   longueur de seconde ; TIMER EN est un écart DISTINCT, et vérifié compatible :
   le test L passe toujours une fois le bit honoré ;
 · ce n'était pas spéculatif. Instrumenté sur machine réelle émulée, TOS 1.02 ET
   EmuTOS écrivent $9 puis $8 dans le registre mode au boot : ils ne basculent
   que le bit0 (banque, alias AM/PM déjà modélisé) et laissent le bit3 POSÉ.
   C'est la confirmation que bit3 = TIMER EN et que l'honorer est sans risque en
   usage normal. Seule la cartouche de diagnostic le coupe, délibérément, pour
   figer l'heure avant de la relire ;
 · et mode_ n'est PAS dans neost.cfg (seuls les 7 champs de date le sont) — ma
   réserve d'hier était en partie infondée. Il est en revanche dans le
   save-state : la version passe donc à v17, un état v16 pouvant porter mode_=0,
   qui figerait désormais le compteur. Les états d'une autre version étaient déjà
   refusés d'office, donc aucune migration silencieuse.

Résultat mesuré : la batterie Z de la cartouche Atari « Mega and ST Field Service
Diagnostic v4.4 » (1990) passe INTÉGRALEMENT sur Mega ST — RAM, ROM, couleur,
clavier, audio, MFP/Glue/vidéo, horloge temps réel (rollover de siècle inclus) et
blitter. Sur ST elle reste à 11 Pass / 0 Fail, inchangée.

Second écart, CLKOUT : NON traité, et c'est délibéré. Hatari ne la modélise pas
(elle n'apparaît que dans le brochage de rtc.c), et aucun consommateur n'a été
observé — la batterie complète exerce le RTC sans elle. L'implémenter serait

events.title: RTC : la seconde dérivait contre la base de temps de la machine
events.message:
RTC : la seconde dérivait contre la base de temps de la machine

Trouvé en faisant tourner la cartouche Atari « Mega and ST Field Service
Diagnostic v4.4 » (1990) en headless — un oracle d'époque que la suite
automatisée n'utilise pas (le palier P1 a sa propre cartouche). Sur Mega ST, son
test L échouait :

    Testing real-time clock
    23:59:59 12/31/99 SAT
    23:59:59 12/31/99 SAT
    C1 clock increment error

alors que docs/IMPLEMENTED.md affirmait que ce modèle « corrige C0 + C1 ».

Le RTC comptait ses secondes avec une CONSTANTE, Rtc::CPU_HZ = 8 021 248 (la
fréquence CPU PAL réelle). Or la machine émulée délivre 160 256 cycles par trame
et NeoST appelle ça 50 Hz, soit 8 012 800 cycles par seconde émulée. L'horloge
était donc 0,105 % trop lente par rapport à TOUT le reste de la machine (~91 s de
dérive par jour), et un logiciel qui mesure une seconde en comptant ses trames
retombait systématiquement juste AVANT le tic.

Mesuré dans la trace des accès : entre la remise à zéro du diviseur (cycle
2005731330) et la relecture (2013751052) il s'écoule 8 019 722 cycles — 1526 de
moins que le seuil. D'où l'absence d'incrément.

Correctif : Machine::beginFrame_ pose la longueur d'une seconde sur la géométrie
verrouillée de la trame (lpf × cpl × refreshHz), et le RTC l'utilise à la place
de la constante (qui reste la valeur de repli). L'horloge suit désormais la même
base de temps que le reste de la machine : 150 trames PAL donnent exactement 3 s
(2 auparavant, l'arrondi en perdait une).

Vérifications :
  · test L Mega ST : Pass, avec les deux cas et le rollover de siècle
    (23:59:59 12/31/99 SAT -> 00:00:00 01/01/00 SUN) ;
  · batterie Z (RAM/ROM/Clavier/Audio/Timing/BLiT) : 11 Pass, 0 Fail, inchangée ;
  · déterminisme save-state : écran ET état re-sérialisé identiques ;
  · run_all.py --tier full : TOUS LES PALIERS OK ;
  · neost-selftest 155 OK / 0 FAIL — régression ajoutée (horloge factice, ni
    machine ni ROM), vérifiée en neutralisant le setter : 4 assertions tombent.

⚠ Une piste écartée en chemin : le bit TIMER EN (bit3 du registre mode), que la
cartouche manipule et que NeoST ignore. Le correspondant ne corrige PAS le
symptôme ; il n'est donc pas inclus, pour ne pas livrer de changement spéculatif
sur une horloge persistée. Reste ouvert, avec la sortie CLKOUT (non modélisée).

docs/IMPLEMENTED.md recalé sur ce qui est réellement vérifié.

events.title: ACIA MIDI : au débordement, c'est le mauvais octet qui était perdu
events.message:
ACIA MIDI : au débordement, c'est le mauvais octet qui était perdu

Troisième trouvaille de la même veine : ce que l'ACIA du CLAVIER modélise et que
l'ACIA MIDI, juste à côté, ne modélise pas.

Sémantique matérielle (acia.c, état STOP_BIT) :

    if ((pACIA->SR & ACIA_SR_BIT_RDRF) == 0) { pACIA->RDR = pACIA->RSR; ... }
    else                                       pACIA->RX_Overrun = 1;

récepteur plein → le NOUVEL octet est perdu, le RDR garde l'ancien. NeoST-MIDI
faisait l'inverse (`rx_.pop_front()`), sous un commentaire affirmant que cela
« modélise en prime l'overrun réel du composant » — c'était l'octet opposé.

C'est le pire choix possible pour du MIDI, où le premier octet porte le STATUS.
Mesuré, note-on $90 $3C $40 émis sans lecture intermédiaire :

  avant : relu 3C 40   <- le status a disparu, deux données orphelines
  après : relu 90 3C   <- comme le matériel ; c'est le 3e octet qui tombe

Un parseur MIDI se désynchronise sur le premier cas et pas sur le second.

Portée honnête : le seul appelant externe (l'anneau MIDI du headless) teste déjà
rxCanAccept() avant de pousser, donc le débordement n'est atteignable que par le
bouclage OUT→IN. Le bit OVRN lui-même reste non modélisé côté MIDI (l'ACIA
clavier le porte, elle) — divergence déjà inventoriée, non traitée ici.

Au passage : le commentaire de l'ACIA clavier annonçait encore un modèle
d'émission « qui ne s'active QUE sous IRQ TX », ce que le correctif précédent a
rendu faux. Recalé.

Régression dans neost-selftest, vérifiée en remettant pop_front() : 2 assertions
tombent. neost-selftest 150 OK / 0 FAIL ; --tier full : TOUS LES PALIERS OK
(dont le test MIDI du diagnostic, qui passe justement par le bouclage).

events.title: ecs: CLUT-keyed RAM palette cache — the walk's per-step re-quant churn (A500)
events.message:
ecs: CLUT-keyed RAM palette cache — the walk's per-step re-quant churn (A500)

Field report: on the A500 the town walk drains and reloads its colours on
every step ('the CLUT keeps unloading/loading'). Measured on the inn
street route: SEVEN full re-bands in sixteen moves, each dragging a full
re-render — the walk's wall-set CLUTs alternate between a handful of
palettes, and the only cache (the disk one) keys on clut+FRAME hash,
which can never hit mid-walk.

This is the ST's st_pcache ported: six RAM entries keyed on the CLUT
alone (hash + full 768-byte verify, MRU). A hit skips the cut entirely
and carries the two guards the ST proved out: indices the cached cut
never saw are re-pointed at their nearest per-band slot (no falling
through the absent-colour bucketing), and when the restored remaps equal
the live ones the planes on screen stay valid — palettes-only, no
force-full, no epoch reset. Fresh cuts and exact disk hits both store.
video.cfg clutcache=off opts out. ~59 KB of BSS.

Same route on the cache build: 3 fresh cuts (first-ever CLUTs only),
3 RAM hits, and the user's exact video shots — the brown door, the
innkeeper event — render correct in emulation.

events.title: ACIA clavier : même bug de TDRE que le MIDI, sur la puce sœur
events.message:
ACIA clavier : même bug de TDRE que le MIDI, sur la puce sœur

Suite directe de la chasse précédente. Hatari acia.c ACIA_Write_TDR efface TDRE
hors de toute condition :

    pACIA->SR &= ~ACIA_SR_BIT_TDRE;    /* TDR is not empty anymore */

et cette fonction sert AUSSI l'ACIA du clavier (acia.c:643, appelée avec
pACIA_IKBD). NeoST ne l'appliquait que sous TIE, ce que le commentaire assumait
comme un modèle volontairement restreint : « le modèle d'émission ne s'active QUE
quand un logiciel pilote l'IKBD par IRQ TX ». La source de vérité dit l'inverse.

Conséquence : la boucle d'attente d'Ikbdws (le TOS SCRUTE le statut, il
n'interrompt pas) passait sans jamais attendre, et les octets d'une commande
IKBD partaient tous au même cycle au lieu d'être cadencés par la liaison série.

Deux correctifs, en miroir exact de ceux du MIDI :
 · TDRE tombe à chaque écriture de données, TIE ou non ;
 · écrire le registre de contrôle ne remet plus l'émetteur au repos — seul le
   master reset le fait (6850).

⚠ Changement de timing au COEUR des étalons (le TOS envoie ses commandes IKBD
pendant le boot), donc traité comme une expérience à annuler si l'image bougeait.
Elle n'a pas bougé : run_all.py --tier full, tous les étalons pixel à
diff_px=0 / 114816 (0.00 %).

Régression dans neost-selftest (un Mfp, un Scheduler, une ACIA — ni machine ni
ROM), vérifiée en remettant la condition : « FAIL TIE coupé : TDRE tombe aussi ».

events.title: ACIA MIDI : TDRE n'était modélisé que sous TIE — plus aucun frein en scrutation
events.message:
ACIA MIDI : TDRE n'était modélisé que sous TIE — plus aucun frein en scrutation

Trouvé par la méthode imposée, en comparant à extern/hatari/src. Hatari
Midi_Data_WriteByte (midi.c:243) efface TDRE HORS de toute condition :

    MidiStatusRegister &= ~ACIA_SR_TX_EMPTY;

sous le commentaire « This is required to accurately emulate the TDRE bit in
status register (fix the program 'Notator') ».

NeoST ne le faisait que si l'IRQ d'émission était armée :

    if (txEnableInt_ && sched_) { tdre_ = false; schedule(MIDI_TX, ...); }

Un pilote qui SCRUTE le statut au lieu d'utiliser l'interruption — le cas
classique, et nommément celui de Notator — voyait donc TDRE éternellement à 1 :
aucune attente entre deux octets, tout le flux MIDI OUT collé au même cycle.
Mesuré avant le correctif : 1000 octets émis d'affilée sans que TDRE ne retombe
une seule fois. Le tempo d'un séquenceur en dépend, et l'horodatage envoyé aux
sorties hôte (midiSinkTimed_) était identique pour tous les octets.

À noter : NeoST vient d'ajouter la clé C-Lab Notator (53b726b) alors que son
ACIA portait précisément le bug que Hatari a corrigé POUR Notator.

Deux correctifs :
 · TDRE tombe à chaque écriture de données, TIE ou non ;
 · écrire le registre de contrôle ne remet plus l'émetteur au repos — seul le
   master reset le fait (6850). L'ancien « TIE coupé -> tdre_ = true » aurait
   sinon réarmé l'émetteur à chaque retouche du CR entre deux octets.

Cubase Lite est inchangé (il pilote par interruption, chemin non modifié) :
run_midi_sequencer.py rend les mêmes 3585 octets, 200 notes, pente de tempo
1.00098, gigue σ 0.44 ms.

events.message:
Auto-plug : la clé du jeu précédent restait branchée au montage suivant

L'auto-plug de disks/dongles.txt ne remplit que les emplacements VIDES et ne
retirait JAMAIS rien. Or le montage à chaud enchaîne les jeux — c'est toute la
raison d'être de la ludothèque et de la borne : la clé du titre précédent restait
donc en place pour le suivant.

Conséquence mesurée, clé Leader Board oubliée sur le port 1 (joyOverlay lui
impose joy |= 0x03, soit HAUT et BAS ensemble — une combinaison qu'aucun vrai
joystick ne produit) :

  manette hôte $00 (repos)  -> le jeu lit $03   HAUT+BAS forces
  manette hôte $08 (droite) -> le jeu lit $0B   droite + HAUT+BAS
  manette hôte $80 (feu)    -> le jeu lit $83   feu + HAUT+BAS

La manette du jeu suivant est donc cassée, en silence. Et comme l'auto-plug
persiste son choix (cfg.joy1 = "leaderboard"), ça survivait au redémarrage.

Correctif : on MÉMORISE ce que l'auto-plug a posé (g_autoPortDev / g_autoCartKey)
et on le retire au montage suivant comme à l'éjection — mais SEULEMENT si c'est
toujours ce qu'on avait posé, sinon la page Dongles perdrait la main.

Le résidu inter-session est couvert aussi : au démarrage, un périphérique que la
table EXPLIQUE pour la disquette montée est marqué image-dérivé (aucun
branchement n'est fait à ce moment), sans quoi la clé persistée par une session
antérieure reste indiscernable d'un choix utilisateur et resterait collée.

Au passage, l'en-tête de CartridgeKey décrivait les lignes U du format de trace
comme des cycles /UDS « dans la fenêtre cartouche » — l'implémentation et la
spec publiée (docs/EXTENSIONS.md:220, destinée aux captures matérielles de

YM2149 : le DAC Pro Sound rendait ses propres save-states irrecevables

Le DAC Pro Sound (08fe5e4) a élargi le domaine des écritures horodatées empilées
dans events_ :

    if (selected_ < 14 || (selected_ == 15 && portBDac_))
        events_.push_back(...);

mais la garde de RELECTURE de ces événements est restée à son ancienne borne :

    a.check(e.reg < 14);        // sans étiquette, de surcroît

Écrivain et lecteur ne s'accordent donc plus. Un save-state pris avec le DAC
branché et une écriture R15 encore en file (le cas NORMAL : events_ n'est vidé
que par synthesizeFrame) est écrit sans broncher, puis REFUSÉ au chargement —
et comme la garde n'avait pas d'étiquette, le diagnostic se résumait à
« invariant rejected: (unlabelled) » puis « truncated/inconsistent file ». Soit
exactement ce que StateArchive.hpp:33-36 avertit de ne pas produire : « une
garde trop stricte, qui refuse un état légitime, est indiscernable d'un fichier
réellement corrompu ».

Mesuré (aller-retour save/load sur une Machine, horloge de cycle câblée comme
le fait le frontend audio) :
  DAC débranché, R15 écrit : save 1261868 o -> load OK
  DAC branché,   R15 écrit : save 1261874 o -> load REFUSE
  après correctif           :                  load OK

La garde reprend le domaine EXACT de write8 (0-13, plus 15 sous DAC ; R14 n'est
jamais empilé) et reçoit enfin son étiquette. L'index restait sûr de toute façon
(le rejeu masque déjà par &15) : c'était une garde de domaine, pas de bornes.

StateArchive suffisent. Vérifiée en remettant l'ancienne borne :

events.title: Layer 9: the panel's mode word is red, like the logo and the score
events.message:
Layer 9: the panel's mode word is red, like the logo and the score

KC: "the text on the left hand side of the top panel should be red, same
as the paradroid logo and the score in the rest of the panel."

The original says so directly. LevelColors ($2844) fills six rows of
colour RAM with bgColor and then overwrites rows 2 and 3, COLUMNS 2 TO
37, with $F2 -- low nibble 2, red:

  2853  LDA #$F2
  2855  LDY #35
  2857  STA $D852,Y      ; $D800 + 82  = row 2, col 2
  285A  STA $D87A,Y      ; $D800 + 122 = row 3, col 2
  285E  BPL _1           ; 36 cells, cols 2-37

The status line's fields are the mode word at col 2, the logo at 15-23
and the score at 30-37 -- all inside cols 2-37, so all three are red on
the C64. We had the logo and the score right and the mode word in
PN_INK_TEXT.

Three routines write that field and two needed changing:

  PnStr (bank 6)       Mobile/Weapon/Transfer/Console and PnBriefing's
                       "Briefing" -- PN_INK_RED after PnAt, which resets
                       the ink: the same two lines the logo and the
                       score already had.

  DbPanelStr (bank 7)  the droid database's "More" and "Console" --
                       DbGlyph's ink is now the variable dbInk, so the
                       PAGE keeps DB_INK white and only the panel field
                       takes DB_INK_PN red. DbPanelStr puts it back.

  XfGlyphAt (bank 7)   the transfer game's verdict messages at col 4 --
                       LEFT ALONE. A different screen with its own
                       palette, and not what was asked for.

Cost: 5 bytes of bank 6, which is down to 4 free, and ~14 of bank 7's
314.

Verified in the panel buffer rather than from a screenshot: the mode
word, the logo and the score all come out logical 2 and nothing else --
71, 55 and 8 bytes with the high plane set and ZERO in any other plane.
Checked on both "Mobile" and "Console".

The icon selection was re-checked on the ct_back path at the same time:
returning from the database with conSel = 1, the ship icon is white and
the other three black, drawn once.

NOT verified: the droid database's own "More", written on its page 3.
Its sibling "Console" write shares the changed path, but page 3 was not
reached in the emulator.

Layer-9 DECISION 19.

conWaitInput ($2C63) writes SpriteColor $F1 -- VIC colour 1, white -- to
the newly selected sprite and puts $FF back on the one it left, taking
that from the sprite table's own field at $6B94+9 (colour 15, light
grey); WrSpriteState ($09B7) STAs the byte into $D027,Y. Nothing else
marks the selection.

Black and white here, because MODE 1 has no grey. KC was shown a 2x2
dither for a real grey, the deck's highlight, and black, and took black:
the same KIND of change as the original's, a brightness step, taken to
its ends. Layer-9 DECISION 18.

A TRANSFORM, NOT A SECOND COPY. An icon is two-colour, so its shape
lives entirely in the LOW nibble of every byte; the high nibble is 0 for
logical 1 and a copy of the low for logical 3, and one patched AND
chooses. Neither bank 6 nor main RAM had room for black artwork.

THE COLOUR IS CHOSEN BEFORE THE DRAW.  KC, on the first build: "the
icons all appear white before then becoming black. when returning to the
menu the icon should be drawn in the correct colour once." Visibly true
-- ConIcons is the SECOND thing ConDraw does and the recolour ran after
every line of text. So ConIconInk4 now fills conInkT (four bytes of main
RAM: &F0 selected, &00 the rest) before anything is plotted, and
ConIcons/ConDroid load it into csn_mask per icon. Main RAM because
conSel is bank 4's and bank 6 cannot read it -- the same reason PN_TABS
and pmShip exist.

ConSprNib was restructured to pay for that in a bank with 16 bytes: its
three stores now share one csn_put that takes a four-pixel pattern in a
low nibble and builds the high plane from it -- the SAME transform
ConIconSel4 uses, so the draw path and the in-place path agree by
construction. That deleted conNib3 (sixteen n*&11 entries, now computed)
and made conDblHi/conDblLo patterns rather than finished bytes. Net cost
to bank 6: 7 bytes.

The in-place transform stays for menu STEPS, which redraw nothing. Only
the two after-redraw paths lost their post-draw call.

WHERE THE SPACE CAME FROM. ConIconSel4 is ~80 bytes and bank 4 had TWO;
the first build overshot by 38. colourMap is ALIGN &100 with 162 bytes of
padding in front of it -- and DELETING THAT ALIGN RECOVERS NOTHING, tried
and measured: tiledefs.asm aligns next and pads by the same amount, and
the bank still ended at &BFFE. The padding is a hole, and a hole only
pays if you put something in it. So the routine is src/consolesel.asm,
INCLUDEd between chardata.asm and colours.asm -- anywhere before that
ALIGN will do, because the pad then shrinks by exactly what was added and
the page boundary does not move. It cannot live in colours.asm: src/data/
is generated. CLAUDE.md now carries the rule, and the 162-byte limit past
which the ALIGN rounds to the next page and costs 256 at a stroke.

Bank 4: 2 bytes free -> 45. Bank 6: 16 -> 9. Main RAM: 6 -> 3.

Verified in the buffer, stepping through the draw itself: mid-ConIcons
and before a single character of text, ship 27 bytes of its final 46 and
deck and alert complete, every byte black and zero white; next dump, 001
white at its full 76 and the others black at 46/160/92. After a step to
conSel = 1, 001/deck/alert every non-zero byte at high = 0 and ship every
one at high = low -- zero malformed bytes, counts unchanged. The marker
column is clear on all four rows.

Two stale comments fixed: console.asm claimed the icons and the marker
were "logical colour 1, white on every deck". The buffer says the icons
were logical 3, and Layer 14 made logical 1 black.

events.title: Layer 9: the console menu moves down one row
events.message:
Layer 9: the console menu moves down one row

KC: the play area has been sixteen rows since 2026-08-21 and the console
menu never moved with it. Spend the recovered row on the menu.

CON_ROW_UNIT/ACC/SHIP/DECK/ALERT: 0, 2, 5, 8, 11 -> 1, 3, 6, 9, 12.
Constants only, so it costs nothing.

WHERE THE C64 PUTS IT. ClearGameScreen ($2BA5) fills 17 rows from $4940
-- $4800 + 320, so screen row 8 -- at 40 bytes a row (FillCRAM $0A52).
So the console area is screen rows 8-24 and ConsoleMain's five lines, at
screen rows 10/12/15/18/21, are console rows 2, 4, 7, 10 and 13.

We are therefore still ONE row above the original, not level with it.
Two rows also fits in sixteen (the alert glyph would land on 13-14 and
its icon on 13-15, filling the area exactly); KC was shown both layouts
and chose one row. Both console.asm and layer-9 DECISION 17 now say so,
and say not to "correct" it to two without asking -- the derivation above
makes two look obviously right, and it is not what was asked for.

THE MENU WAS THREE SETS OF LITERALS that had to move together and could
drift apart:

  - the five text rows                  console.asm
  - the four icon destinations          console.asm, were 2/5/8/11
  - the marker bar CON_MARK0-3          droid.asm, were 3/6/9/12

The icons are now written as CON_ROW_ACC/SHIP/DECK/ALERT. The bar cannot
be: droid.asm is bank 4 and is assembled BEFORE bank 6's console.asm, so
those constants do not exist yet. console.asm ASSERTs the four against
them instead, where both are known -- the bar sits one row into each
icon's three.

Also added ASSERT CON_ROW_ALERT + CON_ICON_ROWS <= PLAY_ROWS. The
existing assert covered the two-row text glyph only, not the three-row
icon beside it, which is the taller of the two and the one that would
actually have clipped.

Verified in the play buffer rather than a screenshot: row 0 empty, text
on 1-2, 3-4, 6-7, 9-10 and 12-13, icons on 3-5, 6-8, 9-11 and 12-14, the
marker bar at row 4 unit 1, row 15 clear.

events.title: Layer 14: the logo screen gets its emboss back, and a random boot deck
events.message:
Layer 14: the logo screen gets its emboss back, and a random boot deck

The C64 logo screen is embossed and ours was one flat colour.

WHY. The screen is hires (Irq1 $2922 writes $D016 = $C8, bit 4 clear), so
a cell is the shared background plus one foreground colour -- and
ShowTitle $2879 makes a SECOND pass over the same 1,000 codes, writing
$D800 from CharColor $0800. Colour is a property of the character CODE,
not of the cell: CharColor's high nibble is a fixed slot and
NewCharColors $3577 patches the low nibble per deck. Slot is artwork,
physical is palette -- the split this port already has.

Matching all 1,000 cells of Title_dat against ref/c64-logo-screen.png on
a fitted grid, the whole screen is five slots:

  slot 0  484 cells  (162,142,229)  code $00, blank        -> logical 0
  slot 9  247 cells  (241,238,251)  white highlights, TL   -> logical 3
  slot 7  249 cells  (100, 79,180)  violet shadows, BR     -> logical 1
  slot 4   17 cells  ( 23, 15, 61)  BY ANDREW / BRAYBROOK  -> logical 1
  slot E    3 cells  green          the three blobs        -> logical 2

The highlight and its shadow are about three character cells apart and
never share one, so none of it needs per-pixel colour. export_title.py
bakes each slot's logical colour into the 36 glyphs (SLOT_LOGICAL) and
that is the whole change: title.asm is still 1,140 bytes, TiCell is
untouched, the RLE stream is untouched. Supersedes layer-11 DECISION 9.

The four fixed slot roles ARE the four tones the logo wants, so the only
substitution is slot E's green taking the deck highlight.

THE RANDOM BOOT DECK (KC). The front end inherits the last deck's
palette, and at a cold boot there is no such deck. It ran on the OS's
MODE 1 default -- logical 0 black, logical 1 red -- which INVERTS a fresh
emboss: the shadow strokes came out brighter than the background they sit
under. Seen in jsbeeb. Any deck palette has the relationship the artwork
wants.

TiBootPal (src/title.asm, so in PARTITL) takes the TEXT palette, not the
play one: that is what the game-over path arrives on, since InfoCall runs
SetTextPal before every front-end screen, so boot and the loop back now
agree. It also dodges decks 0, 5 and 9, whose logical 0 IS white and
would swallow the white highlights.

It absorbed main.asm's boot seed -- the deck and the LFSR seed are the
same sample of the same free-running counter. bootPal, an assembled 1 in
main RAM, keeps it to a cold boot; it cannot live in PARTITL, which is
reloaded from disc on every title and would bring it back set. And it
pages bank 4 itself: boot's last act before TitleSeq is UnpackBankIn on
SWRAM_XFER, so SWRAM_DATA is not the resting state on arrival.

Net -4 bytes of main RAM: the code image ends at &2FFA, 6 bytes free, up
from 2. PARTITL spent 32 of its 89. Bank 4 unchanged.

Verified in jsbeeb: cold boot lands on deck 11 (bootPal 0, deck 11,
palette [4,0,5,7]) -- blue ground, white highlights top-left, black
shadows bottom-right, dark panel lettering, magenta blobs, the same
relationships as the C64 reference. NOT yet seen on the game-over path,
where the inherited palette comes from a deck actually played.

events.title: annotate.py: the annotated listing was missing 43% of the original's data
events.message:
annotate.py: the annotated listing was missing 43% of the original's data

Looking up CharColor ($0800) in paradroid_ce_annotated.asm returned 76
bytes. The table is 256, and paradroid_ce.lst has all of it.

get_content split the line on tabs and returned the FIRST non-hex field.
IDA lays a .BYTE operand list out in tab-separated column groups, so
every group but the first was dropped -- and because dropping one shifts
everything after it, the bytes that survived sat at the WRONG OFFSETS.
CharColor[$16] returned a real-looking byte from a different entry rather
than nothing. Truncation announces itself eventually; misalignment does
not, and the annotated listing is what this project reads the C64
original -- its specification -- out of.

Measured by the new tools/verify_annotation.py, which re-extracts every
.BYTE block from both files and diffs them per address:

                                   before    after
  .BYTE bytes in paradroid_ce.lst  49,537   49,537
  present in the annotated copy    21,405   49,420
  blocks truncated                    295        0
  blocks whose values disagree         96        0

Two details each cost a build: DATA_DIRECTIVE_RE needs its \b (a mangled
one compiled to a literal backspace and matched nothing), and the rejoin
must not insert a comma when the directive itself ends a field -- ".BYTE,"
broke the \.BYTE\s extraction and re-truncated eight blocks.

The remaining 117 bytes are zero page, where annotate.py deliberately
emits `name = $XX`: the address survives and the assembled initial value
does not. The tool reports those separately and passes. Read zero-page
initial values from paradroid_ce.lst.

The exporters in tools/ all parse the raw listing, so src/data/ was never
affected -- confirmed, not assumed.

events.message:
Profils : port0= relu mais jamais appliqué ; overlay borne : la souris passait

Deux trous de symétrie dans le frontend, trouvés en auditant le mode borne et
l'aller-retour des profils.

1. Charger un profil réappliquait consciencieusement TOUS les globals vivants
   (g_autoZoom, g_crtOn/g_crtParams, g_kbdJoyPort, g_joyDeadzone, joymapParse,
   volume, driveSoundOn) — la même liste qu'à l'init du démarrage, SAUF
   g_port0Auto. Or port0= est bien écrit dans les profils (writeConfigKeys,
   avant le garde `full` — vérifié) et bien relu dans cfg.port0. Seule
   l'application en mémoire manquait : g_port0Auto n'était dérivé de cfg qu'en
   UN point, l'init de démarrage.
   Conséquences : la combo « Port 0 » affiche l'ancien choix, une 2e manette
   n'est pas routée sur le port souris, et surtout saveConfig écrit aussitôt le
   port0 du PROFIL dans neost.cfg — fichier et comportement se contredisent,
   puis le comportement change tout seul au lancement suivant. Pire, tout
   réglage joystick touché ensuite réécrit cfg.port0 depuis le global périmé et
   efface silencieusement la valeur du profil.

2. L'overlay borne avale le clavier (onKey) et la manette (joy0/joy1/aux forcés
   à 0), mais pas la souris : ni le mouvement scruté par trame ni onMouseButton
   ne testaient g_kioskDiskMenu. Or en borne la souris est capturée d'office et
   le ST est GELÉ sous le menu (kioskPaused) : les Δ s'empilaient dans
   l'accumulateur non borné d'Ikbd::mouseEvent pour ressortir d'un bloc à la
   reprise (pointeur qui traverse l'écran), et les clics partaient au jeu.

Le second est la rechute exacte du bug des clics sur un port 0 occupé : deux
chemins d'entrée souris qui doivent poser la MÊME question et divergent. D'où
un prédicat unique, mouseReachesSt(), consommé par les deux — le mouvement
consomme toujours le Δ hôte, seul l'envoi à l'IKBD est gaté.

events.title: Port cartouche : l'exclusivité clé Steinberg / EtherNEC ne tenait qu'à l'ordre
events.message:
Port cartouche : l'exclusivité clé Steinberg / EtherNEC ne tenait qu'à l'ordre

setDongle() refuse la clé quand l'EtherNEC ou le NetUSBee est actif (ils décodent
toute la fenêtre cartouche). Mais enableEtherNec() ne testait QUE bus.cart, jamais
la clé : l'interdit n'existait donc que dans un sens, et brancher la clé EN PREMIER
laissait les deux répondre sur le même port.

Le chemin qui déclenche ça n'est pas théorique : en headless, l'auto-plug de
disks/dongles.txt (déduit du NOM DE FICHIER de l'image) s'exécutait AVANT
l'activation réseau. Même état illégal, deux issues opposées :

  --dongle cubase2 --ethernec        -> "--dongle refused: EtherNEC/NetUSBee
                                        decode the whole cartridge window"
  --disk "Cubase 2.st" --ethernec    -> "auto-plug: cartridge key 1"
                                     +  "EtherNEC (NE2000) on the cartridge port"

Trois correctifs :
 · Machine::enableEtherNec refuse si dongle.attached() — l'invariant devient
   symétrique et indépendant de l'ordre, pour tous les appelants (GUI compris) ;
 · headless : l'auto-plug passe APRÈS l'activation réseau, pour qu'un drapeau
   EXPLICITE prime sur un branchement déduit d'un nom de fichier (setDongle
   refuse alors la clé, et --ethernec l'emporte) ;
 · GUI : etherApply/netUsbeeApply pré-testent la clé comme ils pré-testaient
   déjà la cartouche — sinon la case restait cochée sans que rien ne s'active.

Régression dans enec-selftest (il construit déjà une Machine) : les deux sens de
l'exclusivité sont vérifiés. --enec-selftest 9 passed / 0 failed.

events.title: MFP : le reset ne relâchait pas RI (GPIP6), ligne coincée pour toujours
events.message:
MFP : le reset ne relâchait pas RI (GPIP6), ligne coincée pour toujours

Mfp::reset() ramène au repos les lignes d'ENTRÉE du GPIP qu'aucune relecture ne
recalcule — CTS, DCD (« sans cette remise, une désassertion sous --loopback
survivait à tous les resets »), BUSY, et le bouton Multiface. RI manquait à
cette liste, alors que le raisonnement s'y applique mot pour mot.

Deux sources l'assertent, et aucune ne la relâchait après un reset machine :

 · bouclage RS-232 (DTR→RI, cf. le sink port A de Machine) : psg.reset() ne
   retire pas le sink, exactement le cas décrit pour CTS/DCD ;
 · bouton Ultimate Ripper : PortDevices::pressButton tire RI, et c'est
   PortDevices::onVbl qui la relâche à la VBL suivante. Or Machine::reset()
   appelle ports.reset(), qui remet pressed_ à faux AVANT cette VBL — onVbl
   sortait alors immédiatement et PLUS RIEN ne relâchait la ligne.

Mesuré (GPIP d'entrée, pristine = $B1 ; RI est bit6, repos BAS) :
  bouclage, DTR assertée puis reset : $F5 -> $F1   (RI toujours haute)
  bouton URC, reset avant la VBL    : $F1 -> $F1 -> $F1 apres la VBL
  avec le correctif, les deux cas   : -> $B1

Régression ajoutée à mfpSelfTest, section (e) : reset() relâche RI/BUSY/bouton
et rend CTS/DCD à leur repos ACTIF, GPIP d'entrée == $B1. Vérifiée en retirant
le correctif : « FAIL reset : RI (bit6) relâchée got=1 want=0 » et
« FAIL GPIP d'entrée pristine got=241 want=177 ».

--mfp-selftest 31 OK / 0 FAIL ; run_all.py --tier full : TOUS LES PALIERS OK
(les verdicts série P1, qui exercent le bouclage RI, passent).

events.title: neost.cfg : un gain audio NaN rendait la machine muette jusqu'au reset
events.message:
neost.cfg : un gain audio NaN rendait la machine muette jusqu'au reset

Les cinq faders du mixeur (mix_ym, mix_dma, mix_drive, mix_mt32, mix_dac)
passaient par std::atof SANS aucune borne, alors que le fichier a une
convention explicite pour ça (cf. les commentaires de volume= et joydeadzone=).

Et le garde-fou de volume=, justement CITÉ en modèle par celui de joydeadzone,
était lui-même aveugle au NaN :

    if (c.volume < 0.0f) c.volume = 0.0f;
    if (c.volume > 1.0f) c.volume = 1.0f;

Toute comparaison avec NaN étant fausse, « volume=nan » traversait les deux
tests intact. Le test existant couvrait volume=42 et volume=-3, jamais le NaN.

Conséquence mesurée : le gain NaN se propage dans synthBlock, qui recopie
l'échantillon dans l'état du filtre passe-haut (hpfX1_ = s ; hpfY0_ = hp). Une
fois ces deux membres à NaN, tout échantillon suivant l'est aussi — le son est
MORT pour la session, même après avoir remis le fader à 1 et débranché le DAC.
Seul un reset machine (YM2149::reset) le rétablit. hpfX1_/hpfY0_ étant
sérialisés, un save-state pris entre-temps emporte l'empoisonnement.

Mesure avant/après (mix_dac=nan, un bloc synthétisé, puis fader réparé) :
  avant : out[0]=nan          -> apres reparation : out[0]=nan
  apres : out[0]=-0.499023    -> apres reparation : out[0]=0.055149

Correctif : helper mixGain() (NaN -> défaut, sinon bornage 0..2 comme le
curseur 0..200 % de la page Sound) et NaN écarté avant le bornage de volume=.
Le bornage au plus proche est conservé (volume=-3 -> 0, volume=42 -> 1).
Régression ajoutée à neost-selftest, à côté du bloc « valeurs hostiles ».

Deux correctifs : souris du port 0, lignes GPIP au chargement d'état

1. Port 0 pris par un joystick : seuls les MOUVEMENTS souris étaient coupés.
   Les BOUTONS passaient encore par onMouseButton (chemin événementiel), donc
   les clics hôte atteignaient le ST alors que l'interface annonce « the host
   mouse is unplugged » — et ils empiétaient sur la ligne feu du port 0, qu'ils
   partagent sur le vrai matériel. Au passage, le delta curseur est désormais
   CONSOMMÉ même quand la souris est débranchée : il s'accumulait sans borne et
   repartait en un saut géant au rebranchement.

2. loadState : portsApply() forçait les lignes d'entrée GPIP au repos
   (setRs232Ri(false)/setRs232Dcd(true)) APRÈS que mfp.serialize les ait
   restaurées — sur TOUT chargement, même sans aucun périphérique branché.
   L'état RS-232 restauré était donc perdu, et le forçage passant par
   gpipSetLine (détection de FRONT) pouvait lever une IRQ GPIP fantôme.
   portsApply prend un drapeau `fromLoad` : au chargement il laisse les lignes
   restaurées tranquilles et ne re-dérive que GPIP7 (bouton Multiface), dont le
   support monButton_ est hors snapshot alors que PortDevices::pressed_ y est.

  avant le fix : ri=1 gpipInput=$F5 → ri=0 gpipInput=$B5 (GPIP6 écrasé)

events.title: Merge Layer 14's first pass: the floor dither and the text palettes
events.message:
Merge Layer 14's first pass: the floor dither and the text palettes

The deck floor at half intensity — logical 0 dithered 2x2 with logical 1,
which is black on every deck — because the BBC palette is fully saturated
where the C64's is not. It costs nothing in the main loop: the pattern is
baked into the charset at deck load, from inside BuildCharset's own
character walk, and the parity falls out of the byte index.

It turned out to add a FIFTH TONE to a four-colour mode, and decks 0, 5
and 9 spend it: white dithered to the grey their C64 floor actually is.
That made 'four distinct physical colours' the wrong rule, and both
places that enforced it now test four distinct TONES.

Dithering the static screens' backgrounds was tried and reverted — it
cost the text's readability. They take a solid per-deck background
instead, deckTextPal, which is deckPalette with logical 0 replaced and
sits 64 bytes along so one offset picks between them. The deck plan is
the exception: it is a picture of the deck, so it keeps the deck's own
colours. Every switch runs before the draw it belongs to.

Bank 4 came out of it 22 bytes better off than it went in, then spent
most of that again; main RAM and bank 4 both end at 2 bytes free.

docs/layer-14-visual.md carries the four decisions and the numbers.

events.title: Layer 14: set the palette before the screen, not after it
events.message:
Layer 14: set the palette before the screen, not after it

KC: all four switches ran after their draw, so every screen was painted
in the outgoing palette and only corrected once finished — a visible
wrong-coloured pass on every transition.

Each moved to the routine that DECIDES the transition rather than the one
that completes it: ConMenuInit4 for the console open (and ConsoleEnter
now calls it first), ConMenu4's deck arm for the plan, ConPageKeys4's
leave arm for the way back, and InfoCall before it pages bank 7. The way
back to the deck was already right — RedrawAll sets it before its own
draw.

Three of the four are tail calls on arms that already ended in RTS, so
they cost two bytes each rather than three, and ConMarker4 gave three
back when the call left it.

ConsoleEnter calling ConMenuInit4 first is a reorder of game code, and it
is safe because that routine only writes flags — conSel and the key edges
— which nothing in ConsoleOpen reads; the marker is still drawn after.

SetPalette and SetTextPal now preserve X, because InfoCall calls one
before paging and IsEntry takes its selector in X. SetPalPlay clobbers X
too, so the save outlives it: the routine ends in JSR SetPalPlay and an
RTS rather than the JMP it used to. Five bytes, and it removes the trap
that had already caught this once.

Verified in jsbeeb: the 001 screen is drawn in its text palette from the
first frame. Main RAM and bank 4 are both at 2 bytes free.

events.message:
build.ps1: stop when the deck palettes are newer than colours.asm

KC's hand-picked text-screen backgrounds did not appear in a rebuild,
and the reason was not the reader: build.ps1 does not run export_bbc.py,
so src/data/colours.asm was simply the old one. That is deliberate for
the exporters whose input is the C64 listing — it is supplied locally
rather than checked in — and it is fine for a CODE change. It is a trap
for a DATA one: tools/deck_palettes.json is hand-edited in the lab, and
a build after editing it silently used the old palettes with nothing to
say why.

So compare the two timestamps and throw, naming the command to run. Both
files have to exist for the check to fire, so a tree without the listing
is unaffected until it edits the JSON — at which point stopping is
exactly right, because its build would otherwise be wrong.

the window closes itself.

events.title: engine+ste+ecs: the v0.9.7 title regression — palettes commit before the blits, and a replaced CLUT re-quantises eagerly
events.message:
engine+ste+ecs: the v0.9.7 title regression — palettes commit before the blits, and a replaced CLUT re-quantises eagerly

Field report + archaeology: the titles 'displayed perfectly a few versions
ago'. Verified — v0.9.6's are clean; v0.9.7's are not. 87251793 (v0.9.7)
replaced the port's hand-written intro (which pre-installed each screen's
palette) with the engine's own jt919/l19d4 sequence, whose Mac order is
blit-then-commit. On the Mac that whole body runs inside a frame; the
planar backends stamp the visible planes AS the blit runs (seconds at
8 MHz), so each title rendered quantised under the PREVIOUS screen's
palette — the yellow wizard and candy-striped credits. The DOS original
(DOSBox, 0.35 s sampling) shows every title fully-formed and correct, so
this was never faithful in effect.

Three-part fix, verified frame-by-frame in Hatari (STE, real-time):
- l19d4 commits each picture's palette BEFORE its blits (the Mac's net
  frame; the original tail commits skip via the CLUT-unchanged guard),
  and holds presents across the compose (qd_present_hold).
- st/ecs_clut_major_change(): a wholesale CLUT replacement (>=64 entries
  moved clearly) vetoes the registers-only repalette — the split
  heuristic cannot see 'everything moved' — and re-quantises EAGERLY at
  install time, so draw-time stamps after the commit use the new cut.
  Same total cost: the present's CLUT-unchanged guard then skips the
  re-band this replaces; the walk's CLUT alternation stays on the
  palette cache.
- Chunky backends (Falcon/TT/Nova) get the ordering fix for free: the
  commit-first order removes their draw-vs-install colour flash too.

Wizard + Forgotten Realms + credits now compose and settle in their own
colours; settled frames match v0.9.6's.

engine: the plate cache keys on the label TEXT, not just its pointer — the treasure bar drew POOL over EXIT

A1200/ECS real-hardware report: on the treasure screen, SHARE the platinum
then TAKE the ring and the command bar shows POOL where EXIT belongs;
clicking that "POOL" presses (and acts as) EXIT. Reproduced identically on
the Falcon — shared-code, not ECS.

The A/B convicted the command-button plate cache (#138-#141): with
FRUA_NOPLATECACHE the re-laid bar is correct (VIEW POOL EXIT); with the
cache it replays VIEW TAKE POOL. The cache key was (label POINTER, count,
top, left, state) — but a bar re-layout rebuilds its label strings in the
SAME pool slots, so the slot that held "TAKE" now holds "POOL" at the same
address and position, and the stale plate replays. The pressed repaint
misses (state bit differs), which is why the clicked button flashed its
true label — the tell that convicted stale pixels over stale logic.

Fix: a djb2 hash of the label C string (capped at 32 bytes) joins the key;
find and capture both carry it. A reused slot with new text now misses and
repaints; identical text still hits, so the 82->23-tick bar win is intact.

VIEW POOL EXIT with the cache ON, matching the no-cache control frame.

events.message:
ecs: disarm the sprites at display takeover — the pointer-over-title and the left-edge garbage (A1200 real hardware)

The takeover DMACON write only SET raster+copper — sprite DMA stayed
however Workbench left it (on), and the BPLCON2=0 line commented "no
sprites" sets sprite PRIORITY, not sprite enable. On real silicon the
Intuition pointer therefore kept displaying over the title screens (the
original shows no pointer until the menu), and dangling sprite fetches drew
a garbage column at the left edge. Cycle-exact amiberry showed neither,
which is why five weeks of headless runs never caught it.

Fix: clear DMAF_SPRITE (a plain clear, not SETCLR) and disarm all eight
channels (SPRxCTL=0, data words cleared — an armed sprite keeps displaying
its last data even with DMA off) before enabling raster+copper; shutdown
re-sets sprite DMA before LoadView(oldview) so the Workbench pointer
returns after quit. The AGA backend already had the null-sprite discipline
(kept from the retired sprite cursor, #64) and is untouched.

Needs the real A1200/A500 to confirm — the emulator renders identically
either way (verified: boot + title unchanged headless).
events.author: slaapliedje

events.title: installer: the Install icon exits cleanly — CD off the floppy before running
events.message:
installer: the Install icon exits cleanly — CD off the floppy before running

A1200 (WB 3.2, Installer 47.19): a fully SUCCESSFUL install ended with
"Please insert volume OpenUA-ECS-1 in any drive" and the install window
stuck open. The launcher script runs FROM the engine disk, so its shell's
current directory is that floppy's VOLUME; when the Installer hands control
back, AmigaDOS re-validates the CD for the next script line — and the disk
in the drive by then is the last data disk. The WAIT tooltype then kept the
IconX window up on top of it.

Fixes: the launcher does `CD RAM:` first and uses absolute paths throughout;
the WAIT tooltype is gone (the Installer route closes its window itself) and
the instdisk fallback branch pauses explicitly instead ("Press RETURN to
close"); the redundant (protect uaconv +e) tail line is dropped (copyfiles
preserves the bits). instdisk now derives the drive from PROGDIR: (where the
binary was loaded from) rather than the current directory, so the CD change
cannot confuse it — verified headless: CD RAM:, instdisk run from a subdir,
full data+engine install lands. Also: uaconv.c's header caught up with
ADR-0019 (it is an optional tool now, not the install path).

The end-of-install requester itself cannot fire in the harness (filesystem2
volumes are never "removed"), so the exit-clean confirmation needs the next
real A1200 install.

events.title: Layer 14: a solid text-screen background per deck, not a dither
events.message:
Layer 14: a solid text-screen background per deck, not a dither

KC, having looked at DECISION 3 in game: the dither is right on the deck
and wrong behind text — it costs readability and the screens come out
messy. DECISION 3 is reverted in full; the deck keeps its dither.

The problem it was trying to solve stands and is worse than the dither:
several deck floors are far too bright to read white text on — yellow,
cyan, and the white of decks 0, 5 and 9. So the static text screens get a
solid background of their own, chosen per deck.

It touches no drawing code. Those screens already draw their background
as LOGICAL 0, so only what logical 0 looks like changes. export_bbc.py
emits .deckTextPal — the deck's four with logical 0 replaced —
immediately after .deckPalette, so the two are 64 bytes apart and
SetTextPal is SetPalette with palBase 64 higher: no second lookup, no
test in the loop, and the restore is the existing SetPalette. main.asm
asserts the adjacency. The 64 bytes cost nothing: colourMap is page
aligned and there were 226 bytes of padding in front of it.

In at ConMenuInit4 (which covers the deck plan and the database, both
opened inside the console) and at InfoCall. Out at RedrawAll, because
every way back to the deck ends in a full redraw and putting it there
cannot be forgotten by a new exit path.

LoadDeck no longer calls SetPalette, and that is the fix rather than an
economy: the 001 screen is up ACROSS that LoadDeck — it holds the redraw
back — so the deck's colours overrode the text background every time.
ReframeView returns early while a screen is up, so the deck's palette now
lands exactly when the deck does.

The other thing that bit: IsEntry takes its screen selector in X, and
SetPalette leaves X = $FF, which is IS_BLANK. Calling SetTextPal before
JSR IsEntry turned every information screen into the blank. It goes
after, where X is spent.

palette_lab.py gains a fifth picker beside the four logicals and a "text
screen" checkbox that shows the deck through that palette. Colours
already used by logicals 1-3 are disabled and export_bbc.py refuses a
collision, because anything drawn in the background colour vanishes.

19 bytes of bank 4 and 3 of the low overlay, leaving 10 and 1.

events.message:
installer: pure-copy installs — no conversion step, no prompts (ADR-0019)

With the on-load converter back on for the Amiga, the installers stop
converting: instdisk drops its post-engine uaconv run and the "Converting
the art for the Amiga (one time)..." message; the Workbench Install script
drops its conversion message and the delete-the-originals askbool. An
install is now: copy the data disks, copy the engine, done — the engine
converts each art library silently the first time it opens it.

uaconv still ships on the engine disks and installs with the engine, as an
OPTIONAL tool (pre-convert everything / reclaim ~5 MB with -d) — offered in
the README, never run or prompted by the installers. The release-text
template loses its "the Amiga engine does NOT convert DOS art on the fly"
note, which ADR-0019 made false.

events.title: engine: on-load DOS-art conversion back ON for the Amiga (ADR-0019, supersedes ADR-0015)
events.message:
engine: on-load DOS-art conversion back ON for the Amiga (ADR-0019, supersedes ADR-0015)

ADR-0015 compiled the on-load .tlb->.ctl converter out on the Amiga over an
intermittent art-loader hang (2026-07-18, root cause open) — bisected BEFORE
the engine moved onto the big StackSwap stack, which the ADR itself implicates
("raising the stack moved the stall"). Re-tested on the current engine: five
cold .tlb-only autoplay runs (3 AGA, 2 ECS), every touched library forced
through the on-load converter during boot and the walk — all five reached the
menu, converted, completed, and wrote back .ctl files bit-exact to
make gamedata-dos output. No stall.

The Amiga now converts DOS art silently on first touch exactly like the
Falcon/ST (once ever — the .ctl is written back). FRUA_ARTCONV_OFF remains
the bisect hatch. Full rationale + the rollback path: ADR-0019.

The A500 verdict: with the disk cache (each scene once, ever) and the
viewport groups (~1 s on the walk), the ceremony outweighed the wait it

converting). The notice earned its keep when a cold quant froze the screen
~17 s with no way to tell converting from hung; that world is gone.

Removed: ecs_notice, the progress bar, the bar-driven interrupt-state
sampler (its VBL-starvation diagnosis is long closed), the plat_bard
start/stop pair, and the grouped-path progress adapter. The quant now just
runs. Verified: five .tlb-only autoplay runs (3 AGA, 2 ECS) boot, convert
and complete with the notice-free engine.

events.title: skills: the porting kit, distilled — port-ssi-mac-68k, planar-display-kit, hardware-media-kit
events.message:
skills: the porting kit, distilled — port-ssi-mac-68k, planar-display-kit, hardware-media-kit

Three skills capturing what this project discovered the hard way, so the
next SSI title (the ST only ever got Curse of the Azure Bonds; the Amiga
got the whole Gold Box line) starts from the kit instead of from zero:

- port-ssi-mac-68k: what is reusable as-is (toolchain, Mac Toolbox shim,
  HAL, harnesses, media pipeline) vs per-game (the decompilation), the
  THINK C lift workflow and its alias/A5/JT[452] traps, the oracle-build
  discipline, and the Gold Box angle — DAX/DAA art formats already
  reverse-engineered here (docs/dax-format.md, tools/dax_decode.py), and
  the fan-module recreations OpenUA can already play on the ST via uainst.

- planar-display-kit: the 256-colour-art-on-16/32-colour-hardware stack —
  banded quantizer + phase profiler, palette groups (#139: split at
  content edges only, never arbitrary boundaries = the #40 seam), the
  CLUT-guard/repalette/split-guard cache family, the disk palette cache
  with its three paid-for traps, and the one-binary runtime-A/B rule.

- hardware-media-kit: FlashFloppy geometry (rotation, not data rate),
  block-based packing, extract-and-cmp verification, the three install
  routes with the Installer-language and GEM traps, stick layouts, and
  the release discipline (all betas prerelease, ratio-based integrity).
events.author: slaapliedje

events.title: ecs: viewport palette groups — the walk re-band drops ~9.5 s -> ~1.1 s (#139 port)
events.message:
ecs: viewport palette groups — the walk re-band drops ~9.5 s -> ~1.1 s (#139 port)

The ECS re-band ran the median cut per band: 25 cuts a frame, and the phase
profile put cut+buckets at 86% of a ~149,000 raster-line (~9.5 s) re-band on
the 7 MHz 68000. The ST solved this in #139 by splitting at the only lines
where the content really changes — the first-person viewport edges — and
cutting once per group. Ported: with a rendered viewport in the frame, the
re-band cuts 3 groups (chrome above / viewport / chrome below), 32 colours
each. 96 slots against a walk frame whole ~63 colours, so fidelity holds.
Measured on the walk: 16,400-18,900 rl per grouped re-band = ~1.1 s, ~8x.

Screens WITHOUT a viewport (title, menus, event pictures) keep the full 25
per-band cuts: one-time work the disk cache replays forever, per-band
fidelity on big pictures is worth keeping, and their existing cache entries
stay bit-valid (that path is untouched — boot re-bands measured identical
to the pre-change baseline).

Two mechanisms the port needed:

1. dsp_viewport_note: the engine announce of the rendered viewport rect.
   dsp_viewport_commit is gated on the backend supplying a scratch, and the
   ECS supplies none (it renders straight into the engine surface) — the
   first cut registered the commit hook and grouping never engaged. The
   note fires unconditionally at the end of every 3D render; no listener,
   no effect (the ST registers none and is unaffected).

2. A CONTENT fingerprint, not present-order bookkeeping: the announce
   samples 16 spread pixels of the rendered viewport; the re-band re-samples
   and groups only when they still match. A full-screen picture or menu
   overwrites them (falls back to 25 bands — no #40 seam from splitting a
   picture on a stale boundary); HUD/bar updates do not. The first scheme
   cleared a flag per present and most walk re-bands missed it — order
   between render, CLUT install and presents is not stable; content is.
   Verified live: the caravan portrait (drawn over the viewport area)
   correctly re-bands ungrouped; 3 of 3 true walk re-bands grouped.

video.cfg vpgroups=off restores the old path wholesale (one binary, the
runtime-A/B discipline). Falcon/ST/AGA builds link and make test passes;
the AGA/RTG/Falcon chunky backends are untouched (no quantizer there).
