events.title: MIDI : page dédiée, port ALSA sous Linux, panique et journal repliable
events.message:
MIDI : page dédiée, port ALSA sous Linux, panique et journal repliable

« Ajoute la sortie GM et le port MIDI dans l'UI » supposait qu'ils existent : sous
Linux, NON. MidiOutMac.hpp le disait — « hors macOS la classe compile en coquille
vide ». Une page les proposant aurait affiché deux cases mortes.

PORT MIDI RÉEL SOUS LINUX. MidiOutMac devient MidiOutHost (le nom mentait) et gagne
un backend séquenceur ALSA : un port SOURCE « NeoST MIDI OUT » auquel n'importe quel
synthé s'abonne — FluidSynth, Qsynth, un DAW, un expandeur. C'est l'équivalent du
port CoreMIDI de macOS, et la BONNE réponse au répertoire General MIDI du moment :
un MT-32 ne sait pas le jouer. L'encodage passe par snd_midi_event_encode, qui gère
running status et SysEx. Dépendance OPTIONNELLE (pkg-config alsa) : sans elle le
port est simplement indisponible, et l'interface le dit.

VÉRIFIÉ EN FONCTIONNEMENT, pas seulement compilé :
    [midi-out] ALSA port "NeoST MIDI OUT" open
    aconnect -l -> client 128: 'NeoST' / 0 'NeoST MIDI OUT'

PAGE « MIDI » dans la fenêtre Configuration, séparée de Son : la sortie MIDI est un
CÂBLAGE vers l'extérieur, pas un réglage de volume. Elle réunit le port virtuel (avec
le nom du backend, ALSA ou CoreMIDI), le synthé GM — grisé hors macOS avec la raison,
plutôt qu'une case inerte —, le MT-32/CM-32L et son modèle, la fiche de bouclage
OUT->IN (jusqu'ici cachée dans le menu Machine), et un avertissement en clair : un
fichier GM envoyé au MT-32 joue les MAUVAIS instruments, la carte LA n'étant pas la
carte GM.

PANIQUE. Bouton « Panic - all notes off » : CC 120/121/123 sur les 16 canaux, envoyés
AUX DEUX destinations (le MT-32 est un synthé à part, il ne voit pas le flux de
MidiOutHost). Un synthé ne relâche jamais une note tout seul — couper une sortie en
plein accord la laissait tenir indéfiniment.

JOURNAL REPLIABLE. Un fichier GM sur un MT-32 déclenche « Rhythm: Attempted to play
unmapped key NN » à chaque coup de percussion : des centaines de lignes identiques
qui noyaient tout. Les répétitions consécutives sont maintenant comptées et résumées.

Textes de la page volontairement courts et RELUS À L'ÉCRAN : ma première version
était coupée par la largeur du panneau, comme sur la page Hard disks ce matin.

run_all.py --tier fast : TOUS LES PALIERS OK.

events.title: wonderboy/kit: batch 44 phase B — the disk wall is a seam; the title loads
events.message:
wonderboy/kit: batch 44 phase B — the disk wall is a seam; the title loads

THE WALL CROSSED: the sector driver's 1,644 bytes are a SEAM, not a
model. disk_load_file ($5e7c) is the lowest routine with file-shaped
inputs (a 12-char DOS name in, bytes at a destination, 0/negative
out — the resource table's rows ARE the names); everything below is
sector-shaped. The band's crossings enumerated as a SET of four —
the seam's one call, an INTERRUPT crossing (the VBL's floppy-motor

events.title: tools/midi_simplify.py : SMF modernes -> lisibles par un séquenceur ST
events.message:
tools/midi_simplify.py : SMF modernes -> lisibles par un séquenceur ST

Cubase Lite plante à la lecture de fichiers MIDI pourtant valides. Mesuré sur un lot
de 32 fichiers, plusieurs causes se cumulent — aucune n'est « le » coupable :

  · format 1 avec jusqu'à 41 PISTES (blues2), 25, 24, 23… ;
  · division 480 PPQN dans 15 fichiers, valeur de DAW moderne, là où Cubase ST
    travaille en 384 ; delta maximal de 236 660 ;
  · 1 528 méta-événements de texte, paroles et marqueurs, plus 173 « port » (0x21,
    POSTÉRIEUR à ces séquenceurs) et 187 « spécifique constructeur » (0x7F) ;
  · SysEx dans 10 fichiers ;
  · jusqu'à 66 Ko par fichier sur une machine de 1 Mo ;
  · noms hors 8.3, que le GEMDOS ne sait pas montrer.

L'outil produit, au choix : format 0 une piste (défaut, le plus universellement lu)
ou --per-channel, format 1 avec une piste par canal MIDI. 96 PPQN, rééchelonnage sur
les temps ABSOLUS puis re-différenciation (le faire sur les deltas ferait dériver le
morceau), méta réduits à tempo/mesure/armure/fin, plus aucun SysEx, noms 8.3
majuscules uniques et un index NOMS.TXT en CRLF lisible depuis le ST.

--per-channel n'est pas un caprice : mesuré, le format 0 faisait GROSSIR cinq
fichiers (66 -> 73 ko) parce que fusionner les pistes fait alterner les statuts et
neutralise le statut courant — or la charge utile est à 80 % des Note-On, exactement
ce que ce mécanisme comprime. Une piste par canal rend chaque piste homogène :
776 -> 702 ko au lieu de 766.

VÉRIFIÉ que rien de musical n'est perdu, sur les deux jeux : 107 370 note-on,
107 376 note-off, 6 568 contrôleurs, 1 813 pitch-bends — identiques aux originaux,
zéro écart sur 32 fichiers. Et les propriétés visées sont atteintes : 96 PPQN
partout, 0 SysEx, delta maximal ramené de 236 660 à 937, 17 pistes au pire.

Les fichiers .mid de l'utilisateur ne sont PAS commités (contenu tiers) : l'outil
est là pour les regénérer.

events.title: ecs: disk-backed palette cache — the 16-entry cap was THE "converts every screen" bug
events.message:
ecs: disk-backed palette cache — the 16-entry cap was THE "converts every screen" bug

The palette cache held EPC_MAX=16 blobs in RAM and, once full, STOPPED
caching (the add was gated on e_pc_n < EPC_MAX with no eviction). A dungeon
shows far more than 16 distinct scenes, so every frame past the 16th
re-quantised on EVERY view, forever — the A500 "it converts every single
screen" misery. The PROGDIR fix only helped the first 16.

Now the KEYS live in RAM (8 bytes each, EPC_CAP=2048) and the 8.8 KB blobs
live on disk in PALCACHE.ECS: a cache hit reads its blob back, a miss
appends a new one. Effectively unbounded, and it FREES ~141 KB of RAM
(the old 16*8800 blob table is gone) — welcome on a 2 MB ECS machine.

Robustness: the entry count is derived from the file SIZE and new entries
are appended with plain "ab", so there is no in-place header rewrite — an
"r+b" update the Amiga ncrt0 stdio would not do reliably (the first cut
used r+b and silently never grew past the initial entries). File layout is
unchanged (hdr + n*(key+blob)), so v1 caches still load; e_pc_last skips the
disk read when the wanted blob is already live.

Verified headless (ECS, User-Startup CD SYS:): cold boot creates the file
and appends; warm boot loads the keys and HITS them with zero quant; a
deterministic miss (truncate the file to one entry) quantises once and
appends back — the file grows, which the capped version could never do.
Each scene now quantises ONCE, EVER, then reads from disk forever.

events.title: Pages servi par la CI : wasm/ sort du dépôt
events.message:
Pages servi par la CI : wasm/ sort du dépôt

Le bundle WebAssembly n'est plus commité. Le job `wasm` de release.yml le dépose en
ARTEFACT Pages et un job `pages` le publie (build_type=workflow). Une seule
construction Emscripten par push : le job existant sert les deux usages, l'archive
de release et la démo en ligne. wasm/ passe au .gitignore ; un
`cmake --build build-web --target neost-web` le régénère en local.

CE QUE ÇA RÈGLE. En build_type=legacy, Pages servait la branche : le dépôt était
publié EN ENTIER sur habib256.github.io/neost/, ROM Atari et jeux compris — une
contrepartie assumée faute de mieux (TODO.md § contenu propriétaire). Le
déploiement par artefact ne publie QUE le bundle. Et la CI ne pose plus de commit
de bot sur main à chaque push, ce que faisait la recommission du bundle.

L'URL CHANGE : la démo passe de /neost/wasm/ à la racine /neost/. Le lien du README
suit, et DEV.md est réécrit en conséquence.

Troisième état d'un aller-retour assumé, consigné pour qu'on ne le refasse pas :
garde de fraîcheur (tools/wasm_stamp.sh — rouge sans réparer, 2026-08-19 et -21) →
recommission par la CI (réparait, mais commit de bot à chaque push, 8d69296) →
déploiement par artefact (ici). Le motif du retour en arrière d'alors — « le bundle
doit rester dans l'arbre de travail » — reste vrai en local : le dossier est
seulement désindexé, pas supprimé.

Le job publish ne dépend PAS de pages : un déploiement raté ne bloquera pas une
release.

events.title: bug hunt 3 : MT-32 et bruits de lecteur figés à 48 kHz malgré la fréquence négociée
events.message:
bug hunt 3 : MT-32 et bruits de lecteur figés à 48 kHz malgré la fréquence négociée

Audio calcule rate_ = dev->sampleRate ? … : cfg.sampleRate, avec en commentaire
« fréquence réelle NÉGOCIÉE » : le code prévoit donc explicitement que le
périphérique n'accorde pas toujours les 48 kHz demandés, et toute la chaîne suit
rate_. Deux consommateurs y échappaient, tous deux initialisés sur la constante :

    mt32.open(…, 48000, …)                    (main.cpp)
    drive.init(…, 48000)                      (main.cpp)

Sur un matériel qui ne rend que 44,1 kHz, eux seuls sortaient donc ~8,8 % trop haut
et dérivaient du reste du mixage. Le MT-32 étant passé actif par défaut hier, le
défaut concerne désormais tout le monde.

Corrigé : accesseur Audio::rate(), variable audioRate utilisée par midiOutApply (la
lambda s'exécute AVANT que l'objet Audio n'existe), et réalignement juste après
audio.start() quand la fréquence rendue diffère — chemin rare, sans effet quand
48 kHz est accordé.

DÉMONTRÉ, pas seulement raisonné : en forçant la demande à 44100, le journal donne
« device negotiated 44100 Hz (not 48000) — realigning MT-32 and drive sounds » suivi
d'une réouverture du MT-32. Cas nominal revérifié après restauration : 48 kHz, aucun
message, une seule ouverture.

EXPLORÉ, RIEN TROUVÉ — la passe visait la couverture du save-state, que --tier fast
n'exerce QUE dans la configuration par défaut (le commentaire de run_all.py rappelle
qu'une régression v10 y a vécu des semaines) :
  · déterminisme save-state sur 10 configurations (st/megast/ste/megaste, mono,
    4 Mo, ACSI 3 Go, UltraSatan 2 slots, GEMDOS, disquette+HD) : toutes identiques ;
  · 11 états CORROMPUS (tronqués, vidés, aléatoires, 6 bits retournés) chargés sous
    ASan/UBSan : 11 rejets propres avec message, 0 rapport sanitizer ;
  · état rechargé après DISPARITION de ses images disque : pas de plantage, et la
    garde fp nulle de Acsi::cmdReadSector vérifiée à la lecture du code ;
  · 9 fichiers neost.cfg hostiles (mem géant, négatifs, chemins de 20 000
    caractères, doublons, binaire, sans '=') via --from-cfg sous ASan : 0 rapport.

run_all.py --tier fast : TOUS LES PALIERS OK.

events.title: installer: ship DOS .tlb + convert at install with uaconv; include Save A
events.message:
installer: ship DOS .tlb + convert at install with uaconv; include Save A

The Amiga now ships the authentic DOS .tlb art and converts it once at
install (the engine cannot convert at runtime, ADR-0015), rather than
shipping our derived .ctl. The flow:

- mkdatadisks defaults every target to .tlb again; the Amiga set carries the
  DOS art and uaconv converts it in place at install.
- instdisk, after the engine step, runs the installed <dest>/uaconv <dest>
  (SystemTags) — the DOS art is converted with no extra user action, and
  uaconv asks whether to delete the .tlb originals.
- the Workbench Install (AmigaOS Installer) route ships uaconv too and, after
  copying the data, protects it +e and runs it, with an askbool for whether to
  delete the originals (uaconv -d, since the Installer run has no stdin).
- uaconv and uaconv.info ride on the AGA disk and ECS disk 1, and are in
  ENGINE.LST so the instdisk route installs them.

Saves: mkdatadisks shipped the .DSN-root save CRUFT (headless-test leftovers)
because it skipped all of SAVE/. It now drops every savgam*/vault*/cch and
re-adds ONLY SAVE/SAVGAMA.CSV + SAVE/VAULTA.DAT — the authentic Save A, the
sole save on the original HEIRS disks. Placing it needed the Amiga image
writer to recurse (it was one-level); it now walks the staged tree at any
depth. Verified: Save A lands in HEIRS.DSN/SAVE/ bit-exact on both Amiga and
Atari, and instdisk->uaconv converts a .tlb install bit-exact on the 68000.

events.title: installer: uaconv — the Amiga one-time DOS-art converter (.tlb -> .ctl)
events.message:
installer: uaconv — the Amiga one-time DOS-art converter (.tlb -> .ctl)

The Amiga engine cannot convert DOS art at runtime (ADR-0015), so the art
must be converted at install. This is that converter: it scans the OpenUA
folder and its .DSN design sub-folders for DOS HLIB .tlb art, writes the Mac
GLIB .ctl twin the engine loads, then offers to delete the now-redundant
.tlb originals to reclaim the space.

Portable C over stdio + the artconv core (the same one uainst uses for fan
modules); the only platform split is the directory scan (dos.library
Examine/ExNext on the Amiga, POSIX readdir on the host, so the convert path
is host-testable). Colour convert only — no mono synthesis (that is the ST
mono build. install-time job). Borrows uainst_run_big_stack (asl_amiga.c) for
the stack artconv needs.

Verified: host and Amiga (68000) both convert the 23 base libraries + a
.DSN design library BIT-EXACT to make gamedata-dos; the keep/delete prompt
works and defaults to keep on EOF; a second run finds nothing (idempotent).

events.title: ecs: palette cache to PROGDIR: — it was writing to the CWD, so it never persisted
events.message:
ecs: palette cache to PROGDIR: — it was writing to the CWD, so it never persisted

The ECS palette cache (PALCACHE.ECS) is content-keyed and written on every
quantiser miss, so a repeat view of a picture should be instant. On the A500
it re-converted every boot: the cache used a BARE relative path
("PALCACHE.ECS"), and frua boots with the CWD set elsewhere (the mount
User-Startup does `CD SYS:` before running it; a Workbench-icon launch sets
CWD to the drawer, a Shell launch to wherever you were) — so the file was
written to SYS:, never found again, and every boot was a cold cache. DBG.LOG
never had this problem because it already uses PROGDIR:. Same fix here.

Verified headless (ECS mount, User-Startup CD SYS:): cold boot writes
PROGDIR:PALCACHE.ECS (2 entries, 17624 b) and quantises twice; warm boot logs
"palette cache entries loaded = 2", quantises ZERO times, file unchanged.

events.title: installer: Amiga data disks ship .ctl art (the engine cannot convert), quieter disk polling, and a drawer icon
events.message:
installer: Amiga data disks ship .ctl art (the engine cannot convert), quieter disk polling, and a drawer icon

Three fixes from the A500 real-hardware run (2026-08-22), after the
Install icon itself started working:

1. THE GAME DID NOT RUN. "Please insert disk [" with a sword cursor,
   right after a one-second "CONVERTING ART" bar. That is the engine
   cold-disk retry (jt987/l157c) on a missing resource: ALWAYS.CTL,
   "LBLoad: Bad Lib". The DATA disks ship DOS .tlb art (ART=tlb), and
   the ATARI engine converts .tlb->.ctl on first touch (boot.c
   ua_open_art fallback) — but the AMIGA engine does NOT: ADR-0015
   compiled that conversion out, and instdisk copies files verbatim, so
   a .tlb-only Amiga install has no path to the .ctl the engine loads.
   mkdatadisks now defaults amiga to ART=ctl (ship the converted libs,
   23 files, 6 disks); Atari keeps tlb. Reproduced by hiding the .ctl
   twins in the ECS mount (ALWAYS.CTL "Bad Lib"); .ctl-only boots to the
   SSI title with every library loaded.

2. THE POLLING WAS TOO AGGRESSIVE. Each poll of an empty DF0: raised
   AmigaDOS system requester "Please insert a disk in DF0", once a
   second — the installer looked like it was nagging. pr_WindowPtr = -1
   turns the DOS requesters off for the process (a missing disk is then
   a plain open failure, which the poll already treats as "not yet"),
   and the poll interval went 1s -> 2s.

3. NO DRAWER ICON. The Installer-script route makes one via
   (makedir (infos)); the plain instdisk route (WB 3.1, no Installer)
   did not, so the OpenUA drawer had no Workbench icon. instdisk now
   writes <dest>.info from an embedded 346-byte drawer icon
   (installer/drawer_icon.h). Verified under AmigaDOS: DH0:ICONTEST.info
   written byte-identical.

Also fixed a host-only bug the harness surfaced: wait_for_disk spun
forever on a closed stdin (now gives up). make test 471 passed.

and rename-aside rescue landed, now covering every pass). The

events.title: Layer 14: the static screens dither their background too
events.message:
Layer 14: the static screens dither their background too

The deck plan, the droid database pages and the 001 information screens
all lay the deck's logical 0 down as their background, so beside a
dithered deck they were the solid, saturated version of exactly the
colour the dither exists to soften.

dcMask moves to main RAM (lowbss, in the spare bytes at the tail of the
reclaimed workspace). It sat in bank 4 beside BuildCharset that writes
it, and bank 7 cannot see bank 4 — the same reason the string table and
the droid mirrors are main RAM. Absolute addressing costs the same
either side, so bank 4 gets its 2 storage bytes back.

Two entry points in bank 7, because the two costs are different.
DitherCell is 16 bytes at pnDst and rides on DbGlyph: FontCell STORES a
cell, background and all, so a glyph punched a solid hole in the
dithered field, and dithering per glyph keeps the per-pass cost to what
was actually drawn — which matters, because the database is a browser
that redraws its name line every pass. DitherBuf is the whole 10K at
about 170 ms: DbClear ends with it, so every caller gets it, and
ConDeck7 ends with it, which covers 640 plan cells without a call each.

PoDraw's portrait rectangle writes the pattern straight into its clear
instead, being a loop with a byte in hand already. Bit 0 of a buffer
address IS the scanline parity — a row is 640 and a cell 16, both even —
so every one of these gets the phase from Y alone with no extra state.

IsBlank zeroes the masks: it runs at boot, before any deck load has
written them, and lowbss is SKIPped, so DbClear's pass would otherwise
have scattered whatever the RAM held over the buffer the title prints
on.

THE CONSOLE MAIN MENU IS NOT DONE. ConDraw is bank 6, which has 16 bytes
and needs 55; the play buffer is main RAM so a bank-7 routine could do
the work, but only main RAM can page a bank and the cheapest shim is 14
bytes of a region that has 2. ConClear and ConMarkClear want ~30 more
between them. The three routes are costed in docs/layer-14-visual.md.

Verified in jsbeeb: the 001 screen — dithered field, white text with no
solid box behind any glyph, portrait rectangle dithered with it. That
screen exercises all three primitives the database pages use, so they
follow from it; the deck plan's own path is built but not yet seen in
game. The title screen is clean black.

events.title: Layer 14: the dither is a fifth tone, and decks 0 and 9 spend it
events.message:
Layer 14: the dither is a fifth tone, and decks 0 and 9 spend it

KC's palettes, after seeing the dither in game. All sixteen decks now
have a black logical 1 and so all sixteen dither - which finally makes
lowcode.asm's long-standing "logical 1 is black on every deck" true.

Decks 0 and 9 are the interesting ones. Their C64 floor is LIGHT GREY, a
colour MODE 1 does not have and this port has never reproduced. They now
run [7, 0, 4, 7]: logical 0 is WHITE, dithered to grey, with logical 3
white as well. That collision is deliberate and it works, because a
dithered logical 0 is displayed as a 50% blend with black - a tone no
solid entry can be. The dither does not just soften the floor, it ADDS a
fifth tone to a four-colour mode, and on those two decks the fifth tone
is exactly the colour the original wanted.

So "four distinct physical colours" was the wrong rule. Both places that
enforced it now test four distinct TONES: a collision is legal only when
it involves logical 0 on a dithered deck, and verify_bbc.py names the
decks that share rather than failing them. Anything else - a collision
that misses logical 0, or any collision on a deck with a solid floor -
still loses detail for good and is still rejected.

No 6502 change. DitherChar's enable test reads logical 1 alone, and its
comment no longer leans on a distinctness assertion that has been
relaxed: if logical 0 were black too the dither would blend black with
black and simply not show, so the only case the test must catch is a
COLOURED logical 1.

events.title: Layer 14: the floor at half intensity, and the room it found
events.message:
Layer 14: the floor at half intensity, and the room it found

The BBC palette is fully saturated where the C64's is not, so a deck
whose floor is red, magenta, green or cyan reads far harsher here than
the original ever did. Half the floor's pixels now take logical 1 - black
on the decks this runs on - in a 2x2 checker, and it reads at half
strength. KC's decision; the alternatives were previewed first and the
checker won, horizontal stripes losing because the pattern is baked into
the charset and the vertical scroll is one scanline, so they would
strobe.

It is nearly free because the background is ALWAYS logical 0 and logical
0 is %00: shading a floor pixel is one bit of the low colour plane.
DitherChar runs over each character from inside BuildCharset's own loop,
so there is no second walk, and bit 0 of the byte index is the scanline
parity in both halves of a character, so the checker needs no state.
Which pixels are logical 0 is the question SPR_MASKTAB already answers,
and the mask is low nibble only, so a logical 2 pixel cannot be turned
white. Roughly 5 ms a deck load; nothing in the main loop pays anything.

BuildLampChar calls it too, or the ALERT lamp goes solid against a
dithered floor. Decks whose floor is already black are skipped - shading
those with a coloured logical 1 gets louder, not quieter - on a single
test, since the four physicals are distinct.

Stating the logical-0 invariant made two things dead, and removing them
more than paid for the dither: BuildLUTs' background masks computed a
contribution that could only be zero, and .deckBg's only reader was that
lookup. export_bbc.py now REFUSES to write colours.asm if a hand-edited
merge breaks the invariant, and palette_lab.py warns before the build.

Bank 4 goes from 4 bytes free to 26, the low overlay from 2 to 4 (lampInk
moved to bank 4 to cover BuildLampChar's JMP). Main RAM unchanged.

palette_lab.py gains a dither control - checker, vertical, horizontal,
and the shade logical - rendered through the port's own chain, with the
build's actual choice named on the page. verify_bbc.py's charset oracle
applies the dither too, and now says so rather than failing on the four
recharger characters AnimTick rotates in place.

Verified in jsbeeb: the charset and the play buffer both carry the
checker, deck 5 (not dithered) is solid black as before, and the buffer
is byte-identical to the RedrawAll oracle after a diagonal scroll.

events.title: installer: instdisk reads the DRIVE, installs the engine, and gets a GEM front-end; Workbench Install icon
events.message:
installer: instdisk reads the DRIVE, installs the engine, and gets a GEM front-end; Workbench Install icon

Three installer changes, all driven end to end in the emulators.

1. THE A1200 LOOP (first real-hardware run, 2026-08-22). instdisk read
   DISK.LST relative to its current directory — on AmigaDOS a lock on
   the VOLUME "OpenUA-Data-1" — so after the disk-2 swap the OS asked
   for volume OpenUA-Data-1 back, read disk 1's manifest, said "I need
   disk 2", forever. The source is now the DEVICE of the current
   directory (DosList: the volume lock's handler task -> the device
   entry -> "DF0:"), which always means whatever is in the drive. And
   since the OS notices a disk change itself, the Amiga swap prompt
   polls for the expected disk instead of waiting on RETURN.

2. THE ENGINE STEP. After the data set, instdisk asks for the engine
   disk(s) and installs from ENGINE.LST (same header line, then
   "<src> <dest> [a]" — `a` appends, which joins the two ECS halves into
   one frua). mkhwdist writes ENGINE.LST on every raw-binary engine disk
   (Falcon/TT, ST Gotek, AGA, ECS 1+2; the 720K zip disk has none and
   instdisk says so). Host-tested: two data disks, two engine disks,
   the join byte-exact.

3. INSTDISK.PRG — the GEM build (installer/gem_atari.c): file selector
   for the destination, alerts for the disk swaps, a window with a
   progress bar, console silenced. Raw AES/VDI trap bindings in the
   fsel_atari.c style. Driven headlessly under Hatari: a four-disk
   install plus the engine, 118 files, every data file byte-identical
   to the staged gamedata and FRUA.PRG identical to the release.
   Traps: fsel_exinput VALIDATES its seed path (a not-yet-existing
   folder throws "cannot find" and falls back to the floppy, which an
   OK then picks as the destination) — create it first; the VT52
   console paints printf over the desktop — silence it in GUI mode.
   Both INSTDISK.PRG and .TTP ride on Atari data disk 1.

4. THE WORKBENCH INSTALL ICON. An IconX launcher (`Install`) finds the
   OS Installer in SYS:System or SYS:Utilities (standard since 2.0,
   never in the path) and runs Install.script: askdir for the drawer,
   engine copy (ECS: both halves, then Join/Protect/Delete), then
   askdisk for each OpenUA-Data-N volume. Driven headlessly in amiberry
   with the disks mounted as named volumes, NOVICE mode: AGA and ECS
   both land 120 files with frua byte-identical to the release.
   Installer-language traps found the hard way: `dest` is a reserved
   word, `(all)` and `(pattern)` are mutually exclusive, and a
   `(pattern "a|b")` on a directory source silently matches nothing —
   copy files one at a time.

HARDWARE.md describes the three install routes; the data-disk README
explains the engine step. mkdatadisks skips a design's SAVE/ tree.

events.title: wonderboy: batch 43 phase E — M6, run.sh, and M3's first exit on target
events.message:
wonderboy: batch 43 phase E — M6, run.sh, and M3's first exit on target

DELIVERED FOR THE USER: atari/run.sh — the interactive Hatari
launcher. bash atari/run.sh builds the play PRG (frame cap and
watchdog lifted), stages the drive through smoke.py's own machinery
(ROM/memsize/monitor/auto-boot all exported from one place — no
copies), and launches windowed with sound, cursor keys + Right-Ctrl
as joystick 1, Ctrl-Q to quit. What you see, measured: the first
playable stage mid-game (the original's own post-boot RAM; no
title — the boot chain is unported), running INDEFINITELY at 4-5
frames a second on the emulated 8 MHz 68000 (1,000+ frames measured
on both ROMs). Hardened by the gate: spaced ROM paths, the record's
exit semantics.

M6 LANDS — the ordered write timeline: every write to the machine
over 52 frames, in order, reduced to a per-side shape derived from
each side's own buffer addresses (three pinned constants broke at
once on EmuTOS — the tell they were one fact written thrice) and
compared: heartbeat address-for-address, zero palette loads, zero
redundant loads, and the shipped binary's 1,155 PSG writes an EXACT
ORDERED PREFIX of ours — gated on measured PSG noise with a
committed instability floor. Instrument gotchas recorded: Hatari's
two hex spellings of one register, collapsed repeat lines (refused),
the classifier's base-address dependency. THE ORDER-ONLY SINK MUTANT
DIES: invisible to every M5 surface (measured — m5flash entirely
green with it applied), red in m6flash's order row. m6rearm proves
its own invisibility by running the whole M2 differential inside
itself (52 loads / 51 countable redundant — the instrument decided).

M3's FIRST EXIT EXECUTED ON TARGET: the ROUND_END ending driven by
a debugger poke on the play build — loop_ending is now the record's
evidence field, RB_VBL_TICKING asserts the liveness it is named for
(the old frames==requested proxy false-redded every player exit).
Completing M3 (all three endings deliberate + Pterm hand-back
asserted) is owed, and run.sh is the mechanism.

Findings: this port ADDED a screen-base transient the original
lacks (§3 retracted); a FOURTH boot deviation (the boot publishes
BACK where our shim publishes FRONT — cmt 0xf906); an EIGHTH
sweep-lie mode of the phase's own making (a staging test rewrote
the shared disk/ mid-boot). Gates: the author's eight (incl. a
live blocker) + the independent five (the play record's false red,
run.sh's whitespace split, two smuggled policy copies, a stale
base in the headline docstring, a figure the instrument cannot
print) — all fixed, all measured.

Suites: wonderboy 6,140 / kit 392 / hw 56; 13 modes x 2 ROMs green.
Remaining: M3 completion (the three endings + hand-back), then the
ladder is walked. Queued items carried.

events.title: bug hunt 2 : make_hd_image — racine trop petite, image partielle, E2BIG
events.message:
bug hunt 2 : make_hd_image — racine trop petite, image partielle, E2BIG

Deuxième passe, visant une LACUNE DE COUVERTURE réelle : le job sanitizers de la CI
ne lance que --tier fast, qui n'exerce ni l'amorçage disque dur, ni l'UltraSatan, ni
SLIRP. Rien trouvé de ce côté (détail plus bas) ; les cinq défauts sont tous dans
l'outil écrit hier, le code le moins éprouvé du lot.

1. RACINE LIMITÉE À 128 ENTRÉES. NROOT=128 était très en dessous de la convention
   FAT16 de disque dur (512, ce que porte aussi le disque donneur). Au-delà, mcopy
   rendait « No directory slots » et l'image était refusée — une ludothèque de 200
   jeux à la racine ne passait pas. Porté à 512 (coût : 32 secteurs) et doublé d'un
   contrôle en amont qui dit combien d'entrées sont en trop. Vérifié : 400 fichiers
   passent désormais, 9000 rendent un message clair. Vérifié AUSSI que le BPB
   modifié ne casse pas la greffe : A B C sous TOS 1.04, TOS 2.06 et EmuTOS.

2. IMAGE PARTIELLE LAISSÉE DERRIÈRE. En cas d'échec en cours de route, une image
   parfaitement montable et VIDE restait au chemin de sortie — on la monte trois
   jours plus tard sans se rappeler qu'elle a échoué. Construction sous un nom
   temporaire, publication par os.replace, suppression du .part sur erreur.

3. LIGNE DE COMMANDE > ARG_MAX. mcopy recevait TOUTES les entrées en un seul appel :
   950 Ko mesurés pour 9000 fichiers. ARG_MAX vaut 2 Mio sur ce Linux, mais bien
   moins ailleurs (macOS) : E2BIG garanti sur une grosse source. Découpé en lots de
   96 Kio.

4. MESSAGE D'ERREUR ILLISIBLE. run() recrachait la ligne de commande entière —
   972 Ko de chemins pour un « Disk full ». Élidé : 395 octets.

5. PAS DE CONTRÔLE DE CAPACITÉ. L'échec n'apparaissait qu'en « Disk full » de mtools,
   sans dire combien il manquait. Contrôle en amont, avec les deux tailles.

Plus un commentaire devenu faux (« la greffe ne donne pas encore un disque
amorçable ») retiré.

EXAMINÉ, RIEN TROUVÉ — ASan/UBSan (build Debug dédié) sur l'amorçage disque dur
TOS 2.06 + HDDRIVER, EmuTOS + disque 3 Go (9 lecteurs), UltraSatan deux slots,
--slirp-selftest, et SIX images ACSI malformées (tronquée, partition hors disque,
tailles 0xFFFFFFFF, partition sur le secteur racine, partitions superposées, fichier
vide) : 0 rapport. Relu net/Socket.cpp (connect non bloquant + SO_ERROR corrects) et
io/UltraSatan.cpp (bornes INQUIRY et paquets 'US') : rien.

run_all.py --tier fast : TOUS LES PALIERS OK.

Merge: the briefing's chatter, and the sound it exposed

Layer 11f F2, built and signed off 2026-08-22. The block it had
been sitting behind — 33 bytes of effect records against a bank 4
with fifteen — dissolved twice over.

It is not the title's sound. TitleLoop zeroes sndState before
ShowTitle and writes $11 only after it returns, so the C64's logo
screen is silent and the burbling belongs to the scrolling manual.
That made the 50 Hz tick free (the briefing already runs under the
IRQ, and BrWaitField is called exactly once per field) and struck
DECISION 8's whole VSync-throttled TiWait plan.

And the records did not need to be resident. Bank 4 carries one
rewritable scratch slot, effect 29; the three real records live in
bank 5 beside the text, and only the five bytes of a record that
vary are ferried. SndTick is not modified at all.

Then the chatter exposed a signed-off sound: it reuses the lift
blip on voice 2 for 54 fields in every 64, and fx16 is 48%
sub-floor with its bounce straddling the floor, so the clamp had
been collapsing a 108-174 Hz bass warble into two notes at full
volume. It is now periodic bass on a cloned instrument, 6 dB below
the chatter it sits behind. The in-game lift it also reaches was
re-heard and is fine.

Costs: bank 4 15 B -> 4 B, PARBRF 81 B -> 3 B, PARMAN ~120 B,
main RAM unchanged at &2FFE.

events.message:
Close the lift blip's open question in the registers

The one thing on this item that was analysed but never observed:
ChangeDeck posts fx16 on BOTH voices, and now that it is a noise
voice both claims land on the one noise channel. Tested directly —
sndFx1 and sndFx2 both poked to 16 during play, which is what
$271B/$2729 do:

  - the hum's tone channel went to attenuation 15 as the noise
    voice took its voice over (round eight's rule); CH0 needed no
    write, already silent
  - one Noise: 3 control write, one envelope on CH3 (12, 9, 6, 3,
    0, then 6), CH2 sweeping the pitch for the full 27 ticks
  - attenuation 15 on CH3 at the end — nothing stuck — and the
    per-deck hum re-posted on CH1 immediately after

So the mechanism is sound and what is left is taste: one blip per
deck instead of a doubled one, quieter, at its real pitch. That

events.message:
Chatter S5 round 2: the lift blip drops 6 dB

KC: pitch is better, still too loud, and the lift may go quieter
with it. The C64 sustains fx16 at full (SR nibble F), which put it
at attenuation 0 — 6 dB ABOVE the chatter blips it is meant to sit
behind. Now nibble 9 = attenuation 6, so it sits 6 dB below them: a
12 dB swing from what was heard. The 100 ms attack ramp is
untouched, so it keeps its swell; captured on CH3 as 12, 9, 6, 3,
0, then a body at 6.

FX_LEVEL is the second sanctioned place ported sound data may
differ from the C64's bytes, and it is keyed by EFFECT rather than
by instrument on purpose: clone allocation moves instrument
indices, so an index-keyed table would silently retarget the next
time FX_PERIODIC changes. The exporter resolves the instrument at
emit time and asserts every other effect sharing it asks for the
same level — the leak FX_PERIODIC's cloning exists to prevent,
caught at build time instead. fx21, the console beep, is on the
uncloned instrument 10 and is untouched.

events.title: engine: cache the command-button plates — the 68000 bar repaint 82 -> 23 ticks
events.message:
engine: cache the command-button plates — the 68000 bar repaint 82 -> 23 ticks

The command bar cost 82-104 ticks (1.4-1.7 s) per repaint on STE/ECS
against 3-5 on the 020s (#138), after every event modal. #138-#141 had
proven the repaint redundant (FRUA_BARDAMAGE: 0 px changed, three times)
and run the "why is it repainted" question to ground; this closes the
"make the paint cheap" half. jt137 msg 1 rebuilt each word's plate from
FRAME.CTL glyph pieces — left cap, rec[24] middles, right cap, label,
hotkey letter — through the per-pixel l309c -> l2d4e path, for pixels
that never change.

A 16-slot plate cache in jt137's colour paint arm. A miss paints normally
while unioning the rects l309c lands (g_lc_*), then captures that rect
from the chunky surface — exactly what the paint produced, label and
hotkey included. A hit at the same (top,left) with the same label, width
and paint-state bits replays the bytes and stamps them the way l309c's
tail does (planar_viewport_overwrite + qd_planar_bridge_rect +
qd_touch_rows), so the ST/ECS draw-time plane writers see it. B&W keeps
its own path. -DFRUA_NOPLATECACHE is the A/B arm.

Measured on STE with FRUA_BARPROF, A/B on one fixture drive: the 13-item
post-modal repaint 82-90 tk -> 22-24 tk (-72%, 1.4 s -> 0.4 s), 6 plate
hits per repaint once warm, cold entry composes unchanged, and the two
arms' final screenshots are BYTE-IDENTICAL — the replay is pixel-exact on
the planar build. Falcon walks into the same event modal and renders it
correctly.

Also recorded by a FRUA_BAR28 jt993 trace (kept under the flag): #141's
"wall-group reload every frame" was not per frame. Over a four-step walk
the reloads were one at entry (unset slots) and one after the event
modal, armed by l3eea/jt993 pv=6 start=32 — the event picture's palette
over CLUT 32..255, which genuinely wipes the wall bands. Both correct.

events.title: bug hunt : file MIDI du MT-32 sans borne, et nom de volume corrompu en silence
events.message:
bug hunt : file MIDI du MT-32 sans borne, et nom de volume corrompu en silence

Relecture adversariale de mes propres changements de cette session — la note
« relecture adversariale passe 3 » du projet rappelle que 3 correctifs sur ~60
causaient la panne qu'ils visaient. Deux vrais défauts trouvés, tous deux rendus
atteignables par des changements d'aujourd'hui.

1. FILE MIDI SANS BORNE (audio/Mt32Synth, audio/Audio). Mt32Synth::byteAt empile
   dans pending_ dès que le synthé est OUVERT, mais pending_ n'est vidé que par
   render() — appelé APRÈS la sortie anticipée « pas de périphérique » de
   Audio::produceFrame, qui drainait le PSG et le DMA en oubliant le MT-32. Sans
   périphérique audio (ou après une perte de device, cas que ce fichier gère
   explicitement avec sa reprise automatique), la file grossissait donc SANS FIN,
   et au retour du son tout le retard partait d'un coup dans une seule trame.
   Personne ne le voyait tant que le MT-32 était OFF par défaut ; il est ON depuis
   04b8719. Corrigé par un clearEvents() public appelé sur ce chemin, plus un
   plafond kMaxPending en filet si un appelant oublie de rendre.
   ⚠ L'autre sortie (n <= 0, saturation TRANSITOIRE de l'anneau) ne draine
   DÉLIBÉRÉMENT pas le MT-32 : jeter un Note-Off laisserait une note bloquée. Le
   choix est commenté sur place pour qu'on ne l'« uniformise » pas par erreur.

2. NOM DE VOLUME CORROMPU (tools/make_hd_image.py). La greffe écrit le code de
   l'étage 2 à partir de $34, ce qui écrase les 2 derniers octets du champ « nom de
   volume » du BPB : un nom de plus de 9 caractères y était SILENCIEUSEMENT tronqué
   et remplacé par des octets de code. mdir n'y voyait rien — il lit le nom dans
   l'entrée de répertoire racine, pas dans le BPB — donc les deux divergeaient.
   Reproduit avec --label ONZECARACT (BPB « ONZECARAC`\x02 »). Le nom est désormais
   plafonné à 9 caractères quand on greffe, avec un avertissement.

Examiné et jugé SAIN : net/SlirpBackend::poll (index rendu à SLIRP, garde
select_error, bornage), le parseur MIDI (récursion bornée à 1, cap SysEx 4096),
la fenêtre de course byteAt/render (les deux sur le fil d'émulation).
Latent mais NON atteignable, laissé tel quel : l'assert « somme != $1234 » du
secteur racine sans pilote — aucune taille entière de 6 à 4096 Mo ne le déclenche.

run_all.py --tier fast : TOUS LES PALIERS OK.

events.title: Chatter S5 round 1: the lift blip goes periodic bass
events.message:
Chatter S5 round 1: the lift blip goes periodic bass

KC's ear on the briefing: "the background two tones are too loud
and too monotonous... perhaps try periodic bass instead". Exactly
right, and it was on the exporter's own review list.

The offender is fx16 — the lift blip, which the chatter reuses on
voice 2 at $056A and therefore plays for 54 fields in every 64.
It is meant to bounce 108-174 Hz; 48% of that is under the SN's
122 Hz floor and the bounce STRADDLES the floor, so the clamp
collapsed a bass warble into an alternation between N=1023 and
N=967 — two notes, 122 and 134 Hz, at attenuation 0, nearly
continuously. Sparse in a lift, which is why it survived stage 4;
the briefing is what exposed it.

FX_PERIODIC gains 16, so instrument 10 is CLONED rather than
moved — fx21, the console beep, shares it at 254-346 Hz and is
right as a tone. fx16 now runs N 44-72 on the noise channel at
sub-floor 0%, and the flush's round-eight rule silences CH1, so
the drone is gone rather than buried.

The clone cost no RAM, which is the only reason it fits a bank
with four bytes free: export_sound.py now puts clones in
instrument slots NO record references before extending the table.
The C64's table has gaps — nothing names instrument 1 — and a
contiguous emitted table pays for them either way. The fx23 clone
took slot 1 and fx16's took the end slot it vacated.

Verified in jsbeeb: noise register 3 (periodic), the pitch on
silenced CH2 sweeping N 58-72, CH1 at attenuation 15, the chatter
untouched on CH0 at attenuation 3.

events.title: amiga: Mac tempo on every vblank rate, and the needle bump was ring-cursor drift
events.message:
amiga: Mac tempo on every vblank rate, and the needle bump was ring-cursor drift

Two music fixes, both user-heard and user-verified:

1. TEMPO. The Mac VBL sound task counts sixty ticks a second; a PAL
   vblank delivers fifty, so every tune played 17% slow (the Mac tempo
   was only ever right on NTSC by accident). Classic fix: accumulate
   60 per vblank against ExecBase->VBlankFrequency — PAL runs the
   sequencer twice on every 5th vblank, NTSC exactly once. Verified by
   note-onset density: 1.27x against the old take (1.20 expected).

2. THE "VINYL NEEDLE BUMP". The ring model advanced the play cursor by
   FRAME_SAMPLES = 454 per call, but real PAL Paula at period 156
   consumes 227.5 CCK/line x 312.5 lines / 156 = 455.73 samples per
   frame. Under-counting ~86 samples/s, the modeled write head lapped
   the real DMA read head about 21 seconds after ring start and Paula
   replayed ~80ms of stale ring — one audible bump at a FIXED WALL
   TIME. The giveaway was the tempo fix itself: the bump moved to a
   LATER point in the tune, which no music-tied artifact can do. The
   cursor now advances in 24.8 fixed point at the exact rate (PAL
   116667/256, NTSC 98000/256 per vblank), scaled by elapsed CIA-A TOD
   ticks so a missed vblank cannot skew the model either. Bump gone by
   ear on the re-recorded boot.

events.title: Chatter S3: the briefing burbles
events.message:
Chatter S3: the briefing burbles

BmChatter (bank 5, beside the text) is Sound._chatter transcribed:
a counter down every field, a blip picked by a random third every
128, the lift blip on voice 2 at two counter phases, and every 16
fields a signed random walk on voice 1's frequency slide — which
is the chatter itself, the thing that keeps the zipper's rate
moving. BrChatter (PARBRF, main RAM, so allowed to page) does the
half that needs bank 4: land the record in the scratch slot and
post it, or apply the nudge. BrWaitField falls into it, so the
tick is exactly one per field wherever the briefing waits.

BrRun asks for sndState $12 rather than the C64's $11 — the port
has no $11 because its chatter is not inside the driver — and
seeds the LFSR from fieldCount, because PARMAN is reloaded from
disc for every briefing and would otherwise hand every one of them
the same byte. BrDispatch's teardown gets its SndSilence back: the
comment saying nothing had sounded is no longer true.

No SEI anywhere in it. The rupture's T1 stages are deadline-driven
and this runs every field; the three races that buys are all
harmless and the reasoning is in BrChatter's header.

Making it fit PARBRF's &0800 ceiling — which is 81 bytes, not the
1,188 the handover claims for &0C90 — took three turns:
  - the bank is stated, not saved (BrWaitField is only ever
    reached with bank 5 up)
  - only the 5 bytes of a record that VARY are ferried; the three
    blips share their whole tail and the slot ships holding it.
    export_sound.py asserts that, so a release that breaks it
    fails the build rather than the sound
  - brChCnt is not zeroed: a fresh PARMAN brings it assembled at 0

Main RAM: unchanged at &2FFE. Bank 4: 4 B. PARBRF: 3 B.

events.message:
journal : messages Munt préfixés, et l'underrun ne ment plus sur la cadence

Deux nuisances relevées dans un journal de session réel, toutes deux liées à
l'activation du MT-32 par défaut ou masquées par elle.

1. « playSysexWithoutFraming: Header not intended for this device manufacturer »
   sortait BRUT sur stderr, sans préfixe, au milieu du journal de NeoST : c'est
   Munt qui écrit directement (Synth.cpp printDebug par défaut). Un ReportHandler
   récupère désormais ces messages et les préfixe [mt32]. Ce cas précis n'est PAS
   une anomalie — un SysEx adressé à un autre fabricant que Roland ($41) est le
   fonctionnement normal d'un anneau MIDI où le ST parle à plusieurs appareils —
   donc on le signale UNE fois puis on se tait, au lieu de noyer le journal.
   Vérifié au passage, trace NEOST_MIDI_TRACE à l'appui : ce SysEx vient d'un
   logiciel du disque de l'utilisateur, pas de NeoST.

2. « emulation loop: 71.4 real frames/s (expected ~50/60) » : le « 50/60 » était
   codé en dur et FAUX en haute résolution, où le mode mono tourne à 71,2 Hz. On y
   lisait un emballement alors que la boucle était à l'heure. Le message cite
   maintenant les trois cadences nominales (50 PAL / 60 NTSC / 71 mono) ; ce qui
   signale un vrai problème, c'est l'underrun lui-même, pas la fréquence affichée.

events.title: make_hd_image : cartes SD UltraSatan AMORÇABLES — greffe de pilote réussie
events.message:
make_hd_image : cartes SD UltraSatan AMORÇABLES — greffe de pilote réussie

La greffe automatique du pilote TOS fonctionne. Le commit 3c7f02d la déclarait
impossible « sans rétro-concevoir l'installeur d'un logiciel commercial » : c'était
faux, et il a suffi de désassembler le secteur racine (capstone, CS_ARCH_M68K) pour
voir ce qui manquait.

L'amorçage HDDRIVER est en DEUX étages, chacun gardé par une somme $1234. L'étage 1
(secteur racine) choisit la partition dont le drapeau masqué par $F8 vaut $80, lit
son premier secteur, puis REFAIT la même somme dessus — add.w (a0)+,d0 / dbra /
cmp.w #$1234,d0 / bne → abandon — avant jmp (a4). D'où les deux défauts :

  1. mformat écrit un secteur DOS de somme quelconque : l'étage 1 refusait de
     l'exécuter, et la trace ACSI s'arrêtait pile après les secteurs 0 et 2.
     Rattrapage par un mot d'ajustement en $1FE (là où DOS met $55AA, et où le
     disque donneur met déjà le sien).
  2. le code de l'étage 2 commence à $34 — la cible du BRA.S de tête —, ce qui
     empiète sur les 2 derniers octets du champ « nom de volume ». Le copier depuis
     $36, l'offset « propre » d'après le BPB, laissait ces 2 octets s'exécuter et
     faisait dérailler l'étage 2 en silence.

Le BPB de mformat (FAT16, 512 o/secteur) convient tel quel : l'étage 2 sait le lire,
inutile de reproduire les secteurs logiques de 8192 octets du donneur.

Vérifié drvbits=$00000007 (A B C) sous TOS 1.04, TOS 2.06 et EmuTOS, avec
C:\CUBLITE\CB_LITE.PRG accessible. --driver-from redevient le défaut (détection d'un
donneur amorçable dans hd/) ; --no-driver garde le comportement image de données.

events.title: make_hd_image : corrige un diagnostic FAUX — NeoST monte bien les disques durs
events.message:
make_hd_image : corrige un diagnostic FAUX — NeoST monte bien les disques durs

Le commit précédent (04b8719) affirmait, dans l'en-tête de tools/make_hd_image.py
et dans son propre message, qu'AUCUN disque dur ne se montait sous TOS 2.06 et que
NeoST était fidèle sur ce point. Les deux moitiés étaient fausses, pour la même
raison : un protocole de test fautif.

`--keys STR` tape APRÈS le boot. Or TOS 2.06 attend une touche sur son écran
mémoire : il ne la recevait donc jamais, et rien de ce qui suit n'avait de sens.
Avec `--keys-at 700 " "`, TOS 2.06 monte A à I depuis hd/Atari3gb.vhd
(_drvbits=$000001FF, hdv_bpb=$010E86 en RAM — la valeur même qu'Hatari donne).
TOS 1.04, qui n'attend aucune touche, y arrive sans rien de particulier. NeoST
n'a aucune divergence ici.

Second piège consigné : les icônes C:/D:/E: du bureau viennent des lignes #M de
NEWDESK.INF et s'affichent SANS lecteur monté. Juger sur _drvbits ($4C2) et les
vecteurs hdv_* ($472), jamais sur une capture d'écran.

La greffe de pilote, elle, ne marche RÉELLEMENT pas — vérifié cette fois avec le
bon protocole, sous 2.06 comme sous 1.04. Cause localisée : l'amorçage HDDRIVER
est en DEUX étages, du 68000 vit aussi dans le secteur d'amorçage de la partition
(là où mformat écrit un secteur DOS), et ce second étage lit le système de
fichiers tel que l'installeur HDDRIVER l'a formaté (secteurs logiques de 8192
octets, 512 entrées racine, 7 secteurs/FAT). Sur une image de l'outil, le code
lit les secteurs 0 et 2 puis s'arrête, là où l'original enchaîne sur le 242.

--driver-from devient donc EXPÉRIMENTAL et opt-in (le défaut est l'image de
données), avec un avertissement à l'exécution. Pour un vrai TOS, la voie qui
marche est de copier ses fichiers sur un disque déjà préparé par HDDRIVER —
c'est ce qui a été fait pour Cubase Lite (C:\CUBLITE sur hd/Atari3gb.vhd).

libmt32emu (Munt 2.8.3, amont 6e7c01f) passe de dépendance système à copie
vendorisée dans extern/mt32emu, liée en STATIQUE. Le find_package(MT32Emu)
exigeait brew install mt32emu / libmt32emu-dev, qu'aucun runner de CI ni aucune
image de release n'installait : le Roland MT-32/CM-32L n'existait donc dans AUCUN
binaire livré, et son absence ne se signalait que par une ligne de configuration.
Ferme le TODO du 2026-08-21. Code d'amont intact ; seul le CMakeLists du dossier
est de NeoST (API C++ seule, rééchantillonneur interne, en-têtes recopiés dans
build/generated/mt32emu — même schéma que Moira). add_subdirectory est APRÈS le
garde-fou GLFW : seul le GUI s'en sert. LGPL 2.1+ satisfaite par un lien statique
puisque NeoST publie ses sources, cette copie comprise ; détails dans
extern/mt32emu/NEOST_VENDOR.md.

MT-32 ACTIF PAR DÉFAUT (midiOutMt32) : la bibliothèque étant désormais toujours
présente, il n'y a plus de raison d'attendre que l'utilisateur trouve l'option.
Sans ROM Roland, main.cpp:2671 échoue proprement et remet le drapeau à false.

Conflit d'ID ImGui, page Hard disks : IconButton dérive son ID du seul texte de
l'icône, et la page affiche jusqu'à TROIS ICON_FA_EJECT (GEMDOS, ACSI, slot 2).
Deux montés en même temps = « 2 visible items with conflicting ID » et des clics
qui partent sur le mauvais bouton. PushID sur les trois, comme driveRow() le fait
déjà page Disquettes. Au passage, l'ACSI affiche « (empty slot) » quand la cible 0
est vide : acsiActive() est un anyEnabled() sur TOUTES les cibles, donc le slot 2
de l'UltraSatan suffisait à afficher « mounted:  — 0 partition(s) », nom vide et
décompte appartenant à une autre cible.

NEOST_VERSION_STR : variable de cache, donc figée au premier cmake -B build — un
bump de project() était ignoré et --version mentait (0.5.1 pour un projet en
0.5.2). On mémorise la graine et on ré-ensemence si elle a changé ; un -D
explicite reste PRÉSERVÉ (validé sur les trois cas).

tools/make_hd_image.py : dossier hôte -> carte SD UltraSatan (table AHDI écrite à
la main + FAT16 par mtools), avec greffe automatique du pilote TOS depuis un
disque donneur. ⚠ Greffe NON vérifiée de bout en bout : aucun disque dur ne se
monte sous TOS 2.06, pas même un disque d'origine — et Hatari donne le MÊME

Layer 11f: the page-5 portrait, scrolling with the text

BuildIntroSprites ($119A-$11AD) floats the droid as hardware sprites
over the C64's scroll; the port has no sprites on a modal screen -
bank 5 IS the text - so the portrait scrolls WITH the page (KC's
call): BrPortrait picks type rnd AND $F, has PoDraw (bank 7) render
into the parked strip at unit 68 - text columns 34-39, which are
empty on every page-5 row - at its own rows 3-13, snapshots the
rectangle into SPR_SAVE, and the painter copies a 96-byte band back
whenever one of those canvas rows is painted. The picture sits level
with the score table, a mugshot beside the scores, and moves with it.

AND THE OVERLAY'S CEILING IS &0800, MEASURED THE HARD WAY. The first
cut pushed PARBRF to &08B8; it verified byte-perfect at load and the
briefing died on its first text row - the MOS's IRQ writes its sound
workspace and channel buffers at &0800-&08FF (NAUG §6.6) while it
still owns the machine through the title's loads, and it chewed the
overlay's tail; the corrupted BrCell then wandered into the paged
bank (BRK at &800E, error pointer read from the wreck). Bisected by
disabling the portrait logic with the layout kept: still died - the
size alone was fatal. So &0400-&07FF (the language workspace, truly
free) is the whole of PARBRF's ground, GUARDed at &0800 now, and
everything that need not be main RAM moved to briefman.asm in bank 5:
the score-patch writer, the portrait snapshot and the band copy all
run with the text bank paged and touch only main RAM and their own
bank. PARBRF is back to 960 bytes with 64 spare.

to page 5, the portrait beside the live score table, the page
scrolling it away with the text, and fire dropping into a playable

events.title: wonderboy/joust: batch 43 phase D — M5, and a sibling defect measured
events.message:
wonderboy/joust: batch 43 phase D — M5, and a sibling defect measured

M5 LANDS: at the four M2 anchors, twenty registers of the machine
itself — the sixteen shifter pens, resolution, sync, refresh, and
V-overscan — are identical on both sides, captured by the same
debugger commands and parsed by the same code each side, anchored on
the address the binary reports about itself. The YM file is captured
and printed but NOT compared, for measured reasons (vecnoise: five
registers move between two boots of the shipped binary alone). The
rendered picture is byte-identical at all four anchors on both ROMs,
after the round's find: Hatari's drive LED in the border pushes the
PNG from palette to truecolour — --drive-led off, and the bound
measured by same-side repeat runs.

THE FLASH SURVIVOR DIES: the single raiser censused to $1328
(player_weapon_fire's LIGHTNING arm — the mode-shaped EA sweep
self-tested by re-finding 226/226 (d16,PC) operands, and it caught a
reader undercount at $6ee), unreachable in the window twice over, so
WB_FLASH_TIMER is seeded as a DECLARED FABRICATION with the writer's
own operand on both sides at the same instant — and the fabrication
is ASSERTED ARMED (a two-sided differential cannot see a fault that
hits both sides; zeroing the seed must fail the mode). The arm-swap
mutant dead at both arms; the order-only sink mutant reassigned to
M6 with trigger + home.

Controls both directions: m5fault (one pen corrupted, divergence
asserted to be that pen and nothing else), m5skew (the complement;
every surface fails in at least one control, the picture in both).

THE SIBLING MEASUREMENT: Joust's five non-reproducible deep anchors
were re-measured under the fixed settings — the drift is a different
effect (registered at Joust's surfaces with trigger + home), but THE
LED WAS IN JOUST'S PICTURES THE WHOLE TIME, including the one frame
its compare asserts, silently certified because both sides carried
it alike. Removing the chrome made the pen-fault surface STRICTLY
MORE sensitive (a palette-mode PNG's PLTE chunk IS the pens,
verified byte for byte) — Joust's control reclassified, its three
stale framediff PRGs rebuilt (pre-existing freshness refusal), all
five Joust smokes green.

Aucun FujiNet n'a jamais existé pour l'Atari ST : c'était un binding de
référence inventé ici, greffé sur l'opcode vendeur ACSI $60. Un émulateur
d'Atari ST n'a pas à porter du matériel imaginaire.

Supprimé : io/FujiDevice, net/FujiHost{,Live,Replay}, net/MiniJson,
net/HttpClient, tests/fixtures/fuji, dev/fujinet, gemdos/DEMOS/NWGET.TOS,
les drapeaux --fujinet*/--fuji-selftest, les clés fujinet*= de neost.cfg,
l'étalon fuji_selftest, la page GUI et la section de docs/EXTENSIONS.md.

Conservé et repointé : la couche socket partagée qui vivait dans HttpClient
(namespace neonet) est extraite dans net/Socket.{hpp,cpp} — c'est désormais
son seul rôle ; HayesModem et MidiRing y sont repointés. NEOST_FUJI_TRACE
devient NEOST_NET_TRACE. MIDITEST.C/MODMTEST.C (tests du MIDI ring et du
modem, fonctionnalités conservées) migrent vers dev/netdemo/.

Effet de bord bienvenu : l'opcode ACSI $60 retrouve le rejet STRICT sur
toutes les cibles, comme le port de hdc.c — NeoST est plus fidèle qu'avant.

Save-states v12 -> v13 (FujiDevice et Acsi::fujiPending_ quittent le flux ;
bits de drapeau décalés : bit1 EtherNEC, bit2 UltraSatan, bit3 NetUSBee).

events.title: wonderboy/kit: batch 43 phase C — the native crash, diagnosed to a defect
events.message:
wonderboy/kit: batch 43 phase C — the native crash, diagnosed to a defect

THE TOP QUEUE ITEM CLOSED: the parallel-only worker crash was a REAL
DEFECT IN THE RECONSTRUCTION — scene_run_frame indexed the 1 MB
candidate buffer with a raw 32-bit descriptor pointer ($9002e549 →
2.4 GiB out of bounds) where Musashi masks to 24 bits and reads
in-image. Diagnosed with a native backtrace (SIGBUS handler via
sitecustomize) and made deterministic with a PROT_NONE guard from
−16 MiB to +4 GiB; parallel-only because only address-space layout
decides whether the page is mapped. 43B's spawn-table candidate is
REFUTED on the record.

Fixed at the queued depth: scene.c's image-supplied pointers and
map.c's record/cell accesses through bus.h (mask to 24 bits, then
bound). The class swept with a new opt-in guarded plugin: 3 reachable
cases in two routines — one a battery premise (REFUSED_RECORD at
$fffff0) the port never honoured. Rate: 2 of 32 parallel runs before,
0 of 72 after on a hash-checked .so; the stronger same-instrument
pair 5 of 6,140 → 0.

Kit: harness.candidate_image (one candidate-buffer seam) +
guarded_image.py. The gate closed four seam bypasses — the suite's
WILDEST enumerations (65,536 types, swoop states, pickup indices,
PSG opcodes) were self-buffered outside the census — now routed:
9,611 guarded runs, 0 crashes; sibling projects' seven self-buffer
sites registered (three alias live buffers — a different shape).
The zero-guard tripwire aggregates across xdist workers (its second
misfire mode found before it fired).

The bus contract, stated as a SET: identical to the shim on every
out-of-image NON-hardware address; divergent on seven modeled
hardware bytes (enumerated from shim.c) — six cannot pass a
differential (ledger/read-stream vetted), $fffc00 is the one silent
hole, registered. The map pin's death is deterministic UNDER THE
GUARD (8/8), empirical outside it — a mapped page turns the mutant
into a silent heap scribble, the same property that made the
original defect intermittent.

Plate corrections: a nonexistent andi.b #$f9 (the settle arms are
two bclr's — verified from bytes); the retraction scan widened after
colliding with a REAL FDC status test at $63f0 (a scan phrase must
be as precise as the claim it retires).

M5/M3 NOT taken — the crash consumed the phase; flash survivor
still at its M5 home. Suites: wonderboy 6,140 / guarded 6,140 /
kit 392 / joust 4,369 / buggyboy 292 / hw 56; M1+M2 green both
ROMs, M2 byte-exact re-verified by the orchestrator.

events.title: docs/FUJINET.md -> docs/EXTENSIONS.md, et NetBackendSlirp (Internet réel pour la NE2000, en cours)
events.message:
docs/FUJINET.md -> docs/EXTENSIONS.md, et NetBackendSlirp (Internet réel pour la NE2000, en cours)

RENOMMAGE. Le fichier documentait TOUTES les extensions NeoST — UltraSatan
(stockage), NetUSBee, EtherNEC, modem Hayes, anneau MIDI — alors que son nom
n'annonçait que le FujiNet, qui n'a JAMAIS existé sur Atari ST : c'est le seul
binding « de référence » du lot, sans matériel correspondant. git mv (l'historique
suit) + 17 fichiers de références mis à jour ; un tableau en tête distingue
désormais le matériel réel de l'invention NeoST.

NetBackendSlirp (EN COURS — cf. TODO.md, entrée en tête de liste). Donne à la
NE2000 émulée un accès Internet par NAT en espace utilisateur (libslirp) : aucun
privilège, ni pcap ni TAP. L'ST reçoit 10.0.2.15/24, passerelle 10.0.2.2, DNS
10.0.2.3, DHCP servi par SLIRP. Option CMake NEOST_WITH_SLIRP (pkg-config),
drapeaux --slirp / --slirp-restricted, auto-test --slirp-selftest.

État : 3 vérifications sur 4 passent (ARP, DHCP, compteurs — déterministes et
hors ligne, donc CI-ables). La sortie réelle (DNS, opt-in NEOST_SLIRP_ONLINE=1)
reste à finir : le datagramme sort bien (prouvé sur un serveur UDP local) et
SLIRP nous ARPe, mais la réponse n'atteint pas encore l'anneau de réception.

Trois pièges de libslirp déjà résolus, consignés pour ne pas les rechercher :
- register_poll_fd/unregister_poll_fd sont « deprecated » mais appelés SANS test
  de nullité dès la première socket sortante -> SIGSEGV visible en ligne seulement ;
- clock_get_ns doit partir de ~0 : sinon toute socket UDP naît « expirée » (son
  expiration est fixée avec le curtime interne, nul avant le premier poll) ;
- SLIRP ARPe l'invité avant de livrer un paquet entrant — sur un vrai ST c'est
  STinG qui répond, l'auto-test doit le faire lui-même.

Palier fast vert.

events.title: Démo réseau : NeoST atteint theoldnet.com par le modem Hayes (programme 68000)
events.message:
Démo réseau : NeoST atteint theoldnet.com par le modem Hayes (programme 68000)

tools/make_net_test.py génère une disquette dont AUTO\NETTEST.PRG compose
« ATDT <hôte>:80 » sur le modem émulé, envoie une requête HTTP à la main et
affiche la réponse à l'écran. Vérifié sur theoldnet.com : en-têtes HTTP
(Content-Length: 77169, X-Powered-By: Express) puis <title>The Old Net</title>.

C'est le chemin qui marche SANS pile TCP/IP côté ST — le modem est un pont
transparent octets ↔ socket. Le NetUSBee, lui, ne sort pas : son backend est une
boucle locale (cf. TODO.md « EtherNEC — backend réel : SlirpNat »).

Deux pièges consignés dans le générateur, trouvés en le faisant tourner :
- $4BA (horloge 200 Hz du TOS) est en mémoire BASSE, protégée : un PRG tourne en
  mode utilisateur et y prend un bus error → Super(0) ;
- la console ST n'enroule pas les lignes longues, elle écrase la 80e colonne :
  une ligne HTML n'y laissait voir que son dernier caractère (colonne de « > »)
  → repli à 78 colonnes, et CR ajouté sur les LF seuls (le HTML n'a pas de CR).

Au passage : write_fs/build_floppy de make_usatan_test.py prennent le nom du PRG
en paramètre, pour héberger d'autres démos que USTEST.

events.title: amiga: rewrite the synth mixer for the 68000 — music cost 2.47 frames/vblank, now 0.84
events.message:
amiga: rewrite the synth mixer for the 68000 — music cost 2.47 frames/vblank, now 0.84

The follow-up 39551e5e left open: with music audible, synth_render cost
773 beam lines = 2.47 FRAMES per 454-sample fill (~770 cycles/sample) —
the per-sample loop did four read-modify-writes of g_ft_phase[] through
absolute addresses, four inc==0 tests, and tone/sfx tests, every sample.
That cost was the entire VBL starvation and the original stuttering
title music.

The rewrite (output byte-identical to the old mixer, argued in-source):
- active voices compacted once per call, phases in locals for the
  duration — no global traffic per sample;
- wavetable bytes summed UNSIGNED, the -128-per-voice bias folded into
  the final >>2;
- the steady state (music, no tone, no sfx) specialized per voice count,
  register-resident, and clamp-free — the biased >>2 provably fits
  -128..127;
- tone/sfx frames keep the general path: same order, same single clamp;
- catch-up bounded at 2 frames of ring per vblank, so one stall can
  never balloon a later handler.

Measured (cold ECS boot, TOD-qualified timers): loud fills 773 -> 262
lines (2.47 -> 0.84 frames, 2.95x); quiet fills 160 -> 7 lines; all 13
bard windows at 50 Hz with zero gap-3; menu reached; captured fanfare
RMS is steady 3100-4000 where the starved mixer wobbled 1400-5900 (the
"struggling to not die" audio, finally attributed and fixed).

Also: the refill/hook profiling brackets are TOD-QUALIFIED now
(ticks*313 + line remainder). The plain beam-line diff wraps mod one
frame and hid this exact cost as "103 lines" twice — same trap, same
week, both instruments mine.

The Falcon backend still runs the old-shape mixer (identical twin,
platform/sound_falcon.c); its cached 16 MHz 030 never hurt enough to
notice, but the same rewrite ports directly if it ever shows up in a
profile.

  recipe's width now). Seven inside-pins; a mis-anchor moves 25.6% of

  variance measured as a RANGE (536..605 B) owned by the instrument
  and decomposed into four bands with per-band ceilings.
- The program-span equality decomposed exactly: tile bitmaps (zeros
  in the file, asserted), the Copylock scratch (turns over every

events.title: amiga: the VBL starvation was OURS — the sound task costs ~2.4 frames; skip it under the bard
events.message:
amiga: the VBL starvation was OURS — the sound task costs ~2.4 frames; skip it under the bard

Retraction of fec9a19d's verdict. amiberry was innocent (#2288 closed):
a standalone repro with the same quantiser, the same 5-plane banded
copper display, and the same Paula channel state runs a perfect 50 Hz
on the same 68000 config. The trigger the transplants missed was the
TITLE FANFARE: with music audible, plat_sound_vbl's refill + Mac VBL
sound task cost ~2.4 FRAMES per call on the 7 MHz 68000. exec merges
VERTB requests latched while a handler overruns, so servicing locks to
a metronomic every-3rd frame — the clean gap-3 histogram, the
never-pending mainline samples, and the whole chain starving equally,
on real silicon just as in the emulator.

Two instruments had hidden this: the beam-line profiler wraps modulo
one frame (2.33 frames = 729 lines = 103 mod 313 — read as "cheap"),
and the earlier "muted-ring skip" A/B only skipped the REFILL while
the expensive hook kept running, so "the skip changed nothing" pointed
at the hook all along and was read as an acquittal instead.

The fix: while the bard plays (cold conversions only), skip the whole
handler — refill AND hook. Engine audio is muted under the bard
anyway; freezing the sequencer means the music resumes where it
paused, and plat_bard_stop's ring resync re-seats the write point.
Verified cold on the shipped path: every window gap-1, and the two
big conversions drop from 2295+2640 TOD ticks to 394+452 — the wall
time was ~1/5 quant and ~4/5 sound handler.

Localization credits: the phase-attribution probe (gap-3s spread
across ALL quant phases proportionally = not a code trigger), and the
palcache=off subtraction run (still starved with no bard, no notice,
no progress = not the please-wait machinery).

Open follow-up: the hook's ~2.4-frames-per-vblank cost stands whenever
music plays on a 68000 target — title interludes run the same overrun
and under-fill the ring (the original "struggling to not die" audio).
That is now the standing ECS/ST-class perf lever.

bottom dwell, then the next page - page 6 is the way out to the title,
and fire starts the game from anywhere in all of it. The speed is the
original's arithmetic decoded from the listing (MoveScreen SUBTRACTS
ySpd+1 = $FF - joyYDir): 1 scanline a field centred, 2 with M held,
paused with K, and M skips both dwells - so K and M are the stick's
two directions exactly.

The scroll itself is line/scrollS stepped a field at a time on
fieldCount, applied by SetCRTCStart; the window is the deck's own 15
rows (t1i3Hi = HI(T1_I3), stated by the briefing because the two
entry paths disagree about what they left there), and the incoming
16th row is painted at the bottom edge on each row advance - the row
lists make that one short walk. 45 rows of travel = 360 scanlines,
the C64's own $168.

BrPatchScores is UpdateTextScore moved to the read side [DECISION 7]:
BrTimeout patches page 5's two labelled records from bank 7's live
table on the fresh copy in bank 5 - eight BCD digits, leading zeros
blanked (the last never), initials at 11-13. The exporter now labels
those records by TEXT match; the doc's $DD89/$DDB4 were not their
addresses. One bug shipped and came back out: LDA #PN_SPACE followed
by BNE-always never branches, PN_SPACE being zero.

Verified in jsbeeb end to end: play -> ESCAPE -> AAA committed at the
entry -> title -> timeout -> briefing -> M through to page 5 -> "Top
score of the day: 6809 - AEB" and "Worst score of the day: 0 - AAA".

wonderboy: batch 43 phase A — the reconstruction runs on a real 68000

events.title: Layer 11f F4: the briefing on screen, driven from &0400 and bank 5
events.message:
Layer 11f F4: the briefing on screen, driven from &0400 and bank 5

The text pipeline is now two stages (KC): export_briefing.py decodes
the C64 text ONCE into src/data/briefing.txt - hand-editable, verbatim,
the pause-key legend included - and refuses to overwrite it without
--force; make_briefing.py converts it every build (build.ps1 runs it),
validating characters and page width and round-tripping the emitted
glyph indices back against the input.

PARMAN (bank 5) carries the record lists: bank 5 is evicted for the
briefing [DECISION 4] and both exits reload PARASPR via the PARDEPK
dance, so a fire at the next title cannot start a game whose blitter
is briefing text. PARBRF (&0400, the dead MODE 1 charset ground) is
the driver: BrTimeout fetches the text when TiWait's wrap fires,
BrDispatch sits where both post-title paths called GameStartInfo, and
the exit-to-game re-enters TitleSeq's own tail at the new ts_loads
label rather than carrying a copy. TiShow loads PARBRF on every title
so the dispatch is always valid.

The renderer paints canvas rows straight from the per-page row lists -
top halves of a row's records plus bottom halves of the row above's -
through FontCell from the resident font, with DrawChar's wide rule and
the three brExtra glyphs (comma, apostrophe, semicolon) from the bank.
palPlay is stated explicitly: nothing else sets it before a deck loads.

F4 shape verified in jsbeeb over every path: boot->timeout->briefing,
M/K page stepping across all five pages, L->game (blitter reloaded,
playable), ESCAPE->entry->title->timeout->briefing, off page 5->title,
and fire at the title straight to a game.

Also closed: the F1 "loose end" - hsHigh not matching a poked score
was scoreAdd/scoreSub draining through DoScore during the death
sequence. With the queues zeroed the copy is byte-exact. Not a defect.

events.title: fix(mcp): confine tool file I/O to the cache and workspace
events.message:
fix(mcp): confine tool file I/O to the cache and workspace

screenshot and save wrote caller-supplied output paths (creating
arbitrary directories along the way) and symbols_load readFileSync'd
any path unbounded — the MCP server runs with the user's full
permissions, so these were arbitrary filesystem access. New mcp/paths.ts
resolves each path (collapsing .. traversal, case-insensitive on
Windows) and confines it to the MCP cache dir and the server working
directory; symbols_load additionally caps reads at 8 MB. Tool params
that fall outside the roots are refused with an explanatory message.
README documents the confinement.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(mcp): cap trapLog at 2000 entries like the FDC log ring
events.message:
fix(mcp): cap trapLog at 2000 entries like the FDC log ring

A 'log'-mode trap appends on every instruction passing its PC, so long
runs grew the buffer without bound. Route all trap-log appends through
pushTrapLog(), which trims the oldest line past the same 2000-entry cap
the FDC log uses. Tests drive 2500 hits through a log trap and pin the
oldest-dropped ring semantics.
events.author: damieng

events.title: docs(io): document AMX/Kempston 0x1F bus priority in the port chain
events.message:
docs(io): document AMX/Kempston 0x1F bus priority in the port chain

The AMX mouse decodes only A5-A7, so its X-counter port (0x00-0x1F)
overlaps the Kempston joystick port 0x1F; on real hardware both
interfaces contend for the bus. When the AMX mouse is enabled it sits
earlier in the decode chain and wins 0x1F (and 0xDF over the Kempston
mouse) — an intentional priority now stated at the decode site instead
of left as a silent trap. No behaviour change.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(upd765a): route public APIs through physUnit like the rest of the core
events.message:
fix(upd765a): route public APIs through physUnit like the rest of the core

getDiskImage/setTrack/insertDisk/ejectDisk indexed per-drive state with
`unit & 3` while command execution resolves through physUnit() (unit &
1), so a caller passing a logical unit of 2 or 3 would strand a disk in
a slot no drive can address — the +3 only wires two drive-select lines
and units 2/3 alias to drives 0/1. All public APIs now resolve through
physUnit, and the per-drive arrays (pcn/disks/writeProtect/forceReady/
idIndex/flipSide) shrink to physical size so the dead logical slots
cannot be resurrected. Callers only ever passed 0/1, so behaviour is
unchanged; the old test that pinned the un-aliased getDiskImage as "by
design" now pins the aliasing instead.
events.author: damieng

events.title: test(z80): pin R-register M1 counting for DD CB / FD CB
events.message:
test(z80): pin R-register M1 counting for DD CB / FD CB

Review flagged executeDDCB/FDCB as missing the R increment for the CB
opcode byte. Verified against the comp.sys.sinclair FAQ ("The R
Register"): doubly-shifted DD CB / FD CB opcodes increase R by exactly
two on hardware — and the core already does this, because the CB prefix
byte is fetched with its M1 R increment by executeDD()/executeFD()
before dispatch. No behaviour change; new tests pin the hardware values
(plain/prefixed/doubly-shifted, redundant prefix chains, LD A,R's
post-increment read, and 7-bit wrap) so the pattern is not misread
again.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(tzx): clamp zero pulse lengths to 1 T-state at parse time
events.message:
fix(tzx): clamp zero pulse lengths to 1 T-state at parse time

A malformed Pure Tone (0x12) or Pulse Sequence (0x13) with a zero
pulse length makes the playback loop burn through every remaining pulse
in a single advance() — up to 65535 EAR toggles in one frame — and a
Direct Recording (0x15) with a zero sample period never terminates at
all. Zero-length pulses are non-physical; every file-sourced pulse
length (turbo timings, tone, pulse sequence, pure-data bit pulses,
direct sample period) is now clamped to at least 1 T-state when parsed.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(scl): cap catalog at 128 entries and bound-check file headers
events.message:
fix(scl): cap catalog at 128 entries and bound-check file headers

parseScl wrote catalog entries at i*16 without regard for the 128-entry
(8-sector) catalog area, so a fileCount byte above 128 overran the
disk-info sector and file data. It also read header fields before
checking they were in bounds: past-EOF reads yield undefined, and the
resulting NaN arithmetic made every truncation guard compare false,
importing phantom files and poisoning the info sector with NaN.

Clamp the import loop to 128 entries and require each 14-byte header to
be fully in-bounds before reading it. Both regressions are covered by
tests that fail against the old parser.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(zip): cap inflate output at 64 MiB and size results from actual bytes
events.message:
fix(zip): cap inflate output at 64 MiB and size results from actual bytes

inflate() buffered whatever the deflate stream produced with no limit,
so a zip bomb exhausted memory, and it sized the assembly buffer from
the central directory's uncompressedSize claim — an understated claim
made Uint8Array.set throw RangeError past the end, an overstated one
silently zero-padded the tail.

The 64 MiB cap rejects oversized declared entries up front and stops
the stream mid-inflate for bombs; the result buffer is now sized from
the bytes actually produced. Tests cover both lying directions plus a
real oversized stream.
events.author: damieng

events.title: refactor: remove dead trap-log plumbing and duplicate microdrive constant
events.message:
refactor: remove dead trap-log plumbing and duplicate microdrive constant

setTrapLogHtml was never called from production code, so trapLogHtml
was always empty and DrivePane's #trap-log block could never render;
showTrapLog was only ever written false (frame-bridge). Removes the
debug-state signals, the DrivePane block, the frame-bridge write, the
#trap-log CSS, and the test entries that pinned the dead defaults.

Also collapses microdrive.ts's duplicate offset constants
(RECORD_OFFSET === RECORD_DATA_OFFSET === 15) into one.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(wd179x): track register wraps at 8 bits instead of clamping to 0-79
events.message:
fix(wd179x): track register wraps at 8 bits instead of clamping to 0-79

The WD179x track register is an 8-bit counter on real hardware: SEEK
loads the data register verbatim and STEP wraps 0 <-> 255. Clamping to
79 in the shared core bakes a double-density 80-track assumption into
machine-agnostic silicon. Out-of-range cylinders now simply miss on the
next data command (RNF) exactly as they would on a drive without that
many tracks.

The old wd1772 test asserted the clamp; replaced with 8-bit wrap
expectations (SEEK 200 -> 200, STEP OUT at 0 -> 255).
events.author: damieng

events.title: refactor(spi): move ByteReader from spectrum/memory.ts onto the machine SPI
events.message:
refactor(spi): move ByteReader from spectrum/memory.ts onto the machine SPI

The SPI (machines/machine.ts) imported ByteReader from one concrete
machine folder, coupling every machine's contract to spectrum/. Define
the interface on the SPI itself; SpectrumMemory now implements it via
IMachineMemory.

events.title: Layer 11f F1: the high-score entry, SetupPlain, and the briefing export
events.message:
Layer 11f F1: the high-score entry, SetupPlain, and the briefing export

DoHighScore lives in the PARTITL overlay with its own alphabet
(export_hsfont.py); its 25-byte table is in bank 7 so it outlives a
title. Verified end to end in jsbeeb: both arms, the K/M walk, three
initials committed, hsArmed cleared.

SetupPlain (bank 4) replaces SetupMode on the GoTitle path: six CRTC
registers instead of a VDU 22, so the OS no longer clears &3000-&7FFF
