events.title: amiga: the VBL starvation is an amiberry 68000-core artifact — instrument the proof
events.message:
amiga: the VBL starvation is an amiberry 68000-core artifact — instrument the proof

Why the VBL starves during a quant, chased to the end. Four probes, four
eliminations:

- TOD wall clock per bard window: the long conversions really get 1/3
  service (762 calls / 2292 ticks) while short ones get 50 Hz — and every
  earlier rl-clock duration inside a quant was undercounting wall time 3x.
- Arrival-gap histogram: the starved windows are METRONOMIC gap-3 (777x
  and 895x, zero 2s, zero 4s). Not jitter, not load — quantized delivery.
- Mainline sampler (per band, from inside the quant): IPL 0, VERTB
  enabled, master enable on, VERTB never pending in 175 samples. Nothing
  masks, nothing sits unserviced.
- Chain brackets at pri 127 and -128: the FRONT server (ahead of
  graphics/Intuition) is starved to the same 1-in-3 as the tail. No
  server aborts the chain — the level-3 interrupt is taken 1-in-3.

Byte-identical under JIT and true cycle-exact (the earlier "cycle-exact
A/B" was void: sound_output=none makes amiberry silently downgrade
cycle-exact — the warning is in its log). Same machine, same chipset,
same binary, same art on the 68020 core: clean 50 Hz in all 13 windows.
Real 68000 silicon cannot do this (IPL sampled every instruction
boundary; Agnus raises VERTB unconditionally), so this is amiberry's
68000 core quantizing interrupt checks in tight loops. Consequences under
emulation only: rl durations inside big quants are 3x floors, input polls
~17 Hz there. The bard's TOD clock already made tempo immune.

The probes stay in: they cost ~30 cycles/frame plus a few DBG.LOG lines
per cold conversion, and the first boot on a real A600 prints the
histogram that confirms (or overturns) the artifact call on silicon.

Trap recorded in-source: MOVE from SR is unprivileged ONLY on the 68000,
and a compile-time #ifndef guard in a -m68000 binary still executes on an
020 machine — it hung two cross-check boots (the "AGA incompatibility"
was this, retracted). The sampler now gates on SysBase->AttnFlags.

events.title: refactor(ui): move Spectrum font hunting into the machine's ui/ folder
events.message:
refactor(ui): move Spectrum font hunting into the machine's ui/ folder

FontPane (generic UI) branched on machine.kind and baked Spectrum
memory layout into src/ui: the 0x4000 screen-bitmap address math for
tile extraction, the CHARS sysvar read at 0x5C36, and the ROM ©
signature scan.

Move all of it to machines/spectrum/ui/font-hunt.ts and expose it as a
new optional `HuntFonts` contribution in the machine-ui manifest — the
same sanctioned seam as the keyboard-lab preset loaders. The pane now
calls whatever the active machine contributes and reports "not
available" when there is none; no kind branching, no concrete-machine
imports outside the manifest. The hunt module is dynamically imported
on first use, keeping other machines' bundles clean.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(mcp): cap read_memory dumps at 64KB
events.message:
fix(mcp): cap read_memory dumps at 64KB

read_memory.length accepted any positive integer and formatHexDump
walks the full length synchronously, so one flat-space call with e.g.
length=100000000 hung the persistent MCP server. The banked branch was
already clamped by the 16KB bank view; cap length at 0x10000 — a dump
of the entire address space is the most that can ever be meaningful.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(tzx): validate embedded CSW header before allocating pulses
events.message:
fix(tzx): validate embedded CSW header before allocating pulses

The 0x18 block sized its pulse buffer directly from the unvalidated
32-bit pulseCount field — `new Uint32Array(0xFFFFFFFF)` is a 16 GB
allocation attempt, an instant OOM on a malformed tape — and divided
by the sample rate unchecked, poisoning every pulse with NaN/Infinity
on a zero rate.

Reject a zero sample rate (mirroring csw.ts) and reject a pulse count
larger than the RLE byte count: each RLE item yields at most one pulse,
so a bigger claim is corrupt. The allocation is now bounded by the RLE
data length.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(upd765a): mask sector-size N codes to their 3 meaningful bits
events.message:
fix(upd765a): mask sector-size N codes to their 3 meaningful bits

N arrives as a raw byte — from READ/WRITE DATA command streams, FORMAT
TRACK CHRN tuples, and disk-image sector IDs. An unmasked `128 << n`
goes negative for n = 31/63/… (JS shifts mask the count mod 32), so
`new Uint8Array(-2147483648)` threw a RangeError from inside port I/O
and killed the frame loop.

Route every size computation through a shared sectorXferSize() helper
that masks n & 7, matching the WD179x core's treatment; values 0–7 are
unchanged.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(msx): map 48KB cartridges to pages 1–3, not pages 0–2
events.message:
fix(msx): map 48KB cartridges to pages 1–3, not pages 0–2

MSX cartridges decode from 0x4000 upward, but the ≤48KB branch of
buildCartViews filled pages 0–2: page 0 shadowed the BIOS ROM region
and the cart's top 16KB (0xC000–0xFFFF) was unreachable. Map the three
16KB chunks to pages 1–3 instead and correct the doc comment that
baked in the wrong layout.
events.author: damieng

events.title: docs(dsk): record why N=6 decodes as 6144 bytes
events.message:
docs(dsk): record why N=6 decodes as 6144 bytes

The 6144-byte sector size for N=6 (not the nominal 128 << 6 = 8192) is
intentional: these images come off 3" Hitachi DD drives whose tracks
hold ~6.25 KB in total, so an 8 KB sector can never physically exist on
this media — giant-sector protections recorded 6144 bytes under N=6.
Comment it at the decode site so it doesn't get "fixed" back to spec.
events.author: damieng

events.title: wonderboy/kit: batch 42 phase C — THE SPINE CLOSES
events.message:
wonderboy/kit: batch 42 phase C — THE SPINE CLOSES

THE MILESTONE: the spine's inventory reaches ZERO remainder — 898 bytes
in eleven rows, 294 (A) + 380 (B) + 224 (C) = flip_screen (118) +
game_main_loop (106). Every routine reachable from the frame loop, the
VBL and flip_screen is reconstructed. 314 fns / 40,976 B / 92.6%;
wonderboy 6,138, kit 392, joust 4,369, buggyboy 292, hw 56 — all
clean-build serial.

Kit (the sched model's remedy — TRAP_MODEL Phase 8 revised):
- PER-SITE poll counting: a site = the address at which the original
  RE-READS the polled byte (the definition was first written as 'the
  compare' and was wrong on nine surfaces — where a cmpi reads and
  tests in one instruction the two coincide, which made the loose
  reading easy to write); the store fires BEFORE the site's
  instruction; undeclared-site polls refused, symmetrically counted
  on both primitives. RED-first: the deleted-first-wait mutant
  SURVIVES the run-total model and DIES per-site. The $6ca split is
  DISCHARGED, not performed. sched_poll16 = capped iterator.
- HONEST NEGATIVE, stated where maintainers read: the firing rule
  carries the catch; the per-site comparison is an unproven tripwire
  (both isolating composites came back caught by the firing rule).

Reconstruction:
- flip_screen: two word-waits (signed ready threshold; a tick wait
  comparing a copy taken one instruction earlier — cannot be seeded
  past; not.w is a toggle); both deleted-wait mutants CAUGHT; three
  hardware sink registers named by four SURVIVING mutants as the
  honest measure of the shifter-backend hole.
- game_main_loop: the whole frame as one ~245k-instruction run, six
  frames driven; composition finds: panel_refresh_frame republishes
  the actor-table pointer mid-frame (the spawn pass reads the frame's
  choice); the shipped table has no terminator within 1,948 records;
  the unpause runs before the keyboard routine and forgets the
  scancode. Biggest sweep find: a dropped 19,200-byte blit call
  survived on zeros-over-zeros (poison off, unseeded destination) —
  repaired with a keyed screen fill whose delivery is now ASSERTED
  against the built image, not comment-enforced.

Review gate (2 finders, 12 findings applied): the stray-write region
that whitelisted the VBL's own code split into real fields (with a
tripwire test checking every band against the spine walk's entry
set); the held frame given its premise measurement (which corrected
the writer tuple AND the drop-a-call byte count); poll16's refusal
path made symmetric; the running header re-swept; sweep arithmetic
restated with its counting rule (109 sweep runs + 3 RED-first = 112;
48 distinct configurations); ten terminal survivors, each classified.

NOT PLAYABLE YET, stated plainly: on-target backends remain (psg,
sched, hw, a shifter backend), then the .PRG on Joust's pattern —
and the BOOT CHAIN is not in the spine's inventory. Next arc:
on-target backends → the playable .PRG.
events.author: geogeo28

events.title: amiga: the bard keeps time off the power supply — the VBL is starved during a quant
events.message:
amiga: the bard keeps time off the power supply — the VBL is starved during a quant

The tavern revision came back from the user's ear as "slow, with a tick in it,
and it changes mid-tone... it degraded in performance". All three were real,
and the third was the finding:

  ! THE VBL SOUND HOOK RUNS AT 15-31 Hz DURING A QUANT, not 50. Measured: 73
    and 754 bard_vbl calls in windows expecting ~250 and ~1150. A sequencer
    clocked "once per call" therefore ran at a third speed, sagging with the
    cut's workload -- the user heard the tempo change live as the quant's
    phases shifted. Two consequences beyond the bard, both recorded here
    because they outlast it:
      - the ENGINE's ring is refilled by this same starved hook while Paula
        consumes at 50 Hz, so every conversion under-fills it and Paula loops
        stale content. That -- not just the frozen mainline sequencer chord --
        is the root of the "struggling to not die" boot audio.
      - amiga_prof_rl builds on the VBL tick counter, so rl timings taken
        INSIDE a quant undercount wall time. The re-band improvement RATIOS
        measured this week stand (both sides used the same clock); the
        absolute seconds are floors.

The fix: the bard clocks itself off CIA-A's TOD counter -- 24-bit, 50 Hz off
the power supply, immune to interrupt starvation, readable from any context
(read HI to latch, LO to release) -- and advances by ELAPSED ticks per call.
At 15 Hz servicing the envelopes step in chunks of ~3; the tempo is true.
Verified: the same starved windows (73/754 calls) now produce a steady
2900-3800 RMS bard with no sag, approved by ear ("that sounds like the one").

Also in this cut, each mapped to a complaint:
  - "a tick": plucks stepped ac_vol 0->64 instantly at arbitrary waveform
    phase -- a click per note. Both voices now ramp the attack over 3 frames.
  - "somber... more upbeat and adventurous": recomposed from the D dorian
    ballad to D MIXOLYDIAN at ~170 bpm -- dotted rising phrases landing on the
    octave, a walking bass at twice the old rate. The half-rate "tavern
    sustain" decay is gone too (every note was a slow fade -- literally the
    sound of dying), the bass decays to silence instead of holding a
    permanent floor, and the drone sits at 14.
  - the waveform is full-scale (+-120; +-60 left 6 dB unused with Paula's
    volume register already at its 64 max).

All five configs build; 471 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: amiga: a campfire bard plays while the palette quantiser runs
events.message:
amiga: a campfire bard plays while the palette quantiser runs

The user asked for a DSOTS-spirit loading screen -- "please wait" with music --
and, since this is a D&D engine, suggested "old bard sounding tunes" over the
demo's techno. This is that: while a cold conversion runs, a plucked chip-lute
plays sixteen original bars in D dorian over a soft fifth drone. Sparse on
purpose ("campfire bard", the user's pick): one melody voice, plucks left to
ring, ~90 bpm.

It also FIXES something, not just decorates it. The engine's audio could not
cover this window: its notes come from the sequencer in the MAINLINE, which is
busy doing the median cuts, so the VBL ring faithfully rendered whatever chord
was sounding when the cut began -- a 10-20 s frozen drone, first reported by
the user as "something struggling to not die" when a test boot's audio leaked
onto their desktop. While the bard plays, AUD0 (the engine ring) is muted and
restored on stop, so the frozen chord is impossible by construction.

Mechanics: AUD1 melody + AUD2 drone -- channels the engine NEVER uses (its
whole Mac synth is software-mixed onto channel 0). Entirely VBL-driven and
DMA-fed, immune to the stall it decorates: Paula loops a 32-byte triangle by
itself; the VBL only retunes ac_per and walks the pluck envelope down ac_vol.
The waveform is synthesized at start in CHIP RAM and the melody is a period
table -- nothing shipped, nothing licensed. Started on a palette-cache miss,
stopped when the cut lands; stop restores the engine's volume, so like the
notice it cannot outstay the conversion.

  ! the first triangle used a step of 15, which peaks at 165 and OVERFLOWS
    signed char -- still a pitch, but an aliased snarl. +-60 over 16 samples
    is a step of 8. Caught before it ever played.

Verified live off Paula (host-audio capture, per-second RMS): boot audio
~5000 RMS, the bard window 140-780 in clear pluck-decay shapes, engine audio
back at ~5000 the moment the conversion ends, and the next re-band's bard
window starting on cue. The bard sits well below the engine's four-voice mix
(one channel at 64 + drone at 10) -- deliberate, and one line to retune if the
campfire is too shy.

All five configs build; 471 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: amiga/ecs: cache the band palettes on disk, and say "please wait" while cutting them
events.message:
amiga/ecs: cache the band palettes on disk, and say "please wait" while cutting them

The user asked the exact right question: "is that because you're doing a
quantization every time you load the game rather than caching it on disk?" It
was. Every boot ran ~5 re-bands of 25 median cuts each -- ~47 s of quantisation
per boot computing IDENTICAL answers: same art, same CLUTs, deterministic
quantiser.

PALCACHE.ECS: keyed on (CLUT hash, frame hash), stores the POST-unify-border
band palettes + remaps (~8.8 KB/entry, 16 max), written on miss, hit = two
memcpys. Measured: a warm re-band renders in ~3 s against ~12-23 s for a cold
one (the residual is the render itself plus used-set capture, not the cut). A
new design's art means new keys, so it announces and caches itself the same
way. Deleting the file is always safe -- it regenerates. EPC_VERSION must be
bumped with ANY change to quantize.h's output, or a stale file silently pins
the OLD palettes; the header check discards foreign files wholesale.

  ! the hash is shift-add (djb2-style), NOT FNV: FNV's multiply is __mulsi3 on
    a 68000 and hashing the 64000-byte frame would cost ~1.8 s -- a tenth of
    the re-band it is trying to save.

THE FIRST-LOAD NOTICE: a cold cut leaves the screen frozen for ~10 s with no
way to tell "converting" from "hung", so a cache miss now draws PLEASE WAIT...
CONVERTING ART with a REAL progress bar -- quantize.h gains an optional
per-band callback (quant_progress, per-TU static, NULL costs one compare), and
the bands are the honest unit: 25 per cut, 8 px of bar each. Text in slot 31
on a slot-30 box with both copper operands forced readable, drawn straight
onto the visible page. The mechanism needs NO cleanup path: the re-band this
notice precedes ends by installing the fresh palette over every operand, and
the full render that follows redraws every plane -- the work it announces
erases it. Verified live: bar fills left to right across a conversion; warm
boots never show it.

  ! the first layout ran the bar's trough THROUGH the second text line --
    caught in the screenshot, not the code read.

Also muted the two headless capture configs (sound_output=none, local): the X
display is virtual but amiberry's AUDIO is not, and the capture boots were
playing the stalling boot audio into the user's room -- which is itself a
lead: the "struggling to not die" sound during a cold re-band is plausibly
the game's own stream starving while the mainline cuts, and a real Amiga
would reproduce it. Recorded as a hypothesis for the loading-tune work.

All five configs build; 471 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: fix(display): dispose WebGL renderer resources instead of leaking them
events.message:
fix(display): dispose WebGL renderer resources instead of leaking them

WebGLRenderer had no teardown path: toggling the renderer setting
dropped a canvas still holding a live context (7 programs, textures,
FBO, buffers) against the browser's ~16-context-per-page limit, and
model switches orphaned the old renderer's GPU objects inside the
shared context. Selecting an HQx mode before its LUT PNG loaded also
sampled an unbound texture unit for a frame.

- Add optional dispose() to IScreenRenderer; WebGLRenderer deletes its
  programs, shaders, owned textures (tracked explicitly so replaced LUT
  placeholders don't leak), buffers and FBO, optionally losing the
  context.
- setCanvas discards the old canvas element, so it disposes with
  loseContext; createMachine reuses the canvas, so it disposes
  resources only; shell destroy() loses the context.
- Seed HQx LUT slots with a 1x1 placeholder texture so pre-load draws
  sample a defined texture, and ignore LUT images arriving after
  dispose.

Covered by new mock-based dispose tests in webgl-renderer.test.ts.
events.author: damieng

events.title: refactor(tzx): advance the block cursor via nextBlockOffset
events.message:
refactor(tzx): advance the block cursor via nextBlockOffset

The parse loop's main switch re-implemented, case by case, exactly the
offset arithmetic that nextBlockOffset already computes for the up-front
validation pass. Any future edit to a block's layout had to be made
twice or the two passes desync.

Linear cases now fall through to a single shared advance
(o = nextBlockOffset(fileData, blockStart)); only Jump/Call/Return/
Select position the cursor themselves and skip it with `continue`.
Safe by construction: blockOffsets() has already validated every
block's extent before the parse loop runs.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(mcp): cap run frames at 5000
events.message:
fix(mcp): cap run frames at 5000

run.frames accepted any positive integer and runUntil blocks the
single-threaded MCP server for the full count — one call with
frames=100000000 wedged the persistent process with no cancellation.

Cap it at 5000, matching the continue tool's default ceiling.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(scp): clamp flux count and cell expansion on malformed images
events.message:
fix(scp): clamp flux count and cell expansion on malformed images

The per-revolution fluxCount from the TRK header was never validated
against the bytes actually present. Past EOF every 16-bit read decodes
as 0, which only accumulates carry, so a truncated image spun the flux
loop toward ~4 billion iterations — a multi-minute effective hang.

Clamp fluxCount to the available byte pairs before decoding, and budget
cell emission in fluxToCells (2M cells, far above any real track) so a
crafted giant interval cannot amplify into hundreds of millions of
pushed entries.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(tzx): cap loop expansion to reject nested-loop bombs
events.message:
fix(tzx): cap loop expansion to reject nested-loop bombs

Loop Start/End pairs expand at parse time and nest multiplicatively:
each count is up to 65535, so two nested loops re-slice already-expanded
inner bodies and push billions of entries into the block array — a tiny
hand-crafted TZX OOMs or hangs the tab.

Check the projected total against a 262144-block ceiling before
duplicating (real tapes stay orders of magnitude below it) and throw a
clear error when the expansion would exceed it.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(tzx): reject cyclic Jump/Call/Select control flow at parse time
events.message:
fix(tzx): reject cyclic Jump/Call/Select control flow at parse time

Jump targets were range-checked but not cycle-checked, and loops are
expanded at parse time — so a Jump with offset -1 (which targets the
jump block itself) re-parsed itself forever, freezing the tab on a
malformed or legitimately self-looping tape. Call/Select/Return cycles
had the same hazard.

Budget main-loop iterations against the pre-computed block table
(generous headroom for legitimate call/return revisits) and throw a
clear "control flow does not terminate" error when exhausted.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(cpr): treat RIFF chunk sizes as unsigned to prevent parser hang
events.message:
fix(cpr): treat RIFF chunk sizes as unsigned to prevent parser hang

A chunk size with the sign bit set was read as a negative 32-bit value,
slipped past the truncation guard, and rewound the chunk cursor far
before the start of the buffer — where every subsequent read decodes as
size 0 and the parse loop never advances again. A malformed .cpr froze
the tab.

Decode the size with an unsigned shift so it can never go negative; an
oversized size now fails the existing truncation guard and parsing stops
with whatever pages were collected.

Enhance MIDI functionality and audio mixing capabilities

- Updated `.gitignore` to exclude MT-32/CM-32L ROM files.

events.title: The title sits at the same height as the game
events.message:
The title sits at the same height as the game

TiCRTC sets R7 as well as R6, and the value is derived from
FRAME_DROP_ROWS rather than dialled in by eye:

  game    VSync is TAIL_R7 rows into the 13-row tail cycle and the
          panel starts when that cycle ends, so the gap is
          TAIL_CYC_ROWS - TAIL_R7  =  5 + FRAME_DROP_ROWS rows
  title   VSync is at row R7 of a 39-row frame and the display starts
          at row 0 of the next, so the gap is  39 - R7  rows

Equate them: TITLE_R7 = 34 - FRAME_DROP_ROWS. At zero that is 34, the
OS's own MODE 1 value, which is why the two were level before the game's
picture moved and why the title was left behind when it did. Move
FRAME_DROP_ROWS again and both follow.

I said last commit this could not be done with R7, and that was wrong.
It rested on the OS frame's R6 = 32 against VSync at 34 - two blank rows
of headroom, too few to drop R7 into. True of the OS frame, but TiCRTC
has already cut R6 to TITLE_ROWS = 25, which leaves fourteen. The
ASSERT is what says so now, and what will fail if the title ever grows
past the room its own sync leaves it. Nothing had to be redrawn.

Verified through both paths that reach TiShow: the boot, and the
game-over seam, which comes back through SetupMode and sets it again.
Panel top and the title's first ink land within half a character row of
each other, which is where the logo's border starts inside its own row.

events.title: Move the picture 4 rows down the tube
events.message:
Move the picture 4 rows down the tube

The set locks to VSync and counts down from it, so moving VSync EARLIER
in our frame moves the picture DOWN. Nothing else changes: the frame is
still 312 scanlines and the three cycles are untouched, and all that
moves is how the 120 scanlines of blanking are split between the front
porch (picture bottom -> VSync) and the back porch (VSync -> panel top).
It was 80/40 and the picture sat high with the black stacked under it;
it is 48/72 now, both still far beyond PAL's ~5 and ~25.

FRAME_DROP_ROWS is that number in character rows. KC, 2026-08-21: four.
TAIL_R7 becomes 8 - FRAME_DROP_ROWS, so VSync moves from P+272 to P+240.
T1_I1 is derived from the same constant, because the T1 chain is
restarted at VSync and every fire in the frame is measured from it -
shift one without the other and the whole rupture lands 32 scanlines
into the wrong part of the frame.

R7 = 255 had to move from fire 1 to RuptVSync, and this is the part that
was found by building it rather than by reasoning about it. Fire 1 is at
P+44, row 5 of the 7-row panel cycle, so R7 held the tail's value for
the first five rows of every frame - harmless only because that value
was 8, which a 7-row cycle can never reach. At 4 the panel cycle reaches
it at P+32 and fires a VSync of its own, which re-enters RuptVSync
mid-frame, restarts T1 and zeroes ruptState. Fire 1 then never runs, the
play cycle is never set up or unblanked, and the play area is BLACK with
the panel alone on a rolling picture. R7 belongs to the previous cycle,
which for the panel is the tail, and that is where it now is.

The title did NOT move: it runs under SetupMode's ordinary MODE 1 frame,
not the rupture, and matching it is not a matter of dropping its R7 -
that frame has only two rows of blanking between the end of the display
and VSync. It would mean drawing the artwork lower in its own
framebuffer. Recorded in docs/layer-3-scroll.md, not done.

Verified in jsbeeb: boot, the 001 page, gameplay, ESCAPE, the wash and
the game-over seam back to the title. The picture is 32 scanlines lower
and steady, with no roll and nothing lost off either edge.

events.title: wonderboy: batch 42 phase B — seven of the spine's nine
events.message:
wonderboy: batch 42 phase B — seven of the spine's nine

Reconstruction (312 fns / 40,752 B / 92.1%; suite 6,098; kit untouched):
- game_latch_input_and_step_actors ($882), game_snap_follow_cursor
  ($50a), psg_set_drive_select ($624c, PSG Phase-6 pinned),
  floppy_deselect_drives ($6268), round_bonus_run_frame ($e032 — the
  long-queued $e1be reader: a two-phase meter drain whose score add
  carries an X produced INSIDE the run; an empty meter scores one more
  and does not end the drain), round_bonus_setup ($e0a8,
  region-bounded write set), vbl_handler ($716).
- THE VBL CONVENTION, designed from first principles (0 rte in either
  sibling's image — enumerated): checkpoint the rte itself with the
  kit's existing stop_pc; self-witnessing (the body has no rts,
  asserted from bytes) plus a negative control. rte pops a 6-byte
  exception frame and can never reach the 4-byte sentinel.
- Inventory arithmetic to a named remainder, two-sided ledger: 898 =
  294 (A) + 380 (here) + 224 left = game_main_loop 106 + flip_screen
  118 — flip_screen registered at depth: the sched model ACCEPTS the
  natural one-trigger two-wait run (counters cancel; the
  deleted-first-wait mutant survives), so the $6ca split is REQUIRED;
  width needs no new kit primitive, only a capped wrapper.

Review gate (2 finders over the full diff; the bodies re-derived
byte-for-byte and CLEAN): 9 findings applied — headlined by a MEASURED
hole: DRIVE_BITS pinned two unreachable values while missing bits=5,
one of the game's only two reachable ones; the mutant survived the
whole 6,091-case suite twice, now CAUGHT with two bounding neighbours.
Lesson recorded: a value chosen to pin an instruction's width does not
pin what the game does with it — the reachable set is the list a
battery owes a case each. Also: the gate's own mid-phase rewrite swept
to every surface (the retracted width-led framing), a phantom queue
entry landed for real, batch-21b's target-buildability claim annotated
in place (the spine module now gates the PSG backend), round-four
survivors terminally classified (one = the read-after-store class's
EIGHTH sighting), and the scan caught the fix pass's own first rewrite
quoting a retracted phrase.

Sweeps: 58 distinct mutants over 66 runs, five clean rounds.
hw_portability 56 green.

Remaining for the spine: game_main_loop (106 B, waits on flip_screen)
+ flip_screen (118 B, waits on the $6ca split). Then on-target
backends (PSG backend now gates the whole spine module) → the
playable .PRG. Queued adds: whole-body asm() pins for the seven,
capped word-wait wrapper, per-site poll counter.

events.title: Every non-gameplay screen shows all 16 rows
events.message:
Every non-gameplay screen shows all 16 rows

The play area displays sixteen rows and only fifteen are visible: the
sixteenth carries the smooth scroll's sub-row fraction, and the R8 blank
at fire 3 is all that hides it. With the scroll flattened - which every
screen that takes the buffer over does first - that row is real buffer.
The transfer board, the lift's deck select and the deck plan already
showed it, via T1_I3X; the console and its three pages, the four
information screens and the game over's wash now do too. KC, 2026-08-21.

The PORTED pages move down one row onto the C64's own. Its screen area
is rows 9-24 and it puts the database's name line at row 10 and the
content at 12, 14 ... 22 - buffer rows 1 and 3, 5 ... 13. At fifteen
rows the page had to start at row 0 and every line came out one row
high. DB_LINE_ROW0 carries the missing row into dbLineLo/Hi and
DB_IMG_ROW follows it, so the portrait moves with the text; the
information screens and the game-over page ride on the same table. The
console main screen does NOT move - KC's rule is to plot from the top
row, and the top row is still row 0.

Set on entry, restored in ONE place. The four instructions used to be
copied into each screen's exit - three of them in bank 4, which had
three bytes free - and the deck plan's had to be undone by the console's
own the moment the page closed. ReframeView is where every path back to
the deck goes through, so the restore lives there and
ConDeckEnter4/ConDeckExit4 are gone. Bank 4: 3 bytes free -> 60.

Only the high byte is a variable, and structurally so: the two intervals
differ by one character row, a row is 8 scanlines and a scanline is
SL = 64 ticks, so the difference is &200 exactly. t1i3Lo is now a
constant the rupture reads and nobody writes, with an ASSERT to keep it
true. That halved all six sites, which mattered - the main-RAM code
image had FOUR bytes left, not the 47 CLAUDE.md and PLAN.md claimed, and
writing both bytes in ReframeView took it to zero. Both documents' RAM
figures are now measured ones.

ConClear and DbClear grow to PLAY_ROWS: they cleared fifteen because the
last row was never shown, and leaving them would have put a strip of the
deck along the bottom of every console screen. The wash needed no such
change - GoWashRow has always run X = 0-15, because the C64's fills its
whole screen area.

Verified in jsbeeb, not just built: console main, database browser,
stats page, deck plan and the close, reached by walking to a console on
deck 2; and ESCAPE -> explosion -> wash -> 999 page -> title -> new game
-> the 001 page. t1i3Hi reads &1F on every screen and &1D again the
moment ReframeView runs, and the bottom row is clean everywhere.

events.message:
Layer 11d: centre the 999, the way EndGame centres it

$37E8's STA loc_0_365E+1 is not a colour, as the portrait header first
guessed: loc_0_365E is BuildIntroSprites' own LDA #40 / STA SpriteX, and
EndGame patches the 40 to 160. Less the C64's first visible column at
24 that is 136 px in, which puts a 48 px picture exactly in the middle
of a 320 px screen, and $36B3 puts 40 back for every other page.

So PO_DST0 becomes poBase, a variable the caller sets: DbImage writes
the database page's rectangle and IsOverDraw writes PO_DSTMID, unit 34,
which is the same 136 px. KC asked for the 999 to be centred and the
original turns out to agree, so this is a fidelity fix rather than a
preference.

One trap on the way, and the same family as the PAGEBANK clobber earlier
in this layer: PoDraw takes the droid type in A, and DbImage used to
fall into it straight off STA poLastType. The two poBase stores in
between ate the type, and the portrait vanished from three of the four
pages until A was reloaded.

Verified: the 999 centred between Transmission and Terminated, and the
001 back on the left of its own page.

events.title: NuLA plan: b2's HTTP API from its docs, not from its strings
events.message:
NuLA plan: b2's HTTP API from its docs, not from its strings

doc/Debug-version.md documents the lot, and it was already in the tree
when this section was written by grepping the binary. Port 48075 is
0xbbcb; peek takes BEGIN/+SIZE as well as a range; s=SUFFIX picks the
memory view, `i` being the $fc00-$feff I/O one; reset?config= and
load-disc?path= point a RUNNING instance at a config and a disc, so
there is never a reason to kill and relaunch it.

The failed &FE23 poke was not the build being old. It is documented:
host memory-mapped I/O is not well supported, and poke writes emulated
memory rather than the bus. Register-level tests go through paste, and
need no newer b2 — so step 2 no longer asks for one.

events.title: ESCAPE self-destructs and ends the game; DEBUG_RESTART is gone
events.message:
ESCAPE self-destructs and ends the game; DEBUG_RESTART is gone

A way out of a game, and the port's own: the C64 has no equivalent, its
only abort being the RUN/STOP DoPause reads, which pauses. KC asked for
one and it is a game feature, not a debug key.

It kills the player AS A 001, whatever he was riding. CbCheckDeath's
$144D arm already says a captured droid falls back to a 001 and a 001
has nothing to fall back on, so forcing drType to 0 alongside drEnergy
is how "end the game" is spelled in that language - and the explosion,
the sound, the wash, the 999 page and the title all follow with nothing
else added.

It sits BELOW the four modal arms, unlike the R it replaces. R was above
them so a restart could be reached from the console, the lift view or
the transfer; a player-facing quit wants the opposite, because those
states have their own way out and a half-finished transfer applying its
outcome to a player who is already dead is a tangle with no reason to
exist.

ESCAPE is made an ordinary key with OSBYTE 229,1 in GameStartInfo.
Without it the MOS raises an escape CONDITION on the same press, and the
next filing-system call - GoTitle's own *LOADs, on the way out of the
game ESCAPE just ended - fails with Escape.

DEBUG_RESTART is removed entirely: the flag, the key, the loop block,
DEBUG_ANY3 and the !BOOT line, which now reads XFERWIN DECK. ESCAPE
tests Layer 11a's boot split better than R did, because it reaches
GameStart the long way round rather than jumping to it.

Verified in jsbeeb: press, explosion, wash, the 999 page, the title -
and the title's loads run clean, which is the OSBYTE working.

events.title: NuLA: a plan for the VideoNuLA build, as a separate deliverable
events.message:
NuLA: a plan for the VideoNuLA build, as a separate deliverable

Scroll and colour are the two the hardware fixes: control code 2 makes
the horizontal step 1 px instead of 4, which is the whole reason
CAM_TOPSPD is 8 rather than the C64's 7, and the 4096-colour palette
removes the nearest-BBC-hue approximation while leaving the four-colour
merge exactly where it is. Both land in the display path — the buffer,
the blitter and the tile data are untouched.

Costed against the port as it stands: the colour path comes out SMALLER
and faster than the &FE21 machinery it replaces (logical palette mode,
8 writes a swap instead of 16), and pays for the two zero-page bytes the
scroll offset needs. Attribute mode is parked, with reasons.

Verified rather than recalled: b2 implements the full register set
(m_scroll_offset, m_blanking_counter, m_direct_palette, the attribute
emitters), b-em likewise, and jsbeeb parses every control code and
renders only the palette — so the MCP cannot see the headline feature.
b2's HTTP API was driven end to end: peek returns &1100 byte-identical
to PARA on the disc, poke round-trips into RAM, poke does NOT reach the
I/O bus on the build to hand.

Nothing is built. Ships as a second executable on the same disc (10 of
31 catalogue slots used, 40K of 200K), chosen by KC's runtime detection.

events.title: Note for later: time the rupture switch so the TV keeps its lock
events.message:
Note for later: time the rupture switch so the TV keeps its lock

SetupRupture rewrites R4, R5, R6 and R7 from SetupMode's plain 39-row
frame to the three-cycle shape wherever the CPU happens to be, and a
television needs several fields to pull vertical sync back - so the way
into a game, and the way back after a game over, rolls for a moment.

Recorded as an open item in PLAN.md and, with the constraints it has to
respect, in docs/layer-3-scroll.md: switch on a field boundary rather
than mid-frame, order the writes so every intermediate state is still a
legal 312-line frame, and/or blank across the change. R6/R7/R12/R13
belong to the cycle before they fire, R5 must stay away from a cycle
boundary, and R7 must not sit at TAIL_R7 during a filing-system call.

Nothing measured yet; it wants the emulator and then real hardware,
since a TV's tolerance is what is being tuned.

events.title: Layer 11d: blank the strip before the rupture can show the title
events.message:
Layer 11d: blank the strip before the rupture can show the title

The title's framebuffer is &4000-&7E7F and the play buffer sits inside
it. TitleSeq rebuilds the panel and the &5400 tables over their share of
that ground, but nothing owns &5800-&7FFF until something draws there -
and now that the 001 screen holds LoadDeck's redraw back, that is not
until the page is printed. In between, SetupRupture starts displaying
the strip, and what it displayed was the title, smeared.

So TitleSeq blanks it on the way past, immediately before SetupRupture
and after PageLowIn. It is DbClear through a third IsEntry door, because
DbClear is already exactly this and there is no room in main RAM for a
second clear; the page calls it again a moment later, which costs 60,000
cycles once.

IsBlank sets infoAct to $FF as well. lowbss is SKIPped rather than
loaded, so at this point in the boot that byte has never been written,
and a garbage 0 would send InfoCall's continuation into ReframeView
before there is a deck to draw.

Verified from a cold boot: black behind the panel, then the page, then
the deck when the page is dismissed.

events.message:
Layer 11d: the 001 screen, and the printer that was already there

NewShipInfo ($36B9) on the deck's own ground: the Unit type 001 name
line, the portrait, and the original's prose with the ship's name
patched in from shipLevel as $36C7 patches it. Verified in jsbeeb.

PrintTokenString did not need writing. Layer 9's database page had
already ported PrCapitalString, ToUpper, the wrap, ShowRobotType and
BuildIntroSprites, and the 248-string pool ships - so infoscr.asm is the
loop and the screens, and the token bytes are the C64's verbatim. The
geometry is the database page's for the same reason: the C64's rows 10,
12..22 ARE condb's seven lines, and prntX 9 / prntY 12 is line 1 col 9.

The page comes up BEFORE the deck is drawn, as $12C7 is reached before
DoNewDeck: GameStartInfo sets infoActive first, which makes LoadDeck's
ReframeView a no-op, and the deck arrives when the screen is dismissed.

Two hazards recorded in docs/layer-11d-droid-screens.md. PAGEBANK is
LDA #bank and eats A, so the screen selector goes in X - passed in A it
arrived as 7 and redrew screen 6 every pass, forever. And fire cutting
the wait short is the original's own arm, not a bug; test through
DEBUG_RESTART's R, which reaches GameStartInfo without touching fire.

Main RAM paid for it: one paged door for both entry points, $FF in
infoAct for the still-up case, and the flatten done from bank 7 because
bufcore.asm makes SetCRTCStart reachable. The transfer pages and the
game-over page are wired but NOT yet verified.

events.title: Player speed: a ride is fast or slow, and neither judders
events.message:
Player speed: a ride is fast or slow, and neither judders

PlayerSpeed_t's 5 and 6 dithered against the camera's 4 px step exactly
as the 7 did - 4,4,8,4 and 8,4,8,4 - so riding a slow droid was jerkier
than riding a fast one. Both collapse onto CAM_SLOWSPD = 4, the only
dither-free value below CAM_TOPSPD. plySpdTab is now 0,4,4,0,8,0,0,0,8.

DSpeed_t 1 and 2 are indistinguishable under the player as a result, and
both are slower against the 001 than the C64 makes them. KC accepted
that: fast one or slow one is a fine model, and the judder is gone.
Enemy droids move in whole pixels, never dithered, and are untouched.

layer-10 DECISION 11.

Loader: the four banks ship ZX0-compressed, boot 14.4s -> 10.4s

The depacker becomes a macro instantiated twice: bank 4's Zx0Unpack as
before, and PARDEPK, an eighth disc file at &3000 that UnpackBankIn
(nee PageBankIn) JMPs to unpack each bank's stream from &3200 straight
into SWRAM. tools/make_disc.py post-processes beebasm's image: it
compresses the banks with bin/zx0.exe (reference sources in
tools/zx0src/, round-trip-verified through zx0.py every build) and lays
the disc out in boot access order - beebasm's SAVE order had !BOOT and
PARA physically last, a full-disc seek at boot. The raw beebasm image
is NO LONGER BOOTABLE; build.ps1 runs the whole chain.

Banks 16381/15351/16326/15558 -> 10466/2833/3720/8161 bytes; all four
byte-verified against the raw images after an in-emulator boot.

events.title: wonderboy/kit: batch 42 phase A — the spine opens; TRAP_MODEL Phase 8
events.message:
wonderboy/kit: batch 42 phase A — the spine opens; TRAP_MODEL Phase 8

Kit (TRAP_MODEL Phase 8 — scheduled pokes; all three games re-verified):
- emu.run(..., schedule=[{pc|nth, addr, width, value}]): oracle-side stores
  in shim.c, candidate-side sched.c with sched_poll8 AND the capped
  sched_wait8 (OS_SCHED_POLL_MAX, named out-of-band exhaustion) — the
  uncapped-poll hang class is now a 58 s CAUGHT, not a 151 s timeout.
  The pin is the ARRIVAL COUNT vs the candidate's polls, not the store
  (proven load-bearing by a composite mutant). 22 sched cases; kit 383.
- project.toml poked_input_program_data waivers: bounded (no overlaps,
  no span crossing >1 OS field), with a SERVED_OVER_MODEL_FIELDS ledger
  so a hand-staged console key cannot silently become a game-data seed.
- Schedule shape validation before the harness vet; ported_entries now
  reads the candidate's own defined symbols (libc resolution excluded,
  pinned); an inverted build-split comment fixed in FOUR kit files.

Reconstruction:
- THE SPINE INVENTORY, as a tripwire not a snapshot: recursive-descent
  walk from game_main_loop// — 86 routines, 77 verified, 604
  unported bytes; unmatched transfer forms asserted against a pinned
  census (12 opaque transfers, 4 absolute jmps — the tripwire's first
  run caught a bug in its own walk: an opaque call silently shortened
  $50a's extent 52→20 B).
- game_key_actions ($53e, six arms) + game_unpause_on_key_release
  ($638) — the batch-12 registered boundary, ported with scheduled
  pokes modeling the ACIA release. Declaring $604 as poked program
  data ALSO retired the cheat arm unpinned since batch 22 — and the
  gate made the retirement a MEASUREMENT (the named batch-41
  rearm-unconditional mutant run and CAUGHT).
- 305 fns / 40,372 B / 91.2%; wonderboy 5,984, joust 4,369,
  buggyboy 292, hw_portability 56 — all clean-build, serial.

Review gate (4 finders incl. a supplemental after the first diff
snapshot omitted the seven untracked new files — scope regenerated
with add -N): 19 findings applied. Sweeps: 42 distinct mutants over
46 runs, five clean rounds; R1 killed and DISCARDED whole (a killed
round proves nothing); one R5 survivor equivalent by the harness's
own refusal ordering, recorded not forced.

Deferred (queued): the 604 spine bytes (game_main_loop body, VBL,
flip_screen, $50a, $882, $e032/$e0a8, PSG pair); the flute arm
Phase 8 made reachable; pytest-timeout for hang-mutants; poked-input
block relocation; carried items unchanged. Next: finish the spine,

events.title: Layer 11e: the transfer time-up posts ONCE, and fades - $20DA exactly
events.message:
Layer 11e: the transfer time-up posts ONCE, and fades - $20DA exactly

KC nailed it from the sound alone: the C64 time-up fades out where
ours held. The listing agrees - xferDoCounter ($20DA) exits early when
the count is ALREADY zero ($20E0 BEQ), so the $1B post at $2104 fires
exactly once, on the tick the countdown reaches zero. One zipper
instance, 16 gated ticks, then a ~3 s release fade while it keeps
descending: went-on-for-a-long-time WITH the volume fade, precisely.

Stage 3 had restructured the routine with the post in the already-zero
arm - reposting every other pass at full volume: no fade, and the wrap
screaming. The previous commit's alarm substitution treated the
symptom; this restores the C64's own control flow, post included, and
reverts the alarm.

Also captured the transfer-entry pair against theory: both zips hit
the chip tick-for-tick on the C64 arithmetic (fx $1B 3676 down to 244
Hz, fx 9 3571 down to 197, detuned as designed), so the entry-pitch
question is timbre or memory, not data - awaiting KC's A/B against the

events.title: Layer 11e: the transfer time-up stops screaming
events.message:
Layer 11e: the transfer time-up stops screaming

KC found the game-completion sound a bit intense, and the diagnosis is
a genuine cadence deviation: the C64 re-posts fx $1B every 50 Hz
frame, restarting the zipper every tick and PINNING it to its
first-tick frequency - a steady ~240 Hz urgent drone. Our repost runs
at pass rate, every 4 ticks, which lets the zipper wrap mod 65536 and
puts a 3.6 kHz scream tick in every fragment.

A 50 Hz sequencer cannot be pinned from 25 Hz code, and fx $1B data is
untouchable (its full zipper is the transfer-entry siren, signed off),
so the time-up posts fx 8 - the alarm - which at this cadence plays as
a near-steady ~490 Hz warble: the C64 character, an octave up. Zero
bytes, bank 7. An exact-240 Hz custom record is the 11-byte
alternative, noted in the source.

events.title: Layer 11e: the sub-floor mute is the volume, not the period
events.message:
Layer 11e: the sub-floor mute is the volume, not the period

KC heard a click at the hum start on two accurate emulators. The wiki
sn76489 page explains it in its sample-playback section: every
attenuation setting shifts the chip output DC offset, and that offset
IS how PCM playback works on this chip - so writing N=1 (ultrasonic,
tonally silent) while the envelope stepped the volume was a one-sample
PCM pop. A mute on this chip must hold the VOLUME at 15.

SndConv now returns the mute in carry (set = sub-floor on a
MUTE_SUBFLOOR instrument; no period produced at all) and the flush
routes BCS into its existing silent-voice path - attenuation 15,
period untouched. Unmuting writes the period before the volume, so the
tone re-enters cleanly. Captured: the hum cycle is now sweep, one
atten=15 at the reset tick, period-then-atten=10 on the way back, and
the muted opening writes nothing whatever - no DC step exists to hear.
Bank 4: 1 byte free.

events.title: Layer 11e: the hum stays a tone; its sub-floor mutes to N=1 instead
events.message:
Layer 11e: the hum stays a tone; its sub-floor mutes to N=1 instead

KC reverted the periodic-noise hum - the tone version was right, only
the opening drone was wrong. The wiki sn76489 page supplied the proper
tool: period 1 is a 125 kHz square, out of audible range and stripped
by the LM324N, so a MUTE_SUBFLOOR instrument flag (bit 6) sends the
hum instrument sub-floor clamps to N=1 instead of the audible N=1023.
The hum now fades in as its sweep crosses the floor, with a one-tick
articulation gap at each segment reset - no drone. Effects that live
entirely below the floor (the disruptor) keep the 1023 buzz: the flag
would silence them outright. Never period 0 - undocumented on this
chip. The periodic-noise machinery stays in history (dd108a2) for
stage 4.

Planning the fix surfaced a real driver bug: SndConv counted its
shifts in X, and the flush picks the write channel from X after
converting, so every IN-RANGE voice-1 tone effect had been landing on
channel 0. The hum escaped only because its clamped path skips the
shift loops. Counters moved to snTm2; the capture now shows the hum
cycle (N 940 down to 569, one N=1 mute tick, repeat) entirely on
channel 1. Paid for by collapsing the SndTick init head to its one
surviving state value and merging the clamp/mute exit - bank 4 back
to 3 bytes free.

events.message:
Layer 11e stage 2: the SN76489 driver, alive in the IRQ

src/sound.asm (1,018 B, bank 4): a transliteration of the C64 Sound
($0500) game-FX path - request pickup with the disruptor priority bit,
the mod-65536 slide sequencer with bounce and reset segments, a linear
ADSR envelope stepped at 50 Hz, latest-wins noise ownership, and a
diffed chip flush over the stage-0 write primitive with DDRA/ORA saved
once per burst. IrqHandler pages bank 4 in around SndTick via ROMSHAD
and restores what it found - the one sanctioned breach of the bank
rule, recorded in CLAUDE.md. Requests are four main-RAM bytes so every
bank can trigger a sound with a plain STA.

The 629 bytes bank 4 was short came from three places, KC choosing the
first: chardata bitmaps now ship ZX0-packed (1,096 -> 640, unpacked
into the idle sprite save areas at deck load, an 8-byte lampSrc cache
serving the alert lamp live re-colours; charRemap leads the file so its
ALIGN is free), the never-used chain byte and the three deferred
chatter records are gone, and the frequency table halved to 64 midpoint
entries. Bank 4 ends &BFB2 - 78 free - and the build prints the gauge.

Verified in jsbeeb: title, first deck and a DEBUG_DECK hop all render
from the packed charset; effect $12 poked into sndFx1 plays the droid
explosion exactly as the data says (N 263 sweeping to 487, 8-tick gate,
4-per-tick release). One bug found by the first capture and fixed: the
sub-2048 clamp shortcut flattened noise voices; they now pre-scale x16
saturating. Tick costs measured over the shim: 475 idle, 1,161 active,

events.title: wonderboy: batch 41 phase F — 62/62, every dispatch row reconstructed
events.message:
wonderboy: batch 41 phase F — 62/62, every dispatch row reconstructed

THE MILESTONE: all 62 rows of the $938 dispatch table live in C.
302 fns / 40,062 B / 90.5% of believed code; suite 5,907; the $a38..$2461
band's unported bytes = 0 (526 + 1,170 + 62 + the $1f34 dead pair).

Reconstruction:
- $a38 actor_behavior_type01_player (62 B, 16 instructions): nine bsr's,
  the d7 gate, the $6ef0.l / $a32.w guards; exit codes propagate the
  callee's verbatim (0 = own rts). Dispatch-level case enters through
  actor_dispatch_behavior's jmp (a1) with a type-1 record — the flip
  proven end to end, incl. the dispatcher's own X: lsl.w #2 at $92e
  leaves bit 14 of the type, drivable via type aliasing ($0001/$4001/
  $8001/$c001 all reach slot 1).
- Exit codes renumbered into one collision-free space, pinned by a
  scraped no-collision test (a code added without its pin was CAUGHT by
  the sweep when the renumbering mutant survived).
- Ladder-fire proven reachable from bytes (the fall pass clears both
  gates branchless; $151a's byte-wide st/clr.b split them; climb gate
  tst.w $1514.l at $d84) — so the ladder arm's pass-through X matters,
  and it is the dispatcher's.
- UNPORTED_TYPE retired: boundary = slot 29 (shipped bare-rts row)
  poked to $d78 — the dispatcher genuinely follows the poked table;
  eight cases re-aimed; the designed tripwire became
  test_every_row_of_the_dispatch_table_is_reconstructed.
- THE REVIVAL/DEATH SOUND ARMS (gate find, widened by measurement):
  $a76 has two arms ending in sound calls whose exit X overwrites the
  dispatcher's bit — proven under the oracle (revival+ladder+fire
  diverges for type $0001 vs $4001). The port REFUSES out of band
  (WB_PLAYER_EXTEND_UNREAD / WB_PLAYER_FRAME_SOUND_EXTEND) rather than
  guessing; scoped — a revival on a jumping frame runs whole; the
  snd_trigger_effect exit-X derivation is priced in the queue.
- READ-AFTER-STORE 6th sighting, first introduced by a port (the
  $e42 store between $bbc2's tst and subq) — caught by the author's
  own byte re-read, re-read restored, chain mutants green.

Review gate (3 finders + fix pass, 10 confirmed): the revival-arm model
hole and a latent 2-arg ctypes binding of the 3-param frame were the
real two; $1514 census reconciled (the $ff00 clr.l is the writer that
takes both words down); 12-vs-16 instruction count fixed on four
surfaces; the mtime salvage argument RETRACTED (a dirty round proves
nothing either way — only round 3's clean 34/34 establishes coverage);
sweep headline made honest (two measured holes, two unsettled — the
deferred attribution re-run is a queued phase-F item); retraction
streak broken at five (whitespace-normalised scan, 0 violations).

Sweeps: 34/34 clean round + rounds 5-6 on the fixes (5 caught,
1 proven-equivalent death-arm ordering, pinned). hw_portability 56.

62/62 does NOT mean playable: the spine is unported, there are no
on-target backends, and BOOT/RESOURCE loading is untouched. Next arc:
spine → on-target backends → playable .PRG. Queued: snd_trigger_effect
exit-X derivation, the deferred survivor attribution, $e032, odd drift
cursor, hud_meter_charge, actor.c→bus.h, run_reaching/final_pc kit
promotion, TRAP_MODEL stop_pc note, $1ab4 unwind, out/* regeneration.

events.title: Pack the deck maps with ZX0, and retire the level RLE entirely
events.message:
Pack the deck maps with ZX0, and retire the level RLE entirely

Layer 13d, task 4, approved by KC. Rather than compressing the C64's
RLE streams, export_bbc.py now decodes each deck offline — BuildLevel's
exact old semantics, including decks 1 and 2 legitimately running past
their stream into the next deck's data — and ZX0-compresses the decoded
1,024-byte maps. That compresses better than RLE-then-LZ, needs no
scratch anywhere (Zx0Unpack writes straight into the tile map), and
deletes the RLE format from the port: BuildLevel is pointer setup plus
a tail call, and the console's deck plan walks the tile map in place —
main RAM, static after BuildLevel, readable from bank 7 — instead of
decoding a 512-byte staged copy, so ConDeckEnter4 keeps only its t1i3
work. The decoded maps are byte-identical to the C64's; only the
packaging changed.

tools/zx0.py is a line-for-line Python port of Einar Saukas' reference
compressor (BSD-3, github.com/einar-saukas/ZX0) in its default mode —
forwards, interlaced Elias gamma, inverted new-offset-MSB — with its
own decompressor, and every emitted stream round-trips at export time.
src/zx0depack.asm is the 6502 side, written from the reference
compressor's source rather than a recalled depacker.

leveldata's 3,503 bytes become deckPack's 2,183 plus ~230 of depacker:
bank 4 goes from 12 bytes free to 1,161 — the resting-state bank, where
every future gameplay byte has to live.

Verified in jsbeeb: all 16 decks unpacked through a BuildLevel
trampoline and diffed against the offline decode — 16 x 1,024 bytes,
zero mismatches — plus a normal boot playing on its decompressed deck.
The deck plan page still wants an in-game play-check.

Layer 13d, task 3, reversing layer-11's [DECISION 3] with KC: the
48 x 84 portrait IS ported, because the costing that deferred it was
wrong on both ends. Only the LEFT column of BuildIntroSprites' 2 x 4
sprite grid is stored (the right is MirrorSprite's at runtime, ours as
theirs), the 24 records share their images, and the unique pool is 63
sprites = 4,032 bytes of the C64's own data — not 6 K, and never 24 K,
because a multicolour pair is exactly two MODE 1 pixels and PoDraw
expands at draw time the way FontCell expands the font.

tools/export_portraits.py emits the pool, the per-type index and the
multicolour->MODE 1 tables into bank 7; portrait.asm composes them —
rptLen stacking, upper-sprite-wins overlap (bottom-up through
SPR_MASKTAB transparency), pair-reversed multicolour mirrors,
bit-reversed hires mirrors — into DbImage's own rectangle, which is
the C64's sprite X=40/Y=144 translated: buffer rows 2-12, units 4-15.
The rotor-and-digits stand-in and droidicon7.asm are deleted; DbImage
is now a guard (repaint only when the type or a clear demands it) in
front of PoDraw.

paths — 0 of 1,008 bytes differing each. The page itself still wants

Give the title back to the disc, and let a game over reach it

Layer 13d, task 1. The title screen leaves bank 7 and becomes the
PARTITL disc overlay again — [DECISION 6] of layer-11 restored —
assembled at &3000 over PARAFNT's ground and loaded by TitleSeq, which
boot and the new game-over seam now share: load the title, show it,
reload PARAFNT and PARALOW over it, rebuild everything the title's
framebuffer sat on, raise the rupture, take the IRQ back.

GoTick7 ends a game with GoTitle instead of JMP GameStart:
UninstallIrq, SetupMode, RestoreDfsWs, TitleSeq, GameStart. Two things
made that survivable, both measured in jsbeeb rather than recalled:

- InstallIrq now saves the MOS's System VIA IER, ACR and T1 latches
  before clobbering them, and UninstallIrq hands them back — the
  rupture rewrites the latches every field and the MOS's 100 Hz events
  (keyboard scan, clock, disc timeouts) run off what it left there.

- The low overlay buries DFS's workspace at &0E00-&10FF AND the MOS's
  extended vector table at &0D9F (under lowcode2) — the route DFS 1.2's
  FILEV takes into its ROM — so any filing call after PageLowIn jumps
  through game code and dies; *DISC does not recover it. SaveDfsWs
  snapshots both spans (912 B) into bank 6 right before PageLowIn, and
  GoTitle restores them byte for byte before its loads.

The snapshot lives in bank 6, NOT bank 5 as the session plan first
said: the approved "sideview to bank 5" move turned out unbuildable
(sideview.asm is the lift screen's data, read by bank-7 code through
xfer.asm's shared machinery), so the same bank-7 bytes were freed by
rehoming the snapshot instead, leaving bank 5 whole for the flicker.

Verified in jsbeeb over two consecutive game overs: boot -> title ->
game -> death as a 001 -> wash -> title -> fire -> new game.

events.title: amiga/ecs: never paint a screen the palette cannot show (the boot's garbage frames)
events.message:
amiga/ecs: never paint a screen the palette cannot show (the boot's garbage frames)

The user watched the ECS boot on a real desktop: the title sequence rendered as
black with one garbled strip for over a minute. Traced (FRUA_ECSTRACE, new): the
title sequence draws each screen's art and PRESENTS before installing its
palette, so the incremental present converts the new art through the PREVIOUS
screen's bands -- wrong-palette garbage, held on screen for the full length of
the following re-band, twice per title screen.

The backend already detects exactly this condition -- e_new_ink >= 4 schedules a
re-quant -- but only after painting the garbage. Now the incremental branch
pre-scans the announced rows first, and at >= 8 pixels of ink the current bands
cannot show it HOLDS: keeps the announcements pending, shows the last complete
frame, and lets the palette install that follows take the full-render path with
the real palette. The garbage is never painted.

  ! RENDERING IMMEDIATELY IS ALSO WRONG, and it was tried first: re-band and
    render in this present, so nothing depends on a follow-up present ever
    coming. Measured on the boot: the re-quant runs against the CLUT AS IT
    STANDS, which is exactly what is stale -- it painted the whole SSI screen in
    well-quantised garbage and added a 9.5 s re-band per title. No quantiser can
    fix indices whose CLUT entries have not arrived.

  ! ONE HOLD, NEVER TWO. The legitimate new-ink case -- art whose CLUT entries
    are fine but missed the last quant (an event portrait) -- must still paint.
    A second consecutive present with no palette change paints via the bucket
    fallback exactly as before, one modal-loop pass later. A full render also
    clears the hold, so nothing can stick.

A/B on ONE binary (video.cfg inkhold=off; the Amiga side never had a video.cfg
reader, so this adds the ST/Nova contract to ecs_init):
    on:  40 frames -- black, SSI correct, MICRO MAGIC silver (bucket fallback,
         by design), gold on its install. No garbage frame.
    off: config line confirmed, zero holds -- SSI in blue/black wrong-palette
         garbage for ~20 s, a red-striped second flavour after the next draw.
         The user's symptom, reproduced on demand.

Also: FRUA_ECSTRACE (present/flip/render tracing behind FRUA_AMIGAPROF, with an
#error guard for the missing dependency), and the profiler dump now fires on
FULL presents too. Note for anyone reading the traces: the rl clock starts when
the VBL server installs, LATE in the AmigaOS boot, so rl timestamps sit ~60-90 s
behind capture wall time.

All five configs build; 471 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: quantize: the nearest-remap's multiplies cost the ECS boot 35 seconds — b7d628ba was priced on one backend
events.message:
quantize: the nearest-remap's multiplies cost the ECS boot 35 seconds — b7d628ba was priced on one backend

The user booted the ECS build on a real desktop and saw the title sequence as a
single bar with a smear for over a minute. Frame-by-frame capture confirmed it:
~70 seconds of one strip of the SSI screen on black, then everything at once.

Attribution (new apecs timers): 8 full presents in the boot at ~12.2 s each,
86% of it ecs_reband -- 16.8 s per re-band, five of them. Three theories fell
before the right one: unannounced dirty rows (the DIRTYCHECK police reads 0),
per-row conversion cost (that number divided whole-screen render time by an
incremental row counter), and then the real thing:

b7d628ba put the nearest-colour remap into quantize.h scoring candidates with
2L*dr*dr + 5L*dg*dg + 1L*db*db -- three 32-bit multiplies, which a plain 68000
turns into ~200-cycle __mulsi3 calls. The header is SHARED, and it was priced
on the ST, where #139 had already collapsed 25 band cuts to 1-3 group cuts:
+2.9%, measured, honest -- for the ST. The Amiga ECS still cuts all 25 BANDS,
so the same change cost it twenty-five-fold. The build sweep compiled the Amiga
targets all along; compiling is not pricing.

The same expression sits in TWO loops: the present-colour remap and the
absent-colour 4x8x4 bucket table (128 buckets x ntot per band -- the bigger
one; fixing the remap alone bought 5%). A 512-byte square table makes both
shifts and adds. The VALUE is identical, so palettes, remaps and every rendered
frame are bit-for-bit unchanged -- verified on 11 captured title/menu frames
(qband output identical before and after).

Measured on the ECS boot, same drive: re-band 16.8 s -> 9.5 s (-44%), full
presents 97.9 s -> 62.4 s (-36%).

Also in this commit:
 - QUANT_PROF: opt-in phase timers in quant_banded (zero-cost when off).
   Host attribution (qprof, sum-check 97%): buckets 40.8%, cut 29.8%,
   remap 12.8%, keep 9.4%, hist 4.2%. No single free win remains; the rest
   of the 9.5 s is inherent per-band work, and reducing it is the measured
   group-count trade-off (qband: N=5 keeps 65-87% of per-band fidelity at
   1/5 the cuts, but 4 of 11 title screens genuinely need per-band cuts).
 - apecs timers for reband/remap/c2p, the quant phase dump, and the dump now
   fires on FULL presents too -- it hung off the rect path alone, and a boot
   issues no rect presents, so three successive runs printed nothing while
   the counters incremented.
 - tools/quant/qband (per-band vs one-cut error + band divergence) and
   qprof (host phase attribution with the sum check).

★ Traps paid for here, recorded in the comments: a timer bracket must close on
exactly the paths its open ran on (two bugs: a close outside its open's branch
added the absolute clock per skipped band; a close 90 lines BEFORE its open);
and validate the instrument where iteration is cheap -- two emulator runs at
five minutes each went to bracket bugs the host reproduces in one second.

docs: the ECS row of the #148 audit is code-derived — six live attempts never reached the walk

Recording this as unverified rather than letting the code argument pass as an
observation. Six attempts to drive the ECS build to a dungeon walk in amiberry all
failed before reaching it, and every failure was the harness, not the build -- ECS
booted and rendered correctly every time.

The faults are the useful part:
  - DBG.LOG on the emulated DH0 mount LAGS (AmigaOS buffers the write), so polling it
    from the host for "menu: modal up" reports "not yet" long after the menu is up.
    Hatari's GEMDOS mount does not, which is why the same pattern is fine on the ST.
  - the ECS boot is far longer than the ~105 s in the old notes, because #135 put the
    jt919 title sequence in front of the menu; a 230 s fixed wait still landed on the
    SSI logo and the keys drove the title.
  - the hall's character list drains keys while it builds, so ST-sized 5 s settles
    park the drive on ADD A CHARACTER with the party half-seated.
  - amiberry drops keystrokes: attempt 5 reached the hall, attempt 6 with the same
    script lost the Escape and four `b` retries went nowhere.
  - ★ CALIBRATE A FRAME DETECTOR AGAINST A REAL FRAME. Two of the six failures were
    the detector: the menu test looked for 90<g<140 olive when the menu's olive is
    (85,85,68), and the walk test wanted top-2 colours under 60% when a known-good ST
    walk frame measures 60.4% -- it would have rejected a real dungeon frame.

What the ECS row rests on instead: grep -l planar_viewport_register returns only
display_ste.c, and the Amiga build does not link display_ste.o at all. No separate

events.title: docs: audit the other backends for #61's hazard — the ST was the only one exposed
events.message:
docs: audit the other backends for #61's hazard — the ST was the only one exposed

The shape is not "does it have a viewport" but "is anything written to the display
whose content is NOT in the shared chunky surface", because then any copy from the
draw-time plane buffer erases it.

Checked all six. The TT's t_dt and its c2p both derive from g_chunky; ECS and AGA
draw a SOFTWARE cursor that the shim composites into the chunky surface (#64 retired
AGA's sprite cursor, so plat_cursor_active() returns 0 there too); the Falcon is
chunky-native; ST-High and Nova register no draw-time target at all. Only the ST
renders anything into a separate buffer, and dsp_viewport_scratch is registered by
exactly one backend.

That is structural, not luck: ADR-0016's writers stamp planes AND record the chunky
index, so s_chunky stays the source of truth and the plane buffer is a cache that can
always be rebuilt from it. The ST viewport is the sole exception.

Also records that the ST's own coverage is complete -- both incremental arms (BLiTTER
and CPU memcpy) share the hook because it sits before the s_use_blt branch, and the
force-full was already covered by #61 -- and the one piece of deliberate slack:
st_vp_touched tests rows only, so a rect present entirely right of the viewport
re-arms a repaint it does not need. That is 5-7 composites per ~1500 presents, i.e.
optimising 0.09%, and the s_dt paths rebuild whole rows where a column test would
always be true anyway.

events.title: platform: repaint the viewport after a copy that crossed its rows (ST/STE, #148)
events.message:
platform: repaint the viewport after a copy that crossed its rows (ST/STE, #148)

The ST/STE lost the BOTTOM NINE ROWS of the first-person view -- game rows
103..111 came out fully black, the floor's nearest band simply missing -- while
the Falcon rendered the identical frame, same cell and same in-game minute,
complete. It shipped, and it was in every affected walk frame.

The viewport deliberately does not live in s_chunky (ADR-0016 B2): that is what
keeps the roster and chrome on its scanlines static so the row-diff can skip
them. So s_chunky's viewport hole is BLACK -- measured, 0 of 88 columns non-zero
against 88 of 88 in the scratch -- and s_dt, built from s_chunky, carries the
hole too. st_dt_present_full then copies runs of rows from s_dt into the pages,
erasing the viewport's share of every row it touches. A row is only rebuilt when
it CHANGES, which is why the damage is a band and not the whole pane: rows
24..102 are static chrome beside a constant hole, while the compass and the
coordinate/clock box sit at rows ~103..125 and the clock ticks. It stops at 111
because rows 112+ have no viewport to erase.

★ #61 ALREADY FOUND THIS AND FIXED HALF OF IT. Its comment sits in the
force-full branch of the same function -- "this just rewrote BOTH pages from
s_dt, which does not carry the composited viewport (the composite writes the
PAGE, not s_dt). Both pages owe it again." The incremental run copy, which is
the walk's common path, never got the same treatment. This is that treatment.

st_vp_touched() re-arms s_vp_owe when a written span crosses the viewport's
rows, so the st_vp_composite() that already follows every present repaints
instead of returning early. s_vp_have, not s_vp_active: the scratch and the
stamped planes both persist after the commit is consumed, which is what makes
the repaint possible.

★ THE HOOK GOES ON THE COPY, NOT THE BUILD. Hooking st_dt_build_row was tried
first and left one of three drives still showing the band: s_dt PERSISTS with
the hole in it, so a row built once can be re-copied on any later present with
no build to notice. The copy is the event that damages the page.

★ AND AN EARLIER ATTEMPT HOOKED st_blit_rows ALONE AND MEASURED NO EFFECT,
which read as a refutation and was not: CPU68K=68000 implies FRUA_PLANAR, so the
ST's full present goes through st_dt_present_full and never calls st_blit_rows.
The hook was on a path the walk does not take. Both writers are covered now.

ST/STE ONLY: display_ste.c is the sole backend that calls
planar_viewport_register, so every other target (Falcon, TT, Amiga AGA/ECS,
Nova) renders the view straight into the shared surface and has no separate
buffer for a copy to erase. No Amiga counterpart is needed.

A/B on ONE binary, video.cfg `vprepair=off` restoring the shipped behaviour,
three drives per arm at staggered key counts:
    off: run1 clean, run2 BAND x3, run3 clean
    on:  run1 clean, run2 clean x3, run3 clean
Run 2 is the discriminating configuration -- it has reproduced three times --
and runs 1/3 reproduce in neither arm, so a single clean sweep would have proved
nothing. Config confirmed applied on every run.

Cost: 5-7 extra composites over ~1500 presents, vpcomp +43 t200 = ~0.09% of
in-present.
  ! in-present itself read +7.3% and +2.7% across two repeat pairs while the
    BAND BRANCH -- a control the fix cannot touch -- swung +2.2% then -1.1%. Five
    extra composites cannot cost 5%, so the headline delta is drift at this noise
    level. Quote the attributable 0.09%, not the total.

All five configs build; 471 passed, 6 skipped.

events.title: docs: #148 — nine black rows in the ST's 3D view, and the twelve instruments that missed it
events.message:
docs: #148 — nine black rows in the ST's 3D view, and the twelve instruments that missed it

Found by the user in a screenshot taken during the #139 A/B. Game rows 103..111 of
the viewport are fully black on the ST/STE; the Falcon renders the identical frame
-- same cell, same in-game minute, checked at a legible crop -- complete. It ships,
and it is in every affected walk frame.

The cause is still OPEN. This section is mostly about instrument design, because
that is where the cost was: twelve experiments, each individually reasonable, most
of them measuring something other than what I thought.

Eliminated, each by a live A/B: the draw-time viewport writer (vpplanar=off
reproduces), the whole ADR-0016 writer half (PLANAR=0 reproduces), the raster split
(vpbands=off reproduces -- and that arm has ONE palette frame-wide), the engine's
pane placement (Falcon shares it and is clean), the engine's render into the scratch
(poisoning the buffer shows 0 unwritten rows of 88), the composite (a self-triggering
scan on both present hooks never sees a blank row), and a blit clobbering viewport
rows (re-arming s_vp_owe in st_blit_rows changes nothing).

Six stages measure healthy and the output is still wrong, so one of them answers a
question nobody asked. Two live leads are recorded: the composite's own stamp does
not survive to the screen (slot 15 forced across the whole rect in every page leaves
no trace), and the ST/Falcon fork at dsp_viewport_scratch() -- NULL on the Falcon, so
the engine renders straight into the chunky surface, while planar_viewport_register()
runs unconditionally in st_init so NEITHER vpplanar=off NOR PLANAR=0 crosses it.
Every elimination above stayed on the same side of that fork.

The traps are the point, and all were paid for:
  - st_present is the FULL present; the walk presents by RECT.
  - st_present_rect's B2.2 fast path returns early for a rect inside the viewport --
    the walk's own present -- so a hook at that function's tail is DEAD CODE there.
    Measured: 0 calls.
  - st_vp_composite fires ~once per walk STEP, not per present; a probe gated on
    composite #400 never fires.
  - "are the planes zero" is the WRONG QUESTION -- they always hold real non-zero
    slots on the black rows. Five probes tested it and all reported healthy.
  - the defect is VIEW-dependent (cell 12,5), so a fixed-count trigger samples
    whichever frame is up; self-trigger, and require a PARTIAL band or a one-shot
    latches on the legitimate before-the-first-composite state.
  - a QDUMP capture cannot tell a drawn row from a stale one.
  - silence and a reading of zero are identical in DBG.LOG -- print the call count.
  - verify the screenshot geometry: the image is at (96,58), not (0,0).

server, structurally identical to dap.py's: it pushes the live display as

in kind from DAP/MCP and with no VS-Code-specific code in it. Frames are
read via engine.machine.render_screen() directly rather than through the
engine's command queue -- a run() in progress occupies the actor loop for
its entire duration, so a queued read sat unserved (and the live view
visibly froze) until it stopped; this bypass is the same pattern dap.py's
_read_memory_sync already uses for exactly this reason.

vscode-extension/ moves the project's debugger-type registration in-repo
and adds real code for the first time: extension.js bridges the raw
stream into a webview panel (a webview can't open a raw socket itself),
auto-opens on debug session start, and auto-reconnects if the server
restarts.

core/snapshot.py gains write_sna(), the field-for-field inverse of the
existing parse_sna(), needed to package scripts/build_manicminer.py's
output (SkoolKit's Manic Miner disassembly, assembled with sjasmplus) into
a loadable .sna. Verified live end to end, including sending real
keypresses over MCP to get from the title screen into gameplay. Given the
same copyright treatment as the ROM: game_disassembly/ and
.manicminer-disassembly-src/ are gitignored, only the build script is
committed.

events.title: Give the drawing its window back, and let the split survive scrolling
events.message:
Give the drawing its window back, and let the split survive scrolling

KC reported the flicker back, worst on the enemy droids, and suspected
the collision work and the animated tiles had eaten the budget. Both
halves were right. Measured with a zero-byte harness -- breakpoints on
the JSR sites plus elapsed_cycles -- because DEBUG_TIME did not build.

On the LIGHTEST pass the game can have (one sprite, no level draw) the
sprite draw already finished 1,572 cycles past the 24,576-cycle window,
and 16,888 of that window went on work that writes no pixels. AnimTick
alone was 10,060 and found nothing. Every further sprite is +5,182, and
enemy droids are drawn after the player, so they are the ones still
missing when the beam arrives.

PHASE 1 -- empty the window of work that draws nothing.
AnimScan and AnimLamp move below the draw and fill the list for the NEXT
pass; AnimTick keeps only the charset rotation, 10,060 -> 1,558. Same
one-pass pipeline the droid AI took. DoScore and CbDisruptor move to
ml_afterdraw, immediately above ml_passend -- the one point every arm of
the pass converges on -- so they still run with a modal state up, which
is what put them at the top of the pass in the first place.

PHASE 2 -- the split is what prevents flicker, and it was refused on
every pass the player moves. The global vetoes are replaced by a local
test: each writer is one-dimensional (a band is full width, a column
full height, a door and an animated tile are single tiles), so any
overlap component holding a sprite under one of them is FORCED into
tranche A, the tranche already erased while the level draw runs. Spans
are padded by eight, a pass's scroll, because a tranche-B sprite's saved
background was taken last pass. DoRedraws is no longer skipped on a
split pass -- it had to be unskipped, or the deck stops scrolling.

The decision outgrew the eleven bytes the code image had left, so it is
src/sprsplit.asm in BANK 6 behind a bridge on PanelTick's pattern. Every
byte it reads is outside bank 4. The code image goes 11 free -> 323, and
DEBUG_RASTER, DEBUG_DRAW and DEBUG_TIME assemble again; RASTER has been
run and draws its bands correctly.

Measured scrolling diagonally with a 302 on screen: tranche A finishes
2,959 cycles inside the window and sprTr puts the player in A and the
droid in B. Buffer oracle against RedrawAll: 0 of 10,240.

Two instrument fixes came out of it. DEBUG_DECK puts the cursor deck hop
behind a flag. And DEBUG_DRAW's magenta band had no close after the draw
-- it ran on through the droid AI, the panel and the WaitWindowB idle,
reporting 20,000 cycles of display work as sprite work and reaching into
the play area on every pass. It broke when Step 1 moved DroidsUpdate
below the draw. Magenta now ends at the draw and the display-period work
has a red band of its own.
