events.title: identify the terrain nibbles
events.message:
identify the terrain nibbles

Cell addressing is now confirmed outright from the primitives at $0FAE,
$0FEA and $0FD3:

  cell(col,row) = $5700 + row*128 + (col>>1)
  even col -> high nibble, odd col -> low nibble, masks at $0FD1 = F0,0F

so the map really is 256x400 tiles with 16 possible values per tile, which
independently confirms the nibble decoding.

Terrain meanings come from three lines of evidence agreeing: diffing the map
buffer across generation phases, the spatial signature of each value, and the
16 JSR $0FD3 write sites. Duane then supplied an independent community dump of
the historical map, which matches this decode on every continent, island
chain, river course and mountain range.

  0     ocean
  1     shelf / shallows, rings every coast
  2     sparse coastal fringe
  3,4   rare special sites, 14 and 19 cells, unidentified
  5-A   rivers
  B     plain / grassland
  C     forest — eastern North America and the Amazon
  D     mountain — the Rockies/Andes spine
  E     tropical class, Mexico and northern South America; jungle?
  F     native village

Corrects an earlier reading: F is not a scratch marker. $2D23 does use $0F as
a temporary fill, but it unfills it on the second call, so surviving F cells
are villages — matching the reference dump's red squares and the village phase
writing $BF/$FB/$FC/$CF.

Six distinct values for rivers suggests flow direction is encoded per tile,
which fits the manual's emphasis on rivers as the main route inland.

events.title: add a full-run mode so generated worlds get terrain
events.message:
add a full-run mode so generated worlds get terrain

A checkpointed trace captures the disk before the terrain pass is written
back — the pipeline runs twice and only writes after each complete pass — so
generated worlds came out as land and ocean with no rivers, mountains or
shelf. wm_trace.py --full runs the whole pipeline with no checkpoints and
waits for the completion screen instead.

Completion is detected by polling $D021 for green, which the World Maker sets
along with printing "THE NEW WORLD AWAITS!" at $0DFF. Note the VIC returns 1s
in the unused upper nibble of the color registers, so green reads back as $F5
rather than $05; the check masks to the low nibble. Comparing the raw byte
silently never matches, and the run appears to hang when it has in fact
already finished.

A generated world now renders with the same detail as the historical map:
river networks draining to the coast, mountain ranges, lakes, island chains
and the continental shelf.

events.title: decode tiles as nibbles: the map is 256 wide
events.message:
decode tiles as nibbles: the map is 256 wide

Each byte holds two horizontally adjacent tiles, high nibble first. That is
why $0EE4 multiplies the low nibble by 2, and why the byte values pair up as
they do: $BB is two land tiles, $00 two ocean, and $B0 / $0B are land+ocean,
a coastline nibble-swapped for which side the water is on.

The finished map is 256x400 tiles, not 128x400. Rendering bytes as single
tiles still produced a recognizable map, because a 2:1 horizontal squash of
the Americas still looks like the Americas — which is exactly why this went
unnoticed through several passes.

Terrain semantics now come from evidence rather than guesswork. Dumping the
map buffer at $5700 at each phase boundary and diffing gives:

  land-mass phase  writes 0 and B        -> ocean, land, and B0/0B coastline
  terrain phase    writes 1, C, D        -> shelf plus terrain classes
  village phase    writes F paired with  -> sites, F reading as a marker

$11 is the terrain phase's most common write, 1580 of 3439 changed bytes, and
nibble 1 renders as the continental shelf ringing every landmass, which fits.
Nibbles C, D and E are terrain classes whose exact meaning is still inferred;
reading $2AE9, $2D23, $2E32, $3961 and $3EAD would settle them.

Palette coverage is now 100% of tiles on both disks — no unexplained values
remain. The historical map renders with the Great Lakes, Florida, the Gulf of
Mexico, the Antilles chain, the Andes down the Pacific coast, the Amazon basin
river network and the continental shelf.

events.title: correct the map's horizontal offset
events.message:
correct the map's horizontal offset

The map rendered one block too far right: the eastern edge of South America
wrapped around to the left edge of the image. The sector stream starts one
block before the map's true left edge, so the fix is to roll left by 1 block
(16 tiles).

Picked objectively rather than by eye, since eyeballing is what produced the
previous two wrong answers. Scoring each of the eight block-aligned offsets by
how much land the wrap seam cuts through gives an unambiguous winner: at a
1-block roll the seam cuts zero land tiles and column 0 is entirely ocean,
while every other offset slices a continent in half.

The historical map now renders whole and correct — North America with the
Great Lakes, Florida, the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean chain, Central
America, and South America with the Amazon basin, the Andes and the Brazilian
bulge intact.

events.title: fix the map de-blocking: 8 blocks per row, split columns
events.message:
fix the map de-blocking: 8 blocks per row, split columns

The previous commit rendered a recognisable but wrong map. Duane spotted two
artifacts that pinned down exactly what was broken: the continents appeared
twice side by side, and the top half was garbage.

Three corrections, all derived from the code rather than guessed.

Blocks tile 8 per row, not 16. The source row stride is $80 = 128 tiles and a
block is 16 wide, so a memory row spans 128/16 = 8 blocks. At 16 per row two
consecutive map rows land side by side, which is exactly the doubled
continents.

A sector is not row-major inside its block. Tracing X through the loop at
$0F54, each outer pass writes 8 tiles to $0200+8i and 8 more to $0278+8i+8,
which is $0280+8i. So bytes $00-$7F hold the left 8 columns of all 16 rows and
$80-$FF hold the right 8 columns. Reading row-major scrambled the columns
inside every block — the source of the residual corruption.

Cropping must take the longest contiguous run of terrain rows. The historical
disk carries a non-terrain region above the map, and spanning min..max of
map-like rows swallowed it. That was the garbage top half.

The map proper is 128x400 tiles at block-rows 24-48. 7CITIES2.D64 and an
independently generated world now crop to identical geometry, which is a much
better check than eyeballing a coastline.

The historical map now renders cleanly: Great Lakes, Florida, Gulf of Mexico,
the Caribbean chain, Central America, and South America with the Amazon basin
river network. The magenta filaments are rivers, from the RUNNING RIVERS,
TRIBUTARIES phase. Palette coverage is 96.5% for the historical map and 100%
for the generated one.

events.title: decode the map layout: sectors are 16x16 blocks
events.message:
decode the map layout: sectors are 16x16 blocks

The map is stored blocked, not row-major. That is the whole answer to the
problem that has been blocking map decoding since the start.

The World Maker's sector-write loop at $0F54 gathers 16 bytes from each of
16 source rows spaced $80 apart:

  $0F82  STY $29 / STA $2A       ; source pointer
         LDA #$10 / STA $27      ; 16 iterations
  $0F56  LDA ($29),Y / STA $0200,X
  $0F63  LDA ($29),Y / STA $0278,X
  $0F90  LDA $29 / ADC #$80      ; source advances 128 per iteration

So every 256-byte sector is a 16x16 tile block and the in-memory row stride
is 128. Blocks tile left to right, 16 per row, for a 256-tile-wide map.

This explains both earlier failures. Row-major rendering smeared land into
long horizontal streaks because it was reading across block boundaries, and
no stride search ever found a peak because there is no single row stride to
find. Two separate statistical attacks died on this; reading the code that
writes the format solved it on the first attempt. NOTES.md records the
lesson: instrument the producer, do not infer from the product.

tools/map_preview.py renders any map disk to PNG. The historical map from
7CITIES2.D64 now renders as a recognisable Americas — North, Central and
South America, with the Old World down the right edge. The coastline test
set out at the beginning of this work passes.

Terrain semantics are only partly known. $00 is ocean and $BB is land, both
confirmed by diffing a disk either side of the land-mass phase. The rest
group by high nibble ($Bx, $Cx, $Dx, $Ex), which reads as a terrain class
with the low nibble as a variant; the preview colors them as an elevation
ramp, which looks plausible but is inference and is labelled as such. A band
of unmapped values across the upper historical map still renders magenta.

7898113a removed l2d3e's `iy >= 8000` hit-test gate to make the modify-char
stat rows clickable. But the REAL fix landed separately (c3332ed5): those rows
are installed as shape-5 cells at 8000-space y (8036..8056), so they pass the
gate anyway. The removal was therefore redundant — and it changed click
hit-testing on EVERY screen, which is the leading suspect for the reported
post-create "Exit from Play" freeze (create a character -> through the MODIFY
screen -> back to the Hall -> Exit from Play hangs).

Restoring the gate returns the known-good pre-2026-08-10 behaviour on every
screen while keeping the modify stat-click intact — verified live: clicking DEX
then INT still maps to act 3 / act 1 and the DEX selection persists (cur stat 3
on the second click). The two are independent.

only on hardware; the headless harness cannot commit Exit-from-Play at ANY
commit (it shows the same stuck-highlight state on 12ad1063, before all recent
work), so I could not bisect or confirm the cause here. Restoring the gate is
justified on its own merits (it was redundant and non-faithful), and it is the
change most likely to have caused a regression on the click path; hardware
verification is needed. The faithful no-gate form is worth revisiting once the
offending absolute-coord item/method can actually be reproduced.

events.title: run the World Maker headlessly
events.message:
run the World Maker headlessly

Driving the game's menus through the emulator proved slow and unreliable, so
this stops doing that. tools/wm_trace.py pokes game3 into a bare C64 under
vice-mcp, patches out its keyboard wait, and calls its real entry point with
SYS. It formats the attached disk and generates a complete world with no
menu navigation, no joystick, and no disk swapping.

The wait is at $1F7C and polls the keyboard matrix directly ($DC00 row 0,
bit 3 = F7), which is why KERNAL-level input never reached it. Patching the
BNE at $1F8A to NOP NOP falls straight through.

What running it revealed:

  - The pipeline $0E20 is called twice, from $0DB5 and $0DC3, each followed
    by a disk write. The world is generated in two passes.
  - The map is assembled on disk, not in RAM. 104 KB does not fit in 64 KB.
    RAM changes by only ~141 bytes across a whole phase boundary, which is
    what makes generation take 18 minutes — it streams sectors throughout.
  - Because writes only happen after a complete pipeline pass, snapshotting
    either RAM or the disk between phases shows nothing. That approach is a
    dead end and is recorded as such.
  - The land-mass phase writes mostly $00 and $BB. Rendering a generated map
    with $00 as ocean and $BB as land finally produces a recognisably
    map-like image, but land comes out as long thin horizontal streaks, so
    the row stride is still wrong.

A binarized stride sweep over land cells found no peak at any width from 64
to 6000, only monotonic decay. That is the second failed statistical attack
on the map layout; NOTES.md now says not to attempt a third. The next
instrument is a checkpoint on the sector-write routine $0F47, logging
(track, sector, payload) in write order, which gives the layout as ground
truth instead of inference.

Also fixes a race in the snapshot harness: after vice_execution_run the
emulator still reports "paused" briefly, so polling immediately returned at
once and silently produced several identical snapshots taken at the same
instant. It now confirms the machine resumed before waiting for a halt.

events.title: port the multiply and divide helpers
events.message:
port the multiply and divide helpers

The 6502 has no multiply or divide, so the World Maker carries its own.
Both sit under the whole generator, so they need to be right before any
generation phase can be ported.

  $0A51  8x8 to 16-bit multiply, shift-and-add. A x Y, low in A, high in Y.
  $0A6E  16-by-8 restoring divide. (Y:A) / X, quotient in A, remainder in Y.

Arithmetic.swift transcribes both literally, including a wart worth
spelling out: the divide's inner ROL A discards its carry out, so once the
dividend's high byte grows the quotient overflows and the result is simply
wrong. The captured reference proves it — (3:x) / 200 returns a quotient of
0 where real arithmetic gives 3. game3 stays clear of the case by keeping
high bytes small. The Swift port reproduces the wrong answer on purpose;
"fixing" it would silently diverge from the original wherever generation
code depends on the exact result.

tools/arith_reference.py follows the pattern set by rng_reference.py:
poke the original routines into a bare C64 under vice-mcp, drive them with
a loop written into memory, read the results back. Eight multiply sweeps
and seven divide sweeps, 256 cases each, so the tests compare roughly 3840
results against the original. The drivers now signal completion by writing
a sentinel rather than waiting for a non-zero buffer, since a sweep whose
output is legitimately all zeros (multiplier 0) is otherwise
indistinguishable from a driver that never ran.

Also corrects a mistake in NOTES.md. $0F0C was recorded as the land-mass
phase and $1F95 as its printer; both came from a nearest-preceding-JSR
heuristic rather than from reading the code, and both are wrong. $0F0C is
a disk buffer routine. The land-mass generator actually begins at $212A,
where a random byte is divided by 90 and multiplied by 7 to index a table
at $2286 holding three 7-byte records terminated by $FE. The records look
like signed direction vectors, which would fit the plate tectonics model
the manual describes, but that is not yet confirmed.

events.title: port and verify the World Maker RNG
events.message:
port and verify the World Maker RNG

First piece of the Seven Cities of Gold port, and the first one proven
faithful rather than assumed.

The World Maker's random number generator is a 16-bit LFSR at $0AE2 in
game3, with state in zero page $CD (high) and $CF (low). It shifts eight
times per call and returns the low byte. WorldMakerRNG.swift transcribes
it literally instead of simplifying it: ROL on the 6502 is a nine-bit
rotate through carry and the feedback taps are read after four of them,
which is easy to get subtly wrong by reasoning about it algebraically.

The seed is 16 bits, read from the SID oscillator ($D41B) twice at $20CB
during startup, so there are 65,536 distinct worlds. The original also
stirred $CD with a live $D41B read from its raster IRQ handler at $23FC
on every interrupt, which meant no particular world was ever reproducible
even on real hardware. That stirring is deliberately not reproduced, so a
given seed always yields the same world. Nothing is lost: the capability
never existed.

Verification is the point of this commit. tools/rng_reference.py pokes
the original routine into a bare C64 running under vice-mcp, transfers
control with SYS, and captures real 6502 output across five seeds into a
JSON fixture. The Swift tests assert an exact match on both output and
internal register state at every step. The fixture is committed because
the test is worthless without it; 320 bytes of PRNG output is a test
vector, not game content, and no original code, art, text or map data is
included here or ever will be.

The harness was confirmed non-vacuous by mutation: changing the four ROL
rotates to three produces 949 recorded failures.

Also included is the reverse engineering groundwork this rests on: a D64
reader, a recursive-descent 6502 disassembler that separates code from
data by reachability (da65 misaligns badly on these binaries), a JSON-RPC
client for vice-mcp, and NOTES.md recording everything established so far
including several dead ends and the harness gotchas that cost real time.

events.title: Port CRT shader to Emscripten via raw GLES2, fix F4 double-toggle and OSD alpha
events.message:
Port CRT shader to Emscripten via raw GLES2, fix F4 double-toggle and OSD alpha

SDL3 has no stable WebGPU backend, so the web build renders the CRT
post-effect through a raw GL context (WebGL1/GLES2) instead of SDL_GPU,
mirroring the Metal/Vulkan backends behind the same opaque API.

Emscripten backs every SDL_Window with the same canvas, so the
recreate-window workaround used to dodge the Linux stuck-swapchain bug
left the GLES path with no live GL context on the second F4 press
(display going blank); it now just re-creates the GL context on the
existing window instead.

Also fixes the OSD green-interior colour constant, which packed alpha
as 0x00: harmless on the SDL_GPU swapchain paths, but on Emscripten the
canvas alpha channel composites with the page background, rendering the
OSD text black instead of green.

events.title: Six static test droids, and lock the game loop to 25 Hz
events.message:
Six static test droids, and lock the game loop to 25 Hz

Two things that belong together: the pool could not be judged without
something in it, and putting six droids in it immediately showed why
free-running was the wrong choice.

TEST_DROIDS parks six droids around the player at deck load. They are
static in the WORLD, not on the screen, so the deck scrolls past them
the way it will when they move, and the world-to-screen mapping in
droidtest.asm is the part droid.asm will actually need - it is the
same arithmetic DeadZone does for the player, minus the dead zone.
Scaffolding: delete the file and the flag together once droids move.

The frame lock is the substantive change. FRAME_LOCK = 2 fields per
pass, so one pass of our loop is one C64 GameLoop iteration:

  loop iterations per 100 fields   free-running   locked
    player only                       101 (50Hz)   50 (25Hz)
    player + 6 droids                  80 (40Hz)   50 (25Hz)

Free-running looked better until there was a pool to test it with.
The loop does not fit in a field with seven sprites, so it stretched
to 1.25 fields and the player moved 20% SLOWER with droids on screen
than without - speed as a function of how much was visible. Chunkier
motion is the lesser fault, and it is the original's own cadence.

Real-time speed is unchanged. PLY_ACCEL, PLY_DECEL and PLY_MAXSPD now
scale by FRAME_LOCK / PLY_ITER_FRAMES, which cancels at 2 and 2, so
the C64's per-iteration constants apply unmodified for the first time.
Confirmed rather than derived: xSpd tops out at &0700, 7.0 px per
iteration, the same 175 px/s as 3.5 px/field at 50 Hz. What is given
up is the extra smoothness the 50 Hz sampling bought, which was always
a bonus over the original rather than a requirement.

export_droids.py gains the same FRAME_LOCK so drSpeedF stays correct.
Nothing reads it yet, but it would have been quietly wrong by a factor
of two once droids move.

Also records BUGS.md #4, found while looking for a room to put the
droids in: CentreOnDeck picks the view from the centroid of a deck's
tiles and never asks whether the cell it drops the player on is
walkable, so on decks 5 and 14 the player spawns inside a wall and
cannot move at all. Not a Layer 5 regression - CentreOnDeck has not
changed since Layer 3 - and the fix is already implied by the data,
since waypoint 0 of each deck is unused by InitDeckDroids and exists
to be the player's spawn. TD_DECK = 1 meanwhile.

At 25 Hz the budget is ~80,000 cycles a pass against ~68,000 spent on
seven sprites, so the pool now fits and round-robin updating changes
from necessary to merely useful. Tearing is the visible problem.

events.message:
ci : job android (8e paquet) ; empreinte wasm réparée

JOB ANDROID dans release.yml, sur le modèle des sept autres : chaque push/PR
vérifie que l'APK se construit, un tag attache NeoST-<ver>-android-arm64-debug.apk
à la Release (signé clé de DEBUG → installable tel quel ; pas de clé de store dans
le dépôt, cf. packaging/android/README.md § Signature). JDK 17 COMPLET via
setup-java (un JRE n'a pas jlink, dont AGP a besoin — et son erreur ne dit pas
qu'il manque un paquet), composants SDK épinglés aux versions du README (NDK 27,
CMake 3.22, API 34), fetch_sdl.sh, build_apk.sh debug (garde-fous libs+assets
intégrés), vérification STATIQUE du manifeste (aapt dump badging : paquet,
activité lançable, arm64-v8a) — pas d'appareil ni de KVM sur les runners ; le
cœur arm64 est validé par ailleurs, bit-exact sous qemu-aarch64. Le job publish
compte désormais 8 paquets et ramasse aussi les .apk.

RÉPÉTÉ AVANT DE POUSSER dans un clone frais du dépôt (checkout vierge →
sous-module imgui → fetch_sdl → build_apk debug → badging, les mêmes greps que le
job) : c'est ce test qui prouve que le dépôt commité contient tout — le poste de
dev, lui, avait déjà tout sous la main. APK du clone conforme (libs, menu ImGui,
assets ; l'écart de taille zip avec le build local n'est que de la compression).

EMPREINTE WASM : le job wasm du push précédent était rouge sur sa garde de
fraîcheur — à raison. SOURCE_STAMP avait été écrit AVANT le git add complet, et
l'empreinte (assise sur git ls-files src/**) a changé quand les fichiers Android
sont entrés dans l'index. Le bundle, lui, était bon : reconstruit pour vérifier,
il ressort IDENTIQUE AU BIT PRÈS au commité (même md5 — emcc est reproductible à
version fixe sur la même machine). Empreinte réécrite ; leçon : --write toujours
APRÈS le stage complet.

events.message:
android : premier APK (SDL2+GLES2) avec menu façon borne ; WASM plein écran en zoom adaptatif

QUATRIÈME PLATEFORME — APK arm64-v8a (Android 5.0+), packaging/android/build_apk.sh.
Le portage suit le WEB, pas le GUI de bureau : main.cpp rend en OpenGL immédiat
(glBegin/GL_QUADS) et pilote son interface en imgui_impl_opengl2, qui n'existent pas
sur Android. src/android/main_android.cpp transpose main_web.cpp : même shader GLES2,
même chaîne audio partagée (core/AudioMix), même cadence sur le TEMPS ÉMULÉ. Aucune
ligne de neost_core ne change. SDL2 = couche plateforme (fenêtre, GLES, cycle de vie,
tactile, manettes, audio), vendorisé NON commité (extern/SDL2, fetch_sdl.sh), branche
if(ANDROID) du CMakeLists racine sur le modèle if(EMSCRIPTEN). Assets : EmuTOS +
diskA.st SEULEMENT (~1 Mo, garde-fou) — pas de TOS Atari dans un APK.

MENU = LA GRAMMAIRE DE LA BORNE, décalquée : voile sombre et machine EN PAUSE,
ludothèque en rangées énormes (suites du jeu monté teintées et en tête), insérer ne
redémarre pas (seul RESTART relance), page clavier ancrée en bas sur machine qui
TOURNE (répondre à « PRESS SPACE » sans figer le jeu). kioskScanDisks extrait en
io/MediaScan, partagé borne ↔ Android. Deux écarts dictés par le support : rangées
tapables, actions en rangée horizontale. neost-menu-preview (EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
dessine le menu dans une fenêtre bureau au format téléphone — c'est lui qui a
rattrapé l'erreur d'échelle du premier jet (tailles multipliées par uiScale alors
que la police l'était déjà).

CHASSE AUX BUGS, 8 corrections — presque toutes trouvées en comparant à ce que la
borne fait DÉJÀ : injection touche/clic MAINTENUE 4 trames + refus pendant le
maintien (clic raté par les jeux qui scrutent au VBL, touche collée) ; clic fantôme
au ST en tapant le bouton MENU (gate WantCaptureMouse) + compteur de doigts
désynchronisé (reset quand l'UI a la main) ; boucle de rendu LIBRE (~50 rendus/trame
→ vsync, repli si refusé) ; data race sur g_primed (thread audio) ; contexte EGL
perdu en veille (objets GL recréés au retour) ; troncation UTF-8 au bord d'un point
de code ; underruns journalisés (atomique).

WASM PLEIN ÉCRAN = ZOOM ADAPTATIF : cadré sur la ZONE ACTIVE, buffer entier dès
qu'une démo ouvre les bordures (hystérésis ~0,6 s). stContentRegion (latches
compris) extrait de main.cpp en core/Framing.cpp — bureau, kiosk et WASM appellent
la MÊME fonction. Piège MESURÉ : en plein écran le port GLFW d'Emscripten
redimensionne lui-même le canvas à la taille écran (640×400 demandés, 800×600
imposés) → letterbox fait au viewport GL (recette drawStKiosk/Android), canvas rendu
à Emscripten pendant le plein écran, syncCanvasSize compare à la taille RÉELLE pour
restaurer le ratio fenêtré. Le shell signale fullscreenchange (couvre la sortie par
Échap). Vérifié Puppeteer : image plein écran au ratio 1,605 (zone active = 1,600 ;
cadre complet 1,507, étirement écran 1,333), canvas restauré à la sortie.

Au passage : règles .gitignore des binaires ancrées à la racine (/neost) — la règle
nue ignorait AUSSI le paquet Java net/gistlabs/neost/ (trouvé au dry-run du commit).

Validation : cœur ARM64 sous qemu-aarch64 = image et son IDENTIQUES AU BIT PRÈS au
x86-64 (cmp PPM/WAV) ; APK vérifié statiquement (libs, dex, manifeste, SDL_main) ;
--tier fast et full verts ; bundle wasm/ reconstruit, SOURCE_STAMP vérifié.

events.title: Fix window cascade offset: arithmetic on SDL_WINDOWPOS_UNDEFINED corrupts it
events.message:
Fix window cascade offset: arithmetic on SDL_WINDOWPOS_UNDEFINED corrupts it

SDL_WINDOWPOS_UNDEFINED is a magic encoded value (0x1FFF0000 | display
index), not a coordinate -- adding index*40 to it corrupted the encoding
instead of offsetting the position, so every two-up window landed centred
regardless of index. Read back the real position SDL assigned after
creation and offset from that instead.

events.title: Share the loading-screen wait across two-up instances instead of serialising it
events.message:
Share the loading-screen wait across two-up instances instead of serialising it

Each instance held the splash for LOADING_SCREEN_DURATION_MS before the next
one was even created, so -n instances paid N times the startup delay for no
reason -- the wait doesn't depend on anything instance-specific. Split
chq_instance_create (window/audio/splash bitmap) from a new
chq_instance_launch_game (game thread start), and hold the splash once in
main() across every instance's window before any of them launch.

An instance that quits during the shared wait never launches a game thread,
so chq_instance_destroy now skips the game teardown calls for it instead of
dereferencing a NULL game/game_thread.

events.title: Add multi-instance (-n), -quiet, -scale options to SDL3 app for two-up testing

Add multi-instance (-n), -quiet, -scale options to SDL3 app for two-up testing

Runs N concurrent game instances from one process to smoke-test for static
data trampling between them (audit found none: engine/library layers have
no mutable statics). Each instance owns its own chq_sdl_state_t, window and
game thread.

Fixes along the way:
- SDL_PollEvent drains one process-wide queue; polling it per-instance let
  one instance steal another's input. Events are now pumped once per frame
  and dispatched to the owning window by windowID.
- An instance's window stayed open after its close button was clicked,
  because teardown only ran once every instance had quit. Each instance now
  tears down as soon as its own quit flag fires, tracked via a new
  CHQ_FLAG_CLOSED bit rather than a side array.

events.title: Layer 5 step 3: compile the digits, measured at 9%
events.message:
Layer 5 step 3: compile the digits, measured at 9%

Sprite rows 6-13 are drawn by generated code too. The digits are DENSE
where the rotor was sparse - 42.7 opaque bytes of 56 against 3.2 of 7 -
so nothing is saved by skipping transparent bytes; the whole win is
deleting SprFetchRow, which copies and masks all seven bytes of all
eight rows whether they draw anything or not.

Per-type code would be ~1,012 bytes and 24 types is 25K, which does not
fit in the bank. But the number is three independent 8-pixel glyphs and
there are only ten glyphs, so ten routines cover all 24 types and the
three POSITIONS are reached by offsetting bufp and svp by 0, 16 and 32.
Nothing is generated at run time and there is no per-type table.

The glyphs draw without saving. Under a 2 px shift each spills into the
next one's first byte, so the three share columns 2 and 4 - and whichever
writes a shared column first would have to be the one that saves it,
which is not a property a glyph can know about itself. Hoisting the save
into one generic pass over all seven columns removes the question, and
makes the restore a single pass as well, because putting the background
back does not care what was drawn over it.

                  before   after
  SprRestoreAll    3,506   3,260
  SprDrawAll       7,142   6,400
  total           10,648   9,660   -9.3%

That is ~990 cycles against the ~2,600 projected, and the shortfall is
structural rather than a defect. Three glyph positions mean three walks
of the eight rows plus one for the save, where the interpreted path made
one; a walk step is JSR SprNextScan at ~37 cycles, so the block spends
~1,180 cycles advancing scanlines against the old ~296. One walk would
need per-row code covering all three glyphs, which is per-type - the 25K
option deliberately not taken. Recorded in PLAN.md rather than chased,
because step 4 is worth several times more.

Cumulative from the end of Layer 4: 13,998 -> 9,660, a 31% cut. Seven
sprites is still 67.6K against a 40,000-cycle frame, so compilation has
run out of road and the update rate is the whole remaining problem.

The 2 px shifted copy of the artwork is gone with this. Both shifts now
exist as compiled code, and the stored rows are read only by the wrap
fallback, so SprFetchRow shifts the few it needs on the fly and
SprBuildShift is deleted. That reclaimed the 1,743 bytes the glyph code
occupies. The bank ends at &BA84 of &C000 and PARADAT is 59 pages.

Verified byte-identical two ways: the compiled digits against the same
build's interpreted path, forced by patching sd_digit and sr_digit's
LDA sprNoWrap to LDA #0, 0 diffs over the whole 10K; and the restored
buffer against a forced RedrawAll after full-speed diagonal scrolling,
0 diffs.

One method note now in PLAN.md, because it cost an hour: sample the play
buffer inside WaitVSync, not at an arbitrary cycle count. A dump taken
mid-SprDrawSlot shows the sprite half-drawn and is indistinguishable
from missing rows.

events.title: build: `make atari-binaries` -> FRUA.PRG (68000) + FRUA_020.PRG (020)
events.message:
build: `make atari-binaries` -> FRUA.PRG (68000) + FRUA_020.PRG (020)

Two shipping Atari binaries, both with the Nova backend built in:
  FRUA.PRG      68000 codegen — runs on EVERY Atari (ST/STE/Mega STe/TT/Falcon),
                the safe universal build.
  FRUA_020.PRG  -m68020-60 codegen — Falcon030/TT030 only, faster (32-bit
                muls/divs + bitfield ops). The original Mac was pure 68000 THINK
                C, so this is codegen we ADDED; a 68000 machine cannot run it.

The CPU68K value is in the BUILDSTAMP, so each sub-make fully rebuilds on the
switch — two clean compiles, never a mix (the illegal-instruction death that
bit us on 2026-07-15). The target integrity-checks the 68000 binary in place:
it fails the build if any real-code 020 op survives (the ~10 phantom
bfextu/bfins are const lookup tables GCC parks in .text, excluded per CLAUDE.md).

Verified: FRUA.PRG md5 = the consolidated 68000 build (Nova + the modify stat-
click fix); FRUA_020.PRG carries genuine 020 codegen (2223 muls.l/bfextu/bfins
in boot.o). Both gitignored as build artifacts.

The maintainer accepted two binaries over a fat/CPU-detecting single binary (a
runtime codegen switch would mean two copies of the hot loops plus trampolines —
not worth it vs two named PRGs).

events.title: build: compile the Nova backend into every Atari binary (no separate FRUANOVA)
events.message:
build: compile the Nova backend into every Atari binary (no separate FRUANOVA)

Consolidation per the maintainer's suggestion. Nova detection was already
entirely runtime (dsp_detect probes the card and falls back to VIDEL / ST-Low
when absent), so -DFRUA_NOVA only ever controlled whether display_nova.c
compiled to real code (~14 KB) or a 158-byte stub. Making it the default in the
Makefile's falcon branch means ONE binary serves a plain machine and one with a
card -- there is no FRUANOVA.PRG to build, stage, or accidentally ship as the
wrong CPU (which bit us: a 020 FRUANOVA that exited on the Mega STe).

Atari-only: the define sits in the falcon branch, never the amiga branch
(display_nova.c pulls in mint/osbind.h and the Amiga has its own RTG). Verified:
020 and CPU68K=68000 Atari builds both link nova_backend (display_nova.o ~14 KB,
68000 integrity clean); the amiga build compiles unchanged. Falcon boots and
falls back to VIDEL when no card is present (Hatari), exactly as before -- pure
addition, no behaviour change on a machine without a card.

The official release recipe never built a separate FRUANOVA.PRG (that was a
manual hardware-test build), so nothing there changes. docs/aranym-harness.md
updated: no -DFRUA_NOVA step, and nova=force is still needed only under
ARAnyM/Hatari (they report _VDO==3 so dsp_detect picks VIDEL first); real
ST/STE-class hardware fires the probe on its own (_VDO<=1).

events.title: engine: wire the Modify-Character stat click (jt178 shape-5 cells)
events.message:
engine: wire the Modify-Character stat click (jt178 shape-5 cells)

Ports jt178's gated shape-5 install block (CODE 7 0x288a..0x2976), which our
lift had stubbed as "the shape-5 jt452 button bar for mouse clicks is a TODO" —
the reason the Modify screen's stat rows were mouse-dead while the keyboard
command bar worked. The maintainer confirmed the feature IS in Mac 1.0
(BasiliskII) and it is byte-identical in 1.2, so this is a faithful wiring fix,
not a version cherry-pick.

When g_a5_-12911 is set (it is, on this screen), jt178 now streams eight shape-5
cells through jt452: six over the ability rows (8000-space y = 8036/8040/8044/
8048/8052/8056 = STR..CHA, 4 apart), one at 8004 (name), one at (8012,8080)
(HP), each x=8000 rec22=4 rec24=80 with rec[28] bit 4 set (commit-on-click);
jt180() adds bit 1 to the name cell. Shape 5 -> method jt378, the same list-cell
hit-test the treasure / character-select screens use — which was the
maintainer's lead.

Verified live (FRUA_MODIFY + FRUA_CLICKDIAG): the pool goes 7 -> 15 items (8
shape-5), a click on the DEX row hits its cell (iy 8048), l25b6 maps it to act=3
(DEX = stat index 3), move-pending is set, l4d64(3) selects it, and a follow-up
click on INT reports cur stat 3 first — proving the DEX selection persisted. Two
assumptions from the trace were wrong and are noted: -6927 is NOT always 0 (the
commit path sets it), and the cells DO hit-test once present.

Scope: jt178 has exactly one caller in the port (l618c), so this touches only
the Modify screen — no other command-bar screen is affected. Clean 020 and
CPU68K=68000 builds (integrity: 0 real-code 020 ops). 469 passed, 6 skipped.
The FRUA_CLICKDIAG probes (jt452 shape census, l2d3e commit index, l618c act)
are kept gated for the follow-up on the name/HP cells.

events.title: docs: modify-char stat click SOLVED — jt178's -12911-gated shape-5 block
events.message:
docs: modify-char stat click SOLVED — jt178's -12911-gated shape-5 block

The wire is located. jt178 (CODE 7 0x2866) installs the clickable stat cells in
a block gated on g_a5_-12911 (0x288e: tstb -12911; beqw L297a). When set, it
streams EIGHT shape-5 DLItems through jt452: six over the ability rows (y =
8036/8040/8044/8048/8052/8056, 4 apart = STR..CHA), one at y=8004 (name), one at
(8012,8080) (HP, guarded by L38f8). Shape 5 -> method jt378, the SAME list-cell
hit-test the pick-treasure/character-select screens use -- the maintainer's lead
("look for a 'pick item' function like treasure/char-select") was exactly right.

Our jt178 lift OMITS the whole block (l206e; l2170; l2858; l23b4, skipping
0x288e..0x2976) -- and the code comment already admitted it: "the shape-5 jt452
button bar (for mouse clicks) is a TODO." That is why the measured shape census
on the modify screen was 6x shape-1 + 1x shape-7 and ZERO shape-5.

The gate is already satisfied: g_a5_-12911 is set to 1 in our jt452_init. So the
only missing piece is porting the install block. docs/modify-mouse-trace.md now
carries the full spec (cell positions, the jt452(5,...)+token-20 stream, the
L38f8 conditional) and the one thing to verify during the lift -- how a clicked
cell index reaches l4d64 to set the stat cursor -6926 (its ONLY writer).

No code change yet; this is the located wire + implementation spec. The lift
touches shared jt178, so it wants a focused pass with a before/after shape
census on other command-bar screens.

events.title: diag+docs: modify screen installs NO shape-5 stat cell (measured)
events.message:
diag+docs: modify screen installs NO shape-5 stat cell (measured)

Following the maintainer's lead (the clickable stat frame is a "pick item"
list like pick-treasure / character-select), the mechanism is now identified
and the gap measured.

The reusable clickable list is jt169 (List Manager): pick-treasure (l39ac)
runs it over a rect and returns the chosen item; its primitive is a shape-5
DLItem (method jt378, rec[4] = a row-pick proc), installed by jt452(5,...) —
which is what jt158 does.

Instrumenting jt452 (FRUA_CLICKDIAG now logs each allocation's shape) across
the whole modify-screen build shows it installs ONLY 6x shape-1 (the command
bar) + 1x shape-7 (the sentinel). ZERO shape-5. So there is provably no
clickable region over the stat frame — exactly the reported symptom.

What is still open: l618c calls neither jt452 nor jt158 directly (its JT set
is identical to the Mac and audit-clean), and neither l1276/jt886 nor jt895
installs a shape-5 cell in EITHER fork. So the Mac installs the stat cell by a
path not yet located. docs/modify-mouse-trace.md records the decisive finding
and the two fastest ways to close it (a BasiliskII behavioural trace, or a
branch-level read of the shared jt886/jt178 for a shape-5 install our lift
skipped).

Diagnostic only (gated on FRUA_CLICKDIAG); clean 020 build restored.

events.title: docs: modify-char stat click is a Mac 1.0 wiring gap — record it, trace it
events.message:
docs: modify-char stat click is a Mac 1.0 wiring gap — record it, trace it

Two records, per the maintainer's ask ("record it and trace the wire").

1. mac12-hunk-log.md: a NEGATIVE result. The missing mouse stat-editing on the
   Modify-Character screen is NOT a 1.0->1.2 change. Verified in BasiliskII that
   Mac 1.0 HAS it (click a stat/number -> highlights cyan), and CODE 17 (l618c
   + the six stat handlers + its command bar) has zero real hunks between the
   forks. So it is a port wiring gap against a faithful lift, not a version
   difference. This corrects my earlier wrong "DOS-only feature" conclusion.

2. modify-mouse-trace.md: the trace, left OPEN and honest. The click DELIVERY
   chain is complete and correct (l725c -> l690e -> l6b26 -> jt1125 -> l2d3e).
   l618c's edit loop is a faithful lift. But the modify screen's DLItem pool has
   only 7 items (6 command-bar buttons + 1 sentinel, dumped live) and NO stat
   rows -- so l2d3e has nothing to hit on a stat click.

   The doc's value is the ruled-OUT list, so the next session does not re-walk
   these: not per-stat DLItems (no jt452/jt325 install for stats), not the
   move-pending flag (-6927 is written only by l4df0, both callers push 0, so it
   is vestigial here), not a second writer of the stat cursor (-6926 has exactly
   ONE writer in the whole Mac binary, l4d64 at 0x4dd2, reached only from
   keyboard handlers), not a coord test on the captured click (-912/-910 is read
   only by jt1125), not a harness artifact (l0f2e installs nothing FRUA_MODIFY
   skips), not a dropped JT call (l618c/l1276 audit clean).

   What remains: Mac 1.0 makes stats clickable through a path this trace has not
   located. Three candidates and two fast experiments are listed -- the key one
   being to statically count the Mac's own modify-screen DLItem installs: ~7
   means the mechanism is a coordinate test in a method/sheet, ~13 means an
   installer call is missing from our lift.

No code change; the FRUA_CLICKDIAG paint/hitrect probes landed earlier.

events.title: engine: hit-test every DLItem, not just 8000-space ones (modify-char mouse)
events.message:
engine: hit-test every DLItem, not just 8000-space ones (modify-char mouse)

l2d3e's click loop gated the per-item hit-test on `iy >= 8000`, so every
ABSOLUTE-coordinate item (rec16 < 8000) was dropped before its method ran. The
8000-space screens — the icon grid, the Hall — worked; any screen laid out in
absolute pixels was mouse-DEAD. That is the shape of the reported bug: the
modify-character sub-screens are mouse-unresponsive while keyboard accelerators
work.

The gate is not faithful. CODE 3 L2d3e's loop (0x2d84..0x2dac) pushes
(item, cmd=2, cy, cx) and `jsr (a0)` UNCONDITIONALLY — there is no
coordinate-space guard in the Mac. The method scopes the test itself: jt137
msg 2 handles both spaces (jt1135 passes values <=6000 through unchanged), and
a non-clickable item computes a rect the click simply isn't inside, so removing
the gate cannot manufacture a spurious hit. The `hm != NULL` check stays — that
is a PORT-SAFETY guard (the Mac would fault on a null method), not a behaviour.

How this was found: FRUA_CLICKDIAG now logs jt137's paint-y beside its msg-2
rect, in one coordinate space. That KILLED the previous theory — the DONE
plate paints at y=188, inside its hit rect [186,198); paint and hitbox AGREE.
The "painter draws lower than the item" idea was screenshot-to-engine mapping
noise (offsets 48..59 across runs, cy clamped at 199), not a real offset. With
that gone, the real defect was the gate one line up.

PROVEN: the gate is non-faithful (asm), and removing it does not break the
working screens — DONE still commits, sprites still colour, the Hall buttons
still hit. NOT YET DEMONSTRATED end-to-end: an actual dead button coming alive
on a modify sub-screen, because those need a populated roster and every headless
route to one is blocked by imprecise mouse injection (the same injection noise
that faked the paint offset). The fix is correct by faithfulness and matches the
mechanism exactly; the live confirmation is a hardware/real-mouse check.

Also builds clean as CPU68K=68000 (integrity: 0 real-code 020 ops).

events.title: diag: jt137 logs paint-y and its msg-2 rect (FRUA_CLICKDIAG)
events.message:
diag: jt137 logs paint-y and its msg-2 rect (FRUA_CLICKDIAG)

Settles paint-vs-hitbox from inside the engine, in one coordinate space —
the screenshot-to-engine mapping is provably noisy (offsets 48..59 across
runs, cy clamped at 199), so log-line vs log-line is the only trustworthy
comparison.

First run's result is the surprise: on the char-gen screen jt137's msg-1
PAINT arm never fires at all (0 lines across the whole session), while its
msg-2 HITRECT fires constantly. The DONE/EXIT plates are hit-tested by
jt137 but painted by some other path entirely — so the paint position and
the hit rect come from different math and CAN disagree. Next instrument
goes on the painter.

events.title: tools: the icongrid probe disproves my own dating of #137
events.message:
tools: the icongrid probe disproves my own dating of #137

Ran the endpoint calibration the bisect needs, and it overturned the conclusion
I committed in 12917a32. Recording that rather than quietly moving on.

I had said the hand-rolled CLUT install in l09dc was correct when written and
broke later, when the GLIB pool flip (43d813f5, 2026-07-13) made jt468 return
the already-extracted sub-GLIB. That was inferred from commit messages and
never measured. The probe judged 43d813f5^ — the commit immediately BEFORE the
flip — and the grid is ALREADY BLACK there (verdict=bad, meanL=7, satpx=0, and
the frame is unmistakably the grid screen: DONE/EXIT bar, READY/ACTION panel,
TEST/MALE/HUMAN/FIGHTER). So the flip is a sufficient explanation for why the
navigation cannot work NOW, but it is not the point of regression.

Pushed back further: at e05e625b, whose message claims the icon-grid colours
were fixed, the route cannot reach char-gen at all — it stops on the Hall
screen, and the probe correctly reports SKIP instead of inventing a verdict.
So there is no GOOD endpoint: every commit this probe can judge says bad. The
likeliest reading is that the live route NEVER produced a coloured grid, and
e05e625b was verified through the FRUA_BODY harness (which calls jt573 directly
and passes) rather than the live jt574 path — the harness/live divergence that
already cost four wrong theories earlier in this work. Probably not a
regression at all.

The measured mechanism is unaffected: l37aa(set1, 0) returns 0 at HEAD, no
palette is installed, jt124 fixes it, and the Falcon/STe frames prove the fix.
Only the causation claim was wrong. Corrected in the l09dc comment and
docs/jt-call-audit.md, both of which now say the dating is unknown.

Two more infrastructure traps found and fixed while getting here, either of
which would have silently ruined a bisect:

- STRAY SOURCES. The Makefile globs $(wildcard src/engine/*.c), and checkout
  does not remove a file untracked at the old commit but tracked on main — so
  src/engine/a4_map.c was compiled at a commit predating a4_map.h. Reads
  exactly like an unbuildable commit. Now `git clean -fdq src platform compat`,
  scoped and without -x, because -x at the root would delete data/.
- THE HARNESS CHANGED INSIDE THE RANGE. 4017f651 (2026-07-26) taught it to find
  the Falcon TOS instead of requiring FALCON_TOS, so an older checked-out
  harness invoked Hatari with options it rejected and Hatari printed its usage
  text — which reads as "the engine will not boot". The harness is now pinned to
  a shadow tree outside the repo, for the same reason the probe is.

events.title: tools: icongrid probe — a verdict that can say "I could not tell"
events.message:
tools: icongrid probe — a verdict that can say "I could not tell"

The old metric counted DISTINCT COLOURS in the grid region and could not
distinguish "the sprites are black" from "the route never got to the grid".
Worse, it scored the main menu at 14 against a correct grid's 12 — so it was
capable of calling a healthy commit bad, and did.

Replaced with two plain statistics over the cell panel, measured on real frames
of every screen the route can land on:

  screen                meanL   satpx
  coloured grid (good)  121.2   29.1%
  black grid (bad)        3.8    0.0%
  main menu              88.3    2.7%
  PICK race/class        90.7    6.1%

satpx >= 15 -> good (exit 0); meanL <= 20 -> bad (exit 1); anything else is NOT
A VERDICT and exits 125 so bisect skips. Statistics rather than a reference
image on purpose: a crop of the game's rendered UI is copyrighted art and must
not enter the repo. `--classify <png>...` re-checks the thresholds offline.

Pacing is now polling instead of fixed sleeps. Keep screenshotting until the
frame classifies as a grid or patience runs out; `shots` already waits for a
settled frame, so each poll doubles as a stability check. The fixed sleeps were
tuned on a 16MHz run and silently desynced on anything slower — an older commit
booting at 8MHz sat on the PICK screen and got judged there, which is precisely
how a healthy commit produced a "bad" verdict.

Switched from the 68000 ST to FALCON: the bug reproduces identically on
Falcon/VIDEL, ST-Low and NovaGPU (three backends sharing no display code, which
is what proved it engine-level), and Falcon boots in ~10s against the ST's
~200s. Falcon also has 14MB, which is what killed the 4MB-ceiling theory.

events.title: son : chaîne de mixage unique + WASM au modèle push (samples audibles) ; profils de réglages
events.message:
son : chaîne de mixage unique + WASM au modèle push (samples audibles) ; profils de réglages

Deux chantiers, la même leçon : ce qui existe en plusieurs copies finit par diverger.

SON WASM — « les samples ne s'entendent presque pas »
La chaîne de mixage vivait en TROIS copies : Audio::produceFrame (GUI), le dump
--sound-dump du headless (dont le commentaire disait déjà « même chaîne que ») et
le frontend web. Cette troisième était restée sur l'ANCIENNE API : la page tirait
des échantillons quand son nœud audio réclamait un bloc (~43 ms) et le cœur
synthétisait en lisant les registres du YM EN DIRECT. Or un digidrum écrit le
volume à plusieurs kHz et un bruitage DMA dure quelques millisecondes : n'en
garder qu'un point par bloc APLATIT tout ce qui module sous la trame. Il ne
restait que ce qui varie lentement — la mélodie.

- core/AudioMix.cpp : la chaîne devient une unité du cœur (YM horodaté → DMA STE
  horodaté → HPF → gains/tonalité LMC1992), appelée par les trois frontends.
- Web au modèle « push » : son produit PAR TRAME ÉMULÉE, après runFrame, avec
  setCycleClock armé sur le PSG et le DMA — sans lui, synthesizeFrame rend un jeu
  de registres que plus rien ne met à jour et la machine est MUETTE (constaté en
  l'oubliant : sortie à zéro absolu).
- Sortie stéréo (elle était mono), AudioWorklet avec repli ScriptProcessorNode,
  file à coussin de 90 ms + asservissement de débit (±8 éch./trame) sur la
  profondeur renvoyée par la page, garde-fous anti-enflement quand le contexte
  est suspendu, curseur de volume (rampe anti-clic côté cœur).
- tools/make_digidrum_test.py : nouvel étalon qui DISCRIMINE (carré ~997 Hz écrit
  dans le registre de volume à 7 979 Hz) — make_dmasnd_test, flux continu, sortait
  au même niveau avant comme après.

Mesures Chrome (spectre de la sortie réelle) : raie 211 Hz fantôme/saillance ×6
→ 1008 Hz/×28 (référence native 996 Hz/×104) ; −19,8 → −13,7 dBFS. Repli
ScriptProcessorNode vérifié séparément. Non-régression du natif prouvée AU BIT
PRÈS : --sound-dump avant/après l'extraction donne des WAV identiques (cmp).

PROFILS DE RÉGLAGES NOMMÉS
neost.cfg s'écrivait déjà tout seul, mais il n'y a qu'UNE config courante alors
que l'émulateur sert des attelages incompatibles (démo 512 Ko + TOS européen,
crack 1 Mo, .stx qui veut son lecteur B).

- Page « Profiles » (ou Machine → Settings profiles…) : profiles/<nom>.cfg, MÊME
  format que neost.cfg (parseConfigLine / writeConfigKeys / writeConfigAtomic
  partagés). Load / Overwrite / Delete en deux temps.
- Hors profil : rtc= (état machine), kiosk_romdir= (installation), dock=/showXxx=
  /uiVersion= (disposition ImGui) — et ce qu'un profil tait reste inchangé.
- Charger = reqRebuild (applyConfig) + requêtes de montage normales ; une image
  disparue n'est pas inscrite dans neost.cfg (invariant « on ne persiste qu'un
  montage réussi »). Nom de fichier assaini (anti-traversée). Rien ne s'écrit en
  borne (boutons grisés + garde côté boucle).
- Au passage : drivesound= ajouté — la case « Floppy drive sound » se cochait,
  se décochait, et repartait à ON au lancement suivant. Le câblage DriveSound→Audio
  suit désormais la DISPONIBILITÉ des échantillons, pas le réglage.

Validation : python3 tools/run_all.py --tier full → TOUS LES PALIERS OK ; bundle
wasm/ reconstruit et SOURCE_STAMP réécrit.

events.title: platform: video.cfg nova=force, so an emulator can reach the Nova backend
events.message:
platform: video.cfg nova=force, so an emulator can reach the Nova backend

display_nova.c is the only backend with no emulator. dsp_detect gates the probe
on _VDO <= 1 (a real card leaves the cookie reading ST/STE), which also makes
the backend unreachable anywhere else: Hatari reports Falcon AND its VDI
emulation tops out at 4 planes, so the 8-plane screen the probe requires cannot
exist there. Every Nova change therefore costs a round trip through the real
ATW800/2 — including the workstation-leak fix in bbbd5167, still unverified.

video.cfg may now contain `nova=force`, which runs the probe regardless of
_VDO. Read by a small independent helper rather than through videl_cfg_mode(),
because that runs inside videl_init — after a backend has already been chosen.

A config key rather than a -D so ONE binary serves the card and the emulator.
This session already lost time to a field log produced by a build older than
the fix it was meant to be testing; fewer variants is fewer chances to compare
the wrong two things.

Scope, stated plainly: this makes ARAnyM able to exercise the probe, the AES/VDI
workstation open, the depth query and the palette writes — enough to regression-
test the detect leak by counting "nova: card width" in DBG.LOG. It CANNOT
validate nova_hw_inverse, the pen -> hardware-slot table measured on the
ATW800/2. ARAnyM is the same class of target, not the same hardware.

docs/aranym-harness.md records the feasibility work, which is PARTIAL and says
so: ARAnyM boots TOS 4.04 headless at 8bpp, but plain TOS has no HostFS (the
host-folder mapping is a NatFeat), and ARAnyM rejects Hatari's EmuTOS image
outright. EmuTOS-for-ARAnyM boots, yet its default desktop still shows no host
drive, so nothing has actually been RUN under ARAnyM yet and no Nova path has
been verified. Remaining steps are listed there.

Also recorded: `import -window` on a STALE window id hangs and then wedges the
whole X server, so xwininfo and xwd hang afterwards too and Xvfb has to be
restarted. ARAnyM's window id changes between runs, which made this look like
"ARAnyM cannot be screenshotted". Re-query the id before every capture.

events.title: format: exclude hand-aligned headers and slopay-chip from format target
events.message:
format: exclude hand-aligned headers and slopay-chip from format target

clang-format's AlignConsecutive* options only align within a run
uninterrupted by comments or blank lines, so a raw pass over State.h,
Bank3State.h, Bank7State.h, Internal.h, Stages.h, CommonData.h and
Pixels.h flattens their hand-tuned struct/macro columns to minimum
width. format_all.py's align_declarations.py cannot fix this either:
it only realigns function-local variable blocks, not struct fields or

events.title: Layer 5 step 2: compile the rotor, measured at 24%
events.message:
Layer 5 step 2: compile the rotor, measured at 24%

Sprite rows 0-4 and 15-19 are no longer fetched and blitted; they are drawn
by generated 6502 in the data bank with the pixels and their masks baked in
as immediates. The rotor averages 3.2 opaque bytes of 7, and compiled code
costs nothing at all for the transparent ones, where the interpreted path
pays 26 cycles to fetch and 27 to blit each of the seven regardless.

Measured, one sprite, one frame:

                  before   after
  SprRestoreAll    3,490   3,506
  SprDrawAll      10,508   7,142   -32%
  total           13,998  10,648   -24%

Restore came out flat, which is arithmetic rather than disappointment: seven
bytes back costs 91 cycles, and 13 per saved byte plus ~49 to dispatch is 91
again at 3.2 bytes. It is kept because an interpreted restore would force the
draw to save all seven columns, and that costs the draw more than the restore
saves.

One compiled variant per shift rather than eight per alignment: within a
character row a byte is at col*8 + scan, the scan part rides on bufp, and
SprNextScan advances bufp and svp together — so Y is always col*8. That is
what the save-geometry change in 3f69b4d was for.

Rows straddling the end of the play strip have their columns out of address
order and no immediate can express the walk, so those fall back to the
interpreted path; drOfs and the rotor rows in drSprData stay live for it.

Also fixes a latent bug that only bites with more than one slot: sprNoWrap
was a global set by the last slot DRAWN and read by every slot RESTORED. It
is now per slot, alongside the compiled-rotor table base, because restore
runs a frame later — by which time the rotor has turned and the shift may
have changed.

Verified two ways. In Python the generator is checked against the
interpreted path: 320 rows over 8 phases x 21 rows x 2 shifts match what
drOfs would have fetched, and over eight background patterns the compiled
writes equal the interpreted writes and the compiled restore undoes them
exactly. In the emulator, after full-speed diagonal scrolling, disabling the
sprite and letting it restore leaves the play buffer byte-identical to a
forced RedrawAll across all 10K.

Costs 3,159 bytes in the bank, so SPR_SHIFT2 moves &A800 -> &B000 and
PARADAT grows to 48 pages. The staging assert is relaxed to match: staging
now overruns the panel, the mask table and the bottom of the play buffer,
which is safe because PageDataIn is the first thing after the load and
everything above it is rewritten before it is next read. Boot shows a moment
of garbage in the play area.

DEBUG_DRAW gains a second colour while we are here — magenta over the sprite
work, cyan over the redraw as before. SprRestoreAll gets the magenta too:
it is a third of the sprite cost and sits before the cyan band, so tinting
only the draw would understate the sprite budget by a third.

events.title: Record three open defects, and a warning about the debug oracle
events.message:
Record three open defects, and a warning about the debug oracle

RedrawAll's split-row repair executes with correct parameters and has no
effect: at line = 2 display row 0 holds 69 non-blank cells and zero splits,
so the row is left entirely as character row mapYr. That makes the SPACE
redraw an unreliable oracle whenever line != 0 — worth knowing before it is
trusted to judge another layer, hence the pointer from CLAUDE.md.

The other two are visible defects: blank scanlines at the top of the window
after stopping against a wall, and a one-frame wrong top line when stopping
after moving up at full speed. Recorded separately because the second is
self-correcting and moves the other way, so a shared cause is unproven; the
leading hypothesis for it is a raster race rather than a content error.

Each entry carries what has been ruled out as well as what is suspected —
reproducing the ruled-out list is the expensive part.

events.title: ci: débloquer le job wasm — bundle reconstruit + empreinte reproductible
events.message:
ci: débloquer le job wasm — bundle reconstruit + empreinte reproductible

Le job `wasm` de release.yml échouait sur main ET sur le tag 0.5.1, donc
`publish` (qui attend les 7 paquets) restait skipped : la Release 0.5.1 n'a
jamais été attachée au tag. C'était le seul job rouge.

BUNDLE — la garde de fraîcheur avait raison : le commit « démo par défaut en
ST 1 Mo / EmuTOS » avait changé src/web/main_web.cpp sans reconstruire wasm/,
donc index.wasm servait encore l'ancien défaut Mega STE + TOS Atari. Le bundle
est reconstruit (emsdk 6.0.6, -DNEOST_WEB_FREE_ONLY=ON, 9,0 Mo au total) et
vérifié dans un Chromium headless : la démo boote sur « Atari ST · 1 MB » /
etos192us.img, disquette A montée, aucune erreur de page. index.html et
index.data ressortent octet-identiques — seuls index.js et index.wasm bougent.

EMPREINTE — mais elle avait tort aussi : elle ne retombait pas sur la même
valeur d'une machine à l'autre, et aurait donc fini par rougir la CI SANS
qu'aucune source bouge (l'empreinte écrite sur le poste macOS ne correspondait
ni à HEAD ni à son parent recalculés sous Linux). Trois causes, trois
corrections dans tools/wasm_stamp.sh :

  · `find | sort` classe selon la LOCALE — en_US.UTF-8 (macOS) et C (runner)
    n'ordonnent pas pareil dès qu'un « / » ou un « _ » départage deux chemins.
    La liste vient désormais de `git ls-files` : tri par octets.
  · `find` comptait aussi les fichiers NON SUIVIS ; un brouillon oublié dans
    src/ décalait l'empreinte. `git ls-files` ne voit que le suivi.
  · sha256sum n'existe pas sur un macOS sans coreutils, et sha256sum/shasum/
    openssl ne formatent pas leur sortie pareil. L'outil est choisi parmi les
    trois et chaque ligne « empreinte + chemin » est recomposée ici — vérifié
    identique entre sha256sum et openssl.

CI — l'artefact NeoST-web-wasm est téléversé AVANT la garde : quand elle se
déclenche, le zip que le job vient de construire EST le bundle à recommiter,
donc on le récupère depuis la CI au lieu d'installer emsdk. DEV.md documente la
marche à suivre et ne pointe plus le deploy-web.yml supprimé.

events.message:
web: démo par défaut en ST 1 Mo / EmuTOS, et garde contre un wasm/ périmé

DÉFAUTS — la démo démarrait en Mega STE + TOS Atari. Elle démarre désormais en
ST, 1 Mo, EmuTOS 192 Ko US. Deux raisons : le ST est la machine de référence des
jeux et démos de l'époque, donc ce qu'attend un visiteur qui ne lira pas la doc ;
et EmuTOS étant libre, la démo publique n'ouvre plus sur une ROM Atari sous
copyright. Changé AUX DEUX endroits qui décident — main_web.cpp (le C++, seul à
faire foi) et shell.html (badge et sélecteurs). ?machine=megaste reste là.

GARDE — GitHub Pages est repassé en « deploy from a branch »
(build_type=legacy, main/(root)) : la racine sert le README rendu par Jekyll et
/wasm/ sert le dossier wasm/ COMMITÉ. La démo en ligne n'est donc plus produite
par la CI mais par le dépôt lui-même, et un oubli de reconstruction la fige sur
l'ancienne version, en silence — précisément ce qui avait laissé wasm/index.html
sur une coque française pendant des semaines sans que personne le voie.

  · deploy-web.yml RETIRÉ : en mode legacy son artefact Pages est ignoré, il ne
    produisait plus que des runs annulés et l'illusion d'un déploiement.
  · tools/wasm_stamp.sh empreinte les SOURCES du bundle (src/**, web/shell.html,
    CMakeLists.txt) dans wasm/SOURCE_STAMP ; le job wasm échoue si l'empreinte a
    bougé, avec la marche à suivre exacte dans le message.

Pourquoi pas un diff octet du bundle : emcc n'est pas reproductible d'une
version d'emsdk à l'autre et la CI n'a pas celle du poste de dev — la garde
échouerait à chaque run, donc on finirait par la désactiver. Une garde qu'on
désactive ne protège rien. Les sources, elles, se comparent exactement.

events.title: fix(wasm): cadence sur le temps ÉMULÉ, canvas à la résolution ; lien GLFW statique Windows
events.message:
fix(wasm): cadence sur le temps ÉMULÉ, canvas à la résolution ; lien GLFW statique Windows

Trois choses, deux signalées à l'usage.

1. SON « BIZARRE » EN WASM — ce n'était pas la synthèse, c'était l'horloge.
   La boucle exécutait UNE trame émulée par tick requestAnimationFrame, donc à
   la fréquence de rafraîchissement de l'ÉCRAN. Sur un moniteur 60 Hz, une
   machine PAL (50 Hz) tournait à 120 % ; sur du 120/144 Hz, bien pire. Rien
   n'était faux dans le YM — le son est simplement ce qui s'entend le plus vite.
   Même modèle que le frontend natif : une échéance porte la prochaine trame,
   chaque trame la repousse de SA durée (la géométrie décide : 50/60/71 Hz), un
   tour rAF exécute 0, 1 ou 2 trames selon ce que le temps réel réclame.
   Plafond à 4 contre la spirale au retour d'un onglet en arrière-plan, et on ne
   re-téléverse pas la texture quand aucune trame n'est due.

2. LA FENÊTRE SUIT LA RÉSOLUTION. Le canvas était créé une fois en 640×400 et
   l'image ST y était ÉTIRÉE : une trame overscan 416×276 — dont l'affichage
   correct fait 832×552, ratio 1.507 — sortait déformée de 6 % pour entrer dans
   un cadre 1.6. uploadFrame() pose désormais la taille d'affichage réelle à
   chaque changement de résolution, aspect pixel ST compris (≤480 px de large
   ×2, ≤300 lignes ×2 — la règle de main.cpp, donc 320×200, 640×200 et 640×400
   couvrent la même surface). La page étant en width:100%/height:auto, c'est la
   taille intrinsèque du canvas qui fixe le ratio : la poser suffit.

3. WINDOWS, 5e mur : le paquet dépendait de glfw3.dll — attrapé par le garde
   anti-DLL du script, exactement ce pour quoi il existe. Cause : la cible
   importée `glfw` passe le chemin ABSOLU de l'import-lib, et un chemin
   explicite échappe à -static. On passe par -lglfw3 (que -static résout vers
   libglfw3.a) avec la ligne exacte de `pkg-config --static --libs glfw3` : la
   liste vient du paquet, pas d'une devinette. Ajouté aussi ole32/oleaut32/uuid/
   winmm, que miniaudio n'auto-lie que sous MSVC (#pragma comment).

NON corrigé, relevé en chemin : la sortie web est MONO
(createScriptProcessor(…, 0, 1)) là où le bureau est stéréo DMA L/R, et
setCycleClock() n'est jamais posé côté web — les digidrums et le sync-buzzer,
qui dépendent du cycle DANS la trame, perdent leur placement. Les deux
demandent de basculer le web du modèle « pull » vers le « push » du bureau.

téléversement du framebuffer ARGB du Shifter a besoin. Seul l'EN-TÊTE est
ancien : tout pilote réel expose ces formats depuis vingt ans. gui/
CrtEffectStack.cpp et gui/OpenGLShader.cpp incluaient déjà <GL/glext.h> pour
cette raison ; main.cpp était le seul resté sur le gl.h nu. Même schéma partout.

Au passage, deux replis HOME → USERPROFILE, que Windows aurait rendus muets sans
casser la compilation — donc invisibles en CI :

  · plus gênant, le garde « dossier trop vaste » ne protégeait plus le dossier
    personnel : il refuse la racine ET tout ancêtre de HOME, or sans HOME ce

events.title: fix(wasm): exceptions natives — la démo web s'arrêtait au boot depuis toujours
events.message:
fix(wasm): exceptions natives — la démo web s'arrêtait au boot depuis toujours

Symptôme signalé sur https://habib256.github.io/neost/ : le boot se déroule
normalement ([Bus] TOS loaded, [FDC] drive A, « NeoST started ») puis
« Aborted(undefined) » avec ___cxa_throw dans la pile, en pleine boucle
principale.

Cause : la cible web n'activait AUCUN support d'exceptions. Emscripten neutralise
alors les `catch`, et son ___cxa_throw appelle littéralement abort() — vérifié
dans le binaire déployé :

    ___cxa_throw = (ptr,type,destructor) => { …; uncaughtExceptionCount++; abort() }

Or Moira SIGNALE les bus errors et address errors du 68000 en LANÇANT
(Cpu68k::raiseBusError → `throw moira::BusError`, DoubleFault, et le `catch`
interne de Moira::processException). Et sonder le matériel en provoquant des bus
errors est EXACTEMENT la façon dont EmuTOS détecte la machine. Le port web ne
pouvait donc pas survivre au boot : la première sonde le tuait. Ça ressemblait à
un gel plutôt qu'à un plantage — l'écran reste sur la dernière image.

Ce n'est pas une régression récente : entre le dernier déploiement d'avant-hier et
celui d'aujourd'hui, le seul changement non-textuel de src/ est kUiVersion dans
main.cpp, qui n'est même pas compilé dans la cible web.

-fwasm-exceptions et non -fexceptions : les deux corrigent, mais l'émulation JS
coûte 48 trampolines invoke_ — chaque appel pouvant lancer repasse par
JavaScript, dans le chemin chaud d'un émulateur. Mesuré sur ce projet :

    sans exceptions (déployé, cassé)  4 726 855 o   ← ne démarre pas
    -fexceptions      (JS)            6 464 199 o   48 invoke_
    -fwasm-exceptions (natif)         6 381 846 o    0 invoke_

Le natif est à la fois plus petit et sans aller-retour JS. Support navigateur :
Chrome 95+, Firefox 131+, Safari 15.2+. Les drapeaux vont sur neost_core (c'est
là que Moira est compilé), pas seulement sur l'exécutable web, et à la
compilation COMME au lien.

Vérifié : WebAssembly.validate() accepte le module (opcodes EH natifs), le JS
généré n'a plus ni abort() dans ___cxa_throw ni trampoline. wasm/ régénéré au
passage — l'artefact suivi était resté sur l'ancienne coque française.

⚠ Validation en NAVIGATEUR non faite : l'extension Chrome n'est pas connectée
dans cette session. La preuve est au niveau du code généré, pas à l'exécution.

events.message:
fix(windows): écarts d'API MinGW dans GemdosHd (mkdir, constantes access)

Deuxième mur du portage : mkdir() de MinGW ne prend PAS de mode — Windows n'a
pas de bits de permission POSIX — et les constantes F_OK/W_OK/R_OK d'access()
n'y sont pas définies. Plutôt que de réécrire les appels site par site (six
mkdir/access dans le fichier) et de faire diverger le code POSIX, le bloc de
compatibilité _WIN32 déjà présent ramène l'API Windows à la forme POSIX :
mkdir(p,m) → _mkdir(p), plus les trois constantes. Le corps du fichier reste
écrit une seule fois, et Linux/macOS ne voient rien passer.

Relevé en même temps le reste des appels du fichier (rmdir, unlink, rename,
chmod, utime, getcwd, access) : MinGW les fournit tous avec la signature POSIX,
seul mkdir divergeait.

events.message:
feat(windows): paquet Windows x64 (MinGW-w64, tout statique) — 0.5.1

NeoST ne sortait que pour Linux, macOS et le navigateur. Ce commit ajoute un
septième artefact de release : NeoST-<ver>-windows-x86_64.zip, à déballer et à
lancer, sans rien à installer.

MinGW-w64 (MSYS2/MINGW64) et non MSVC : le code est écrit pour GCC/Clang (options
-W…, C++20 exigé par Moira) et se compile ainsi tel quel. MSVC aurait imposé de
porter les options ET la chaîne de dépendances vers vcpkg, pour le même binaire.

TOUT EST LIÉ EN STATIQUE (libgcc, libstdc++, winpthread, GLFW). Ce n'est pas un
confort : une DLL oubliée est INVISIBLE en CI — MSYS2 les a dans son PATH — et
fatale chez l'utilisateur, qui reçoit « libstdc++-6.dll introuvable » au double-
clic. build_mingw.sh inspecte donc les imports des deux exécutables et refuse le
paquet si l'un d'eux dépend d'autre chose que des DLL Windows ; le job CI vérifie
en plus qu'aucun .dll n'a été livré dans le zip.

Portage, quatre points — aucun changement de comportement sur POSIX :
  · main.cpp : dossier de l'exécutable via GetModuleFileNameW. La variante W et
    non A — un chemin accentué (« C:\Users\Frédéric ») ressort en mojibake avec
    l'ANSI et plus aucune donnée n'est trouvée. Boucle de redimensionnement
    bornée à 32768 (limite NT) au lieu d'un MAX_PATH supposé suffisant.
    fileExists() passe de stat() à std::filesystem::exists(ec).
  · Acsi.cpp : taille de l'image par std::filesystem::file_size au lieu de
    stat().st_size.
  · Fdc.cpp : write-protect par les permissions std::filesystem (owner_write),
    où Windows reflète son attribut « lecture seule » — même sémantique
    qu'Hatari, qui décide d'après stat() et jamais d'après le format d'image.
  · GemdosHd.cpp : realpath() → std::filesystem::canonical, statvfs() →
    GetDiskFreeSpaceExW (sans quoi Dfree rend les valeurs factices et trompe
    « Informations disque » comme tout installeur).

⚠ Piège refermé dans le même geste : canonical() rend des séparateurs '\' sous
Windows, or tout GemdosHd compare avec PATHSEP ('/'). Sans generic_string(), le
test de préfixe du BAC À SABLE échouait — chaque accès aurait été rabattu sur la
racine du lecteur, en silence. C'est le garde anti-évasion, il ne doit pas
tomber en marche.

Le job CI tourne sur windows-latest et EXÉCUTE le binaire produit : --version
comparé à la version du paquet, boot EmuTOS 500 trames, capture non uniforme —
le même smoke que les six autres paquets, pas un contrôle symbolique. Gardes de
contenu identiques (liste autorisée de ROM, diskA seule, polices présentes).

Version 0.5.1. Doc : README (tableau des 7 paquets + avertissement SmartScreen,
le paquet n'est pas signé), CHANGELOG, et CLAUDE.md qui distingue désormais
cibles de DÉVELOPPEMENT (macOS/Linux) et cible LIVRÉE non développée (Windows).

Vérifié côté Linux : run_all.py --tier full intégralement vert après le portage
(les changements touchent FDC et GEMDOS, deux sous-systèmes que la suite couvre).

events.title: Layer 5: save sprite backgrounds in screen geometry
events.message:
Layer 5: save sprite backgrounds in screen geometry

The save area now mirrors the screen's own addressing. A screen byte
within a character row is at col*8 + scan, so a slot's save block is
laid out the same way: SPR_BLOCK = 56 bytes per character row, blocks
in sequence. One Y -- always col*8 -- now addresses both sides,
(bufp),Y for the screen and (svp),Y for the save, and SprNextScan
walks both pointers: +1 within a character row, +(stride - 7) across
one, stride being 640 for the screen and 56 for the save.

Three things fall out of that:

  - X is free. It was carrying sprSaveIdx.
  - The fifteen absolute save addresses that SprSetSlot and
    SprRestoreSlot rewrote per slot are gone; setup is one call.
  - The wrapped-row slow path is one pass instead of two. It needed
    two because each pass wanted the register the other held. The
    save side never wraps, so X can index the row data while Y
    alternates between 0 for the walked bufp and col*8 for svp -- and
    A survives LDY, so the background is read once, not twice.

The carry-free pointer advances are legal because 21 scanlines
starting at scan 0-7 touch at most four character rows, putting the
furthest byte at 3*56 + 48 + 7 = 223. Slots stay page-aligned, so
neither svp nor (svp),Y leaves its page. Asserted.

This is cycle-neutral, and deliberately so: STA (svp),Y costs one
more than STA abs,X, repaid by the pokes and index maintenance it
removes. Measured with seven slots live over 20M cycles, mapHX lands
on 141 both before and after -- unchanged to well under 1%. The point
is structural. A compiled blitter cannot poke a save address into
each of its ~72 stores, so an X-indexed save area would rule
compilation out; this is the shape that lets the immediates be baked
in.

Verified: with seven slots at varied Y, unit and shift the play
buffer is byte-identical to RedrawAll across all 10K, and the whole
buffer is byte-identical to the pre-change build for the same input.
Code is 132 bytes smaller.

events.message:
i18n: interface et journaux entièrement en anglais

L'UI ne devait plus contenir un mot de français, les messages de journal non
plus. Les commentaires du code et la documentation restent en français
(cf. CLAUDE.md).

Interface (src/main.cpp, web/shell.html) :
  · barre de menus, barre d'outils, barre d'état et ses infobulles ;
  · fenêtre Configuration et ses onze pages (Machine · Memory · ROM/TOS ·
    Floppies · Hard disks · Cartridge · Screen · Sound · Input · Emulation ·
    Kiosk), y compris les paragraphes explicatifs et le pied de page ;
  · fenêtres Memory (hex), CPU 68000, Joystick, Debugger, CRT Effects ;
  · messages transitoires (save-state, montages, glisser-déposer, bascule borne) ;
  · shell WebAssembly (titre, contrôles, aide, statuts) + lang="en".

Deux conséquences NON cosmétiques, traitées ici :
  · DockBuilderDockWindow() apparie les fenêtres par titre LITTÉRAL : les trois
    titres renommés (Memory (hex), CRT Effects, Debugger) sont mis à jour dans
    applyDockLayout(), sinon elles flottent au-dessus de l'écran ST ;
  · kUiVersion 2 → 3 : un imgui.ini existant indexe ses nœuds d'ancrage sur les
    ANCIENS titres, la disposition doit être resemée une fois.

Journaux (21 fichiers, ~176 messages) : neost-headless --help au complet, plus
[main] [cfg] [kiosk] [kbd] [joystick] [state] [mouse] [Bus] [NeoST] [config]
[cpu] [gluestat] [varline] [spec512] [save-state] [FDC] [msa-selftest] [STX]
[acsi] [gemdos] [mfp] [acia] [joy] [fpu] [Audio] [DriveSound] [CRT] [web].
Fragments ternaires compris (OUI/non, actif/inactif, ÉCHEC, BORNE/BUREAU,
lecture seule, protégé en écriture). Unités Ko/Mo → KB/MB, « %lld o » → « %lld B ».

Ce qui ne bouge PAS, pour ne rien casser en aval : étiquettes de journal, noms
d'options, spécificateurs de format, champs de trace. La CI ne greppe que

events.title: fix: mouse hit-testing on HiDPI/letterboxed windows (MacBook Pro report)
events.message:
fix: mouse hit-testing on HiDPI/letterboxed windows (MacBook Pro report)

The window-to-canvas mapping computed its scale from logical window
points and never floored to an integer, while renderer_present scales in
output pixels and floors the 320x200/320x256 game canvas. The two agreed
only when the window was an exact integer multiple of the canvas, so at
scale 3 and fullscreen 16:10 the mouse worked, but on an external
monitor, an odd --resolution, or a resized window they diverged and
clicks landed off-target or were rejected. This is why the holomap,
orbit, and landing navigation controls could not be clicked.

Extract the presentation transform into one SDL-free renderer_map_point()
used by both renderer_present() and the mouse mapping, so draw and
hit-test can never drift. Route the main.c mouse helpers (holamap, orbit,
navigation key/action) through renderer_window_to_canvas(). Add
tests/test_renderer_map.c covering Retina/HiDPI, letterbox with
fractional integer scaling, the launcher canvas, and widescreen
pillar-boxing; the Retina case fails against the old points-based math.

All 63 tests pass.

events.title: platform: cache dsp_detect — every palette write was leaking a VDI workstation
events.message:
platform: cache dsp_detect — every palette write was leaking a VDI workstation

The NovaGPU menu hotkey letters paint correctly once and go black on the next
redraw. DBGNOVAT.LOG says why, and it is not the palette.

qd_set_palette() calls dsp_detect() on EVERY palette write. On the Nova path
that reaches dsp_backend_nova(), which calls nova_open_ws() — appl_init +
v_opnvwk — and on success deliberately returns with the workstation still OPEN
for init()/shutdown(). Nothing closed the previous one and nova_open_ws
overwrites s_handle unconditionally, so each palette write leaked one VDI
virtual workstation AND one AES application slot.

The field log shows the shape exactly: "nova: card width = 640" (a detect-only
line) appears 12 times during boot, the twelfth landing on the same line as
"menu: modal up". So the menu's first paint happens right as VDI runs out of
handles. After that v_opnvwk fails, s_handle goes to 0, vs_color writes to
nothing, and dsp_detect starts handing back the ST/STe backend instead of Nova
— the next redraw resolves its colours against a CLUT nobody is updating any
more. Correct once, black afterwards, and Nova-only because no other backend
allocates anything in its probe.

Fix: cache the result. dsp_detect answers a hardware question that cannot
change while we run, so answering it once is also just correct — and it drops a
per-palette-write probe from every Atari backend, not only Nova. Plus a
belt-and-braces guard in dsp_backend_nova: an already-open workstation is the
normal steady state on this path, so reuse it rather than stacking another.

Verified: Falcon char-gen frame md5-IDENTICAL, Mega STe 4MB boots to the menu
with the hotkey letters intact. 469 passed, 6 skipped.

NOT verified on the card — Nova cannot be exercised under Hatari (dsp_detect
returns VIDEL on _VDO==3 before the probe, and the probe needs an 8-plane VDI
screen while Hatari's --vdi-planes tops out at 4). The check on hardware is
DBG.LOG: "nova: card width" should now appear exactly ONCE, not twelve times.
