events.title: joust/recreate: the four giants — 65/75
events.message:
joust/recreate: the four giants — 65/75

update_objects, render_object_body (+ its two entry aliases), collision_check
and wave_manager: ~7,700 bytes, the densest code in the game. One agent each,
in parallel on disjoint files, then a consolidation pass.

Two errors in decomp.c's own inventory, both confirmed from the bytes
- update_objects runs 0x12014..0x12605 = 1522 bytes, not 1512. The inventory's
  figure ends INSIDE the neg.w at 0x125fa.
- wave_manager is TWO NON-CONTIGUOUS CHUNKS: 0x1783c..0x17e79 (1598 B) and
  0x17012..0x17437 (1062 B), the second reached only by the beq.w at 0x178a0 and
  ending in its own rts. 1598+1062 = the 2660 the inventory counts, and a linear
  sweep cannot see the split. Review confirmed it independently: exactly one
  branch in the whole image targets 0x7012, and no relocated pointer does. The
  64 bytes at 0x17e7a are not padding — two relocated pointers from inside the
  egg scatter point into them; it is that scatter's scratch list.

Flag bit 12 is now exercised, from both readers
It was set and tested only in unported code, so the differential had never
touched it. render_object_body's site turns out to select between two EXACTLY
INVERTED mappings of drift direction onto draw_half_select — bit clear keeps the
leading cell when drifting left, set keeps the wrap column. All four leaves are
driven, asserted off the ORACLE's final image so a case that missed the branch
fails, and paired with a proof the bit is inert away from the edge.
update_objects' latch needed its own guard: without test_removed_beats_a_
surviving_egg, deleting the bit-12 TEST just latches the bit one instruction
later onto the same tail, and every other case would still pass.

Handshakes between separately-ported functions, now confirmed at both ends
- effect_table really is (old AND NOT new), and the kinds are 1-BASED — which is
  exactly why dissolve_platforms indexes platform_sprites one record low.
- collision_check's dismount sets the egg's spawn flags: the victim's type bits
  bumped one and capped at 3, so each hatched generation comes back tougher,
  plus bit 7, the "never drawn" flag update_egg_draw reads to skip the erase.

Things the original does that a reconstruction would get wrong
- 0x13e6a is start_death_anim INLINED MINUS its clr.b OBJ_EGG_CHAIN, so a player
  killed by a pterodactyl KEEPS the chain a joust-loss clears. A reconstruction
  that simply called the verified start_death_anim would pass the obvious
  assertion, so both halves are pinned.
- wave_manager scatters EGGS by spending the same three type counts the rider
  loops read, leaving them at -1 — that is the entire mechanism by which an egg
  wave has no riders. The old comment omitted it.
- The gladiator bounty is announced and never paid; type 2's facing test is
  inverted relative to types 1 and 3; the survival banner is recoloured AFTER
  score_update returns, legal only because score_update preserves a0.
- Three dead sites reproduced or documented: the tail at 0x12546 (no branch in
  the image targets it), cmpa.l #enemy_objects at 0x1320c (no branch consumes
  its condition codes), movea.l (a7),a0 at 0x13c76 (clobbered before any read).

Coverage, measured by the reviewer rather than reported
  collision_check     383/383 instructions
  render family       573/573
  wave_manager        278/278 + 223/223
  update_objects      366/369 — the 3 misses are exactly the dead tail
Mutation sweeps: 40/40, 29/29, 14/14, 16/16, plus 4 independent spot-checks.

Two tests that could not fail, both found and fixed
- test_poison_would_test_a_different_function asserted the poisoned run stores a
  different flags word — but poison inverts every oracle-written byte including
  that word, so it was satisfied by construction. Rewritten to compare executed-
  PC sets via the oracle's coverage bitset, and proved able to fail by making
  both runs take the same path.
- Three of four fuzz batteries had no `assert ran`, so zeroing the case count
  reported 8/4/6 green tests while 320/240/240 randomized cases silently stopped
  running. Proved by zeroing one and watching all 8 fail.

poison is unsound wherever output steers control flow — measured every time
render: prev_dst is a screen POINTER dereferenced next frame, so a poisoned one
is a wild address and the candidate takes SIGBUS. objects: rng_ptr is rewritten
every slot and read back two instructions later. collide: inverting the flags
word raises OBJ_FLAG_RESPAWN and 7 of 8 probed shapes then wrote nothing at all.
wave: the bytes written ARE next pass's branch selectors. Kept on exactly one
case across all four files, where the written bytes steer nothing.

Consolidation
17 constants hoisted to addrs.h / object.h / joust.h and 6 object-record bits
given one spelling each, chosen from instruction evidence — bit 5 is
CORPSE_INSIDE because its set condition is purely positional, bit 6 is WINGS_UP
because both tails TOGGLE it, bit 11/10 are FLAP_REQUEST/FLAP_TAKEN because bit
10 only makes sense as "already acted on". No value changed.

Verified (all four run by the committer)
  projects/joust/recreate     3776 passed  (was 2326)
  tools/recreate_kit            44 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged)

Remaining 10: the init/title chain (_start, init_system, init_game, init_video,
title_screen), check_highscore, read_joysticks, update_pterodactyl and the two
palette routines. Tracked: a third set of two-names-one-bit collisions, which
the name-keyed duplicate pin cannot see by construction — an address-keyed pin
would close the whole class.

events.title: recreate_kit: close the one-sided os_* refusal, a false-green class
events.message:
recreate_kit: close the one-sided os_* refusal, a false-green class

Deleting the Bconstat gate from Joust's CANDIDATE left all 2325 tests green.
os_bconin with nothing pending returned 0 and touched neither its out-param nor
the image, so the candidate behaved identically whether or not it checked —
while the identical call on the ORACLE side set g_unmodeled and rejected the
run. The refusal was one-sided, and it was a class, not one gate: every os_*
helper whose unmodeled answer the candidate discards was a silent candidate-side
no-op. So a reconstruction could DROP a guard the original has and stay green,
because the oracle refuses to run that case at all.

That mattered now rather than later: the Joust init/title chain is next and is
exactly the trap-heavy code the hole affects.

The fix
- os.h routes every sentinel through os_refused(sentinel), which tallies AND
  returns it unchanged, so a helper structurally cannot do one without the other.
- The counter lives in src/os_refusal.c, swept into every candidate the way
  dosound_log.c already is; harness.differential() resets before each candidate
  run and raises on a non-zero count, with a message that says why a clean diff
  proves nothing rather than merely that it happened.
- Builds that must not tally define OS_NO_REFUSAL_TALLY and get a no-op inline.
  shim.c does. Named for what it selects rather than OS_ORACLE, because
  on-target Atari builds need the same no-op and should not have to claim to be
  the oracle. Runtime selection was never possible — same header, different
  binaries. A Joust on-target .PRG will need the define; documented.

Two subtleties
- os_fcreate refuses THROUGH os_fopen, so it must not tally twice. Pinned:
  delta 1, never 2.
- os_crawio must NOT tally an idle console — that is a legitimate result for a
  non-blocking read, not a refusal. os_bconin was split so both share the
  non-refusing core.
Both restructured helpers were proved behaviour-identical to the old code
exhaustively: all 65536 opcodes x 9 D0 values for os_gem_trap, and every
device x pending x char combination for os_bconin/os_crawio. Zero differences.

Proof in both directions
- It fires: deleting Joust's Bconstat gate now fails
  test_poll_quit_key_no_key_returns_at_once and
  test_hiscore_key_input_no_key_returns_at_once, by name.
- It does not false-positive: all four suites green from forced rebuilds.
- BuggyBoy did NOT move (292 / 732), so nothing there was relying on the hole.
- Honest caveat: the os_fopen shape is caught wherever a case REACHES the call
  (built by hand: 0 byte diffs with the tally off, raise with it on), but no
  case in the suite reaches it — every quit case stages HIGH.SCO. The tally
  closes the class; it does not invent the case. An earlier draft of this
  message claimed both deletions fail by name; that was an overclaim.

What the review caught in the fix itself
- The poison re-run was uncovered. _attribution_check calls the glue a SECOND
  time, and a refusal reached only on the poisoned image was tallied into a
  count nobody read. Now reset and vetted on both runs. General lesson: a
  per-run ledger must be reset and checked on every run, and differential() has
  two.
- The ABI probe failed open. It had copied the Dosound ledger's optional
  hasattr shape — correct there, because Dosound has an oracle-side witness for
  when the ledger was needed. The refusal tally structurally cannot have one, so
  a missing symbol would mean silently no checking forever. Now a hard import
  requirement.
- No test drove a real os.h refusal: the first pin called os_refused directly,
  so reverting any of the 11 call sites stayed green. Now test/os_refusal_probe.c
  + test_os_refusal.py, 31 pins — one per branch, each refusal AND each served
  call — verified non-vacuous by reverting os_fclose's site.

TRAP_MODEL.md also records four gaps the input layer found and never wrote down
- A poked constant only survives if the routine does not initialise it first
  (both Joust IKBD routines clr.l ikbd_packet before waiting).
- The Fopen->Fcreate fallback is unreachable by construction.
- Pterm does not simply stop the run: the pushed selector lands ON the sentinel
  long (00 00 00 02 -> 00 4c 00 00) and emu.run tests `reached` before the
  unmodeled causes, so the message is "did not reach rts", not the honest one.
  Verified empirically rather than taken on trust.
- Model writes bypass logw, so poison never attribution-checks them.

Verified (all four run by the committer)
  projects/joust/recreate     2326 passed  (2325 + one new pin)
  tools/recreate_kit            44 passed  (13 + 31 refusal-branch pins)
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged)

Known, tracked: render/atari/build.sh does not link (g_load_graphics,
g_xbios_setpalette, g_dosound). None of its cores includes os.h so this is not
from here, but no test gate covers that script — worth confirming against an
older commit.

Nine functions across three parallel batches: the two the sound layer unblocked,
the egg subsystem, and player control.

Unblocked (4)  score_update, score_update_p1, score_update_p2, lava_troll
Egg (3)        update_eggs, update_egg_draw, update_egg_physics
Player (2)     control_player, player_death

A name that meant two different bits
OBJ_FLAG_REMOVED was (1u << 12) in world.h and (1u << 13) in egg.h — same name,
different values. Invisible to the constant pin (it scraped only integer
literals, not the shift form) AND to the compiler, since no translation unit
includes both headers. The disassembly settled it: TWO GENUINELY DIFFERENT BITS
are in play, so the defect was the shared NAME, not either value.
  bit 13 = dead, i.e. not a live rider on the playfield. Set by a death
    (0x14098/0x13ac8/0x13e72) AND by the egg hatch (0x1277e); cleared when the
    rider is placed (0x1252a/0x11f60); tested at 12 sites.
  bit 12 = removed, on its way off the board. Set at 0x124ac, tested at 0x12438
    and 0x12faa — a bit names.txt did not document at all.
  start_death_anim sets both, hence its 0x3000.
Both reconstructions were byte-correct against their own disassembly, so the
differential had nothing to catch. This was found by an agent noticing that two
headers it could not both include disagreed — no test could have seen it.
The scraper now reads the (1u << N) form: 7 previously-invisible constants, no
pre-existing drift, and three pins that were impossible before — including one
whose comment had said only literal-spelled flags could be pinned. That comment
is deleted, not amended.

The egg subsystem has exactly one rts
0x1261e, the loop running out of slots. update_egg_physics's edge branch does
`adda.w #$4,a7 ; bra.w 0x1285c` — it discards its own bsr return address, so A7
BALANCES and the loop's rts returns to update_eggs' caller on physics' behalf.
Entering at 0x12606 therefore always returns normally and NO checkpoint is
needed anywhere in the file. Entered standalone at 0x12a2a the edge branch pops
one longword past emu.STACK_TOP, so a second sentinel is poked there — inside
the guard band the diff already excludes. The two exits are distinguished
explicitly: a negative (without that sentinel the run cannot reach rts) paired
with a positive (draw_dst present in / absent from the oracle's write set).

Checkpointed, with what each does NOT prove written down
control_player's restart path is checkpointed at 0x11e44, the first of three
unported calls: it proves both guards route there and that game_over_flag := 1
is the only write on that side, and nothing past it. Its tail (0x11e50) is
verified separately at its own entry and deliberately NOT called from
control_player, since check_highscore and init_game sit between them. Every
checkpoint is PAIRED with a never-returns proof — which is what caught one such
pair being staged with no registers, so D0 was 0, the run returned immediately,
and the "proof" was asserting nothing.

Original bugs reproduced, not smoothed
- lava_troll's respawn/in-lava drop has TWO DEAD STORES: `clr.w troll_state` is
  overwritten by the tail's `move.w d0,troll_state`, so the hand stays flagged
  out and the NEXT call retracts it.
- A carry out of the score's leftmost digit lands on +0x3d — the colour byte of
  the string's own control pair, so an eight-digit score recolours its HUD row.
- player_death with all 24 message slots taken writes its 12-byte banner record
  over addresses 0..0xb, the bottom of the vector page.
- draw_lives(enemy) still draws player 1's row; both bodies reload A0.

Corrections to existing documentation
- platform_edge_table's push bytes were documented BACKWARDS: +8 is the vertical
  response, +9 the horizontal.
- egg_sprite_ptrs is a JUMP TABLE {sprite.l, handler.l} entered via jmp (a2),
  not a sprite table. Records 3, 24 and 31 are all zero and would jmp 0; none is
  reachable from a state the game writes.
- The score's units digit is held at '0' at four sites, which is why the
  promotion sweep stops one short of it — so `addq.b #5,67(a0)` is 50 points,
  not 500. start_death_anim's comment corrected.

poison is unsound where output steers control flow
Measured, not assumed: control_player writes the flags word it branches on, and
poisoning FLAG_ON_PLATFORM sets bit 13, sending the attribution re-run through
hover_dead_rider instead of steer_rider. poison is now kept only where the
written bytes steer nothing, with the reason named at each site. Second sighting
of this limit — draw_string was the first.

Coverage
44 mutations on the egg subsystem (40 caught, 4 honestly unpinned with the
reason at the site — including one the game's own data cannot reach, where
fabricating a platform record was declined); 13 + 21 on score/troll; 38 on
player across two sweeps. Several sweeps found real holes: a promotion test that
never reached its bound, a flap-toggle case unreachable from a set start state,
and a mutant caught only by fuzz until a named test was added.

Verified (all four run by the committer, not taken from a report)
  projects/joust/recreate     2325 passed  (was 1645)
  tools/recreate_kit            13 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged)

Remaining 16 are the four giants (wave_manager 2660, render_object_body 2232,
collision_check 1712, update_objects 1512), the init/title chain, check_highscore
and read_joysticks. Bit 12 stays unexercised by the differential until
update_objects and render_object_body land — both its readers live there.

events.title: joust/recreate: sound and input — 50/75, and the trap model's first real test
events.message:
joust/recreate: sound and input — 50/75, and the trap model's first real test

Takes Joust from 44/75 to 50/75. These six are the FIRST reconstructions to run
real game code through the TOS trap model added in 3a09f1b. The model held —
nothing forced a workaround and the kit was not touched — and it produced a
precise map of its own edges, which is worth as much as the functions.

Sound (3)   play_sound  snd_poll_done  snd_tone_sweep
Input (3)   poll_quit_key  hiscore_key_input  hiscore_joystick_input

play_sound existed only as a `static` copy inside object.c, cloned when
ptero_spot_player needed it. The real one is now exported from sound.h and the
copy is gone, which UNBLOCKS score_update x3 and lava_troll.

The false-green class this batch found
Deleting the Bconstat gate from the CANDIDATE leaves all 1644 tests green.
os_bconin with nothing pending returns 0 and touches neither the out-param nor
the image, while the identical call sets g_unmodeled on the ORACLE side and
rejects the run. The refusal is one-sided. Reproduced independently in review,
and it is a general class, not one gate: every os_* helper whose unmodeled
answer the candidate discards behaves this way — os_fopen on an unstaged name is
the second instance. So a reconstruction can DROP a guard the original has and
stay green, because the oracle refuses to run the case at all. init_system and
title_screen are both unported and both trap-heavy; the warning is now in
input.c's header rather than only in a task. Closing it needs a candidate-side
tally in the kit, tracked separately.

Where the differential cannot reach, pin against the original's machine code
snd_tone_sweep's loop start values are (mostly) unobservable: every pass rewrites
the same registers and both bge loops end below zero whatever they started at.
Rather than call them verified they are pinned against the shipped binary's own
instruction encodings at 0x10980/0x10988 — opcode, immediate AND target address.
Review then corrected the claim in the useful direction: the differential DOES
pin the pitch start's parity and sign (residue 0xfffe vs 0xffff), so only the
magnitude among non-negative even values needs the encoding pin. An overstated
limitation is as harmful as a hidden one — someone trusting "nothing reaches
this" deletes the sole pin in a tidy-up.

Verified with limits, stated rather than implied
- snd_tone_sweep: the intra-pass ORDER of its 7 register writes is invisible
  (Giaccess is modelled as a register file, not an ordered ledger, unlike
  Dosound). Shipped order checked by hand at 0x10990..0x10a3a.
- hiscore_joystick_input is verified FROM 0x1454e only. The routine clears
  ikbd_packet before waiting, so HARNESS.md's state-level poking cannot survive
  it — a poked constant only helps if the routine does not initialise it first.
  The prologue and the blocking wait are not verified and cannot be.
- poll_quit_key's P/p pause needs a SECOND keystroke; the console model delivers
  one per run, so its loop is verified separately entered at 0x11d64. Its
  Fopen->Fcreate fallback is unreachable by construction (os_fcreate = os_fopen +
  truncate) and is reproduced unverified.
- read_joysticks stays BLOCKED, twice over: the same IKBD wait, and a body that
  is nothing but two calls to the unported control_player. A checkpoint would
  prove one clr.l and leave a function called read_joysticks that reads no
  joysticks.

Technique worth reusing
- Every stop_pc test is PAIRED with a proof the run does not reach rts — a
  checkpoint run that fell through would stop at the sentinel and pass silently.
- Five quit-path traps change no memory, so a 9-call battery checkpoints past
  each one's stack cleanup and reads the pushed arguments back out of the
  oracle's write set. Same shape as the BuggyBoy real-hardware palette bug, where
  the harness confirmed THAT Setpalette was called but never WHICH palette.
- A glue may refuse a call the original makes: g_pause_until_key probes once and
  returns a sentinel rather than entering an unbounded spin, keeping the
  reconstruction itself uncapped and faithful. New convention, in the README.

68000 gotcha, second sighting
bge/bgt/blt after subq test N==V, so 0x8000-1 = 0x7fff and 0x80-1 = 0x7f both
read NEGATIVE. The first cut used (int16_t)result >= 0 and the differential
caught it at cursor 0x8000. Modelled as subq_condition() at two sites; the world
layer's flame rollover was the same trap.

names.txt
Six globals the input layer introduced had no var line, so harness.label() would
have reported a divergence at 0x10d20 as `saved_joyvec+4` — misattributing the
saved-resolution word in the very diff meant to localise it. Added, with
ikbd_cmd_mouse_rel noted as the data byte a linear sweep renders as `move.b d0,d2`.

Verified (all four run by the committer, not taken from a report)
  projects/joust/recreate     1645 passed  (was 1058)
  tools/recreate_kit            13 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged)
Mutation: 15/15 sound, 25/28 input (3 shown equivalent under the model), plus 4
independent spot-checks in review.

events.title: joust/recreate: 16 more functions, and the last inferred names discharged
events.message:
joust/recreate: 16 more functions, and the last inferred names discharged

Takes Joust from 28/75 to 44/75. Two batches again ran in parallel on disjoint
files (src/score.c and src/world.c with their own headers and tests), preceded
by a dedup pass so the two new headers land on a clean base rather than making
the duplication 4-way.

Scoring / lives / messages / hiscore (8)
  find_free_message  draw_messages  draw_lives  draw_lives_p1  draw_lives_p2
  flash_hiscore_color  draw_hiscore_cursor  draw_hiscore_entry

World / platforms / troll (8)
  draw_platforms  flash_spawn_pad  start_death_anim  troll_erase_hand
  troll_draw_hand  dissolve_platforms  raise_floor  animate_ground_shrink

No name in this project is inferred any more
Both remaining `# ctx` tags are discharged by reconstructing the routine and
rendering its sprite data. One name held, one did not:
- animate_ground_shrink HOLDS. 0x18636/0x187e6 are lava flames — four 18-row
  frames 0xd8 apart, colours 3/7/8/9. One creeps right, one left, and on wave 3
  ground_x0/ground_x1 close in one pixel per step behind them, so the ground
  narrows from both ends with a flame at each retreating edge.
- draw_spawn_sparkle DOES NOT. 0x1194c is a solid tapering trapezoid (30/26/22)
  painted in a flat cycled colour, and for ALL FOUR spawn points it lands exactly
  on the colour-4 pad (30/28/24) already baked into that platform's own bitmap:
  x = 67/9/38/27 = cells*16 + shift. Corroborated by the spawn record's own
  +12/+10/+18 fields. It repaints the pad while a rider materialises, one pixel
  inside it. Renamed **flash_spawn_pad**; independently re-derived before applying,
  because a names.txt rename steers every future reader.

Two names.txt comments were wrong, and one name was wrong while UNTAGGED
- dissolve_platforms' sprite base is 0x119c4, not 0x119c8: EFF_KIND is 1-BASED,
  so the base sits one record below platform_sprites, sign-extended from 16 bits.
- raise_floor does not paint "the two halves" of the exposed row. paint_floor_row
  leaves a1 advanced 0x28 and the caller adds 0x50, so the strips are cells 0-4
  and 15-19 — the lava either side of the ground platform, overlapping it by one
  cell at each end.
- 0x10d66 was `bytes_per_row`, recorded as CONFIRMED. It is a byte countdown:
  move.b #$28 at init, subq.b #1 in animate_ground_shrink, reset to #$3. An ST
  row pitch is 0xa0, a word, and is never decremented. Now ground_anim_timer.
  Caught only because the world layer needed the address and named it
  independently — the `# ctx` tag tracks names we know are uncertain, not the
  ones we are confidently wrong about.

Behaviour that had to be modelled exactly
- draw_lives IGNORES its argument: it dispatches on a full cmpa.l against
  player2, but both bodies reload A0 from a constant, so draw_lives(enemy) draws
  player 1's row. Honouring the parameter would read better and be wrong.
- draw_messages draws an expired message once more in colour 0 — that final draw
  IS the erase. Skipping it cleanly leaves the pixels on screen.
- animate_ground_shrink's two flames are NOT symmetric: the right rolls over on
  subq.w + bge (N==V, the sign of the true difference, so phase 0x8000 rolls over
  though the stored 0x7fff looks positive); the left uses addq.w plus a separate
  cmpi.w, where the wrapped value decides. The first reconstruction had this
  backwards.
- flash_hiscore_color's Setcolor is off-image, so the reconstruction returns the
  colour word and the test compares it against the argument the original pushed.

Coverage
- Mutation-swept: 29/29 on the scoring layer, 26 on the world layer (23 killed,
  2 provably equivalent, 1 a real hole where a uniform screen fill made all four
  bitplanes identical), plus 6 spot-checks in review.
- Four world batteries never varied screen_base, so a reconstruction that
  hard-coded 0x70000 would have passed them. Closed and proven: hard-coding the
  base now fails exactly one named test per battery.
- The dedup landed a structural guard — test_no_constant_is_defined_in_two_files
  globs include/*.h + src/*.c, so the 9-constant duplication cannot silently
  return. It needs no exclusion list: the scraper requires an integer literal, so
  include guards fall out for free. Its blind spot (expression-valued macros) is
  stated in the docstring, not glossed.

Blocked, and recorded as blocked rather than pending
score_update x3 and lava_troll need play_sound, which exists only as a `static`
duplicate inside object.c; wave_manager needs find_free_message x20 plus the
score_update pair; check_highscore needs the input pair AND never returns
(0x448e -> 0x44ae -> 0x448e), so it will need a stop_pc checkpoint. Four of the
six unblock together with the sound layer.

Verified (all four run by the committer, not taken from a report)
  projects/joust/recreate     1058 passed  (was 610)
  tools/recreate_kit            13 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged; one pre-existing 1-in-8
    xdist flake in test_composed_frame, A/B-confirmed at HEAD, tracked)

events.title: joust/recreate: 20 gameplay functions — drawing and object layers
events.message:
joust/recreate: 20 gameplay functions — drawing and object layers

Takes Joust from 8/75 to 28/75. Two batches run in parallel with disjoint file
ownership (src/draw.c + include/draw.h + test/test_draw.py, and the object
equivalents), so neither could clobber the other; names.txt and STATUS.md were
withheld from both agents and integrated here, which is why they move in this
commit rather than theirs.

Drawing layer (11)
  fill_screen  draw_string  select_sprite_base  blit_pattern_rows
  draw_object_data  draw_object_mask  blit_mask_wide  blit_sprite_planes
  paint_floor_row  blit_sprite_mask  blit_sprite

Object / physics / collision (9)
  test_overlap  pixel_collision  joust_bounce  check_platform
  erase_egg_sprite  draw_egg_sprite  ptero_avoid_platform  ptero_spot_player
  count_objects_and_pad

Faithful to the original, deliberately
- fill_screen writes 4001 cells of 8 bytes = 32008 bytes from screen_base — EIGHT
  PAST the 32000-byte framebuffer, on every call. Confirmed from the instruction
  stream (`move.l #$fa0,d3` + dbf), reproduced rather than clamped.
- draw_object_data and draw_egg_sprite: stopping on row 0 leaves draw_rows = 0,
  which the wrap pass's subq.b reads as 256, so it marches 256 scanlines down.
- ptero_spot_player's `cmpi.w #$ff29` is provably dead — every value it rejects
  is already rejected by the later signed `ble #$8`. Kept as shipped.
- count_objects_and_pad's between-wave walk follows the message's SCREEN pointer
  (+4), not its string pointer, so it counts screen bytes to the first zero.

Behaviour the reconstructions had to model exactly
- draw_object_data re-reads playfield_bottom EVERY row, and computes its
  lava-exit row count as a FRESH read of draw_rows minus the counter
  (sub.b/neg.b) — not from a loop index. Both are observable when a sprite is
  drawn over those globals.
- blit_sprite_planes runs three passes per row (middle, leading, trailing) and
  RE-READS the trailing cell's four source words after the first two have
  written. Only observable at shift >= 9.
- test_overlap's y-band test is `add.b`, so y's low byte wraps instead of
  carrying; its column offset comes from `divu.w #$a0` including the overflow
  case where the 68000 leaves the destination untouched.
- ptero_avoid_platform writes only D1's LOW word, so the high half returns the
  caller's value on the clear exits and the divu remainder on a hit.

Both drafts were wrong, which is the argument for the harness
The two batches were seeded from drafts left by agents killed mid-work. Neither
draft had ever produced a green run, and both were broken:
- object.c's egg row stride compensated for a pointer advance that never
  happened (the blit takes dst/src by value) — 23 failing tests. A test bug
  (`sum(1 << rng.randrange(16))` instead of OR) meant the fuzz batteries had
  never once run.
- draw.c interleaved reads with writes in blit_sprite_planes' trailing pass and
  hoisted draw_object_data's per-row re-read. Notably the first test written for
  the ordering bug PASSED against the broken code, because it used shift 6.

Coverage is pinned, not asserted
- Mutation-swept: 78 mutations on the object layer (72 killed, 6 analysed as
  provably equivalent mutants and documented); 17 on the drawing layer; 11 more
  on the read-once guarantees, each failing a NAMED test.
- Four routines claimed "every field is read once, before the loop" with nothing
  pinning it — re-reading per row passed all 600 tests. Now pinned by aiming the
  destination at the record itself (blit_mask_wide, blit_sprite_planes, and both
  ground blits).
- test_draw.py had no constant pin, and drift there is invisible to a
  differential by construction: staged inputs land in dead memory, both cores
  agree on the game's own static data, and the suite goes green proving nothing.
  Demonstrated — SPRITE_WRAP_X 0x130->0x140 and A_DRAW_HALF_SELECT +2 each passed
  301 tests silently; the latter collapsed all 7 half_select cases into one,
  leaving two branches untested while reporting coverage. Both now fail a named
  test. test_constants.py's docstring claimed to cover "every address a test
  enters the oracle at", which had become false; narrowed to what it checks.

Verified (all four run by the committer, not taken from a report)
  projects/joust/recreate      610 passed  (was 143)
  tools/recreate_kit            13 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged)

Deferred (tracked): update_egg_physics needs the whole egg subsystem — it
discards its return address and tail-jumps into update_egg_draw, which jumps
back into update_eggs; draw.h and object.h duplicate ~9 constants (all values
verified identical, no TU includes both) as the cost of the parallel split.

events.title: recreate_kit: model the seven TOS traps Joust needs
events.message:
recreate_kit: model the seven TOS traps Joust needs

Joust's sound, input and high-score-save layers were gated on traps the shared
model did not service. Adds GEMDOS Super/Fcreate/Fwrite, XBIOS Giaccess/Random
and BIOS Bconstat/Bconin (the whole trap #13 arm was unmodelled), following
HARNESS.md's rule: model hardware at the STATE level as harness-poked constants,
never at the live-input level, since the candidate is pure C with no analogue.

The contract is preserved throughout: refuse rather than fabricate. Fwrite past
its reservation raises instead of inventing a short count; Fcreate of an
undeclared file raises instead of inventing a staging address; Bconin with no
key pending raises instead of returning a plausible zero. Pterm and Dgetdrv were
found in the census and deliberately left raising — Pterm never returns, so
there is no post-state to diff, and Dgetdrv asks about a machine we do not have.

Design choices, each with its limit recorded in TRAP_MODEL.md
- Super is a token cookie, decided by reading all six call sites: three discard
  the return value, one round-trips it verbatim, and the floppy routine tests
  the S bit itself. An S-bit flip would perturb A7 and the stack guard for no
  observable gain. Consequence stated plainly: `move sr` reads S=1 all run, so
  Joust's three floppy Super sites are unreachable under the oracle.
- Giaccess gets an in-image register file fed by Giaccess only. Feeding it from
  the direct $ff8800 writes as well would have broken BuggyBoy outright — its
  g_REFRESH emits the PSG stream into out-params, not memory, so oracle-side
  image writes would fail every test_refresh_* for reasons unrelated to any
  reconstruction. Instead a guard REFUSES any run touching both paths; Joust
  genuinely uses both (Giaccess x10 for sound, a direct drive-select at
  0x1553c), so the guard is live, not theoretical.
- Random is a poked 24-bit input, not a generator: one call site, consumed as
  `andi.l #$fe,d0`, and a program looping for a different value blows the
  instruction cap and raises rather than producing a wrong image.
- Bconin CONSUMES the key rather than latching it — Joust's consumers are
  per-frame loops, and a latched key would make every frame re-read the same
  letter, which no real run does.

Hardening found along the way
- A direct $ff8800 READ was served as a fabricated 0 — the contract's own
  forbidden case, live in Joust's drive-select, where it zeroes port A's
  preserved upper bits. Now refuses. BuggyBoy never reads the ports (its driver
  is lea + move.b/clr.b, and Musashi's clr emits no dummy read), so this costs
  nothing there.
- The PSG guard tapped only byte accesses, so a word/long write would touch the
  chip untallied and silently disarm it. All six callbacks now tally, across the
  whole $ff8800..$ff88ff block rather than the 4-byte pair — a mirror at
  $ff8804 or an odd alias at $ff8801 was the identical vector.
- os_fread/os_fwrite bounded `count` but not `buf`: Fwrite(6, 4, 0xfffffff0) was
  SERVED, memcpying ~4 GiB outside the image. Both pointers and staging+cursor
  are now bounded, subtraction-form.
- g_psg_latch leaked across runs, so a run whose first PSG touch was a bare data
  write inherited the previous run's register selection — order-dependent under
  -n auto. Reset per run. (Pre-existing; folded in because it is a cross-run
  state leak in code two games now share.)
- Crawio was a second, contradictory console model. Unified — and it must honour
  Crawio's direction word, since only w==0xff reads and anything else writes, so
  a program printing a character would have eaten a keystroke Bconin was waiting
  for.

Recorded rather than left as a trap for later
- Joust's raw-floppy routine (0x152dc) is now UNVERIFIABLE: the direct PSG read
  is refused on its own, so no emu.run reaching 0x15544 can be green. Stated in
  TRAP_MODEL.md, the Joust README and STATUS.md, with a warning against
  "fixing" the rejection by narrowing the guard. It is not a row in STATUS.md's
  75-function table, so the 8/75 accounting is unchanged.

Verified (all four run by the committer, not taken from a report)
  projects/joust/recreate      143 passed
  tools/recreate_kit            13 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged)
Every guard is mutation-tested: disarm it and a named test fails. Two mutations
survived on first attempt (the 32-bit PSG write tap and the multi-cause
rejection path) because no test covered them; tests were added and both then
failed as required.

Deferred (tracked): the os_* helpers write g_mem directly, bypassing logw(), so
their bytes are absent from the oracle write-set and the poison pass does not
cover them; OS_SCREEN_BASE and OS_KBDVBASE are still unvetted.

  observable gain. Consequence stated plainly: `move sr` reads S=1 all run, so
  Joust's three floppy Super sites are unreachable under the oracle.
- Giaccess gets an in-image register file fed by Giaccess only. Feeding it from
  the direct $ff8800 writes as well would have broken BuggyBoy outright — its
  g_REFRESH emits the PSG stream into out-params, not memory, so oracle-side
  image writes would fail every test_refresh_* for reasons unrelated to any
  reconstruction. Instead a guard REFUSES any run touching both paths; Joust
  genuinely uses both (Giaccess x10 for sound, a direct drive-select at
  0x1553c), so the guard is live, not theoretical.
- Random is a poked 24-bit input, not a generator: one call site, consumed as
  `andi.l #$fe,d0`, and a program looping for a different value blows the
  instruction cap and raises rather than producing a wrong image.
- Bconin CONSUMES the key rather than latching it — Joust's consumers are
  per-frame loops, and a latched key would make every frame re-read the same
  letter, which no real run does.

Hardening found along the way
- A direct $ff8800 READ was served as a fabricated 0 — the contract's own
  forbidden case, live in Joust's drive-select, where it zeroes port A's
  preserved upper bits. Now refuses. BuggyBoy never reads the ports (its driver
  is lea + move.b/clr.b, and Musashi's clr emits no dummy read), so this costs
  nothing there.
- The PSG guard tapped only byte accesses, so a word/long write would touch the
  chip untallied and silently disarm it. All six callbacks now tally, across the
  whole $ff8800..$ff88ff block rather than the 4-byte pair — a mirror at
  $ff8804 or an odd alias at $ff8801 was the identical vector.
- os_fread/os_fwrite bounded `count` but not `buf`: Fwrite(6, 4, 0xfffffff0) was
  SERVED, memcpying ~4 GiB outside the image. Both pointers and staging+cursor
  are now bounded, subtraction-form.
- g_psg_latch leaked across runs, so a run whose first PSG touch was a bare data
  write inherited the previous run's register selection — order-dependent under
  -n auto. Reset per run. (Pre-existing; folded in because it is a cross-run
  state leak in code two games now share.)
- Crawio was a second, contradictory console model. Unified — and it must honour
  Crawio's direction word, since only w==0xff reads and anything else writes, so
  a program printing a character would have eaten a keystroke Bconin was waiting
  for.

Recorded rather than left as a trap for later
- Joust's raw-floppy routine (0x152dc) is now UNVERIFIABLE: the direct PSG read
  is refused on its own, so no emu.run reaching 0x15544 can be green. Stated in
  TRAP_MODEL.md, the Joust README and STATUS.md, with a warning against
  "fixing" the rejection by narrowing the guard. It is not a row in STATUS.md's
  75-function table, so the 8/75 accounting is unchanged.

Verified (all four run by the committer, not taken from a report)
  projects/joust/recreate      143 passed
  tools/recreate_kit            13 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate   292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster   732 passed  (unchanged)
Every guard is mutation-tested: disarm it and a named test fails. Two mutations
survived on first attempt (the 32-bit PSG write tap and the multi-cause
rejection path) because no test covered them; tests were added and both then
failed as required.

Deferred (tracked): the os_* helpers write g_mem directly, bypassing logw(), so
their bytes are absent from the oracle write-set and the poison pass does not
cover them; OS_SCREEN_BASE and OS_KBDVBASE are still unvetted.

events.title: Correct attribution and stale figures in the root README; link the C reconstruction
events.message:
Correct attribution and stale figures in the root README; link the C reconstruction

The two READMEs disagreed on who made the game -- the root said "Linel /
Software 2000", werner-c said "Bertelsmann Software / Rainbow Arts" -- so rather
than pick one, the manuals in this repo settle it. The German
Bedienungsanleitung cover reads "© 1987 ariolasoft GmbH", "Ein Unternehmen der
Bertelsmann AG", Carl-Bertelsmann-Str. 161, Gütersloh. Both files now say that,
and the year is given as © 1987 with a note that the disks are usually dated
1988. The binary itself carries no publisher string -- only Motorola FFP and
CP/M-68K library copyrights, which incidentally corroborate the Alcyon/DRI
toolchain.

The character attribution was wrong too: Werner is by Brösel (Rötger Feldmann),
published by Semmel Verlach, not Rolf Kauka / Bontje. The English manual's
back-page catalogue address is Semmel Verlach's.

Counts brought in line with the rest of the docs: 356 functions, of which 238
are the game's and 118 are library, and 264 of 273 globals named -- the root
README still claimed "~336 functions and ~230 global variables". The sound
section said "~30" register dump tables; there are exactly 36, at
0x274FC-0x27933, 30 bytes each.

Finally, the root README never mentioned werner-c/ at all, so the buildable C
reconstruction -- the largest artifact in the repo -- was invisible to anyone
landing on the front page. It now has its own section linking the sources and
their README.

events.title: Rename local variables to their C names
events.message:
Rename local variables to their C names

154 locals renamed across 106 functions, plus 43 that already matched, leaving
211 of 266 C locals (79%) present in the database.

Locals resist this less well than globals. Ghidra orders them by stack offset
while C declares them in source order, so declaration-order zip and difflib
line-alignment agree only 125/139 where both apply -- against 119/121 for the
globals. Where they disagreed, line-alignment won: it reads actual usage in
matched statements instead of assuming the two orderings coincide. On pmiles,
for instance, declaration order claims a=sVar1 while alignment shows a=sVar3.

34 mappings were dropped for colliding on the same Ghidra variable and 12
renames were rejected (8 stale names from a cached decompilation, 4 clashes
with a name already live in the function). Those keep Ghidra's names.

The displaced names are recorded per function in namemap.md, but unlike the
functions and globals they are not treated as irreplaceable: locals are
function-scoped and the C sources carry equivalent names at the same positions.

Note the plugin's parameter naming is inconsistent across endpoints --
rename_function_by_address takes snake_case (function_address, new_name),
rename_data takes newName, and rename_variable takes functionName/oldName/
newName. Worth knowing before scripting against it.

events.title: Rename 248 Ghidra globals to the C short names and reconcile types
events.message:
Rename 248 Ghidra globals to the C short names and reconcile types

Globals had no ready-made mapping the way functions did: the header's comments
describe them ("Getrez() screen resolution") rather than naming their Ghidra
counterpart. So each pairing was derived and cross-validated rather than looked
up -- by usage fingerprint (which functions reference it), by first-appearance
order within a function, and by difflib alignment of each C body against the
decompiled body. Where methods overlap they agree 119/121. Two globals where
they disagreed were dropped rather than guessed.

248 of 273 referenced globals are mapped. The 25 that are not are BSS scalars
referenced by identical sets of functions, which no available signal separates;
they keep their descriptive names and are listed in namemap.md.

Types were reconciled the same way the prototypes were -- Ghidra keeps the
richer type wherever it is ABI-identical: the GAME_STATUS enum on rover, and
long against the C's LONG (both four bytes on 68000). Nine genuine undefined2
scalars became short, and sfctmp went from undefined data to a defined,
labelled short.

Two things worth recording. The eight palettes are confirmed twice over:
data.c's definition order zips against ascending DATA addresses, and every
semantic name agrees independently (palneba -> NEBEL_FOG, palnebb ->
NEBEL_CLEAR). And DATA follows link order while BSS does not -- the initialised
tables run meiern -> bau -> auto -> panik, matching the translation units
recovered from TEXT, but BSS is interleaved, which is why the address-order walk
that works on TEXT cannot map it.

The binary itself has no DRI symbol table (SYMTAB=0), so no original names were
recoverable; namemap.md remains the only record of the descriptive ones.

events.title: Match Ghidra prototypes to the C sources and set the calling convention
events.message:
Match Ghidra prototypes to the C sources and set the calling convention

All 238 game functions now carry an explicit __stdcall convention -- Ghidra's
68000 name for the standard C convention (args right-to-left on the stack,
caller cleans, return in D0), which is what Alcyon emits. Two functions were
still on "default"; pascal, the other plausible entry, would have been wrong.

Prototypes were merged rather than overwritten, because the database held type
information the C dialect cannot express: VdiRasterOp and AtariST_Scancode
enums, and void * where Alcyon C has to write BYTE * for lack of a void type.
Overwriting those with the C spelling would have lost information for no gain,
so Ghidra's type wins wherever it is ABI-identical and more specific.

That left 16 real edits: six undefined returns and three undefined2 parameters
in bau.c, stileat's return narrowed from uint to the short it actually returns,
and eight param_1 placeholders given their C names. Verified afterwards: 238/238
__stdcall, zero remaining undefined, enums intact, decompilation clean.

Arity agreed for all 238 with no exceptions -- an independent check on the
reconstruction. LONG maps to Ghidra int rather than long (both four bytes on
68000), so those never disagreed either.

events.title: Remove the Python/SDL2 port, superseded by the C reconstruction
events.message:
Remove the Python/SDL2 port, superseded by the C reconstruction

The Python port (48 files, ~6300 lines) was the exploratory reimplementation
that mapped out the game's behaviour. werner-c now supersedes it: it is the
original C, compiled by the original Alcyon C 4.14 into a runnable
WERNER.PRG, with every data table read from the binary rather than inferred.

Worth recording why this is not a like-for-like loss. The reconstruction
showed the port had two palette bugs it could not have found on its own,
because it derived palettes from the PC1/SCH file headers while the game
actually uses tables in its DATA segment:

  - COLOR_TABLE_MENU differs from MENUE.PC1's own header at index 13
    (0x0667 vs 0x0067), so the menu rendered one colour wrong throughout.
  - COLOR_TABLE_NEBELFAHRT_A is flat 0x555 grey -- that table IS the fog.
    Nebelfahrt starts on it and "clears" by swapping palettes; sourcing from
    NEBEL1.PC1's header gives full colour immediately, so the port's fog
    effect was structurally wrong.

Also drops .claude/launch.json, which only launched the port's two servers.

The port remains in history if it is ever wanted back.

events.title: joust/recreate: differential reconstruction, first 8 functions
events.message:
joust/recreate: differential reconstruction, first 8 functions

Stands up projects/joust/recreate/ on the shared kit and verifies 8 pure leaf
functions byte-for-byte against the original 68000 code. Second game on the
harness, which is what turned the kit's BuggyBoy-shaped assumptions into real
defects worth fixing.

Verified (8/75)
  rng_advance  pos_to_screen  screen_to_pos  blit_copy  blit_or  blit_andnot
  make_fill_pattern  fill_pattern_n

Two of Joust's ABIs are invisible to a whole-image diff, so test/abi.py pokes a
68000 stub into free image space and enters the oracle there: a relocated A7
with a pre-poked return slot for the stack-frame routines, and a jsr + result
store for the register-return ones. Every case below is therefore a real
image comparison, not a register spot-check.

68000 semantics the differential caught (none visible in decompiled C)
- rng_advance's immediates are RELOCATED: `cmpi.l #$7832` is really #$17832 and
  `move.l #$0` is #$10000 — the fixups land on the instruction's immediate
  operand, not on a pointer in data. The compare is signed, so a cursor driven
  past 0x7fffffff never wraps.
- pos_to_screen folds both offsets with adda.w — low word, sign-extended — so
  from y=205 the screen address runs backwards.
- screen_to_pos's divu.w #$a0 can overflow (dividend >= 0xa00000); the 68000
  leaves the destination register untouched, so the routine silently carries
  the raw offset onward. Modelled in divu_w().
- The blitters count with subq.b (low byte only, 0 means 256); fill_pattern_n
  counts with subq.w (0 means 65536 cells = a 512 KiB fill).

Faithful to the original's bugs, deliberately
- screen_to_pos scales by mulu.w #$16 (22) where 16 is required — a radix slip
  in the 1985 original. It survives only because the function is unreferenced.
  Reproduced, pinned by name; a "corrected" version fails the differential.
- make_fill_pattern is degenerate in the shipped binary: four identical
  btst #0,d0 blocks, d2 cleared and never written. Confirmed original bytes —
  the depacker was exonerated by token trace and the mid-entry-alias theory
  disproved by reference search. All three fill_screen callers pass colour 0,
  so its only exercised behaviour is "clear to black".
- The blit glue re-reads cols from the caller's frame every row, as the original
  does (the row branch targets `move.w 12(a7),d0`); blit_rect keeps the hoisted
  form for real C callers and says so.

Kit hardening (shared — all of it surfaced only with a second game)
- GEMDOS Malloc is served from a fixed OS_HEAP_BASE = 0x20000, which lies INSIDE
  Joust's program (0x10000-0x2b7ae). Since the candidate mirrors the same
  constant by convention, a Malloc would have had both sides scribble the same
  bytes over the same program bytes and the differential would diff CLEAN — a
  false green. Joust is exempt (verified: 22 trap #1 sites, all with in-line
  3f3c selectors, no 0x48/0x4a at any alignment), but the exemption was a
  declaration in project.toml, so it is now enforced at runtime: shim.c counts
  serviced Mallocs and emu.run() refuses any run where one was served while
  OS_HEAP_BASE overlaps the program.
  Keyed on the overlap, not the flag, so it stays correct if OS_HEAP_BASE or a
  project's load_base later moves. For BuggyBoy the predicate is false
  (PROGRAM_END 0x1bcf8 < 0x20000) and it is a provable no-op.
  Two rounds of review were needed to get this right: the first version keyed on
  the heap POINTER MOVING, which Malloc(-1) and Malloc(0) defeat (size rounds to
  0, block still served at 0x20000) — and Malloc(-1) is the canonical GEMDOS
  largest-free-block query. The second lived in differential(), bypassed by ~27
  direct emu.run() callers including the poison pass, the one re-run that
  perturbs memory specifically to reach code the clean run never did.
- The Dosound ledger compare was blind past saturation: 300 vs 300 calls
  diverging at #257 compared two 256-entry truncations as equal. Now refused.
- tos_malloc_unused must be a real TOML boolean; "false" is truthy in Python and
  would have silently waived a safety check.
- The ledger implementation was duplicated in both games' src/os.c; hoisted to
  tools/recreate_kit/src/dosound_log.c with a shared OS_DOSOUND_LOG_MAX, so the
  oracle's cap and the candidate's cannot drift apart.

Docs (gotchas found here, written as general procedure)
- A relocation fixup can land on an instruction's IMMEDIATE OPERAND, silently
  yielding a plausible-looking wrong constant.
- ADDA.W adds the low word sign-extended; DIVU.W/DIVS.W overflow leaves the
  destination untouched.
- A desynced linear sweep DROPS instructions, so a trap census must be a byte
  scan, not a listing grep: prg_dis misses a real BIOS Bconstat at image
  0x11c2c. Of 72 even-aligned 4e4x words in Joust, six are ASCII inside string
  tables ("NO" in MONO.ERR, "NG" in CONGRATULATIONS!, "NB" in UNBEATABLE, "NO"
  in NO BONUS AWARDED); the real census is 66.

Verified
  tools/recreate_kit           13 passed
  projects/joust/recreate      90 passed
  projects/buggyboy/recreate  292 passed  (unchanged)
  projects/buggyboy/remaster  732 passed  (unchanged)
Every guard above is mutation-tested: disarm it and a named test fails.

Deferred (tracked): OS_SCREEN_BASE is still unvetted; stage_files() has no slot
bound check; test_os.py and test_os_vs_tos.py keep unpinned local OS_HEAP_BASE
literals; loop_passes/COUNT_MASK_* are 68k idioms that belong in machine.h.

events.title: fix: bug hunt multi-agents — 22 correctifs (3 critiques mémoire)
events.message:
fix: bug hunt multi-agents — 22 correctifs (3 critiques mémoire)

Chasse à 6 lentilles parallèles (cœur CPU/Bus/état, vidéo, I/O disque, périphériques,
audio & concurrence, plus le travail non commité du frontend), chaque lot passé à un
sceptique mandaté pour RÉFUTER : 26 findings bruts → 22 confirmés, 4 réfutés.

SÉCURITÉ MÉMOIRE — 3 critiques, chacune reproduite avant/après :

- Save-state / framebuffer : curW_/curH_ étaient restaurés sans invariant les liant à
  la taille de frame_, et le court-circuit « même w/h » de resizeFor() empêchait la
  réallocation → écriture hors du tas dès le 1er renderLine (repro : stack smashing +
  core dump ; contre-épreuve : le même état avec frame_ à la bonne taille tourne).
  ar.check posés APRÈS podVec(frame_) — l'ordre importe, avant ils compareraient la
  taille de la session courante — sur géométrie, mode et aires actives ; taille du
  tampon intégrée au test de resizeFor.

- Parseur STX : TrackImageSize (16 bits venus du fichier) n'était jamais confronté à
  la fin du tampon, alors que readTrackStx boucle dessus sans garde → jusqu'à ~64 Ko
  lus hors du tas sur une .stx tronquée (mesuré : 65535 annoncés pour 6 octets
  disponibles ; vérifié à 6 après correctif). Plafonné sur le reste réel, dans
  l'esprit du clamp de msa.c:205 — tronquer plutôt que rejeter garde exploitable une
  image partiellement valide. Hatari a le même trou (stx.c:1095) mais NeoST borne
  tous les autres champs : c'était le dernier.

- Save-state PSG : RegEvent::reg relu brut (0..255) indexait audioRegs_[16], écrasant
  les pointeurs de events_ puis les std::function voisines. check(reg < 14) — borne
  exacte de write8, donc zéro faux rejet — plus un masque par ÉVÉNEMENT (pas par
  échantillon, donc gratuit).

Même classe d'invariants « fichier forgé passé le CRC » : envPos_ < 96 (le repli
-=64 ne ramène pas une valeur folle dans les bornes), fifoPos_/fifoNb_ de la FIFO DMA
son + masque dans fifoPull (seul accès non masqué), mwSteps_ dans [0,16]. Et la borne
FDC fifoSize_ <= 16 corrigée en < 16 : fifoPush écrit fifo_[fifoSize_], donc 16 était
la seule valeur toxique que l'invariant laissait passer.

FICHIERS — une .msa illisible ne détruit plus l'image source : une longueur de run RLE
non plafonnée (cas nommément prévu par msa.c:205-210) faisait échouer tout le décodage,
et le repli montait les octets COMPRESSÉS comme .st brut et INSCRIPTIBLE — le premier
write sector de l'invité recopiait 512 octets à un offset arbitraire dans le .msa de
l'utilisateur. Clamp porté + repli en lecture seule dès que l'en-tête ressemble
vraiment à une .msa (looksLikeMsaHeader : mêmes contrôles que decodeMsa, le magic seul
ferait des faux positifs sur des .st légitimes).

VIDÉO — trois consommateurs manquants, alignés sur video.c :

- V_OVERSCAN_NO_DE était détecté fidèlement (port de video.c:2916-2925) mais consommé
  NULLE PART : une trame dont le DE vertical n'est jamais activé s'affichait
  normalement au lieu de sortir à l'index couleur 0, et le compteur vidéo avançait à
  tort — un programme qui vérifie son retrait de bordure haute en relisant $FF8209
  concluait à la réussite. Branché sur ses trois consommateurs Hatari : rendu
  (video.c:3988), stride du compteur (raster non avancé dans cette branche) et Timer B
  en event-count (video.c:3649, dont liveLineDisplayed est le pendant exact). Le
  drapeau étant sticky et noircissant toute la trame, la détection est verrouillée par
  un cas d'auto-test Glue dédié AVANT ses effets, avec contre-épreuve (la même bascule
  avant Top_Pos reste un retrait de bordure haute ordinaire).

- videoCounter() ignorait BORDERMASK_LEFT_OFF_2_STE/_MED (+20 o, video.c:1514-1517)
  que glueLineBytes créditait déjà : la ligne valait 180 o pour l'accumulation
  inter-lignes mais 160 pour l'offset intra-ligne, et le gel de fin de ligne tombait
  40 cycles trop tôt. Ordre de la chaîne repris d'Hatari.

- Fenêtre verticale plus COURTE que curAH_ (VO_BOTTOM_SHORT_50, −29 lignes) : le
  garde-fou de commitScanline étant imbriqué dans `vcLineY_ >= curAH_`, il ne couvrait
  que le cas plus LONG, et le compteur avançait sur des lignes non affichées. Borné
  dans glueLineBytes plutôt que dans la boucle de commit : la cadence de capture
  lineSnap_ reste intacte — c'est elle qui tient les sprites d'Enchanted Land et
  l'ancre de Lethal Xcess.

DIVERS — verrou NEOST_LINELEN à sémantique inversée : Machine lit la VALEUR (défaut
ON, 0 = OFF), les 3 sites Shifter testaient la seule PRÉSENCE de la variable, donc
NEOST_LINELEN=0 désactivait une moitié et ACTIVAIT l'autre : l'A/B documenté mesurait
un hybride jamais validé. Lecture unifiée (envFlag), défaut de CHAQUE site inchangé —
unifier les défauts activerait un rendu non revalidé — docs rectifiées.

FPU : infini GÉNÉRÉ empaqueté avec la mantisse $8000… au lieu de la forme canonique 0
(floatx80_default_infinity_low) → deux motifs binaires différents pour +∞ selon qu'il
est chargé ou calculé, alors que decodeFmt rend déjà la bonne forme (INF_SIG séparé
d'INF_LOW, appliqué aux 3 seuls sites d'empaquetage d'infini) ; FGETEXP d'un NaN
rendait l'opérande BRUT, sans quiéter le SNaN ni lever FPSR.SNAN (délégué à
propagateNaN1, comme le voisin FGETMAN) ; FMOD empruntait le court-circuit de FREM sur
expDiff < 0, sautant arrondi de précision et UNFL (softfloat.c:3048 vs 2941).

Blitter : les accès bus CPU étaient datés dans l'horloge du CŒUR alors que les
fenêtres sont armées dans celle de l'ORDONNANCEUR — 40 cycles d'écart, les cycles que
Moira::reset() consomme avant l'ancrage de la 1re trame — donc fenêtre PRE_START ratée
(busCountError_ jamais posé) et tranche reprogrammée trop tard. Datation unifiée sur
Scheduler::liveNow(). L'ancrage de la trame sur sched.now() reste délibéré.

MIDI : la file de bouclage OUT→IN croissait sans borne (~11 Mo/heure pour un séquenceur
qui n'a aucune raison de lire MIDI IN, recopiée dans chaque save-state, RDRF collé donc
IRQ ACIA permanente sous RIE). Bornée à la profondeur physique d'un 6850, ce qui
modélise en prime l'overrun.

UB : mwData_ << 16 débordait un int signé dès que le bit 15 de $FF8922 était posé —
atteignable par du code invité, sans save-state.

VALIDATION — suite --tier full verte avant et après, relancée à chaque étape des trois
modifications vidéo prises une par une. Cuddly Demos et Enchanted Land, non couverts
par une référence enregistrée, comparés au pixel contre des captures figées avant
travaux : 0 px. Auto-tests Glue 34 → 39 cas. Build ASan/UBSan complet sans rapport sur
boot, save/load, .stx forgée, état forgé, Cuddly et No Cooper. Auto-test de
déterminisme save/load identique, et un save-state légitime se charge toujours — les
nouveaux invariants ne produisent aucun faux rejet.

events.title: feat(gui): mode ancré ImGui (dockspace) + bascule GUI ⇄ kiosk à chaud
events.message:
feat(gui): mode ancré ImGui (dockspace) + bascule GUI ⇄ kiosk à chaud

Deux ajouts au frontend fenêtré, plus les correctifs de leurs premiers défauts.

Mode ancré : dockspace ImGui semé une fois (`g_dockSeeded`, persisté dans la même
section d'`imgui.ini` que la taille de fenêtre — seul moyen de distinguer « première
exécution » d'« l'utilisateur a tout désancré exprès », le nœud existant dès le 1er
DockSpace()). Réglage `dock=` dans neost.cfg. Nécessite la branche DOCKING d'ImGui
d'où le bump du sous-module (v1.92.8-23 master → v1.92.8-docking-85).

Bascule à chaud : F8, menu Machine et action « DESKTOP MODE » du menu borne font
l'aller-retour sans relancer l'application. La machine traverse intacte (instantané
mémoire pris avant, rechargé derrière — d'où l'application à une frontière de trame,
loadState refusant le milieu de trame) ; le contexte GL, ses textures et la passe CRT
survivent. Géométrie fenêtrée mémorisée pour la sortie de plein écran.

Correctifs des défauts trouvés à la relecture de ce travail :

- Le gel de la configuration kiosk était DÉFINITIVEMENT rompu par un aller-retour F8 :
  `switchKioskMode(false)` remet g_kiosk à false, ce qui rendait la main à la douzaine
  de saveConfig du GUI pour le reste du processus, et le retour en borne réécrivait
  neost.cfg avec le disque et les réglages du visiteur. « Lancé en borne » est un
  invariant de DÉPLOIEMENT distinct de l'état courant → g_kioskLaunched, testé dans
  saveConfig (le seul écrivain légitime de la borne passe déjà force=true).

- L'émulation joystick-clavier restait armée en revenant au bureau depuis une session
  lancée en --kiosk : la capture de lambda `kbdJoyDesk = g_kbdJoy` est évaluée APRÈS
  `g_kbdJoy = g_kiosk`, donc valait true, et la sortie « rendait » un réglage qui
  n'avait jamais existé — flèches et Ctrl droit avalés sans rien afficher, seul remède
  F11 que rien ne signale. Ne se reproduisait que sur les déploiements borne.

- La fenêtre était replacée en (0,0) à la première sortie de borne : g_winX/g_winY
  n'étaient jamais renseignés quand la session démarre en --kiosk (la TAILLE l'était
  via imgui.ini, pas la position). En bi-écran la fenêtre atterrissait sur le mauvais
  moniteur, barre de titre hors champ sous X11. Drapeau g_winGeomValid explicite (un
  test sur (0,0) recentrerait une fenêtre légitimement placée à l'origine) + centrage
  sur la zone de travail du moniteur, relevé AVANT glfwSetWindowMonitor(…, nullptr, …)
  qui le remet à null.

events.title: ethernet: never deliver a card its own frames back
events.message:
ethernet: never deliver a card its own frames back

Bridged onto a host adapter that reflects multicast, an emulated card is
handed everything the guest sends to a multicast group. On IPv4 that is
invisible: a reflected mDNS query is answered by nobody and dropped. On IPv6
it costs the guest every address it has.

IPv6 duplicate address detection sends a neighbour solicitation for the
tentative address to that address's solicited-node multicast group, and a
solicitation for the address arriving from somewhere else is exactly what a
duplicate looks like. The guest hears its own, concludes the address is
taken and withdraws it, and does the same for the link-local one, so it ends
up with no IPv6 address at all and every command answers that there is no
route. The stack cannot defend itself: the solicitation is correct in every
respect and RFC 4861 forbids the source link-layer address option on it, so
the only evidence of self-origin is the ethernet source address, which the
IP layer never sees. Real hardware on a real switch does not reflect, and
neither does SLIRP, which is why this needed a bridged run to find.

a2065.cpp already dropped a self-sent frame when the destination was a
unicast address ("not for me2") or the broadcast address ("not for me3").
Multicast fell through both. Add the third case.

ne2000.cpp had no self-source test at all, so unicast and broadcast echoes
were delivered too. Fold the station address comparison, which already
existed in two spellings for the dp8390 and the plain NE2000, into one
helper and use it for the source as well as the destination.

sana2.cpp dropped a self-sent broadcast only. Widen that to any self-sent
frame, which is the same rule as the other two.

The filter has to stay in the card and cannot move to ethernet.cpp, because
"my address" is a different thing in each one. The A2065 rewrites MAC
addresses on the way past, so the address on the wire is realmac while the
address it hands ethernet_open() is fakemac, the one the guest programmed;
a filter on ndd->mac would silently do nothing on the very card the fault
was found on. The NE2000 reads its address out of register or PROM state the
guest can change, and uaenet.device is the only one for which ndd->mac is
right. Each card already owns its receive accept filter, so this is one test
added to each of three existing filters, not a new layer.

Boards covered: A2065 and Ariadne (a2065.cpp); Ariadne II, Hydra AmigaNet,
LAN Rover/EB920, X-Surf, X-Surf-100 Z2 and Z3, NE2000 PCI, NE2000 ISA and
NE2000 PCMCIA, all of which go through ne2000_init_2(); and uaenet.device.

Verified on the A2065, which is the one card there is a driver to hand for.
Bridged onto a real LAN, an Amiga TCP/IP stack with an unpatched build of
master reports no IPv6 address at all, not even a link-local one; with this
change the same guest takes a SLAAC address from the LAN's router, pings
2606:4700:4700::1111 three times for three replies and completes a nine hop
IPv6 traceroute to it, and the IPv4 lease, ping and traceroute are unchanged.
The emulator's own -a2065log2 dump of the two runs says why: of the frames
arriving with the guest's own source address and a multicast destination,
the unpatched build delivered 7 of 10 to the guest and this one delivers 0
of 15. A bridged bsdsocket conformance run is 23/23 either way. The NE2000
boards and uaenet.device are by inspection and compilation only; no SANA-II
driver for any of those boards was available to exercise them.

events.title: tools: extract the differential harness into tools/recreate_kit/
events.message:
tools: extract the differential harness into tools/recreate_kit/

The Musashi-backed differential harness was BuggyBoy-shaped: a second game
would have had to copy it. Hoist the game-agnostic machinery into a shared
kit, bound to a project by a small project.toml.

Moved (the renames landed early in 6a21db9 — see below)
- oracle/{loader,emu,isa_conformance,tos_probe}.py, oracle/shim.c,
  include/{machine.h,os.h}, test/harness.py -> tools/recreate_kit/.

Binding
- project.toml per game (prg / names / lib / load_base / image_size);
  project.load() resolves it, and a 16-line test/harness.py shim binds the
  kit before re-exporting it, so all ~40 existing test files keep their
  `from harness import differential` untouched. That is what makes the
  292-test gate below meaningful rather than circular.
- kit.mk holds the shared build rules; a project Makefile is now 3 lines.

Fixes from the review (the kit was not actually game-agnostic)
- harness.py hard-bound g_dosound_log_{count,args,reset} at import, so a
  candidate .so without them failed with dlsym: symbol not found BEFORE any
  test ran — Joust would have been dead on arrival. The ledger is now
  optional, byte-identical when present. If the ledger is absent but the
  oracle actually issued Dosound traps, we RAISE rather than skip: silently
  skipping is precisely the off-image divergence the ledger exists to catch.
  Verified against a purpose-built stub .so, not by inspection.
- The trap model's fixed addresses (OS_HEAP_BASE / OS_FS_TABLE / OS_FS_STAGING)
  are kit-wide but were tuned for BuggyBoy; a game whose text reached 0xbf000
  would have had its staged-file table written over its own code with no
  assertion. Now guarded at import with a diagnostic naming the project.toml.
  Not derived from image_size: the C side cannot read project.toml, so that
  would need a generated header — a guard is the honest fix, not fake generality.
- make clean in one project deleted the SHARED oracle. Split: per-project
  clean removes project build artifacts, the kit has its own clean.
- Dropped -Iinclude from OCFLAGS: the project's include/ was on the path while
  compiling the shared liboracle.so, so a stray include could silently make the
  shared artifact game-specific with no cross-project way for make to notice.
- Unbound-loader/emu now raise a message naming project.load() instead of
  TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'.

Kit self-tests (new tools/recreate_kit/test/, run by its own make test)
- test_os_memory_map.py pins os.h against harness.py's Python mirror of the
  same constants. Both sides of that pin moved into tools/ while the test that
  held them equal stayed in BuggyBoy; this restores it kit-side. Mutation-checked.
- test_trap_tables.py pins prg_dis.py's XBIOS map against the Ghidra script's.

Out of spec but required: 13 files under remaster/ import the oracle and would
have broken silently. Patched with the same bind idiom; full remaster suite run.

Verified
- tools/recreate_kit          6 passed
- buggyboy/recreate         292 passed  (exact pre-refactor baseline)
- buggyboy/remaster         732 passed
No test_*.py was edited to reach those numbers; the single test-file touch is a
skip-reason string in test_isa_vs_tos.py.

Note on history: the 8 file renames were swept into 6a21db9 ("remaster: 50/60 Hz
tempo fix") by a concurrent session committing with -A, and c18dd3b absorbed this
change's recreate/README.md edits the same way. Both are already pushed, so this
is a forward-only fix rather than a rewrite; HEAD is coherent again as of here.

Known and deliberately not fixed: stage_files() does not check slot < OS_FS_SLOTS,
so a 9th staged file would overwrite the staging region. BuggyBoy stages 2.

events.title: ne2000: validate host frame size before reading its header
events.message:
ne2000: validate host frame size before reading its header

A bridged host adapter does not deliver one wire frame per callback. With
Receive Segment Coalescing, or across a veth/bridge/virtio path where Linux
GSO segments are carried whole, several TCP segments arrive merged into a
single frame: 11734 bytes and 32858 bytes were both observed on a bridged
run against a helper on the LAN. At the other end, a TAP or TUN backend can
return a read shorter than an ethernet header.

gotfunc() handed the frame to ne2000_canreceive() before checking anything,
and ne2000_canreceive() reads the first six bytes to run the address filter.
A short frame is therefore read past its end. The size check that follows was
correct for the oversized case, so nothing was copied out of bounds, but it
only ran after the header had already been inspected.

Check the size first, reject anything that cannot be a frame or cannot fit a
queue slot, and only then look at the header. Also bail out if the receive
queue has not been allocated, matching gotfunc() in a2065.cpp.

This is the same class of fault as 8da8821d49 fixed for the A2065, where an
11734-byte frame was memcpy'd into a 4000-byte stack buffer and ended the
process. The NE2000 code already bounded its copy and already queued frames
for the hsync drain, so it never crashed; this closes the remaining read.

Covers every board that goes through ne2000_init_2(): Ariadne II, Hydra
AmigaNet, LAN Rover/EB920, X-Surf, X-Surf-100 Z2 and Z3, and the NE2000 PCI,
ISA (x86 bridgeboard) and PCMCIA cards. uaenet.device (sana2.cpp) already
rejects len < 20 as its first act and needs nothing.

Verified by inspection and by building; none of these boards has a SANA-II
driver available here to exercise the path end to end.

events.title: tools: correct the TOS XBIOS trap table (decimal-as-hex)
events.message:
tools: correct the TOS XBIOS trap table (decimal-as-hex)

TOS references print XBIOS opcodes in DECIMAL; several were pasted into our
tables as hex literals, so 0x20 was labelled Supexec when 0x20 = 32 = Dosound.
That mislabelled Joust's entire sound layer and produced a family of wrong
function names until body reads caught it.

Tables
- prg_dis.py / AtariOsTrapAnnotate.java: XBIOS keys corrected and completed
  (Iorec 0x0E, Rsconf 0x0F, Random 0x11, Scrdmp 0x14, Bioskeys 0x18,
  Ikbdws 0x19, Giaccess 0x1C, Xbtimer 0x1F, Dosound 0x20, Setprt 0x21,
  Kbdvbase 0x22, Vsync 0x25, Supexec 0x26, Puntaes 0x27). The bogus
  0x28/0x2A entries are gone. Both tables now hold the same 23 XBIOS keys.
- Comments lead with the decimal->value conversion rather than "keys are in
  hex", which restated the very misconception that caused the bug.

Verification
- Re-running prg_dis on JOUST.PRG resolves all 71 trap sites with no
  "XBIOS ?" left (was 18 unknown, 4 wrong).

Harness
- recreate/oracle/shim.c dropped XBIOS 0x28/0x2A from the no-op arm. Those
  selectors existed only because of the wrong table; under correct numbering
  they are XBIOS 40/42, which BuggyBoy never issues. Treating them as modelled
  returned a fabricated d0=0 with modeled=1, bypassing the `default:
  modeled = 0` guard whose job is to make the oracle REFUSE to diff against a
  fabricated result. No result was actually mis-verified, but the safety
  property was broken. buggyboy `make test`: 292 passed (unchanged).

Docs
- tos-os-calls.md: note that these lists are the common selectors and
  prg_dis.py is canonical, so a missing entry is not evidence of a bad
  annotation; plus the gotcha that this fix does NOT self-heal an existing
  Ghidra DB (reapply.sh is -noanalysis, so BuggyBoy's DB still carries
  xbios_supexec on a wrapper that is really Dosound).
- joust names.txt / README.md: the "the tools are wrong" notes were still in
  the present tense and are now false; reworded to past tense.

Deferred (tracked, deliberately not folded in)
- The tables remain hand-mirrored across Python/Java/prose, violating
  CLAUDE.md §5. The fix is a canonical tools/tos_traps.tsv both tools read,
  which needs a headless Ghidra run to verify script-dir path resolution.
- prg_dis mis-decodes MULU.W/DIVU.W immediates as and.w/or.w to an address
  register (an illegal 68000 encoding) - found while reading Joust's
  pos_to_screen; same class of defect, separate fix.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: fix the music tempo on a PAL machine (50/60 Hz sync bit)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: fix the music tempo on a PAL machine (50/60 Hz sync bit)

Every tune played ~17% too slow on real hardware. Pitch was right; only the
tempo dragged.

The original's REFRESH (@0x1b096) reads the shifter's sync bit every frame --
`btst #1,$ffff820a` -- and branches its tempo prescaler on it:

  60 Hz (bit clear): tick the prescaler; on its 6th frame reload and SKIP that
                     frame's advance -> 60 x 5/6 = 50 note-advances/second
  50 Hz (bit set):   branch over the prescaler; advance EVERY frame -> 50/second

The prescaler exists only to normalise the musical tempo across PAL and NTSC.
Our port ran the 60 Hz path unconditionally at 50 Hz: 50 x 5/6 = 41.7
advances/second = 16.7% slow, which matches the reported "15-20%" exactly.

Why nothing caught it: the oracle reads $ffff820a as 0 (the address is above
the image), so recreate models the 60 Hz path unconditionally -- its own
comment says so -- and remaster is pinned to recreate by the sound
differential. All 730 tests agreed with each other and with the oracle while
disagreeing with the hardware. It is the same blind spot as the off-image
palette seam: a hardware READ the oracle cannot see is invisible to the whole
differential.

Fix: rm_sound_video_50hz carries the bit; the on-target VBL pump refreshes it
from $ffff820a each frame, exactly where the original reads it (and legally --
the VBL runs supervisor). The host default stays 0, so the differential is
byte-for-byte unchanged.

Pins (property tests -- the oracle cannot express this branch):
  test_tempo_is_the_same_at_50hz_and_60hz     all 11 tunes, both standards
  test_50hz_path_does_not_tick_the_prescaler  the branch really skips the subq
Mutation-verified: reverting the fix fails the first.

Deferred: recreate's g_REFRESH keeps the 60 Hz assumption -- correct for the
oracle, wrong on a PAL machine if that binary is run for audio.

Verified: make test 732 green, goldens x5 MATCH, staged BUGGYBOY.PRG boots
clean on real TOS 1.04 / ST / 4 MB.

events.title: buggyboy: names.txt — 0x120f8 is ikbd_send_byte, not set_rez
events.message:
buggyboy: names.txt — 0x120f8 is ikbd_send_byte, not set_rez

Decoded from the opcodes: move.b d0,$8be6 / move.l #$8be6,-(sp) / clr.w -(sp)
/ move.w #$19,-(sp) / trap #14 — that is Ikbdws(count_m1=0, buf), sending ONE
IKBD byte. It touches no resolution and no video register.

main calls it four times at boot to configure the IKBD (the same job remaster's
kbd_install does). Found while checking whether the original changes the video
frequency to explain a music-tempo difference on real hardware: it does not.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: free-running presentation is the default (C1 now opt-in)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: free-running presentation is the default (C1 now opt-in)

The original presents free-running — flip_screen @0x121f8 toggles flip_idx,
pokes the video base registers directly, and does ONE XBIOS 37 Vsync. No
quantization. recreate's g_flip_screen reproduces that; this shell did not.

C1's even-vblank lock rounded every present UP onto a 2-vblank grid
(present = ceil(render / 40 ms) x 40 ms), which on real hardware made the port
play SLOWER than the original despite rendering faster (STE gate: 97.75 ms
render, 160 ms present, vs the original's ~110 ms free-running) and made a
32 MHz accelerator worth almost nothing — 97 ms and 82 ms land on the same
slot. Matching the original is this port's contract, so free-running is now the
default and the lock is opt-in via -DGAME_PRESENT_LOCK.

Pure knob inversion: the new default BUGGYBOY.PRG is byte-identical to the old
-DGAME_PRESENT_FREERUN build, and a -DGAME_PRESENT_LOCK build is byte-identical
to the old default. No pixels change either way — the frame drawn is the same
bytes, only when it is shown moves.

Measured, same scene (run_cadence.py ste 200, with and without --lock, STE
driving): median 7 vs 8 vblanks/present, mean 6.94 vs 7.36 — the lock was
rounding 83 of 199 presents that finished in 7 vblanks up to 8.

Neither shape tears: both poke the base mid-frame and the shifter latches it at
the vblank the flip's Vsync lands on. What the lock bought was an EVEN cadence
(free-running jitters 5/6/7 vblanks with the render's phase), not tear-freedom;
an earlier note in this tree claimed otherwise and is corrected.

run_cadence.py's --freerun flag becomes --lock (free-run is now the baseline).

Verified: make test 730 green, goldens x5 MATCH, make gate green, staged
BUGGYBOY.PRG boots clean on real TOS 1.04 / ST / 4 MB.

(supervisor, interrupts masked around the write), then ONE XBIOS 37 Vsync —
free-running, no quantization. recreate's g_flip_screen reproduces that shape
faithfully; remaster's show_surface does not (it adds the C1 grid and uses

Also corrects an earlier claim: free-running does not tear. Both shapes latch
