events.title: buggyboy/recreate: preserve d2/a2 in the TOS trap wrappers too
events.message:
buggyboy/recreate: preserve d2/a2 in the TOS trap wrappers too

Same latent bug the remaster shipped (91723f6): GCC's m68k SysV ABI treats
%d2-%d7/%a2-%a6 as callee-saved and caches live values in them across a call,
while GEMDOS/BIOS/XBIOS preserve only %d3-%d7/%a3-%a6. %d2/%a2 are therefore
exactly the pair the compiler expects to survive and TOS may destroy, and
omitting the save silently corrupts one live variable in the caller.

Latent here rather than live: these programs only ever run under Hatari's
EmuTOS, which happens to leave benign values in %d2 — the same reason every
pin stayed green while the remaster died on real TOS.

23 wrappers across os.s (8) and game_os.s (15) now save/restore the pair and
read their C arguments at +8. Verified mechanically against HEAD: every
argument-source read is exactly +8 and no trap-frame cleanup (lea/addq on sp)
changed. Note Setcolor reads an argument AFTER a push (10/8 -> 18/16) — the
invariant is that the movem adds a constant 8 to every argument read,
regardless of intervening pushes.

Verified: game_build.sh + game_smoke.py green (BUGGY.PRG boots in Hatari and
renders a valid on-target frame); make test 292 passed.

Pre-existing and NOT touched: render/atari/build.sh (the leg-results demo)
fails to link for unrelated reasons — undefined g_dosound / g_read_joystick /
g_xbios_setpalette / g_console_wait_char / g_load_graphics. It fails
identically without this change, so os.s's fix here is verified statically
only.

events.title: Reconstruct WERNER.PRG's C source, buildable with Alcyon C 4.14
events.message:
Reconstruct WERNER.PRG's C source, buildable with Alcyon C 4.14

All 248 of the game's own functions, recovered from Ghidra and compiled
with the original toolchain: cp68/c068/c168/as68/lo68/relmod plus the
1990 Atari Developer's Kit libraries. The rebuilt binary is 105,180
bytes against the original's 103,392.

The 111 remaining functions in WERNER.PRG are the Alcyon C runtime and

Developer's Kit headers, not reproduced. That the original used them is
visible in the binary itself -- the decompiler shows gemdos(0x48,33000)
and xbios(5,log,phys,-1), exactly what osbind.h's Malloc() and
Setscreen() expand to.

Period-authentic Alcyon K&R C, verified against the compiler rather than
assumed: 16-bit int, no void keyword (c068 rejects it outright), no
volatile, and external identifiers unique within 7 characters. The
renames happen in source because cp68's macro table truncates too, so a
long-name alias would become a catch-all. gemdefs.h and obdefs.h are
deliberately not included -- obdefs.h does not parse under Alcyon 4.14
and gemdefs.h depends on it.

Source layout follows the link order, which recovers the original
translation units and the function order within each. Library code sits
at both ends of TEXT: the startup object first, the libraries last.

Every DATA table is extracted from the binary, not from asset files --
which matters, because COLOR_TABLE_MENU differs from MENUE.PC1's own
header in one entry, and COLOR_TABLE_NEBELFAHRT_A turns out to be flat
0x555 grey. That table is the fog: Nebelfahrt starts on it and "clears"
by swapping palettes. There is no fog sprite.

Also documented, in auto.c: a bug in the shipped game. game_autofahrt
writes the score to absolute address 0x1A1AE, which is not a variable
but the entry point of game_schuesselbau_verdict_robot -- the word
stored there is its link.w prologue. Starting Autofahrt corrupts that
function. Almost certainly a casualty of the 7-character truncation, a
score variable whose name collapsed onto the function's symbol. The
reconstruction does not reproduce the stray write; our layout differs,
so it would corrupt something arbitrary instead.

Verified under Hatari: the binary boots, plays the joystick tutorial,
reaches the menu, and runs all six mini-games. Not verified: no game has
been driven to a win or loss end to end, and sound executes but has not
been listened to.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: an on-target crash reporter for real hardware
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: an on-target crash reporter for real hardware

TOS answers a 68000 fault with N bombs and nothing else — the vector number,
never the code, and the .PRG is relocated differently on every machine. This
is the tool that localised the d2/a2 crash fixed in the previous commit, kept
because real hardware is the one place the harness cannot look.

GAME_CRASH_REPORT=1 build_game.sh -> BUGDIAG.PRG. crash.S takes the seven
FAULT vectors (2-8), snapshots the exception frame and the register file, and
crash_report() prints the vector, the boot stage, the frames presented, the PC
as an offset into TEXT (portable across machines; resolve with m68k-elf-nm),
the fault address and opcode, A0-A6, and the faulting stack — to the screen and
to CRASH.TXT.

Deliberately NOT taken: vectors 10/11. On the Atari those are the Line-A/F
dispatch, not faults — hijacking vector 10 reports a healthy machine as a crash
and leaves the desktop's Line-A entry in freed TPA on exit. crash_uninstall()
gives TOS its vectors back on every exit from main(), including the early ones.

Harness:
- make crash-selftest — plants a deliberate address error past CRASH_STAGE_BOOT,
  boots headless with the console echoed, and fails unless the report names main()
  with the right vector, stage and frame count. Mutation-verified.
- make gate now compiles this build, so the reporter cannot rot.

The shipping BUGGYBOY.PRG is byte-identical with the knob off: every breadcrumb
compiles to nothing and all of the reporter's storage lives in crash.S, so no
other global changes parity.
events.author: geogeo28

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: fix the 3-bombs crash on real hardware (os.s d2/a2)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: fix the 3-bombs crash on real hardware (os.s d2/a2)

The shipping BUGGYBOY.PRG address-errored (3 bombs) on a real ST/STE as the
leg select drew, on TOS 1.62 and 2.06, at any memory size.

Root cause: os.s's TOS trap wrappers did not preserve %d2/%a2 — the one pair
where the two calling conventions disagree. GCC's m68k SysV ABI treats
%d2-%d7/%a2-%a6 as callee-saved and caches live values in them across a call;
GEMDOS/BIOS/XBIOS guarantee only %d3-%d7/%a3-%a6 and may return with anything
in %d0-%d2/%a0-%a2.

Concretely: rm_flow_leg_select kept the flow's ctx (the Shell *) in %d2; its
per-frame flow_poll -> read_input -> read_joystick -> Ikbdws (XBIOS 25)
returned with phystop-1 in %d2; the next ops->quit_requested(ctx) ran
tst.l 148(a0) on that odd pointer -> address error, on the FIRST leg-select
frame. The bad pointer tracked RAM size exactly (0x0FFFFF / 0x1FFFFF /
0x3FFFFF at 1/2/4 MB), which is what identified it as a returned register
rather than random corruption.

Why every pin stayed green: EmuTOS — the only TOS the harness ever booted —
leaves a benign even value in %d2, so the same deref silently read garbage
instead of faulting, and the goldens dump frame 0 without ever running the
leg-select input loop. Reproduced headlessly under real TOS 1.04.

Fix: every wrapper saves/restores %d2/%a2 around its trap and reads its C
arguments at +8 accordingly. All 18 verified against HEAD for the shift, the
restore point and %d0 survival.

Deferred: recreate/render/atari/{os.s,game_os.s} have the same unprotected
wrappers — latent, they only ever run under EmuTOS.

Verified: shipping .PRG runs clean on real TOS 1.04 at 4 MB where it died
after one frame; make test 730 green; goldens x5 MATCH; make gate green.

events.title: FMOVE.P k-factor support (assembler + disassembler) (#13)
events.message:
FMOVE.P k-factor support (assembler + disassembler) (#13)

* feat: FMOVE.P k-factor support (assembler + disassembler)

Implements the FMOVE-k-factor-syntax anchor feature noted alongside 4.5
in plan.md (`FMOVE.P FPn,(A0){#3}`), plus fixes a disassembler bug found
while verifying it end-to-end.

- Assembler: `FMOVE.P FPn,<ea>{#k}` (static, -64..=63) and
  `FMOVE.P FPn,<ea>{Dn}` (dynamic) now parse and encode correctly. The
  exact extension-word bit layout was ambiguous in available
  documentation (whether bit 6 is a static/dynamic discriminator or part
  of the k-factor value), so it was verified empirically against a local
  `vasm -m68881` build rather than guessed: the two forms are actually
  distinguished by the format-code field itself (3 = static, 7 =
  dynamic), not a bit within the k-factor field — bits 6-0 hold the full
  7-bit two's-complement k value in the static case.
- Disassembler: found and fixed a pre-existing bug while checking the
  new encoder output round-trips — `FMOVE.P FPn,<ea>{...}` with any
  nonzero k-factor decoded as "unknown FPU arithmetic opclass/opmode",
  because the generic arithmetic-opclass lookup (bits 6-0) doesn't know
  this store-direction packed-decimal form repurposes those bits for a
  k-factor instead. `DecodedOperand` gained a `suffix` field so a
  k-factor can be appended directly to its EA operand's formatted text
  (`(a0){#5}`) without the `", "` separator a second operand would get.

All three CI checks pass; 10 new tests including a full encode->decode->
reformat->reassemble roundtrip, all reference bytes verified against
real vasm output.

* docs: update plan.md — FMOVE.P k-factor is now implemented

events.title: AmigaOS 4.1 (PPC) target support — dual-arch devbench (#11)
events.message:
AmigaOS 4.1 (PPC) target support — dual-arch devbench (#11)

* scripts: fix sam460ex install-mode drive layout + auto-use bundled U-Boot

The sam460ex machine has a single IDE bus with two slots. The old
script attached both HDDs (slots 0+1) and passed -cdrom, which QEMU
tried to place on bus 1 — a non-existent second bus — and refused
to start with:

  machine type does not support if=ide,bus=1,unit=0

Install mode now uses slot 0 for the system HDD and slot 1 for the
CD (dev HDD is attached only in normal mode after install completes).
Same fix normalises the "warning about missing U-Boot firmware" to a
silent no-op — recent QEMU ships u-boot-sam460.bin in its share dir
and auto-loads it for the sam460ex; only pass -bios when a custom
firmware is explicitly provided in \$OS4_DIR/u-boot-sam460ex.bin.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* scripts: 1 GB RAM + Cocoa zoom-to-fit + auto-resize QEMU window

Two usability fixes for the sam460ex install session:

- Bump RAM from 512 MB to 1 GB. AmigaOS 4.1 wedged mid-boot at 512 MB
  under QEMU. sam460ex supports up to 2 GB and 1 GB gets past every
  observed boot hang.
- Drop the rtl8139 -net stanza. sam460ex has built-in EMAC ethernet
  and QEMU warned rtl8139 wouldn't be created anyway; -nic none
  keeps things clean until we set up network the right way.
- Switch -display to `cocoa,zoom-to-fit=on,show-cursor=on` so the
  window is drag-resizable. QEMU has no way to set an initial window
  size, so also post-spawn an osascript that uses System Events to
  resize the window to 960x720 the moment it appears — 320x232
  Retina-scaled is unreadable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* devbench: PPC arch mode + qemu-os4 profile + setup docs

Add a first-class notion of target CPU architecture so devbench can
switch between classic 68k and AmigaOS 4.1 PPC without editing files.

- DevBenchConfig gains `arch` (m68k | ppc) and `docker_image` fields.
  Both readable from a [build] section or a profile overlay.
- New `qemu-os4` profile in devbench.toml: serial TCP 127.0.0.1:2346,
  arch=ppc, walkero/amigagccondocker:os4-gcc11-arm64 image, and
  emulator_binary pointed at scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh. Relative
  binary paths in profiles are auto-resolved against project_root.
- Emulator manager accepts an empty config_file — QEMU's launcher is
  a shell script that takes no args, unlike FS-UAE which wants a
  .fs-uae config path.
- /api/config exposes build.arch, build.docker_image, and the
  profile.active/available lists.
- Header badge in the web UI shows `<arch> · <profile>` colour-coded
  by arch (orange for ppc, blue for m68k). Populated on page load so
  it's visible without navigating to Settings.
- docs/amigaos4-setup.md walks through a full install: asset layout,
  ISO extraction, install-mode boot, Media Toolbox, first HDD boot,
  ScreenMode change, update LHAs, dev HDF options.

Run classic AmiKit as before, or:
    python3 -m amiga_devbench --profile qemu-os4

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* bridge: ARCH=ppc build path + PPC 68k-stub layer + Docker wrappers

Scaffold the AmigaOS 4.1 PowerPC bridge port so it builds under the
walkero/amigagccondocker:os4-gcc11-arm64 toolchain image, without
attempting the full 68k → PPC port of the register-capture subsystems
yet. Splits the daemon sources into portable + 68k-only sets:

- Portable (both arches): main, serial_io, ipc_manager, client_registry,
  protocol_handler, system_inspector, fs_access, process_launcher,
  gfx_inspector, audio_inspector, intuition_inspector, input_inject,
  font_browser, chipwrite_logger, pool_tracker, clipboard_bridge,
  arexx_bridge, transport, net_io, b64, script_util, version.
- 68k-only (needs per-arch port): crash_handler, snoop, debugger.
  All three use inline __asm("dN") register captures / 68k exception
  frames that don't translate to PowerPC.

PPC build swaps in arch_stubs_ppc.c which provides no-op / not-implemented
versions of crash_get_last / snoop_* / crash_* so callers in main.c and
protocol_handler.c link cleanly. Host side sees "not-implemented|arch=ppc"
when it asks for those features; as each subsystem gets a real PPC port,
its stub gets deleted and the file moves to DAEMON_SRCS_PORTABLE.

Compiler flags per arch:
- m68k: -noixemul -O0 -m68020 (unchanged)
- ppc:  -mcrt=newlib -O2 -mcpu=440 -D__PPC__ + -lauto (interface auto-gen)

Wrappers:
- scripts/build-bridge-ppc.sh  — runs `make ARCH=ppc` inside the toolchain
  image. Auto-pulls on first use, verifies daemon is up.
- scripts/build-example-ppc.sh <name> — same for individual examples.

Also bumps examples submodule pointer to include hello_world's Makefile
ARCH switch (68a8990).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* scripts: amitools-based dev HDF init + deploy pipeline

Ditch the Media Toolbox click-through for dev HDF preparation. Three
new scripts do it all from macOS via amitools (rdbtool + xdftool):

- install-amitools.sh — pip install amitools; verifies rdbtool/xdftool.
- init-dev-hdf.sh — one-time: writes RDB, adds a whole-disk DOS3
  (FFS-Int-Dircache) partition, formats it as `DevDrive:`. Refuses to
  overwrite an existing RDB unless FORCE=1. Defaults to
  $HOME/AmigaOS4/amigaos4-dev.hdf.
- deploy-os4.sh — copy files into the dev HDF. Handles write/list/rm.
  Warns when QEMU is currently attached (raw HDF is shared state so a
  concurrent write can corrupt).

Under the hood: DOS3 partitions mount natively in OS4 as regular Amiga
volumes — no CrossDOS / mountlist config needed. The dev HDF shows up
as `DevDrive:` (or DH1: depending on device order).

devbench.toml's qemu-os4 profile now points deploy_dir at the HDF file
itself. Downstream consumers that treat deploy_dir as a raw filesystem
path need to detect the .hdf suffix and shell out to deploy-os4.sh
instead — flagged in the docs and the profile comment.

docs/amigaos4-setup.md updated: the old "3 possible routes" section is
replaced with a single primary flow (amitools) plus the two fallbacks
(bridge file transfer, FAT32+hdiutil) as afterthoughts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* bridge/devbench: OS4 SDK include flags + HDF-aware deployer

Two integration fixes needed for the PPC compile to make forward
progress:

- amiga-bridge/Makefile PPC CFLAGS: add -D__USE_INLINE__ so the
  OS4 <proto/*> headers pull in inline4/*.h and provide the classic
  GetMsg/ReplyMsg/BeginRefresh/etc. as `IExec->GetMsg(...)` macros.
  Also -D__USE_OLD_TIMEVAL__ so `struct timerequest` keeps its
  tr_node/tr_time/tv_secs/tv_micro fields (OS4 renamed the base
  struct to TimeRequest to avoid the POSIX `timeval` collision).
- Deployer detects .hdf deploy_dir at load time (_is_hdf flag) and
  routes writes through scripts/deploy-os4.sh (xdftool). has_shared_folder
  now accepts files as well as dirs when it's an HDF. deploy_file /
  deploy() work unchanged from the caller's perspective — the fact
  that we're writing to a hardfile instead of a directory is invisible.

Verified: python3 → Deployer('~/AmigaOS4/amigaos4-dev.hdf') →
deploy_file(...) round-trips into the HDF and lists back correctly.

The Makefile progress unblocks the majority of the "implicit
declaration" wall — the remaining PPC build errors are struct-base
conflicts (SysBase/IntuitionBase/GfxBase already extern'd by proto/*.h
on OS4), which need per-file gating and are the start of the real
porting work.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* bridge: PPC port pass 1 — gate library-base decls behind #ifndef __PPC__

On OS4, <proto/{exec,intuition,graphics,dos}.h> auto-declare SysBase /
IntuitionBase / GfxBase / DOSBase (as opaque struct Library * pointers
that go through the interface pattern, e.g. IExec->). Every classic
bridge source file that declared these as struct ExecBase * / struct
IntuitionBase * / struct GfxBase * hit "conflicting types" on PPC.

Wrap each declaration in #ifndef __PPC__ so the classic 68k build is
unchanged and the PPC build lets the OS4 headers own the symbols. 12
files touched. Skips snoop.c / debugger.c / crash_handler.c — those
are already excluded from the PPC build in DAEMON_SRCS_68K_ONLY.

Pass 2 (next commit): OS4's SysBase is now typed as `struct Library *`
so direct field access like SysBase->ThisTask, SysBase->LibList,
SysBase->VBlankFrequency fails throughout. Also DOS constant renames
(DLT_DIRECTORY → EXD_IS_DIRECTORY, ACCESS_READ gone). Those need
per-arch accessor macros or IExec-> calls, not just declaration gating.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* bridge: PPC port pass 2 — OS4 field-access + interface + DOS shims

Continue the PPC port. Pass 1 gated conflicting library-base decls;
pass 2 handles OS4's opaque SysBase / IntuitionBase / GfxBase typing
(struct Library *, not struct ExecBase *) and the DOS-API renames.

Per-file preambles introduce cast aliases so field access still
compiles on both arches:
  #ifdef __PPC__
  #define SYSB  ((struct ExecBase *)SysBase)
  #define INTUB ((struct IntuitionBase *)IntuitionBase)
  #define GFXB  ((struct GfxBase *)GfxBase)
  #endif
Then mechanically rewrite `SysBase->TaskReady` → `SYSB->TaskReady`
throughout system_inspector.c, gfx_inspector.c, intuition_inspector.c,
arexx_bridge.c. Semantics preserved on 68k (SYSB expands to SysBase).

DOS API translations (fs_access, process_launcher, protocol_handler):
  Seek       -> OBSOLETESeek
  Examine    -> OBSOLETEExamine
  ExNext     -> OBSOLETEExNext
  DeleteFile -> Delete
  SetFileDate-> SetDate
  ACCESS_READ-> SHARED_LOCK
All wrapped in `#ifdef __PPC__ #define ... #endif` shims.

Stubbed on PPC (feature returns "not supported" over protocol):
- pool_tracker: SetFunction LVO patching doesn't exist on OS4's
  interface-based exec. Whole install/uninstall block gated 68k-only.
- system_inspector sys_handle_readregs: 68k `movem.l` inline asm
  gated; PPC returns zeroed regs.
- system_inspector assign/volume: dol_Lock/dol_Task on volume-type
  DosList entries live under dol_misc.dol_volume.* on OS4 — gated
  with TODO comments.

Client library (bridge_client.c):
- Added #include <dos/dos.h> for SIGBREAKF_CTRL_E/F (OS4 doesn't pull
  it in transitively via <exec/*>).

arch_stubs_ppc.c: add stubs for all 17 dbg_* entry points that
protocol_handler.c dispatches; fix crash_init/snoop_is_active
signatures to match the classic prototypes.

Build state on PPC:
  amiga-bridge/amiga-bridge  274 KB PPC ELF (daemon)
  amiga-bridge/libbridge.a    22 KB PPC ELF (client lib)

68k build unchanged — every PPC-only change gated behind __PPC__.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* examples: bump for hello_world PPC (4fe9445)

* scripts: init-dev-hdf names the partition DH1 to avoid clash with system DH0

Both HDDs defaulting to DH0 (rdbtool's default) caused OS4 to mount just
the system drive; the dev drive showed up as an unmountable 'please
insert DevDrive:' phantom. Passing name=DH1 makes it unambiguous.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* scripts: attach dev HDF to sam460ex sii3112 ide.1 explicitly

The implicit -drive if=ide,index=1 form was leaving the dev HDF
invisible to OS4 — Media Toolbox showed a single drive despite
QEMU accepting the command. Root cause: sam460ex's on-board sii3112
SATA controller exposes two 1-unit buses (ide.0 and ide.1), not the
classic master/slave two-slot layout. QEMU pre-populates ide.1 with
an empty ide-cd, so index=1 collides with that default CD-ROM
device (bus supports only 1 unit).

Explicit -drive if=none,id=devdrv + -device ide-hd,bus=ide.1,unit=0
overrides the default CD and lands the dev HDF where OS4 expects to
see the second SATA disk.

Discovered via qemu monitor `info qtree` after the previous attempt
failed with "Can't create IDE unit 1, bus supports only 1 units".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* scripts: dev HDF uses realistic 1040×16×63 CHS geometry

amitools' auto-selected geometry (32768 cyl × 1 head × 32 sec) triggered
OS4 Media Toolbox's 'serious errors' warning and stopped the sii3112
SATA driver from auto-mounting the drive on boot. Classic PC-style
16 heads × 63 sectors is what the SATA driver expects; 1040 cyls at
that ratio gives exactly 512 MB.

Note: chs= only takes effect at CREATE time — subsequent `open` calls
re-detect geometry from file size and land on the same broken default.
So the script now deletes and recreates the HDF (only when FORCE=1)
instead of trying to re-init an existing container.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* examples: bump for void_trader PPC (a5c174e)

* scripts: deploy-os4 nudges OS4 to reload dir after xdftool write

When QEMU is running against the HDF, xdftool writes go straight to
disk but OS4's filesystem has already cached the directory. New files
are invisible until something forces a re-scan.

If devbench is up on 127.0.0.1:3000 and reachable, deploy-os4.sh now
POSTs `diskchange DH1:` through the bridge after each write. OS4
re-reads the directory blocks and the new file appears in `list DH1:`
immediately. Fails silently if devbench / bridge isn't up (user runs
diskchange manually in that case).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs+scripts: consolidate dual-arch (68k + PPC) support

Unify the classic 68k and new PPC OS4 paths so both targets work
from a single install with minimal per-invocation config. New/updated:

- scripts/install-toolchains.sh — one-shot Docker pull for both
  cross-compilers (amigadev/crosstools:m68k-amigaos +
  walkero/amigagccondocker:os4-gcc11-arm64/amd64 by host arch) plus
  the gdb-multiarch image. Idempotent.
- scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh gets --gdb / --gdb-port flags that enable

- scripts/gdb-os4.sh — wrapper that runs gdb-multiarch (from the

  to QEMU's stub via host.docker.internal.
- docker/Dockerfile.gdb — minimal ubuntu:24.04 + gdb-multiarch image
  (walkero's PPC toolchain image doesn't ship a gdb).
- docs/quickstart.md — unified walkthrough for both targets: install
  once, pick profile per session, deploy transparently. Cross-links
  the deeper docs.
- CLAUDE.md: bump the top-of-file description to mention both targets,
  add PPC C conventions (per-file lib-base gating,
  __USE_INLINE__/__USE_OLD_TIMEVAL__ flags, Delay(1)-triggers-DSI
  gotcha, no chip register access on sam460ex), add PPC build commands
  and dual-arch deploy paths.

Profile switching from devbench.toml already works and the web UI's
header badge shows arch/profile in orange (ppc) or blue (m68k). The
qemu-os4 profile's deploy_dir points at the .hdf and Deployer detects
that suffix + routes through scripts/deploy-os4.sh (xdftool). MCP
`amiga_deploy` and the web UI's Deploy button work transparently on

* examples: bump for void_trader CPU-burn frame cap (23e58ed)

  relative-path invocation works. On Linux, add --add-host=
  host.docker.internal:host-gateway so the GDB target resolves inside
  the container (macOS/Docker Desktop handles this automatically).

Devbench (Python):
- config.py save_config: now serialises active_profile, every
  [profiles.*] table (preserving unknown keys), and the [build] section
  (arch, docker_image). Earlier version silently wiped the qemu-os4
  profile on a web-UI Save. Added helper for TOML string escaping and
  scalar dumping. Verified via round-trip test.
- deployer.py deploy_smart: wrap the sync self.deploy() call with
  asyncio.to_thread so the xdftool subprocess (30 s timeout) doesn't
  freeze the ASGI event loop when deploy_dir is an HDF.
- emulator.py read_config / write_config: guard against an empty
  _config_file (Path("") resolves to CWD; read would return dir bytes
  and blow up, write would land at CWD/.tmp). Return "" / no-op for
  QEMU profiles that don't need a config file.

Bridge (C):
- system_inspector.c sys_handle_libfuncs: PPC branch returns
  "ERR|LIBFUNCS|not supported on OS4 (interface-based exec)" — the
  classic implementation walks a 68k jump-table format that doesn't
  exist on OS4.
- system_inspector.c sys_handle_capabilities: remove LIBFUNCS from the
  advertised list on PPC via a small conditional macro so hosts don't
  try to invoke it.
- system_inspector.c sys_handle_sysinfo: add __PPC__ branch that
  reports "PowerPC" up front, bypassing the 68k AttnFlags bitfield
  ladder that would otherwise mis-report "68000".

Docs:
- CLAUDE.md + docs/amigaos4-setup.md: consistent HDF concurrency
  warning — deploy writes to the raw HDF while OS4 holds it, both
  sides cache the FS independently, corruption is possible. Refuses
  by default (FORCE=1 to override), and the diskchange nudge only
  refreshes OS4's view, doesn't make the write atomic.
- docs/amigaos4-setup.md: document the clean first-run order
  (init-dev-hdf → start-qemu-os4 --install → start-qemu-os4) so users
  don't hit the missing-HDF error.

devbench.toml:
- qemu-os4 profile drops the fixed docker_image tag — the ppc-image.sh
  helper now selects it at build time based on the host arch.

Validation:
- All 8 scripts pass `bash -n`.
- Python round-trip test: load → apply qemu-os4 → save → reload → all
  4 profiles + active_profile + arch survive.
- PPC bridge rebuilds cleanly (272 KB daemon + 22 KB libbridge.a).
- Classic 68k bridge still builds cleanly.

* python-os4: CPython 3.12 phase-1 bootstrap scaffolding

Working starting point for porting CPython 3.12.7 to AmigaOS 4.1 PPC.
Not yet a runnable interpreter — see python-os4/README.md for the
"what works / what blocks" summary. Real-world Phase 1 estimate
holds: 1-2 more focused weeks to a linked python binary, 3-5 weeks
total to `print(1)` running.

What ships in this commit
- Dockerfile layering deadsnakes Python 3.12 over the walkero PPC
  toolchain (walkero/amigagccondocker:os4-gcc11-arm64) so
  PYTHON_FOR_BUILD version-matches the target.
- build.sh iteration script: configure / make / clean / shell.
  Force-includes amiga_shim.h into every CFLAGS invocation and
  overrides Modules/Setup.local after configure so our disable
  list stays in effect.
- setup.local disables ~30 stdlib modules whose C deps we haven't
  shimmed (_socket, _ssl, syslog, termios, _sqlite, mmap, fcntl,
  readline, _ctypes, _decimal, _elementtree, pyexpat, ...).
- amiga_shim.h/c: POSIX gap-fillers newlib omits.
  - Real stubs: unsetenv, initgroups, setrlimit, getrlimit
  - Prototype-only (function exists in newlib, header hides it):
    fileno, fdopen, popen, pclose
  - Constant defs: O_NOFOLLOW / O_CLOEXEC / O_DIRECTORY = 0
  - Signal / rlimit constants (RLIMIT_* set 0..9)
- configure.amigaos.patch: the entire CPython-source patch — 24
  lines, 2 hunks in Python-3.12.7/configure adding
  `*-*-amigaos*` cases so the triplet is a recognised cross target.
  Applied out-of-band; the CPython tree itself is git-ignored.

Progress markers reached
- configure completes with --host=powerpc-unknown-amigaos
- ~73 core interpreter .o files compile cleanly (ceval, compile,
  import, marshal, unicode, symtab, tracemalloc, GIL, ast, parser)
- Hard-float ABI matches newlib libc (was soft-float initially,
  broke linking against libgcc.so)
- SSIZE_MAX gap fixed via CFLAGS -D

Still blocking Phase 1
- Every make iteration reveals 1-2 more POSIX gaps to shim/skip.
  Currently: fork/execve/PyOS_AfterFork_Child family (deep — needs
  SystemTagList-based subprocess replacement long term), sundry
  socket/rlimit/signal constants, and open() flag constants.
- Once shims cover the last of them, the link step should run and
  we can try executing the binary under QEMU sam460ex to see
  what runtime blows up.

* start-qemu-os4: --net flag for user-mode NAT (e1000)

Off by default because base OS4 installs may not have Roadshow
configured; on with --net for AmiUpdate / web browsing / any
network-dependent step.

Motivated by the python-amigaos4 port: our interpreter is linked
against newlib.library 53.68+, but base OS4.1 FE ships 53.30 and
even Update 3 only reaches 53.34. Getting to 53.68 requires
AmiUpdate, which needs the guest to have working TCP/IP.

Also removes the outdated comment that said networking was
impossible because rtl8139 wasn't sam460ex-supported — e1000 is.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* start-qemu-os4: switch --net NIC from e1000 to rtl8139

Base OS4.1 FE ships rtl8139.device out of the box (via Devs/Networks). e1000 needs a driver install that isn't present. Realised while trying to configure networking for the python-amigaos4 AmiUpdate path.

* start-qemu-os4: use explicit -netdev + -device for rtl8139

The `-nic user,model=rtl8139` shorthand is silently rejected by QEMU's sam460ex machine ("not supported by this machine?"). The explicit two-flag form `-netdev user,id=n0 -device rtl8139,netdev=n0` works - QEMU attaches the card to the PCI bus and OS4 can enumerate it.

* docs: add OS4 networking + AmiUpdate procedure

Documents the QEMU rtl8139 setup that actually works on sam460ex (explicit -netdev + -device form; the -nic user,model=rtl8139 shorthand is silently rejected). Covers Roadshow config (SYS:Prefs/Internet, rtl8139.device unit 0, DHCP) and points at os4depot for the initial AmiUpdate install. Motivated by the python-amigaos4 port needing newlib.library 53.68+.

* mcp: add amiga_fetch_url + amiga_install_lha

Host does the HTTP work (curl-equivalent via urllib), then pushes the bytes to the Amiga over the serial bridge and (optionally) shells out to LhA for extraction. Composes cleanly with the existing push_file + script_execute primitives - no bridge protocol changes.

Motivating case: pulling amiupdate.lha from os4depot straight into RAM: without needing working networking on the OS4 side. Also useful for os4depot-hosted libraries we need to sideload for the python-amigaos4 port (newer newlib.library.kmod etc.).

* start-qemu-os4: hostfwd tcp:2347->guest:2345 for TCP bridge

The amiga-bridge daemon already supports TCP mode via bsdsocket.library (net_io.c) as used by the pi-amikit and real-amiga devbench profiles. Launch on OS4 with `amiga-bridge TCP 2345`. Host reaches it at 127.0.0.1:2347 via QEMU port forward. 2x throughput vs serial-over-TCP + reliable at 7 MB+ transfers (serial was failing intermittently).

* bridge PPC: default to TCP transport, qemu launcher: net-on default

Three linked changes so the QEMU/OS4 setup does the right thing out
of the box:

- amiga-bridge/src/main.c: on __PPC__ builds the default transport is
  now TCP :2345 (was serial). Serial is still reachable via the
  explicit 'SERIAL' arg. The pivot commit (task #48) made TCP the
  intended path; this makes it the actual path when the daemon is
  launched with no args from Workbench / a shell.
- scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh: default --net ON. The PPC bridge's TCP
  mode needs a NIC in the guest, so the script's job is to bring
  one up unless the caller explicitly says otherwise (--no-net).
- devbench.toml [profiles.qemu-os4]: connect port bumped 2346 -> 2347
  to match the hostfwd tcp:2347-:2345 the launcher sets up. This is
  the wire that runs bytes:
    devbench :2347 (host)
      -> QEMU hostfwd
      -> guest :2345
      -> amiga-bridge (TCP)

Fallback path (bridge with SERIAL arg + devbench on :2346) still
works if you set 'SERIAL' explicitly and bump the profile port back.

* start-qemu-os4: -device usb-tablet for absolute-position mouse

Fixes click-drift where the OS4 cursor visually is at one place but
the click event lands somewhere else — happens whenever the guest
frame size does not match the host window size (i.e. any zoom-to-fit
or high-DPI mac window). Common ppc-amigaos + QEMU + cocoa gotcha.

Same fix I applied on fix/devbench-tcp-keepalive; landing it here on
feat/fractalus too because this is where the current QEMU launcher
lives.

* tools: https_get — sidecar CLI for AmiSSL HTTPS from Python

Python-on-OS4's _ssl module can't do TLS end-to-end: its socket() opens
a bsdsocket handle via newlib's own bsdsocket base, and AmiSSL's
SSL_set_fd expects fds AmiSSL knows about — cross-base handoff returns
EBADF at handshake time (task #94). No easy fix without patching either
_ssl.c or newlib to share bsdsocket bases.

Workaround: ship AmiSSL's OpenSSL CLI + this thin wrapper, and have
Python shell out via os.system with pipe redirection. Google's homepage
returns 81KB of HTML end-to-end through this path from Python-on-OS4.

- https_get.c is a self-contained C client (~70KB stripped) that opens
  bsdsocket + amissl explicitly and uses BOTH via InitAmiSSL. It works
  for the socket + TLS handshake round-trip when linked against
  libamisslauto BUT still hits the same fd-mismatch EBADF Python does —
  kept here as reference material for the interop bug and as a
  build-recipe example for future ppc-amigaos tools.

- The actual working path is:
    type <req> | DH1:openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername SNI \
      -CApath DH1:AmiSSL/Certs -quiet >out
  See python-amigaos4/amiga_bindings/amiga/https/ for the Python
  wrapper that packages this.

- Makefile builds via walkero/amigagccondocker:os4-gcc11-arm64; the
  compiled binary is .gitignore'd — rebuild via `make` in docker.

* start-qemu-os4: zoom-to-fit=off by default, fixes mouse-pointer drift

Symptom: click on a menu item, OS4 registers the click 20-40px above.
Cursor visually where you moved it, but hit location is wrong. Gets
worse as the QEMU window drifts further from the guest's native
framebuffer size — after several boots + resizes today it was 30+
pixels off.

Root cause: with -display cocoa,zoom-to-fit=on the Cocoa layer scales
the guest's framebuffer to fill whatever window size you have, but
the USB tablet input path (added earlier for absolute mouse coords)
still reports at the guest's *native* resolution. Cocoa's scale
factor isn't applied to input events, only to output pixels — so
visible cursor and click coord diverge by exactly that factor.

Two workable options:
  1. Keep zoom-to-fit=on, use relative mouse — but then the cursor
     accumulates drift over time, worse than this bug.
  2. Turn zoom-to-fit OFF — window shows the framebuffer 1:1, tablet
     coords match what you see, cursor never drifts.

Went with (2). Now the window is fixed-size at the guest's native
resolution; users can Cmd-drag the corner if they want, but the
default is unambiguous.

Override kept per-run:
  DISPLAY_ARG=cocoa,zoom-to-fit=on ./scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh

* start-qemu-os4: revert to zoom-to-fit=on default, keep the opt-out

The previous fix (zoom-to-fit=off) made the window fixed at the
guest's native framebuffer — accurate mouse, but too small to
actually use. Prior default (zoom-to-fit=on) is resizable but has
the mouse-drift issue on macOS Retina.

Verdict: resizable-with-drift is the less-bad default for daily use.
Users who need pixel-exact mouse (e.g. mid-app menu clicking) opt in:

    DISPLAY_ARG=cocoa,zoom-to-fit=off,show-cursor=on ./scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh

Better long-term: raise OS4's ScreenMode inside Prefs → Screen. A
1024×768 or 1280×1024 guest gives a bigger window at 1:1 AND keeps
the mouse accurate.

Documented both paths in the header comment.

* start-qemu-os4: drop usb-tablet by default, use click-to-grab

Symptom: clicking in the QEMU window did nothing — mouse cursor
visible but not captured, no clicks reaching OS4. -usb -device
usb-tablet requires OS4's USB stack to recognise the HID device;
after today's crash-reboot cycles it stopped doing so and left the
window mouseless.

Reverted to the classic QEMU-Cocoa click-to-grab mode: click in the
window → mouse captured, use it, Ctrl-Opt-G to release. Works on
any guest, no driver assumptions, no drift on Retina (deltas are
relative and don't care about scale factor).

Tablet still available for anyone who wants the hover-to-click UX:
    USB_TABLET=1 ./scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh

Now prints a Mouse: line at startup so users can see which mode is
active without inspecting the QEMU cmdline.

* scripts: mac2amiga + amiga2mac — Mac<->Amiga clipboard bridge

The QEMU cocoa display doesn't share clipboard between Mac host and
guest, so you can't cmd-c on the Mac and paste on the Amiga. These
two tiny wrappers use the amiga-devbench HTTP API
(/api/tools/clipboard/set and .../get) that pipes text over the
serial bridge to the Amiga's clipboard.unit.

  mac2amiga    reads Mac clipboard (or stdin) and puts it on the
               Amiga clipboard, ready to paste in any Amiga app
  amiga2mac    pulls the Amiga's clipboard onto the Mac clipboard
               (or stdout if piped)

Both take DEVBENCH_URL env override, default http://localhost:3000/.

Tested both directions end-to-end against the current QEMU OS4 target.

events.title: file_transfer: resume push after bridge reconnect instead of aborting (#13)
events.message:
file_transfer: resume push after bridge reconnect instead of aborting (#13)

Long file pushes (3MB+ is common) frequently wedge the OS4 bridge mid-
transfer under sustained data flow.  Before this: the chunker printed
'Failed at chunk N (offset X/Y)' and returned a bytes_transferred=X
error, and the caller had to restart the whole transfer from byte 0.

After: on _push_chunk failure with a dead connection, block up to
120s waiting for the SerialConnection auto-reconnect loop to bring
the bridge back, then re-issue the SAME chunk at the SAME offset via
WRITEFILE (which addresses by explicit offset — no append weirdness).
Continue until done or MAX_RESUMES=5 outages exhausted.

Net effect: a 4MB push that hits a 30-second bridge stall completes
after ~40 seconds total, instead of blowing away 2.9MB of already-
transferred data and starting from scratch.

Cap at 5 resumes so a permanently dead bridge fails visibly instead
of looping forever.  Every reconnect logs the offset it's resuming
from so the operator sees what happened.
events.author: geekychris

events.title: devbench + qemu-os4: TCP bridge as default, plus TCP keepalive on host (#12)
events.message:
devbench + qemu-os4: TCP bridge as default, plus TCP keepalive on host (#12)

* devbench: TCP keepalive + tighter silence timeout for faster peer-death detection

QEMU killed hard (or cable pulled, container OOM'd, etc.) leaves the
TCP socket in a half-open state — reader.read() blocks forever because
the kernel never gets FIN. Previously we only noticed after the
45-second bridge-silence watchdog fired.

Two changes:
- Set SO_KEEPALIVE on the connected socket, with TCP_KEEPIDLE=10s /
  TCP_KEEPINTVL=5s / TCP_KEEPCNT=3 (macOS TCP_KEEPALIVE fallback for
  the idle knob). ~25s to detect dead peer at the TCP layer, then our
  existing _tcp_read_loop finally clause + _schedule_reconnect kick in.
- Drop BRIDGE_SILENCE_TIMEOUT from 45s -> 15s. Bridges send HB every
  ~1s in normal operation; 15s comfortably covers any legit long
  SCRIPT / LISTDIR pause but catches "peer went away and TCP hasn't
  noticed yet" an order of magnitude faster.

Net effect: after a QEMU restart, devbench reconnects on its own in
15-25s instead of 45s+ (or never, if the peer never sends FIN and the
silence watchdog somehow missed).

Repro that motivated this: kill QEMU while devbench is connected,
restart QEMU on the same port. Before this patch, amiga_ping kept
timing out until an explicit amiga_connect nudge. After: connection
is restored automatically.

* qemu-os4: default to TCP-over-bsdsocket bridge transport, add profile

The OS4 amiga-bridge speaks TCP-over-bsdsocket by default (task #48 in
CLAUDE.md's history — the pivot) and it's the faster + more robust path
than serial.device. Wire QEMU + devbench so this is the default rather
than the fallback.

- scripts/start-qemu-os4.sh: add -net user,hostfwd=tcp:127.0.0.1:2345-:2345
  so the guest's bridge listen socket surfaces at 127.0.0.1:2345 on the
  host. Docstring at the top explains transport choice + how to launch
  the bridge on OS4 side (`DH1:amiga-bridge TCP`).
- devbench.toml: new [profiles.qemu-os4] block, mode=tcp, port 2345.
  Use with `python3 -m amiga_devbench --profile qemu-os4`.
- devbench-ppc.toml: standalone PPC config bumped from :2346 (serial
  fallback) to :2345 (TCP) with a note explaining both.

Serial fallback on :2346 stays wired up — bridge launched with no arg
still uses serial.device, still reachable at 127.0.0.1:2346 via QEMU's
existing -serial tcp:: forwarding. Useful for console output and for
diagnosing bsdsocket-side issues.

* start-qemu-os4: use -netdev/-device (modern syntax) so sam460ex accepts the NIC

Old -net nic,model=rtl8139 form silently failed with 'not supported by
this machine' on sam460ex — OS4 saw no ethernet device at all, and 'ping
google.com' failed even after Roadshow was up. Modern -netdev id=n0 +
-device rtl8139,netdev=n0 is what sam460ex's PCI bus actually wants.

* os4-qemu-config.md: reference doc + zoom-to-fit=on for resizable window

Captures the actually-working sam460ex + rtl8139 + hostfwd + TCP-bridge
config in one place. Points explicitly at the two things that keep
getting reverted:
  1. the modern -netdev/-device NIC syntax (old -net nic shorthand
     silently fails on sam460ex),
  2. launching the bridge with 'TCP' arg (serial fallback masquerades
     as 'connecting' but drops all messages).

Also -display cocoa,zoom-to-fit=on so the QEMU window is draggable
instead of stuck at the guest's frame size.

* start-qemu-os4: refresh banner + add usb-tablet for accurate clicks

Banner text still said 'Serial: TCP port 2346' and told you to connect
devbench to that — leftover from the pre-TCP-bridge days. Rewritten
to lead with the TCP-mode bridge on :2345 and explicitly call the
serial :2346 path what it now is (console + fallback).

Also added -usb -device usb-tablet so QEMU sends absolute pointer
coords instead of relative deltas. Fixes click-drift where the OS4
pointer visually is at one place but the click event lands somewhere
else — happens whenever the guest's frame size doesn't equal the
host window size (e.g. any zoom-to-fit resize).

events.title: Fix screen hover tooltip CCK/plane-address accuracy
events.message:
Fix screen hover tooltip CCK/plane-address accuracy

CCK was derived by snapping to the nearest matching BPL1 DMA-fetch
event, so it only appeared where bitplane DMA happened to land on
that exact word (blank over background/border) and jumped in
word-sized (~8 CCK) steps instead of tracking the hovered column
exactly. It's now computed directly from the hovered canvas-x via
the same beam-position formula computeSlotFromBeamPosition already
uses, so it's always present and exact.

Plane addresses now come from a new per-pixel PixelSnapshot.planeAddr
array, populated inline in decodeScreenPixels' existing per-pixel bit
decode (which already resolves BPLCON1 scroll and per-plane DDF
margin correctly), instead of a separate word-index guess in
computeHoverExtra. That guess didn't account for scroll delay
extending the display past a line's nominal fetch-window width, so
the last few scrolled-in pixels of a line showed no address/colour
info at all. Fixed by extending decodeScreenPixels' per-line decode
width by that line's own BPLCON1 delay, mirroring the existing
head-side margin-word compensation at the tail.

events.title: Minesweeper: Fix potential overflow in victory check
events.message:
Minesweeper: Fix potential overflow in victory check

This doesn't affect the current boards (which max out at 16x16) but
with a larger board the number of unrevealed cells would be greater
than 255 and overflow an 8-bit counter. Switch to a 16-bit counter.

events.title: feat: Phase 4 features — CPU gating, roundtrip test, fuzzing, DC.X/DC.P, expr consolidation, floppy filesystem, OPT tracking (#12)
events.message:
feat: Phase 4 features — CPU gating, roundtrip test, fuzzing, DC.X/DC.P, expr consolidation, floppy filesystem, OPT tracking (#12)

Implements all remaining Phase 4 roadmap items from plan.md:

- 4.2: central mnemonic->min-CPU gating table (m68k-core/src/cpu_gate.rs),
  wired in at a single point before dispatch. Closes several previously
  ungated mnemonics (CAS2, PACK/UNPK, RTM, BKPT, RTD, MOVEC, FBcc/FDBcc/
  FTRAPcc/FNOP all silently accepted on --cpu 68000 before). CLI --cpu
  validation added (unknown CPU strings previously mapped to the most
  permissive level instead of being rejected).
- 4.3: systematic encode->decode->reencode roundtrip test over all 71
  golden vectors. Found and fixed: missing size suffix on several
  disassembled mnemonics (TST/CLR/NOT/NEG/NEGX/ADDQ/SUBQ/EOR/ANDI/EORI/
  CMPI/ADDI/SUBI/ORI), and MOVEC entirely undetectable by the decoder
  (no opcode pattern).
- 4.4: cargo-fuzz setup, 6 targets (disassemble, amiga_hunk_parse,
  assembler_pipeline, floppy_adf, floppy_uae, floppy_ipf) + CI smoke job.
  Found and fixed 8 real panics/overflows/OOMs: UTF-8 char-boundary
  panics in tokens.rs and three parens-register parsers, an OOM from an
  unbounded allocation in amiga_hunk.rs's Reader::bytes, index-out-of-
  bounds on UNPK/PACK/CAS with no operands, an i32::MIN abs() panic in
  format_signed, integer overflow in a hunk symbol address computation
  and in 7 branch-displacement computations in the disassembler, and a
  hunk body/declared-size mismatch causing an out-of-range slice.
- 4.5: real DC.X (IEEE-754 80-bit extended) and DC.P (packed BCD)
  conversion from decimal literals, replacing the previous hex/raw-only
  limitation. $-prefixed hex literals still work as a raw fallback.
- 4.6: removed m68k-core::expr (no parser, no symbol table integration,
  zero external callers) in favor of the already-canonical
  m68k-asm::directives::parse_simple_expr evaluator. Verified the
  consolidated evaluator doesn't have the recursion-limit issue expr.rs
  originally had.
- 4.7: m68k-floppy gains read-only OFS/FFS filesystem support
  (amigados.rs: root block/hash table traversal, file header + data
  block reassembly for both OFS and FFS) and ADF image writing
  (adf_writer.rs: blank image creation, bootblock checksum compute/
  verify/repair, empty-disk formatting). CLI gains --list/--extract/
  --fix-bootblock.
- 4.9: OPT directive now tracks flag state (OptState) instead of
  silently discarding every argument; malformed entries warn.

All three CI checks (cargo test --all, clippy -D warnings, fmt --check)
pass throughout, including for the separate fuzz/ crate.

events.title: Redesign blit-region highlight to compute chip addresses directly
events.message:
Redesign blit-region highlight to compute chip addresses directly

Replaces the old fetch-time cursor/marking approach (which required
mirroring custom.c's own fetch-timing internals and drifted out of
sync at region edges) with a draw-time lookup: bvis_project now
derives the chip-RAM word a displayed pixel came from directly from
a per-line snapshot of each plane's bitplane pointer, fetch mode, and
real fetched-word count, then queries the blitter write-tap for that
exact address.

Fixes several edge-alignment bugs found along the way: DDFSTRT/DDFSTOP
region-width clamping using a direct per-plane fetch counter instead of
an unreliable display-side counter, and BPLCON1 scroll-delay handling
for the read side (using the clean toscr_delay_shifter source rather
than the SPEEDUP-contaminated toscr_delay_adjusted).

Rebuilds puae.wasm/puae.js from the updated libretro-uae submodule.

events.title: joust: verify the ctx name map — 73/75 confirmed, 37 renamed, +1 function
events.message:
joust: verify the ctx name map — 73/75 confirmed, 37 renamed, +1 function

The 56 '# ctx' names (behaviour-inferred, never body-read) are now
verdicts: 73 of 75 functions CONFIRMED from the 68000 asm (Ghidra
renders most register-argument routines as bare 'return;', so
tools/prg_dis.py disassembly was the evidence surface, not decomp.c
alone), 37 RENAMED with recorded evidence, 2 honestly still ctx
(sprite-render questions that extract_graphics.py would settle).

Headline: the whole 'graphics/input' cluster around 0x10a56 was the
SOUND DRIVER — set_color_lvl is play_sound (XBIOS Dosound via a
priority-gated sound_table), read_key_flag is snd_poll_done (Giaccess
mixer poll), init_gfx is snd_tone_sweep, wait_vsync is read_joysticks
(IKBD interrogate 0x16 — nothing waits on vblank), poll_key is
poll_quit_key (Ctrl-C: silence PSG, save HIGH.SCO, restore, Pterm).
Root cause is a broken XBIOS table in the SHARED trap-annotate tools
(decimal opcode numbers entered as hex: 0x20 labelled Supexec is
actually Dosound, 0x1f/0x18/0x21 likewise, 0x19 Ikbdws + 0x1c Giaccess
missing) — fixed in tools/ in the next commit, not here.

Other substantive renames: the egg lifecycle family (update_eggs +
erase/draw/physics — 'alloc_object' allocated nothing), spawn_wave is
update_pterodactyl (4-slot table, edge entry, mouth-only kill),
advance_scroll is rng_advance (walks the program image as an RNG),
count_objects_and_pad is a frame-time equaliser, the troll draw/erase
pair was swapped, raise_floor/paint_floor_row/dissolve_platforms are
the wave-transition world morphing. Two stubs were real (fill-pattern
builder, sprite-base select); screen_to_pos is dead code with a broken
x reconstruction (x22 vs x16). Untagged-name correction:
xbios_setcolor -> flash_hiscore_color. Var fixes: p1_x/p2_x pointed at
y; num_players is players_alive; screen_left/right are platform-0's
ground x range.

Map now documents the 0x4e-byte object record (incl. the egg
sub-record and ASCII score digits), the flags-word bit map, platform /
spawn / message / sound table formats: vars 26 -> 95, cmts 21 -> 76,
75/75 exported clean.

Leads recorded in README: make_fill_pattern's four byte-identical
btst/or blocks look like a possible depack_gamex.py LZSS over-repeat
(a live Hatari dump would settle it); ghidra_proj project.prp OWNER
was stale (ganneheim -> geogeo, gitignored file, buggyboy's has the
same issue).

Small debts (all recorded leftovers from the cleanup/naming arcs):
- PORTING.md intro: the 'Phase B has started… a leg still cannot be
  finished' progress paragraphs were weeks stale — replaced with the
  true current state (port complete, perf campaigns closed; the doc
  stays as the how-to recipe).
- render/atari/README.md: 'Hatari needs a 4 MiB machine' predates the
  slice-10 diet — now says runners default to 4 MiB but the game needs
  1 MB (the --memsize 1 goldens are the standing pin).
- gen_hud_fixture.py -> hud_capture.py (git mv): it generates nothing
  since the demo retirement — it is the HUD-input capture library
  gen_game_fixture.py calls. All 6 references updated (Makefile
  GATE_DEPS, the import, README table, PORTING, adapter.py comment).
- results.c: RS_SCORE_NUM_M1 merged into NUM_MAX_CELLS_M1 — same value,
  same fact (draw_num_thunk's preset cell count), one name (CLAUDE.md §5).
- PERF30's 0xfff8 note CLOSED with a keep-all-three verdict: COL_ALIGN /
  COARSE_MASK / RR_D7_WORD_MASK are three different facts coinciding at
  one value — folding them would assert an equivalence the engines
  don't share (§6's coincidence rule). Recorded so it isn't re-opened.
- .claude/settings.json: dead run_hatari.py-as-a-command permission
  removed (retired with the HUD demo).

C5 campaign close (PERF30 closing note): two slices landed, STE gate
105.47 -> 97.75 ms / drive 97.34 -> 89.80 over the campaign, play-test
PASSED (user, 2026-07-27 — controls, audio by ear, side-by-side vs the
original). Remaining faithful levers quantified and DECLINED: the
one-excursion Supexec (0.80-1.47 ms gate, supervisor-stack risk, and
the C5 routes already batch their own passes — the cheap 80% of the
idea) and build_road_geometry 1.61x (~1.5 ms, CPU-shaped, an A-series
item not an STE one); neither moves the locked present cadence, the
player-visible surface. Beyond them: Tier-C fidelity trades only (C2/
C3), sign-off-gated. Re-open only for those or a 1 MB margin squeeze.

Pins: BUGGYBOY.PRG byte-identical (133cae22..); make test 730 (gate
rebuilds through the renamed module).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: retire the standalone HUD demo
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: retire the standalone HUD demo

The demo (render/atari/main.c + build.sh + run.sh -> HUD.PRG) was the
pre-game HUD-only on-target pin. It stopped linking when hud.c grew
calls into events.c (fixing the link set cascades ~15 symbols — most of
the game), its HUD.PRG was a stale Jul-21 binary whose MATCH validated
stale code, and the full game + frame-0 golden harness has long
superseded everything it proved. Retired rather than repaired.

Removed: main.c, build.sh, run.sh (git rm); stale HUD.PRG / hud.bin /
hud_fixture.h / golden.bin / palette.bin artifacts (untracked; backed up
in the session scratchpad).

Surgery, with the dependency evidence:
- golden.bin/palette.bin were demo-only: written only by
  gen_hud_fixture.main() (invoked only by build.sh), read only as
  verify_frame's DEFAULTS — the sole live caller (run_golden.py) passes
  explicit per-leg paths. Generation removed with the demo.
- gen_hud_fixture.py stays as a pure capture library (gen_game_fixture
  imports its asset/palette baking; Makefile GATE_DEPS lists it as a
  dependency source) — main()/CONTROLS gone, __main__ exits with a
  pointer. Now-misnamed; rename deferred as it ripples through 4 files.
- run_hatari.py is now explicitly a library module: demo main() gone,
  __main__ exits with a pointer to run_golden.py; verify_frame paths
  are required args; the needs_data opt-out existed only for HUD.PRG
  (all six call sites resolved True) so staging is unconditional —
  behaviour-identical for every live caller.
- Docs: render/atari/README.md reframed around the game + golden
  harness with a one-paragraph history of the demo; PORTING.md step 7
  and docs/binary-formats.md's verify example now cite run_golden.py.

Pins: BUGGYBOY.PRG byte-identical (133cae22..addbd); make test 730;
goldens st+ste MATCH; run_ste_selftest MATCH (covers the needs_data
removal); all runner modules import clean; disk/ = the trio.

Noted, not touched: .claude/settings.json carries a now-dead permission
entry for run_hatari.py-as-a-command (user-owned settings).

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: readability sweep — name the remaining magic literals
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: readability sweep — name the remaining magic literals

Zero-cost by construction and by pin: #define/enum introduction, literal
-> name substitution and comment fixes only — BUGGYBOY.PRG is
BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-sweep build (sha256 133cae22..addbd, re-hashed
after every file), make test 730, STE sweep 5,624/0, goldens 5/5.

Reconstruction (naming only, no values changed):
- sound.c/sound.h — the user-named priority: the note-stream command
  bytes 0x80..0x8c are now the SND_OP_* opcode family (REST, FLAGS_CLEAR,
  PORTAMENTO, GLIDE_DOWN/UP, LOOP, VIBRATO, SET_BIT1, END_TUNE, SET_F13,
  SET_BIT12, SET_R6_SRC, ENV_HOLD), each grounded in its handler +
  recreate reference + docs/sound.md; unrecovered musical intents keep
  the offset+role convention (SET_BIT1/SET_BIT12 say so). Plus
  SND_FLAG_ON, SND_VC_NOTE_HOLD, SND_MOD_RESTART/VALUE_MASK,
  SND_EG_PHASE_MASK, and a separate VC_EF_* vocabulary for SND_VC_ENV_FLG
  (borrowing VC_F_* would have asserted a shared vocabulary the driver
  doesn't have). A typedef compile-time assert pins the family to the
  dispatch window (SND_OP_REST == SND_CMD_LO, ENV_HOLD == +12) so a
  renumbered opcode cannot compile silently.
- results.c (LEG_*), events.c (FX_* block offsets + flag masks),
  object_list.c, object.c, road.c (reused road_const.h names), flow.c,
  gameplay.c, blitter_sweep.c (SWEEP_LOG_MAX), hud.c, assets.c, blit.c,
  player.c.
- Deferrals closed: object.c's duplicate COL_ALIGN + OBJ_ROAD_START_OFF
  now come from blit_const.h / scroll_const.h; BLT_ENDMASK_ALL applied in
  blitter_selftest.c; crash-lock literal duplicated across
  events.c/player.c hoisted to game.h (RM_CRASH_LOCK_SPIN/_SLOW).

Review gate (high) caught five false comment claims the hash could not:
the endmask2 absolute (blitter_skew puts a colour fill there), the
results.c divider side/target, blit.c's 'no second copy' claim, the
SND_TUNE_ON 0xff aliasing SND_TEMPO_ACC (load-bearing arithmetic, not
just 'nonzero'), and an SND_OP_ENV_HOLD comment claiming unconditionally
what only the shipped tune data guarantees (now honestly unpinned in a
comment: 0x8c always precedes a note in SND_CONST).

Deliberately unnamed: byte extractions (& 0xff), dbf sentinels,
geometry.c's nibble fixed-point masks (function comment covers them),
psg_regs/psg_src table values. Still open (recorded in PERF30): 0xfff8
has three legitimate names; results.c's NUM_MAX_CELLS_M1 duplicate.

Docs: docs/sound.md gained the opcode table; PERF30 A3 dedup deferral
marked closed.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 2 — HUD dashboard composite on the blitter
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 2 — HUD dashboard composite on the blitter

Route (byte-exact, fourth blitter route, second table-less one):
- src/blitter_dash.c: 8-pass AND/OR cookie-cut of the phase-7 dashboard
  composite — 4x LOP=AND from each group's mask word, 4x LOP=OR from
  {ink_a, ink_b, ink_b, ink_c}; x_count 8 groups x y_count 40 rows,
  src/dst pitch both 104. THE finding: ARENA_ROW_STRIDE ==
  SCREEN_ROW_BYTES (static-asserted), so the chip reads the LIVE per-leg
  art IN PLACE — no materialised stream, no invalidation, +16 B BSS, and
  the mid-leg probe_collision word mutation cannot go stale. Poke-batched
  (36 register writes vs blit_run's 136), ONE Supexec, shared-bus restart
  loop (HOG A/B: only ~0.5 ms better, declined per the slice-1 policy;
  GAME_DASH_HOG=1 knob). Bound on the blitter probe alone.
- include/dash_const.h: ONE home for the dashboard geometry — collapses
  DASHBOARD_DST (hud.c literal), DASH_ROWS/GROUPS (independent copies in
  plane.h AND events.c), ARENA_ROW_STRIDE and RM_DASH_SRC_OFF (events.c +
  results.c); game_main.c pins the adapter-baked ARENA_DASH_SRC_OFF equal
  by static assert.
- The census's 7-pass refinement is algebraically WRONG (planes 1/2 share
  ink_b but not background: ROAD_TOP_FILL puts 0x0000 vs 0xFFFF under
  them) — shipped as CAUGHT sweep mutation 14 instead of code. It passes
  on the all-opaque baked atlas (14/16 catches): a baked-art-only pin
  would have blessed it — the dash_pristine trap, now a measurement.

Cadence (leg 0): STE gate 99.25 -> 97.75 ms (-1.5%), drive 90.72 ->
89.80 (-1.0%); ST bit-identical at the gate, drive delta is tick-phase
noise (draw_frame cycle-identical under Musashi). Realized saving is
~half the census projection (isolated-loop vs in-frame measurement gap;
flagged honestly in BLIT_STE_SPEC §17 rather than repeating ~3.3 ms).

Harness:
- src/blitter_sweep.c + run_ste_sweep.py: dashboard section — CPU vs
  blitter over all 5 legs' REAL live art (init_leg_dash +
  draw_leg_labels + a marker-stepped variant) + baked atlas +
  all-transparent extremes, over seeded-LCG and top-fill backgrounds
  (a uniform background hid mutation 14 — vacuity hole closed); a
  distinct-art hash count (must be 8) pins the staging itself.
- Mutations 11-14 (LOP swap / x_count+1 / y_inc short / p2-copy) all
  CAUGHT, 1-10 unregressed; per-route positive mutation selectors.
- game_main.c + run_cadence.py: dash routed/declined counters
  (201/251 routed, 0 declined); VBLS_PER_FRAME_HEADROOM 12 -> 16 +
  CELL_TIMEOUT_S so the stock-ST gate cell completes (slice-1 deferral).
- Pins: make test 730; sweep 5,624/0-XOR; goldens x5 st + x5 ste at
  default AND --memsize 1; A/B 0-mismatch; 1 MB STE all four routes
  bound, free TPA 184,188.

Memory: +16 B BSS -> 1 MB STE margin 9,564 -> 9,548 B.

Docs: BLIT_STE_SPEC §17 (+ §7 item 1 closed measured-NO-GO: CLIP is
0.225 ms/frame, objshift2 issues zero clip calls in real play; §14 muluw
note closed NO-GO on size: 0.028 ms for 5,120 B of margin); PERF30 C5
slice-2 note + census closures; README/STATUS: draw_hud is 19.06 ms on
LIVE art, not 16.27 — the published number was measured on the baked
opaque atlas (baked-vs-live footnote added).

Known honest gaps (named in §17/STATUS): the odd-address tripwire is
structurally unreachable (like slice 1's); the 24-bit address truncation
predates all four routes; the boot bind is evidenced only by the cadence
route counters.
events.author: geogeo28

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 1 — road fine-scroll on the blitter
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C5 slice 1 — road fine-scroll on the blitter

Route (byte-exact, third blitter route, the first with no lookup table):
- src/blitter_scroll.c: the 13,440-B constant top fill = TWO source-less
  passes (HOP=ONE, LOP=ONE/ZERO over the even/odd plane-word pair grid,
  write-only bus cycles); the band copy = ONE whole-band blit (+ a wrap
  blit when edge>=1, skipped at edge==0 — x_count 0 means 65,536); the
  4-word masked seam stays on the CPU, after the main blit. All passes in
  ONE Supexec, on the shared-bus restart loop (HOG measured 1.0% faster,
  declined — a ~3 ms whole-CPU freeze no pin can see; GAME_SCROLL_HOG=1
  keeps the A/B reproducible). Bound on the blitter probe ALONE, before
  table placement can veto anything — a 1 MB STE that loses the object
  tables keeps the scroll on the chip.
- include/scroll_const.h: ONE home for the scroll geometry + the shared
  head (rm_scroll_advance) and seam row both routes must run identically.
- src/scroll.c: split into head + rm_scroll_draw (the byte-exact
  reference); copy_run rewritten as a post-increment pointer walk — the
  split alone cost +13,690 cyc/frame (GCC stopped strength-reducing across
  the boundary); the rewrite recovered it and 1,254 more (11.91 ms, ST
  gate 130.30 / drive 99.40 — the ST got slightly FASTER).
- include/blitter.h + src/blitter.c: blit_poke split out of blit_run;
  blit_start_and_wait_shared — §2's documented restart loop was broken
  (no explicit start: first bset reads pre-start BUSY=0 and falls through
  after one 64-word burst), corrected here and in the spec.

Cadence (leg 0): STE gate 105.47 -> 99.25 ms (-5.9%), drive 97.34 ->
90.72 (-6.8%); vs stock ST now gate -23.8% / drive -8.7%.

Harness:
- src/blitter_sweep.c + run_ste_sweep.py: exhaustive 640-case road-scroll
  section (every reachable hscroll_pos, both delta signs, whole-ScrollState
  compare, guard bands); mutations 7-10 (fill LOP / x_count+1 / no-wrap /
  seam-first) all CAUGHT, 1-6 unregressed; per-route mutation gating so a
  scroll mutation no longer inflates the skew table by 61 KB.
- game_main.c + run_cadence.py: scroll routed/declined counters in the
  cadence tail (gate 201/0, drive 251/0).
- Pins: sweep 5,608/0-XOR; goldens x5 st + x5 ste at default AND
  --memsize 1; A/B 0-mismatch; make test 730.

item updated; road-scroll route itself is immune — no table).

README perf+memory tables, STATUS blit_road_scroll row.

(Musashi, identical staged gate frame — the original reproduces Part 0
to the cycle: 880,376 cyc / 110.05 ms):

  ratio 0.808): ~100.1 ms = ~0.91x the original — the first
  configuration where the port beats the hand-written original,
  at byte-identical pixels. The original never touches the blitter
  (verified: zero FFFF8Axx refs), so 110.05 is its STE number too.

48,632 B program (text carries globals + stack; data=0 bss=0) + one
Malloc of exactly 388,616 B (the same number the remaster's arena
models) = 437,248 B TPA held, 469,248 incl. the TOS-owned second
screen (physbase_tbl[4] IS buf_aux — it allocates only one screen of
its own). START.PRG's hard-coded 0x77000 scratch pins a 512 KB ST
design target (medium-high confidence): the earlier '512 KB was not
enough' claim in §15 was unsupported and is corrected — the remaster
needs 1 MB (as required); the original was likely a 512 KB title.
A 512 KB remaster would be a separate ~270 KB campaign.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 10 — 1 MB diet: fits a 1 MB ST and STE like the original
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 10 — 1 MB diet: fits a 1 MB ST and STE like the original

Reconstruction: two measurement-first moves take the shipping footprint
1,132,000 -> 707,840 B, under the measured 1 MB TPA (EmuTOS 905,448 B,
TOS 1.04 940,906 — Malloc(-1) probe at --memsize 1).

(1) The 2x128 KB SCREEN_OVERDRAW tails were sized to folklore: the reach
census (tools/reach_census.py + reach_probe.c, 5,240 composed + 4,000
forced-branch + 305 staged frames, all legs/scenes) measured the TRUE max
write past the visible 32,000 bytes at 8 BYTES (render_road; every object
engine stays below 32,000; nothing ever draws below the screen — the
off-screen cull idea is moot, both family predicates are horizontal).
Tail -> 0x1000 (512x margin; 36,096 keeps the 256-alignment), -253,952 B,
SCREEN_TAIL_LIVE(8) names the legitimate prefix. Standing guards so the
number can never rot into folklore again: the host suite canaries the
whole tail on every compared composed frame (mutation-checked: +0x800
draw reddens 16 tests), trace builds scan the full 4,088-byte tail per
present on target (mutation-checked: 100 presents trip), adapter.py
regex-reads both constants from game_main.c (one source of truth), and a
new 32-case below-screen sweep section pins the chip path against the
tail (all sweep comparisons now span screen + tail).

(2) skew_table + objsh2_cache (170,432 B) leave BSS: placed into the free
TPA above BSS at boot only when the blitter binds. os.s _start captures
the basepage and initial SP; rm_blit_bind_all computes the window
(base = align(p_bbase+p_blen), ceiling = min(p_hitpa, SP) - 16 KB stack
margin), memsets the block, hands out pointers. No Mshrink/Malloc — the
shell owns the TPA, the same 'ample RAM' the original relied on. The
unplaced state is TOTALLY safe: skew route starts latched-full, objsh2
declines on a null cache at its single entry, both flushes are null-safe
total functions, and the sweep consumes the bind result and reports a
clean DECLINE (verified via GAME_FORCE_NO_BLITTER) instead of crashing.

Harness: run_golden/run_ste_golden take --memsize (validated; arg wins
over RM_MEMSIZE); census/sweep pin themselves to 4 MB (CENSUS.PRG alone
is 1.4 MB); the reach census + dispatch sweep drivers land in tools/ so
the 8-byte number stays reproducible; blit.c's RM_HOST_ASSERT moved after
the clip test (fully-left-clipped no-write blits no longer abort the
host — the old code formed the wild pointer before checking).

Result: a 1 MB ST fits with +197 KB spare; a 1 MB STE fits WITH the
blitter tables placed (route live, 14,092 B spare above the stack margin
— the thin-margin watch item, observable via the cadence 'free TPA bytes'
counter). NEW STANDING PIN: goldens x5 st + x5 ste at --memsize 1, next
to x5 + x5 at default. make test 730 (host canary live); sweep 4,968
cases 0-XOR; A/B 0-mismatch; cadence in noise (105.47 / 97.34 ms), 0
canary trips.

Docs: BLIT_STE_SPEC §15 + supersession notes on every '2 MB minimum'
claim (§8/§11/§12/§14); PERF30 C4 slice-10 note.

events.title: release: v1.0.2 — resolve full-audit findings across the assembler, disassembler, and floppy readers (#11)
events.message:
release: v1.0.2 — resolve full-audit findings across the assembler, disassembler, and floppy readers (#11)

* fix: resolve all Phase 1-3 audit findings plus B10/Bcc.l relaxation

Fixes 22 bugs from the 2026-07-24 code audit (plan.md), ranging from a
completely inert branch-relaxation loop that silently desynced every
label after a short branch, an all-CPU Xn/displacement field swap in
brief-format indexed addressing, and wrong size bits on ADDA/SUBA/CMPA.L,
down to DoS-prone unbounded allocations in the floppy/hunk readers and
several panics on malformed input (integer overflow in DS/DCB, a
generic-recursion blowup in the expr.rs shift/neg evaluator).

Also implements two related Phase 4 features: FBcc/FDBcc now accept
label operands (B10), and Bcc/BRA/BSR branch relaxation gained a third
(68020+ long-displacement) size tier so out-of-word-range branches no
longer desync pass 1's label estimates from pass 2's actual encoding.

Every fix ships with regression tests; full suite (374 tests across all
crates), clippy, fmt, and the golden vector suite are all clean. See
plan.md for the itemized findings, root-cause notes, and verification
details.

* release: bump to v1.0.2

Bugfix release: 22 bugs found and fixed across all crates since v1.0.1
(dead branch-relaxation loop desyncing labels, brief-format indexed EA
field swap, ADDA.L/SUBA.L/CMPA.L size-bit encoding, DoS-prone unbounded
allocations in the floppy/hunk readers, several input-triggered panics,
and a handful of validation/output-format bugs). Also adds label
support for FBcc/FDBcc and a 68020+ long-branch size tier to relaxation.
No breaking API changes.

events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 9 — colour engine routed via the skew table: GO

Reconstruction: the shipping STE build routes rm_blit_objshift's BASE
family through a 128-entry no-eviction first-sight table (sprite key +
src arena pointer; rows grow on demand — prefix-stable, so a grown entry
is byte-identical) behind a boot-bound rm_blit_objshift_fn, mirroring the
objshift2 pattern (static CPU-asm default, no NULL window; seam in
object_list.c). -DRM_STE_OBJSH_ROUTE and its glue are deleted; the
pre-shift path and its 219 KB cache leave the shipping link (sweep-only,
still pinning the pre-shift recipe). Poke batching: blit_skew_begin owns
per-blit invariants incl. X_COUNT (latch-reloaded per line,
sweep-verified), passes grouped 4 AND then ORs — 42 register writes per
6-pass blit vs blit_run's 102; src_addr must re-poke (the chip walks it).
Shared blit_start_and_wait gives the HOG policy one owner;
rm_blit_bind_all / rm_blit_flush_all enumerate the engines once.

The census key-union measurement forced the per-leg flush: the census now
dumps sprite-key set contents and the runner unions legs 0-4 — converged
per-leg sets are 78/75/79/98/79 but the cross-leg union is EXACTLY 128,
the table capacity, zero headroom. start_leg() flushes (live set <= 98,
~30 spare, warm-up = the measured cold-table drive); a saturation latch
retires the route to the pixel-identical CPU hybrid on overflow instead
of scanning 128 probes per blit forever.

full-decline / latched-decline / flush-rearm; declined cases must leave
the framebuffer untouched then complete byte-exactly on the CPU) with the
NOGROW mutation caught only by it; cadence tail gets a magic+count header

(-19.2% vs stock ST), STE drive 99.22 -> 97.18 ms (-2.5% vs stock, NO

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 8 — hardware-skew colour recipe proven byte-exact
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: C4 slice 8 — hardware-skew colour recipe proven byte-exact

Reconstruction: src/blitter_skew.c blits the colour engine's BASE family
from UNSHIFTED, colour-independent bitmaps (M = ~(A|B|C)&D, planes A/B/C,
D&~M pre-folded) with skew = fine_x and NO FXSR/NFSR — the one polluted
source read per line lands exactly in the bits endmask1 = 0xFFFF>>k /
endmask3 = ~(0xFFFF>>k) already block, src_y_inc = 0 spans the packed row,
and the colour fill rides in the OR-pass endmasks (dst |= src & e), so the
bitmaps are colour-independent for arbitrary fills and a zero plane skips
its pass (game blits average 6 passes; fills verified binary over all
legs). Public seam pre-built for the slice-2 table: ObjshSkewBitmaps +
materialise-into-entry + blit-from-entry, with the scratch-backed wrapper
as the swept entry point.

Harness: the sweep runs THREE grids (objshift2 / pre-shift / skew) —
4800 cases, 0 mismatch (720 + 704 + 704 handled); non-vacuity is gated by
C-emitted expected-BASE counts in a self-describing report tail (a
forced-decline build fails loudly — verified); --mutate all catches all 5
recipe mutations (704/704/643/660/297 failing skew cases) with the other
grids skipped and clean; the bench checks the handled flag, times the blit
passes in isolation (the old subtract-two-totals estimate was an 8x-low
artifact), and adds a game-realistic binary-fill variant. Makefile: the
skew file joins STE_SRC (host .so exclusion — the missed line broke the
host link) and GATE_DEPS. objsh_is_base is shared (blitter.h) by the
census and skew paths; OBJSH_PLANES / OBJSH_MAX_ROWS hoisted to
blit_const.h as the single source; signed per-row source walk kept
host-safe (blit.c's form).

Cost (Hatari, swept shape base_cells 2 x 32 rows): materialise 13,520 cyc;
passes 16,680 synthetic / 12,920 game fill; CPU asm 33,960 — 0.78x with
per-call materialise, 0.38x from a table. Hatari's blitter timing is a
model, not cycle-exact hardware (recorded in §13).

Docs: BLIT_STE_SPEC §13 (calibrated register recipe + pins + caveats,
supersedes §11's 3264-case figure); PERF30 C4 slice-8 note.

Deferred to slice 2: per-pass register-poke batching, the shipping-path
clip-test dedup in blitter_objshift.c, the SYS_HZ200 -Warray-bounds
pragma. Validation: make test 730; shipping BUGGYBOY.PRG sha256-identical.

feat: Memotech MTX model grouping, ROM slots, BASIC pane + keyboard fixes (#26)

* docs: design for MTX model grouping, per-ROM slots, shorter labels

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: group MTX models, split firmware into five ROM slots, shorten labels

The Memotech hardware UI collapsed all five separately-fetched firmware ROMs
(OS/BASIC/ASSEM/CP/M/FDX) into one system-ROM slot, listed the three MTX models
loose in the machine menu, and used verbose hardware-option labels.

- Reuse the Spectrum multi-slot ROM mechanism at an 8K stride: models.ts now
  dispatches romPageSlotCount/defaultRomPageLabel per family and adds
  romSlotSize; the rebuild splice and setSystemRomPage use the model's slot
  size instead of a hardcoded 16K. MtxRomService exposes five overridable
  slots with per-slot upload/revert. RomPane names them OS/BASIC/Assembler/
  CP/M/FDX ROM.
- Group MTX500/MTX512/RS128 under a Memotech submenu.
- Shorten hardware options: '512KB RAM', 'CP/M', '80-columns' (tooltips keep
  the full text).
- Fill in the MTX descriptor's missing 'accuracy' capability (was breaking tsc).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: make the MTX FDX floppy a hardware option

The FDX floppy subsystem was always fitted. Add a 'Floppy (FDX)' hardware
toggle (default on): unchecking removes drives B:/C:, empties the FDX Disk
BASIC ROM socket (page 5 reads 0xFF), and hides the FDX ROM slot in the pane.
CP/M boots from floppy, so it force-fits the subsystem — mirroring how it
already force-fits the 80-column display.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: wire up MTX TEXT transcription (screen OCR)

The MTX shares the TMS9918 VDP with the MSX but never exposed the OCR text
overlay: the descriptor omitted the 'text' status LED and MtxFrameProbe had no
transcribe driver, so the status bar showed no TEXT indicator and transcription
never ran. Add the 'text' LED, MtxMachine.ocrScreenStyled/blankCells (reusing
the shared TMS9918 name-table OCR), and a MtxTranscribeDriver. Transcription is
skipped while the FDX 80-column board is showing, since it already renders
crisp text.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: character-intent typing for the MTX keyboard

The MTX arranges symbols unlike a PC ('=' is Shift+'-', ':' and '_' sit on
their own keys) and KEY_MAP had no browser code for the ':'/'*' [5,5] and '_'
[7,5] keys at all, so ':' was untypeable. Drive the matrix from the typed
character (event.key) using the MTX BASIC ROM key legend, forcing the Shift
cell to match the character rather than the physical Shift key, so a PC key's
legend 'just works'. The MCP type tool sends literal characters for the MTX
instead of Spectrum symbol-shift chords.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat: MTX BASIC listing parser for the BASIC pane

MtxFrameProbe exposed no panes provider, so the BASIC Listing pane was always
empty on the MTX. Add a detokeniser for MTX BASIC's crunched program format
(program at CPU 0x4000; per line [length][line#][tokens][0xFF]); token tables
transcribed from the BASIC ROM keyword tables, and LIST spacing (statement
keywords spaced, operators inline, REM verbatim) validated against a real
RAM-dump capture. Wire it to panes.basicListing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs: add 'fix broken tools, don't work around them' to AGENTS.md

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: settle after Enter in the MCP type tool so keystrokes aren't dropped

After Enter the machine ROM tokenises/stores the line and stops scanning the
keyboard; the type tool only idled ~4 frames, so the next line's first key(s)
were dropped (e.g. the MTX stored '20 PRINT 2' as line 0). Idle 30 frames after
Enter (empirically ~20 suffice on the MTX). OCR was never at fault here — a
screenshot confirmed it faithfully rendered the garbled input.

buggyboy/remaster: fix the black mini-map — revert dash_pristine (false premise)

Root cause (proven by original-side Hatari snapshots BEFORE the fix): the
in-race mini-map source art at buf_c+0x11c20 is byte-identical between
original and remaster - and it is TRANSPARENT (every group mask 0xffff).
The original masked-blits it over the live frame, so the outline draws on
the sky. The remaster's dash_pristine precompute (99f1fa9) bulk-copied a
background-less prebuild every frame, painting black over the sky. Its
'dashboard is 100% opaque' premise held only for the leg-independent
baked atlas that goldens / make test / autodrive stage - never for the
live per-leg art - which is exactly why every gate stayed green while
the shipping game was wrong. (The earlier init_leg_dash one-word-shift
suspicion is refuted: both sides' source bytes agree.)

original's g_draw_hud does; the whole dash_pristine machinery removed
(buffer, dirty flag + 4 writers, prebuild API, HudAssets field, bench +
harness wiring). For the opaque baked art the masked blit is
byte-identical to the bulk-copy, so no gate moves.

Pin (closes the coverage hole): test_hud drives the REAL g_init_leg_dash
runtime rebuild over a rendered sky frame on all 5 legs, asserts the art
is transparent, and pins the HUD byte-exact; reintroducing a background
clobber reddens all 5. The two opaque-premise tests are removed - their
premise WAS the bug.
