events.title: globals: fix pst_arr + usr_buf under-declarations (real OOB bugs)
events.message:
globals: fix pst_arr + usr_buf under-declarations (real OOB bugs)

Round-4 audit found two arrays declared smaller than Ghidra's ROM
slots, with the port actually writing past the declared end:

pst_arr:
  - Port had `short pst_arr[4]` -- valid indices 0..3
  - Multiple action handlers write pst_arr[4]:
      * csrc/abathrm.c:181 lcp_st = pst_arr[val]  (val up to 4)
      * csrc/abathrm.c:244 lcp_st = pst_arr[pick] (pick up to 4)
    The uses via `val`/`pick` variables can hit index 4, spilling
    into the next BSS global (lcp_frdO in the port).
  - Ghidra `triggered_event_list` @ 0x2b6da is 10 shorts (20 bytes)
  - Fix: pst_arr[10] to match ROM

usr_buf:
  - Port had `char usr_buf[32]`
  - cmd_upp(str, usr_buf) walks the parser input from g_cdinb
    (bounded < 38) and writes one byte per alphabetic char to
    usr_buf.  A run of 38+ letters would overflow.
  - Ghidra `user_input_buffer` @ 0x4b782 is 42 bytes.
  - Fix: usr_buf[42] to match ROM

Neither has caused visible crashes in prior stability runs because
BOTH stomp into adjacent BSS globals that happen to get restored
by legitimate writes on the next tick.  Still latent memory
corruption bugs.

Round-4 also verified matching sizes on 20+ other arrays
(scn_cmn[30], comp_tok[15], mi_evrt/evtt/evst[16], g_mstr[132],
g_msmk[16], g_aqueu/g_apriq[10], g_cmmip[15], pk_pwc/pk_ph/pk_ch/
pk_psh/pk_phsf/pk_phrf, PSG_ENVELOPE[14B]).

mi_ntLp[64] vs ROM 26, g_sfDoB[256] vs ROM 56, aes_intO[16] vs ROM 8,
wp_ans[10][12] vs ROM 64.  Port allocates more but never OOBs.

docs: fix command_input_buffer -> cmd_inp inversion, add command_input_ptr

Batch 5's agent flagged a suspect in the map that turned out to be real.

Ghidra has THREE distinct symbols in this cluster:
  command_input_buffer     @ 0x4d28a   (char[64] buffer)
  command_input_buffer_pos @ 0x4d00c   (short cursor)
  command_input_ptr        @ 0x2c6fc   (char* walking the buffer)

  command_input_ptr    -> cmd_inp   (correct pair for the walker)

events.title: Persist duplicateOfPrevious through .puaeprofile save/load
events.message:
Persist duplicateOfPrevious through .puaeprofile save/load

The duplicate-frame flag (b3d99bd, "Flag duplicate frames") only ever
lived on FrameCapture -- extension-host-only, in-memory -- not on
RawCapture, the thing that actually gets serialized. The later
multi-frame save/load rewrite (d693f4d) rebuilds FrameCapture[] fresh
from RawCapture[] on every load, with nothing to set the flag again, so
it silently vanished on any save->reload regardless of whether the
underlying detection worked live.

Moved duplicateOfPrevious onto RawCapture itself, so it's carried
through save/load for free the same way every other raw-capture field
already is, instead of needing separate persistence wiring that's easy
to forget (as just happened). Added it to the .puaeprofile format's
per-frame frameMeta (renamed from frameImages, since it's no longer
image-only) and patched the two checked-in fixtures' embedded JSON to
match the field rename.

   @ 0x298F4 = 20; g_mtspb = 20") and via mq_stap/mq_advs cross-
   compare (both port and Ghidra store into the *prescaler* on each
   sequencer step, which the port calls g_mtpre).  Corrected pairs:

     midi_tick_prescaler (0x1226e) -> g_mtpre
     midi_ticks_per_beat (0x298f4) -> g_mtspb

   Ghidra rename staged in ~/ghidra_scripts/lcp_rename_map.tsv,
   ordered so the intermediate free-then-reuse of `g_mtspb` doesn't
   collide.

2) mq_stop() as-committed used `g_mnevi` for the note-event drain
   loop, but every other MIDI function (mq_pars, mq_rmev, mq_pshl,
   mq_popl, mq_advs) reads/writes `mi_evi` for the same role.  The
   port has both `g_mnevi` (short in globals.c, only assigned in
   mq_setp) and `mi_evi` (used everywhere else) -- a port-side
   duplicate at distinct addresses.  Ghidra has ONE global at
   0x4b9ca (`midi_note_event_index`).  mq_stop's `g_mnevi > 0`
   drain loop would therefore never enter, since g_mnevi stays 0
   after boot while mi_evi tracks the real queue depth.  Fixed to
   use mi_evi.

The port-side g_mnevi/mi_evi (and g_mnevc/mi_evcn) duplication is
noted for follow-up: consolidating them into a single global would
remove the alias and simplify future audits.

events.title: midi_seq: add mq_stop + mq_extm (parity with ROM; no call sites yet)
events.message:
midi_seq: add mq_stop + mq_extm (parity with ROM; no call sites yet)

Two ROM entry points the port had left unimplemented:

  mq_stop (Ghidra midi_seq_stop @ 0x1103c)
    Drain scheduled MIDI events via mq_expN, emit note-off (velocity
    zero) for every note still tracked in mi_noSt[], then clear the
    g_msmsa flag so mq_tick stops processing sequencer events.

  mq_extm (Ghidra midi_seq_exit_timer @ 0x11162)
    Xbtimer(0, 0, 0x1c, mi_svtv) -- disables MFP Timer-A and
    reinstalls the ISR pointer saved into mi_svtv by mq_intim.

Also adds the note-tracking table:
  mi_noSt[128]  <=>  Ghidra midi_noteon_state @ 0x53df8
  Value 0 = note not sounding.  Non-zero low nibble = the
  mi_chmap[] index that owns the note so mq_stop can emit
  note-off through the correct MIDI channel on shutdown.

Neither function is called from anywhere yet -- present for parity
with the ROM and to unblock a future exit-cleanup hook.  Ghidra
symbols renamed via rename_function_by_address; mi_noSt added to
the globals cross-reference map.

Binary size 127412 -> 127725 bytes (+313: two small functions +
128-byte mi_noSt table + Xbtimer wrapper pulled in).

events.title: tools: gen_ghidra_rename_tsv.py -- preserve leading U+FEFF BOM in TSV
events.message:
tools: gen_ghidra_rename_tsv.py -- preserve leading U+FEFF BOM in TSV

Four Ghidra symbols (action_queue, action_priority_queue,
action_list_size, soundeffect_priority_table) carry a leading U+FEFF
BOM in their actual Ghidra names.  RenameLcpGlobals.java's safety
check does an exact getName().equals(expected) comparison, so the
TSV must emit the actual name (with BOM) rather than the
BOM-stripped display key we use for lookup.

Previous pass drifted on these 4:
  SKIP g_aqueu @ 0003f6f8: expected action_queue but found action_queue
  SKIP g_apriq @ 0003d004: expected action_priority_queue but found ...
  SKIP g_aliss @ 0003ca74: expected action_list_size but found ...
  SKIP sf_pri  @ 0002b44c: expected soundeffect_priority_table but ...

Same-looking strings on the console because the BOM is invisible.

Fix: keep BOM-stripped key for hash lookup, but write the untouched
Ghidra name to the TSV as the "expected current" field.  Now 290/290
match, ready to re-apply.

events.message:
tools: gen_ghidra_rename_tsv.py -- correct extractor for Ghidra rename map

The previous hand-rolled regex in one-off shell blocks silently skipped
any row where the identifier had a trailing [] inside the backticks
(sprite arrays: sprite_active_image, sprite_mfdb_image, action_queue,
psg_envelope, etc.), leaving those Ghidra symbols un-renamed.
User caught this: sp_draw decompile still showed sprite_active_image
after all three rename passes had "succeeded".

New script handles:
  - identifiers with optional [] suffix inside backticks
  - optional parenthetical annotation in the Ghidra column
    (e.g. `screen_mfdb` (compositing target))
  - Ghidra symbols exported with a leading U+FEFF BOM
  - leading-underscore variants (some symbols appear both ways)

Skips identity pairs, deduplicates.  Now extracts 290 pairs from the
map (was 267 with the broken regex).  All 290 land on valid Ghidra
addresses -- MISSING=0.

Usage:
  python3 csrc/tools/gen_ghidra_rename_tsv.py

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: demo at -O2, double-buffered (no tear, no shift)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: demo at -O2, double-buffered (no tear, no shift)

Two on-target fixes to the interactive demo:
- build_demo.sh: -Os -> -O2 (matching recon) so the blit primitives inline; this
  ~halves the render cost (see tools/bench.py). The single-frame output is
  unchanged (still MATCHes golden on the 68000).
- demo_main.c: double-buffer the display. The old single-buffer memcpy to the live
  screen every frame tore badly at ~10 fps; now we render off-screen and flip the
  video base at the vblank via Setscreen. The two buffers are aligned to 256 bytes
  at RUNTIME (the ST shifter only uses the high/mid base bytes, so a non-256-aligned
  base is rounded down -> the image shifted); link-time alignment wasn't enough
  because the GEMDOS load base needn't be 256-aligned.
- os.s: add Cconis (non-blocking key poll), Vsync, and Setscreen trap wrappers.
events.author: ganneheim

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: per-function 68000 cycle bench vs recon (+ machine model)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: per-function 68000 cycle bench vs recon (+ machine model)

Adds a cycle-accurate perf comparison of the remaster render cores against
recreate's recon, both cross-compiled to m68k and run under Musashi on the SAME
staged leg-1 frame.

- tools/bench.py: loads bench.elf (remaster) + recon game.elf, runs each stage via
  emu.run_bench, prints instructions/cycles/ms and the remaster/recon ratio; also
  benches g_render_road_machine (the byte-exact register/goto model).
- render/atari/bench_main.c + bench_build.sh: zero-work bench_<fn> entry wrappers
  that call each core with structs staged from the demo fixture; build to bench.elf
  at -O2 (matching recon).
- render/atari/gen_demo_fixture.py: extract staged_image() so the fixture bake and
  the bench measure the identical frame (else frame content skews the ratios).
- STATUS.md: perf section with results.

Findings: remaster is 0.96x the recon overall — on par or ahead per stage —
render_road 0.91x, and 0.89x vs the machine model (GCC optimises the native-pointer
C better than the hand-threaded transcription). The earlier "2x slow" was purely
-Os not inlining the blit primitives; -O2 fixes it. Remaining gap is algorithmic.

Root cause — leg 1 starts flat (seg_data all -2 for ~25 steps) and the baked

- os.s: add Cconis (non-blocking key poll) + Vsync (XBIOS 37) trap wrappers.

band scrolls + hills advance); the first frame (speed 0) still MATCHes golden on

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: interactive road + HUD demo on 68000, steer live
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: interactive road + HUD demo on 68000, steer live

An on-target GEMDOS demo (DEMO.PRG) that drives remaster's whole ported road
pipeline on a real 68000 and steers it with the arrow keys. Each frame runs
rm_build_road_geometry (from the current pose) -> rm_render_road -> rm_draw_hud
and blits. Controls: left/right steer curvature, up/down crest/dip the near
slope, space cycles the view bank, R resets, Esc/Q quits.

On-target:
- render/atari/demo_main.c: the interactive shim — bake-fed structs, the per-key
  steer loop, first-frame dump for the headless check.
- render/atari/gen_demo_fixture.py: bake the render_road static tables
  (param/edge/texture), the geometry const sources, the initial pose and the HUD
  assets into demo_fixture.h; emit golden.bin (recreate's g_build_road_geometry +
  g_render_road + g_draw_hud on the same pose).
- render/atari/build_demo.sh, run_demo.py: build DEMO.PRG (geometry+road+hud+text
  cores) and headless-verify its first frame == golden -> MATCH on the 68000.
- render/atari/gen_hud_fixture.py: refactor the asset/define/palette baking into
  reusable helpers (hud_asset_arrays / hud_state_defines / race_palette) shared by
  both demos; no behaviour change (HUD.PRG still MATCHes).

Gotcha:
- The cores read the baked tables with be16/be32 (word/long moves), which fault on
  an odd address on the 68000. Plain uint8_t[] has no alignment guarantee, so the
  fixture arrays and BSS scratch are aligned(2) (68000's requirement).

  screen_mfdb -> mf_scrp        (WRONG; should be g_srmfd)
  soundeffect_playing_flag -> g_sfacf   (WRONG; should be g_sfplf)

Verified via renderf.c:197-211 (blkcp32 src/dst order matches
Ghidra sc_ren8) and renderf.c:234-236 (post-Setscreen `if (g_sfacf
!= NO)` matches Ghidra `if (soundeffect_active_flag != NO)`).

Correct pairs:

  screen_mfdb (compositing target)  -> g_srmfd
  MFDB_screen_ptr (source screen)   -> mf_scrp

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: extract plane.h cell ops (fill / and / overlay)
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: extract plane.h cell ops (fill / and / overlay)

The HUD repeated three two-line patterns that all operate on one ST "cell" (the
two plane-longs at `a` and `a`+4), differing only in the transform: plain fill,
AND-with-mask, and masked overlay. The overlay was moreover identical to text.c's
blit_row. Collapse all of them into a shared plane.h:

  cell_fill(px, at, lo, hi)                  -> wr32 both halves
  cell_and(px, at, mask)                     -> AND both halves
  cell_overlay(px, at, mask, ink, lo, hi)    -> (bg & mask) | (ink & fill)

Every 2-line write pair in hud.c is now one named op; text.c's blit_row is gone
(uses cell_overlay). No behavior change (pure refactor) — full suite 30 green.

events.title: buggyboy/remaster: take Framebuffer* in the render primitives
events.message:
buggyboy/remaster: take Framebuffer* in the render primitives

The dst buffer was uint8_t *px — the same type as the font/string/asset
pointers, so nothing stopped a wrong pointer being passed as the framebuffer.
Take Framebuffer* instead: the type now says exactly what it is, and the
compiler rejects passing an asset buffer as the draw target. (A bare pointer
typedef would read nicely but give no such safety — it converts freely to/from
any uint8_t*.) rm_glyph_run + the HUD phase functions take Framebuffer*; the
one-word leaf helpers (blit_row, overlay_word) stay raw addresses.

test_text binds the first arg as POINTER(Framebuffer) to match. Full suite 30
green (pure type change; codegen identical).

events.title: letload: drop (unsigned char) casts in fl_ltpl to match Ghidra literally
events.message:
letload: drop (unsigned char) casts in fl_ltpl to match Ghidra literally

Ghidra's fl_ltpl compares the byte-pointer's raw value against 31 and
' ' -- signed char throughout.  The port had explicit (unsigned char)
casts that made bytes >= 0x80 count as printable instead of as
terminators.  LETTER.TXT ships pure 7-bit ASCII so this has no
observable effect on the shipped data, but the cast is a Ghidra
divergence and would produce garbled line-index tables under any
future 8-bit charset translation of LETTER.TXT.

events.title: S34+S35: case-insensitive asset lookup, Android touch fixes, Amiga sound repair
events.message:
S34+S35: case-insensitive asset lookup, Android touch fixes, Amiga sound repair

Case-sensitive filesystems (Linux, Android, R36S) never found SWOS files whose
capitalisation differed from our hardcoded literals, so the game reported "no
data" even when the files were in the right folder. Windows dev machines cannot
reproduce it. DataPaths gains ResolveFile/ResolveDir (exact case first, then a
case-insensitive probe returning the real path); every SWOS data lookup now goes
through it: the boot gate, TEAM.* enumeration, the grafs atlases, pitch variants,
charset, CD cue/img resolution and the .RAW sample index.

Amiga in-match sound had never been play-tested and was wrong three ways, all
verified by decoding SFX.SNG against the original 68k:
  - a goal played instrument 36, which in the original is only ever the
    near-miss "ooooh"; goals and misses were literally the same sound. Goals,
    penalties and full time now play the song-6 roar (instr 28 + 27).
  - the crowd bed ran at 8000 Hz instead of 16574 Hz, over an octave low on the
    quietest sample in the bank, so there was effectively no crowd.
  - the module's volume ramp was ignored, so reactions ended on a hot sample and
    were audibly chopped; the decay is now baked into the PCM.
Full time was silent on Amiga (win/lose/draw samples are PC-only).

Android had two inescapable dead ends: pausing hid the touch overlay while
nothing on a touch device could emit ui_cancel, and the full-time screen waited
on a keyboard-only ui_accept. The pad now stays up while paused (icon quits,
fire resumes) and every fire tap raises a discrete accept. Menu touch zones use
the bare bar instead of the match grace strip, which had been swallowing the
option rows' arrows and flipping the options page instead of changing a value.

Import/UX:
  - BOTH floppies are required: SFX.IN2 lives on disk 1, so "only disk 2 is
    used" was wrong and cost users all Amiga sound. Wording corrected, and the
    importer no longer short-circuits on graphics alone, so adding the missing
    disk later actually completes the import (bank probe invalidated after).
  - SOUND option always toggles instead of silently refusing an unavailable
    choice, and boot auto-selects a source that exists.
  - First-run screen prints on-screen diagnostics (searched paths, .adf counts,
    storage reachability, which of graphics/teams is missing) so reports from
    Android and handhelds are actionable.

Android storage: extraction output moves to the app-private dir; the public drop
folder stays in Download/OpenSWOS. Android export presets sign with the Godot
keystore so release exports are installable.

GFX_Promo/ (111 MB of personal media) added to .gitignore.

events.title: buggyboy: cycle-accurate per-frame benchmark (original vs recon)
events.message:
buggyboy: cycle-accurate per-frame benchmark (original vs recon)

Measure the in-race pipeline's 68000 cost under Musashi, no Hatari needed,
to quantify why the reconstruction runs slower on a stock ST.

Harness:
- shim: tally each instruction's cycles (osh_num_cycles); add trap-free
  osh_run_bench to run our cross-compiled m68k recon functions (their OS-trap
  vectors sit inside the recon .text, so osh_run's vector install would corrupt
  them). emu: expose `cycles`, add run_bench.
- tools/bench_frame.py + `make bench`: stage a real mid-race frame, then time
  each pipeline function twice — the original machine code (emu.run) and the
  recon cross-compiled to m68k (game.elf, the BUGGY.PRG code, via run_bench).

Finding (stable across legs/frames): recon is ~2.1x slower than the original.
draw_game_objects + render_road dominate absolute cost; blit_road_scroll has
the worst efficiency gap (~2.8x, a move.l (a1)+,(a0)+ copy GCC doesn't match).
A compiler-efficiency gap, not an algorithmic regression (behaviour is verified
byte-identical). hatari --cpuclock 16 covers it.

Docs:
- README: Benchmarking section.

events.title: buggyboy: fix tunnel palette + 3 real game_update divergences
events.message:
buggyboy: fix tunnel palette + 3 real game_update divergences

Reconstruction (src/game_update.c):
- Mode-4 palette-fade must Setpalette the RACE palette (0x17fa2), not the
  0x17fb0 scratch base. The original stages the record into 0x17fb0.. then
  `suba #$18,a0` rewinds A0 to 0x17fa2 before the trap; the staging writes
  overlap race_palette regs 5/7-11 (a partial in-race fade), so reg0 stays
  black. Loading the +7-shifted scratch (reg0=tan) turned the tunnel
  background tan and shifted every colour -- the reported bug.
- Section-G spin/fx select read obj-0x1c/-0x1b; should be obj-2/-1 (a1 =
  obj+0x1e after the fx-block copy, then `suba #$20`) -- mis-selected the fx.
- fx_block_2e: byte store where the original's last write is `move.w`
  (word 0x003e).
- Section-H horizon-event dispatch passed d5=0; should be horizon_row /
  horizon_row+2 so handlers clear the obj_active/event_type slots (state
  drifted over real play otherwise).

Verification:
- make test green (272). The three image-affecting fixes were found by a
  game_update-vs-oracle differential over the real leg-0 course data (the
  random-data suite never triggered them). The mode-4 Setpalette target is
  off-image, so invisible to the whole-image oracle; verified by a Hatari
  memory snapshot -- recon vs original had byte-identical game state, but the
  recon's hardware palette held the +7 scratch while the original's held race.

Docs:

Confirmed via cp68 preprocess: STATE_CARRY_WALK_FRAME_0 and
STATE_CARRY_WALK_FRAME_1 both truncate to STATE_CARRY_WALK_FRAME
(22 chars) in cp68's macro-name lookup table.  cp68 emits
`warning: redefining STATE_CARRY_WALK_FRAME` on the second define
and silently overwrites the first -- so any code that referenced
STATE_CARRY_WALK_FRAME_0 would resolve to 37 (the FRAME_1 value),
not 36.

Currently no .c file references either macro so no runtime effect,
but the collision is a latent trap for future code.  Fix by dropping
the "FRAME_" prefix to match the neighboring STATE_STR_CLIMB_F0 /
STATE_STR_TOP_F0 / STATE_STR_DESC_F0 / STATE_STR_BTM_F0 convention
already in use (18 chars, safe).

to 22 to match its own docstring (which correctly documents the
empirical cp68 limit).  The old default of 19 was too conservative
and missed this class.

events.title: mq_tick: byte-faithful asm port of Ghidra 0x1219a (SR-manipulating ISR)
events.message:
mq_tick: byte-faithful asm port of Ghidra 0x1219a (SR-manipulating ISR)

The C mq_tick + mq_hlpr.s wrapper couldn't emit the ROM's SR-touching
instructions -- `move sr,dn`, `andi.w #imm,dn`, `ori.w #imm,dn`,
`move dn,sr` -- because Alcyon C 4.14 has no way to spell them.
The ROM uses them to raise IPL to 7 on ISR entry (block preemption),
then lower to 5 during the long mq_advs / psg_upEn sub-calls (so
higher-priority interrupts like VBL and RS-232 can still preempt
them), and restore on exit.  Without that, psg_upEn ran at whatever
IPL Timer-A came in at (probably 6) and blocked every other MFP
interrupt for its full duration.

Ports as csrc/tools/dk/mq_tick.s, byte-faithful vs the ROM
disassembly.  Verified in the linked PRG:

    Ghidra 0x1219a:  00 7c 07 00        ori.w #$700,SR
    Port   0x118f0:  00 7c 07 00        ori.w #$700,SR      (match)

    Ghidra 0x1219e:  52 b9 00 04 b7 ac  addq.l #1, g_mtcou
    Port   0x118f4:  52 b9 00 01 b2 6a  addq.l #1, _g_mtcou (match encoding;
                                                             addr differs by
                                                             linker layout)

Every opcode, addressing mode, and branch displacement (0x16, 0xac,
etc.) is identical between Ghidra and the port -- only the absolute
addresses of the global variables differ, which is expected since
our linker places them at different runtime locations than the ROM.

The ISR now:
  - masks all interrupts on entry (ori #$700, SR)
  - lowers to IPL 5 before jsr _psg_upE / _mq_advs
  - restores full SR on return from each sub-call
  - terminates with `rte` (not `rts`) -- installed by Xbtimer(31, ...)
    directly, without a C-callable wrapper

Deletes:

events.title: audit: re-enable sp_spud(-1,1,NO); fix chk_actT hunger predicate
events.message:
audit: re-enable sp_spud(-1,1,NO); fix chk_actT hunger predicate

Two literal-audit findings from the parallel audit pass, both
verified against Ghidra ROM disassembly.

main.c step 27 — sp_spud call was disabled with the wrong constant.
Ghidra ROM at 0x15846-1584e:
    3f 3c 00 01    move.w #1,  -(sp)   ; layer_p = 1
    3f 3c ff ff    move.w #-1, -(sp)   ; g_seid  = -1  (~SPRITE_UNUSED_0)
    4e b9 00 02 48 fe    jsr sp_spud
The port had `/* if (g_lcldd == 0) sp_spud(0, 1, NO); -- disabled */`
-- wrong constant (0 vs -1) AND commented out.  Re-enabled with the
correct -1 so the g_seid<0 early-exit fires as ROM intends.  Only
observable effect: g_seaim[0] = g_seaim[7] = NULL before cs_mvIn.

ai.c chk_actT hunger predicate — Ghidra fires KITCHEN_CABINET when
    hunger>0 AND rnd>skip AND
    ( (sick   AND food_slots > 0) OR
      (healthy AND lastAct != KITCHEN) )
Port had:
    (healthy OR food_slots > 0) AND lastAct != KITCHEN
which is different for the case (sick + food_slots > 0 + lastAct ==
KITCHEN): Ghidra keeps eating, port refused.  A sick resident could
stall on hunger.  Fixed to Ghidra's boolean shape.  Verified with
Ghidra's check_for_any_action_triggers decompile.

Also: fix the test_longrun_stable.sh bus-error filter -- single-
quoted 'PC=\$fc0174' passes to grep as literal `PC=\$fc0174` but
the log has `PC=$fc0174`, so the filter never matched and every
run reported a "crash" from the harmless boot warning.  Simplified
to `grep -v fc0174` (unquoted, matches the substring anywhere on
the line).

Long-run stability test still passes: PSNR 24.87 dB, 0 real bus
errors.

events.title: docs+test: CLAUDE.md + long-run stability regression check
events.message:
docs+test: CLAUDE.md + long-run stability regression check

CLAUDE.md at repo root -- distilled the faithful-port principle from
my auto-memory into a version that ships with the repo, so a fresh
clone / a new session loads the rules automatically instead of
depending on out-of-tree memory.

The core rule: Ghidra-faithful means LITERAL-faithful.  A shape-match
audit ("both check if(key), both set tx_sctm=160") is not enough --
the 2026-07-19 getKey `!= 0` runaway was a shape-match pass that
missed `!= 0` vs `!= -1` (keycode_enum_none).  Every audit must diff
numeric literals, comparison operators + operand values, sentinel
return values, bitmasks, shift counts, loop bounds -- not just
control-flow shape.  See f1a5349 for the concrete case.

csrc/tools/test_longrun_stable.sh -- regression check for the class
of bug that motivated the CLAUDE.md rule.  Runs LCP.PRG under Hatari
--auto for 15000 VBLs, extracts a frame at VBL 3000 (early) and one
at VBL 13000 (past the ~11500 VBL corruption threshold), and computes
per-pixel PSNR via ffmpeg.  Clean run scores > 20 dB even with the
resident walking between rooms; a getKey-style runaway that fills
the top strip with striped garbage drops it below 15 dB.  Threshold
is 18 dB.

Also filters the harmless boot-time $41fffe / PC=$fc0174 Bus Error
that TOS always emits during its RAM-size probe -- otherwise every
run reports a "crash" that isn't one.

Verified: current tree passes with PSNR 24.87 dB and zero real
bus errors.  With the getKey fix reverted (checked locally), the
same script correctly reports VERDICT: CORRUPTED.

events.title: tick: fix getKey() return-value check (!=0 → !=KEY_NONE)
events.message:
tick: fix getKey() return-value check (!=0 → !=KEY_NONE)

The K&R port had `if (key != 0)` in tick.c and games.c around every
getKey() call.  getKey() returns KEY_NONE (-1) when the keyboard
buffer is empty, not 0 -- so `-1 != 0` was always true, and the
"a key was received" branch fired on every single game tick.

In tick.c that meant `tx_sctm = 160` (the split-copy compositor
timer) was reset on every tick, permanently locking sc_ren8 into
the letter-scroll-pane rendering path.  After ~11500 VBLs the
accumulated split-copy top-strip contents produced the visible
red-stripe corruption over the upper 2/3 of the screen (task #45)
and eventually a TOS bus error at $fd2284 / $fd225a as garbage
state fed into VDI.

Ghidra's decompile has the check right: `keycode != keycode_enum_none`
in game_tick_and_animate at the same spot.  Our port mistranslated
that as `!= 0`.

Fix: use KEY_NONE (-1) in all three sites -- tick.c's main input
path, tick.c's g_inpmd (command-mode) path, and games.c's
mini-game key drain + poll.  With the fix, a fresh 25000-VBL
--auto run stays clean throughout (verified frame 13000 matches
frame 3000 pixel-for-pixel).

Root cause traced via runtime instrumentation: sampled tx_sctm at
VBL 3000 (=160) and VBL 12000 (=159) -- clearly stuck at max
instead of counting down.  That pointed to a keypress every tick,
which in turn pointed at the != 0 mistranslation.

events.title: Add MOS 6526 CIA timer emulation and fix BASIC SYS line parsing

Add MOS 6526 CIA timer emulation and fix BASIC SYS line parsing

Implement MOS 6526 CIA 1 and CIA 2 interval timer emulation (`CiaState`)
in `UnpackerMemory` to handle hardware delay countdowns, 16-bit counter

Together, these changes enable `c64_thats_the_way_scoop.time_cruncher.prg`
and other CIA-dependent binaries to unpack cleanly to entry `$0801`.

events.title: palette: restore ROM vdi_colt; brown-tank was launcher artifact
events.message:
palette: restore ROM vdi_colt; brown-tank was launcher artifact

vdi_colt was flipped to identity in 2abfe8a on the theory that Alcyon
vdibind/Hatari doesn't apply the TOS default VDI->palette permutation,
so an identity mapping was needed for color_enum N to land on palette
slot N.  The theory turns out to hold only when LCP.PRG is launched
via COMMAND.PRG, which leaves the workstation in a state that also
collapses vsl_color's colour argument into pen 15 (dark brown 0x410)
regardless of index -- so both empty and filled tank rows appeared
brown, and identity happened to make the empty rows land on grey
palette-12 by accident.

Launched directly from the GEM desktop (Hatari --auto), TOS opens a
fresh workstation with its default permutation active, and the ROM's
"cancel TOS's permutation" table {0,2,3,6,4,7,5,8,9,10,11,14,12,15,
13,1} is what maps color_enum N onto palette slot N correctly:
color_enum 13 (blue) -> vdi_colt[13] = 15 -> TOS remaps VDI 15 ->
palette 13 = main_pal[13] = 0x007 blue.  Verified visually against
the water tank in the kitchen.

Also drop the stale y1=y2=174 preset in updWtLv (the loop body sets
both every iteration) and note the launcher constraint above sc_sdtb
so future readers know why Setscreen looks fragile.

events.title: palette: fix vdi_colt to identity so VDI colours land in the right slots
events.message:
palette: fix vdi_colt to identity so VDI colours land in the right slots

The 1985 ROM chose vdi_colt[] to CANCEL OUT TOS's standard ST-low
VDI-color-to-palette-slot permutation.  Under real TOS 1.04,
`vsl_color(vdihnd, 15)` displays palette slot 13 because VDI's
default LUT maps VDI-color 15 -> palette 13.  The ROM's vdi_colt[13]
= 15 was picked precisely to route color_enum 13 (blue) through
that permutation into palette 13 (0x007).

Our stack -- Alcyon DK vdibind.a + Hatari's VDI -- does NOT install
that permutation.  VDI-color N passes straight through as
palette-slot N.  With the ROM's vdi_colt still applying its own
permutation, every colour ended up in the WRONG palette slot:
color_enum 13 (blue) went via vdi_colt[13] = 15 into palette 15
(dark brown 0x410).  That's why the water tank read as brown, and
by extension anything drawn through the VDI wrappers -- lines,
fills, cursors -- got its hue permuted twice.

Investigation
=============

Bisected by patching updWtLv to bypass vdi_colt (direct color 13
in the vsl_color call).  Water tank rendered blue immediately,
confirming VDI is identity-mapped in our environment.  Reverted
the surgical patch and fixed the root cause in vdi_colt itself:

  vdi_colt[16] = {  0,  2,  3,  6,  4,  7,  5,  8,       (before -- ROM)
                    9, 10, 11, 14, 12, 15, 13,  1 }
              -> {  0,  1,  2,  3,  4,  5,  6,  7,       (after -- identity)
                    8,  9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 }

Every VDI drawing call site continues to use `vdi_colt[color]`
verbatim -- no touch to render.c / gfx_prim.c / mini-games /
tvanim.  Only the table values change.

Verification
============

Water tank now renders blue (verified visually in a 3000-VBL
Hatari capture, cropped to the tank rectangle).

Full test sweep (SKIP_TITLE=1 + SKIP_MIDI=1):
  Alcyon build:      54 OK, 0 missing
  frame_hash:        33/33 match golden
  test_stairs.sh:    PASS
  test_stairs_up.sh: PASS

Frame_hash still matches because boot-time VDI calls hit slots
(0, 4, 8, 9) where the old and new tables happened to agree.
Later runtime drawing (water tank at least) now uses correct
colours.

Closes the last standing correctness bug from the deviation audit
(task #32).

events.title: Address code-review findings on the profiler frame-alignment fix
events.message:
Address code-review findings on the profiler frame-alignment fix

A review of the three prior commits (flame-graph anchor fix + frame
alignment fix) surfaced 8 findings, all addressed:

Correctness:
- Guard against a single throwaway retro_run() call crossing more than one
  true frame boundary: a new g_wprofMarkersAllowed flag (set only after the
  throwaway call returns) prevents a second crossing from emitting a
  spurious inter-frame marker that would zero g_wprofRegEnabled and lose
  register-trace data for the whole capture.
- buildSampleSlots' anchor search now requires a candidate's next few
  samples to also resolve nearby before accepting it, instead of trusting
  the single earliest match unconditionally — guards against an isolated
  coincidental same-address occurrence (e.g. a shared subroutine an
  interrupt handler also calls) winning over the genuine start.
- wasm_profile_emit_frame_marker now returns whether it actually wrote the
  marker; the caller's emitted-count only advances on success, instead of
  drifting from the buffer's real contents when it's nearly full.

Efficiency:
- g_wprofActive now stays 0 until the precise true-vsync boundary fires
  (not armed-then-rewound), so the throwaway alignment frame does none of
  instrHook's stack-walk/register-snapshot work for data that would just
  be discarded.
- The anchor-candidate search resolves all 32 candidates in one shared
  O(N) pass over the DMA grid instead of 32 independent O(N) scans.

Cleanup:
- Extracted wasm_profile_reset_counters(), shared between
  wasm_profile_prepare() and the boundary hook.
- Extracted wasm_profile_on_frame_boundary() as its own function, keeping
  profiler-capture bookkeeping structurally separate from
  puae_debug_frame_boundary_notify()'s original replay/stepBackFrame
  purpose.

Verified: single-frame and 4-frame captures both show every frame's
CPU-sample anchor exactly matching its DMA grid's true start (vpos 0),
register data still correctly present for frame 0 in both cases. Full
suite (801 unit tests, wasm integration tests including stepBackFrame,
lint) passes.

events.title: midi: land the PSG envelope processor (psg_upEn)
events.message:
midi: land the PSG envelope processor (psg_upEn)

Replaces the psg_upEn no-op skeleton with the full 891-instruction
port of psg_process_envelopes (Ghidra 0x115ae).  Called at 50 Hz
from mq_tick, this is the last piece of the 1985 audio stack --
with it in place, notes played by mq_dise get proper ADSR shaping
instead of abrupt attack + cut-off.

Per-channel ADSR state machine (5 phases):
  ENV_ATTACK   ramp current_volume from start_vol -> attack_target_vol
                       over attack_duration ticks
  ENV_DECAY    ramp attack_target_vol -> decay_target_vol over
                       decay_duration ticks
  ENV_SUSTAIN  ramp decay_target_vol -> sustain_target_vol over
                       sustain_duration ticks
  ENV_RELEASE  ramp down to 0 over release_duration ticks
  ENV_FADEOUT  final tail (rare -- used when the sustain step
                       overshoots zero volume)

Each phase uses Bresenham-style integer interpolation:
  ramp_delta = (target - current) * rate_table[timer]
  each 50 Hz tick: accum += delta; while accum > 360: volume +=
    direction; accum -= 360

Duration = 0 skips the phase immediately (goto fall-through
matches Ghidra's switch-case order).  After each channel's math,
the volume is clamped against max_volume (the velocity-derived

psg_wr.

                                preserved verbatim

events.title: structs: migrate PSG_ENVELOPE to 14-byte Ghidra runtime layout
events.message:
structs: migrate PSG_ENVELOPE to 14-byte Ghidra runtime layout

Prerequisite for porting psg_process_envelopes.  Ghidra's runtime
struct is 14 bytes (confirmed by `muls.w #0xe` at 0x115c0), not the
9-byte on-disk layout the port had.  The new layout adds 5 fields
the old struct was missing and MOVES several existing fields:

  offset  new field                old field
     0    phase                    phase
     1    attack_start_vol         phase_timer     (moved to 10)
     2    attack_duration          attack_start_vol
     3    attack_target_vol        attack_duration
     4    decay_duration           decay_duration
     5    decay_target_vol         sustain_level   (removed)
     6    sustain_duration         release_duration
     7    sustain_target_vol       current_volume  (moved to 12)
     8    release_duration         max_volume      (moved to 13)
     9    ramp_direction           (was end of struct)
    10-11 phase_timer  (short)
    12    current_volume
    13    max_volume

Silent-bug catch
================

The old struct was actually broken -- psg_cpE's 8-byte memcpy into
`.attack_start_vol` corrupted `current_volume` and `max_volume` with
what should have been decay_target / sustain params.  The corruption
went undetected because psg_process_envelopes (which reads those
fields) wasn't ported yet, so nothing ever observed the wrong values.

The new layout maps the 8-byte disk block onto offsets 1..8
(attack_start_vol .. release_duration), which is the correct
ADSR-parameter region.  current_volume + max_volume are outside the
memcpy window, matching Ghidra.

mq_dise field access
====================

`mq_dise` reads attack_start_vol / attack_duration / current_volume /
max_volume / phase_timer / phase.  All six still exist in the new
layout, at new offsets.  Direct field access via -> / . recompiles
transparently to the new byte positions.

Verification (all with SKIP_TITLE=1 + SKIP_MIDI=1):
  Alcyon build:      54 OK, 0 missing
  sizeof(PSG_ENVELOPE) == 14 -- verified with compile-time assert
  frame_hash:        33/33 match golden
  test_stairs.sh:    PASS
  test_stairs_up.sh: PASS

Stair-test offsets unchanged (psg_envelope[3] grew 15 bytes but
sits after globals.o + sprglobs.o in link order, so the addresses
of lcp_x / g_wtx / lcp_st / g_wyx are unaffected).

Next: extract midi_envelope_rate/time/sustain/release tables from
ROM, add psg_channel_ramp_delta/accum globals, port
psg_process_envelopes.

events.message:
midi: land the sequencer parser + 8 helpers; wire mq_advs; SKIP_MIDI guard

Full port of midi_seq_parse_events (Ghidra 0x10388) plus the seven
helpers it calls -- read_note_duration, push_loop, pop_loop,
remove_event, expire_notes, send_note_off, queue_note_event,
send_program_change.  mq_advs upgraded from skeleton to the real
three-phase state machine (WAIT_NOTE_EXPIRE / PARSE_NEXT_EVENT /
SONG_ENDING).

New sequencer state (all in globals.c):

  mi_seqE, mi_dptr           stream-end + loop-return scratch
  mi_evTf                    event-decoded-this-pass flag
  mi_nnOn, mi_lasT, mi_nnOf  per-event note-on / sustain / off flags
  mi_ccha, mi_cnot           current logical channel + note number
  mi_nmof                    two-bit transpose-mode field
  mi_nlpA, mi_nlp0           accent flag + duration in ticks
  mi_slop                    song is in loop-flag mode
  mi_ndt[32]                 duration lookup (ROM 0x298f6, 21 real)
  mi_evq[60]                 3-word note event queue (20 concurrent)
  mi_evi                     queue length (units of one word)
  mi_lstk[50], mi_evcn       loop stack (24 nested + slack)
  mi_nOS[128]                per-MIDI-note active-channel bookkeeping

New enum:
  SEQ_PHASE_WAIT_NOTE_EXPIRE = 0

Ported helpers (all in midi_seq.c):
  mq_rdur   midi_seq_read_note_duration     look up next event's ticks
  mq_pshl   midi_seq_push_loop               push {addr, count} pair
  mq_popl   midi_seq_pop_loop                pop / decrement / return
  mq_rmev   midi_seq_remove_event            shift queue after expire
  mq_snof   midi_seq_send_note_off           velocity-0 to MIDI OUT
  mq_expN   midi_seq_expire_notes            per-tick queue drain
  mq_spgm   midi_seq_send_program_change     0xCn if program changed
  mq_qnne   midi_seq_queue_note_event        stash entry + Note-On
  mq_pars   midi_seq_parse_events            walk the compact stream

parse_events preserves Ghidra's nested-while structure as gotos
(`top:` at the loop head) for byte-for-byte fidelity with the
1985 source.  Handles the full command byte set: 0x00 (tick sep),
0x01..0x7F (3-byte note events with the byte0/byte1 flag matrix),
0x82 (bar marker), 0x85 (loop start), 0x86 (loop end), 0xFF (EOS).

Testability -- new -DSKIP_MIDI flag
===================================

The 200 Hz Timer-A handler runs concurrent with the game loop but
fires at times that shift by a few cycles between Hatari boots.
That makes the game's state at any fixed VBL count non-deterministic
enough to fail the warp-based stair tests and to churn frame_hash
goldens every run.

installed for automated tests.  Interactive builds get the real
handler and hear music.

(before: only SKIP_TITLE=1).

events.title: midi: wire Timer-A install via mq_hlpr.s asm wrapper
events.message:
midi: wire Timer-A install via mq_hlpr.s asm wrapper

Adds the missing interrupt-mode wrapper that lets Xbtimer install
the C mq_tick handler.  K&R C functions return via RTS; MFP timer
handlers must return via RTE.  The 4-instruction wrapper in
mq_hlpr.s saves scratch registers, JSRs into the C body, restores,
and RTEs.

Files:
  csrc/tools/dk/mq_hlpr.s   new -- the wrapper (labelled _mqisr;
                                              _mq_tickA would truncate to
                                              _mq_tick under as68's 8-char
                                              symbol cap and collide with
                                              the C entry point)
  csrc/tools/alcyon_link.sh assemble mq_hlpr.s alongside gemstart.s
  csrc/init.c               uncomment the xbios(31, ...) install --
                                              points at (long) mqisr

Debug story (why the first attempt still crashed):
  * as68's `.globl` behaves as "export if defined here, import if
    referenced but undefined".  Without `.globl _mq_tick`, as68
    created a spurious LOCAL BSS symbol for _mq_tick at value 0.
    The JSR then resolved to BSS start (uninitialised memory) via
    that local, not to the real C function in midi_seq.o.
  * Adding `.globl _mq_tick` back tells as68 to leave the symbol
    as an undefined external so the linker resolves it correctly.

Verified stable across 3 repeated frame_hash runs.  The tick
counter runs at ~307 Hz (MFP mode 5, data 0x28) and mq_tick is
guarded by g_msmsa == NO in the default state, so nothing audible
changes yet -- but the plumbing is live.

Frame hashes DO shift vs the previous golden because the timer
running steals CPU cycles from the game loop, so the "frame at
second N" is one animation tick earlier.  Golden updated to the
new baseline; game still runs to completion, 33/33 frames stable.

Stair-test offsets rebased (globals.o + midi_seq.o grew).

Verification (all with SKIP_TITLE=1):

events.title: Fix profiler frame-boundary markers misaligned for frame 1+ in multi-frame captures
events.message:
Fix profiler frame-boundary markers misaligned for frame 1+ in multi-frame captures

The previous fix (5b9dab5) only corrected frame 0's start: it rewound the
CPU-sample buffer to the true vsync via puae_debug_frame_boundary_notify(),
but the markers separating frame 0/1, 1/2, etc. were still inserted by
frontend_shim.c right after each retro_run() call returned — the same
few-scanlines-late point that made frame 0 imprecise before. That
misattributed each subsequent frame's first few lines to the *previous*
frame's tail (and over-extended that previous frame by the same amount),
reintroducing a small CPU/DMA misalignment on every frame after the first.

Now markers are emitted from the same precise per-vsync hook as the frame 0
reset, tracking how many of them (numFrames - 1) are still owed.

Verified directly: in a fresh 4-frame capture, every frame's CPU-sample
anchor now exactly matches its own DMA grid's true start (vpos 0) — frames
1-3 previously showed a ~0.6% (vpos 1) discrepancy. Full test suite (800
unit tests, wasm integration tests including stepBackFrame/rewind which
share the modified hook, lint) passes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: Graham Bates

events.title: Fix CPU profiler still missing ~1% of instructions at each frame's start
events.message:
Fix CPU profiler still missing ~1% of instructions at each frame's start

The previous frame-alignment fix armed recording synchronously right after
a "priming" retro_run() call returned, but retro_run() only returns once
the CPU execution loop notices the libretro_frame_end flag — confirmed via
direct instrumentation to happen a few scanlines *after* the true vsync
(vpos wrapping to 0), not at it. So recording was still arming a few lines
late, silently dropping genuinely-executed instructions at the very start
of every capture.

Now: arm recording immediately (at whatever imprecise raster position),
run one throwaway partial frame, and let puae_debug_frame_boundary_notify()
— an existing hook that already fires with exact precision at the true
vsync (previously only used by rewind/stepBack) — rewind the CPU-sample
buffer right at that boundary, discarding whatever accumulated before it.
The DMA/copper grids needed no equivalent change; their own double-buffer
toggle already happens automatically at that same precise point.

Verified directly: "first CPU code fetch anywhere in the grid" now lands
at exactly vpos 0 (was vpos 3) across multiple capture-timing offsets, and
the flame graph's real anchor position improved from ~0.96% to ~0.05% of
the frame. Full test suite (800 unit tests, wasm integration tests
including stepBackFrame/rewind, lint) passes.

events.title: buggyboy: play engine idle + crash sounds on-target (Dosound A0 list)
events.message:
buggyboy: play engine idle + crash sounds on-target (Dosound A0 list)

Follow-up to the countdown fix. The game's sound EFFECTS (not the REFRESH-driven
music) are all XBIOS Dosound command lists that stop_music/stop_music_chk hand to
TOS in A0: the leg-start countdown (0x18bba/0x18bca), the engine idle when
stationary (0x18ba2, a repeating-envelope tone), the collision/spin sound
(0x18b78), and the crash sound (0x18b92). Dosound writes the YM2149 directly, so
the differential harness never saw the A0 list and the reconstruction dropped it
on every stop_music call — leaving all these effects silent on-target.

Thread the list faithfully (it is the original's A0):
- g_stop_music / g_stop_music_chk take a list_off and issue it via a new g_dosound
  seam (no-op in os.c for the .so; real XBIOS 32 in game_main.c, gated on hw_ready).
- Pass the right A_dosound_* list at each call site: game_update idle/collide,
  draw_crash_fx crash, game_main countdown (now routed through g_stop_music instead
  of a separate Dosound call).
- addrs.h: the five A_dosound_* list offsets.

Off-image, so the differential suite is unchanged (261 pass); test_stop_music
updated for the new signature. Verified headlessly (hatari --trace psg_write):
engine idle now emits reg13=0x0e (repeating envelope) continuously at speed 0,
alongside the 4 countdown beeps (reg13=0x00).

events.title: buggyboy: play the leg-start countdown beeps on-target (XBIOS Dosound)
events.message:
buggyboy: play the leg-start countdown beeps on-target (XBIOS Dosound)

The leg-start '3-2-1-go' countdown was silent in the playable PRG. It is not
produced by the game's own VBL music driver (REFRESH) but by TOS's XBIOS Dosound
engine: stop_music (0x12ec4), after parking the VBL sound vector, issues
Dosound(A0); main (0x1021c) hands it a beep command list on each of the four
race-start settle frames (3x 0x18bba then 0x18bca). All of it is off-image
(Dosound writes the YM2149 directly), so the differential harness never saw it —
the calls were dropped as no-ops and the VBL install had replaced TOS's _vblqueue
(dropping its Dosound stepper).

Reconstruction (PRG-only; cores + differential suite untouched, 261 pass):
- game_os.s: real Dosound XBIOS-32 wrapper.
- game_main.c: preserve TOS's _vblqueue entries after our handler (mirrors
  main 0x101b8) so TOS's per-VBL Dosound stepper runs; issue Dosound(beep/go)
  at the four settle frames (mirrors main 0x1021c-0x10250).
- game_main.c: clear conterm (0x484) to silence the TOS key-click (a separate
  divergence: present in ours, absent in the original which clears it @0x101dc).

Verified headlessly (hatari --trace psg_write): 4 beep sequences now drive the
YM hardware envelope (reg8=0x10, reg7=0xfe) at leg start.

Docs: names.txt (dosound_beep/go lists + stop_music note); on-target-execution.md
gains a fifth bug class (off-image OS services relied on for output); render/atari
README note.

events.title: Fix CPU profiler flame graph showing a spurious gap at frame start
events.message:
Fix CPU profiler flame graph showing a spurious gap at frame start

buildSampleSlots (columns.ts) anchored sample 0 to its own address via an
unbounded scan of the whole DMA grid. When that instruction's own fetch was
invisible in the grid (already retired before the very next fetch landed),
the search would latch onto a much-later same-address loop revisit instead
of the true start, rendering a large false gap at the left of the flame
graph for any program with a long-running per-iteration loop. Fixed by
anchoring on whichever of the first ~32 samples resolves earliest in the
grid instead.

Also aligns capture start to the true frame boundary before CPU/DMA
recording arms (wasm_profile_start), so frame 0 always starts at the
raster origin rather than wherever the CPU happened to be when Capture
was invoked.

events.title: games: complete blackjack mini-game port (pk_bjMn body)
events.message:
games: complete blackjack mini-game port (pk_bjMn body)

Replaces the pk_bjMn skeleton with the full 1270-instruction port
of poker_blackjack_main.

Per-round flow (Ghidra LAB_0001bcc8):
  1. plEr card + bet displays; init bets = 0; F1 Bet / F10 Quit
  2. Bet-entry loop: F1 adds a chip (cap 20), F3 enters, F5 clears
     back to zero.  pk_dpile[10] used as a scratch bit for "player
     entered a bet vs cleared" -- preserved verbatim.
  3. Deal 2 cards each (player face-up, computer[1] face-down)
  4. pk_cnbj on both hands -> up to 4 natural-blackjack branches:
       both natural  -> "You have BLACKJACK...but so do I !!"
       player only   -> "You have BLACKJACK!!" + pk_sbet win
       computer only -> "I have BLACKJACK!!" + pk_sbet lose 2x
       neither       -> full game
  5. Split branch (pk_ph[0] == pk_ph[1]): F1 Split / F3 No-split.
     On split: initialise pk_psh, chip match from player to equal
     first bet, natural-blackjack check on each split half.
  6. Double-down: F1 Double / F3 No-double per hand.  Sets pk_pcc
     or pk_pscc to CARD_BJ_STEP to force pk_bjr to auto-hit once
     and stop.
  7. pk_bjr hit-loop per hand (single or split).  On bust: refund
     the bet to computer, set pk_bs1 / pk_bs2.
  8. Dealer turn: reveal down card, 3-tick "two-value picker" that
     compares chsc(0) vs chsc(1) and picks the largest score <=21.
     Bust or stand.
  9. Compare pk_pscore vs pk_cscore -> pk_sbet transfer messages
     ("I win.", "You win.", "It's a tie...", "Your first hand
     loses.", "You win with your second hand.", etc.).
 10. Cleanup on quit (LAB_0001bd9e): tx_sctm=0, no_keyin=NO, Mfree,
     moff().

Ghidra's `_poker_computer_card_count` / `_poker_card_deck_index`
memory-aliased pair, which the decompiler shows twice under wrong
names, are mapped to pk_c1bj / pk_c2bj (natural-blackjack flags
on first/second hand).  Similar for `_poker_computer_hand_value_lo`
/ `_hi` -> pk_bs1 / pk_bs2 (bust flags).  These are just short
storage slots the 1985 code reused as scratch across scopes; the
port picks a name matching the semantic role in each use site.

The dealer's score-picker `midi_dma_start_lo` is genuinely a shared
memory slot with the MIDI DMA start register on the ST -- 1985 code
reused it as scratch during blackjack because the sequencer's DMA
was inactive.  Ported to a dedicated pk_pscore short instead.

Naming detail: entry point stays pk_bjMn (the pre-existing symbol
agames.c calls).  The body cannot be forwarded via a wrapper --
`pk_bjMn` and `pk_bjMn_body` both truncate to `_pk_bjMn` under
Alcyon's 8-char external cap.  Same lesson as pk_main.

events.message:
games: complete poker mini-game port (pk_show + pk_main body)

Second half of the poker port.  Replaces the pk_main skeleton with
the full 819-instruction Ghidra port, and lands pk_show (the 530-
instr poker_showdown) that pk_main invokes to resolve every hand.

pk_show hand-comparison ladder (rank tiebreaks preserved exactly):
  * straight / flush / straight-flush: high card of sorted hand
  * trips / full house / four-of-kind: rank of the pair/trip card
  * two pair: high pair rank, then low pair rank, then kicker
  * one pair: pair rank, then kicker ladder from top down
  * high card: full kicker ladder from top down
Winner announced, then blinks (5x on/off), then pk_annr transfers
the pot.  Sets pk_round = 1 as a "hand completed" side-flag.

pk_main structure (labels match Ghidra LAB_00018xxx / 00019xxx):
  1. Malloc + pk_ldCrd + mg_stp + reset money/pot + initial display
  2. Per-round loop:
       a. plEr card area; pk_ante (with quit-check exit)
       b. pk_evhs -- deal 5+5, animated
       c. pk_cbet("Do you feel lucky today?") first bet round
       d. Computer sees or passes.  On see: drain player's bet
          chip-by-chip.
       e. Discard phase: F1 Draw / F3 Stay / 1..5 toggle cards.
          Selected slots highlight to CARD_HIGHLIGHT and re-deal
          uniquely (checking across both hands AND pk_dpile).
       f. pk_cdrw -- computer's draw phase
       g. pk_cbet("Want to make a bet?") second bet round
       h. Multiple branches:
          - Computer passes with weak hand -> "Ok, I'll call" +
            pk_show
          - Computer passes bluff -> makes a bet (5..15 clamped),
            F1 See / F3 Fold player choice, then raise-fold-call
            escalation loop
          - Computer sees + folds ("I feel unlucky") -> player
            takes pot
          - Computer sees + calls -> pk_show
          - Computer sees + raises -> patches pk_rm with two-digit
            raise amount, drains player's response chip-by-chip,
            "You think I'm bluffin'?" F1 See / F3 Fold prompt,
            then raise-fold-call escalation as above
  3. Cleanup (Ghidra LAB_00018da0): tx_sctm=0, no_keyin=NO, Mfree,
     moff().

Gotos preserved verbatim (cleanup, endround, discard_loop,
raiseloop1, raiseloop2) so the port stays byte-comparable with the
1985 asm shape -- structuring away the gotos would fundamentally
change the compiled output.

declared wrapper collided with the pk_main symbol at Alcyon's

events.title: walk: work around Alcyon C preprocessor macro-name collision
events.message:
walk: work around Alcyon C preprocessor macro-name collision

Alcyon C 4.14's macro name lookup truncates identifiers so that
STATE_STAIR_DESCEND_FRAME_0 (17) collides with STATE_STAIR_DESCEND_
FRAME_3_STEP (20).  The later #define wins, so every
`lcp_st = STATE_STAIR_DESCEND_FRAME_0` in walk.c was emitting
`move.w #$0014, lcp_st` (=20), not `#$0011` (=17).

Effect: during stair descent the state cycle was
  20 → 21 → wrap → 20 → 21 → wrap → 20 ...
instead of 17 → 18 → 19 → 20 → 17.  The resident's Y position
still advanced, but sp_updb saw the same lcp_st every tick, so
body_frT[20] → body frame 16 kept getting composited — the sprite
"fell without animation".

Same collision hits STATE_STAIR_TOP_FRAME_0 (13 → 16),
STATE_STAIR_BTM_FRAME_0 (21 → 24), STATE_STAIR_CLIMB_FRAME_0
(9 → 12) in the CLIMB/TOP/BTM branches.

Fix: replace the 14 affected `_FRAME_0` uses in walk.c with
numeric literals (9, 13, 17, 21) with an explanatory comment.
The enums.h definitions are left in place; other files whose
usage of these particular macros isn't observably broken are
untouched.

Runtime evidence — sp_updb state distribution during descent:
  before:  {20: 65, 24: 24}  (stuck)
  after:   {17:21, 18:21, 19:19, 20:19, 21:22, 22:22, 23:22, 24:22}

test_stairs.sh and test_stairs_up.sh both still pass.

frames during descent/ascent.

events.title: Save/load every frame of a multi-frame profiler capture, not just frame 0
events.message:
Save/load every frame of a multi-frame profiler capture, not just frame 0

Saving a .puaeprofile only ever persisted ProfilerManager.getLastRaw()'s
single frame, and the file editor always posted a one-element frames
array -- so reopening a saved multi-frame capture could never show more
than one frame, regardless of how many were actually captured.

.puaeprofile now stores every frame (section names prefixed "f0:",
"f1:", ...; per-frame thumbnail/full-frame JPEG dimensions). No backward
compatibility with the old single-frame layout -- this extension isn't
published, so there's nothing to preserve; decode requires the current
format outright.

ProfilerManager.getLastRaw() -> getAllRaw() (RawCapture[]); saveProfile()
persists them all. On load, profileLoader.ts rebuilds every frame via a
new buildFramesFromCaptures(), extracted from ProfilerManager.capture()'s
live multi-frame loop so both paths share one implementation: frame 0
keeps its real disassembly, later frames reweight it, exactly as a live
capture already does. combineFrames() (the all-frames combined model)
and buildFrameRangeModel() (shift-click sub-range selection) are
similarly extracted and now shared between a live session and a loaded
file -- a loaded multi-frame document's filmstrip behaves identically to
a live capture's, including range selection, which previously could
never even be reached in the file editor (frames.length was always 1).

Regenerated the replay fixtures against the real captured bytes (using
puae/kick34005.A500, now available locally): migrated template.puaeprofile
to the new format in place, and built a new template-multiframe.puaeprofile
(two frames of genuine captured profile/DMA/copper data) with replay
coverage for independent per-frame decode and the combined model.

events.title: Preserve real aspect ratio in multi-frame profiler filmstrip thumbnails
events.message:
Preserve real aspect ratio in multi-frame profiler filmstrip thumbnails

wasm_profile_save_thumbnail() downscaled each frame into a fixed 160x100
buffer using independent x/y scale factors, stretching whatever the real
framebuffer's aspect ratio is (~320x256, ~1.25:1 for a typical PAL screen)
to fill that box's 1.6:1 shape -- squashing every multi-frame capture's
filmstrip thumbnails. The single-frame capture path (getFramebuffer in
rpc.ts) already computed its thumbnail size from the real aspect ratio,
so this was a batch-path-only regression relative to that.

Since every frame in one capture shares a single screen resolution (the
same assumption g_wprofFullFrames already relies on), the actual
thumbnail size (g_wprofThumbW/H) is now computed once from frame 0 by
scaling uniformly (one factor for both axes) to fit within a
WASM_THUMB_MAX_W x WASM_THUMB_MAX_H bound -- that bound now just caps
storage, it isn't the stored shape. wasm_profile_get_thumb_w()/_h() and
the per-frame pointer stride report the real per-capture size, which
rpc.ts already queries once and applies to every frame. No JS changes
needed: the filmstrip CSS already renders each thumbnail at its own
intrinsic aspect ratio (height: 52px; width: auto).

events.title: Fix stale pre-AGA BusOwner ordinals in the thumbnail DMA usage bar
events.message:
Fix stale pre-AGA BusOwner ordinals in the thumbnail DMA usage bar

computeDmaBar (the little stacked bar drawn under each profiler filmstrip
thumbnail) classified DMA cells by hardcoded BusOwner ordinal ranges that
predate AGA support. Adding BPL7/BPL8 shifted SPRITE0-7/COPPER/BLITTER/
BLOCKED up by 2 (see BusOwner's comment in profilerTypes.ts), but this one
classifier was never updated to match, unlike every other BusOwner
consumer in the codebase.

Concretely: BLITTER (25) matched none of the stale ranges and fell into
the near-transparent idle bucket, so the blitter never showed a bar at
all. COPPER (24) was silently merged into the CPU bucket, SPRITE6/7
(22/23) were mislabeled as Copper/Blitter-colored segments, and BPL7/BPL8
(14/15) were miscounted as sprites.

Switched the classification to reference the BusOwner enum directly
instead of magic numbers, so it can't drift out of sync again.

events.title: Scale the CPU profile buffer per frame, not once for the whole multi-frame capture
events.message:
Scale the CPU profile buffer per frame, not once for the whole multi-frame capture

g_wprofBuf held the entire multi-frame capture's decoded-instruction
stream in one fixed-size static array, reset once per capture rather
than per frame. 76438d8 cut its cap 4x (4MB/~174k samples -> 1MB/~43k
samples) reasoning only about a single frame's worst case, but the
cap is actually shared across all N frames of a multi-frame capture:
once busy frames exhausted it partway through, later samples AND the
frame-boundary markers themselves were silently dropped, so a 10-frame
capture could come back as 6 frames, with the frame where the cap hit
missing its CPU data entirely.

g_wprofBuf is now allocated per capture in wasm_profile_prepare(numFrames)
at numFrames * WASM_PROFILE_BUF_WORDS_PER_FRAME -- one frame's worth of
headroom for every frame actually requested, matching the existing
per-frame allocation pattern already used for the DMA/copper/full-frame
buffers in frontend_shim.c. Single-frame captures are unaffected (same
1MB/frame budget as before).

events.title: sp_lcpf: work around Alcyon C (unsigned char) miscompile in mirror branch
events.message:
sp_lcpf: work around Alcyon C (unsigned char) miscompile in mirror branch

Alcyon C 4.14 miscompiles `(unsigned char) short_value` — it emits ext.w
which sign-extends the low byte, so any source byte >= 0x80 (e.g. 0xcc,
0xfd) becomes a negative signed word used as a rev_tab index and reads
garbage from memory before the table. In the mirror branch this zeroed
plane-1 bits (rev(0xcc)=0x33 was lost), so left-facing body sprites
rendered as a hollow black outline with only plane-0 bits present.

Replacing (unsigned char) with `& 0xff` forces the compiler through a
bitwise AND that it emits correctly. Runtime dump confirms dest col 1
row 0 now writes 0x3c00 0x3300 (was 0x3c00 0x0000).

buggyboy: inline the screen-fill cell copy (snappy leg-select menu)

screen_fill_span/_rect copied each 8-byte colour cell with a memcpy call, so a
full-screen fill was ~1900 jsr-memcpy calls (3 stack pushes + cleanup each),
every frame. draw_leg_results full-screen-clears on every leg-select frame, so
this dominated the menu's frame time and made arrow-key stepping sluggish (the

on the 68000, byte-order-safe on the little-endian test host). The inner loop is
now two move.l per cell, no call. Speeds up every fill (menu, results, HUD,
race backgrounds). All 253 differential tests stay byte-identical; verified on

events.title: buggyboy: fix Crawio wrapper reading high word of its arg (F-keys, ESC)
events.message:
buggyboy: fix Crawio wrapper reading high word of its arg (F-keys, ESC)

The Crawio wrapper did `move.w 4(%sp)` to fetch its `short w` argument, but the
C ABI passes `short` in a 4-byte slot — on big-endian m68k the value sits in the
LOW word (6(%sp)), so it read the high word (0x0000) instead of 0x00ff. GEMDOS
Crawio(0) writes a NUL char and returns 0, so every console poll silently did
nothing: leg-select F1-F5 (console scancode) and the in-race ESC-to-quit both
went through it and were dead. Read the longword and push its low word, the same
idiom Fcreate/Fopen already use. Verified on Hatari: F1 starts a leg, ESC quits.

events.title: buggyboy: make the on-target PRG run at ~ST speed (native-endian access)
events.message:
buggyboy: make the on-target PRG run at ~ST speed (native-endian access)

The playable PRG ran ~4x too slow on a stock 8 MHz ST — menu and race alike,
independent of render_road. Root cause: the big-endian image accessors
(be16/be32/wr16/wr32 in machine.h) compiled to a byte-by-byte lsl-#8 shuffle
on EVERY multi-byte access in every draw/blit routine. Those helpers exist to
preserve the 68000's byte order on the little-endian test host, but the m68k
target is itself big-endian, so there they are just aligned move.w/move.l.

Fixes (PRG-only; the differential harness is untouched — 253 tests still green):
- machine.h: #if __BYTE_ORDER__ == __ORDER_BIG_ENDIAN__ -> native aligned
  load/store on-target; keep the byte assembly on the little-endian host so the
  verified behaviour is byte-identical. Kills the shuffle (PRG ~40% smaller).
- game_build.sh: -O2 (was -Os) + -fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns (stop GCC
  turning the hand-written mem* loops into self-calls).
- game_main.c: long-word memcpy/memset when aligned.

Also fixes the apparent screen-shift, which was frame-overrun tearing: with the
frame back inside the 20 ms vblank budget, flip_screen latches cleanly.

Tooling:
- oracle shim/emu: expose osh_num_insns() — per-run instruction count for
  perf profiling (read-only, additive; how render_road/menu costs were measured).

Docs: render/atari/README Performance note (endian gotcha + --cpuclock), and a
machine.h pointer in recreate/README.

events.title: main: call initBM() at boot to fill bm32or/bm32and, fixing sprite corruption
events.message:
main: call initBM() at boot to fill bm32or/bm32and, fixing sprite corruption

Root cause of the body-sprite "random stripe pattern" bug: initBM()
was declared extern in main.c but never called.  bm32or and bm32and
stayed at BSS-zero for the whole run, so sp_lbbd's 30-bit dilation
loop failed on every iteration -- `mask & bm32or[bit]` was always 0,
the flag branch never fired, and `img` stayed 0 for all 21 rows of
every one of the 98 body frames.  sp_lbbd wrote 0/0 to dest,
producing an all-zero body mask.

Downstream effect: sp_draw's NOTS_AND_D pass on an all-zero mask is
a no-op (~0 AND dest = dest), so the S_XOR_D pass just XORed the
sprite image onto whatever floor pixels were there -- the scattered
red/green/blue/yellow pixels the user reported.

Found via a scripted Hatari-debugger flow:
  1. Rebuilt LCP.PRG without lo68's -s (kept the DRI symbol table).
  2. Wrote a Python DRI->nm converter (/tmp/lcp_syms.txt).
  3. Loaded symbols with `symbols /tmp/lcp_syms.txt <TEXT_base>`.
  4. Used `b <cond> :once :file <cmds>` so a runtime breakpoint could
     trigger memory dumps that fire at the actual boot point rather
     than at pre-boot debugger entry.
  5. Dumped:
     - body_shp -> valid pointer to bshdbuf @ 0x6089e
     - body_ptr -> valid pointer to body_buf @ 0x28024 with real
       sprite data ($3c $cc ... at row 0)
     - bshdbuf -> **all zeros** after sp_lbal returned
     - bm32or -> **all zeros**  <-- the actual bug
Once bm32or was identified as zero, the missing initBM() call was
obvious: same class of bug as the earlier initBRev/rev_tab fix from
commit a4a1085.

Fix: call initBM() right after initBRev() in main().  Not a Ghidra
step (the ROM ships bm32or/bm32and as static const long[32] tables
in DATA); the port has to compute them at runtime because Alcyon C
doesn't accept `UL` suffix on hex constants > 0x7FFFFFFF.
Commented inline as a port-specific fixup.

Verified: 5000-VBL CI smoke clean, body sprite now renders with a
proper mask (head + body + outline visible in the middle-floor
bathroom instead of the scattered rainbow pixels).  Golden re-recorded.

buggyboy: 256-align the display buffers at runtime + drop debug ifdefs

The ST video shifter can only display from a 256-byte-aligned base (low 8 address
bits ignored). physbase_tbl held image+offset, but GEMDOS loads image at an
arbitrary (non-256) address, so the displayed base was truncated ~24 bytes below
the drawn data. Round each buffer's runtime address up to a 256 boundary. Also
removed the NO_IKBD/NO_SND/SKIP_ATTRACT bisection ifdefs now that the game runs.

events.title: init: implement bldBRev / restore initBRev call to fill rev_tab
events.message:
init: implement bldBRev / restore initBRev call to fill rev_tab

Prior state was inconsistent: tables.c declared rev_tab[256] in BSS
(uninitialised) with a comment claiming initBRev() would populate it
at boot -- but initBRev's body was still the pre-BSS-refactor no-op
that returned immediately.  Sprite mirroring in sp_lcpf was thus
reading all-zero bytes, silently corrupting the mirrored bitplanes.
Somehow gameplay still smoke-tested clean, but the mirror-heavy
left-facing frames were wrong.

Port bldBRev (Ghidra 0x1680e, build_bit_revert_table) as its own
function so the two-level structure matches the ROM:

  for i in 0..255:
      v = 0
      for j in 0..7:
          if bm_msb_lsb[j] & i:
              v |= bm_lsb_msb[j]
      rev_tab[i] = v

initBRev is now a one-line wrapper -> bldBRev().  frame_hash golden
re-recorded because the mirrored sprites now render correctly, so the
first 2000 VBLs' pixel output differs from the pre-fix baseline.
CI stays green.

events.title: midi_seq: port mh_scat (MIDI header 0x84) from stub to real body
events.message:
midi_seq: port mh_scat (MIDI header 0x84) from stub to real body

The eight MIDI handlers I'd listed as walker-only stubs turn out to
be mostly already-real:

  * mh_chac (0x11246) -- matches raw disasm byte-for-byte:
    reads p[2] into g_mchcn, calls mq_bust.
  * mh_temp (0x11264) -- matches: reads p[1] into mi_temp,
    computes g_mtspb = 2400 / mi_temp, advances by 2 (not 3).
  * mh_volu (0x1129c) -- ROM is bare p+=2; port matches.
  * mh_proc (0x1132c) -- ROM is bare p+=3; port matches.
  * mq_bust  -- fully implemented, matches
    midi_seq_build_scale_table decompile.
  * mq_sepc  -- fully implemented (program-change dispatch).
  * mq_dise  -- fully implemented (~100 lines, MIDI OUT + PSG).

Only mh_scat was really a stub with a gap.  Ported it faithfully
from the raw disasm at 0x112a4..0x1131e:

  mi_dvel = p[2];
  if      (mi_dvel < 0x17) psg_dvol = 5;
  else if (mi_dvel < 0x27) psg_dvol = 7;
  else if (mi_dvel < 0x37) psg_dvol = 9;
  else if (mi_dvel < 0x57) psg_dvol = 11;
  else if (mi_dvel < 0x67) psg_dvol = 13;
  /* mi_dvel >= 0x67: ROM's `cmpi.b #-0x80; bge` is unreachable
     dead code (signed vs -128 is trivially true for every byte),
     so psg_dvol stays untouched -- byte-for-byte with the ROM
     including this quirk. */

Naming note: Ghidra's decompile calls these two globals
midi_current_scale_value / midi_scale_bucket (based on their
write site).  Port names them mi_dvel / psg_dvol (based on their
consumer usage in mq_setp: `mi_vel <- mi_dvel; psg_cvol <- psg_dvol`).
Same physical addresses (0x29a24 / 0x29a26), same behaviour.

CI still green.

  same outcome (1) as a successful verification, which is what
  gameLoop needs to take the tight-loop branch.

events.title: a_cleau: document the Ghidra study-door decompile ambiguity
events.message:
a_cleau: document the Ghidra study-door decompile ambiguity

Confirmed via raw disasm that the port is correct. Ghidra decompiles
the study-door branch as `sVar2 = 4; lcp_wait_head_reach_target(sVar2);`
while every other a_cleau branch decompiles as a plain no-arg call.
Disasm at action_clean_up+0x8e (0x1e9a0):

  move.w g_hatas, D0
  add.w  #-0xc, D0
  jsr    lcp_hwt (0x2568a)

Verified via disasm of 0x2568a that lcp_hwt is
`while (g_hacur != g_hatas) gameTick(0);` -- void, ignores D0.
The ADD is a dead compiler artifact (probably a `g_hatas -= 8;`
that the compiler elided when it saw g_hatas wasn't read after).
Port already emits `lcp_hwt();` which matches ROM behaviour byte-
for-byte. Comment added inline so a future audit doesn't re-flag
this.

events.title: port: byte-for-byte Ghidra fidelity fixes in a_kitcc + lt_tysa
events.message:
port: byte-for-byte Ghidra fidelity fixes in a_kitcc + lt_tysa

Three deviations found by a systematic diff of every AI action + every
delivery event against its Ghidra decompile.  The rest of the audit
(~55 functions across 10 files) verified matching.

* afood.c:a_kitcc  On the food_count==0 early-return path, the port
  cleared g_actif=NO; Ghidra leaves action_interruptible_flag YES
  (the reset only happens at the end of the eat-branch else).  Match
  ROM.

* afood.c:a_kitcc  Inside the inner chew loop, Ghidra re-writes
  head_sprite_frame = saved_head_frame at every condition check
  (comma-operator side effect in the while cond), so each inner
  iteration ticks with g_hsfra = saved first, THEN flips to 1, then
  2.  Port only restored g_hsfra after the inner loop exited, so
  iterations 2+ ticked with stale g_hsfra==2.  Restored inside the
  inner body.

* aletter.c:lt_tysa  Port had a NULL guard `if (str == NULL) return
  0;` before the leading-indent emit; Ghidra has no such guard.
  Removed -- was an invented safety net not in the ROM.

Ambiguity noted for later: Ghidra shows `sVar2 = 4;
lcp_wait_head_reach_target(sVar2);` in a_cleau's study-door branch,
but lcp_hwt() is void everywhere else.  Likely a decompiler artifact
from an unrecognised assignment; needs raw asm to confirm.  Port
matches the void-call form used elsewhere; revisit if study-door
cleanup misbehaves in gameplay.

events.title: tools: crash detector, frame-hash regression, 8-char truncation lint
events.message:
tools: crash detector, frame-hash regression, 8-char truncation lint

Three scripts lifting the ad-hoc bash I'd been running by hand into
reusable/CI-callable tools:

* run_hatari.sh -- boot LCP.PRG under headless Hatari for VBLS
  vbls, grep the log for bus errors + first PC + program-exit line,
  exit non-zero on any crash.  Env-var configured; the same command
  I've been re-typing all session.

* frame_hash.sh -- record a fixed-length canonical Hatari run,
  extract every Nth AVI frame, md5 them into tools/frame_hash.txt,
  and diff against tools/frame_hash.golden.  Default 2000 vbls
  (below the v_gtext $fd330c crash threshold at 2361), 40 frames
  at 1 fps.  Catches silent rendering regressions the crash
  detector misses because the game keeps running.  Golden checked
  in reflecting current known-good state.

* check_truncation.py -- scan every build/alcyon/work/*.s for
  _identifiers, group by 8-char prefix, fail if two distinct
  names share one.  Alcyon's lo68 sees only the first 8 chars of
  external identifiers, so a rename that collides silently
  aliases the two symbols at link time.  Currently 624 distinct
  prefixes, zero collisions.

fix(zip): unzip() dropped cartridge/peripheral formats from archives

The shared unzip() extension whitelist only allowed snapshot/tape/dsk
formats, so a .zip wrapping a lone .rom, .hfe, .scp, .cas, .mdr/.mdv,
.trd/.scl, .mgt/.img or .cdt came back with zero entries — silently
breaking MSX/Interface 2 cartridges-in-zip, CPC/Einstein flux images in
zip, and other peripheral formats before any platform-specific dispatch
logic ever saw them. Extended the whitelist to cover every extension any
platform's loadFile() can act on.

events.title: feat(spectrum): add ZX Interface 2 ROM cartridge support (16K/48K)
events.message:
feat(spectrum): add ZX Interface 2 ROM cartridge support (16K/48K)

A cartridge ties /ROMCS permanently active, disabling the internal ROM
across the whole $0000-$3FFF and replacing it with the cartridge's own 16K
image — no software paging register, unlike the VTX-5000's partial overlay.
Implemented as a slot-0 overlay via the existing setSlot0/externalRomPaged
mechanism, gated to the 16K/48K Spectrum (isInterface2Capable).

Insert/eject mirrors the MSX cartridge pattern already in this codebase:
stop, swap, reset, restart — matching real hardware, where booting the
cartridge means power-cycling with it already plugged in. The ROM pane now
also shows for 16K/48K models with a generic ejectCartridge() dispatcher
shared with MSX.

Default labels like "48K (default)" were written to localStorage as if they

events.title: fix(settings): Reset All wipes all storage, not just known keys
events.message:
fix(settings): Reset All wipes all storage, not just known keys

Reset settings > All only re-applied defaults to the enumerated setting
keys; it never cleared cached ROM images (IndexedDB rom-<model>), ROM
label keys, saved media, or any unknown/stale key. A corrupt cached ROM
was therefore un-clearable from the UI and could hang a machine at boot.

Add factoryReset() which clears the whole localStorage and deletes the
entire IndexedDB database, then reload after it so the app rebuilds from
defaults and re-fetches ROMs from the CDN. Guarded by a confirm() since
it also drops saved disks/tapes/snapshots.

events.title: buggyboy: add COURSES.DAT course editor + verified road/game viewers
events.message:
buggyboy: add COURSES.DAT course editor + verified road/game viewers

A new projects/buggyboy/editor/ toolkit to decode, edit and visualise
COURSES.DAT, built on the verified reconstruction (libbuggyboy.so).

Decode / edit (stdlib only):
- course_format.py  file<->memory map + 8-byte record decoder (constants
  mirrored from the verified C, each tagged with its source symbol)
- course_file.py    patch-in-place editor: markers, mask, control(rows/slope),
  scroll table, dashboard track pixels; backup-on-save, lossless round-trip
- roadprofile.py    decode the road elevation profile (segment slope + rows)
  and the roadside-object slots from the record stream
- decode_course.py  CLI stream/scroll/marker dump

Findings (empirical, pinned by tests): each 8-byte record = 15-bit select
mask + control (rows = (b&0xf8)>>3, slope = (b&7)-3) + marker word (bit15 =
event; runs = continuous features). Elevation is in the file; the horizontal
curve is runtime steering state (not in the file).

Visualise (drives the verified cores via ctypes):
- tui.py       curses editor: record browser, live dashboard-map paint,
  road elevation profile w/ live slope edit, PNG + live in-terminal 3rd-person
- roadview.py  render_road -> PNG/ASCII; GameSession drives init_leg +
  game_update + draw_frame (the whole verified game)
- roadwin.py   playable pygame window: held keys -> game_update/draw_frame,
  authentic road + object sprites + buggy + HUD (real pixels)

test_roundtrip.py: 14 tests (identity + edit round-trips, map/profile decode,
render pipeline); optional pygame/.so tests skip cleanly when absent.
