events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify game_update @ 0x1110e (89/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify game_update @ 0x1110e (89/91)

The per-frame in-race game-logic driver — the root of the three remaining
orchestrators (intermission + init_playfield both call it). No OS traps and it
returns each frame, so it verifies run-to-rts against the Musashi oracle despite
being the largest single function (2452 bytes, ~50 state globals + 7 tables).

Reconstruction (src/game_update.c, sections mirror the decomp)
- 1-11 (common path): pending-marker gate + engine-sound; input; fire ->
  dashboard-variant anim; bonus-time countdown; lean-anim + spin overrides;
  crash/auto-steer script vs live steering; engine-RPM/speed model + EGFREQ;
  scroll speed + view-flags wrap; wheel position + lean; road-curve integration,
  edge clamp, off-road crash; then build_road_geometry + return.
- 12 (course advance, view-wrap frames): collision probe, road_seg_data +
  road_curve_tbl shuffles, packed course-record unpack (control-code expansion),
  sprite-mode dispatch (scroll/palette), fx-block rebuild, event-jump-table
  dispatch, and the checkpoint/collision/score markers.
- gu_dispatch_event: table-driven event-jump-table dispatch to the evt_* family
  (evt_flag_gate alt entries; score-message groups A/B/C with per-entry gate +
  delta -> add_score + play_event_tune(8); checkpoint counters).

Test (test/test_game_update.py, ~580 cases; poison off — game_update is a
stateful RMW function, so the plain whole-image diff is the correct check)
- common-path fuzz (400); course else/pull/modes/crash/course fuzz; event
  dispatch idx 1-23. Full suite green (243 passed).

Fixes from code review: the fx-block base clear is clr.l (not a word); the
edge clamp uses lsr.w (unsigned); the score-message dispatch handles idx 14-23
distinctly (not collapsed into one handler).

Residuals (read-verified): sprite-mode 6 (object-display palette-swap
recw-0x7db4 write), the probe_collision D1-return path, and the idx 6/12
evt_flag_gate d7=6 variant.

events.title: osbind: cast macro args to declared trap-ABI types
events.message:
osbind: cast macro args to declared trap-ABI types

Every osbind macro in csrc/include/osbind.h now casts each arg to
its trap signature type so call sites can pass anything convertible
without having to know the underlying ABI (WORD=short, VOIDP/LONG
=long). Matches the update to ~/hatari-c/TOOLS/INCLUDE/osbind.h.

The prior port had macros like Fopen(n,m) -> gemdos(0x3D, n, m)
which forwarded args as-is; when a caller passed `Fopen(name, 0L)`
the mode (declared WORD in the trap) got pushed as 4 bytes instead
of 2, and the trap handler read only the top word.  For -1L / 0L
this happens to give the right value; for other mode/attr values
it would be wrong.  The new form always pushes the correct size:

  Fopen(fn*, mode WORD), Fcreate(fn*, attr WORD),
  Fread/Fwrite(h WORD, cnt LONG, buf*),
  Fsfirst(pat*, attr WORD), Fclose(h WORD),
  Malloc(sz LONG), Mfree(p*), Super(ssp*), Dsetpath(p*)

Note: does not resolve the WRITE_LETTER freeze yet (bus error at
PC=$abf4 writing $fffffffe -- SP corruption from somewhere).

events.title: xbios: pass correct arg types per Alcyon prototypes
events.message:
xbios: pass correct arg types per Alcyon prototypes

Alcyon OSBIND.O's xbios() is a variadic trap wrapper.  Callers must
push args at their DECLARED sizes to match what TOS reads from the
trap-frame stack:

    void Setscreen(VOIDP log, VOIDP phys, WORD mode)
    void Setpalette(VOIDP pal)
    void Dosound(VOIDP p)
    void Midiws(WORD n, VOIDP buf)
    LONG Giaccess(WORD data, WORD reg)

The port had been passing everything as (long) to force 4-byte
pushes, which mismatches WORD args by 2 bytes.  The old form
`Setscreen((long)g_dscp, -1L, -1L)` worked "by luck" for Setscreen
because -1L's upper half also reads as -1 WORD, but Alcyon's
compile-time-known arg-slot sizing then differs from what the
trap handler expects.

Fixes across 5 files, 7 Setscreen sites, 3 Setpalette, 1 Dosound,
1 Midiws, 6 Giaccess.  Also see the OSBIND.O text-segment
disassembly (16-byte identical shape for _xbios, _bios, _gemdos):

    23DF <saveret.L>    MOVE.L (A7)+, saveret   ; pop RA
    4E4E                TRAP #14                ; XBIOS
    2F39 <saveret.L>    MOVE.L saveret.L, -(A7) ; push RA back
    4E75                RTS                     ; caller cleans args

Note: this fix alone does not resolve the letter-writing action
freeze -- LCP.PRG still bus-errors at PC=$fd330c dereferencing a
bad pointer ($14e3bbe4) during the first prCh call.  The upstream
issue is elsewhere (likely a wrong prototype we haven't found yet
or an arg-slot corruption in one of the surrounding calls).

events.title: sf_sl: re-enable in main + rely on named osbind macros
events.message:
sf_sl: re-enable in main + rely on named osbind macros

sf_sl now uses fr_read(fhandle, 2L, &size) directly (matching
Ghidra's decompile), skipping the byte-reassembly path the old
port shim required.  Malloc/Fclose go through the named osbind
macros added in the previous commit.  With those two changes,
the loop completes cleanly and sf_sl is re-enabled at main.c:243.

Root-cause hypothesis for the earlier red-screen crash: the old
`_gemdos(GEMDOS_Malloc, (long)(size + 4), 0L, 0L)` form pushed
14 bytes on the stack for a trap that expects 6 (fn:2 + size:4).
Alcyon's variadic gemdos() forwarded them unchanged; the extra
padding may have interacted with the trap #1 ABI in a way that
corrupted state.  Once the call became `Malloc((long)(size + 4))`
-> `gemdos(0x48, size)` with the expected stack layout, the crash
disappeared.

Verified by tracing every Ghidra step (25..39) with Cconws and
confirming the game enters gameLoop with LCP + dog sprites
rendered in the house.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify draw_game_objects @ 0x12ef6 (89/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify draw_game_objects @ 0x12ef6 (89/91)

Reconstruction
- Per-frame scene/object draw orchestrator (a6 = draw_buffer). A deterministic
  PREFIX advances three pieces of state: the marker-decay slot (clear this
  frame's 14-record slot @marker_base+off, count down, decrement @+off+cd or
  retire the slot), the road-colour animation counters (view_parity/anim_counter
  += 2; anim_word + colour pair indexed by counter&0x1e), and the bonus-window
  flag animation. Then it draws ground, fg sprite, the roadside objects
  (draw_object_list split into passes around the active-sprite list: pass 1 =
  the `count` active rows, pass 2 = the remainder, both with count-derived
  a5/a3/d6), the scaled object, and the buggy — the last object pass ordered
  against the buggy by view & 4.

events.title: buggyboy: shard the 5 heavy fuzz/blit tests across xdist workers (3.4m -> 1.8m)
events.message:
buggyboy: shard the 5 heavy fuzz/blit tests across xdist workers (3.4m -> 1.8m)

Harness:
- The 5 tests that dominated the suite (100-183s each) were single pytest items,
  so xdist couldn't split them and one gated the whole parallel run. Shard each
  by separating case generation from checking: a generator replays the one seeded
  RNG stream (cheap) and a `chunk`-parametrized test runs only iterations where
  `i % FUZZ_CHUNKS == chunk`. Coverage is byte-identical (round-robin is an exact
  partition of the iteration range); re-seeding per chunk would change inputs.
    - test_obj_blit_engine::test_bare_fuzz            (183s, /8)
    - test_obj_blit_engine::test_bare_widths_every_fine_x (107s, parametrized by fine_x)
    - test_blit_objshift_w2::test_fuzz                (156s, /8)
    - test_blit_objshift::test_fuzz                   (155s, /8)
    - test_blit_objshift2::test_fuzz                  (153s, /8)
  Full suite 3m24s -> 1m50s. Sub-8s fuzz tests left un-sharded (an order of
  magnitude below the parallel floor; sharding would add worker overhead + diff).

Docs:

  parallelizes" recipe (generator + chunk parametrize).

events.title: port: shrink all identifiers to 8 chars + fix screen-buffer align
events.message:
port: shrink all identifiers to 8 chars + fix screen-buffer align

Alcyon C 4.14's `as68` truncates external symbols at 8 chars. The
build script's Python post-process was catching this per-name but
silently aliased any pair that collided; three groups were already
broken (`_schedule_row_0/1/2`, `body_lcp_file/buffer`,
`pex_lcp_file/buffer/ptr`).  Renamed all 248 identifiers over
8 chars to unique <=8-char forms and verified zero collisions
across 725 link-visible defs.

Also fixed a screen-buffer alignment hack: `g_dsb = g_srptr - 254`
aliased the dest_scr_buffer target directly onto the visible
screen.  Raw disasm of fill_top_rect_with_background at 0x1686c
and setup_screen_buffer at 0x16576 both show the same
`(base + 0x200) & ~0x1FF` align-up pattern that Ghidra's decompile
folds into misleading `+0x7F` / `+0x12F` literals.  dest_scr_buffer
is now an independent aligned buffer; sp_imfs and renderf.c page-
flip alt switched from 256- to 512-align to match Ghidra's `~0x1FF`
mask.  dest_scr_buffer_storage grown to 34816 bytes so worst-case
+512 align slack + 32000-byte screen fits with margin.

Restored Ghidra step 4 `gemdos(Dsetpath, "data")` in main() -- the
missing CWD change was making file_open(sounds.lcp) hang in its
retry loop.

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify draw_object_list @ 0x1306e (88/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify draw_object_list @ 0x1306e (88/91)

Reconstruction
- The per-frame roadside-object display-list dispatcher (register-glue). Two
  nested loops walk the object list; each object's a3 flag word gates a SPECIAL
  pass (record @buf_a+0x21d0+d6, only when the word is negative) and a NORMAL
  pass keyed on the low 6 bits (type -> record @buf_a+0x8a0+type*0xd0+d6). Each
  record yields colour, a buf_c-relative src long, rows-1, a vertical seed byte,
  the obj_type_jumptable index, and per-object x/dst offsets; the resolved
  handler is jsr'd. a0/a3/d2/d3/d4/d6 are saved/restored around the jsr, so the
  per-object vertical + x dst adjustments are temporary.
- Handlers wired: noop (bare rts), objsprite t1/t2/t4/w88, the t4+t1 stub
  @0x131ac, and the handler_lo mid-entries 0x1466a (0x98) / 0x144b2 (0x90, via
  the g_blit_objshift_w2 family). obj_handler_lo shared by both mid-entries.
- Decode note: prg_dis mis-renders the vertical-position muls.w/mulu.w as
  `and.w ...,a7`; the real math is (vseed-rows).b * view_flags >> 4 * width.
- d6 is sign-extended into the record base (adda.w), matching the 68000; the
  real caller (draw_game_objects tail) always passes d4=0 (one outer row).

Test
- test_object_list.py: isolating cases for every handler + jump-table index,
  the vertical offset, per-object x/dst offsets, the bonus-window type clamp,
  and the special pass; a 400-seed 15-object fuzz over the real d4=0 case; and
  explicit multi-row (d6-step) cases. Full suite green (187 passed).

Docs

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct blit_objshift 0x90 width-family (0x144ac entry)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct blit_objshift 0x90 width-family (0x144ac entry)

Reconstruction
- Generalize g_blit_objshift into blit_objshift_family(..., base_cells): the
  68000 packs two entry points into one unrolled blitter, the wider entry
  walking further down the shared LEFT/RIGHT clip ladders (BLIT_OBJSHIFT_SPEC
  §5). base_cells=1 = the 0x14680 entry (0x98 ceiling); base_cells=2 = the
  0x144ac entry (0x90 ceiling, 2-cell base) exposed as g_blit_objshift_w2.
- Dispatch generalized: base_ceiling = RIGHT_BOUND - 8*(base_cells-1); LEFT
  k=-A/8 clipped columns -> s=base_cells-k straddles with k-1 skipped columns
  (a0/a1 += 8 each), k>base_cells -> rts; RIGHT s=(RIGHT_BOUND-A)/8, s<0 -> rts;
  rewind = ROW_REWIND + 8*(total_cells-1). Reuses the verified objsh_* cells.
- Closes the "deeper unrolled bodies are dead" gap: the 0x90 family (LEFT-2 /
  RIGHT-2 / 2-cell base) is dispatched by draw_object_list object types 13-15.
- Removes now-orphan objsh_dispatch + OBJSH_LEFT_EDGE_COL.

Test
- test_blit_objshift_w2.py: enters at 0x144c8, sweeps every fine-x x every
  0x90-family case (LEFT-1/2, BASE, RIGHT-1/2, clipped both ends) x colour x
  rows x stride + 4000-fuzz poison. Green. test_blit_objshift (0x98 family)
  stays green (base_cells=1 reproduces the prior behaviour).

Docs

globals: fix _soundeffect_priority_table with real Ghidra values

Ghidra 0x2b44c dumps as a 32-byte array indexed by SOUND_EFFECT_ID.
Port had 32 guessed short values (0/5/3/8/etc) with a comment
"values chosen so the game's observed behaviour survives" -- a
placeholder that should have been a verification finding from the
start.

Real values (lower = higher priority):
  entries 0..5 (footsteps): 30
  entries 6..11 (TV, speech, head_nod, greeting, click, typewriter): 15
  entries 12, 13 (DOORBELL, DOORBELL_ECHO): 0 (beats everything)
  entries 14..18: 15
  entry 19 (WATER_TAP): 14
  entry 20 (ALARM_CLOCK): 16
  entry 21 (PHONE_RING): 1 (near-highest)
  entry 22 (SNORING): 15
  entries 23-31: garbage past the enum (SFX_* stops at 22)

Impact: previously DOORBELL had priority 2 (should be 0), PHONE_RING
had 9 (should be 1), so doorbell was preempted by any lower-value SFX
and phone ring was easily interrupted.  Real behavior: doorbell wins,
phone ring nearly wins.

events.title: sprglobs: seed g_selaf / g_seslm from Ghidra .data initializers
events.message:
sprglobs: seed g_selaf / g_seslm from Ghidra .data initializers

Ghidra dump at 0x2b6ee shows sprite_layer_flags[0..1] = 1 (SPRITE_IN_FRONT)
and [2..59] = 0.  Port had entire array in BSS = 0.  The pit that
opens: sp_upds has a special-case block at its top that reads
`if (sprite_layer_flags[0] == SPRITE_HIDDEN) sprite_active_image[
sprite_slot_map[0]] = NULL;`.  With the array BSS-zero, that fires
every frame and clears sprite_active_image[3] -- which is the LCP
body slot.

Also seeds g_seslm from Ghidra 0x2b766: {3, 4, 9, 9, ...}.  Index 0
maps to hardware slot 3 (LCP body), index 1 to slot 4 (LCP head),
rest to slot 9 (off-screen sentinel).  With BSS-zero, everything
mapped to slot 0 which sp_upds treats as "unused dog slot" -- the
LCP head/body sprites would land in the wrong slot on the first
tick.

globals: seed initial values Ghidra sets in .data (not BSS)

Dumped every Ghidra data-segment initializer and diffed against the
port.  Fixing five that were BSS-zero in the port but non-zero in
Ghidra's binary (would matter for animation gates and sentinels):

  g_cmmin  (clock_minute       @ 0x2b562):  0 -> 5
  g_chhou  (clock_hour         @ 0x2b564):  0 -> 6
  g_hatas  (head_anim_target   @ 0x29b98):  0 -> 8
  g_hacur  (head_anim_current  @ 0x29b96):  0 -> 8
  g_hamod  (head_anim_mode     @ 0x29b9a):  0 -> -1 (HEAD_ANIM_DISABLED)
  g_hadec  (head_anim_delay    @ 0x2ba2a):  0 -> 1

The clock ones are the ones the user's frozen-clock report chases:
clock_redraw_hands does `if (g_cmmin == time_minutes) return;` and
returns immediately when both are 0.  With clock_minute pre-seeded
to Ghidra's 5, the first game_tick body call sees a mismatch,
paints over the pre-existing 5:06 hands, and updates g_cmmin to
time_minutes so subsequent calls no-op until time actually advances.

The head-anim ones matter for sp_lcha: g_hamod = 0 (which is now
HEAD_ANIM_SHOWER after the enum realignment!) makes every horizontal
picker take the shower-mode branch, and g_hadec = 0 makes the
first decrement return early forever.  Setting them to Ghidra's
real defaults fixes both.

misordering ~10 of Ghidra's ~20 boot steps.

game), cl_drini (clock_draw_initial: white pixel + clock_redraw_hands),
cutscene_new_lcp_move_in_stub (minimal replacement for the full
move-in cutscene: seeds lcp_x=300, lcp_y=190, lcp_state=
STATE_STAND_SIDE_VIEW, dog position, head anim, and clears
intro_sequence_active so the event queue can drain).

Rewritten main() sequence with per-step Ghidra references:
  step  6: setup_screen_buffer
  step  7: init_bitmask_tables
  step  9: lc_load (was called at step 14 previously - CRITICAL fix)
  steps 11-13: decompress_scn (house.scn)

  step 16-19: lcp_create_random (NEW) + al_locs (body.lcp + PEx.LCP)

stub now sets those before endless_game_loop runs, matching Ghidra's

up to the top-floor study door and executes ACTION_PEEK_AROUND.

animation are running.

events.title: Fix player starting state + re-enable AI trigger
events.message:
Fix player starting state + re-enable AI trigger

Two blocking bugs the user reported that my earlier "byte-for-byte
verification" completely missed because I never verified the boot
sequence or the game-loop wiring:

1. endless_game_loop had check_for_any_action_triggers() commented
   out with a stale rationale ("crashes on uninit house geometry").
   The AI dispatcher never ran, so the resident never picked any
   action.  Re-enabled -- the crash the comment worried about was
   from the earlier enum/table bugs that this session fixed.

2. Initial lcp_x=160, lcp_y=100 was a placeholder from before the
   port had any real boot code.  Ghidra's binary leaves both in
   BSS (=0) and lets cutscene_new_lcp_move_in set them to (300, 190)
   -- the position after the doorbell/door-open sequence, at the
   right-hand edge of the ground floor.  Seed the port's static
   initializer with (300, 190) so we start from a valid on-floor
   position without needing the whole cutscene ported yet.

3. lcp_state = 0 used to mean STATE_STAND_IDLE, but after the
   PLAYER_STATE enum realignment (984174b) STATE_WALK_FRAME_0 = 0
   and STATE_STAND_IDLE = 8.  Reading body_sprite_frame_table[0]
   still gives body frame 0 (walk mid-step) so the resident looked
   frozen in a walk pose.  Seed lcp_state = STATE_STAND_SIDE_VIEW
   (=34), which is what the cutscene establishes right before it
   hands control to the AI dispatcher.

The user was right: my earlier verification checked only that
individual functions matched Ghidra's decompile shape.  It never
verified that the boot path actually ran end-to-end, so the fact
that the AI tick was #ifdef'd out (in a stale-workaround comment)
went unnoticed across the entire session.

events.title: midi_seq: fix mh_chac / mh_temp / mh_volu against Ghidra
events.message:
midi_seq: fix mh_chac / mh_temp / mh_volu against Ghidra

Verified Ghidra 0x11246 / 0x11264 / 0x1129c disassembly against the
port's header handlers.  Findings:

  mh_chac (0x80, channel count) at 0x11246
    Ghidra: reads p[2] into midi_channel_count (0x298f0), calls
    midi_seq_build_scale_table with that value, advances p+3.
    Port was a pure no-op stub.  Added the missing global (Alcyon
    8-char-safe short name g_mchcn since midi_channel_map already
    truncates to _midi_ch), the read, and the mq_bust call.

  mh_temp (0x81, tempo) at 0x11264
    Ghidra: reads p[1] into midi_tempo, then computes
    g_mtspb (0x298f4) = 2400 / midi_tempo, advances p+2.
    Port had p[2] into g_mtspb (wrong side effect) and advanced p+3
    (wrong stride).  Now matches: single-byte payload, ticks-per-beat
    computed from tempo.

  mh_volu (0x83, volume) at 0x1129c
    Ghidra: pure p+2 advance, no side effect.  Port had p[1] into
    midi_default_velocity and advanced p+3.  Now matches: skip 2 bytes.

Assembly diff confirmed against Ghidra's exact instruction sequences
(muls.w #0x960 -> divs, move p[2] -> globals, addq.l #0x2/3 for
pointer advance).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: midi_seq: neutralise mh_scat's wrong mq_bust() call
events.message:
midi_seq: neutralise mh_scat's wrong mq_bust() call

Two bugs stacked: (1) mh_scat called mq_bust() with no argument, so
Alcyon K&R semantics passed uninitialised stack as the scale value,
(2) even with the right argument the semantic was wrong -- Ghidra's
0x84 header handler at 0x112a4 does NOT invoke midi_seq_build_scale_
table.  Instead it stores the raw byte at 0x29a24 and a bucketed
odd-integer (5/7/9/11/13/15 based on thresholds 0x17/0x27/0x37/
0x57/0x67/0x80) at 0x29a26.  midi_seq_build_scale_table is called
from the song-load path elsewhere, not from the header parser.

For now the stub is a no-op with a TODO -- MIDI playback isn't yet
active in the boot flow the port exercises (midi_is_playing guards
in sf_irqp / sc_ren8), so this change removes the corrupted
mq_bust call without introducing new state divergence.

The port had:
  - COLOR_black = 1, COLOR_white = 0 (Ghidra: 0 and 14)

for the print_char color arg (COLOR_black=0), was `move #1,(sp)`

events.title: Align PLAYER_STATE/HEAD_ANIM/SFX/HOUSE_POS enums with Ghidra
events.message:
Align PLAYER_STATE/HEAD_ANIM/SFX/HOUSE_POS enums with Ghidra

Discovered during function-level verification: the port's enums.h had
made-up values for most non-walk PLAYER_STATE entries, plus wrong
values for HEAD_ANIM_MODE, SOUND_EFFECT_ID, and HOUSE_POS.  Every call
site that used those named constants was silently writing the wrong
value to lcp_state / g_hamod / sfx / dest position.

Concrete proof: Ghidra a_nodh at 0x21fa4 writes 0x22 (34) to lcp_state
but the port's a_nodh compiled to 'clr _lcp_sta' (0) because the port
had STATE_STAND_SIDE_VIEW = 0.  After this fix the same source now
compiles to 'move #34,_lcp_sta', matching Ghidra byte-for-byte.  Same
recovery applies to every "STATE_STAND_SIDE_VIEW" callsite (34+ of them).

Enums dumped verbatim from the Ghidra binary.  Notable value shifts:
STATE_STAND_IDLE 0->8, STATE_STAND_FACING_SCREEN 28->33,
STATE_STAND_SIDE_VIEW 0->34, STATE_CROUCH_DOWN 34->35,
STATE_REACH_INTO_CABINET 32->90, STATE_PHONE_PICKUP/TALKING 74/75->56/57,
STATE_YAWN_* 17/18->82/83, STATE_DANCE_STEP_* 61/62->80/81,
STATE_EAT_BITE/CHEW 63/64->71/72, STATE_SHOWER_STAND 65->64;
HEAD_ANIM_DISABLED 0->-1, WALKING 1->0x42, READING 4->0x41;
SFX_* mostly renumbered (FOOTSTEP_STAIRS 12->0, DOOR_OPEN 3->14, etc.);
HOUSE_POS: BTM_STAIR_LANDING 40->32, DOG_BOWL 42->33, etc.

Also removes STATE_EXERCISE_CROUCH (Ghidra folds it into
STATE_CROUCH_DOWN=35), keeping the name as an alias for compat.
POS_BTM_SCREEN_EDGE local #define in movement.c removed in favour of

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify the object-sprite blit engine @ 0x131f6
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify the object-sprite blit engine @ 0x131f6

Reconstruction (shared object-block blit engine; not among the original 91):
- One parameterized fine-x 4-plane masked sprite blitter spanning 0x131f6..
  0x13c8a (~2708 bytes), reached by ~18 object-type jump-table entries that
  preset a width family (0x80/0x88/0x90/0x98 -> base cell count 0xc0/0xb8/0xb0/
  0xa8) and join the shared body. Kernel = the same 4-word transparency mask as
  blit_objshift (~(w0|w1|w2|~w3), 0xFFFF-seeded so the high word rotates into
  the straddled column) but a plain shifted-OR copy with NO color_pairs. Modeled
  as one objsprite_core (width_idx + ladder rung) with thin g_objsprite_t* glue
  per entry; the 0x145fc per-view register transform is reconstructed inline
  (objsprite_view_transform), verified transitively through the view wrappers.
- Two spec errors caught against the oracle and corrected (documented in
  OBJ_BLIT_ENGINE_SPEC.md): the mask seed is 0xFFFFFFFF (moveq #$ff), and the
  0x145fc offset mask is 0xFFE0 (moveq #$e0) — not the zero-high-word variants.
- addrs.h: A_obj_view_xform (0x1722a). names.txt: proto/cmt for all 16 entries
  + the helper.

Harness:
- test_obj_blit_engine.py: whole-image differential vs the Musashi oracle across
  every width family x fine-x x dispatch branch (LEFT ladder / BASE / WIDE
  ladder / off both ends) x rows, plus the bare / a6-relative / view-transform /
  scan-table / bsr-hi wrapper classes, poison on. Green byte-for-byte (168).

Deferred (sound, noted with TODO): t53 (0x13204 alt entry) is verified by
candidate-consistency vs the oracle-verified t4 — its dispatch reads a caller-set
CCR flag the differential harness cannot control (adda.w sets no flags). The
mid-body re-entries t60 (0x13444) / t61 (0x13784) need a live jump-table register
snapshot (draw_object_list, still unverified) and are left as TODO, not faked.

Fourth object-block unit; collapses ~4 apparent engines + the entry swarm into
one parameterized reconstruction.

events.title: Faithful port pass: game_tick, dog pipeline, table sizes, per-var Ghidra fixes
events.message:
Faithful port pass: game_tick, dog pipeline, table sizes, per-var Ghidra fixes

Live-verified against Ghidra via HTTP scripts (FindSymbols, DumpByName,
DumpFromFile, CheckFunctions).  Ghidra address / value / size dumps are
authoritative for every change below.

New files
- csrc/sprload.c: sprite pointer registration pass.  sp_reglp() drives
  the second-pass loop over sprites_files (mirrors Ghidra main
  0x1579c..0x15828) and, via sp_regs + sp_genma, populates
  dog_sprite_pointers, dog_mask_pointers, g_sedeh, g_sedew keyed by
  sp_fidx[50] (Ghidra sprite_file_index_table @ 0x2A084).  Owns the
  14 KB sp_mbuf mask buffer.  Kept out of globals.c so Alcyon C168's
  fixed-size symbol table doesn't overflow.
- csrc/tick_tables.c: animation frame tables consumed by
  game_tick_and_animate (clock/dog-eating/alarm/phone/fire/petting)
  plus a handful of frame-state globals.  Same rationale for keeping
  them out of globals.c.

Ghidra-faithful port additions
- tick.c: full game_tick_and_animate rewrite matching Ghidra 0x256A6
  in both paths (idle animation loop + carrying-object reposition).
  Adds the clock pendulum, dog-bowl countdown, fire, alarm, phone,
  record player, TV static, and keyboard-dispatch blocks that the
  earlier stub skipped.  Uses the new tick_tables.c tables.
- dog.c: added dg_ipos (Ghidra dog_init_position) -- sets
  dog_x=100, dog_y=195 and clears the two dog sprite slots via
  sp_spud(SPRITE_UNUSED_0).  Renamed from dog_init_position to
  dg_ipos to avoid the 8-char linker collision with dog_initialized
  (both truncate to _dog_ini).
- main.c: wires sp_reglp after al_lost and dg_ipos after lc_load so
  the dog pipeline is ready before endless_game_loop.  Full palette
  Setpalette + Physbase snapshot in the aes_vdi_jnit tail.  Full

events.title: Fix TypeError crash on an incomplete bit-op source line
events.message:
Fix TypeError crash on an incomplete bit-op source line

instructionAttrs's bit-op (bchg/bset/bclr/btst) branch accessed
parsed.operands[1].value with only an optional-chain guard on
`operands` itself, not on index 1. parseLine explicitly tolerates
incomplete lines (its own docstring says so, for "as you type"
editing), so a bit-op with only one operand entered so far (e.g.
"btst d0" before the destination operand is typed) has
operands.length === 1, and indexing [1] reads undefined --
.value then throws. Reachable during normal editing, not a rare
edge case. Added the missing guard and a regression test.

events.title: Fix disassemble() returning more rows than requested, and other bugs
events.message:
Fix disassemble() returning more rows than requested, and other bugs

- disassemble() violated the DAP disassemble contract (must return
  exactly `count` rows): when a negative instructionOffset needed
  padding rows for addresses before available memory, the code pushed
  the padding AND then still sliced `count` more instructions,
  returning count+paddingCount rows instead of count. Reachable via
  ordinary UI scrolling near the start of available memory, not an
  edge case. Also capped padding itself at `count` for the case where
  the negative offset alone would need more padding than the whole
  request budget.
- MAX_BYTES_PER_INSTRUCTION was 8, but 68k's true worst case is 10
  bytes (e.g. MOVE.L $12345678.L,$12345678.L -- long-absolute source
  and destination, not rare in code addressing hardware registers
  directly). Undersizing it could under-fetch the backward-estimate
  buffer and fail to find baseAddress in the decoded output at all.
- Padding rows carried a placeholder addr:0, which is a meaningful
  Amiga address (reset SP/PC vectors) -- if the source map has any
  entry covering it, a padding row (meant to represent unavailable
  data) could get a plausible-but-bogus symbol/location attached.
  Skip the source-map lookup for padding rows specifically.

An existing test asserted the old buggy row-count behavior as
correct; fixed it to match the DAP contract and added a case for the
padding-exceeds-count edge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Fix breakpoint/watchpoint tracking corruption on emulator-call failure
events.message:
Fix breakpoint/watchpoint tracking corruption on emulator-call failure

Every "set breakpoints" method (source, instruction, function, data,
temp) pushed its new tracking entry into the corresponding array/map
BEFORE the await that arms it in the emulator, with no rollback on
failure. A failed setBreakpoint/setWatchpoint/setRegisterWatch call
(e.g. a transient RPC error) left a phantom entry permanently tracked:
invisible to the DAP client (never in any removal loop), unremovable,
and able to misroute a later real breakpoint/hit at the same address
through the wrong code path.

Also: setInstructionBreakpoints and setFunctionBreakpoints had no
try/catch at all, so a single failed setBreakpoint call aborted the
whole batch instead of reporting that one breakpoint as unverified.
The custom-chipset-register data breakpoint path (one DAP variable
that can need two underlying watchpoints at different addresses) now
rolls back the first watchpoint if the second fails, instead of
leaving it live in the emulator but untracked. Every removal loop
(source/instruction/function/data/register-watch) now catches each
individual removal failure so one bad removal doesn't abort the
array/map reset that follows it, leaving later entries stuck in a
"removed on the emulator side but still tracked" state.

Reconstruction (2nd object-block sub-pixel blitter; not among the original 91):
- blit_objshift2 @ 0x13ed6 (~1830 bytes) — a fine-x-shifted masked sprite
  blitter used by the 0x13e68 object-handler family (via 0x13e8e). PURE LEAF;
  no Ghidra decompilation (disassembly-driven). DISTINCT from the colour-indexed
  blit_objshift @ 0x14680: it builds its transparency mask from only two source

  (left off-screen / L0C / L1C / L2C / base / W2 / W1 / W0 / right off-screen)

  word stays 0xffff into rol.l; straddle cell uses 32-bit lsl.l/rol.l by
  16-fine_x; left-edge cell uses 16-bit lsl.w (writes col1); right-edge cell
  uses 16-bit lsr.w by fine_x (writes col0). Reuses rotl32/dup16.

events.title: Fix (long) cast on file handle -- HOUSE RENDERS!
events.message:
Fix (long) cast on file handle -- HOUSE RENDERS!

fr_read (and every other GEMDOS Fread/Fclose/Fwrite call) was
casting the short file handle to (long):

    err = _gemdos(GEMDOS_Fread, (long) fileHandle, count, (long) buffer);

Alcyon's variadic _gemdos wrapper pushes each argument at its natural
type width, so the (long) cast pushed 4 bytes where TOS expects 2.
The trap handler then read:
    SP+0 : func code (short) = 0x3F -- OK
    SP+2 : handle (short) = HIGH word of the long handle = 0x0000
    SP+4 : count (long) = (fh_lo << 16) | (count_hi) -- corrupted
    SP+8 : buffer (long) = (count_lo << 16) | ... -- corrupted

So TOS was silently reading from handle 0 (stdin) with a huge bogus
count, returning 0 bytes for every call.  Files were "opening"
successfully but Fread was never actually reading anything -- the
buffers stayed at whatever pattern they had after BSS init and
GEMDOS_Malloc filling.

Explanation for the striped house: our LCP sprite draws looked
plausible because sp_lbal generated deterministic pixel data
from the (mostly-zero) body_lcp_buffer.  Same for the house
compositor -- it faithfully blk-copied a uniform pattern from
the untouched g_srptr buffer.

Fix: pass fileHandle as its natural short type across every
_gemdos(GEMDOS_Fread/Fclose/Fwrite/...) call.  Bulk-patched save.c,
assets.c, letload.c, cards.c, sound.c.

Result: HOUSE.SCN decompresses correctly, blkcopy32 copies real
house pixels into the compositor, and the ST shifter shows the
full LCP living room -- yellow-walled kitchen, blue-walled
bedroom, cyan bathroom, TV / stereo / plants / staircase, dining
table -- matching the reference screenshot from a real ST run.

Palette is slightly off (yellow walls instead of green) but the
scene structure is exact.  That's the next thing to look at once
we chase the remaining check_for_any_action_triggers NULL deref
and the palette applies_clothing_colors init function.

events.title: Rewrite decompress_scn literal path with explicit np sequencing
events.message:
Rewrite decompress_scn literal path with explicit np sequencing

Alcyon C 4.14 mis-compiles the K&R idiom
    lit = *np++;
    lit = (lit << 4) | *np++;
    lit = (lit << 4) | *np++;
    lit = (lit << 4) | *np++;
into code that produces the SAME output for every iteration, and
the sequence itself always fires -- regardless of the outer `if
(*np == 0x0F)` guard, so decompress_scn returned repeated 0x1D78
in every out_words[] slot instead of walking the word dictionary.
That's why the compositor blk-copied a uniform pattern out of
g_srptr and the display looked like vertical stripes.

Rewrite with each *np dereference on its own statement and an
explicit np = np + 1 between reads.  The literal branch now reads
what it claims.

Visual output still shows stripes though, because the SIZE and
DICTIONARY reads are also returning garbage (verified by dumping
sizebuf and word_dict values back to the console -- body_size
comes back 0 or 2 instead of 20048, and word_dict[0] is 0x1E7A
instead of 0xFFFF).  The root cause is elsewhere -- probably an
issue with the fr_read wrapper or the local unsigned-char array
storage under Alcyon.  Leaving that for the next session.

events.title: Double scrbufA + 256-align both page-flip screens
events.message:
Double scrbufA + 256-align both page-flip screens

Previous port put the compositor at scrbufA + 0xCE (odd offset
from BSS start) and the alt physbase at scrbufA + 0x19A -- Ghidra's
literal offsets in the original binary, where SCREEN_BUFFER_A
happened to be placed at an odd address so both landed 256-aligned.
Our linker puts scrbufA on an even boundary so those same offsets
land on unaligned addresses, and the ST shifter's Physbase register
IGNORES the low 8 bits of an unaligned pointer, so Setscreen(-1,
alt, -1) actually shows the aligned-down address (~206 bytes
before what we composed).

Grow scrbufA to 64 KB and split it into two 256-aligned 32 KB
screens:
  compositor:  align_up_256(scrbufA)          (~scrbufA + 0x000)
  alt physbase: align_up_256(scrbufA) + 0x8000 (~scrbufA + 0x8000)
Both are 256-aligned regardless of where the linker puts scrbufA
so the shifter shows exactly what the compositor wrote.

The visible frame is still striped rather than the house scene --
that's a separate issue (probably the decompress_scn output or the
blkcopy32 source pointer) that needs its own investigation.

events.title: Fix short-vs-byte offset in check_time_based_actions
events.message:
Fix short-vs-byte offset in check_time_based_actions

Ghidra:
    *(short *)((int)activity_schedule_table[0]
               + (int)(short)(lcp.activity_level << 1)
               + (int)(short)((hours_since_wake / 2) % 3 << 4))

The (int)ptr cast makes the following `+ offset` a *byte* offset --
the << 1 and << 4 already yield byte counts (2 bytes per short,
16 bytes per row).  Our port had

    *((short *) activity_schedule_table[0]
      + (lcp.activity_level << 1)
      + (((hours_since_wake / 2) % 3) << 4))

which is short-pointer arithmetic, so the compiler scaled the same
constants by ANOTHER factor of 2 -- we were reading 2 rows and 2

events.title: Replace hardcoded 0x2CA00 alt buffer with scrbufA-relative offset
events.message:
Replace hardcoded 0x2CA00 alt buffer with scrbufA-relative offset

Root cause of the persistent \"PC in TOS ROM with \$XXXX\$XXXX
repeated-word crash\":

Ghidra's screen_render_8hz page-flip toggles current_screen_mfdb->
fd_addr between save_physbase and a hardcoded 0x2CA00.  In the 1985
binary that literal is SCREEN_BUFFER_A + 0x19A -- an offset INSIDE
the same BSS array that sp_imfs uses (SCREEN_BUFFER_A + 0xCD for
the compositing MFDB).  Both the alt physbase and the compositing
target live inside SCREEN_BUFFER_A, 205 bytes apart.

Our port's linker places scrbufA at a DIFFERENT BSS address, so the
literal 0x2CA00 in renderf.c lands on totally unrelated globals.
When blkcopy32 writes 32000 bytes to that unrelated location, it
silently overwrites part of our own BSS (probably MFDB structs, VDI
state, dog_x/y, sprite tables...) -- so the third or fourth sc_ren8
iteration crashes deep inside TOS's VDI dispatcher with garbage
MFDB pointers containing the corrupted data.

Fix: compute the alt buffer as (char *)scrbufA + 0x19A so the two
buffers stay inside the same 33 KB scrbufA region, matching the
1985 memory layout.

Runtime dump before the fix showed dst cycling through
    30DC8 (initial scrbufA + 0xCD)
    28000 (save_physbase, GEM screen)
    2CA00 (wrong -- into unrelated BSS)
after the fix:
    30E94 (initial scrbufA + 0xCE, even-aligned)
    28000 (save_physbase)
    30E94 (scrbufA + 0x19A instead of 0x2CA00) [dumped as 30E94
           because that address happened to equal + 0xCE +
           some offset in this build -- next test will confirm]

TOS ROM VDI crash is now gone.  New crash is a NULL read at PC in
our text (~\$1e386) op \$3d50 = MOVE.W (A0), disp(A6) with A0 = 0,
much easier to diagnose.

events.title: Fix 8-char external-symbol aliasing across 5 collision pairs
events.message:
Fix 8-char external-symbol aliasing across 5 collision pairs

Alcyon's linker sees only the first 8 characters of external symbol
names (i.e. the C name's first 7 chars plus the leading underscore),
so any two source-level names that agree on their first 7 chars are
silently merged into a single BSS block.  We hit this earlier with
body_shape_data / body_shape_data_buf; the same trap was hiding in
five other pairs I hadn't audited.

Audit found (via nm68 + .comm inspection of the generated .s):
    SCREEN_BUFFER_A / SCREEN_BUFFER_B      -> _SCREEN_
    bitmask_32bit_or / bitmask_32bit_and   -> _bitmask
    current_screen_mfdb / currentPosition  -> _current
    midiEventPtr / midiEventSize           -> _midiEve
    file_load / file_load_letter_template  -> _file_lo
Each pair emitted `.comm _<7chars>,SIZE` twice, and the linker
collapsed them into one storage block.  bitmask_32bit_or and
bitmask_32bit_and overlapping meant init_bitmask_tables' second pass
overwrote the first pass' entries, so the "OR" and "AND" tables
returned identical values -- silently corrupting sp_lbbd / sp_lbhd.
The SCREEN_BUFFER_A/B overlap meant setup_screen_buffer and
sprite_init_MFDBs pointed g_srptr and g_srmfd.fd_addr at the SAME
33 KB of memory, so the background copy and the compositing target
raced through each other.  file_load / file_load_letter_template
overlap meant our just-ported Ghidra file_load wrapper aliased the
letter-template loader, corrupting either or both depending on link
order.

Rename each collision to a distinct <=7-char C name (kept the
Ghidra-canonical spelling where possible, moved the second symbol
to a short alias):
    SCREEN_BUFFER_A -> scrbufA
    SCREEN_BUFFER_B -> scrbufB
    bitmask_32bit_or  -> bm32or
    bitmask_32bit_and -> bm32and
    currentPosition   -> curPos       (midi_seq.c local-ish name)
    midiEventPtr      -> midiEvP
    midiEventSize     -> midiEvS
    file_load_letter_template -> fl_ltpl  (Ghidra file_load stays)

Verified via nm68 that each pair now emits distinct `.comm` blocks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Index g_otmfd as MFDB array, not byte offset (od_draw)
events.message:
Index g_otmfd as MFDB array, not byte offset (od_draw)

Ghidra: `object_tab_mfdb + object_index` (pointer arithmetic with
MFDB stride).  Our port had `(MFDB *)((char *)g_otmfd + g_oiidx)`
which treats g_oiidx as a raw byte offset -- for any non-zero
object ID that lands on a misaligned MFDB structure, so VDI got
junk width / height / fd_addr and crashed inside its clipper.

Rewrite as `&((MFDB *)g_otmfd)[g_oiidx]` so the stride is
sizeof(MFDB) = 18 bytes, matching the shape of the Ghidra
disassembly (which multiplies index by 18 before the base add).

events.title: Scale sp_updb / sp_lchu frame offsets by 168 / 84
events.message:
Scale sp_updb / sp_lchu frame offsets by 168 / 84

Ghidra's `body_lcp_file + frame` / `body_shape_data + frame` (and
same for pex_lcp_file / head_shape_data) is decompiler shorthand
for `+ frame * frame_stride` -- the disassembly at 0x2669a shows
`muls.w #0x54, D0` (=*84) for the shape-data offset and
`muls.w #0xa8, D0` (=*168) for the source file offset.  Our port
took the decompile literally so `body_lcp_file + 22` gave 22 bytes
into the file instead of 22*168 = 3696 bytes, and sp_lcpf read
garbage.

Multiply explicitly:
  body.lcp     -> 168 bytes per body frame (21 rows * 8 bytes/row)
  body_shape   ->  84 bytes per body frame (21 rows * 4 bytes/row)
Same 168 / 84 stride for the head pair.

events.title: Force even alignment on g_srmfd.fd_addr (SCREEN_BUFFER_A + 0xCD)
events.message:
Force even alignment on g_srmfd.fd_addr (SCREEN_BUFFER_A + 0xCD)

Ghidra sprite_init_MFDBs writes screen_mfdb.fd_addr = SCREEN_BUFFER_A
+ 0xCD.  In the 1985 binary the linker placed SCREEN_BUFFER_A at an
odd address so + 0xCD (=205, itself odd) landed on an even byte
suitable for 68000 MOVE.L reads/writes.  Our modern linker aligns
BSS on even boundaries, so + 0xCD is odd -- which trips an Address
Error inside blkcopy32's `MOVE.L (A1),(A0)` the first time sc_ren8's
full-screen background copy runs.

Round SCREEN_BUFFER_A + 0xCD UP to the next even byte in our port
so the destination pointer matches the parity the 1985 code
depended on.

Next crash is a NULL read further inside game_tick_and_animate --
one of the sprite tables still uninit.

events.title: Read _hz_200 / _vbclock directly from $04BA / $0462
events.message:
Read _hz_200 / _vbclock directly from $04BA / $0462

Matches Ghidra screen_render_8hz's shape:
    saveSSP = _gemdos(Super, 0);
    save_hz200 = _hz_200._2_2_;   // low word of _hz_200 (long)
    save_vbclock = _vbclock;
    _gemdos(Super, saveSSP);
Ghidra resolves _hz_200 to absolute address $04BA and _vbclock to
$0462 -- both TOS system variables in low memory, bumped by TOS's
own timer / VBL IRQ handlers.  In our C port that means a direct
long deref of *(long*)0x04BA / *(long*)0x0462 in supervisor mode.

No game-side IRQ handler needed for the frame-rate gate -- that
mirror was our port's earlier fiction.  midi_seq_init_timer at
Ghidra 0x11112 drives the MFP Timer A (200 Hz sound-engine tick),
NOT the frame timer.

Also: remove diagnostic gemdos/bios markers from endless_game_loop
so it matches Ghidra faithfully now that the frame gate works.

events.title: Port setup_screen_buffer/sprite_init_MFDB/copy_screen from Ghidra
events.message:
Port setup_screen_buffer/sprite_init_MFDB/copy_screen from Ghidra

Faithful ports of three Ghidra-verified routines that main() at
0x00015546 chains together to allocate and initialise the double-
buffered compositing screen.

- gfx_prim.c setup_screen_buffer (Ghidra 0x16576):
    * MFDB_A.fd_addr = NULL (source MFDB for vro_cpyfm, NULL = "device
      screen" per VDI convention)
    * g_srptr = align_up_512(SCREEN_BUFFER_B + 0x12F)
    * sprite_init_MFDB(0x1D00, &MFDB_screen_ptr, g_srptr,
                       scale*320, scale*200)
    * copy_screen(vdihandle, &MFDB_screen_ptr)
- gfx_prim.c sprite_init_MFDB (Ghidra 0x16612): populate an MFDB with
  address, dimensions, wdwidth, stand=0, nplanes=4.  The first arg
  is unused (nplanes is hardcoded); kept to match the original.
- gfx_prim.c copy_screen (Ghidra 0x164FA): vro_cpyfm(handle,
  ALL_WHITE, points, &MFDB_A, dst) with points covering the full
  destination rectangle.  Snapshots the visible physbase into the
  memory buffer described by dst.

- globals.c: add screen_scale_factor=1, MFDB_A={0}, and 33280-byte
  BSS SCREEN_BUFFER_B[] (0x12F header + 512-byte align slack + 32000
  pixel bytes for 320x200 ST low-res).
- enums.h: define ALL_WHITE=0 (VDI raster-op mode for "fill with 1s")
- main.c: call setup_screen_buffer() in place of the ad-hoc Malloc
  block I had here.  Init order now matches the top of Ghidra's main.

LCP.PRG advances through appl_init/graf_handle/v_opnvwk, palette,
asset loads, HYBER save (g_lcldd=1), house.scn decompress, then
enters endless_game_loop and takes the lcp_enter_study_and_save
branch (since a save was loaded).  It exits cleanly there rather
than bus-erroring, which is a step forward -- the tight-loop path
still needs midi_seq_init_timer + sprite_init_MFDBs before frames
tick and sprites draw.

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify render_road (84/91)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify render_road (84/91)

Reconstruction:
- render_road @ 0x19144 (2256 bytes) — the pseudo-3D road rasterizer, the
  densest function in the binary (PURE LEAF). Draws the perspective road one
  scanline at a time across seven dbf bands; each row pulls a control long from
  road_width_tbl (a5) + a perspective param (a4) and dispatches on flag bits to
  a 16-pixel-column 4-plane blit variant, copying road-texture columns from
  buf_b into the screen band (a2 = draw_buffer + 0x4100) and filling the
  interior/shoulders with solid plane patterns. Faithful 1:1 machine model with
  goto labels named by Ghidra address; 16-bit-wrap-faithful throughout.
- The near/far band copies have distinct blit tails (band B via a "second"
  selector, band C via rr_band_C_near/_far, band D via "second") — reusing a
  near tail for its far copy shifted the edge cell by one column.
- render_road_thunk @ 0x15af6 (bra.w 0x19144) is a plain alias.
- RENDER_ROAD_SPEC.md: the authoritative per-band spec (flag legend, table map,
  16-bit-wrap notes) used to drive the reconstruction.

Harness:
- test_render_road.py: whole-image differential vs the Musashi oracle, fuzzed
  across all seven bands and every flag family, poison/attribution on, plus the
  thunk-alias entry. Green byte-for-byte (129 passed).

Docs: names.txt (render_road_thunk, road_edge_sel), STATUS.md 82->84/91.

events.title: feat(tape): add CSW tape support
events.message:
feat(tape): add CSW tape support

Parse CSW v1/v2 square-wave captures (RLE and zlib Z-RLE) into a packed
pulse block that replays through the existing PULSES phase via genuine
edge-sampling — CSW has no discrete data blocks, so the ROM instant-load

set-level block seeds the initial polarity.

loader/restore/picker paths, TapePane, the ZIP loadable-extensions
filter, and the MCP load tool. Verified end-to-end by edge-loading a real
v1 CSW (Macadam Bumper, 788961 pulses) to its full loading screen.

events.title: bridge: fix SCRIPT payload truncation at 479 bytes (v1.20) (#9)
events.message:
bridge: fix SCRIPT payload truncation at 479 bytes (v1.20) (#9)

handle_script copied the whole script text through a static 480-byte
buffer in one pass, silently dropping everything past byte 479. Long
multi-line scripts lost their tail commands, and a line cut mid-Echo
broke output capture (the sentinel still ran, so the host saw a clean
but empty result).

Convert the ';' separators back to newlines in 480-byte chunks instead,
so scripts up to the 8 KB protocol line limit are written intact.
Verified on real hardware with a ~1 KB script that previously lost its
last five commands.

Rebased from xphileby's #7 onto current main and bumped from v1.19 to
v1.20 to avoid a version-tag collision with the v1.19 phase-counter
change already on main. Source only — the amiga-bridge binary needs a
`make bridge` rebuild in a follow-up commit before deployment (Docker
was unavailable on the machine that did the rebase).

events.title: Fix unbounded growth of VariablesManager's handle maps
events.message:
Fix unbounded growth of VariablesManager's handle maps

variableHandles/locationHandles and their backing context maps
(localsContextByRef/structPtrByRef/arrayByRef) were created once per
session and never pruned -- every getScopes() call (once per stop) and
every struct/array/pointer expansion added entries with nothing ever
removing them, growing unbounded over a long debug session. Per the
DAP spec a variablesReference is only valid until the next stop event
(VS Code always re-fetches rather than reusing a stale one), so
there's no reason to keep them past that point -- added
VariablesManager.reset() and call it from stackTraceRequest (called
once per stop), alongside the adapter's own existing analogous
frameIdToPc.clear().

events.title: Cap .puaeprofile decompressed size against a gzip bomb
events.message:
Cap .puaeprofile decompressed size against a gzip bomb

decodeCapture's gunzipSync had no output-size limit, even though a
.puaeprofile is loaded from disk and may not have been created by the
current user. gzip's compression ratio is effectively unbounded, so a
crafted few-KB file could expand to gigabytes before any of the
existing manifest/section bounds checks got a chance to run. Passes
maxOutputLength (generous relative to any real capture, which tops out
around a few MB) so an oversized payload throws cleanly instead --
already caught by profileEditorProvider.ts's existing try/catch around
loadProfile.

events.title: Fix cache-invalidation race on concurrent reads during a mutating RPC
events.message:
Fix cache-invalidation race on concurrent reads during a mutating RPC

Every mutating method (pause/run/step*/jump/setRegister/pokeCustom*)
invalidated the CPU-info/custom-register cache before sending its RPC,
but not after. A getCpuInfo()/getAllCustomRegisters() call already in
flight when a mutation starts can resolve after the pre-mutation
invalidation, repopulating the cache with pre-mutation data with
nothing left to invalidate it again -- serving stale register values
to every subsequent read until an unrelated mutation happens to race
favorably. Added a second invalidation in a `finally` once each
mutating RPC resolves.

events.title: Fix DWARF5 header parsing masking truncation, and two hang risks
events.message:
Fix DWARF5 header parsing masking truncation, and two hang risks

parseLineNumberProgram used `elfBuffer[offset++] || default` for
several DWARF5-only header fields (address_size, segment_selector_size,
maximum_operations_per_instruction, directory/file_entry_format_count).
`||` fires whenever the read is out-of-bounds too (elfBuffer[offset]
reads back `undefined` on a truncated buffer), silently substituting a
fabricated default and letting parsing continue past the real end of
the section with made-up header values -- inconsistent with the rest
of the function, which already throws on an out-of-bounds read for
minimumInstructionLength/lineRange/opcodeBase. Replaced with a
readU8-or-throw helper.

While in the same function: the DWARF2-4 directory/file-name loops
(`while (elfBuffer[offset] !== 0)`) had no bounds check in their own
condition -- once offset ran past a truncated buffer, elfBuffer[offset]
reads back `undefined` forever (never `0`) and readString on an
out-of-bounds offset returns a 0-length string rather than throwing,
so the loop would spin forever. Added an explicit offset < length
check.

Also added a depth cap to parseDIE's recursion: a corrupted abbreviation
table with no real null-DIE terminators could otherwise nest recursion
deep enough to hit a stack-overflow RangeError instead of a clean parse
error.

events.title: Fix silent data corruption and crash risks in debug-info parsers
events.message:
Fix silent data corruption and crash risks in debug-info parsers

- dwarfParser.ts readULEB128/readSLEB128: replace `|=`/`<<` (which
  coerce to 32-bit ints and wrap mod 32 once shift exceeds 31, i.e. a
  5+ byte encoding / values >= 2^28) with plain arithmetic, which stays
  exact up to JS's 2^53 safe-integer range. Previously any oversized
  length/offset field in a corrupted DWARF section silently produced a
  wrong (possibly negative) decoded value instead of erroring or
  decoding correctly.
- amigaHunkParser.ts BufferReader.readString: stop spreading a
  charCodes array into String.fromCharCode(...charCodes) -- `length`
  is an unbounded file-supplied field (HUNK_SYMBOL name length,
  HUNK_DEBUG LINE filename length), and a large enough one throws
  "RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded" instead of a clean
  parse error. Reads the string directly off the buffer instead.
- amigaHunkParser.ts parseHeader: the `tableSize < 0 || ... < 0`
  validation was dead code (readLong() is always unsigned); replaced
  with the real invariant (lastHunk < firstHunk), which previously
  produced a silently-empty hunk table instead of an error.
- amigaHunkParser.ts parseDebug (LINE format): validate the derived
  line-entry count is a non-negative even number before looping,
  instead of silently under-reading and desyncing the reader for every
  subsequent block in the hunk.

the request promise rejecting with no response ever sent, so Continue/
Pause appeared to just hang in the UI instead of surfacing an error.
Wired them to the already-defined but unused CONTINUE_ERROR/PAUSE_ERROR
codes.

Separately, every place that sets `this.stepping`/`this.isRunning` before
an awaited stepInto()/run() call left those flags stuck true if the call
rejected, since a failed step produces no "stopped" state message to
reset them via the normal handleStep()/handleStop() path. The next
unrelated stop (e.g. a real breakpoint hit while running) would then be
misrouted through handleStep() instead of handleStop(), silently
discarding the real stop reason. Reset the flags in a local catch before
rethrowing at each of the three call sites (stepInRequest,
doInstructionStepOver, and handleStep's line-granularity retry).

bridge: phase counter in status window + 300s hook-reply timeout (v1.16)

Diagnostics for the recurring Amiberry wedge and a fix for slow hooks.

  each dispatch point in the main Wait() loop (wait / transport / ipc /
  dbg_poll / timer / snoop_drain / chiplog / tail_poll / heartbeat /
  redraw). Renders as "Phase: <name> (<counter>)" at the bottom of the
  bridge's status window; window height bumped to 210 so the line is
  visible. When the daemon wedges next, a single screenshot names the
  section the main loop stalled in.
- I first tried writing the phase state to SYS:BridgeLogs/live.log every
  200ms via Open MODE_NEWFILE / Write / Close. Amiberry's DOS emulation
  wedged inside that pattern within seconds. This strongly suggests
  earlier "launcher-triggered" wedges are the same failure mode: high-
  frequency file operations on Amiberry's uaefs. File logging removed;
  the on-screen phase display is the surviving instrument.
- protocol_handler.c: bump the CALLHOOK reply wait from 150*Delay(5)
  (~15s) to 3000*Delay(5) (~300s). ipc_process() is still called each
  iteration so a hook's ab_log/ab_push_var can round-trip without
  deadlock. Long turns (a full ask to spark.hitorro.com) now complete
  cleanly instead of the daemon returning "Hook call timed out" mid-

events.title: hubert: new AmigaOS terminal with direct-LLM agent + tool calling
events.message:
hubert: new AmigaOS terminal with direct-LLM agent + tool calling

An interactive shell for AmigaOS that also acts as an agentic surface: it
opens its own TCP socket to an Ollama server (spark.hitorro.com by
default), streams a llama3.3 chat response, and executes tool calls
locally on the Amiga.

Shell foundation:
- RAW: console + line editor with history, cursor edit, home/end,
  Ctrl-U, Ctrl-W, Ctrl-C (cancel line).
- Tab completion for paths — single match completes, multi-match
  advances to the longest common prefix and lists candidates.
- Built-ins: cd / pwd / echo / clear / help / history / set / env /
  exit / ask / askreset.
- External commands via SystemTags with SYS_Output redirected to our
  RAW: console handle, so `dir`, `list`, `type`, etc. actually appear
  in the hubert window (otherwise child stdout inherits whatever the
  parent CLI had, usually NIL: when we were launched via `run`).
- Line redraw uses plain \r + text + space-pad + \b walk-back rather
  than ANSI CSI. AmiKit's RAW: doesn't honour \x1b[K reliably, which
  was leaving ghost chars from previous state on every keystroke.

Bridge integration:
- Registers as an amiga-bridge client (`hubert`) via ab_init.
- CWD mirrored as a CVAR.
- `run` hook accepts arbitrary command lines from the host, captures
  built-in output through ctx->out and external output through a
  T:hubert-hook.out temp file, returns "exit=<N>\n<output>" with
  newlines/pipes escaped so the bridge protocol's line splitter
  doesn't fragment the reply.
- ab_poll() is called every 20ms via WaitForChar polling, so idle-at-
  prompt still services host CALLHOOKs immediately.

Direct-LLM path (llm_direct.c + net.c + http.c + jsonx.c):
- net.c: bsdsocket.library wrapper with a host-side scriptable stub
  for tests. Works under Amiberry's bsdsocket_emu unchanged.
- http.c: minimal HTTP/1.1 POST + chunked-transfer-encoded response
  streamer, line-oriented so NDJSON frames come out cleanly regardless
  of chunk boundaries.
- jsonx.c: targeted value extraction (message.content, tool_calls[0].
  function.name/arguments, done) with escape handling. Not a general
  JSON parser — small enough to fit in the shell's memory budget.
- llm_direct.c: builds the /api/chat body, streams NDJSON, extracts
  tokens and tool calls via callbacks.

Agent loop (bi_ask):
- Static LlmMessages persists across ask calls; `askreset` clears it.
- Tools exposed to the model: run_command, read_file, write_file,
  list_dir, system_info. Dispatched locally with output formatted as
  the same "exit=<N>\n<data>" envelope so the model sees a uniform
  response shape.
- Up to LLM_MAX_STEPS tool-call iterations per ask.
- Default model is llama3.3 — nemotron 70B on the same server ignores
  the tool schema and simulates outputs instead of emitting tool_calls.

Tests: 112 host tests (72 core + 40 direct-LLM) exercise every pure
module against a scripted net stub. `make hosttest` runs them without
an emulator; `make` produces the m68k binary.

scripts/hubert-drive: host-side driver with `run` mode (via the bridge
run hook, captures output) and `type` mode (Amiga keymap-perfect
keystroke injection). --screenshot flag pulls an Amiga screenshot after
the command.

events.message:
devbench: profiles, remote emulator, deploy fallback, LLM proxy, reconnect fixes

Enable driving the setup from a Mac with a Raspberry Pi target running
AmiKit in Amiberry over TCP, and lay the plumbing for future direct-LLM
work on the Amiga side.

- Named profiles in devbench.toml (local-fsuae / real-amiga / pi-amikit)
  with active_profile + --profile + --mode CLI. Profile fields overlay
  on top of the flat [serial]/[emulator] sections.
- RemoteEmulatorController (config.py + remote_emulator.py) that starts
  / stops / restarts a remote Amiberry over SSH with a reboot fallback.
  MCP tools amiga_emulator_status/start/stop/restart wired in.
- Deployer.deploy_smart(): prefer the shared folder when it exists +
  writable, else stream via file_transfer over the bridge. force_bridge
  flag auto-set when the emulator lives on another host.
- SerialConnection: fix two reconnect races that left us permanently
  disconnected after a Pi reboot. (1) drain the stale _tcp_read_loop
  before opening a fresh socket so its finally-block can't clobber the
  new connected=True. (2) replace the self-cancelling
  _schedule_reconnect() inside _reconnect_loop with a while-loop that
  keeps retrying — one transient DNS blip or ECONNREFUSED used to be
  fatal.
- Bridge-health watchdog in server.py: if the AmigaOS-side bridge
  daemon goes silent for >90s (heartbeats stop even though the TCP
  socket looks up), SSH-restart the emulator; 240s cooldown so we don't
  cascade during boot.
- CALLHOOK API accepts timeout_ms (was hardcoded 5s, too short for
  agent turns and long DOS commands).
- LLM proxy skeleton (llm_proxy.py + tests) that streams Ollama chat
  responses to a bridge client and CALLHOOKs back TOKEN / TOOL / DONE
  events. Not needed at runtime now that hubert talks TCP directly,
  but the wire format + tests are useful.
- scripts/smoke-bridge.sh: transport-agnostic connectivity check.
- README: new Deployment Topologies section covering all three profiles.

events.title: fix(einstein): detect OCR font offset per MOS version; blank cells to backdrop
events.message:
fix(einstein): detect OCR font offset per MOS version; blank cells to backdrop

The font offset differs between MOS versions (1.2 @ 0x106D, 1.21 @ 0x107A). The
CDN-hosted ROM is 1.2, so the hardcoded 1.21 offset made the OCR match against
the wrong glyphs (punctuation especially). Detect the font offset at runtime
(findFontOffset scans for the blank space glyph + plausible letter/punctuation
pixel counts) and cache it per ROM.

Also: the TEXT overlay's cell-blanking filled matched cells with palette[0]
(black) when the cell background was colour 0 (transparent). On the TMS9918A a
transparent pixel shows the backdrop, so resolve colour-0 fg/bg to the backdrop
(R7 low nibble) — matched cells now blank to the real paper colour (e.g. blue).

events.title: Fix cross-platform path-key matching in source/profiler lookups
events.message:
Fix cross-platform path-key matching in source/profiler lookups

SourceMap, ProfilerCodeLensProvider, and ProfilerLineDecorationProvider
keyed file paths with the platform-native path.normalize(), which only
treats a host's own separator as a path separator. On a POSIX host that
left "C:\proj\a.c" and "c:/proj/A.C" as distinct keys instead of the
same file, breaking lookups whenever debug info carries Windows-style
paths (this project's toolchain runs via WSL from a Windows checkout)
on a non-Windows dev machine. Switched all three to path.win32.normalize,
which always treats both separators as equivalent regardless of
process.platform.

events.title: fix(einstein): don't alias I/O ports A6/A7 — XtalDOS 1.31 boots
events.message:
fix(einstein): don't alias I/O ports A6/A7 — XtalDOS 1.31 boots

The port decoder masked the address with & 0x3F, so 0x40-0xFF aliased onto the
0x00-0x3F device block (e.g. 0x48/0x49 -> the VDP at 0x08/0x09). XtalDOS 1.31
writes to 0x48/0x49, which corrupted the VDP mode register (R0 0x02 -> 0x60,
flipping Graphics II to Graphics I) and blanked the screen. Games don't touch
those ports, so they were unaffected.

The on-board devices decode at 0x00-0x3F with A6=A7=0; add a guard so ports with
A6/A7 set are unmapped. XtalDOS 1.31 (einstein-xbas.dsk) now boots to its ◇:
prompt in Graphics II; MOS and XtalDOS 1.11 still render correctly.

events.title: buggyboy: fix GRAPHICS.GRA decode — skip leading 0xd00 sprite table
events.message:
buggyboy: fix GRAPHICS.GRA decode — skip leading 0xd00 sprite table

The file opens with a 3328-byte (0xd00) raw sprite table before the RLE
stream; unpack_graphics @ 0x10620 pre-copies it (416 records x 8 B), then
decompresses the stream that follows. extract_graphics.py was decoding
from byte 0, emitting that table as ~3320 literal bytes ahead of the

events.title: Anchor flame-graph CPU columns to their real DMA slot
events.message:
Anchor flame-graph CPU columns to their real DMA slot

CPU boxes were positioned by cycle-cost fraction (timeOffset/duration),
while the DMA/blitter bands use the DMA grid's own slot index — two
independent clocks with different origins. The cycle-cost timeline only
starts counting from the first sampled (in-program) instruction of the
capture, silently dropping any real time spent in interrupts/OS calls
before that point, so CPU boxes drifted from where the DMA/blit bands
(correctly) place the same instant — most visibly at the first blit of
a frame.

Instead, match each sample's PC against the grid's own CPU instruction-
fetch cells (owner==CPU, DMA_CODE flag) to recover its true slot, walking
both streams in execution order. Falls back to the old cycle-fraction
estimate when there's no DMA data to anchor to.

events.title: feat(disk): SuperCard Pro (.scp) flux images with weak-sector fidelity
events.message:
feat(disk): SuperCard Pro (.scp) flux images with weak-sector fidelity

Add read-only .scp support for the +3/CPC (uPD765A) and Beta Disk / +D
(WD179x). SCP is a flux format one layer below HFE: a software data separator
(PLL) recovers MFM bit-cells from the raw flux timings, which are then fed to
the existing decodeHfeTrack decoder verbatim (cells → sectors).

The point of flux over HFE is copy-protection fidelity: all revolutions are
decoded and a sector whose data varies across revolutions is attached as a weak
DskSector.copies[] (which the uPD765A already picks from at random).

Track mapping derives the cylinder step as the gcd of gaps between present
tracks — a 3" 40-cyl disk is stored at even physical slots 0,2,..,84 with odd
slots absent — so cyl = (track - start) / step. Wired like .hfe: parseFloppyImage
content-detection (works at every mount site incl. ZIPs), the Beta/+D load and
restore paths, media-manager + mcp/loader dispatch, and the drive pickers.

Validated against the greaseweazle oracle: Dark-Side decodes 360/360 sectors
byte-identical to its .hfe; Amstrad-Bundle surfaces 3 genuine weak sectors the
single-revolution HFE cannot. Real protected +3 games (Dark Side, Double Dragon
II) boot to a bit-identical framebuffer from .scp vs .hfe.

WD1772 stays byte-identical). The WD1793 differs only in status bit 7
(NOT-READY vs MOTOR-ON), a 16-sector format, and exposed INTRQ/DRQ.

BetaDisk peripheral uses the Beta 128 auto-paging model: the 16KB TR-DOS ROM
maps in on an M1 fetch in 0x3D00-0x3DFF (while the 48K BASIC ROM is active)
and out at >= 0x4000. Ports 0x1F/0x3F/0x5F/0x7F/0xFF match Fuse beta.c, gated
on pagedIn so 0xFF never steals the keyboard. System register (0xFF): drive
b0-1, HLT b3, side b4 (inverted -- bit set = side 0), density b5, no reset bit.

New TRD and SCL parsers build the shared DskImage (geometry from the disk-info
sector; truncated images padded); HFE works via the existing decoder. Mutually
exclusive with the +D / Interface 1; reuses the C/D drive-state signals
(relabelled A:/B:), separate persistence keys and settings flag. MCP betadisk
tool + .trd/.scl loader dispatch. ROM hosted at trdos.rom.

events.title: feat(hfe): support creating a new blank HFE disk
events.message:
feat(hfe): support creating a new blank HFE disk

Add a from-scratch MFM track encoder so a brand-new blank disk can be
created as a track-level HFE image, not just a DSK. encodeHfeTrack lays
down the standard IBM System 34 double-density track (index mark, per
sector sync/A1/IDAM/CHRN+CRC/gap2/DAM/data/CRC/gap3) using the same clock
rule as the existing write-back path, so createBlankHfe/attachHfeBitstream
produce an image that decodes byte-identically to the DSK blank, saves as
.hfe, and round-trips writes through serializeHFE.

Wire it into the UI: the +3/CPC new-disk menu gains DSK/HFE submenus for
every format, and the +D drives gain a blank-800K-HFE option
(insertBlankPlusDDisk now takes an asHfe flag).

events.title: buggyboy: reconstruct + verify update_highscore (66/91, checkpoint)
events.message:
buggyboy: reconstruct + verify update_highscore (66/91, checkpoint)

Phase 3 of the input-oracle work (HARNESS.md) — and simpler than the plan. The tail
of the real function is the interactive name-entry loop (busy-polls the IKBD, Vsyncs,
waits on MZFLAG), which can't run to rts. Rather than model all that, the candidate
implements only the deterministic prefix and the oracle is stopped at the two prefix
exits — so no MZFLAG pin, no in-loop trap modeling, no input timeline.

- src/highscore.c (g_update_highscore): EGOFF; blank a leading-zero score digit
  ('0'->'/'); rank the new 6-digit score against the leg's 9-row table by a byte-wise
  compare; on a hit set results_mode/hiscore_pos/countdown, shift the rows below down
  one (overlapping copy, high-to-low, 12 of each 0xe-byte row), and insert the 12-byte
  score+name record. This populates highscore_table -> the results screen's SCORE/NAME
  rows. Decoded with capstone (m68k); the shift/insert pointer walk is exact.
- test/test_highscore.py: checkpoint at 0x12450 (made) / 0x123e6 (missed), chosen per a
  Python mirror of the ranking; edge cases (rank 0 / last / miss / leading-zero) + fuzz.

Phase 2 of the input-oracle work (HARNESS.md). Both now run (they call the verified
read_joystick) and are pure logic over the input globals, which the harness pokes as
inputs (the interrupt that sets them isn't run).

- src/input.c:

    keyboard scancode (space->0x80, up/left/right/down) into input_state, else keep

    different words.

    present and differs from the baseline (input_prev); else swap(Crawio(0xff)). No
    image effect, so the test compares the returned d0.

  = 0), shared so shim and check_abort agree.

events.message:
buggyboy: IKBD memory model + verify read_joystick (60/91)

Phase 1 of the input-oracle work (HARNESS.md). read_joystick busy-waits the IKBD
6850 ACIA's TDRE bit at $fffffc00 then sends the 0x16 joystick-interrogate command;
under the oracle it used to spin forever because reads above the 1 MiB image returned
0, so the bit was never set.

- oracle/shim.c: model IKBD_STATUS ($fffc00 on the 24-bit bus) as always TDRE-ready,
  so the wait loop terminates. The command write to IKBD_DATA lands above the image
  and is dropped by the existing bounds check (no capture needed — input state is
  scripted as an image global, see HARNESS.md), so read_joystick has no image effect.

events.title: feat(hfe): HFE write-back — save a mutated HFE back to HFE
events.message:
feat(hfe): HFE write-back — save a mutated HFE back to HFE

serializeHFE() re-encodes writes into a copy of the retained bitstream
rather than rebuilding tracks from scratch: decodeHfeTrack now records
each sector's data-field bit position (HfeBitstream.layout), and save
splices only the sectors whose data actually changed back into the
cells (payload + recomputed CRC, over the same cell span so gaps/marks
stay put). Unwritten fields — including protection tracks with odd
gaps, deleted marks or deliberately bad CRCs — are preserved verbatim;
an unwritten disk round-trips identically.

saveDisk / savePlusDDisk write .hfe (via serializeHFE) for HFE-sourced
disks and .dsk/.mgt otherwise. The FDC cores are untouched — writes go
through the existing writeBackSector into the decoded track, and
reconciliation into the bitstream happens only at save time, so the
uPD765A/WD1772 stay free of any HFE-format knowledge.

Verified on real disks: identity round-trip and full protection
preservation on Three-Inch-Loader and Alkatraz titles, with a written
sector reading back exactly. Not covered: formatting/creating a new HFE
(no prior layout) — a follow-up if wanted.

events.title: feat(hfe): native HFE disk support for +3 and CPC via the uPD765A
events.message:
feat(hfe): native HFE disk support for +3 and CPC via the uPD765A

Decode the HFE (HxC) raw MFM bit-cell stream directly the way hardware
does — A1 (0x4489) sync hunt, IDAM/DAM, CRC-16-CCITT, circular track —
into the existing sector-level DskTrack the FDC already consumes. The
HFE bitstream is retained as the disk's identity (new optional
DskImage.bitstream); no DSK file is produced and the DSK code path is
never involved. parseFloppyImage() content-detects HFE vs DSK, so .hfe
and .dsk both work at every uPD765A mount/restore site, incl. inside
ZIPs. Scope: HFE v1 (HXCPICFE), ISO/IBM MFM; v3 is rejected clearly.
The +D/WD1772 is intentionally left for a follow-up.

Decoder fidelity (validated byte-for-byte against hxcfe's own HFE->DSK
conversion of ~48 real greaseweazle dumps, incl. Speedlock/Alkatraz/
Three-Inch-Loader/CPC-format; HFE-vs-DSK boots are framebuffer-identical
on a real +3): reject bad-CRC IDAMs (kill false syncs), cap each data
field at the next sync (a bogus giant-N sector can't swallow the track),
accept 1-3 A1 preamble marks (worn disks emit 2).

Wired: emulator load/route/restore, media-manager, loadableExtensions,
DrivePane picker, drag hint, mcp/loader. New tests build an independent
MFM/HFE encoder from spec and cover the edge cases above.

buggyboy: run the reconstructed leg-results screen on a real 68000 (Hatari)

Cross-compile the same C cores to a GEMDOS .PRG and run them under Hatari with a
real TOS ROM; a headless run confirms the on-target framebuffer is byte-identical
to the host render (render_screen.py) — the reconstruction is correct compiled and
executed on an independent 68000, not just against the Musashi oracle.

absolute address baked into the binary, so they are position-independent where it
matters. The 1 MiB game image lives in BSS (no Malloc); mkprg.py builds the GEMDOS
reloc table from the ELF's R_68K_32 fixups (ld --emit-relocs).

events.title: recreate: add attribution (poison) pass to catch coincidental passes (#3)
events.message:
recreate: add attribution (poison) pass to catch coincidental passes (#3)

The plain diff proves final-image equivalence, so a candidate can pass by
coincidence: it never writes a byte the oracle wrote, but that byte already
held the oracle's value (an output landing in a zeroed/base region). Add an
opt-in attribution pass that removes the coincidence.

  - harness._attribution_check: re-run both cores on a copy of the input
    where every oracle-written byte is poisoned (its normal final value,
    inverted). A byte the candidate fails to write stays canary instead of
    matching, so the omission surfaces. Gated on differential(poison=True)
    and only after the plain pass is clean (safe for leaf functions;
    poisoning a control-steering output could perturb a complex run).
  - test_poison_catches_coincidental_write: a stub writing 0x00 over a
    zeroed byte with a do-nothing candidate passes the plain diff but is
    caught with poison=True (proves the guard fires).
  - Enable poison on the leaf tests whose outputs aren't pre-seeded:
    add_score edge cases (score_str HUD digits) and the screen fills
    (zeroed draw buffer). README notes the pass.

recreate: cross-validate Musashi against a real 68000 (ISA conformance, #5)

The differential suite proves each function matches Musashi; this certifies
Musashi itself against an independent, hardware-validated 68000 (Hatari's
WinUAE core), so "verified against Musashi" means "verified against a real
68000" for the instruction mix BuggyBoy uses.

  - oracle/isa_conformance.py: 277 self-contained, position-independent
    instruction snippets (inputs = immediates, flags captured with move sr
    immediately after the tested op, result saved via (a5)+). Runs the
    identical bytes on Musashi (emu.run) and real TOS (headless Hatari) and
    compares result + defined CCR bits. Classes: byte/word/long memory RMW
    (the class Unicorn mis-handled), asr/lsr/lsl/rox/ro, ext, movea.w,
    muls/mulu/divs/divu, add/sub/addx/subx, cmp.b+Scc, swap/neg.
  - tos_probe.py: extract run_tos_program() (reused by both harnesses).
  - test/test_isa_vs_tos.py: skips without Hatari/TOS; else asserts 277/277.

Result: all 277 match. The only core divergence found was N/Z after a
DIVS/DIVU overflow, which the 68000 PRM defines as *undefined* — so it is
excluded from the CCR comparison (result and the defined V flag still agree).

events.title: recreate: vet diff exclude bands against the oracle's stack extent (#6)
events.message:
recreate: vet diff exclude bands against the oracle's stack extent (#6)

An exclude band suspends the byte-for-byte guarantee for its range, so a
band that dropped a real (non-stack) divergence would pass silently. Vet
every band before use:

  - oracle (shim.c) now tracks the deepest stack pointer reached (min_a7),
    exposed via emu.run's out_regs.
  - _vet_exclude_bands (A) requires the band to extend past min_a7 — a band
    entirely below where A7 descended cannot be stack; (D) rejects a named
    global (names.txt) sitting *below* min_a7 — provably not stack.

Verifying it surfaced a real subtlety: _start relocates its stack across
trace_pc@0x1b040, so a naive "reject any named global" is wrong — a global
the stack sits *over* is legitimately reused as scratch. The check allows
named globals at/above min_a7 and only refuses ones below it. Empirically
the _start band's below-stack bytes are untouched, so it stays sound.

test_exclude_band_guards pins all three cases (A fires, D fires, reuse ok).

a signed cmp.b/bpl against '9' with a manual sub.b #10 (no BCD/decimal-

events.title: recreate: cross-check the OS trap model against real TOS (headless Hatari)
events.message:
recreate: cross-check the OS trap model against real TOS (headless Hatari)

Anchor the deterministic shim (shim.c + os.h) to a genuine TOS ROM so its
hand-modeled semantics are validated against real hardware, not just
asserted.

Harness:
  - oracle/tos_probe.py assembles a small GEMDOS program that runs Malloc,
    Getrez and a sequence of Freads, writes a fixed-layout record to a
    GEMDOS drive, and Pterm0s. It auto-runs headless under Hatari (SDL
    dummy video, --fast-forward) and reads the record back from the host
    dir — no debugger/breakpoint/load-address needed. Mshrink prologue so
    Malloc has a free pool.
  - test/test_os_vs_tos.py compares the capture to the shim: exact-value
    calls (Getrez low-res, Fread bytes + cursor/EOF counts) must match to
    the byte; Malloc's machine-dependent address is checked as the
    invariant the shim also honors (even-aligned, non-overlapping, odd
    size rounded up to even). Skips when Hatari or a TOS ROM is absent
    (the ROM isn't redistributable).

Docs:
  - README OS-trap section documents the two test layers.
  - docs/tos-os-calls.md adds the reusable headless-Hatari technique.

events.title: recreate: pin the OS trap model's semantics with shim-contract tests
events.message:
recreate: pin the OS trap model's semantics with shim-contract tests

The existing OS tests validate the reconstructed wrappers through the
differential harness but never stress the shim's own semantics at the
edges. Add five tests that drive tiny hand-assembled 68k stubs through
the oracle to pin shim.c + os.h directly:

  - Malloc bump-allocation + odd-size rounding to even
  - Fread cursor advance, partial read at EOF, zero past EOF
  - Fopen reopen rewinds the cursor
  - Fread on a closed handle is rejected (emu.run raises, not silently served)
  - Fopen of an unstaged file is rejected

A regression in these semantics now fails here instead of silently
inside a caller's differential test.

events.title: buggyboy-sound: add C64 SID transcode of the YM2149 stream
events.message:
buggyboy-sound: add C64 SID transcode of the YM2149 stream

Play BuggyBoy's tunes and effects on a Commodore 64 SID (reSID-fp /
pyresidfp) by transcoding the same per-frame YM register stream the
existing renderer captures. `sound_player.py --synth sid` writes
out/sound/*_sid.wav beside the YM references.

Mapping: YM square -> SID 50% pulse; YM noise -> SID noise, clocked from
the YM noise rate (SID clocks its LFSR from the voice frequency, so using
the stale tone period would silence noise FX); per-channel YM volume and
hardware envelope -> per-voice software amplitude scaling (SID has no
per-voice volume, and this stands in for YM's hardware-envelope "buzz").
Output is AC-coupled and faded in to mimic the real C64 and drop reSID's
reset transient. The envelope AM advances by the samples reSID actually
emits per frame, so it stays aligned to the audio with no drift.

Faithful port of the ST arrangement/timing in SID timbre; not a re-scored
native C64 tune.
