Nouvelle action du menu in-game (START) : une ligne par manette hôte détectée
(pastille d'activité pour identifier physiquement chaque stick), le FEU fait
tourner son rôle AUTO → PORT 1 → PORT 0 → OFF. AUTO = affectation historique

events.message:
fix(video): ancre du commit scanline = fenêtre Glue LIVE — Lethal Xcess (STX) en jeu réparé

Régression du commit au HBL (70f1533) : commitScanline/endVideoLine calaient
la scanline committée sur liveStartHBL_ (VDE_On STICKY, posé à 34 par TOUTE
bascule 60 Hz avant la ligne 63 — même une paire 60/50 qui n'ouvre PAS
réellement le haut, Hatari exigeant que le 60 Hz couvre la comparaison de fin
de ligne 33). La calibration du loader de Lethal Xcess émet une telle paire à
la ligne 32 de CHAQUE trame puis relit $FF8209 en fin de trame : le commit sur
l'ancre sticky avançait le compteur vidéo à travers les 29 lignes de bordure
haute (160 octets chacune, glueLineBytes ignorant la fenêtre VERTICALE) → le
poll lisait base+228 lignes au lieu de base+199 → le jeu croyait son overscan
ouvert → écran en jeu déchiré (HUD dupliqué, bandes décalées) puis chargements
en échec.

Fix : Shifter::commitAnchor() = max(liveStartHBL_, glueStartHBL_) sur trame à
écritures freq/res (la machine Glue LIVE fait foi), LATCHÉ au 1er commit de la
trame (une re-fermeture tardive ne ré-indexe pas lineSnap_/vcLineY_ — verrou
Cuddly conservé), reset à beginFrame, sérialisé → save-states v6. Un vrai

events.title: DeskTop: Support dragging files onto ProDOS applications
events.message:
DeskTop: Support dragging files onto ProDOS applications

ProDOS-8 supports a protocol for "interpreters", system files that can
be passed a file path to open. It is documented at
https://prodos8.com/docs/techref/writing-a-prodos-system-program/

Examples include TTS.SYSTEM (included in EXTRAS/, from
https://github.com/a2stuff/prodos-sam), EDIT.SYSTEM (from
https://github.com/bobbimanners/emailler), and FLOW.SYSTEM (from
https://github.com/a2-4am/flow).

Neither ProDOS-8 nor DeskTop have a general purpose file type
association mechanism like the GS/OS Finder or macOS. DeskTop only has
some hard-coded file type associations, like $D9 gets opened with
TTS.SYSTEM, and support for the BASIS.SYSTEM fallback interpreter. So
if those didn't know about your file types and interpreter, you were
out of luck.

Now, to open a specific file (e.g. READ.ME, a text file) with a
specific interpreter (e.g. EDIT.SYSTEM) you can now drag the file icon
onto the app icon. As long as the app is a SYS file with the ".SYSTEM"
suffix and it has the correct header bits, the app will be launched.

Resolves #903

Increment 5. Watchpoints via le conteneur Guards de Moira (debugger.watchpoints) :
Moira teste l'accès dans sa couche dataflow (peekM/pokeM) et appelle
NeostMoira::didReachWatchpoint → hit « break-after-access » (préemption après
l'instruction fautive). API Cpu68k : setWatchpoint/clearWatchpoint/clearAll/has/count/
byIndex + breakpointHitIsWatch() (distingue watchpoint vs breakpoint PC). Le skip-once

($8001.w → EA $FFFF8001) ne matcherait jamais un watchpoint sur $FF8001. Court-circuité
hors watchpoints (flags & CHECK_WP &&) → zéro impact normal.

Watchpoints (ajout/liste/retrait), la ligne EN PAUSE indique l'adresse accédée.

events.title: Fix CPU profiler hang/timeout on 68020/030 and fast-RAM captures
events.message:
Fix CPU profiler hang/timeout on 68020/030 and fast-RAM captures

Chases four compounding issues, most severe last: raw TypedArrays sent
over the webview<->extension postMessage bridge get flattened into slow
per-element array-likes (~800ms/MB), so getProfileData/getProfileRegs
now ship base64 strings instead; 68020/030's cycle-exact accounting lets
far more instructions retire per profiled frame than other CPU models
for the same program, so the profile/register buffer caps are now much
tighter; the render loop's wall-clock-based frame pacing could accrue an
unbounded "catch up" backlog after a long synchronous capture call, now
capped; and the emulator was resuming free-running immediately after
wasm_profile_start() returned, competing with the RPC queue throughout
the whole data-retrieval sequence — now the capture explicitly pauses
first and only resumes afterward if it was actually running before.

events.title: fix(resume): reliable refresh resume — sync snapshot save + correct +3 ROM
events.message:
fix(resume): reliable refresh resume — sync snapshot save + correct +3 ROM

Two bugs broke 'resume where you left off' on page refresh:

1. saveHMRState ran in a beforeunload handler but awaited an async
   CompressionStream deflate, so the localStorage write usually never
   completed before teardown — leaving a stale snapshot. Added a synchronous,
   uncompressed SZX writer (saveSZXSync) and made saveHMRState fully sync.

2. restoreHMRState restored the +2A/+3 ROM page with the plain-128K formula
   ((7FFD>>4)&1), ignoring the high ROM bit in 1FFD bit 2. A +3 game using
   ROM 3 resumed into ROM 1, freezing its ROM-dependent interrupt routine
   (silent music, frozen colour/border effects) while input still worked.
   Centralised the bank/ROM restore in a shared applySZXPaging() used by both
   the resume path and the file-load path so they can't drift again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat(debug): step into the interrupt handler when the CPU is halted
events.message:
feat(debug): step into the interrupt handler when the CPU is halted

Single-stepping called cpu.step() directly, which never asserts the maskable
interrupt (that only fires at the frame boundary in runFrame). On a HALT the
step just refetched the NOP forever — only R advanced — so the interrupt
service routine was unreachable from the debugger. stepInto/stepOver now
synthesise the frame interrupt when the CPU is halted with interrupts enabled,
landing PC on the first ISR instruction. DI HALTs (waiting on NMI) still spin.

cleared on insert, eject, and save. The flag flows through the per-frame

there are changes worth downloading (in-session writes aren't persisted

events.title: a4091: emulate 53C710 SCSI loopback pins
events.message:
a4091: emulate 53C710 SCSI loopback pins

The ncr7xx SCSI pin test drives the output latches and reads them back through the bus input registers in loopback mode. Model the A4091 loopback path for SBDL, SBCL, and SSTAT1, and add the missing SOCL write latch.

SCNTL1.ADB now latches instead of aborting the setup write, allowing the loopback reads to observe the driven SODL and SOCL state.
events.author: codewiz

events.title: lsi53c710: reject illegal group-3 SCRIPTS opcodes
events.message:
lsi53c710: reject illegal group-3 SCRIPTS opcodes

The 53C710 only supports Memory Move in SCRIPTS group 3. Opcodes with reserved bits set, including the 53C810+ Load/Store-register forms, should raise DSTAT.IID instead of being executed.

This prevents garbage fetched from non-responding addresses from causing stray DMA or register accesses during the ncr7xx bus access test.

events.title: Replace deprecated noweb toolchain with self-contained weave.py
events.message:
Replace deprecated noweb toolchain with self-contained weave.py

Recent TeX Live releases no longer ship the noweb LaTeX package, and the
noweave/notangle command-line tools are effectively deprecated. Convert the
build to a self-contained Python weaver/tangler plus a vendored noweb.sty,
mirroring the approach used by ali_baba_reveng.

- Add weave.py: a standalone noweb weaver + tangler (stdlib only). It weaves
  main.nw into main.tex using the noweb macros, and tangles the <<*>> root

events.title: Fix Multiface crash on Return after a second NMI press
events.message:
Fix Multiface crash on Return after a second NMI press

pressButton() called cpu.nmi() unconditionally, but a real Z80 NMI is
non-maskable — it fires even while the CPU is mid-ROM. Pressing the
button again before "Return" pushed a second return address onto the
game's stack and clobbered IFF2 (nmi() sets iff2 = iff1, and iff1 was
already false from the first NMI). The MF ROM's "Return" only unwinds
one level, so the leftover stack entry got popped and jumped to later
— after the ROM had already paged itself back out — running whatever
happened to be at that address in the game's own memory.

pressButton() is now a no-op while already pagedIn. Real hardware has
no legitimate use for a second press before the first session ends.

events.title: Fix Multiface hang: pageOut must not disarm the interface mid-session
events.message:
Fix Multiface hang: pageOut must not disarm the interface mid-session

f399b80 made MF128/MF3 ports invisible until the NMI button arms them,
but also cleared the armed latch on every pageOut(). Real Multiface
ROMs page out and back in many times per session as part of normal
operation (e.g. the MF3 menu borrows the underlying ROM's
HALT/keyboard-scan idle loop by paging out, then must page itself back
in once a key is pressed). With the latch cleared on that first
internal page-out, the follow-up page-in was silently ignored and the
machine hung — reproduced live: pressing NMI on a +3 reached the menu,
but the ROM's own idle-loop page-out immediately disarmed it, ,so it
could never page back in to handle the keypress.

armed now only clears on reset(), matching what the original finding
actually required (invisible before the button is ever pressed) without
assuming an incorrect auto-disarm-on-return semantic.

events.title: Fix tape playback "correcting" the trailing checksum byte
events.message:
Fix tape playback "correcting" the trailing checksum byte

buildRawData always recomputed the XOR checksum from flag+payload,
even though the parser had the genuine on-tape byte available and
discarded it. This silently "fixed" deliberately-bad checksums — a
common protection technique on Spectrum tapes, not just CPC/CDT
(whose data blocks carry their own CRCs and already had this handled
via an opt-in rawDataBlocks flag).

parseTAP and parseTZX (standard/turbo blocks) now always attach the
verbatim on-tape bytes via DataBlock.rawBytes, which playback already
preferred over buildRawData when present. Since Spectrum tapes now get
the same treatment as CPC/CDT, the rawDataBlocks option is no longer
meaningful and is removed along with its call sites.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix .z80 snapshots dropping AY state and ignoring +3 port 0x1FFD
events.message:
Fix .z80 snapshots dropping AY state and ignoring +3 port 0x1FFD

The saver wrote 0 for both the AY selected-register byte and the 16
AY register-content bytes (mislabeled "reserved"), so any .z80 saved
from a 128K/+2/+2A/+3 machine always came back with AY registers
reset — 128K .z80s loaded with garbled music. Neither side handled
the 55-byte v3 extended header's port 0x1FFD byte at all, so +3
snapshots taken in an all-RAM CP/M configuration reloaded with ROM
paging instead and crashed immediately.

loadZ80 now reads the AY selected register + 16 register bytes
(byte 38, bytes 39-54) and, for +2A/+3-class memory, the 1FFD byte
(byte 86, only present in the 55-byte header) — applying specialPaging
and the correct 4-ROM-page select the same way the existing SZX flow
already does. saveZ80 takes optional ayRegs/ayCurrentReg parameters
(mirroring saveSZX) and writes a 55-byte header with hwMode=7 when the
memory is +2A/+3-class, adding the 1FFD byte; 128K/+2 keeps the
54-byte header unchanged. media-manager.ts's .z80 branch now restores
AY state after load, mirroring its existing SZX branch.

events.title: Fix four uPD765A FDC spec deviations
events.message:
Fix four uPD765A FDC spec deviations

- Overrun (ST1.OR) now correctly sets ST0 IC=01 (abnormal termination).
  It previously left ST0 as normal completion, even though the CPU
  genuinely failed to service the data register in time.

- Multi-track (MT) reads restart the sector count at literal sector 1
  on the new side after a head switch, not the command's original
  starting R — the two only coincided by accident on disks that start
  numbering at 1. Removes the now-unused exStartR field.

- SK (Skip) is now honoured on Read Data/Read Deleted Data: a sector
  whose address-mark type doesn't match the command is skipped
  entirely (not transferred, not a termination point) and the search
  continues to the next sector, instead of always behaving as SK=0
  (read the mismatched sector and terminate after it).

- Duplicate sector IDs (deliberate on copy-protected tracks) now
  resolve to the first physical occurrence instead of the last —
  matching real hardware, where the FDC stops at whichever copy the
  head reaches first during rotation and can't see ahead to a later
  duplicate.

events.title: Fix AMX mouse firing PIO interrupts with interrupts never enabled
events.message:
Fix AMX mouse firing PIO interrupts with interrupts never enabled

pioControlWrite parsed the interrupt-control word's mask-follow bit
(D4) but never looked at D7, the actual Interrupt Enable flip-flop.
A real Z80 PIO powers up with interrupts disabled; here moving the
mouse under any IM2 program vectored through the interrupt table
regardless, crashing programs that never armed interrupts (or armed
with an uninitialised/still-zero vector table entry).

Tracks per-port intEnabledA/intEnabledB (set from D7 of the interrupt
control word, cleared on reset) and gates interruptWithVector on it in
drainMovement. Direction latches (dirX/dirY) still update every step
regardless — those reflect direct hardware lines, not the interrupt
path — so polled-mode software is unaffected.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix Multiface 128/3 paging ports being live before the button is pressed
events.message:
Fix Multiface 128/3 paging ports being live before the button is pressed

MF128/MF3 decoded their page-in/page-out ports (0xBF/0x3F) and the
0x7F3F/0x1F3F latch readback unconditionally. Real MF128/MF3 hardware
gates those ports behind a latch armed only by the button's NMI, so
they stay invisible until invoked — otherwise any stray IN on those
(very common) port numbers during normal gameplay pages the MF ROM in
mid-game. MF1's narrower bit-mask decode has no such latch on real
hardware and is unaffected.

Adds a `armed` flag to Multiface: set by pressButton, cleared on
page-out (and reset), and consulted by the MF128/MF3 port checks in
io-ports.ts.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix +2A/+3 wrongly exposing the Ferranti floating bus
events.message:
Fix +2A/+3 wrongly exposing the Ferranti floating bus

Unattached I/O ports fell through to Contention.floatingBusRead
unconditionally, returning live VRAM bytes on every model. Real
hardware only floats the bus this way on the Ferranti ULA (48K/16K/
128K/+2); the Amstrad gate array (+2A/+3) drives unattached ports to
0xFF instead, which is why Arkanoid hangs on a real +3.

Adds a hasFloatingBus flag to MachineVariant (true for Ferranti
variants, false for Amstrad) and gates the floating-bus read in
io-ports.ts on it.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix redundant DD/FD prefix chains costing 8T, double-bumping R, and being interruptible
events.message:
Fix redundant DD/FD prefix chains costing 8T, double-bumping R, and being interruptible

A repeated prefix byte (e.g. DD DD 23) rewound PC and returned to
step(), letting the frame loop re-fetch that byte as a fresh top-level
instruction. That double-counted the byte's M1 cycle (8T instead of
4T), incremented R twice for one fetch, and — because control returned
to the frame loop between prefix bytes — let a pending interrupt be
accepted mid-chain, which real Z80 blocks for the whole prefix stream.

Fix: continue the chain in place by calling into executeDD/executeFD
directly instead of returning, so a run of prefixes resolves within a
single step() call, matching hardware.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix AY noise LFSR running at twice the hardware rate
events.message:
Fix AY noise LFSR running at twice the hardware rate

The noise generator shared the same /8 master-clock tick as the tone
and envelope generators, so it shifted every 8*NP master cycles.
Real AY-3-8910/YM2149 hardware has an extra /2 prescaler ahead of the
noise counter, shifting every 16*NP cycles. All noise-based sound was
an octave too bright.
events.author: damieng

events.title: Make MCP parseAddr reject invalid addresses instead of returning NaN
events.message:
Make MCP parseAddr reject invalid addresses instead of returning NaN

parseInt on a typo'd symbol name or non-hex garbage returned NaN, and
NaN & 0xFFFF is 0 — so write_memory silently wrote to address 0x0000,
read_memory dumped 0x0000, set_register set PC=0 and echoed "PC = NaN",
and breakpoints were registered at addresses that could never hit.

parseAddr now validates the hex digits (for plain, 0x- and $-prefixed
forms alike) and throws a descriptive error, which the MCP SDK returns
to the client as a proper tool error. Symbol resolution and the
identifier-shaped-hex fallback (`face`) are unchanged.

events.title: Fix swapped Kempston mouse left/right buttons
events.message:
Fix swapped Kempston mouse left/right buttons

The Spectrum button map put DOM left on bit 0 and right on bit 1, but
the Kempston mouse button port 0xFADF is D0 = right, D1 = left,
D2 = middle (active low) — confirmed against FUSE (ui_mouse_button maps
left to bit 1 and right to bit 0) and the WoS hardware ports reference.
Every left/right click in Kempston-mouse software was inverted. The
previous mapping (and its test) came from a since-vanished reference
page that had the two bits backwards.

The CPC's explicit map already had the correct layout, so only its
"swaps vs the Spectrum" comments needed correcting.

events.title: Fix crash chaining consecutive TZX Direct Recording blocks
events.message:
Fix crash chaining consecutive TZX Direct Recording blocks

When a Direct Recording block ended with pause=0, advanceDirect()
called beginBlock() for the next block and then unconditionally nulled
directData. If the next block was also a Direct Recording block (the
normal way long sampled recordings are split), beginDirectBlock() had
just installed its data — the null clobbered it and the next advance()
threw "Cannot read properties of null" at the block boundary.

Clear directData before the hand-over instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: Fix FDC format flag surviving an aborted FORMAT_TRACK
events.message:
Fix FDC format flag surviving an aborted FORMAT_TRACK

exFormatting was only cleared by finishFormat(), so a FORMAT_TRACK
terminated early — by the MSR overrun path or by a machine reset —
left the flag stuck. The next ordinary WRITE_DATA completion was then
misrouted into finishFormat(), which reinterpreted the written sector
bytes as C/H/R/N ID tuples and rebuilt (destroyed) the current track
in the disk image.

Clear the flag in finishExecution(), the choke point every execution-
phase termination passes through, and in reset(), which bypasses it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: qt: let Cmd+Q close the launcher on macOS
events.message:
qt: let Cmd+Q close the launcher on macOS

The launcher runs as a modal QDialog::exec() with no application event
loop and no menu bar. Escape works because QDialog maps it to reject()
internally, but macOS disables the auto-generated application menu (and
its Cmd+Q) while a modal session is active, so Cmd+Q was swallowed by
the OS and never closed the dialog. Bind QKeySequence::Quit directly on
the dialog so it is handled inside the modal loop, mirroring Escape.

events.title: cmake: own the qemu-uae plugin provisioning
events.message:
cmake: own the qemu-uae plugin provisioning

The mandatory qemu-uae.so plugin was only buildable from a sibling
qemu-uae source tree; distro builds without one configured fine, built
fine, and then failed at install time when the install rule referenced
the never-built plugin (GitHub issue #6). Both CI workflows carried
their own duplicated checkout/build/strip plumbing for the
uae-ppc-plugin builder instead.

Resolve the plugin at configure time, in order: prebuilt
WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_PLUGIN_FILE, the sibling qemu-uae source tree, an
uae-ppc-plugin builder checkout (WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_BUILDER_DIR, default
sibling; WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_QEMU_TARBALL feeds it a local QEMU tarball for
offline distribution builds), or a build-time clone of the builder
(WINUAE_QEMU_UAE_BUILDER_FETCH, default ON). When nothing applies the
configure fails with the list of options. On Linux the plugin target is
part of the default build so plain build+install flows always bundle
the plugin.

Drive the builder through an OUTPUT-based custom command so repeated
`all` builds and CPack preinstall do not rerun the external builder once
qemu-uae.so is already present.

The Ubuntu and macOS workflows drop their manual plugin build steps and
pass the builder checkout to CMake; stripping moved into the builder
wrapper script.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: add Scale2x GLSL scaler to the shader pipeline
events.message:
od-unix: add Scale2x GLSL scaler to the shader pipeline

The Filter page's filter selector only offered "None" (GitHub issue
#4): the generic gfx_filter config option cannot carry named shaders
outside the Windows Direct3D path, and the Unix GL presenter had no
scaler stage.

Carry the selection as a new unix.gfx_shader target option (parsed and
saved in od-unix/config.cpp, no generic code changes) and implement
Scale2x/EPX as a stage in the GL presenter's fragment shader, selected
through a uniform. The scaler forces nearest-neighbour sampling, runs
before the color/scanline/noise stages, and applies to the emulation
frame only, leaving the status line untouched. The launcher's Filter
selector offers Scale2x when the shader pipeline is available, and the
value round-trips through the config (covered by the roundtrip smoke).
events.author: reinauer

events.title: Fix snapshot load applying to a destroyed machine after model auto-switch
events.message:
Fix snapshot load applying to a destroyed machine after model auto-switch

ensure128kROM() destroys the current machine and creates a new one, but
applySnapshot kept using its captured spectrum parameter afterwards:
stop/reset/load/start all hit the destroyed instance, and start() fully
resurrected it — two frame loops, two AudioContexts, and two renderers
fighting over the same canvas whenever a 128K snapshot was dropped on a
48K machine.

ensure128kROM now returns the machine in service ({spectrum, model}) or
null, and applySnapshot re-binds to it before touching anything. The
refreshed model also fixes the SZX path applying 128K-style paging when
the upgrade actually produced a +2A/+3 (port 1FFD ROM bits were dropped).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: od-unix: mirror Windows GUI option gating in Qt launcher
events.message:
od-unix: mirror Windows GUI option gating in Qt launcher

Bring the Qt launcher's control enablement to parity with the Windows
GUI's enable_for_*dlg/values_from_cpudlg logic, with the constraining
option always acting as master:

- Gate Z3 Fast, Z3 Chip, processor slot RAM and Z3 mapping mode by the
  24-bit addressing checkbox (enable_for_memorydlg). Previously a 68000
  could be combined with Z3 RAM and the config booted with it.
- Stop force-unchecking 24-bit addressing when a Z3 RTG board is
  selected, and stop writing cpu_24bit_addressing=false into the config
  whenever a Z3 RTG board is present.
- Apply CPU selection side effects: 68000/68010 force 24-bit addressing
  on, 68030+ force it off; FPU selection is remapped on user-driven CPU
  changes (external to internal at 68040+, internal to 68881 below,
  None on 68000/68010 with More compatible or memory cycle-exact).
- Enable FPU radios per Windows rules; block JIT while an MMU is
  selected; disable More compatible under memory cycle-exact; disable
  the CPU speed slider under full cycle-exact; gate the CPU frequency
  controls.
- Chipset page: clear and disable Wait for Blitter under Immediate
  Blitter or memory cycle-exact with 68000/68010; force NKRO on for UAE
  and A2000-8039 keyboard modes; disable the DMA/memory cycle-exact
  checkbox below 68020.
- Advanced chipset page: disable all manual controls while Compatible
  Settings is checked (enable_for_chipsetdlg2); 1M chip jumper also
  requires 512 KB chip RAM.
- Display page: disable resolution and line-mode controls while
  autoresolution is active, keep interlaced modes tied to the line-mode
  split, gate VGA autoswitch by hires or better with line doubling, and
  disable frame skipping under memory cycle-exact.
- Re-run all gating after loading a configuration file.

The sound page and accelerator board controls already follow the same
Windows gating rules, so leave them unchanged.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: Fix EI interrupt shadow: run one instruction after EI before accepting INT
events.message:
Fix EI interrupt shadow: run one instruction after EI before accepting INT

The frame loop cleared cpu.eiDelay unconditionally after every step,
including the step that executed EI itself, so a pending frame INT was
accepted between EI and the following instruction. Real Z80 defers
acceptance by exactly one instruction: EI:DI is atomic and EI:HALT can
never take the INT in between (an ISR ending EI:RETI would otherwise be
re-entered before RETI, leaking 2 stack bytes per frame).

Capture eiDelay before step() and clear it only if it was already set,
matching the pattern cpc-machine.ts already used.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: a2065: drop frames that cannot fit receive ring
events.message:
a2065: drop frames that cannot fit receive ring

The receive queue can stall forever if the packet at its head is larger
than the current descriptor ring can accept. Check the full frame size,
including padding and FCS bytes, before trying to drain the queue.

Drop packets that can never fit and reject packets that would overflow
the temporary frame buffer when the emulated FCS is appended.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: slirp: harden restart and DNS handling
events.message:
slirp: harden restart and DNS handling

Reset transient SLIRP state when the backend is restarted, and make
DHCP DNS advertisement depend on an available resolver.

Keep host loopback resolvers unchanged instead of rewriting them to the
virtual host address. The guest still talks to the SLIRP DNS proxy, but
the proxy must query the resolver configured on the host.

This keeps the emulated network usable after reconfiguration and avoids
advertising a DNS forwarder that cannot answer.

things around to make stuff happy again.

Comment the endgame chain; settle the Competence Rating formula

Competence Rating (RatingScore, ex-'EndgameFlag') decoded exactly:
  crew term  = sum of 2 x strength over live human crew (no Android)

alien killed = crew+rooms+oxygen; escape/crew-lost/oxygen-out with
destruct armed = crew+oxygen; ship exploded = oxygen only; alien

events.title: Decode the 238 encounter marker: press-time RmveGrille->ATTACK swap
events.message:
Decode the 238 encounter marker: press-time RmveGrille->ATTACK swap

The stub cluster at $B2B9-$B31D is the hostile-in-room menu logic,
run by RoomModeDispatch before EVERY mode-0/1 action dispatch:

- ForceAttackRowIfHostile ($B2C0): in the room view, when the alien
  (slot 0) — or, once AlienActiveFlag is $FF, the alien-target/Android
  slot — is in the viewed actor's room, the special row (cell 13) is
  forced to 52 'ATTACK' and redrawn. If the press landed on 49
  'RmveGrille', the mirror byte is set to 238: the swap happened under
  the cursor within the same key release.
- SpecialRowAction ($B306): 238 -> restore 52 but still start the
  timed grille removal — the player's original intent is honoured;
  only the next press (row visibly ATTACK) runs StartAttack ($9275,
  action state 4, countdown 40, replaces any pending job).
- Also: row 8 (front-hand item) presses cancel the pending countdown
  ((IX+0)=0 never fires — ResetCrewTimers only dispatches on 1->0).

Verified end-to-end in the skoolkit simulator (scripted Short Game,
alien poked into Ripley's room: mirror 49->238->52, cell13->52,
state 3 timer 180; second press -> state 4 timer 40).

Also named from the same investigation: SetActionTimer's formula and
its tables (GrilleTimeBySlot $83EA, ActionTimeByStrength $83F2,
ActionTimeBySlot $83FA — 6 bytes only, slots 6-7 read into
TileTableBounds), JonesCatchBySlot $83E2, RefreshSpecialRow $B0B8,
and the InputScannerTable $A405 (was 'glyph codes?'): OptionsScreen
patches the scanner CALL operand at $874D per input device.

events.title: Fix Exomizer v3 unpacking to match unp64 output
events.message:
Fix Exomizer v3 unpacking to match unp64 output

Implements a heuristic for Exomizer v3 compressed files to match unp64
behavior. When unp64 analyzes Exomizer v3 files, it statically scans
backwards from the end of the packed data for a 'CLI; JMP' sequence
to extract the entry point and trims the start address to D (skipping
the BASIC stub). This commit introduces the same heuristic to finish_unpack
so that regenerator2000's output range and entry point perfectly match
unp64's analysis for these files.
events.author: ricardoquesada

- Add redirect mechanism in Phase 2 loop to handle multiple BASIC SYS redirects for 2-pass depackers.
- Cascade range detection to higher boundaries if written+diffed bytes exist above the current boundary.
- Skip trailing cluster trimming during range detection when dealing with disjoint regions from in-place depackers.
- Fix traveler.tiny_crunch test assertions and add a debug test.

events.title: fix(cpu): improve STOP handling for 68000 by continuously comparing IPL/mask during STOP state
events.message:
fix(cpu): improve STOP handling for 68000 by continuously comparing IPL/mask during STOP state

The 68000 now re-arms CHECK_IRQ during the STOP state if the IPL exceeds the mask, ensuring that IRQs raised before the STOP are properly handled. This change addresses a timing issue where the CPU would remain inactive until the next pin change, leading to delayed IRQ delivery. The fix has been validated against benchmarks from Super Hang-On, confirming accurate IRQ handling during STOP conditions.

events.message:
fix(video): datations lecture/écriture du compteur vidéo ramenées ENSEMBLE aux valeurs fidèles (menu Cuddly verrouillé 100 %)

Le menu robot de The Cuddly Demos clignotait verticalement (bistable,
~10-47 % de trames ratées : fenêtre 34..310 ↔ 63..263, briques en
escalier). Chaîne causale MESURÉE à l'oracle (traces video_addr +
cpu_disasm/cpu_video_cycles alignées par landmarks f02e/f200/f264) :

- le synchroniseur de la démo (pc=f264) émet une paire 60/50 Hz par ligne
  et sort quand l'octet bas de $8209 dépasse $40 (comparaison SIGNÉE) ;
- chemin CPU inter-trame et ancre VBL = Hatari EXACTEMENT (f200 à +16548
  du handler VBL des deux côtés — la convergence instruction tient) ;
- mais la VALEUR lue était 4-6 octets plus petite au même instant : la
  sortie glissait de L34 (Hatari, marge +6..10) à L36 → paire suivante
  une ligne trop tard → retrait bordure haute raté → le clignotement.

Cause : kVideoCounterReadOffsetCyc=-14 et kSyncWriteOffsetCyc=-6
intégraient une « origine d'horloge trame −8 » co-calibrée le 2026-07-02
AVANT le fix du double comptage STOP — un artefact. Les deux datations
reviennent ENSEMBLE (+8) aux valeurs fidèles théoriques de la table §8 du
doc de convergence : read = fin d'accès −8 = **−6**, write = fin d'accès
Moira = **+2**. (A/B : NEOST_VC_OFF=-8 NEOST_SYNC_OFF=-8 = ancien.)

Bonus (gated NEOST_LINELEN, défaut OFF) : videoCounter() mappe la lecture
sur la grille RÉELLE des débuts de ligne (glueLineStart_), port de
Video_ConvertPosition/Video_CalculateAddress sur nCyclesPerLine réel.

Validé (défauts, sans env) : Cuddly menu 250/250 trames verrouillées
(225/250 avant, mur régulier = Hatari) ; EL loader + top-trick 40/40 ;
LX titre propre ; SHO byte-identique ; étalons 19/19 + TOUS OK.

events.title: fix(blitter): le restart BUSY avec y_count résiduel 0 ne relance plus 65536 lignes
events.message:
fix(blitter): le restart BUSY avec y_count résiduel 0 ne relance plus 65536 lignes

Bureau TOS 1.06 STE scramblé au moindre redraw (drag d'icône, fenêtres —
rapport GUI sur Beyond the Ice Palace, reproduit headless --walk-mouse) :
le driver blitter du TOS re-pose BUSY après chaque blit (protocole
restart) ; NeoST relisait alors y_count=0 comme 65536 (règle valable à
l'ÉCRITURE seulement) et relançait un blit de 65536 lignes qui labourait
toute la RAM.

Port fidèle Hatari :
- yLatch_ = compteur Y VIVANT, conversion 0→65536 À L'ÉCRITURE du
  registre $FF8A38 (Blitter_LinesPerBitblock_WriteWord, blitter.c:1356) ;
- start() avec résiduel 0 (transfert déjà fini) → BUSY et HOG effacés,
  aucun blit (Blitter_Control_WriteByte, blitter.c:1433-1437) ;
- runSlice consomme/repose le latch (readback 16 bits inchangé).

Un blit légal de 65536 lignes (écrire 0 PUIS démarrer) reste exact (B1).
Validé : bureau propre après clic-glissé (tos106fr STE 1m), étalons
19/19 + TOUS OK.

events.title: fix(cpu): les exceptions Moira ne fuient plus hors de l'émulateur (crash BIP)
events.message:
fix(cpu): les exceptions Moira ne fuient plus hors de l'émulateur (crash BIP)

Beyond the Ice Palace plantait au lancement depuis le bureau TOS
(terminate : moira::AddressError non rattrapée). Cause : trois chemins
de Moira::execute() appelaient exec* SANS la garde processException —
TRACE (l.281), PRIVILEGE depuis STOP (l.319) et le mode LOOPING — et un
vecteur d'exception IMPAIR y fait jeter AddressError depuis jumpToVector.
Sur un vrai 68000 c'est une ADDRESS ERROR (groupe 3) à prendre, pas un
abort de l'émulateur.

Corrigé aussi dans processException :
- « throw df » lançait un POINTEUR que catch(DoubleFault&) ne rattrape
  pas → double faute désormais HALT direct ;
- AddressError/BusError PENDANT le traitement d'une exception groupe 0
  (vecteur bus error impair, pile en zone bus-error) = double faute →
  HALT fidèle, plus de fuite.

Banc de régression : tools/make_trace_odd_test.py (vecteur TRACE impair
+ bit T → écran vert si l'address error est prise, crash avant le fix),
enregistré comme étalon « trace_odd ». Étalons : TOUS OK. Lancement BIP
validé headless via DESKTOP.INF #Z (Pexec sous AES, intro + parchemins
propres).

events.title: fix(cpu): double-prise HBL du pré-armement — remplacé par le commit au dispatch
events.message:
fix(cpu): double-prise HBL du pré-armement — remplacé par le commit au dispatch

RÉGRESSION Super Hang-On (course injouable, rapportée en GUI) : le pré-armement
de broche (efe485e, défaut HBL ON) créait une DOUBLE-PRISE — la broche montait
mi-instruction via sync(), l'exception partait DANS le bloc, l'IACK effaçait le
pending, puis le callback du dispatch RE-levait la broche → 2ᵉ HBL. Mesuré au
banc poll-entry : exceptions en période LIBRE ~427 cyc (6 par 5 lignes) au lieu
d'une par ligne — fatal aux rasters de course de SHO.

Le modèle FIDÈLE, mesuré à l'oracle Hatari instrumenté ([HPIN]/[HEXC] dans
notre clone) : Hatari CE ne lève PAS la broche mi-instruction pour les INT
vidéo — CycInt est traité À LA FRONTIÈRE d'instruction et intlev_load →
ipl_fetch_now commit l'IPL SANS délai → l'exception démarre AU MÊME CYCLE que
le changement de broche (exc−pin = 0 sur 12709/12711 échantillons).

- NEOST_PIN_ARM → défaut 0 (pré-armement retiré, gardé opt-in expérimental) ;
- raiseHbl/raiseVbl → commit immédiat A/B-able NEOST_RAISE_COMMIT (bit0 HBL,
  bit1 VBL), DÉFAUT 1 = HBL seul : le commit VBL casse le loader d'Enchanted
  Land (couplage VBL↔IKBD/FDC, même signature que le pré-arm VBL — à creuser).

RÉSULTATS : cadence d'exception NeoST = Hatari EXACT ({508,512,520} @ 2:2:1,
séquence par-5-lignes {x+8,x+4,x+4,x,x} identique, E-clock {2,4} identique) ;
**flicker EL 40/40 (top-trick parfait, une première)** ; moteur EL verrouillé
aux positions Hatari-exactes 376/384 ; étalons 19/0 + TOUS OK ; LX 0,00 % ;
SHO attract atteint la grille de course proprement.

events.title: Initial commit: byte-exact Smuggler's Cove disassembly
events.message:
Initial commit: byte-exact Smuggler's Cove disassembly

Complete, recompilable disassembly of the ZX Spectrum 48K text adventure
Smuggler's Cove (Quicksilva, 1983 - John R. Keneally).

- All engine code carved into per-routine files, named and documented;
  all data decoded (objects, vocab, messages, command DB, pictures).
- Self-contained build (no original game files required); verified
  byte-exact via md5 (f6f5ffc1d306b0a5ab949463df4d553f).
- Provably relocatable (org-shift test: all references symbolic).
- Validated against real gameplay via an RZX replay trace.
- Pictures decoded + rendered; command effects and object flag bits
  decoded; every region identified (no unknown data left).

Original game files are not included (see LICENSE); the source rebuilds
the game from hand-written assembly.

feat(cpu): règle ipl_fetch_next complète dans pollIpl (gated NEOST_IPLFETCH)

Port fidèle des trois cas de WinUAE ipl_fetch_next (newcpu.c:4996-5011) :
- cd  = clock − dernier changement de broche ≥ 4 → nouvelle valeur ;
- cdp = clock − changement PRÉCÉDENT (ipl_pin_change_evt_p, nouveau champ
  iplChangeClockPrev) ≥ 2 → valeur PRÉCÉDENTE ;
- sinon → DIFFÉRÉ (≙ regs.ipl[1]) : nouveau champ iplDeferred, appliqué à la
  frontière d'instruction SUIVANTE dans la boucle execute (≙ rotation
  ipl[0]=ipl[1] de la run loop WinUAE, newcpu.c:5693).

Reste gated (défaut OFF, byte-identique) : mesuré au banc poll-entry, la règle
seule est insuffisante (54/180 vs 5 phases Hatari) et IPLFETCH=1 casse
toujours le loader d'Enchanted Land — la parité exige (a) l'audit des points
d'échantillonnage PAR instruction (POLL_IPL Moira vs fin−4 uniforme WinUAE +
re-sample « pre+2 » mid-accès), (b) la broche MFP niveau 6 exacte (la chaîne
TIMER_B→MFP_IRQ est encore dispatch-late : broche tardive + report = un octet
FDC raté dans le loader). Cf. docs/MOIRA_WINUAE_CONVERGENCE.md (3ᵉ passe).

Étalons 19/0 + TOUS OK (défaut inchangé).

events.title: fix(shifter): compteur $8209 des lignes à tricks — port fidèle Video_CalculateAddress
events.message:
fix(shifter): compteur $8209 des lignes à tricks — port fidèle Video_CalculateAddress

Le lock à −16 du moteur fullscreen d'Enchanted Land en jeu (freq 360/368 au
lieu de 376/384 Hatari, invariant sous tous les balayages CPU) venait du
MODÈLE VIDÉO : pour l'offset intra-ligne, Video_CalculateAddress
(video.c:1508-1565) NE lit PAS DisplayStart/EndCycle de la Glue — il
reconstruit le départ et la taille depuis le borderMask :
  - LEFT_OFF → ds = LINE_START_CYCLE_71 = 0 (pas le HDE_On_Hi=4 de la Glue),
    LEFT_PLUS_2 → 52 ; scroll STE prefetch → lineStart−16 ;
  - fin = ds + CurSize×2 avec CurSize par la table de bordures
    (fullscreen = 230 ; l'ancien (End−Start)/2 donnait 229) ;
  - clamp droite → += LineWidth×2 (STE) ; LEFT_OFF → NbBytes −= 2 SANS garde ;
    NO_DE → 0.
L'erreur de 2-4 octets sur les lignes à tricks faussait l'estimation faisceau
du stabilisateur d'EL (poll $8209 sur lignes fullscreen) → il plaçait ses
impulsions −16 cyc → elles rataient la fenêtre bordure-droite (372,376] →
retraits G/D sporadiques, scroll qui saute.

RÉSULTAT : le moteur d'EL verrouille désormais à 376/384 = HATARI BYTE-EXACT
(res à −4, une case). Trames verrouillées : churn ~20 % vs 17 % Hatari
(légitime — le paysage scrolle) ; le taux de lock (55-66 % vs 100 % Hatari)
reste borné par la reconnaissance IPL (front suivant : ipl_fetch_next complet
— seuil cdp sur le changement PRÉCÉDENT, report ipl[1] à la frontière
suivante, re-sample mid-accès — et broche MFP exacte ; NEOST_IPLFETCH actuel
casse le loader EL). Étalons 19/0 + TOUS OK, LX 0,00 % churn.

⚠ Bancs poll/poll2 : la comparaison mono-trame est invalide — la phase
E-clock précesse (période 5 trames, 5 contenus distincts dans l'AVI, chaque
frame dupliquée ~2× à ~60 fps) ; poll2 n'est byte-exact sous AUCUNE phase
depuis les changements d'entrée (broche exacte/HBL 508) : l'ancien 180/180
était co-calibré avec l'entrée d'AVANT — à re-fermer avec le front
reconnaissance.

events.title: fix(beam-sync): broche IPL au cycle exact (pré-armée) — le « −12 » attribué
events.message:
fix(beam-sync): broche IPL au cycle exact (pré-armée) — le « −12 » attribué

Attribution des 10-12 cycles manquants de latence d'exception (banc poll-entry) :

1. Le « −12 » était un ARTEFACT DE TRACE : le Tracer logue l'instruction AVANT
   le check d'IRQ → la dernière ligne avant un handler est un fantôme (loggée,
   préemptée, jamais exécutée). Instrumenté au vrai chemin (NEOST_EXC_DIAG →
   [EXC]/[JTV]/[PIN] gated, Moira vendorisé) : latence d'exception NeoST =
   Hatari EXACTEMENT ({56,60} ; idle+PClo 12, iack E+14, SR/PChi 8-10, jtv 20).

2. La VRAIE divergence : la broche IPL montait au DISPATCH de bloc (0..24 cyc
   après l'instant vrai, jitter = dépassement de la dernière instruction du
   bloc) — Hatari la lève dans do_cycles, en cours d'instruction. Fix : broches
   PRÉ-ARMÉES (Cpu68k::armHblPinAt/armVblPinAt posées à la planification,
   appliquées par le hook sync() au cycle bus près, mid-instruction ; le
   dispatch BLOC est conservé). NEOST_PIN_ARM (bit0 HBL, bit1 VBL), défaut 1 =
   HBL seule : la broche VBL exacte casse le loader d'Enchanted Land
   (chargement infini — couplage VBL↔IKBD/FDC à investiguer).

3. Position de l'INT HBL : retour au fidèle cpl−4 = 508 (Hbl_Int_Pos_Low_50,
   video.c:978 — le commentaire HBL_VIDEO_CYCLE_OFFSET=0 de video.h est
   trompeur). Le passage à 512 ne gagnait qu'en compensant la broche tardive.

Pièges documentés : la phase E-clock précesse de −4/trame (160256 ≡ 16 mod 20,
période 5 trames) → comparer poll-entry à 5 trames consécutives de l'AVI
Hatari ; les constantes IACK sont absorbées par les boucles 12 cyc.

Validé : étalons 19/0 + TOUS OK, LX titre 0,00 % churn, EL intro + jeu OK
(flicker 36-38/40). Reste (borné) : micro-structure de reconnaissance IPL
(poll-entry 72-136/180) et lock moteur EL à −16 (invariant sous tous les
balayages CPU → suspect modèle vidéo des lignes à tricks).

events.message:
fix(beam-sync): refonte coordonnée — résidu de phase +24 attribué et corrigé

Le clignotement EL / jitter LX / overscan vertical étaient un CUMUL de 4 biais
+ 2 bugs structurels, tous mesurés à l'oracle Hatari (2.6.1-devel, extern/hatari) :

1. IACK sur-compté +8 : E-clock+bloc relocalisés AU point d'IACK réel via les
   hooks iackSyncBefore/After (Moira vendorisé), NEOST_IACK_AT défaut ON —
   le motif mod-20 des positions d'IRQ émerge (= Hatari).
2. chipWait8 alignait le point-MILIEU de l'accès Moira au lieu du DÉBUT
   (wait_cpu_cycle_read) → fin d'accès ≡0 mod 4 = Hatari.
3. Origine d'horloge trame +8 vs Hatari : datations calibrées à l'oracle —
   read videoCounter −14 (banc poll + variante lsr#3 exposant le bit 3 :
   l'ancien +4 était faux de +8 octets, invisibles en palette), write
   freq/res −6 (calibrateur loader EL = Hatari exact). Rustines +16/+4 retirées.
4. IRQ HBL à la frontière de ligne (512, HBL_VIDEO_CYCLE_OFFSET=0) au lieu
   de cpl−4 (calibration périmée). NEOST_HBL_OFF pour A/B.
5. Commit du compteur vidéo à DE_end → commit PARESSEUX (≙ Video_EndHBL) :
   une impulsion 60 Hz datée 376 arrivait après le commit → $8209 figé →
   le scan de calibration du loader EL ne convergeait JAMAIS (bloqué $ee78).
6. Video_RestartVideoCounter porté (event VC_RESTART, ligne 310/260 cyc 56) :
   base relue APRÈS le handler VBL du jeu — le stabilisateur d'EL lisait
   l'ancien buffer double-buffer toute la trame.

Validé : poll-bench 180/180 byte-identique Hatari (2 variantes), loader EL
réparé (sondes 456/452/448/444 = Hatari exact), bordure haute EL stable
(38-40/40), Lethal Xcess titre 0,00 % de churn (résolu), Super Hang-On OK,
étalons 19/0 + TOUS OK (overscan_top re-baseliné : l'ancienne référence était
fausse de 24 px, vérifié pixel-à-pixel contre Hatari).

Reste (pièce vidéo) : le moteur fullscreen d'EL verrouille à 72 % avec ses
impulsions freq à −16 vs l'oracle in-game → micro-sauts de scroll (cf.
docs/MOIRA_WINUAE_CONVERGENCE.md, bloc 2026-07-02).

events.title: Fix crash and menu no-op in map copy/paste
events.message:
Fix crash and menu no-op in map copy/paste

Ctrl+C/Ctrl+V on the map widget crashed with a std::vector bounds
assertion in State::_pasteMap(): it computed a "one past the end"
pointer via _map[width*height], which is undefined behavior for
std::vector::operator[] (unlike a plain C array). Newer libstdc++
builds with bounds-check assertions enabled (e.g. Fedora) abort on
this; other builds silently did pointer arithmetic. Switched to
_map.data() + width*height, mirroring the equivalent C-array logic
in _pasteChars.

Separately, Edit > Copy and Edit > Paste from the menu were silent
no-ops: MainWindow::bufferToClipboard() and the paste sanity check
both gated on QWidget::hasFocus() for the charset/tileset/map
widgets, but opening the Edit menu steals keyboard focus away from
them before the slot runs, so hasFocus() was always false. Added an
event filter that tracks whichever of those three widgets last had
focus and used that instead, so the menu actions work the same as
the keyboard shortcuts.

events.title: ppc: flush QEMU JIT after 68k cache changes
events.message:
ppc: flush QEMU JIT after 68k cache changes

OS3.x/WarpOS can patch PPC code and page tables from the m68k side in shared RAM. QEMU does not see those writes through the PPC softmmu, so stale translation blocks can survive until the m68k/PPC handoff deadlocks.

Import the optional ppc_cpu_flush_jit hook, mark QEMU PPC code cache state dirty on 68040 instruction-cache and MMU ATC flushes, and consume one coalesced flush at the next m68k-to-PPC handoff. Skip the flush while the m68k is halted so PPC-only OS4 execution is not forced to retranslate continuously.

events.title: Scale on-screen keyboards proportionally with the display scale
events.message:
Scale on-screen keyboards proportionally with the display scale

The 48K rubber and +/128K hard keyboards were fixed-pixel mock-ups tuned
for the ~42/48px units the 3x display scale happens to produce. A single
container breakpoint shrank only the unit pitch while every legend size,
glyph offset and block swatch stayed in absolute px, so the keyboards
only looked right at 3x and broke at 2x/1x (the pane narrows with the
canvas, firing the breakpoint and leaving the legends full-size).

Drive the key unit from the display scale via a new --display-scale CSS
variable, and express every internal metric as a multiple of a per-board
"design pixel" (--u1 for the 48K, --pu1 for the Plus/128K, including the
moulded groove gradient stops) so each face scales as one rigid block.
3x is byte-for-byte identical to the previous layout; 2x/1x now scale
down proportionally. Removes the now-dead 520px/560px breakpoints.

events.title: Fix one-scanline FLASH tear in high-accuracy renderer at column 0
events.message:
Fix one-scanline FLASH tear in high-accuracy renderer at column 0

renderLineSegment gated the display-cell draw on `xEnd > borderLeft`.
When a progressive render chunk ends exactly on the left display edge
(xEnd == borderLeft), the Ferranti +1 cell offset asks for col 0
(colEnd=1), but the strict `>` skipped the draw while
renderPendingScanlines still advanced nextDisplayCol past it. Col 0 was
then never drawn that frame and kept the previous frame's pixels — on a
column-0 FLASH cell (the editing cursor, bottom-left) this showed as a
single scanline with inverted flash bits, at flash transitions. The idle
HALT loop produces beam chunks that land exactly on borderLeft, so it
only surfaced in real time (not in headless tests).

Use `xEnd >= borderLeft`; `colStart < colEnd` is the real authority for

events.title: devbench: idle-timeout for screenshot collection (full screen over serial)
events.message:
devbench: idle-timeout for screenshot collection (full screen over serial)

The screenshot collector used a fixed 120s total deadline. A full 1280x1024
screen over 115200 serial streams for ~3-4 minutes (one row at a time), so the
hard deadline truncated it (only ~407/1024 rows saved). Switch to an idle
timeout: keep collecting as long as rows keep arriving, give up only after 20s
of silence, with a 600s absolute backstop. Completes any-speed transports; over
TCP it still returns in ~1-2s.

Pairs with the v1.18 bridge fix (don't hold LockIBase across the transfer): the
machine stays responsive while a full serial screenshot streams to completion.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: xphileby

events.title: bridge: don't hold LockIBase across slow screenshot transfer (v1.18)
events.message:
bridge: don't hold LockIBase across slow screenshot transfer (v1.18)

amiga_screenshot held LockIBase(0) — a global Intuition lock — for the entire
duration of streaming the screen. Over TCP that's ~1-2s (unnoticeable), but over
115200 serial a full 1280x1024 screen is ~2-3 minutes of transfer, during which
all of Intuition is locked: no mouse, keyboard, or redraw. The machine looks
frozen (it isn't — it recovers when the transfer finishes), so users reboot.

Fix: a tiered output sink that buffers the formatted protocol lines during the
locked capture, then drains them to the wire AFTER UnlockIBase:
  - RAM    : AllocMem the whole output (any roomy machine — always this)
  - FILE   : spool to a T: temp file when RAM is too tight (helps iff T: is on
             real storage, e.g. a hard disk)
  - DIRECT : neither available (low-mem box with T:=RAM:, or floppy-only) — fall
             back to sending under the lock (brief freeze, but correct)
Applies to all three capture paths (true-colour RTG, 8-bit chunky, planar). The
lock is now held only for the fast CPU-bound capture, not the slow transport.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: xphileby

events.title: devbench: robust per-chunk file-transfer retry for lossy serial links
events.message:
devbench: robust per-chunk file-transfer retry for lossy serial links

Bulk transfers (push_file/pull_file) failed over a real 115200 serial link: a
single dropped byte corrupts a chunk's long hex line and the old retry only
fired on a missing ack — a corrupt-but-acked chunk was accepted (caught only by
the final CRC, with no recovery), and APPEND retries could duplicate data.

- push: write every chunk with WRITEFILE at an explicit offset (never APPEND) so
  a retry overwrites the same span (idempotent — a lost ack can't duplicate).
  Verify the daemon's echoed byte count equals the chunk length; retry on
  timeout/err/short-write.
- pull: guard the hex decode (a dropped byte -> odd-length hex), require each
  chunk to decode to the requested size (else retry the same offset, no
  misalign), and re-download the whole file if the assembled CRC mismatches;
  fail loudly instead of silently returning a corrupt file.
- smaller chunks (4000 -> 1024 B) + more retries (3 -> 6): shorter lines transfer
  clean far more often over a lossy link; negligible cost over TCP.

Verified over real serial (Amiga Paula 115200 -> CH340): a 6 KB push+pull that
previously failed at chunk 0 now round-trips byte-for-byte, CRC verified both
ways. Unit tests cover short-write retry, idempotent offsets (no APPEND),
give-up-after-max, and pull short-read retry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: xphileby

events.title: bridge: re-arm serial read after RX error so it can't wedge (v1.17)
events.message:
bridge: re-arm serial read after RX error so it can't wedge (v1.17)

The daemon's main loop only re-arms the async serial CMD_READ after a
*successful* byte (the `while (transport_check_read(&ch))` body calls
transport_start_read()). serial_check_read() clears read_pending and returns 0
when a read completes with an error — common at 115200 when bytes arrive faster
than the 1-byte read loop drains them (Paula receiver overrun). So a single
transient RX error left no read posted and permanently wedged serial RX (and
spun the main loop, flooding heartbeats).

Fix: in serial_check_read(), on any non-byte completion, clear io_Error and
re-post the read so RX self-recovers.

Found by driving the bridge's serial transport on WinUAE: PING worked, then
LISTVOLUMES/LISTDIR got nothing (RX stuck) until this fix. After it, RX:10
commands round-tripped with no wedge. Verified end-to-end over a real serial
link (Amiga Paula 115200 -> CH340 USB-serial): 43/44 serial-relevant MCP
operations pass (the exception, push_file, is unrelated 115200 byte-loss on
bulk transfers).

events.title: bridge: clean not-found errors, captured DOS output, NIL stdin for launches (v1.16)
events.message:
bridge: clean not-found errors, captured DOS output, NIL stdin for launches (v1.16)

Fixes three bugs from the bulk-transfer session (BUGS_mcp_bridge.md A/B/E):

- A: amiga_read_file / amiga_list_dir on a missing path waited out the full
  timeout and printed a misleading "busy/wedged" message. The bridge already
  replies ERR instantly; the host waiters only listened for the success event
  and dropped it. New _send_await() subscribes to the target AND err, so both
  now return a prompt "Not found or unreadable: <path>".

- B: amiga_dos_command returned only "[OK] Started (proc N)" with no output.
  Rerouted through the async-SCRIPT capture path (script_execute) so stdout/
  stderr are captured and returned. Runs async on the bridge, so a long command
  no longer blocks other requests.

- E: a child blocking on stdin could wedge the whole bridge. proc_run_async
  passed SYS_Input,0 (inherited the daemon's input); now opens a dedicated NIL:
  for the child's stdin so it gets EOF instead of hanging. The SCRIPT path
  already used NIL: input.

Verified live on AmigaBridge v1.16 in WinUAE (AmigaOS 3.2): missing paths
return instantly; Echo/Version/lha give real output; Ask and `lha ?` no longer
wedge (ping stays alive). Host unit tests pass.

events.title: bridge: fix list_dir truncation, read-past-EOF wedge, large-drive free space (v1.15)
events.message:
bridge: fix list_dir truncation, read-past-EOF wedge, large-drive free space (v1.15)

BUG1 (LISTDIR silent truncation): fs_list_dir packed every entry into one
8KB line and break'd when full, so large dirs were cut (442 entries -> 349)
with no indication. Now it serializes one page per LISTDIR, reports the TRUE
grand total, and the host pages (LISTDIR|path|startIdx) until it has them all.

BUG2 (READFILE wedged the daemon): protocol_send_file hex-encoded into a
902-byte buffer, so any read > 450 bytes overran static memory and hung the
daemon (reboot to recover) - not an EOF issue at all. Size hexbuf to
BRIDGE_MAX_LINE and cap the read so the FILE line fits; fs_read_file treats a
seek at/after EOF as a clean 0-byte read; pull_file advances by bytes actually
received.

BUG3 (wrong free space on big drives): VOLUMES computed blocks*blockSize/1024
in 32-bit, overflowing past 4GB (43GB free showed as ~3.5GB). Divide first so
it stays exact up to the 32-bit id_NumBlocks limit.

Verified on WinUAE (500-entry dir, 1.2KB reads, past-EOF) and on the real
Amiga (MEDIA2: 442 entries in full, 900-byte + past-EOF reads with the daemon
still ping-alive, MEDIA2 free space 44949938KB / ~43GB). Host paging unit test
added.

events.title: profiler: don't silently truncate an out-of-range CFA offset in the unwind table
events.message:
profiler: don't silently truncate an out-of-range CFA offset in the unwind table

The packed emulator unwind format has only 12 bits for the CFA offset
(0-4095). A function with a large stack frame and no frame pointer can
have CFA = SP + offset >= 4096, which buildUnwindTable masked with
`& 0xfff` instead of rejecting - computing a wrong, truncated CFA and
corrupting every saved-register read derived from it (so the profiler
would attribute that function's cycles to bogus parent frames), with
no diagnostic.

Detect the out-of-range offset and skip the row instead, leaving its
slots at the existing "no unwind info" zero sentinel (the call stack
just stops there rather than continuing with corrupt data), and log a
warning so it's visible if it happens.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: profiler: don't fall through to a same-named global for an unaddressable local
events.message:
profiler: don't fall through to a same-named global for an unaddressable local

resolveNameToLValue matched a local by name, and if locationToAddress
couldn't resolve it (register-resident location, or a 'cfa' location
with no CFI for that pc), silently fell through to a same-named global
and returned its address instead. A hover, watch, or setVariable/
setExpression on such a name would target the wrong memory - read or
write hits global storage while believing it's the shadowing local.

A local name match now always shadows the global, returning undefined
when it can't be addressed rather than resolving to the global.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: profiler: exclude vasm local labels from the symbol set, not just one query
events.message:
profiler: exclude vasm local labels from the symbol set, not just one query

findSymbolOffset's excludeLocal flag fixed the flame graph's function
naming, but getSymbols/getSymbolLengths still treated `.`-prefixed
local labels (e.g. a macro's `.\@` branch target) as real symbols. The
webview's symbol list (built from these) still split a routine's
length at its first local label and could resolve addresses past it
to the wrong name — disagreeing with the flame graph for the same PC.

Push excludeLocal down into getSymbols/getSymbolLengths themselves so
buildSymbolList (and any future consumer) excludes local labels by
construction instead of needing to remember the flag, and pass it from
syntheticLabel's Kickstart path too (latent today, but the same class
of bug if a future ROM symbol set ever has local labels).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: profiler: stop flame graph splitting on macro-local labels
events.message:
profiler: stop flame graph splitting on macro-local labels

Macro-internal labels (e.g. vasm's \@ unique-id local labels used for
polling loops like BLIT_WAIT) were treated as distinct functions by
findSymbolOffset's nearest-preceding-symbol lookup, and even after
excluding local labels by name, the per-PC line-table file/line still
varied across call sites for the same function. Resolve file/line at
the symbol's own address instead of pc so every instruction in a
function (macro-expanded or not) maps to one consistent location.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: bridge: run SCRIPT async so DOS commands can't freeze the bridge (v1.14)
events.message:
bridge: run SCRIPT async so DOS commands can't freeze the bridge (v1.14)

Problem A: amiga_run_script -> SCRIPT -> handle_script ran the command via
SystemTags(SYS_Asynch=FALSE), blocking the daemon's main loop for the whole
command duration. Proven on WinUAE: a 'wait 10' produced a 10s gap with zero
heartbeats; a slow/interactive/hung command froze the bridge indefinitely.

Daemon (handle_script): run the script ASYNCHRONOUSLY with output captured to
T:ab_sout_<id> and reply 'ASYNC|<file>' immediately, so the main loop never
blocks. A '###ABDONE###' sentinel is echoed at the end (guarded by 'FailAt 255'
so a non-zero RC can't abort before it) to mark completion. Also fixes the old
sync path truncating output at 511 bytes.

Host: shared script_execute() helper (used by amiga_run_script, /api/script and
the web-UI _run_script) parses the ASYNC reply and polls the capture file for
the sentinel, returning full output; falls back to legacy sync for old daemons.

Problem B: ~25 tools returned "No response (bridge may not support X)" on any
timeout, which read as "unsupported" even when the bridge was merely busy/hung
(Problem A) or disconnected. New _bridge_no_response() reports the real cause
(lost connection vs communication timeout), explicitly "NOT an unsupported
command".

Verified end-to-end on WinUAE through devbench: async script + output capture,
a quick command succeeding while a slow one runs (bridge stays responsive), and
the corrected error wording. Plus unit tests (tests/test_script_async.py) and a
direct daemon test of the non-blocking behaviour.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: feat(cpu): implement NEOST_IPLFETCH for accurate IPL recognition timing
events.message:
feat(cpu): implement NEOST_IPLFETCH for accurate IPL recognition timing

Added a new feature to enhance IPL recognition timing in the CPU by implementing NEOST_IPLFETCH. This feature allows immediate recognition of the IPL pin while maintaining the previous value if the pin changes within a specified cycle range. Additionally, diagnostic tracing for the HBL handler has been introduced to facilitate cycle-exact comparisons between Moira and WinUAE. Adjustments to IPL delay thresholds are now also made dynamically based on CPU speed changes.

events.message:
od-unix: enable threaded CPU support

Match the Windows target by enabling the shared threaded CPU path on

semaphore helpers, but sysconfig.h did not expose WITH_THREADED_CPU.

events.title: cfgfile: handle missing command line option values
events.message:
cfgfile: handle missing command line option values

parse_cmdline_option() keeps unknown command line options in the
all_lines list. A trailing option such as -G reaches this path without
a value, which passed NULL to my_strdup() and crashed before the GUI
could start.

events.title: od-unix: fix config values lost in the Qt launcher round trip
events.message:
od-unix: fix config values lost in the Qt launcher round trip

Loading a configuration file could silently change it (GitHub issue #1,
"CPU and RAM are often not the ones I set"):

- The chipset_compatible handler synced the quickstart model combo
  without blocking its signals, so loading any config with a
  chipset_compatible value re-applied the whole quickstart model preset
  over the explicit settings (FPU, compatibility flags, floppy count).
- FpuInternal was -1, which QButtonGroup treats as auto-assign and
  checkedId() returns for "no selection": the CPU-internal FPU button
  could never be selected programmatically, so fpu_model vanished from
  every 68040/68060 configuration on save, start, and each F12 visit.
- nr_floppies had no load handler, so drive-enable states never
  followed the loaded config.

Configs without a quickstart line also no longer gain a synthesized
quickstart key: quickstart mode now turns off when loading a full
configuration and is re-enabled by an explicit quickstart setting.

Verified by a new roundtrip harness: WINUAE_QT_CONFIG_ROUNDTRIP_OUT
makes the launcher load the given config, export the merged config, and
exit; unix-smoke-config-roundtrip.sh (in winuae_unix_smoke_basic)
compares CPU/FPU/MMU/memory/floppy keys across three machine profiles.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: match Windows GUI button semantics in runtime (F12) UI
events.message:
od-unix: match Windows GUI button semantics in runtime (F12) UI

The runtime GUI's bottom button row behaved like the pre-start launcher:
Quit and Cancel both just closed the dialog and resumed emulation, Reset
reverted the UI to A1200 quickstart defaults, and Restart was hidden.
Mirror the Windows GUI (IDC_RESETAMIGA/IDC_QUITEMU/IDC_RESTARTEMU):

- Quit requests uae_quit() and exits the emulator.
- Reset applies the edited configuration and hard-resets the Amiga
  (uae_reset(1,1)), then resumes.
- Restart is shown in runtime mode and returns to the launcher through
  uae_restart().
- Start is relabeled OK while emulation is running; Cancel and closing
  the window still resume without applying changes.

The launcher result carries the new quit/restart states and a hard-reset
flag through the bridge; pre-start behavior is unchanged.

Also write floppy paths and the first CD slot into the merged config
even when empty, so ejecting media in the runtime GUI reaches the
core's disk-change detection instead of silently keeping the old image.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: seed Qt launcher from default.uae at startup
events.message:
od-unix: seed Qt launcher from default.uae at startup

The shared core loads <configurationpath>/default.uae into the prefs at
startup (main.cpp real_main), but the Qt launcher built its state from
scratch, so the default configuration had no visible effect unless the
GUI was disabled. Pass the file as the launcher's initial config path
when it exists, matching the Windows "save as default.uae" behavior.

Configs given on the command line keep precedence: the launcher's own
argument parsing decides, exposed through the bridge so gui_init does
not duplicate it. The bridge no longer infers runtime mode from "an
initial config path is present"; gui_display passes it explicitly.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: cmake: name the Unix binary winuae
events.message:
cmake: name the Unix binary winuae

The installed Linux command, the .desktop entries, and the WinUAE.app
bundle all use the name winuae while the build tree produced
winuae_unix. Set OUTPUT_NAME on the winuae_unix target so the binary is
winuae everywhere, drop the now-redundant install RENAME, and update
the smoke script defaults, bundling scripts, and README accordingly.
macos-bundle.sh keeps a fallback for build directories from before the
rename. The CMake target names are unchanged.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: ship starter filter presets
events.message:
od-unix: ship starter filter presets

The Filter page's preset list was empty until the user saved their own
(GitHub issue #4). Add a set of bundled presets built from the portable
filter controls the Unix GLSL pipeline implements (Sharp Pixels, Soft
Bilinear, CRT Scanlines, Warm TV), installed under the shared data
directory on Linux and into the app bundle resources on macOS.

The preset combo lists user presets and bundled presets together; the
user directory wins on name collisions, saving always writes to the
user directory, and loading falls back to the bundled file when no user
preset of that name exists.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: od-unix: persist host settings in winuae.ini
events.message:
od-unix: persist host settings in winuae.ini

The Unix port had no equivalent of the Windows registry/winuae.ini
store: the Qt Paths page reverted to hardcoded defaults on every start
(GitHub issue #2).

Port the ini-file mode of the od-win32 registry abstraction into
od-unix/registry.cpp on top of the shared ini.cpp, with the same
registry.h API. The store resolves to winuae.ini next to the executable
when present (portable mode, matching Windows), otherwise
$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/winuae/winuae.ini on Linux and
~/Library/Application Support/WinUAE/winuae.ini on macOS; the
WINUAE_INI environment variable overrides the location.

The Qt launcher loads the Paths page directories and flags from the
store and saves them when the dialog closes, through new host-setting
hooks on the provider struct. The core path fetchers consult the stored
values between per-config unix.*_path overrides and the built-in
defaults, so the configured directories also apply outside the GUI.
Settings flush on dialog close and at gui_exit.

Covered by winuae_unix_registry_test (value types, subtrees,
enumeration, deletion, and persistence across reopen).

events.title: fix(beam-sync): VC_WAIT défaut 2→0 — RAM_SLOT double-comptait le wait $8209 → EL en jeu réparé
events.message:
fix(beam-sync): VC_WAIT défaut 2→0 — RAM_SLOT double-comptait le wait $8209 → EL en jeu réparé

Diff de datation sur l'oracle Enchanted Land EN JEU (débloqué cette session via
SPACE/cmd-fifo) : le wait-state +2 par-lecture sur $FF8205/07/09 (NEOST_VC_WAIT=2)
DOUBLE-COMPTAIT le +2 que NEOST_RAM_SLOT (passé défaut-ON) fournit déjà → les
boucles de poll fullscreen d'EL dérivaient de +4 cyc/itération :
  $ee78 (sync-scroll, lecture simple) = 24 vs Hatari 20
  $3700 (double lecture)              = 40 vs Hatari 36
→ le CPU échantillonnait le faisceau au mauvais cycle → SCRAMBLE plein écran.

Fix : NEOST_VC_WAIT défaut 2→0 (Shifter.cpp). Avec : les deux boucles = Hatari
EXACTEMENT, et EL en jeu passe de garbage scramblé à paysage rocheux NET.

Validé : étalons BYTE-IDENTIQUES (spec512/overscan_top/scroll/glue 19-0) ;
EmuTOS boote ; LX inchangé (cassé indépendamment). L'ancien commentaire « +2
requis sinon LX/EL noir » datait d'AVANT RAM_SLOT défaut-ON → corrigé.

docs/MOIRA_WINUAE_CONVERGENCE.md : recette EL en jeu fiable (clé = SANS --fastfdc,
qui cassait le loader → faux « périmé »), oracle EL in-game DÉBLOQUÉ (SPACE
scancode 57 via cmd-fifo, réputé impossible), résolution VC_WAIT, et résidu
(bande droite) tranché = NON la datation écritures (kSyncWriteOffsetCyc
load-bearing) mais le chantier V2 res-switch / géométrie par-ligne.

profiler: persist kickstart ROM identity in saved .vamigaprofile

getKickstartInfo() exposes the live ROM identity to the save path. Legacy files
without the field decode to the sentinel (flat [Kickstart], unchanged).

events.message:

Plumb the custom-register file added to the capture snapshot through the host:

events.title: profiler: synthetic [IRQ]/[Kickstart]/[External] buckets + no-CFI blob nesting
events.message:
profiler: synthetic [IRQ]/[Kickstart]/[External] buckets + no-CFI blob nesting

Bumps vamigaweb_fork (out-of-program samples emitted + [IRQ] dispatch-gap marker). Host-side syntheticLabel classifies a leaf PC: IRQ_MARKER -> [IRQ]; ROM range -> [Kick] <name> when Kickstart symbols are loaded (else flat [Kickstart]); loaded program segment -> normal; else [External]. The top-level CPU total now reaches ~100% (was ~75%).

applyContextReuse nests context-less leaves under the calling function (ports the old ext's lastCallstack reuse): out-of-program [Kickstart]/[External], and in-program no-CFI leaves (an #embed'd binary / hand-asm called via jsr, e.g. ThePlayer). The no-CFI-blob path is gated to DWARF programs (getUnwindRows non-empty) so pure-assembly captures, where depth-1 is legitimate, are unaffected. Rebuilt vAmiga.wasm.

events.title: profiler: fast webview data path (resource-fetch bulk + model store)
events.message:
profiler: fast webview data path (resource-fetch bulk + model store)

Captures took ~1s to display in dev builds. Two causes, both fixed:

1. Bulk binary (DMA grid + chip/slow snapshot) was sent via webview.postMessage, which serializes large binary slowly (cross-process, ~0.3-0.8ms/KB; a 1MB array ~820ms). Now the extension writes the bulk to a temp file in globalStorageUri (added to localResourceRoots) and posts only its asWebviewUri; the webview fetches it (~10ms for 1.6MB) and decodes it (src/profilerBulk.ts pack/unpackBulk). connect-src added to the webview CSP. Live panel and .vamigaprofile editor share this path.

2. The model (with the large typed arrays) was a React prop, and React's DEVELOPMENT build deep-serializes props every render for its performance/components track (~1s). The model now lives in a module store (modelStore.ts), read via getProfileModel() with useModelVersion() driving re-renders — never a prop/state/hook value, so it's never serialized. Production React strips that instrumentation (esbuild sets NODE_ENV=production when minifying), so releases were already fine; this fixes the dev loop (~1s -> ~20ms).

events.title: profiler: .vamigaprofile capture documents (save/load)
events.message:
profiler: .vamigaprofile capture documents (save/load)

Adds a binary profile document that is the save/load artifact, the dev fixture, and the test input through one shared pipeline. Refactors capture into a pure seam (RawCapture -> buildModelFromCapture) used by both live capture and file load.

Format (src/vamigaProfile.ts): gzip of [magic][manifest JSON][raw sections] — profile stream + optional DMA grid / chip+slow snapshot, with the program ELF embedded and the relocation (segmentOffsets/baseDir) recorded so absolute captured PCs re-symbolicate identically on load. encode/decode are pure + unit-tested (round-trip, alignment, bad-magic).

Save: a webview toolbar button posts saveProfile; the provider embeds the ELF + relocation grabbed once per session at capture time (so saving works even after the emulator/session closes), writes the file, opens it, and closes the live panel. Embedding is required and fails loud rather than writing an unloadable file.

Load: a read-only CustomEditor for *.vamigaprofile rebuilds the SourceMap from the embedded ELF + relocation and runs buildModelFromCapture (profileLoader.ts), hosting the profiler webview in file mode (Capture/Save hidden; jump-to-source works). Replay test exercises the whole chain against a committed fixture.

Session-constant data (symbols, ELF) is sent/read once per session, not per capture. mode is baked into the webview HTML so it holds even if a load fails.

events.title: CPU profiler Phase 4: DMA profiling + inline call frames + webview polish
events.message:
CPU profiler Phase 4: DMA profiling + inline call frames + webview polish

DMA profiling: captures the DMA grid + chip/slow snapshot in the same frame as the CPU profile (rides wasm_profile_start). src/dma.ts decodes the binary grid into IDmaModel; FlameGraph draws a time-aligned DMA band above the CPU rows (channelStyle colors, coalesced runs, addr/value/R-W tooltips); topDownGraph groups the TimeView under top-level CPU and DMA nodes. Symbolization moved webview-side (model.symbols + createSymbolizer); custom-register names consolidated in webview/shared/customRegisters.ts (copperDisassembler reuses it). Unwired memory/register reconstruction lives in webview reconstruct.ts; both inputs (grid + snapshot) ride the model.

Inline call frames: expandPc expands each captured PC into its physical function + DWARF inlined_subroutine chain (the unwinder can't see inlined frames), so they show as their own boxes in the flame graph and TimeView, suffixed ' (inlined)'. Line attribution follows addr2line --inlines.

Webview polish: fixed DMA channel colors (constants are 0xAABBGGRR -- red/blue were swapped); TimeView header uses the UI font + matches the old extension's swatch/divider; default time unit is % of Frame; captures now survive a webview reload (provider caches the last model and re-posts on ready instead of re-capturing).

Includes the matching vamigaweb_fork pointer (DmaProfiler) + rebuilt vamiga/ wasm. 531 tests pass.

events.title: dwarf: DWARF5 rnglists, cross-CU ref_addr, complete DW_OP table, fail-loud
events.message:
dwarf: DWARF5 rnglists, cross-CU ref_addr, complete DW_OP table, fail-loud

Fixes two parser gaps that surfaced once the CPU profiler started expanding inline frames (DWARF5 a.elf):

1. Range lists: discontiguous inlined subroutines use DW_AT_ranges, which in DWARF5 points into .debug_rnglists (DW_RLE_* entries), not .debug_ranges. The parser only knew the old begin/end format and was reading rnglist offsets out of .debug_ranges -> garbage ranges -> spurious inline frames at random PCs. Now parses .debug_rnglists with a version-aware getDieIntervals (fixes lexical-block ranges too).

2. Inline names: an inlined function's name lives on its abstract instance, reached via DW_AT_abstract_origin -- here a DW_FORM_ref_addr, i.e. a cross-CU reference. The resolver added cuStartOffset (correct only for CU0) and searched only the current CU, so names resolved to '???'. Now resolves ref_addr against the .debug_info section base + a global DIE map, and resolveDieName follows abstract_origin/specification/linkage_name (demangled).

Also corrects the DW_OP enum (dup/drop/over/pick/swap/rot/xderef were off by two, colliding with constu/consts/... and mis-sizing operands) and replaces the partial op switch with a complete, operand-accurate DW_OP table. Unimplemented DW_OP/DW_CFA/DW_RLE encodings and a missing range section now throw instead of silently desyncing/producing garbage -- preferred during development.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: CPU profiler (Phase 3): top-down TimeView + recursive unwind fix
events.message:
CPU profiler (Phase 3): top-down TimeView + recursive unwind fix

TimeView: sortable top-down function table below the flame chart,
ported from vscode-amiga-debug (React, react-window, codicons).
Filter computes filterExpanded synchronously (plain useMemo, not
useMemo+setState) to avoid the one-keystroke lag. Empty filter
guard matches FlameGraph behaviour.

CpuProfiler.cpp: fix recursive-call unwind truncation. The old
`ret == pc` no-progress guard fired when two nested frames shared
the same call-site return address (e.g. fib(4)→fib(3) and
fib(3)→fib(2) both produce RA = fib+0x22). Replaced with
`cfa <= a7` checked before updating a7, which correctly tests
whether the stack actually advanced. Adds a comment on pre- vs
post-instruction memory timing safety.

events.message:
CPU profiler (Phase 2): time-ordered flame chart

Replaces the aggregated call-tree view with a time-ordered flame chart
(x = cycles in execution order) that matches the old vscode-amiga-debug
renderer at the UI/UX level:

- IProfileModel (nodes/locations/samples/timeDeltas) built extension-side
  from InstructionSample[]; per-sample stream retained for future
  coverage/disassembly enrichment (ProfilerManager.getSamples())
- buildColumns (columns.ts) ports the old stacks.tsx column layout:
  one column per instruction, adjacent identical stacks merged
- FlameGraph.tsx rewritten: 2D-canvas, drag-to-pan with pointer capture
  (robust off-iframe release), mouse-wheel zoom centred on cursor,
  double-click zoom with quadratic easing, keyboard nav (arrows/Enter/Esc),
  synced horizontal scrollbar, nice-number ruler, filter dimming
- Toolbar: filter box (text + match-case + regex toggles), unit dropdown
  (cycles / µs / rasterlines / % of frame), Ctrl+click jumps to source
  (reveals already-open editor via findOpenColumn)
- Tooltip: MiddleOut filename ellipsis, total/self/aggregate time,

events.message:
CPU profiler (Phase 1): call-tree flame graph for m68k C/C++ programs

Adds a "VAmiga: Open CPU Profiler" command that captures one frame of CPU
execution and renders a symbolicated flame graph with per-function cycle costs.

Pipeline: DWARF .debug_frame -> dwarfParser.evaluateUnwindRows (constant-state
rows) -> unwindTable.buildUnwindTable packs a 6-byte {cfa,r13,ra} entry per
2-byte code location -> uploaded to the emulator's fork-local CpuProfiler (see
the vamigaweb_fork submodule bump) -> binary u32 stream read back over HEAPU8
(no JSON/base64) -> profilerManager decodes + symbolicates + aggregates into a
call tree -> lean canvas flame graph webview (framework-neutral; the WebGL/Preact
graft and DMA/copper views are later phases).

The panel auto-captures one frame on open and offers a "Capture frame" button to
re-capture. Multi-frame and live capture are deferred future phases.
