events.title: demangle: fix OOM/hang on internal-linkage (static) names ending in digits
events.message:
demangle: fix OOM/hang on internal-linkage (static) names ending in digits

GCC marks static symbols with a leading 'L' after _Z (e.g. _ZL6Wait10v for
`static void Wait10()`). The parser didn't strip it, desyncing the name parse;
for names ending in digits this looped forever and exhausted memory (hit at
launch via parseELFSymbols on a fixture with such a function).

Strip the leading 'L', and add progress guards in parseArgsUntil /
parseTemplatePlaceholders / parseTypeList so a non-consuming sub-parse can never
loop. Adds regression tests for static functions and adversarial digit-heavy
manglings.

events.message:
feat(cpu,beam-sync): RAM_SLOT+IACK défaut ON — déclenchent l'overscan beam-sync

Les deux flags ENSEMBLE font tomber la dérive du faisceau sur Hatari (+78/ligne)
et déclenchent l'overscan d'Enchanted Land (banc make_respulse_test.py vs oracle
--trace video_res) — séparément aucun ne suffit (RAM_SLOT seul +64, IACK seul
verrouillé). Corrige la conclusion « RAM_SLOT/E-clock = pas d'impact jeu » (qui
valait pour les flags testés EN ISOLATION, jamais ensemble sur le rendu de bordure).

Root cause (banc N=38) : sans les flags le handler HBL d'EL est ~88 cyc trop rapide
→ l'impulsion res se VERROUILLE à cyc ~480/ligne → ne balaye jamais les fenêtres de
retrait → trick=0, zéro overscan. Avec les deux : dérive +78/ligne = Hatari.

- src/core/Cpu68k.cpp : g_ramSlot, g_iackOn défaut true (NEOST_*=0 pour désactiver, A/B)
- tests/reference/overscan_top.ppm : re-baseliné (56 px en bordure overscan SEULE ;
  zone active byte-identique Hatari ON et OFF — validé à l'oracle Hatari)
- doc maître + CHANGELOG : diagnostic corrigé (phase CPU↔faisceau, PAS largeur
  d'affichage) ; résidu = overscan vertical (phase absolue par-ligne, alternance 76/80)

run_etalons : TOUS OK. EmuTOS boote proprement. A/B : NEOST_RAM_SLOT=0 NEOST_IACK=0
reproduit l'ancien comportement (banc respulse trick=1→0).

events.title: bridge: pass keyboard qualifiers through input injection (v1.13)
events.message:
bridge: pass keyboard qualifiers through input injection (v1.13)

input.device hands an injected IND_WRITEEVENT to Intuition with its
ie_Qualifier as-supplied, so injecting a Ctrl/Shift/Alt rawkey before a
key never made the following key carry the modifier - every injected key
reported a bare keycode and Ctrl/Alt/Shift bindings were silently dropped.

Track keyboard qualifier keys in g_keyQuals (down sets, up clears, Caps
toggles) and OR it into ie_Qualifier for injected key and mouse events.
Verified on real hardware against MCAmiga: Ctrl+F9 swaps panels, Ctrl+F1
no longer opens Help, Shift+F9 invokes diff.

Also make the Makefile auto-generate header dependencies (-MMD -MP), so
bumping the version in bridge_internal.h rebuilds protocol_handler.o and
the reported version no longer goes stale.

events.message:
bridge: base64 screenshot payloads + wider capture (v1.10)

Add a reusable base64 codec (src/b64.c: b64_encode/b64_decode) - 33%
encoding overhead vs hex's 100%, alphabet safe for the pipe/newline line
protocol - and use it for the SCRRLE screenshot rows instead of hex. On
top of RLE this mainly helps detailed/incompressible regions where RLE
can't shrink much (worst case 1.34x on the wire instead of 2.0x).

base64's lower overhead also lets one row carry more pixels per line, so
the true-colour width cap rises from 1344 to 1920 - 1600/1920 RTG modes
are no longer left-truncated.

Round-trip unit-tested (base64+RLE); verified on real hardware, image
pixel-perfect. b64.c is shared infrastructure for further bulk paths.

events.title: bridge: RLE-compress screenshot rows -> ~13x faster captures (v1.9)
events.message:
bridge: RLE-compress screenshot rows -> ~13x faster captures (v1.9)

Each row was sent as raw hex (3 bytes/pixel true-colour, 1 byte/pixel
chunky), so a 1280x1024 desktop was ~7.9 MB on the wire regardless of
content - even though a Workbench screen is mostly large flat-colour
areas.

Daemon (gfx_inspector.c): RLE-compress each row with a TGA/PackBits
scheme (run packets + literal packets, so incompressible data costs at
most 1 header byte per 128 pixels and never blows up), hex-encode the
result, and emit it as SCRRLE|row|hex. Used for both the true-colour
(bpp=3) and chunky (bpp=1) paths; the host infers pixel size from the
SCRINFO depth. Width capped so a worst-case row still fits one line.

Host: decode SCRRLE back into the existing true-colour / chunky render
structures (screenshot.rle_decode + rle_lines), parse/publish the new
line type, and collect it in both the MCP tool and the web endpoint.
SCRRGB/SCRDATA paths kept for backward compatibility.

Round-trip unit-tested (flat ~100x, random +0.3% worst case, run
boundaries). Verified on real hardware, image pixel-perfect incl. the
anti-aliased logo/gradient:
  original 21.5s -> v1.8 4.4s -> v1.9 ~1.6s for 1280x1024 true-colour.

events.title: bridge: WaitSelect-based writes + faster RX parse -> ~5x screenshots (v1.8)
events.message:
bridge: WaitSelect-based writes + faster RX parse -> ~5x screenshots (v1.8)

Daemon (net_io.c): replace the Delay(1) poll on EWOULDBLOCK with
WaitSelect() for writability. The old loop sent at most one socket
buffer's worth per 20ms tick, throttling bulk responses to ~one
screenshot row per tick (~370 KB/s). WaitSelect wakes the instant the
send buffer drains, so transfers run at link speed. Also set TCP_NODELAY
(don't hold each row waiting for an ACK) and enlarge SO_SNDBUF (more
queues before back-pressure) on the accepted client socket.

Host (serial_conn.py): the RX line handler rebuilt every line char by
char to strip control bytes - millions of iterations on the event loop
per capture. Fast-path lines that are already clean printable ASCII
(all hex pixel rows), falling back to the scan only for noisy lines.

Measured on real hardware (1280x1024 true-colour, ~7.9 MB):
21.5s -> 4.4s steady state. Image verified intact, no disconnects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: xphileby

events.title: bridge: don't drop TCP peer on transient backpressure (v1.7)
events.message:
bridge: don't drop TCP peer on transient backpressure (v1.7)

net_write() gave up and dropped the client after only ~50 EWOULDBLOCK
retries (~1s) and never reset that counter on partial progress. A full
true-colour screenshot is ~7.9 MB; any brief host-side stall during the
transfer (e.g. the read thread still settling right after a reconnect)
would exceed the 1s budget and the daemon would close the connection
mid-stream -> truncated capture (observed: 1024-row screenshot cut to 87
rows, coinciding with a 'disconnected' event in the host log).

Reset the stall counter whenever any bytes get through, so a slow-but-
moving link never trips it, and only give up after a long *sustained*
stall (~30s) with zero progress, i.e. the peer has really gone. Verified
with repeated full-frame captures immediately after a restart - the
previous failure window - with no disconnects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

bridge: true-colour RTG screenshots + read real video mode (v1.2)

The screen is actually 1280x1024 32-bit BGRA, but BitMap.Depth caps at 8 and
lied. Detect the real depth with GetBitMapAttr(BMA_DEPTH); for >8bpp read the
BGRA32 framebuffer straight from Planes[0] at the real BytesPerRow stride
(=width*4) and emit RGB rows (SCRRGB|row|hex). No cybergraphics needed (it is
absent from the toolchain) - Planes[0] is a CPU-readable linear framebuffer on
this Picasso96/VideoCore setup. Verified on real HW: full 1280x1024 truecolor
capture in ~5s, matching the actual desktop (blue gradient, colour icons).

Host: protocol.py parses SCRRGB; amiga_screenshot collects RGB rows; new
save_screenshot rgb_lines path renders truecolour. 8bpp(ReadPixelArray8)/
planar(AGA) paths still apply for those modes. Version bumped to v1.2.

events.title: bridge: enable FIOASYNC so the daemon wakes instantly on TCP data
events.message:
bridge: enable FIOASYNC so the daemon wakes instantly on TCP data

Setting SBTC_SIGIOMASK alone does not generate SIGIO on RoadShow; the
socket must also have async delivery enabled via IoctlSocket(FIOASYNC).
Without it the daemon only serviced the socket on its 200ms timer tick,
so every request paid up to ~200ms latency (PING RTT ~202ms; a 67-chunk
file push took ~14s). Enabling FIOASYNC on the listen + client sockets
makes the stack signal the task immediately.

Verified on real AmigaOS 3.2 + RoadShow (PiStorm):
  PING RTT       202ms -> 12ms   (~17x)
  push_file rate 1879  -> 23620 B/s (~13x; 26KB now 1.1s vs 14.1s)

events.title: bridge: poll transport each loop iteration so TCP can accept
events.message:
bridge: poll transport each loop iteration so TCP can accept

The SIGIO-driven drain never fired on RoadShow, so the daemon listened but
never called accept() — clients connected (backlog) but got no READY/replies.
Drain the transport unconditionally each loop iteration instead; the loop
wakes >=5x/sec on the 200ms timer, so accept/recv works without relying on
the stack's SIGIO. Verified end-to-end on AmigaOS 3.2 + RoadShow: client
loopback connect -> READY|1.0 -> PING -> PONG.

events.title: fix(spectrum): don't contend IR on the HALT refresh cycle
events.message:
fix(spectrum): don't contend IR on the HALT refresh cycle

The frame-loop HALT path probed contend(ir) during the M1 refresh (T3-T4),
over-contending HALT whenever I:R landed in contended RAM. The Z80 core's HALT
and normal-M1 paths deliberately do NOT contend the refresh — the ULA stalls
only on the opcode fetch (PC), and azesmbog's ULA128 timing test (real-hardware
calibrated) sets I=0xFE with contended bank 7 at 0xC000 specifically to assert
this. The two HALT paths disagreed; this aligns the frame loop with the core.

PC (fetch) contention is still applied via read8(pc); only the spurious refresh
IR probe is removed, and the slow path now fast-skips when PC is uncontended
regardless of IR.

The ULA128 test does HALT (IM2 frame sync) with I=0xFE, but that contention
only ever affected the sync HALT, never the OUT-chain measurement (no HALT in
the chain), and the interrupt is frame-fixed — so the stripe result is
unchanged either way, and removing it matches real hardware. Baseline passed on
48K/128K/+3; the post-fix run is still worth a confirming look.

fix(z80): reset SP to 0xFFFF (power-on convention)

RESET leaves SP undefined on real silicon, but the universal power-on
convention — and FUSE — is 0xFFFF, which some test ROMs assume. zx84 reset it
to 0. Align with the convention (the Z80 test harness already initialises
sp=0xFFFF, so this just makes the reset default match). Harmless for the
Spectrum, whose ROM loads SP before using the stack.

Scope limited to SP: AF/AF' are also 0xFFFF on real power-on but are left at 0
for now (the instruction-test harness doesn't override A/F, so changing them
would ripple through many tests — a separate triaged change).

Update the two tests that referenced the old sp=0 default.

events.title: docs(fdc): note seek/recalibrate ST0 reports HD=0 by design
events.message:
docs(fdc): note seek/recalibrate ST0 reports HD=0 by design

A reading of the datasheet (where the SEEK command byte carries an HDS field)
suggests cmdSeek should latch the head bit into the seek-complete ST0. It
should not: the uPD765A returns HD=0 in the SENSE_INTERRUPT status after a seek
regardless of HDS, and SEEK and RECALIBRATE behave identically. FUSE models this
explicitly (sense_int_res[0] = status_register[0] & 0xfb, 'return head always
0'), the +3 internal drive is single-sided, and software polls SE + unit after
a seek, never HD. Comment both handlers so the omission reads as intentional.

No behavioural change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: test(fdc): pin matching-DDAM multi-sector read result; document CM choices
events.message:
test(fdc): pin matching-DDAM multi-sector read result; document CM choices

Investigating report #6 (control mark not flagged abnormal) showed the b9a93ab
refactor changed a multi-sector READ_DELETED over all-matching-DDAM sectors from
ST2=0x40 (old: last sector's raw DSK flag leaked) to ST2=0x00 (command-relative
CM clears matching marks). That ST2=0x00 is hardware-correct and consistent with
the protections' single-sector DDAM checks — verified by booting Platoon
(Speedlock 1988) and Barbarian II (Speedlock 1989), both of which use that
multi-sector pattern and load fine.

Add a regression test pinning ST2=0x00 (+ EN at EOT) for that read so the
raw-flag leak can't return. No behavioural change — comments only in the core:
why subsequent-sector flags are command-relative, and that a non-final control
mark is reported as a normal termination by deliberate choice (one behavioural
reference, FUSE, flags it abnormal; no documented +3 protection exercises a

events.title: fix(fdc): terminate multi-sector reads at a CRC/control-mark sector
events.message:
fix(fdc): terminate multi-sector reads at a CRC/control-mark sector

advanceSector() overwrote exST1/exST2 from each new sector unconditionally,
so a data CRC error (ST1.DE/ST2.DD) or DDAM control mark on a *non-final*
sector of a multi-sector read was erased — finishExecution only ever saw the
last sector's flags. The real uPD765A stops AT such a sector and reports its
CHRN; it does not read on to R+1.

Add a non-final-sector termination guard in advanceSector (reads only, before
EOT): a data CRC error ends the read abnormally (ST0 IC=01); a command-relative
control mark (DDAM mismatch, SK=0 semantics) ends it normally with CM set, no
End-of-Cylinder. The final/single-sector case still falls through to the
existing EOT path, and the exSingleSector / overrun protection paths are
untouched.

Extract the per-sector flag logic (undersized / unreadable-weak /
command-relative CM) into sectorReadFlags(), shared by cmdReadWrite (first
sector) and advanceSector (subsequent + MT side-1 sectors) so every sector of
a read is handled identically — previously only the first sector got the
careful treatment and the rest were taken raw.

Rewrites the SK test (it encoded the old read-through bug) to assert correct
SK=0 termination, and adds a mid-stream-termination suite (CRC mid-read,
read-through-then-stop, DDAM under READ_DATA, READ_DELETED mark inversion,
final-sector EN unchanged). Full suite green; the Speedlock/US Gold protected
+3 titles (Operation Wolf, Batman, Chase H.Q., Gauntlet, Operation Thunderbolt)
still boot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat(fdc): implement 765A MT (multi-track) head switching
events.message:
feat(fdc): implement 765A MT (multi-track) head switching

READ_DATA/WRITE_DATA with the MT bit (bit 7) set were treated identically
to MT=0: the command terminated with End of Cylinder at the starting head's
EOT and never continued onto the other side. A cross-side read returned only
side 0 — a silent partial read reported as success.

advanceSector now, on reaching EOT with MT set on head 0 and a side-1 track
present, switches to head 1, reloads the side-1 track, restarts the sector
count at the command's first R, and continues; EN is only reported once side
1 also reaches EOT. Single-sided disks (no side-1 track) fall through to the
existing EN termination, so the common single-sided internal-drive case is
unchanged. Works for read and write.

Turns the old FUTURE-noted test green and adds multi-sector-per-head and
single-sided-fallback coverage.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(fdc): reject unimplemented 765A SCAN commands instead of faking a read
events.message:
fix(fdc): reject unimplemented 765A SCAN commands instead of faking a read

SCAN_EQUAL/LOW_EQ/HIGH_EQ were dispatched through cmdReadWrite() with
isWrite=false, so they streamed disk data out to the host (wrong data
direction — SCAN is host-writes-comparison-bytes) and never set ST2.SH/SN.
SCAN was effectively unimplemented but silently mis-executed as a read.

No known +3 software issues SCAN (the command was buggy on early NEC 765 /
Intel 8272 parts; +3DOS and CP/M Plus never adopted it), so rather than
implement it speculatively, reject it as an invalid command (ST0 IC=invalid),
log the opcode/unit/CHRN loudly, and latch a one-off flag the frame bridge
surfaces as a red toast: 'Unsupported 765A FDC SCAN command'. If real
software ever trips it, we'll see it and can implement it properly then.

Replaces the old test that documented the buggy passthrough with three that
pin the reject-and-notify contract.

The Nova VGA graphics card adapter for the Falcon has specific quirks:

Polish: add SPA flight-model and chargen point-buy algorithm sections

Two new sections in the Algorithm descriptions chapter -- the two deepest
remaining algorithm gaps a porter needs, both prose-only and render-free:

- 'The space-flight model' (SPA): the real-time rotation/thrust torus
  simulator that the rest of the turn-based game is not. Documents ship
  state (position + signed velocity + coarse-4 heading), the integration

  star/dock/collide hazards, and PLR_VESSELS as the only bridge to the
  castle endgame at 20 kills.

  PLR_HITS+2i, the 30-point pool with floor 10 / ceiling 25, the race and
  class bonus deltas applied after point-buy with no ceiling re-check (so a
  Dwarf Fighter can exceed 25 Strength), sex as cosmetic, and the derived
  starting values coming from the GAME_IMAGE snapshot (starting level 1).

The TM craft-interior renderer cannot be faithfully imaged from the
materials on hand. SHAPE_STEP/BLIT_LINE is a scanline run-length blitter
(not a self-contained vector interpreter like the DNG/SPA shape galleries
that rendered cleanly), and CRAFT_GFX is pre-rasterized hi-res byte runs,
not (dx,dy,pen) vectors. The stroker and ANIM_SETUP dereference ~13

shape-actor engine sets up at runtime -- verified by grep that none of
them is initialized in any of the 16 targets.

reconstructing the live cell-projection state, with no correctness
guarantee, which risks shipping a broken render. Left un-imaged and
documented in prose + the verbatim HEX blob + the SHAPE_STEP/BLIT_LINE

events.message:
Synthesis: the porting-notes chapter (all six synthesis types complete)

Fifth synthesis chapter and the capstone of the design layer: a catalogue
of the recurring 6502/Apple-II idioms, what each means, and its portable
replacement.

- Self-modifying code: patched-JSR/JMP dispatch (a function-pointer
  table), patched operands as variables (including the stale-on-disk
  STALE_FFFF sentinel that running code overwrites), and patched opcodes
  toggling actors (a boolean).
- Multi-entry routines: the CLC / .byte $B0 / SEC carry dual-entry and the
  .byte $2C BIT-absolute skip, both portable as defaulted parameters.
- Inline-argument calling conventions (JSR followed by data) as ordinary
  function arguments, with the disassembler trap they create.
- Numbers and tables: binary quantities with BCD displays, precomputed
  squares/perspective/row-address tables (keep the contents where they
  encode tuning, drop them where they are only speed), little-endian
  16-bit pairs.
- Machine and OS seams: soft switches, the VBL beat (and the mouse-card-
  as-VBL trick), the file library and overlay model, the hooked reset
  vector -- none change visible behaviour.

The synthesis layer now has all six section types the synthesize skill
calls for: overview/architecture, data structures, algorithms, rendering,
and porting notes. Prose-only: all 16 targets byte-perfect, hygiene green,

events.title: Synthesis: the Algorithm descriptions chapter
events.message:
Synthesis: the Algorithm descriptions chapter

Third synthesis chapter, after the data-structure reference: the game's
non-trivial mechanics as platform-independent pseudocode plus design
intent -- the parts a porter cannot recover by translating instructions.

- The two PRNGs: the library lagged-additive generator (atmospheric,
  reseeded from cursor-flash timing, genuinely unpredictable) versus the
  dungeon Fibonacci seed stepper (A' = A+B+9, B' = A), deterministic so
  every dungeon level regenerates identically.
- The turn economy: food spent in BCD hundredths via TICK, faster
  transports costing less food and less time per step.
- Procedural dungeon generation: the position-derived seed, the five
  generation passes (lattice edges 6/6/8, walls+force-fields 2*level+1,
  containers, fixed cells and parity-swapped ladders, monsters), and the
  cell-byte nibble packing with its blocking rule.
- The dungeon ray marcher: stepping the facing vector, inspecting the
  ahead and two side cells via exact +/-90 integer rotation, with all the
  perspective in the DNG_GEOM table; plus the depth-scaled vector shapes.
- Shop pricing: base cost = item_index squared (a squares table) scaled
  by a charisma/wisdom/intelligence haggle factor.
- Monster spawning (tier-gated on a rising difficulty bar, hp and exp
  scaling from tier) and greedy integer-sqrt pursuit with melee-vs-armour.

events.message:
TM fully decomposed: the time-machine endgame, byte-perfect

TM ($8956-$AD11, 8123 bytes) is the final overlay -- the endgame battle
against Mondain inside the time machine, reached when CAS sets TM_REVEAL.
Decomposed across 37 chunks (27 plated routines): the fixed-point math +
BCD-print suite, TM_ENTRY + gem-socket setup, the launch/time-travel
narration, combat-scene setup, the main loop + patched-JSR dispatch,
TM_ATTACK, TM_CAST + the 11-entry spell table + magic missile + the
INTERFICIO-NUNC backfire, TM_GET (destroy the gem), the interior-grid move
handlers, Mondain's AI (approach/melee/cast with 3 spells), TM_DEATH, the
scene tick + cell helpers, the wireframe SHAPE_STEP stroker + BLIT_LINE
blitter + projection tables, the cell grid, and CRAFT_GFX.

The win condition is now pinned in code end to end: Mondain is shielded by
GEM_HP=$7EF4 (16-bit, 1000). Striking him drains it via HIT_RESOLVE, but
killing him before the gem is gone only yields " ...or is he?" (he
regenerates). TM_GET on the gem cell -> "The Gem is DESTROYED!" sets
GEM_GONE; then GEM_HP->0 -> "THOU ART VICTORIOUS!" -> TM_VICTORY loads NIF,
hooks Control-RESET, and melts the screen into the victory image. The
SPA->CAS->TM win loop is fully decompiled at every link.

Names introduced: TM_ENTRY, TM_ATTACK/CAST/GET/MOVE_*/PASS/etc. (TM_*
prefix -- the bare CMD_* collide with OUT/DNG), HIT_RESOLVE, TM_VICTORY,
GEM_HP/GEM_GONE, MONDAIN_TURN/MELEE/CAST/HIT, the CELL_STATE/CELL_COL grid,
SHAPE_STEP/BLIT_LINE/PROJ_TBL renderer, POPUP_TEXT/_NF, DRAW_SOCKET.

events.title: GEN fully decomposed: the new-game overlay and its disk formatter, byte-perfect
events.message:
GEN fully decomposed: the new-game overlay and its disk formatter, byte-perfect

Decompose the GEN overlay (8932 bytes, $8956) into 37 literate chunks:
the title menu and its two paths (generate new character / continue
previous game), the character generator (point-buy attribute editor,
race/sex/class/name pickers with their bonus tables, the save prompt),
the local text/window helpers, and -- the intricate half -- a complete
bundled disk formatter.

The formatter is two layers and the only code in the game that bypasses
the MLIB library to touch the drive directly: RWTS_FORMAT ($A800), a
hand-rolled Disk II RWTS that steps the arm 35 tracks and writes 16
6-and-2 GCR sectors per track with read-back verification through the
raw $C0xx soft switches; and FORMAT_VOLUME ($A119), a ProDOS
volume-directory writer that lays down the four directory blocks and the
allocation bitmap via the MLI. DO_FORMAT brackets both with a zero-page
save/restore.

Pins the code/data interleave: the file block-copies the 13-page
GAME_IMAGE to $6000 to start a new game, FORMAT_VOLUME code follows in
the same pages, and BOOT_IMAGE ($A3C5-$A7B7) is a ProDOS boot loader
stamped onto the new disk -- pure data in GEN's address space, emitted
as HEX. Chargen math recovered: six 16-bit stats, a 30-point pool,
floor 10 / ceil 25, and the canonical race/class attribute bonuses.

events.title: feat(mcp): reset_trap — break on reboot to 0x0000 with culprit + stack
events.message:
feat(mcp): reset_trap — break on reboot to 0x0000 with culprit + stack

Custom loaders treat a tape edge-timeout as a fatal read error and
RET/JP/RST 0 to 0x0000 (the ROM reset); runaway crashes land there too.
reset_trap arms a hook on the per-instruction onTrap path that breaks the
instant PC reaches 0x0000 via control flow (guarded so the power-on boot
PC=0 can't false-fire), capturing the culprit instruction, the unwound
return-address chain, and the paging state. Surfaced inline in run /
step_frame / continue, and included in continue's armed-trap guard.

events.title: fix(tape): emit a terminating edge at end of tape so custom loaders don't reboot
events.message:
fix(tape): emit a terminating edge at end of tape so custom loaders don't reboot

A custom turbo/speedlock loader reading the final bit of the last block
needs one more edge after the last data pulse to terminate its pulse-
timing loop. Mid-tape that edge comes from the next block's pilot; at
end-of-tape with a zero/short pause the deck froze the level instantly,
so the loader hunted for an edge that never came, timed out, and (for
turbo loaders like Thundercats 128K) RET-chained to 0x0000 — rebooting
the machine.

enterPause now holds a ~945T terminating pause with a low-flip when no
block follows, guaranteeing the closing edge. This matches FUSE/
libspectrum end-of-tape behaviour. Mid-tape zero-pause blocks (continuous
multi-block loaders) are deliberately left untouched — their next block
supplies the edge.

Adds regression tests covering both the terminating edge on a final
pause=0 block and the unchanged mid-tape zero-pause transition.

feat(mcp): library tool — load catalog titles by exact name with load verdict

Adds an mcp__zx84__library tool that reproduces the app's one-click Library
play headlessly: resolve a title against the ZXDB catalog (reusing planLoad/
fileUrls/resolveGame from src so the MCP makes the same model/file decisions as
the UI), download CDN-first then via the file-proxy Worker, unzip, mount, and
arm the auto-boot trap. Supports file= (pick an inner archive member), id=
(disambiguate duplicate titles), and refresh= (re-fetch the catalog).

With frames=N it runs the loader to a pass/fail verdict using the end-of-tape
oracle: a load FAILS when the tape reaches its end while the CPU is still
polling the EAR port (loader stranded), and LOADS when EAR polling stops.

- mcp/catalog.ts: Node-side catalog fetch/cache/gunzip + findGames/suggestTitles
- mcp/loader.ts: bootWaitPc, mountAndArm (faithful to autoBootLoad), runLoadVerdict
- mcp/tools/media.ts: register the library tool

events.title: MI.U1 text-output cluster RE'd: MSG_PRINT, STR_NTH, PUTCH, PRINT_HEX
events.message:
MI.U1 text-output cluster RE'd: MSG_PRINT, STR_NTH, PUTCH, PRINT_HEX

Round 5. Call census across all seven overlays identified the engine
API band ($80xx-$84xx); the most-called routine, $8119 (349 calls),
is MSG_PRINT. Decomposed $8037-$8143 out of the engine stub:

- MSG_PRINT/MSG_AT: inline zero-terminated text after the JSR,
  $7F+n = tab; the convention behind every prompt in the game.
- STR_NTH/STR_FIRST/STR_NTH_CAP: print the Xth string of a packed
  table (inline table pointer; last char of each string carries the
  high bit). CAP_FLAG doubles as first-letter state.
- PUTCH layout codes: '|' newline, '~' NL+col1, '}' conditional
  NL+col1 - explains the |}~ characters throughout the string data.
- PRINT_HEX/PRINT_DIGIT, NEWLINE/CR with TEXT_SCROLL at $1592,
  WIN_SHRINK; font blitter FONT_DRAW at $15B0 lives in low RAM,
  installed by MAKE.INDATA (EQU stubs pending that RE).

events.title: U1.SYSTEM launcher and the $B700 file library, byte-perfect
events.message:
U1.SYSTEM launcher and the $B700 file library, byte-perfect

Round 1. u1system verifies 1682/1682. The launcher prints the Origin
banner, copies page-one helpers (inline-string printer, reset
trampoline, BRUN-startup-file) to $0100, installs a resident MLI
wrapper library at $B700-$BAFF (protected via the system bitmap),
establishes the ProDOS prefix (GET_PREFIX, else derived from the
launch path at $0280), and BRUNs U1.INTRO.

The library is the game's entire disk interface: 20 JSR vectors with
inline arguments (zero-terminated path text or pointer variants) for
BLOAD/BLOAD_AT/BSAVE/BRUN/SET_PREFIX/DESTROY/QUIT/READ_BLOCK/
WRITE_BLOCK/PARSE/raw-MLI, BIN-type and 64K checks, MLI error
translation to game codes, parameter blocks in page $BA, file buffer
at $BB00. RORG chunks carry run-time addresses for the relocated
code. All hygiene metrics zero; PDF builds (70 pages).

events.title: refactor(plus3): port +3 disk protection detection to the staged dskmanager-rust flow
events.message:
refactor(plus3): port +3 disk protection detection to the staged dskmanager-rust flow

Replace the flat priority-list of independent detectors with the
fingerprinting flow from dskmanager-rust: T0 ASCII signatures -> T0
geometry classification -> per-class resolver -> Track 1 -> high-track
probes -> mid-disk sweep -> stripped-FDC / unknown fallbacks.

Speedlock is now recognised by geometry (deleted-data marks, 5x1024 data
side, big weak sectors) rather than ASCII signatures; CPC vs +3 is
distinguished by the T0 sector-ID base, giving Hexagon/Speedlock (CPC)
vs +3 variants. A lone FDC error on a high track of an otherwise-clean
disk is treated as dump noise (returns '') rather than Unknown. Output
is the bare scheme name. Test suite rewritten to the new flow (74 cases).

events.title: fix(ay): anti-alias ultrasonic AY tones to kill the title-screen whine
events.message:
fix(ay): anti-alias ultrasonic AY tones to kill the title-screen whine

A channel parked at tone period 0 (e.g. Chase HQ II's title screen) clamps to
period 1 ≈ 110 kHz. Point-sampling that ultrasonic square at the output rate
aliased it down into the audible band as a high-pitched whine; on real hardware
the channel is inaudible.

Add a Sound-panel Anti-alias selector with four modes: Filter (mute an
ultrasonic period≤1 channel — the new default), Box filter (per-sample
averaging), Low-pass, and None (raw point-sampling). The AY core default stays
'none' so the VGMPlay conformance tests keep deterministic output; the app
applies the saved mode on machine creation.

events.title: refactor(tape): remove edge-loading acceleration entirely
events.message:
refactor(tape): remove edge-loading acceleration entirely

The fingerprint-based edge accelerator forged a loader's exit state (B,
carry, EAR bit) from a guessed edge length. That synthesis is inherently
loader-specific, so it loaded some titles correctly and corrupted others
(e.g. Bleepload: wrong bytes, garbled screen, game never starts) — an
unwinnable game of whack-a-mole.

Delete it wholesale: edge-loader.ts, the §4/§5 tap.ts plumbing
(onEdgeScheduled, inAcceleration, singleEdge, edge-flag categorisation),
the "Fast edge loading" toggle + setting, and docs/edge-loading.md.

Loading is now the standard, reliable model used by mainstream emulators:
 - Fast ROM loading (LD-BYTES trap) for standard blocks
 - Turbo while loading runs the REAL loader code faster — cannot corrupt
What remains is a minimal LoaderDetector (auto play/stop only) that never
touches CPU/tape data, just decides when the tape runs and exposes
loaderActive to engage turbo.

events.title: feat(ui): hold status LEDs on for 500ms past last activity
events.message:
feat(ui): hold status LEDs on for 500ms past last activity

The activity LEDs (AY-3-8912, RAINBOW, EAR, TAPE, BEEP, KEY, KEMPSTON,
MOUSE, DISK) were painted straight from a single frame's activity
counters, so bursty events (AY register writes, attribute rewrites, EAR
samples, port reads) strobed the indicators on and off.

Latch each activity LED on for 500ms past its most recent activity via a
shared ledLatched() helper: anything that touched it in the last 500ms
keeps it lit. Setters still run every frame but Solid dedupes equal
values, so an LED transitions only on an activity edge or 500ms after
activity ceases — instant-on, smooth-off, no flicker. Applied on both the
Spectrum and CPC LED paths. tapeTurbo and the transcribe-mode half of
TEXT stay immediate (sustained state, not bursts). resetLedActivity()
clears the hold on model switch.

events.title: fix(tape): make Fast edge loading accelerate standalone, not just under turbo
events.message:
fix(tape): make Fast edge loading accelerate standalone, not just under turbo

The edge accelerator did `cpu.tStates += adv`, inserting the full real
pulse length (~2168T pilot) into the CPU clock per skipped edge. At the
realtime frame cap that fits only ~32 pilot edges/frame — exactly
realtime — so Fast edge loading gave zero standalone speed-up and only
ever multiplied the turbo frame-rate. It also hand-advanced the tape AND
bumped the clock, so the per-instruction advanceTapeTo() double-advanced
the tape, racing it ahead of the loader and (via the fromAcceleration=
false edge callback) invalidating the length pipeline every other IN,
desyncing the forged-bit decode.

Make it a genuine time-skip per docs/edge-loading.md §4.5: advance the
tape across exactly one edge without moving cpu.tStates, then re-anchor
the host tape clock (new optional EdgeLoaderHost.syncTapeClock) so the
catch-up advance doesn't double-count. Fast edge loading now accelerates
on its own (~4-6x, bounded by the ROM's own LD B,$16/DJNZ per-edge
delay); turbo still stacks on top for near-instant loads.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: perf(turbo): drive turbo off a MessageChannel pump, not rAF
events.message:
perf(turbo): drive turbo off a MessageChannel pump, not rAF

Turbo execution was bound to requestAnimationFrame: capped at the vsync
rate and deliberately using only ~70% of each frame interval (overrunning
the rAF deadline makes the browser throttle rAF down). That ~30% idle per
vsync was a hard ceiling.

Drive turbo from a MessageChannel postMessage loop instead. Each burst
runs frames for a fixed wall-clock budget (TURBO_PUMP_BUDGET_MS = 8ms)
then re-arms via postMessage, which re-fires in well under a millisecond
and isn't vsync-locked — so bursts run back-to-back, using the main
thread near-continuously. The rAF loop now only renders the latest frame
and runs the 60Hz UI upkeep. Measured ~1.6x (80x -> 130x) and no longer
capped by the display refresh rate.

runTurboBurst now takes an explicit budgetMs (the pump sets cadence), so
the Spectrum's adaptive rAF-interval budget math is gone. Breakpoints hit
mid-burst are left set for the next rAF onFrame to pause on (both Spectrum
and CPC pause paths verified). Channel torn down in destroy().

feat(library): one-click play with model-aware auto-boot

Resolve each catalog entry into explicit 48K-tape / 128K-tape / disk
slots (model implicit in the slot), and pick the load target + boot
method per machine in planLoad:

The 48K loader drives the real key matrix (J, SYM+P, SYM+P, ENTER) with
debounce gaps — a cold jump to LD-BYTES (0x0556) loads nothing because
IX/DE/A' are undefined and the BASIC loader never runs. Repeating the
" key needs a longer release gap so the ROM re-debounces it.

the trap never fired). A tape-only game on a +3/+2A now ejects any disk
in A: first, so the Loader falls through to the cassette loader instead

build(catalog): keep per-model tapes, disk sides, and the ZXDB id

ZXDB tracks machine type per download, and an entry can carry distinct
48K and 128K tapes plus multi-side disks (Side A/B, Disk 1/2). The build
previously collapsed each entry to one tape + one disk and dropped the
machine type, so those variants were lost.

Now emit, per game:

  d / ds[]    disk (side A) plus extra [link, label] sides

Genuine disk sides ((SideA), (Disk1SideB)) are kept with labels derived
from the filename; fix/alt re-dumps ((Fixed), _2, (alt), (lightgun)) are
collapsed to one. Model is now implicit in the slot (f=48, k=128,
d/ds=+3), replacing the explicit m field.

events.title: fix(z80): contend internal cycles of indexed and INIR/INDR instructions
events.message:
fix(z80): contend internal cycles of indexed and INIR/INDR instructions

Indexed (DD/FD) instructions advanced their post-displacement internal
cycles with bare tStates increments, skipping the contention probes that
exec-main and exec-ed apply to every internal cycle. IX/IY-heavy code in
contended RAM mistimed.

- LD r,(IX+d), ALU A,(IX+d), INC/DEC (IX+d): 5 internal cycles now
  contend at the d-byte address (PC-1); INC/DEC's read->write internal
  cycle also now contends at the operand address.
- LD (IX+d),r: was +4/write/+4 (write@T+15); now 5 internal/write/+3
  (write@T+16), matching the read variant.
- LD (IX+d),n: was +1/write/+4; now 2 internal @ n-byte/write/+3.
- INIR/INDR: the write's completion 3T now precedes the 5 internal
  cycles, so their probes land at T+16..20 instead of 3T early at T+13.

Totals are unchanged (19/23/16/21T); only contention-probe placement and
peripheral-visible write timing differ. OTIR/OTDR already placed their
internal cycles after the I/O cycle and are untouched.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(z80): no contention probe during the M1 refresh cycle
events.message:
fix(z80): no contention probe during the M1 refresh cycle

Every M1 (and each prefix fetch) probed ULA contention at the refresh
address IR during T3-T4. The ULA only stalls the CPU on MREQ cycles and
the refresh is not one — FUSE models an opcode fetch as a single 4T
contended read at PC with no IR probe. The bogus probe was invisible in
normal use (I=0x3F points at ROM) but azesmbog's hardware-calibrated
ULA128 timing test runs with I=0xFE while contended bank 7 is paged at
0xC000, so every instruction in the display fetch window gained phantom
delays (NOPs 8T, OUT (C),r up to 26T), smearing the test pattern from
the paper area down. Simulating the test's full OUT chain against the
TAP bytes shows 97.4% line-to-line stripe coherence with pure I/O
contention extras and no IR refresh probe — the real-hardware model.

Internal no-MREQ cycles at IR (PUSH, DJNZ, RET cc, RST, LD A,I, ADD HL,
block I/O) are genuine and keep their probes.

TS_SCREEN_128=14361 against TS_SCREEN_48=14335 — a +26 model delta,
which in our first-pixel convention is 14336 + 26 = 14362. With 14364

events.title: fix(contention): 128K display origin and measured floating-bus sequence
events.message:
fix(contention): 128K display origin and measured floating-bus sequence

Two hardware-fidelity fixes:

- TIMING_128K.displayOrigin was 14362, derived by analogy with the 48K's
  contentionStart+1 relationship. The 128K has 63 lines above the display,
  so the first pixel is at 63 x 228 = 14364 (contentionStart + 3T), the
  same relationship the +2A entry already used. The old value rendered
  128K border/multicolor effects 2T (4 pixels) early.

- floatingBusRead modelled each 4T cell as pixel,pixel,attr,attr with the
  bus driven on all 128 fetch T-states. Measured hardware (FUSE, Sinclair
  Wiki) interleaves two character columns per 8T block — pixel n, attr n,
  pixel n+1, attr n+1 — then releases the bus for the idle half, which
  reads 0xFF. Tests rewritten to pin the documented sequence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix(contention): anchor IN-side I/O contention at the IORQ cycle start
events.message:
fix(contention): anchor IN-side I/O contention at the IORQ cycle start

The Ferranti four-case I/O contention rule is defined relative to the
start of the IORQ cycle, but applyIOContention probed from whatever
cpu.tStates was when the port handler fired. OUTs fire at cycle start
(correct); INs fire 3T into the cycle — the late sample point tape edge
loaders need — so every IN's contention probes were anchored 3T late on
48K/128K/+2. applyIOContention now takes the caller's offset into the
cycle and walks its probes from the true cycle start, decoupling the
contention anchor from the data sample point (the FUSE approach).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(z80): I/O cycle timing, R on interrupt ack, CPxR repeat flags
events.message:
fix(z80): I/O cycle timing, R on interrupt ack, CPxR repeat flags

Four hardware-accuracy fixes to the Z80 core:

- OUTI/OUTD/OTIR/OTDR emitted the port write at T+9 instead of T+12;
  the (HL) read cycle's 3T were lumped into a trailing +=7. The OUT now
  lands at the start of the real IORQ cycle, and the OTIR/OTDR repeat's
  five internal contention probes now run at the correct T-states.
- IN r,(C) and INI now tick 3T before portIn so the sample lands late
  in the IORQ window, matching the IN A,(n) convention that tape edge
  loaders depend on (ED 78-based loaders previously sampled 3T early).
- interrupt() and nmi() now increment R: the acknowledge is an M1 cycle,
  so R advances like any opcode fetch (bit 7 preserved).
- CPIR/CPDR repeating iterations now take F5/F3 from the high byte of
  the rewound PC (Banks/hoglet 2018 block-flags research), matching the
  LDIR/INIR/OTIR repeat paths. zexall cannot catch this; z80test does.

Instruction totals are unchanged (12/16/21T); only intra-instruction

events.title: fix(tape): accelerate ROM-trap loads of oversize blocks
events.message:
fix(tape): accelerate ROM-trap loads of oversize blocks

The LD-BYTES trap declined any block whose payload length didn't exactly
equal DE, so tapes carrying blocks one byte longer than requested fell
back to real-time loading. The real 48K ROM reads exactly DE bytes plus
a parity byte and ignores trailing bytes, so such blocks load fine on
hardware — e.g. the Paperboy (1989, MCM) re-release ships an 18-byte
header read with DE=17, and data blocks one byte over their declared
length. Decline only when the block is shorter than DE; copy DE bytes
and consume the whole block otherwise. Looser than FUSE's exact check,
but the trap doesn't verify parity anyway so fidelity is unchanged.

test: acceleration reliability regression tests

Coverage for all four acceleration fixes:

- dt=0 edge boundary: verify that when tStatesToNextEdge() returns 0,
  the acceleration still crosses the edge and advances phase.
- Single-edge advance: verify singleEdge=true stops after one edge
  while singleEdge=false crosses all edges within the advance window.
- Post-acceleration auto-stop suppression: verify synthetic B=0xFE
  does not poison auto-stop — lastBRead fix keeps bDiff in-shape.
- Pipeline reset on play-state change: verify onTapePlayStateChange
  clears all four length pipeline fields plus accelMode.
- Per-signature auto-stop thresholds: verify Speedlock (threshold 4),
  Alkatraz (threshold 3), and unknown/default (threshold 2) all stop
  the tape only after the correct number of out-of-shape reads, and
  respect per-signature gap tolerances (2000T for Speedlock, 1500T for
  Alkatraz, 1000T default).

events.title: fix: tape deck single-edge advance for surgical acceleration
events.message:
fix: tape deck single-edge advance for surgical acceleration

Add a singleEdge parameter to TapeDeck.advance(). When true, the method
processes at most one edge boundary and returns, preventing the surgical
loader accelerator from crossing multiple pulse boundaries in a single
step. Without this, dt can span across short sync pulses into the data
phase, causing the two-slot length pipeline to receive the wrong edge
category and desync the accelerator.

The edge-loader's accelerate() now calls tape.advance(dt, true) so each
acceleration step processes exactly one edge.
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix: edge loader acceleration reliability
events.message:
fix: edge loader acceleration reliability

Three fixes for the edge-based tape acceleration system:

1. Handle dt=0 in accelerate(): when tStatesToNextEdge() returns 0 (the
   edge is exactly due), the old code skipped tape advancement but still
   mutated CPU state — the loader would re-read the same edge. Now
   advance at least 1 T-state so the edge fires and earBit toggles.

2. Fix lastBRead after acceleration: the old code set lastBRead to the
   synthetic B value (0xFE or 0x00), which poisoned auto-stop — the
   next real IN would compute a wild bDiff and, combined with any
   >1000T byte-processing gap, auto-stop would pause the tape mid-load.
   Now predict the expected B at re-entry (+1 for INCREASING, -1 for
   DECREASING) so the first bDiff after acceleration stays in-shape.

3. Reset edge pipeline on tape play-state change: onTapePlayStateChange
   now clears lengthKnown1/2 and lengthLong1/2, preventing stale edge
   data from a previous block contaminating the pipeline after stop.
events.author: damieng

events.title: feat(cpc): CRTC frame-restart on live R4 enables rupture/split-screen
events.message:
feat(cpc): CRTC frame-restart on live R4 enables rupture/split-screen

The CRTC now re-reads R4 (vertical total) at each character-row boundary and
restarts its internal frame when reached — resetting the row/raster counters
and reloading the memory address from R12/R13 live. Reducing R4 (or R7)
mid-frame therefore restarts the frame early with the current screen base,
which is how hardware rupture / split-screen works: the lines below the
restart are re-based to a new address. R5 vertical-total-adjust scanlines are
also now sequenced before the restart.

This is transparent to standard programming: for R4=38/R9=7/R5=0 the restart
coincides with the host frame loop's 312-line count, so MA progression and
frame timing are identical (verified: real os6128 boots pixel-perfect,
tStatesPerFrame=79872). R12/R13 stays frame-latched (correct 6845 behaviour;
per-frame hardware scrolling already worked) — a mid-row R13 write does not
shift the current row.

Adds tests for the restart point, R5 adjust, mid-frame R4 rupture with
R12/R13 reload, and the no-mid-row-reseed invariant.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: docs(cpc): correct CAS READ trap scope to headers-only
events.message:
docs(cpc): correct CAS READ trap scope to headers-only

Verified the instant-load trap against a real CDT (2048.cdt) + real os6128
firmware via headless boot. The record layout and CRC convention are
correct (extracts the real filename + full 2K data records). But only the
64-byte file HEADER actually instant-loads: making the header instant
shifts the firmware's cassette timing so the following data block pulse-
plays past before its own CAS READ is reached, and the trap then declines
on the drifted block. Bulk file data still pulse-loads via tapeTurbo.

Corrects the previously overclaiming comments (which said the layout was
unverified and implied full-load coverage) in cpc-tape-loader.ts and
cpc-machine.ts. A true data instant-load needs the pulse engine and trap
to share tape position without starving the firmware's inter-block edge
sync — a deeper rework, attempted and reverted (see project notes).

Adds spec-derived tests for the previously-untested CPC raster core:
- CRTC: frame geometry (64x312), R5 vertical adjust, R12:R13 decode,

events.title: fix(cpc): cassette motor is PPI Port C bit 4, not bit 5
events.message:
fix(cpc): cassette motor is PPI Port C bit 4, not bit 5

The CPC 8255 PPI assigns Port C bit 4 (0x10) to cassette motor control;
bit 5 (0x20) is cassette write data. We had the motor on bit 5. Confirmed
against Caprice32 (cap32.cpp: `tape_motor = val & 0x10`, read back on
bit 4). Low blast radius — tape advance is cadence-gated, not motor-gated,
and the 6128 firmware never spins the motor relay — but tapeMotorOn (UI
LED, snapshot Port-C readback) was driven off the wrong bit.

events.title: feat(cpc): instant firmware tape loading; unify tape-loader naming
events.message:
feat(cpc): instant firmware tape loading; unify tape-loader naming

CPC instant load: a normal BASIC `RUN"` never executes the &BCA1 RAM
jumpblock — the firmware reaches its cassette block-read routine
internally (CAS IN CHAR refilling its buffer). Trap that internal routine
instead, located by a version-independent signature scan of the lower OS
ROM (os464/os664/os6128), re-scanned when ROMs change. On a successful
load, resume in the routine's teardown tail (entry + 0x0D) with the
post-read register state (IX = buffer, DE = page-adjusted count, carry =
success) so the firmware runs its own motor-off / PPI restore.

Naming: unify the three tape acceleration features across CPC and ZX as
Fast ROM loading / Fast edge loading / Turbo while loading. Rename the
settings signals (tapeFastRom/tapeFastEdge/tapeTurbo) and the machine
field (tapeInstantLoad → tapeFastRom); persisted setting keys are kept
stable so saved prefs survive. Surface all applicable toggles per machine
(wire up the previously-orphaned edge toggle; expose Turbo on the CPC).

events.title: fix(tape): instant loader corrupted stack on partial LD-BYTES entry
events.message:
fix(tape): instant loader corrupted stack on partial LD-BYTES entry

The ROM-trap instant loader fired at 0x056C and unconditionally popped
two words, assuming the 0x053F (SA/LD-RET) filler that LD-BYTES pushes
at 0x0561 is always on the stack. Loaders that CALL into LD-BYTES after
that push (e.g. Solseed enters at 0x0562) never stack the 0x053F, so the
top word is the caller's real return address. The extra pop discarded it
and jumped PC to garbage, unwinding back to the BASIC main loop which
then HALTed with interrupts disabled -- a permanent hang.

Pop the 0x053F only when it is actually present, matching FUSE (sets
PC=0x05E2 and lets the ROM's bare RET pop once) and ZEsarUX (single
pop_valor() at its 0x0562 trap). The normal LOAD path is unchanged.

Adds the MGT +D disk system for the 48K/128K/+2 (and, per models.ts, +2A/+3):
a WD1772 FDC, the 8KB G+DOS shadow ROM, and 8KB +D RAM overlaid into slot 0.

loadPlusDDisk), io-ports.ts (port wiring + RAM write gate), emulator.ts

events.title: fix(cpc): make Multiface Two Return survive mid-session enable
events.message:
fix(cpc): make Multiface Two Return survive mid-session enable

Two related fixes to the MF2 freeze cartridge's I/O shadow (the snoop of
write-only chip registers the toolkit's Return replays to restore state):

- Freeze recording while paged in. The shadow must hold the *interrupted
  program's* chip state, captured at STOP. Recording continued while the
  toolkit ran, so its own OUTs (UI mode/colours/ROM paging) clobbered the
  shadow and Return restored the toolkit's state — wrong mode/RAM config,
  crash. The real MF2 PAL gates capture the same way (cf. Caprice32).

- Seed the shadow when the cartridge is enabled mid-session. The PAL only
  captures while fitted, so switching MF2 on after boot left the shadow
  blank and Return crashed. seedShadow() reconstructs it from the live
  Gate Array / CRTC / ROM-select / PPI state by replaying the equivalent
  OUTs through recordOut, so STOP->Return restores the running program
  without a reboot.

events.title: refactor: extract shared frame driver into BaseMachine
events.message:
refactor: extract shared frame driver into BaseMachine

Spectrum and CpcMachine held two near-identical copies of the rAF frame
loop, wall-clock pacing, audio back-pressure, start/stop/destroy/tick/
runUntil lifecycle, and the MCP debug-surface fields. That scaffolding
now lives once in BaseMachine; both machines extend it.

Each machine supplies only what differs via hooks: runFrame(),
framePixels(), inTurbo(). The turbo path legitimately diverges, so it is
an overridable method — the base default is the CPC's fixed budget, and
the Spectrum overrides runTurboBurst()/exitTurbo() with its adaptive,
rAF-cadence-aware budget and accuracy/contention swap. Behaviour is
preserved verbatim.

Also dedupe the three emulator.ts mouse helpers behind one activeMice()
accessor instead of repeating the asSpectrum/asCpc branch.

Note: the live rAF frameLoop is not covered by the test suite (tests
drive tick()/runUntil()), so turbo/audio pacing wants a dev-server smoke
check.

events.title: feat(cpc): add Kempston and AMX mouse support
events.message:
feat(cpc): add Kempston and AMX mouse support

Reuse the existing Mouse pane for the CPC. Hardware port maps from CPCWiki.

Kempston: ports differ from the Spectrum (X=&FBEE, Y=&FBEF, buttons=&FAEF;
decoded on A10/A8/A4/A0, clear of the FDC) and the button bits are swapped
(bit0=right, bit1=left, no middle). KempstonMouse gained a ctor button-bit
map so the shared class serves both machines.

AMX: a different device from the Spectrum's Z80-PIO AMX — it rides keyboard
matrix line 9 (joystick 0), pulsing a direction bit LOW per mickey and
retiring one mickey per line-9 deselect. New CpcAmxMouse + a CpcKeyboard.amx
hook. The per-direction backlog is capped at one frame's drain so the pointer
stops promptly instead of coasting (the AMX's ~300Hz poll rate otherwise
leaves queued movement draining for ~0.7s after the mouse stops).

Machine-aware emulator mouse helpers; MOUSE LED wired for CPC.

Tests: tests/cpc/cpc-mouse.test.ts (button layouts, pulse/consume semantics,
keyboard integration, port decode, backlog cap).

events.title: feat(cpc): add Multiface Two (freeze cartridge + STOP/NMI)
events.message:
feat(cpc): add Multiface Two (freeze cartridge + STOP/NMI)

Add the Romantic Robot Multiface Two to the CPC, mirroring the Spectrum
Multiface: a Hardware-pane toggle and a red STOP button (NMI to 0x0066).

The cartridge is an 8K ROM + 8K RAM in one persistent 16K buffer overlaid
into slot 0 (ROM 0x0000-0x1FFF, RAM 0x2000-0x3FFF) via new CpcMemory
setSlot0Overlay/clearSlot0Overlay. Paging is OUT-decoded (&FEE8 in / &FEEA
out). The ROM (cpc-multiface2.rom) is fetched from the CDN and cached.

Crucially the cartridge snoops every OUT into a RAM shadow at the hardware
offsets (GA/CRTC/upper-ROM/PPI), because those chips are write-only and the
toolkit's Return reprograms them from that shadow; without it Return
restored garbage and crashed the CPC.

(↑ at 0x5E, caret displaced to 0xA0), Greek letters, box/block graphics and
arrows. ASCII codes are matched first so letters/digits always win a glyph
collision with a high-range graphic, leaving real text uncorrupted. Codes
with no Unicode equivalent (blank mosaic, DEL checker, 0xEF, 0xFC/FD) are
left unmapped so they read as spaces.

Source for the mapping: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amstrad_CPC_character_set,
cross-checked against the 6128 lower-ROM font glyphs.

Drop text-panel from SPECTRUM_ONLY_PANES so the Text (OCR) settings pane is
available in CPC mode — its font/size/offset/scale settings already feed the
CPC overlay path in Screen.tsx.

events.title: feat(cpc): add mode-aware screen OCR / TEXT overlay
events.message:
feat(cpc): add mode-aware screen OCR / TEXT overlay

The CPC renders text through a fixed 8x8 font in the lower OS ROM
(&3800, 256 glyphs MSB-first), so OCR is deterministic rather than the
Spectrum's heuristic font hunt. New CpcScreenText decodes each 8x8 cell
mode-aware (mode 0/1/2 -> 4/2/1 bytes/col -> 20/40/80 cols; pixel decode
mirrors GateArray.plotChar, addressing mirrors renderScanline), treats
any non-zero pen as ink, and matches the ROM font normal + inverse.

Wires it up end to end: CpcMachine.ocrScreenForMcp (real, was a stub),
ocrScreenStyled (text + coloured HTML + match mask) and blankCells for
the framebuffer; the frame-bridge CPC branch drives the TEXT LED and the
transcribe overlay; Screen.tsx positions the overlay over the CPC active
area (border-crop viewport + pixelAspectX); the TEXT LED click guard is
relaxed from spectrum to machine. OcrGridName splits into SpectrumOcrGrid
and CpcOcrGrid so OCR_GRIDS/detectGrid stay Spectrum-only.

Verified against real OS6128+BASIC+AMSDOS: the boot banner OCRs cleanly
at auto grid 40x25. Tests paint glyphs via the documented CPC address
formula + per-mode pen packing and assert recovery in all three modes,
inverse video, and row stride.

events.title: Add zero-cost trace-BP mode + FSUAE_NO_UAEFS env gate
events.message:
Add zero-cost trace-BP mode + FSUAE_NO_UAEFS env gate

Two follow-on features for high-volume divergence-bisection work between
FS-UAE and external Amiga implementations (e.g. fast68k Verilator + a
bare-A500 RTL build):

Trace breakpoints. Install a BP with `trace=1&out=PATH` and every hit
silently captures {PC, D0, A0, A2, A3, A6, SP, stack[0..3]} to the file
and auto-resumes — no debugger entry, no client poll, no 50 ms
ws_pulse_thread latency. Sustains ~600K hits/sec because the hook only
runs from inside the CPU's existing BP-match block, and short-circuits
when no trace BPs are armed.

ep_resume now re-arms `do_skip=1; debugging=1; SPCFLAG_BRK` whenever
any BP is installed. Without this, deactivate_debugger() leaves
`debugging=0` and the CPU loop never calls debug() to check BPs, so
externally-installed BPs silently never fire.

FSUAE_NO_UAEFS=1 suppresses the K1.2/K1.3-specific KS12_BOOT_HACK that
maps the UAE filesys autoconfig card at $E90000. Used for
apples-to-apples chipset + allocation-pattern comparisons against
bare-A500 RTL where the UAE-FS card is absent and consuming chip-RAM
differently.

Files:
- fsuae_rpc.cpp — trace BP state, hook fn, /v1/trace endpoint, ep_resume re-arm
- patches/0002-alloc-trace-and-no-uaefs.patch — debug.cpp BP-match call-site + arm_bp_skip + expansion.cpp env gate
- build.sh — apply 0002 as non-fatal Layer 2
- README.md — document both features

slirp: harden backend reinitialization

Ariadne can close and reopen the selected Ethernet backend while

to be stopped, and ignored initialization or thread start failures.

reuse BOOTP leases across backend restarts.

events.title: fix(fdc): fail reads of undersized bad-CRC weak protection sectors
events.message:
fix(fdc): fail reads of undersized bad-CRC weak protection sectors

Ocean's "Game, Set and Match" +3 loader pairs a perfect filler sector
(T0 R=130, 512x0xA7) with a deliberately-unreadable weak sector (T0
R=121, 128-byte N=0, ST1/ST2=0x20) and wipes RAM (reset to 48K BASIC)
unless the weak-sector read FAILS. The FDC was reading it as a clean
success - the undersized-sector exception even stripped its CRC-error
bits - so the protection's must-fail check inverted and fired the bomb.

Report No Data + abnormal termination (and keep the sector's own error
bits) when an undersized sector also carries a genuine data-CRC error
and is not DDAM. Undersized DDAM payload sectors and full-size weak
sectors are unaffected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(media): re-mount persisted disks and tapes after a page reload
events.message:
fix(media): re-mount persisted disks and tapes after a page reload

init() skipped restoreMedia() whenever createMachine() restored an HMR/SZX
snapshot. That snapshot only captures RAM/CPU/AY state, not the mounted disk
and tape images (which are persisted separately, one blob per drive/tape in
IndexedDB). The snapshot is saved on every beforeunload, so a hard reload
restored the machine state but silently dropped the media.

Always restore media now: restoreMedia() loads the FDC image and tape blocks
plus UI state without touching the restored RAM, so a reload keeps both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: fix(fdc): READ_TRACK transfers sector data fields, not the raw track
events.message:
fix(fdc): READ_TRACK transfers sector data fields, not the raw track

READ TRACK (Read Diagnostic) on the uPD765A transfers the sectors' data
fields in physical order from the index hole, reporting the last sector's
real CHRN — not the gap/sync/ID/CRC bytes. We returned a 6250-byte raw track,
so loaders reading offset-sector tracks (Alkatraz tracks 7-31, R177+) got
0x4E gap filler where they expected data and failed with a disk error.

Now reads the sectors' data fields, honours EOT as a sector count, and reports
the true R so the loader learns the offset. Removes the now-unused raw-track
builder and CRC helpers. Fixes Alkatraz +3 (California Games).

Also simplifies the 0.4.1 changelog entries to one-liners.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: damieng

events.title: fix(fdc): abnormal termination on data CRC error; keep deleted-data sectors stable
events.message:
fix(fdc): abnormal termination on data CRC error; keep deleted-data sectors stable

The uPD765A signals abnormal termination (ST0 IC=01) on a data CRC error during
READ_DATA. We returned ST0=0x00, so Hexagon-protected +3 disks read their
CRC-flagged sector, saw a clean read, and rebooted/hung. Now matches the
datasheet and Fuse's upd_fdc.c.

Also stop randomising a sector that carries both the control mark (deleted-data
address mark) and a data CRC error: that data is stable and meaningful (used by
Hexagon as a decryption key), so randomising it corrupted the key. Only a bare
CRC-error sector (weak, Speedlock-style) still varies per read.

Fixes the unreleased Ultimate compilation (Pssst, Tranz-am, etc.). Bumps to 0.4.1.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: DeskTop: Add Startup.Items support
events.message:
DeskTop: Add Startup.Items support

If a "Startup.Items" folder is present in the system directory, (i.e.
adjacent to DESKTOP.SYSTEM), then on startup, after windows are
restored, each item in the directory will be opened one by one.

Anything that can be opened with File > Open works. Putting
accessories, folders, and previewable files (text, graphics, etc) into
the folder makes sense. It makes even more sense to put aliases in the
folder, rather than moving or copying the originals in.

For example, after creating the "Startup.Items" folder, hold down Open
Apple and Solid Apple and drag in the "Round.Corners" accessory from
Extras into "Startup.Items" to create an alias. Then when you restart
DeskTop it will automatically run the accessory.

Putting something like a system or binary program in there doesn't
make a lot of sense since DeskTop needs to exit to run it.

Add SDL3 Amiga emulation and CMake build

Introduce a build system and an SDL3-backed Amiga compatibility shim to run the original Juggler raytracer on modern platforms. Adds CMakeLists, CMakePresets.json and vcpkg.json (default manifest-mode SDL3 via vcpkg; can be disabled with -DJUGGLER_USE_VCPKG=OFF), and .gitignore updates. Adds src/emulate-amiga.c (SDL3 texture/preview, HAM emulation, Amiga-like APIs), minimal Amiga headers (src/exec/*, src/intuition/*), a consolidated rt.h for shared types/decls, and updates to rt1.c/rt2.c/rt3.c to modernize prototypes/returns and integrate the compatibility layer. Also adds LICENSE.txt, a preview image, and expands README with a Modernization section documenting the approach and known issues.

events.title: ppc: avoid QEMU IRQ lock inversion
events.message:
ppc: avoid QEMU IRQ lock inversion

QEMU 10 and newer take the BQL inside ppc_set_irq(). The external
interrupt path can call into QEMU while still holding the UAE PPC
spinlock.

That can deadlock if the main thread waits for QEMU BQL while the
QEMU CPU thread waits for the UAE spinlock.

Use the release-spinlock path for external interrupt injection. This
matches the ordering used for QEMU memory mapping and state changes.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: ethernet: defer NIC receive injection to hsync
events.message:
ethernet: defer NIC receive injection to hsync

A2065/Ariadne injected packets directly from the host network
callback. With SLIRP or pcap this callback can run on a helper
thread, so receive DMA and interrupt updates could race PPC I/O
callbacks.

Queue received frames and drain them from the device hsync
handler, where the rest of the emulated card state is updated. Also
stop the NE2000 host callback from draining its queue, leaving that
work to the existing hsync path.

events.title: slirp: check TCP connect completion with SO_ERROR
events.message:
slirp: check TCP connect completion with SO_ERROR

The nonblocking connect path treated a writable socket as connected
and then used a zero-length send as the failure probe. That is not a
reliable completion check and can mis-handle failed or pending guest
TCP connects.

Use getsockopt(SO_ERROR) when select reports the socket writable. Keep
pending connects pending, and only clear SS_ISFCONNECTING after the
host socket has no pending error.

events.title: pcem: hide unused CPU catalog declarations
events.message:
pcem: hide unused CPU catalog declarations

The embedded bridgeboard glue provides its own file-local CPU tables
and model_init() helper. The public PCem header declarations are not
used by the UAE integration, and some of the names collide with those
local definitions when compiled as C++.

Disable the unused declarations in the imported headers instead of
removing individual entries. This avoids mixed-linkage conflicts while
leaving the original declarations visible in the source for reference.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pci: forward-declare bridge memory banks internally
events.message:
pci: forward-declare bridge memory banks internally

The PCI bridge code maps the config, I/O, memory, and bridge banks
before their definitions later in pci.cpp. Clang requires declarations
before those uses.

Keep the declarations and definitions in an anonymous namespace. The
objects remain private to pci.cpp even though the forward declarations
use extern syntax.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: pass MIDI parser a byte buffer
events.message:
pcem: pass MIDI parser a byte buffer

Midi_Parse() takes a BYTE pointer. Store the uint8_t input in a local
BYTE before passing it on so the call does not depend on uint8_t and
BYTE being the same typedef on every host.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: select Voodoo codegen by host capability
events.message:
pcem: select Voodoo codegen by host capability

The imported Voodoo code only enabled its x86 code generators through
Windows-oriented preprocessor checks. That left Unix x86 builds with
the recompiler disabled even when the matching generator was compiled.

Derive explicit PCEM_VOODOO_CODEGEN macros from the host CPU and use
those macros for init, close, rendering, and the default recompiler
configuration.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: avoid dynamic offsetof in Voodoo codegen
events.message:
pcem: avoid dynamic offsetof in Voodoo codegen

The Voodoo x86 code generators compute offsets into array members
with offsetof(type, field[index]). Some compilers reject that
expression form.

Add helpers that derive the offset from field[0] plus an element
stride. That preserves the generated offsets without relying on a
runtime-indexed offsetof expression. This matches the same cleanup
merged upstream in 86Box.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: fit graphics sources into C++ builds
events.message:
pcem: fit graphics sources into C++ builds

WinUAE builds the imported PCem graphics sources as C++ files.
The MGA source includes C atomics directly, and the BT482 RAMDAC
source uses C allocation declarations through C++ headers.

Use C++ atomics when compiling MGA as C++, and include the C++
cstdlib wrapper where the BT482 RAMDAC needs those declarations.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: make MGA high-bit masks unsigned
events.message:
pcem: make MGA high-bit masks unsigned

MGA defines several bit-31 masks from a signed int literal.
Shifting a signed 1 into the sign bit is undefined behavior in C.

Use UINT32_C(1) so the masks are built in unsigned arithmetic.
This matches the same cleanup merged upstream in 86Box, with the
extra OPTION_POWERPC mask that exists in this imported copy.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: pcem: fix helper thread handles
events.message:
pcem: fix helper thread handles

The PCem compatibility layer returned a raw uae_thread_id as a
thread_t pointer and then waited on that value through the semaphore
API. That was pointer-shaped on some targets, but it was not a valid
wrapper around UAE's thread API.

Store the uae_thread_id in an explicit PCem handle object, join it
with uae_wait_thread(), and free the wrapper after wait or close. Reset
and signal PCem events through the existing semaphore object instead of
passing the address of a local pointer copy.
events.author: reinauer

Add run.sh launcher + USAGE.md + ARCHITECTURE.md, refresh ROADMAP

The repo now has a one-command-to-debugger entry point:

    ./build.sh         # build the patched binary once
    ./run.sh <cfg>     # launch + open browser

run.sh:
- Validates the binary exists
- Kills any existing instance (idempotent re-launch)
- Redirects stdin from /dev/null so the patched console_get() does

  (pause+inspect, single-step, BPs, WPs, snapshots, register writes,

- ARCHITECTURE.md — how the patch actually works inside FS-UAE
  (threads, pause semantics, watchpoint bank-rewrapping, single-step,
  web UI delivery, WebSocket handshake)
- ROADMAP.md rewritten — clearer "done", "next" (1-2 hour wins),
  "medium" (1-day items), "larger" (1-week items)

events.title: Add exec.library FD annotation — JSR/PEA -nn(A6) get function names
events.message:
Add exec.library FD annotation — JSR/PEA -nn(A6) get function names

The most useful single addition for Amiga code reading: every JSR -nn(A6)
or PEA -nn(A6) gets annotated with the exec.library function name (the
most-called library on the Amiga, accessed via the convention
"MOVEA.L $4.W, A6" + JSR -nn(A6)).

New endpoints:
- GET /v1/fd/exec               full exec.library FD table
- GET /v1/fd/lookup?offset=N    single lookup (negative or positive)

Annotation:
- GET /v1/disasm?...&annotate=1 inlines "; exec.FuncName()" on matching
                                lines.  Heuristic matcher looks for
                                "(A6, -$XX)" form in the disasm output.

Built-in table covers ~80 exec functions for Kickstart 1.3+ (exec V34):
- Memory: AllocMem, FreeMem, Allocate, Deallocate, AvailMem, ...
- Lists: AddHead, AddTail, RemHead, Insert, Remove, Enqueue, FindName
- Tasks: AddTask, FindTask, Wait, Signal, AllocSignal
- Ports: AddPort, PutMsg, GetMsg, ReplyMsg, WaitPort, FindPort
- IO: OpenDevice, DoIO, SendIO, CheckIO, WaitIO
- Libraries: OpenLibrary, CloseLibrary, MakeLibrary, MakeFunctions
- IRQ: SetIntVector, AddIntServer, RemIntServer, Cause
- Resources: AddResource, OpenResource, ...
- Core: Supervisor, Forbid, Permit, Disable, Enable, Alert, FindResident

The web UI now requests annotated disasm by default.

Demonstrated end-to-end: in the K1.3 autovec L1 handler at $FC0CC0,
PEA -$24(A6) gets annotated as "; exec.ExitIntr()" — exactly the
expected behaviour.

events.title: v3: WebSocket events, embedded web UI, symbol resolution, value-match WP
events.message:
v3: WebSocket events, embedded web UI, symbol resolution, value-match WP

This release upgrades fsuae_remote_patch from a JSON-RPC backend to a
complete cross-platform Amiga debugger.

New: embedded web UI

- Open http://127.0.0.1:8765/ in any browser
- Live CPU registers (changed values highlighted)
- Disassembly view with current-PC marker
- Memory hex dump with ASCII alongside
- Chipset state (DMACON decode, INTENA/INTREQ, beam pos, copper/bpl ptrs)
- Breakpoint + watchpoint installation by clicking in the UI
- Last-WP-hit display (the actual triggering PC, not the post-IRQ PC)
- WebSocket-driven live updates; falls back to polling every 2s

Single .html file embedded into the fs-uae binary via tools/embed_html.py
generating web_index.inc. No external file dependency.

New: WebSocket event stream

- GET /v1/events with Upgrade: websocket
- Frames: {"event":"hello"|"paused"|"running"|"wp_hit", ...}
- Pulse thread polls debugger_active + memwatch_triggered every 50ms,
  broadcasts state transitions to up to 8 connected clients
- Includes a tiny inline SHA-1 + base64 for the handshake; no OpenSSL

New: symbol resolution

- GET /v1/symbols (full table, ~140 entries)
- GET /v1/symbols/lookup?addr=X (single lookup)
- Built-in table: all 68k exception vectors ($0..$BC), every chipset
  register at $DFFxxx (DMACON, INTENA, BPLCON0, COP1LC, etc.),
  CIA-A and CIA-B registers ($BFExxx / $BFDxxx)
- The web UI uses these to annotate disassembly inline

New: value-match watchpoints

- val=HEX + valmask=HEX query params on POST /v1/watchpoints
- Fire only when written value matches (after masking)
- Useful for catching specific signatures landing at a probed address

Stability fixes:

- signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_IGN) at RPC init — broken client disconnects no
  longer crash fs-uae via SIGPIPE
- SO_NOSIGPIPE per-socket on macOS
- Disconnected WebSocket clients are reaped from the broadcast list

Patch additions to FS-UAE:

- newcpu.cpp: post-reset hook re-calls memwatch_setup() so watchpoints
  survive uae_reset()
- debug.cpp: un-statics mwhit + memwatch_triggered (for /v1/watchpoints/last)

Demonstrated end-to-end:
- WebSocket handshake correct (SHA-1 accept-key verified)
- Pause/resume events deliver within one 50ms pulse
- fs-uae stays alive across many WS connect/disconnect cycles
- Web UI rendering exercised manually

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Add /v1/watchpoints/last — get actual triggering PC
events.message:
Add /v1/watchpoints/last — get actual triggering PC

A watchpoint pause is sometimes preceded by an IRQ — by the time the
RPC client polls /v1/state and sees "paused", the CPU may have already
left the PC that caused the trigger and entered the IRQ handler. The
visible /v1/cpu PC is then misleading for finding the offending code.

FS-UAE records the PC at trigger time in the internal `mwhit` struct
(set inside memwatch_func before SPCFLAG_BRK fires). Expose it via
a new GET /v1/watchpoints/last endpoint that returns:

  {
    "ok": true,
    "hit": true|false,
    "slot": N,
    "addr": "0xHEX",       (address that was accessed)
    "pc":   "0xHEX",       (PC at access time — the actual culprit)
    "rwi": "R|W|RW|...",
    "size": N,             (access width in bytes)
    "value": "0xHEX",      (written value, for writes)
    "access_mask": "0xHEX" (source: CPU/blitter/copper/etc.)
  }

Implementation:
- Patch un-statics `mwhit` and `memwatch_triggered` in debug.cpp so
  the RPC can read them.
- ep_wp_last formats the JSON; "hit": false when memwatch_triggered=0.

This makes watchpoint-driven bisection much more reliable: the PC
field tells you exactly which instruction wrote the byte, not just
"some instruction did, and then an IRQ fired".

Demonstrated end-to-end: caught the K1.3 IRQ-dispatcher install at
slow $C096C0 via mustchange=1 watchpoint on chip $C0, then walked
the call chain via /v1/disasm to identify the gate (LIB_VERSION <= 35
check at $C094DC) and the builder (CopyMem at ROM $FC2F80 copying
from chip $10EB0 to slow $C094D4).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Major: mem/cpu write, disasm, chipset snapshot, state load, sticky pause
events.message:
Major: mem/cpu write, disasm, chipset snapshot, state load, sticky pause

The big one. Adds enough to FS-UAE to be a real cross-platform debugger
API:

New mutation endpoints:
- POST /v1/mem?addr=HEX&hex=BYTES         write bytes to memory
- POST /v1/cpu?reg=NAME&value=HEX         write a register (d0..d7,
                                          a0..a7, pc, sr, usp, isp)

New inspection endpoints:
- GET /v1/disasm?addr=HEX&count=N         disassemble N instructions
                                          (m68k_disasm_2 -> JSON lines)
- GET /v1/custom                          chipset register snapshot:
                                          DMACON, INTENA/INTREQ,
                                          BPLCON0, VPOSR/VHPOSR, ADKCONR,
                                          DIWSTRT/STOP, DDFSTRT/STOP,
                                          COP1LC/COP2LC, BPL1PT..BPL8PT

New state endpoint:
- POST /v1/state/load?path=ABS_PATH       restore_state() wrapper

Critical bugfix — sticky pause:

The fs-uae debugger's inner loop calls console_get(stdin). When stdin
is /dev/null (the common case for an RPC-driven background process),
fgets returns NULL, console_get returned -1, and debug_1 immediately
exited. This meant /v1/pause and BP/WP hits would briefly halt the
CPU, run a few cycles of debugger output, then resume — instead of
*staying* paused.

Patched console_get to: on EOF, sleep 20 ms and return 0 (empty line)
while debugger_active is still set. The debugger loop now reliably
sleeps until /v1/resume clears debugger_active.

This unblocks the entire RPC workflow — pause now actually pauses,
and writes (mem, reg) stick across subsequent reads.

Demonstrated end-to-end: with these changes we successfully bisected
to find that Kickstart 1.3's IRQ-server dispatcher install routine
runs at slow RAM $00C096C0, gated by a LIB_VERSION <= 35 check at
$00C094DC. The install bytes are NOT in K1.3 ROM as a static template
— they're built dynamically.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
