events.title: Add /v1/step single-step + /v1/watchpoints rearm + mustchange filter
events.message:
Add /v1/step single-step + /v1/watchpoints rearm + mustchange filter

New endpoints:
- POST /v1/step?n=N                 execute N instructions then re-pause
- POST /v1/watchpoints/rearm        re-call memwatch_setup() explicitly

Watchpoints gain a mustchange=1 query param: when set, the WP only
fires on writes that ACTUALLY change memory (skips writes-of-same-value).
Useful for finding the "first modifying write" to an address after a
memset-style init.

/v1/resume now auto-calls memwatch_setup() if any watchpoints are active.
This is required because /v1/reset re-initializes the memory bank
dispatch table, clobbering the WP bank-wrapping. Auto-rearm-on-resume
makes the typical reset+resume+walk pattern work without manual rearm.

Implementation:
- skipaddr_doskip un-statics in debug.cpp (the trace counter)
- ep_step sets skipaddr_doskip+exception_debugging+SPCFLAG_BRK, leaves
  `debugging=1` so CPU re-enters debug() after each instruction, and
  clears debugger_active so debug_1()'s stdin-read loop returns. This
  combo makes single-step actually advance one instruction at a time.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
events.author: geekychris

events.title: Add breakpoints, watchpoints, reset, state, pause-at-boot
events.message:
Add breakpoints, watchpoints, reset, state, pause-at-boot

New endpoints:
- GET  /v1/state                          poll for BP/WP hits after resume
- POST /v1/breakpoints?addr=HEX           install PC breakpoint
- GET  /v1/breakpoints                    list active breakpoints
- POST /v1/breakpoints/clear              remove all breakpoints
- POST /v1/watchpoints?addr&size&rwi      install memory watchpoint
- GET  /v1/watchpoints                    list active watchpoints
- POST /v1/watchpoints/clear              remove all watchpoints
- POST /v1/reset?hard=1                   trigger emulator reset

New env var: FSUAE_RPC_PAUSE_AT_BOOT=1 makes the emulator start paused,
which lets clients install breakpoints/watchpoints before any instruction
executes — useful for catching very-early-boot ROM behaviour.

Implementation: the patch un-statics memwatch_setup() and initialize_memwatch()
in debug.cpp so fsuae_rpc.cpp can install watchpoints without re-entering
FS-UAE's interactive debugger command parser. Direct writes to bpnodes[]
suffice for breakpoints.

Includes examples/catch_chip_ram_init.sh demonstrating the full
launch -> install WP -> resume -> auto-pause flow on the original
motivating problem (find where Kickstart populates chip RAM $C0-$FF).

events.title: uae/string: guard _strtoui64 compatibility macro
events.message:
uae/string: guard _strtoui64 compatibility macro

Some host C libraries or compatibility headers can provide
_strtoui64 before this header defines the TCHAR-style aliases.

Only provide the fallback when it is missing, and map it to
strtoull so the unsigned conversion matches the name.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: gfxboard: rewind Picasso IV flash before autoconfig
events.message:
gfxboard: rewind Picasso IV flash before autoconfig

Picasso IV autoconfig is read from the flash image, but the
initializer can run more than once while the expansion list is
scanned and sorted. loadp4rom() leaves the flash zfile positioned
later in the image, so a later dry scan read all-0xff data and the
board looked like it had no autoconfig block.

Seek back to the beginning before reading the Picasso IV
autoconfig bytes so repeated scans see the same board data.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: isofs: avoid undefined timezone sign extension
events.message:
isofs: avoid undefined timezone sign extension

make_date() sign-extends the ISO9660 timezone byte when the high
bit is set. (-1 << 8) shifts a negative signed value, which is
undefined behavior in C++.

Use ~0xff to build the same extension mask without relying on
that undefined shift.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: jit: use ucontext_t for gregset access
events.message:
jit: use ucontext_t for gregset access

The generic Unix exception path works with ucontext_t directly. Use that
typedef instead of struct ucontext so platforms that expose only
ucontext_t still build.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: softfloat: drop stale float_raise declaration
events.message:
softfloat: drop stale float_raise declaration

float_raise() is provided as a static inline helper by
softfloat-specialize.h. Remove the separate external prototype from
softfloat.h so the header does not advertise a non-existent external
definition.
events.author: reinauer

events.title: softfloat: copy mod/rem quotient through uint64_t
events.message:
softfloat: copy mod/rem quotient through uint64_t

floatx80_mod() and floatx80_rem() take a uint64_t quotient pointer,
while the FPU wrapper stores the quotient in uae_u64. Copy through a
temporary so the call does not depend on those typedefs being the same
type on every host.

events.title: softfloat: use lowercase macro header name
events.message:
softfloat: use lowercase macro header name

The source already includes the macro helper as softfloat-macros.h.
Rename the tracked file to match that spelling so case-sensitive file
systems do not depend on the old all-caps name.

events.message:

cfgfile: map legacy toccata_mixer setting

The old toccata_mixer option enabled the board but did not carry the

codec_start() allocated the record buffer even when host capture setup

Keep every QEMU output voice on a small linked list instead of

Update all active QEMU voice volumes, only run QEMU board audio when a
voice is active, clamp writes to the sample buffer, and return no input
data until the capture path has a real backend.

events.author: tonioni

events.title: jit/x86-64: fix FPU FLDCW codegen crashes on 64-bit hosts
events.message:
jit/x86-64: fix FPU FLDCW codegen crashes on 64-bit hosts

The x86-64 JIT could crash when compiling FPU rounding-mode changes
(FLDCW with an indexed operand) via two defects in codegen_x86.cpp:

1. x86_64_rex() dereferenced its 'b' (REX.B) pointer unconditionally and
   ignored 'r'/'x'. raw_fldcw_m_indexed() passes its index register in the
   'x' (REX.X) slot with b == NULL, so the function read through a NULL
   pointer; an index register in r8-r15 would also have been mis-encoded.
   x86_64_rex() now null-guards each pointer and emits REX.R/X/B (and W).

2. raw_fldcw_m_indexed() loaded the 64-bit base of the x87 control-word
   table into RAX. RAX is allocatable (not in always_used[]) and may hold a
   live m68k value mid-block, and a LOWFUNC cannot declare a register
   clobber, so the allocator's view of RAX was silently corrupted; a later
   access through that register (e.g. MOVEM.L ...,-(An)) then dereferenced
   the table pointer as an m68k address and faulted. The base is now
   materialized in a push/pop-preserved scratch register chosen to differ
   from the index register.

Only x86-64 is affected; the 32-bit path uses a direct FLDCW [reg] encoding
and ARM64 uses different codegen.
events.author: midwan

events.title: flowchart: add movement action handler diagrams
events.message:
flowchart: add movement action handler diagrams

Four per-routine decision-tree flowcharts for MAIN_LOOP's phase-3 SMC
slots: DO_ASCEND ($6378), DO_DESCEND ($63B4), DO_MOVE_RIGHT ($6409) and
DO_MOVE_LEFT ($646D, the structural mirror of right). Branch structure is
exact; multi-instruction blocks (floor-index propagation + hit-slot wipe,
descent self-stop SMC patch + ZP_LAST_DIR refresh, stance walk-cycle) are
summarized. Includes a shared notes block on floor mirrors, the stance
gating, and the DESC_LANDED_CLEAR shared tail. Derived from the movement
action handlers chunk in main.nw.

events.title: flowchart: add MAIN_LOOP per-frame expansion diagram
events.message:
flowchart: add MAIN_LOOP per-frame expansion diagram

Second Mermaid diagram expanding MAIN_LOOP ($67CB) into its ~25 ordered
per-frame subroutine calls, grouped into 9 phases plus a Game-entry box.
Entry point (GAME_START_INIT -> JMP MAIN_LOOP) is pinned to the top; the
per-frame loop returns to the $67CB frame top, not through GAME_START_INIT.

Subgraphs are declared in reverse order so dagre renders them top-to-bottom
(last-declared floats to the top; see mermaid-js/mermaid#2789); an inline %%
comment documents this. Single-line subgraph titles + subGraphTitleMargin
avoid the multiline-title overlap (#3806).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Container env: uv, runtime claude-code upgrade, host state + SSH mounts
events.message:
Container env: uv, runtime claude-code upgrade, host state + SSH mounts

- Dockerfile: install uv/uvx; move npm global prefix into the user's home
  so claude-code can self-upgrade without EACCES; auto-invalidate the
  install layer via ADD of the npm "latest" metadata; mark the bind-mounted
  repo as a git safe.directory.
- docker-compose.yml: bind-mount a host state dir (~/drol-re-claude-container-state)
  and the host ~/.ssh (read-only).
- docker-entrypoint.sh: set git user identity; symlink Claude state to the
  host-mounted dir (preserving atomic-rename writes); install host SSH keys
  and seed github.com known_hosts.

events.title: Decompose level-1 $6700-$72FF HEX blob into 18 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks
events.message:
Decompose level-1 $6700-$72FF HEX blob into 18 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks

Splits the last large raw HEX blob in the level1 target (the 3072-byte
$6700-$72FF game-engine/attract window) into per-routine L1_ chunks,
each mirroring its drol.bin twin: FLOOR_ENEMY_ADVANCE tail, FLOOR_ENEMY_DRAW,
SFX_TONE, MAIN_LOOP, DRAW_ENTITIES, LEVEL_INTRO_TICK, the special
tick/draw/step/inactive group, COMPANION_UPDATE, RESCUE_UPDATE,
DIFFICULTY_UPDATE, LIFE_LOST_HANDLER, ATTRACT_LOOP, START_ATTRACT, the
table pad, and SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_HI. Adds a Pages 67-72 subsection with an
L1-label/drol-twin/span/bytes/role table. level1 stays 100% byte-perfect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Fix cursor position drifting when applying enums and analyzing
events.message:
Fix cursor position drifting when applying enums and analyzing

When enum definitions are inserted or external labels are toggled, the
underlying disassembly vector length and indices change. The view's
cursor index was previously left untouched, causing it to point to a
different logical line. Added `preserve_cursor` to capture the current
address and reset the cursor to the matching line after the state
change, preventing drift.

Fix Windows ARM64 JIT startup

Enable the ARM64 JIT build path, keep natmem above 4GB, reserve the full direct-memory window, commit read-only natmem gaps, and install a Windows ARM64 vectored exception handler for JIT access faults.

Add a GitHub Actions Windows ARM64 binary job that installs the ARM64 MSVC tools and builds winuae_msvc.vcxproj directly without ARM64-building host generator projects.

Validated with ARM64 Release and FullRelease MSBuild builds, plus VMware Windows ARM64 runtime logs showing the handler catching ramsey_low probes instead of crashing.

events.title: Add support for target-specific custom enums in disassembler
events.message:
Add support for target-specific custom enums in disassembler

This adds robust support for custom enums, allowing users to replace raw numeric values (immediate operands, data bytes, and data words) with semantic names across all supported assemblers (64tass, KickAssembler, ca65, and ACME) in a target-specific way.

- 64tass formats enums using named dictionaries (e.g., Colors.BLACK)
- KickAssembler formats enums inside .enum blocks (e.g., Colors.BLACK)
- ca65 formats enums inside .enum blocks and double-colon scopes (e.g., Colors::BLACK)
- ACME formats enums using flat underscore namespaces (e.g., Colors_BLACK)

Precedence models shadow local > global > built-in, and enums are cloned and embedded permanently on use to guarantee portable, self-contained saves.

Fixes https://github.com/ricardoquesada/regenerator2000/issues/22

events.title: perf(z80): inline fetch8/fetch16, trim step+runFrame hot paths
events.message:
perf(z80): inline fetch8/fetch16, trim step+runFrame hot paths

CPU-internal cleanup chasing the post-flat-memory profile (read8 is now
3.6% self; the cost sits in the dispatch infrastructure).

- Inline fetch8 and fetch16 at all 41 call sites across exec-main/ed/
  index/cb and step(). Eliminates one Z80.prototype.* call per opcode
  byte fetch — Firefox can't reliably inline through that boundary, so
  the call-frame overhead was dominating fetch8 self-time at 12.5%.
  Delete the now-dead fetch8/fetch16 methods from core.ts.

- Drop postStepHook from step() and core.ts. It was assigned only to
  null and ceremonially restored by the MCP trace tool; pure dead
  weight on every instruction. Strip the corresponding save/restore
  from mcp/tools/trace.ts.

- Drop the elapsed<=0 defensive bump and step()'s return value. Nobody
  reads it; it was a guard against opcodes that don't bump tStates,
  which we'd treat as a real bug now.

- runFrame: cache watchActive once per frame. The post-step
  portWatchHit/memWatchHit null-compare ran on every instruction even
  when no watchpoints were set. Caching collapses the common case to
  a single boolean.

- runFrame: hoist advanceTapeTo's playing/paused early-exit into the
  loop body, skipping the method-call frame when tape is idle. Add
  a synchronous ula.tapeActive = false in onPlayStateChange so the
  hoisted check doesn't strand a stale tapeEarBit when the tape stops
  mid-frame.

events.title: fix(memory): write-through for aliased bank slots
events.message:
fix(memory): write-through for aliased bank slots

When two slots map the same RAM bank (e.g. port 0x7FFD currentBank=5
puts bank 5 into both slot 1 and slot 3, or currentBank=2 into slots
2 and 3), real hardware sees both windows as the same physical chip.
The previous flat-memory commit only synced the slots at map-in time
(source-fallback in _switchRam); subsequent CPU writes to one slot
silently failed to appear at the other.

FUSE handles this naturally because its hot path is pointer-based
(memory_map_read[page].page[offset]) and two slots can point at the
same bank. Our flat model needs explicit write-through.

Implementation:
- slotAlias: Int8Array(4) — slot index of the mirror, or -1. Refreshed
  via _refreshAliases() after every paging change.
- io-ports write8 (CPU hot path) and memory.writeByte (debug/snapshot
  path) check slotAlias and store to the mirror when non-negative.
- setBankFromSnapshot already iterated all slots holding the target
  bank, so it was already alias-correct.

Hot-path cost: one Int8Array load + a predictable-false branch in the
common no-aliasing case. The branch is dead-cheap for SpiderMonkey to
predict.

Adds four tests in memory.test.ts covering the live write-through case,
the alias-break case (data preserved on the still-mapped slot), and
the snapshot path.

events.title: perf: flat 64KB memory + contend closure swap for Firefox turbo
events.message:
perf: flat 64KB memory + contend closure swap for Firefox turbo

Three related changes that target the per-instruction hot path Firefox's
JIT couldn't optimise through the previous closure indirection:

1. contendN early-out on accurateTiming. The wrapper now bails before
   the loop in turbo mode instead of dispatching the closure N times.

2. Swap cpu.contend between accurate impl and no-op on turbo enter/exit.
   _contendAccurate holds the cycle-exact implementation; NOOP_CONTEND
   is a module-scope empty function. SpiderMonkey can inline the no-op
   at the hundreds of bare this.contend(addr) sites across exec-main/
   ed/index/cb instead of indirecting through an assigned closure with
   an interior accurateTiming branch.

3. Flat 64KB memory model. SpectrumMemory now backs the Z80's address
   space with a single Uint8Array(0x10000); RAM banks become cold
   storage for unmapped banks. The hot read path collapses from
   slots[addr>>>14][addr&0x3FFF] (two array loads) to flat[addr&0xFFFF]
   (one). Bank switches do 16KB memcpy back to cold + 16KB memcpy in
   from cold; the same-bank short-circuit keeps no-op switches free.

   getRamBank(n) returns a live flat.subarray view if the bank is
   currently mapped, cold storage otherwise — so screen rendering,
   snapshot save, debug tools, and frame-bridge all work without
   explicit flush calls. setBankFromSnapshot writes to both cold and
   any live mapping for consistency. Bank aliasing (currentBank=5
   putting bank 5 into slot 1 and slot 3) is handled via source-
   fallback on load: the new slot copies from the live aliased slot
   rather than stale cold storage. Cross-slot write-through is not
   modelled — real software almost never relies on it.

Profile chain on Firefox turbo: contendN 28.7% -> 0, runFrame self
22.1% -> 5.6%; cpu.read8 should drop substantially in the next pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: perf: cache slot contention + inline memory hook hot path
events.message:
perf: cache slot contention + inline memory hook hot path

Two related optimisations to the per-instruction memory access path:

1. Per-slot contention cache. Contention now owns a Uint8Array(4)
   slotContended, refreshed on every paging change via a new
   memory.onSlotsChanged callback. isContended(addr) collapses from
   bankAt() + variant.isContended() (virtual dispatch through the
   strategy object) to a single array load. Verified that every variant's
   isContended depends only on (slot, bank), never the in-slot offset,
   so the cache is exact. Helps accurate-timing mode too (MCP, tests).

2. Capture stable references in installMemoryHooks. memory.slots and
   contention.slotContended are now exposed and captured as closure
   locals, and read8/write8 index them directly instead of going through
   memory.readByte / contention.isContended method calls. Same change
   for cpu, replacing s.cpu.* chains throughout the hot path. This
   should let SpiderMonkey monomorphise the read path the way V8 already
   does (Firefox lagged Edge by ~1.7x before).

memory.bankSwitch and bankSwitch1FFD mutate _slots directly without
going through updateSlots, so onSlotsChanged is fired at the end of
each method to keep the cache exact.
events.author: damieng

events.title: perf(turbo): skip ULA contention via cpu.accurateTiming flag
events.message:
perf(turbo): skip ULA contention via cpu.accurateTiming flag

Per-instruction ULA contention is the dominant non-CPU cost in the hot
path: every memory read/write/IR-refresh runs isContended -> bankAt ->
variant.isContended (virtual dispatch through the strategy object) plus
a contentionDelay() with a floating-point division when contended.

Add cpu.accurateTiming (default true) and short-circuit the contention
chain in read8/write8/contend/portIn/portOut when it is false. The UI
turbo path in frameLoop toggles it off on enter and back on exit, in
the same block that saves/restores scanlineAccuracy.

MCP (mcp/tools/trace.ts, mcp/tools/machine.ts) and the test suites
never set spectrum.turbo, so they keep cycle-exact timing. The default
path is unchanged; only the explicit UI turbo opts out.

Measured ~3x speedup in Firefox and ~5x in Edge on a 240Hz display.
events.author: damieng

events.title: perf(turbo): adaptive rAF budget, skip audio, throttle UI
events.message:
perf(turbo): adaptive rAF budget, skip audio, throttle UI

Turbo mode previously capped at a hard 14 frames per rAF with full audio
generation and per-rAF UI reactivity, which left a lot of CPU on the table
and did not scale to high-refresh displays.

- Replace the fixed frame cap in frameLoop with a time budget adapted to
  the measured rAF interval (70% EWMA-smoothed, clamped 1.5-14ms). Avoids
  overshooting the cadence and triggering browser rAF throttling on
  240Hz displays.
- Force scanlineAccuracy='low' while turbo is active and skip the bulk
  renderFrame() on intermediate frames in a batch -- only the final frame
  produces displayed pixels. Convert scanlineAccuracy to a getter/setter
  so external writes (e.g. applyDisplaySettings after a renderer swap)
  update the saved user choice instead of clobbering the forced 'low'.
- Skip per-instruction mixer.accumulate/generateSamples in turbo (the
  buffer fills faster than realtime and the sound is unrecognisable).
  Cache the turbo flag once per frame so the hot loop does not re-read
  two properties per instruction.
- In frame-bridge onFrame, throttle the heavy Solid.js batch() block
  (LEDs, registers, sysvar/BASIC, transcribe/OCR) to ~10Hz during turbo.
  Speed readout, breakpoint check, and floppy sound updates still run
  every rAF.

refactor(mcp): split src/mcp-server.ts into mcp/ module tree

The MCP server is a Node-only entry point with no place in src/ (which is
browser/Solid code) — Vite and tsconfig both had to special-case it. Move
it under a top-level mcp/ folder and split the 1705-line monolith into
focused modules so tools are easier to read and become unit-testable.

Layout: mcp/server.ts is the entry, mcp/tools/*.ts groups tool handlers
by topic (machine, memory, breakpoints, traps, io, media, trace,
peripherals, symbols), shared helpers (state, format, loader, traps,
fdc-log, rom-fetch, hex) sit at the mcp/ root. installTrapHook and
wireFdcLog now take spec as a parameter instead of closing over module
state, which removes a circular-import risk and makes them directly
testable.

Also drops the tsconfig exclude so MCP code is finally type-checked, and
moves the ROM cache from src/.cache/ to mcp/.cache/.

refactor(tape,audio): make cpuClock a required constructor arg

TapeDeck and AudioMixer previously defaulted cpuClock to Z80_CLOCK_48K
as a class-field fallback, requiring callers to remember a post-
construction assignment to get the right clock for non-48K machines.

hardcoded to 48K timing when in fact every production caller already
supplies the variant's clock. Drop the default, make the arg required,
and let the compiler catch silent miswiring.

events.title: feat(tape): edge-loader subsystem with surgical accel, fixed auto-stop, split UI toggles
events.message:
feat(tape): edge-loader subsystem with surgical accel, fixed auto-stop, split UI toggles

Replaces the LoaderDetector + loader-signature pair with a unified EdgeLoader
that handles §2 auto play/stop, §3 structural fingerprinting, and §4 surgical
edge acceleration (see docs/edge-loading.md). Fixes a clutch of issues that
showed up while loading Speedlock 1:

- accelerate(): refresh lastTStatesRead/lastBRead to post-accel CPU state.
  Without this, advancing tape by a full pulse (~2168T for pilot) left the
  next IN A,(\$FE) computing a huge tDiff and a synthetic bDiff outside
  {0,1,0xFF} -- auto-stop fired two reads later and the leader bars flapped.

- Auto-stop: require BOTH wide tDiff AND unexpected bDiff (was OR). The 48K
  ROM's LD-MARKER reloads B,\$B0 between every bit, so under OR a couple of
  close bit boundaries stopped the tape mid-block during sync->data.

- loaderActive: set on in-shape polling while already playing, not just on
  the §2 'start' event. The instant-ROM trap and manual Play both unpause
  the tape without firing 'start', so spectrum.ts's per-frame tapeLoading
  check never saw a signal to engage tape turbo on the post-trap stage.

- tapeLoading: gate on !tape.paused. loaderActive is sticky between
  start/stop events, so without this gate auto-rewind / TZX stop / manual
  pause kept turbo engaged after the tape stopped advancing.

UI: split the previous one-toggle into three independent settings --
'tape-instant-rom', 'tape-edge-loading' (default off, menu entry hidden
pending wider testing), and 'tape-turbo-load' -- surfaced in the tape menu
under a separator. DropDownMenuButton gains a separator: true item type.

Tests: 43 cases in tests/tape/accelerated-loaders.test.ts cover the
fingerprint table, accel-safe gating, the auto-stop AND condition, the
mid-tape pause->turbo-release path, and the standalone 'turbo with edge
accel off' case.

events.title: refactor(tape): align ROM trap with FUSE — trap at 0x056C, paging-aware
events.message:
refactor(tape): align ROM trap with FUSE — trap at 0x056C, paging-aware

Move the LD-BYTES trap from 0x0556 to LD-START at 0x056C (FUSE's trap
point, just past the EX AF,AF' and BREAK check). Two reasons:

  1. A handful of protected loaders CALL 0x056C directly to reuse part
     of LD-BYTES without the entry preamble. Trapping at 0x0556 misses
     those; 0x056C catches both entry paths.
  2. The trap now jumps PC to 0x05E2 (POP AF; RET) on success and lets
     the real ROM clean up the stack — no manual SP pop, no IFF
     fiddling. The POP AF loads F=0x3F from the 0x053F pushed at
     0x0561, giving carry=1 = "load succeeded" naturally.

Replace the byte-sniff (memory[0x0556]==0x14) with a proper paging
check on memory.isBasicRomActive(). The 48K BASIC ROM is always
romPages[length-1]; the helper also rejects specialPaging and
externalRomPaged (Multiface/VTX-5000) states. Previously a custom RAM
bank with 0x14 at 0x0556 would have mis-fired on +2A/+3.

Add a FUSE-style block-length sanity check: if block.data.length !==
DE the trap declines and the real ROM runs LD-BYTES at full fidelity.
This lets custom-speed turbos and protected blocks coexist with the
trap — the heuristic only fires for exact-match standard blocks.

To support the decline-without-side-effects contract, split
nextDataBlock() into peekDataBlock() (advances over cosmetic blocks
but leaves the data block in place) + commit. The trap peeks, checks
flag/length, and only commits on success.

Drop the unconditional 2168 T-state injection; the real LD-BYTES
preamble accounts for those T-states naturally, and the POP AF; RET
cleanup at 0x05E2 covers the rest.

Tests rewritten to pin the new contract: decline on no-block /
flag-mismatch / length-mismatch / short-block / long-block; on
success copy bytes, set PC=0x05E2, leave SP and IFFs untouched.

Cross-referenced against FUSE tape.c (Philip Kendall, GPL-2.0),
ZEsarUX storage/tape.c, and JSpeccy Tape.java.

events.title: refactor(plus3): split disk-format/protection detection out of dsk.ts

refactor(plus3): split disk-format/protection detection out of dsk.ts

Extract detectDiskFormat, detectProtection and all 15 detector helpers
into src/plus3/disk-detect.ts. dsk.ts shrinks from 745 to 417 lines and
imports the two public functions.

Bug fixes uncovered while expanding test coverage:

- serializeDSK now aligns each track's allocation to a 256-byte multiple.
  The EDSK per-track size table at 0x34 stores size/256, so unaligned
  totals (from short protection sectors etc.) caused the writer's offsets
  and the table to disagree, corrupting every subsequent track on read.

- Detector ordering: detectDiscsys now runs before detectPlayers
  (DiscSYS's CHRN-all-equal-index is a strict superset of Players'
  r-and-n-equal-index, so the reverse order misclassified every DiscSYS
  disk as Players). detectStudioB now runs before detectPms for the
  same reason -- Studio B / DiscLoc layouts also match PMS's unsigned
  heuristic.

- detectFrontier rewritten. The signed signature was truncated to
  "W DISK PROTECTION..." (worked only as an accidental substring of
  "NEW DISK..."); the unsigned heuristic looked for T0/S0=4096b + T9
  1-sector -- the opposite of the real disk layout. Confirmed against
  a CPDRead dump: T0 = 9 x 512b PCW sectors, then >=10 subsequent
  tracks each a single 4096-byte sector with R=1.

Test coverage grows from 69 to 157 (91 in dsk.test.ts + 95 in the new
disk-detect.test.ts), covering every format-detection branch, every
detector with positive + guard-rejection cases, all 10 Speedlock signed
variants, all 4 P.M.S. variants, and the new Frontier real-disk layout.

events.title: fix(ocr): un-pin shifted-coincidence font scan bug
events.message:
fix(ocr): un-pin shifted-coincidence font scan bug

scanBanksAtOffset's per-glyph "does any character slot in this 768-byte
window match?" question doesn't care WHICH slot matches, so any window
overlapping the real font by a multiple of 8 bytes scores 100% by
matching every screen glyph against the wrong character slot. With
zero padding ahead of the font those shifted twins all clear the
existing space-slot prefilter, and the byte-by-byte sweep hands the
earliest 0.95+ scorer to the early-exit — silently returning a window
that decodes screen 'A' as some other code entirely.

Add a structural prefilter: slot '!' (window bytes 8..15) must be
non-empty. Every real font (ROM, CHARS, +3 editor, the Nicety fixture
added here) populates '!' as a real glyph; every shifted-down twin
ends up with either the real font's empty space-slot OR pre-font
padding in '!', so they fail before scoring.

The previously-pinned screen-text cases get re-fixtured around the
Nicety 8×8 font (public-domain, 768 bytes, every printable slot
populated) so the test surfaces the bug under the conditions a real
font would meet — the synthetic sparse GLYPHS map only defined 6
letters and would itself fail the new prefilter.

events.title: fix(spectrum): un-pin AY sample-rate and eiDelay-INT bugs

fix(spectrum): un-pin AY sample-rate and eiDelay-INT bugs

AY sample rate: drop the hard-coded 44.1 kHz. Spectrum now constructs
the AY from `audio.sampleRate` and resyncs it (plus cyclesPerSample and
the DC-blocker alpha) via a new `AY3891x.setSampleRate()` once
`audio.init()` reports the AudioContext's real rate. `Audio` stops
forcing 44.1 kHz on the context and defaults to 48 kHz so consumers
reading the field before init() see a representative value.

eiDelay INT: `intPending` was `intT === 0 && !iff1`, treating DI as the
only reason a frame-boundary ack could fail. When `eiDelay` was the
blocker, the retry never armed and the INT was silently dropped. The
INT line is held LOW for the model's window regardless of which flag
blocked the ack — gate `intPending` on `intT === 0` alone so the
existing retry covers both cases.

Both pinned `it.fails` cases in tests/spectrum.test.ts are inverted to
positive assertions. The AY test also pins `cyclesPerSample` to the new
rate so a future partial fix gets caught.

events.title: Fix unpacker entry point for Exomizer variants that exit via BASIC RUN
events.message:
Fix unpacker entry point for Exomizer variants that exit via BASIC RUN

When the Exomizer depacker decompresses to the full $0800-$FF3F range,
RAM underneath BASIC/Kernal ROM gets written. This caused three
interacting bugs:

1. handle_rom_entry's written-bypass skipped ROM interception when
   written[pc] was true, regardless of whether ROM was mapped. Now it
   checks the PLA bank register: if ROM is mapped at that address, ROM
   interception still fires.

2. Phase 2's written exit condition (pc >= ret_addr && written[pc])
   falsely triggered for ROM addresses like $A659 because the RAM
   underneath was written. Added !in_rom_or_io guard to skip ROM/IO
   addresses.

3. Phase 2's Exit/BasicRun handler used the ROM PC as the entry point
   instead of re-parsing the SYS address from the freshly decompressed
   BASIC program. Now it calls find_sys_address() when PC is in BASIC
   ROM.

Add test for hw20131031.prg verifying entry=$3000, range=$0800-$FF3F.

events.title: Replace strncat() with Str_Copy()
events.message:
Replace strncat() with Str_Copy()

gemdos.c uses strncat() as a replacement for the non-portable strlcpy()
in a couple of places. While the usage looks correct here, strncat() is
generally quite a bad function (since the length parameter does not
directly specify the size of the destination buffer, and you always have
to remember to take the additional NUL character into account in your
calculations), so we should rather completely ban it from the Hatari
sources. Let's use our own Str_Copy() function instead, that way the code
is much easier to understand.
events.author: Thomas Huth

events.title: Fix false trimming for binaries with natural zero-gaps (f600.prg)
events.message:
Fix false trimming for binaries with natural zero-gaps (f600.prg)

When diff_end is well below the scan ceiling (gap > 128 bytes), the
output ends naturally with no depacker workspace to separate. Skip
trim_trailing_clusters in this case to avoid false positives from
natural zero-runs in program data.

f600.prg unpacks to $0801-$FEFF with a 50-byte zero gap at $FA0B
that was falsely identified as a workspace boundary. The output
ends cleanly at $FEFF with $FF00-$FFFF completely untouched.

Side effect: PUCrunch test now includes 10 extra bytes of depacker
workspace ($3209 vs $31FF) since its diff_end is far from the
$9FFF scan ceiling. Negligible for practical disassembly.
events.author: ricardoquesada

events.title: Support unpacking through $D000-$DFFF I/O region
events.message:
Support unpacking through $D000-$DFFF I/O region

Some depackers (e.g. thats_the_way_scoop.prg) run in all-RAM mode
and decompress data through the I/O region into $E000+. The previous
code split the scan at $CFFF and never checked beyond.

Fix with a cascading boundary strategy:
  Level 1: $0800..$9FFF (typical program area)
  Level 2: $0800..$CFFF (includes BASIC ROM area)
  Level 3: $0800..$FFFF (full RAM)

Each level is only tried when the previous scan's detected end
touches its ceiling (within 256 bytes), keeping the range tight
so trim heuristics remain effective for workspace-heavy depackers.

Also fix trim_trailing_clusters Check 2 gap threshold from 4 to 2
bytes — the McCracken compressor's output/workspace boundary has a
2-byte gap that needs to be detected.

Fix IO suppression test to set PLA register $01 to $37 before
testing, matching real C64 default bank configuration.

Tested: roma.exe.prg ($0801-$C8C5), thats_the_way_scoop.prg
($0801-$E750), mule_mccracken_compressor.prg ($0800-$9D05).
events.author: ricardoquesada

events.title: Fix output range detection for binaries unpacking above $9FFF
events.message:
Fix output range detection for binaries unpacking above $9FFF

Two bugs in detect_output_range / trim_trailing_clusters:

1. Primary scan capped at $9FFF, missing output in $A000-$CFFF.
   Programs decompressing into the BASIC ROM area (all-RAM mode)
   were truncated. Extended primary scan to $CFFF (I/O boundary).

2. trim_trailing_clusters Check 2 (proportional tail) triggered on
   single-byte coincidental matches (e.g. a $00 in unpacked data
   matching the snapshot). Added gap_len >= 4 requirement so only
   real gaps qualify as output/workspace boundaries.

Tested with roma.exe.prg which unpacks to $0800-$C8C5.

events.title: Fix bank-aware I/O emulation for C64 depacker (Dali)
events.message:
Fix bank-aware I/O emulation for C64 depacker (Dali)

The UnpackerMemory Bus implementation unconditionally suppressed reads
and writes to the I/O region ($D000-$DFFF), returning 0 for reads and
silently dropping writes. This ignored the C64 PLA bank register ($01)
which controls memory mapping.

When both LORAM (bit 0) and HIRAM (bit 1) of $01 are clear (e.g.,
$01=$34, all-RAM mode), the real C64 PLA maps plain RAM at $D000-$DFFF
instead of I/O chips. Depackers like Dali use this mode to decompress
data across the full 64KB address space.

The bug caused the Dali depacker to crash mid-decompression:
- Depacker writes to $D000-$DFFF were silently dropped
- A corrupted RTS jumped to $D8D9 (I/O region), where get_byte
  returned 0 (BRK opcode) instead of the actual decompressed data
- BRK vectored to $FFFE/$FFFF = $0800, causing premature exit at
  instruction 354K instead of running to completion at 597K

Fix: Check the bank register in get_byte/set_byte. I/O is only
suppressed when CHAREN (bit 2) is set AND at least one of LORAM/HIRAM
is set, matching the real C64 PLA truth table.

Also add find_entry_in_snapshot() for scanning the pre-decompression
memory snapshot for JMP instructions that reveal the true program entry
point when the depacker overwrites it during decompression.

events.title: Use hybrid range detection to exclude depacker tables
events.message:
Use hybrid range detection to exclude depacker tables

Depackers like PUCrunch write Huffman/entropy tables just past the
decompressed output. These are contiguous with the output and differ
from the snapshot, making them indistinguishable from real data using
a simple written bitmap or snapshot diff alone.

Fix: use a hybrid approach combining both methods:
- Start addr: first byte in the written bitmap (catches all writes)
- End addr: last snapshot-diff byte, trimmed of small trailing diff
  clusters separated by snapshot-matching gaps (removes depacker
  tables), then extended through written zero-fills (includes
  trailing zeros the depacker wrote to zero-initialized memory)

This correctly produces $0800-$31FF for all three packers:
- LXT/Dali: simple in-place decryption
- Exomizer: inline packer with trailing zero output
- PUCrunch: stores 10 bytes of tables past the output

events.title: Use written bitmap for output range detection
events.message:
Use written bitmap for output range detection

Replace snapshot diff with the write-tracking bitmap for detecting the
unpacked data range. The snapshot diff missed bytes that were written
with the same value as the initial memory (e.g., trailing zeros),
causing the end address to be $301A instead of $31FF.

The written bitmap tracks every set_byte call during emulation,
regardless of whether the value changed, giving the correct range.
Also removes the 64KB snapshot clone, saving memory.

events.title: Fix unpacker Phase 2 for inline packers (Exomizer)
events.message:
Fix unpacker Phase 2 for inline packers (Exomizer)

Inline packers like Exomizer have their depacker code split between
low memory (stack page) and high memory (within the loaded data).
The depacker bounces between these regions during decompression.

The old Phase 2 exit condition (PC >= ret_addr) caused premature exit
on the first jump back to high memory, before decompression started.

New exit conditions for Phase 2:
- PC >= ret_addr AND mem[PC] was written during emulation (jump to
  freshly decompressed code = depacker finished)
- PC >= ret_addr AND PC outside original loaded data range AND
  significant bytes written (decompression to new area)
- ROM exit vector or BASIC RUN detection

Verified: Exomizer-packed file now unpacks correctly with entry=$2E00,
362K instructions, 11KB output. LXT/Dali packer still works.
events.author: ricardoquesada

events.title: Add 6502 emulation-based binary unpacker
events.message:
Add 6502 emulation-based binary unpacker

Implement an unpacker that emulates the 6502 CPU to decompress packed
C64 binaries (Dali/LXT, Exomizer, ProByte, etc.) using the mos6502
crate. The design follows unp64's two-phase algorithm:

- Phase 1: Run from SYS entry until PC drops below RetAdr to find the
  depacker address
- Phase 2: Continue execution (no reset) until the depacker finishes
  and jumps back above RetAdr to the unpacked program

Key features:
- ROM execution interception (GETIN, CLRSCR, SETNAM, IOINIT, RESTOR,
  CHROUT) with force_rts fallback for unrecognized ROM code
- BASIC RUN detection (IsBasicRun1/IsBasicRun2 vectors) to handle
  packers that trigger BASIC RUN after decompression
- Memory snapshot diff for packer-agnostic output range detection
- BASIC SYS parser with arithmetic expression support
- Undocumented/illegal NMOS 6502 opcode support via Nmos6502 variant
- TUI integration via Tools > Unpack Binary menu item

Add test files for LXT/Dali and Exomizer compressed binaries.

events.title: Bootstrap Godot project + adf/rnc/team decoders + variant abstraction
events.message:
Bootstrap Godot project + adf/rnc/team decoders + variant abstraction

Three CLI tools and a Godot project that proves the PC/Amiga variant
abstraction works end-to-end:

- tools/adf-extract: pure-C# Amiga DD ADF reader (OFS + FFS). Verified
  against both SWOS Amiga floppies (125 files extracted, OFS Standard,
  volumes "SWOS" and "SWOS2").
- tools/rnc-decode: RNC ProPack v1 decoder. Both Amiga SWOS executables
  (165735 and 168061 bytes packed) decompress with CRC OK to 351596 and
  357226 bytes respectively. Implementation follows aybe/RNCUnpacker's
  model: 2-byte init, eager refill (bitcount < 16), p starts at offset 0.
- tools/team-decode: SWOS PC/Amiga TEAM.* parser. Verified team header
  (coach offset +0x24 not +0x26 as some specs claim), 3-bit-nibble skill
  packing, decimal nation-code filename suffix. ARSENAL TEAM.008 yields
  ARSENE WENGER as coach and Bergkamp with all-8 P/S/H/T/C/Sp/F.
- game/: Godot 4.6.2 + C# (.NET 9) project with IAssetSource interface
  and concrete PcAssetSource + AmigaAssetSource implementations. Game
  builds + runs headless, loading 1730 PC teams and 1616 Amiga teams from
  the local reference data — both yielding identical first team
  (ALBPETROL PATOS / FATMIR DOGANI / LEONARD HASA) which proves the
  format truly is shared across variants.

Tooling itself is held in .tools/godot/ (portable, gitignored). Original
SWOS data dirs stay gitignored. CLAUDE.md and READMEs updated to match
working build/run commands.

events.title: disasm: per-stage variable-name aliases (HERO_X / HERO_Y for the
events.message:
disasm: per-stage variable-name aliases (HERO_X / HERO_Y for the
four playable-walking stages)

The existing SPECIAL_PURPOSE_VARS table aliases the engine-managed
slots in the 0xE0..0xFF range (HERO_POS_LEFT_RIGHT etc.) globally,
because those vars have stage-invariant meaning. General-purpose
vars (0x00..0xDF) are bytecode-managed and their roles vary by
stage: var 0x01 in LAKE / PRISON / CAVES / CAPSULE is conventionally
the hero's screen-X (verified by comparing call patterns and
position-test predicates), but in INTRO it is a djnz loop counter,
in ENDING / TANK a scratch X-coord register, and in CODE_WHEEL /
PASSCODE a copy-protection symbol-rotation index. A global alias
would mis-name the var in five of nine stages.

Adds a `stage_specific_vars` field to ReleaseData with shape

  &[(u32, &[(u8, &str)])]

(outer key: stage index, inner pairs: (var_id, alias_name)). The
disassembler's variable_name lookup is now a method on
AwvmDisassembler that consults this table for the current
game_level first, falls back to the global SPECIAL_PURPOSE_VARS
table, and last resort emits the literal `[0xNN]` form.

`output_disasm_headers` also emits `<NAME> EQU 0x<NN>` for the
current stage's aliases, alongside the existing SPECIAL_PURPOSE_VARS
EQU declarations, so re-disassembled `.asm` files stand alone for
the assembler.

Per-release tables: msdos and amiga get full HERO_X / HERO_Y
coverage on stages 2/3/4/6 (Lake, Prison, Caves, Capsule). gba_usa,
genesis_europe, snes, symbian_demo only get aliases for the stages
their STAGE_TITLES already names — Caves and Capsule are TODO-named
on those releases and will get aliases when those banks are
identified.

Backwards compatible: `verify_stage 29/29` and `verify_unified
27/27` still pass against the existing source tree (which still has
[0x01] / [0x02] literals; the encoder resolution is symbol-based, so
explicit literal addressing keeps working).

events.title: asm/disasm: also default `zoom=0x40` for full-form CINEMATIC video
events.message:
asm/disasm: also default `zoom=0x40` for full-form CINEMATIC video
when compact form cannot encode the same call

Follow-up to 207a072 (which only defaulted `type=1`). The previous
analysis incorrectly claimed that `zoom=0x40` had to stay explicit
in all full-form CINEMATIC default-zoom cases to disambiguate
against compact form. That is only true when compact form COULD
have encoded the same call, i.e.:

  - byte-literal x ≤ 0xFF
  - byte-literal y ≤ 0xFF
  - offset ≤ 0xFFFE
  - type = CINEMATIC

When ANY of those constraints is violated (variable x/y, large x/y,
large offset, or VIDEO2), compact form is impossible, and dropping
`zoom=0x40` from source is unambiguous.

Across the 5 disassembled ports, 2,139 source lines fell into the
full-form-CINEMATIC-default-zoom case. Of those, only 92 are
truly ambiguous (byte-literal x ≤ 0xFF AND y ≤ 0xFF) — the other
2,047 have variable x or y, or x/y > 0xFF, and were carrying
`zoom=0x40` redundantly.

Encoder change (asm.rs): when source omits `zoom=`, only pick
compact form (opcode 0x80+) when ALL compact constraints hold.
Otherwise fall through to full form with default zoom=0x40 (no
extra bytes, no var-zoom opcode bits set). Backwards-compatible
with explicit `zoom=0x40`.

Decoder change (disasm.rs): for full-form CINEMATIC default-zoom
output, drop the `, zoom=0x40` suffix unless compact form could
have encoded the same call. The 92 ambiguous lines retain explicit
`zoom=0x40` as the marker that forces full-form encoding (vs the
compact form the encoder would otherwise pick).

Tests: 5 new round-trip cases on top of the 4 from 207a072:
  - var-x, var-y, large-x: omitting zoom matches explicit zoom=0x40
  - byte-literal-small case: omitting zoom picks compact (opcode
    0x80+); explicit zoom=0x40 forces full form (opcode 0x40-0x7F).

Source-tree migration in a separate commit in
another-world-source-reconstruction (~26,000 lines simplified;
92 byte-literal-ambiguous lines retained with explicit `zoom=0x40`).
verify_stage 29/29 + verify_unified 27/27 stay green.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: asm/disasm: omit `type=1` from `video` instruction (default)
events.message:
asm/disasm: omit `type=1` from `video` instruction (default)

The `video` instruction's `type=` keyword has two values:
  type=0 → VIDEO2 (shared-bank polygons, ~16% of calls)
  type=1 → CINEMATIC (per-stage polygons, ~84% of calls)

Across the 5 currently disassembled ports, 47,867 of 56,779 video
instructions (84%) had `type=1`. Spelling it out in source text
adds visual noise without distinguishing one call from another.

Encoder change (asm.rs):
  - When source omits the `type=` keyword, default to CINEMATIC (1).
  - Existing source with explicit `type=1` keeps assembling to
    byte-identical output. Backwards-compatible.

Decoder change (disasm.rs):
  - Compact form (opcode 0x80..0xFF, always CINEMATIC): emit
    `video offset=…, x=…, y=…` (drop `type=1, ` prefix).
  - Full form CINEMATIC (opcode 0x40..0x7F, opcode & 3 != 3):
    emit `video offset=…, x=…, y=…, zoom=…` (drop `type=1, `).
  - Full form VIDEO2 (opcode & 3 == 3): unchanged — keeps explicit
    `type=0`. VIDEO2 is the minority case and stays spelled out.

Ambiguity-avoidance: the full-form CINEMATIC default-zoom case
(opcode 0x40-0x7F, no var-zoom bits) keeps `zoom=0x40` explicit.
Without that field, the source text would be indistinguishable
from compact-form CINEMATIC (which has no zoom byte in bytecode).

Tests (asm.rs): 4 new round-trip cases pin down that compact form,
full-form default zoom, and full-form variable zoom all produce
byte-identical output whether `type=1` is explicit or omitted; and
that `type=0` (VIDEO2) still emits the expected opcode bit pattern.

Source-tree migration of `type=1, ` prefix removal across the 5
ported sources (47,867 lines / 701 files in
`another-world-source-reconstruction`) is in a separate commit
in that sibling repo. Its verify_stage 29/29 + verify_unified 27/27
round-trip tests all stay green.

events.title: Fix disassembly cursor jumping to external labels on hex right-arrow
events.message:
Fix disassembly cursor jumping to external labels on hex right-arrow

When 'Display External Labels at top' (settings.all_labels) is enabled,
external label definition lines are prepended to the disassembly array.
Some of these lines have large addresses (e.g. $989A) and appear before
the main binary body in the array.

The bug was triggered by pressing right-arrow in the hex dump at the last
column of a row whose content is a large multi-byte block (e.g. .fill):

1. get_line_index_containing_address($3A10) found the fill block at $3A00 ✓
2. The row-boundary filter rejected it ($3A00 < row_start $3A10)
3. The fallback get_line_index_for_address($3A10) ran its old third pass
   'first line with address >= target', which found the prepended external
   label at $989A before reaching the real fill block — wrong destination.

Fix (two layers):

* disassembly.rs — get_line_index_for_address: split the old third pass
  into a content-first pass (!bytes.is_empty() && address >= target) and
  a label-inclusive fourth pass as last resort. This prevents external
  label lines from being returned before real content when all_labels=true.

* view_hexdump.rs — sync_hex_to_disassembly: add an extra guard to the
  fallback chain: after get_line_index_for_address, if the result is a
  content-free line (external label), fall back to the original containing
  block. This handles the large-fill-spanning-row-boundary case where no
  content line exists at or after row_start_addr.

Also fix a pre-existing compile error in dialog_go_to_symbol.rs tests:
LabelKind::System -> LabelKind::Platform (variant was renamed earlier).

Tests added:
- state::disassembly: test_get_line_index_prefers_content_over_external_label_on_third_pass
- ui::view_hexdump: test_sync_hex_to_disassembly_fill_block_row_boundary_with_all_labels

Fix KickAssembler screencode roundtrip for non-letter chars $00/$1B-$1F

Screen codes $00 and $1B-$1F map to ASCII $40-$5F non-letter characters
(@, [, \, ], ^, _) in handle_screencode_text. KickAssembler's
screencode_mixed encoding only case-swaps letters, so these characters
passed through unchanged, causing the assembler to produce the wrong
byte (e.g. '^' -> $5E instead of screen code $1E).

Fix format_screencode in formatter_kickasm.rs to detect non-letter
characters in the ASCII $40-$5F range and emit them as raw .byte
values using the original screen code (ASCII - $40).

Add regression test test_screencode_non_letter_chars_as_raw_bytes
covering all six affected characters and a mixed letter/non-letter case.

events.title: asm: emit a `<output>.symbols.txt` sidecar listing every label def
events.message:
asm: emit a `<output>.symbols.txt` sidecar listing every label def

Side-output that lists every label-definition's bytecode address
as `address<TAB>name`, in source order (with duplicates retained
when the same name is defined multiple times). EQU values are
NOT included; tools that need EQUs can parse them from source
directly.

Used by the archaeology repo's `tools/resymbolize_literals.py` to
answer "which name(s) live at address X" — the question the
in-memory `asm.symbols` table can't answer because it collapses
collisions to the last-wins entry.

The sidecar is always emitted next to `.bin`; it adds <100 KB
even for the largest stage and costs negligible time. No CLI
flag.
events.author: felipesanches

events.title: disasm: drop the `;@raw=…` fallback in classify_encoding
events.message:
disasm: drop the `;@raw=…` fallback in classify_encoding

awvm-asm rejects `;@raw=` since 2026-05-04 (commit a1c6661), so
emitting it from the disassembler creates output the assembler
won't read. Drop the fallback: canonical encodings now produce
text without any annotation, and the four catalogued
non-canonical patterns continue to emit `;@enc=alt`,
`;@enc=legacy_d`, `;@enc=legacy_e`, or a `_trailing=0x00`
operand.

If a fresh extraction surfaces a fifth non-canonical pattern,
verify_stage / verify_unified will catch it (byte-match fails)
and the new pattern needs a new arm in `classify_encoding`.

verify_stage 29/29 + verify_unified 27/27 still pass.
events.author: felipesanches

events.title: asm: rip `;@raw=` parsing (Phase 2 of migration)
events.message:
asm: rip `;@raw=` parsing (Phase 2 of migration)

The source-reconstruction tree has been fully migrated off
`;@raw=` annotations:
  - per-branch sources: 0 `;@raw=`
  - _unified/ tree: 0 `;@raw=`
  - audit --strict: OK across active levels

(See archaeology repo's `tools/resolve_raw_collisions.py` and
`docs/raw_to_enc_migration_plan.md`.)

This commit removes the `;@raw=` parser from awvm-asm:
  - delete `parse_raw_marker` function
  - drop `Instruction.raw: Option<Vec<u8>>` field
  - drop the `;@raw=` short-circuit at the top of `encode()`
  - turn any source line containing `;@raw=` into a hard parse
    panic with a pointer to the migration plan

The runtime behaviour for `;@enc=…` markers (`alt`, `legacy_d`,
`legacy_e`, setPalette `_trailing` operand) introduced in
ad99497 is unchanged. Existing source assembles byte-identically
(verify_stage 29/29 + verify_unified 27/27).

Going forward, `;@raw=` is strictly forbidden. New non-canonical
encoding patterns must be added via an explicit `;@enc=…` form
or a new dedicated operand syntax.
events.author: felipesanches

events.title: asm + disasm: support `;@enc=…` named encoding selectors
events.message:
asm + disasm: support `;@enc=…` named encoding selectors

Adds explicit named-encoding selectors so the source can request
non-canonical AW VM byte forms without resorting to `;@raw=`
byte-override fallbacks:

  - `;@enc=alt` on a `video … zoom=[var]` line: opcode bit 1
    (0x02) instead of canonical bit 0 (0x01) for the zoom-as-var
    flag. Both decode identically, but the original Chahi-era
    bytecode mixes the two — this preserves the bit-1 form.

  - `;@enc=legacy_d` / `;@enc=legacy_e` on a `bankSwitch N` line:
    the operand word becomes `0x07Dx` / `0x07Ex` instead of the
    canonical `0x3E8x`. The disassembler accepts both, prints a
    "WARN: uncommon value" for the legacy forms; this lets the
    encoder reproduce them on demand.

  - `setPalette N, _trailing=0xNN`: explicit waste-byte operand
    (canonical hardcodes 0xFF; three places in the original
    bytecode use 0x00 for `setPalette 0x00`).

Disassembler classifies each instruction's byte form post-decode
and emits the appropriate `;@enc=…` marker (or `_trailing=…`
operand). For patterns not yet catalogued, falls back to the
existing `;@raw=…` annotation so byte-match never breaks during
the migration.

The `;@raw=` parser path is retained as a transitional fallback;
it will be removed entirely once every load-bearing `;@raw=` in
the source tree is migrated to a named form. Plan and acceptance
criteria in `another-world-archaeology/docs/raw_to_enc_migration_plan.md`
and tracking issue #0083 in the same repo.

Validated: existing source tree (with `;@raw=` annotations
preserved) still byte-matches via verify_stage 29/29 and
verify_unified 27/27 (the new code paths only fire when
`;@enc=…` markers are present).
events.author: felipesanches

events.title: Emit chaos_creatures from gen_chaos_data_c.py in real piece-code order via the $E3E0 lookup table, matching the actual game's piece-code mapping rather than chaos.py CREATURES display order.
events.message:
Emit chaos_creatures from gen_chaos_data_c.py in real piece-code order via the $E3E0 lookup table, matching the actual game's piece-code mapping rather than chaos.py CREATURES display order.

Previously the generator iterated chaos.py CREATURES (sorted by name_addr for the HtmlWriter's display table) and emitted entries in that order, with the implicit assumption that chaos_creatures[i] = piece code (i+1). The chaos.ctl annotation at $E3E0 ("39 two-byte pointers ... indexed by piece code minus 1") is the actual source of truth for the piece-code-to-creature mapping, and that ordering is completely different - e.g. Bat is real piece 22, Ghost is 29, Magic Fire is 35.

Now: the generator reads the $E3E0 entries, pairs each name_addr with the chaos.py CREATURES tuple by name_addr to inherit the undead/flying/mount flags, and emits chaos_creatures with one entry per piece code 1..40. Piece 1 is the corpse placeholder at $E440 (empty name); piece 40 is Wall (special case at $EA16, not in $E3E0).

Also emit named piece-code constants in chaos_data.h: CHAOS_PIECE_GHOST=29, CHAOS_PIECE_WRAITH=31, CHAOS_PIECE_MAGIC_FIRE=35, CHAOS_PIECE_BLOB=34, plus the structure codes 36-40, so port code can refer to them by name.

Resolve the BA77 scan_line_squares annotation: confirm and document that piece codes 29 (Ghost), 31 (Wraith), 35 (Magic Fire) plus corpse-flagged tiles get overpainted with the empty highlight sprite at $EB51 immediately before the Bresenham line walk in $98DB. This is the LOS transparency mechanism - empirically verified by user testing 2026-05-02. Removes the 'needs further verification' caveat that was on the original annotation.

Update $BABE annotation to make explicit that the highlight sprite at $EB51 is empty (32 zero bytes) and that calling $BABE on a transparent piece's tile ERASES that piece's pixels for the duration of the LOS check.

events.title: Add tools/trace_los.py and tools/debug_los.py for investigating the LOS transparency mechanism.
events.message:
Add tools/trace_los.py and tools/debug_los.py for investigating the LOS transparency mechanism.

The harness currently fails to reproduce the live game's LOS-blocking behaviour - even Wall and Giant Rat (which empirically block in-game) come back clear under trace. A sanity check that pre-paints framebuffer pixels confirms $98DB itself works, so the bug is that the IM 2 ISR / MPRINT-driven board-render path doesn't actually paint sprites under trace.py interrupt simulation. Left in tree as a starting point for further investigation; see chaos-c docs/los.md for the empirical state.

events.title: Annotated all 127 remaining untitled routines, taking the disassembly to 100% c-routine coverage (335 of 335 routines now carry titles, descriptions and labels).
events.message:
Annotated all 127 remaining untitled routines, taking the disassembly to 100% c-routine coverage (335 of 335 routines now carry titles, descriptions and labels).

Wave 3 covered 62 routines: the magic-weapon common-paths ($837D-$8486), the Subversion / RaiseDead / Turmoil sub-routines ($851B-$872B), the spell-orchestration helpers ($9324-$97BB), the board / range / cursor helpers ($BE86-$C0D8) including the chessboard-distance predicate at $BEE8 (formula: 2*max(dx,dy) + min(dx,dy)), and the AI movement and target-evaluation helpers ($C9D4-$CDB8).

Wave 4 covered the remaining 65 routines: the game-load preamble ($5B00-$5BB3), the working-memory stubs ($7700-$7D52), the summon / placement / line-of-sight helpers ($9856-$9DAA), the inter-turn animation block ($A0FE-$A956), the pre-movement state init cluster ($AB0A-$ABDC), the IM 2 sprite-cycling interrupt service routine and its inner helpers ($DF0C-$DFB9), the board-to-pixel converter at $E005, and the entire orphaned dead-code block at $D588-$D8C4 which is never called from live code (per the existing $D52E annotation).

Speculative entries are clearly marked with "exact role not yet verified" rather than over-claiming. The Wave 3 / Wave 4 dispatched read-only research agents had varying confidence on the deeper helper routines; conservative wording reflects that.

events.title: Documented the seven utility, attack and alignment spell handlers - Disbelieve, Subversion, Raise Dead, Turmoil, Shadow Form, Law/Chaos shifters, and the four alignment attacks - with the dice predicate, validation chain and post-success state changes verified against the Z80.
events.message:
Documented the seven utility, attack and alignment spell handlers - Disbelieve, Subversion, Raise Dead, Turmoil, Shadow Form, Law/Chaos shifters, and the four alignment attacks - with the dice predicate, validation chain and post-success state changes verified against the Z80.

Flagged Subversion's dice direction as inverted versus the alignment attacks: same offset-19 stat, opposite comparison, so high-stat creatures are easier to subvert and harder to alignment-attack. Left in the doc as a note since it could be deliberate or a flipped-comparison bug.

Fixed the Decree / Justice naming swap in the alignment-attack human cast loop. The multi-shot rule is 1 shot for spell indices 45-46 (Vengeance, Decree, bias +/-1) and 3 shots for 47-48 (Dark Power, Justice, bias +/-2).

Confirmed the Law / Chaos shifters are a thin wrapper around the standard dice routine - the world-balance shift happens inside spell_casting_check on success.

Confirmed Raise Dead has no separate magic-resistance check despite earlier descriptions implying one.

Confirmed Disbelieve consumes its slot whether or not the target was an illusion. Single BIT 4 test on the target's +481 byte decides whether to destroy.

Documented Turmoil's bit-7 marker mechanism that prevents pieces being re-shuffled within the same pass.

events.title: snes + gba_usa: fix 0x2F9D address mistake + add inner-label semantic names
events.message:
snes + gba_usa: fix 0x2F9D address mistake + add inner-label semantic names

The previous commit (5c528db) put the GBA `IF_BEAST_NEAR_THEN_REACT_…`
entry at gba binary 0x2F9D — but that's a different (unrelated)
bytecode location. The actual GBA address for that routine is
0x2FE8.

Fixed + extended both ports' entries with inner-label semantic
names so the rename canonicalizer can fully unify the
beast-proximity-routine region:

  snes (cart):
    (0x2F9C, "DEAD_LABEL_2F85_RET")             ; dead routine ret
    (0x2F9D, "CHECK_IF_BEAST_IS_NEAR_LESTER")
    (0x2FC3, "CHECK_IF_BEAST_IS_NEAR_LESTER__OUT_OF_RANGE_RET")
    (0x2FC4, "IF_BEAST_NEAR_THEN_REACT_ELSE_KILL_THREAD")
    (0x2FCB, "IF_BEAST_NEAR_THEN_REACT_ELSE_KILL_THREAD_2")

  gba_usa:
    (0x2FC0, "DEAD_LABEL_2FA9_RET")             ; dead routine ret
    (0x2FC1, "CHECK_IF_BEAST_IS_NEAR_LESTER")
    (0x2FE7, "CHECK_IF_BEAST_IS_NEAR_LESTER__OUT_OF_RANGE_RET")
    (0x2FE8, "IF_BEAST_NEAR_THEN_REACT_ELSE_KILL_THREAD")
    (0x2FEF, "IF_BEAST_NEAR_THEN_REACT_ELSE_KILL_THREAD_2")

The dead-routine wrapper is at cart 0x2F85 / gba 0x2FA9 — its
first instruction is `jmp CHECK_IF_BEAST_IS_NEAR_LESTER`, so
everything below (including its `ret` at the end) is dead code.
Naming it `DEAD_LABEL_<addr>_RET` makes that clear in the source
and lets cross-branch unification proceed (the dead bytes are
identical between ports; they just had divergent labels for the
ret target).

Result on the LAKE unification (in another-world-source-
reconstruction): 18 → 11 ;@if blocks. All 11 remaining are real
semantic differences between the ports (gba-only `song` calls,
cart-only `ret` instructions, a `PAUSE_SLICES` tuning value
divergence, a trailing-FILL chunk-padding length difference).
This is the theoretical floor — no tooling artifacts left.
events.author: felipesanches

events.title: snes + gba_usa: add semantic labels for the LAKE beast-proximity routines
events.message:
snes + gba_usa: add semantic labels for the LAKE beast-proximity routines

Two routines in LAKE (level 1) appear at swapped addresses between
the ports — same code, but they trade physical offsets:

  Routine A: range-check.
    Tests whether [0x0C] (subject) is within ±[0x13] of [0x01]
    (target center); sets [0x07]=1 if in range, 0 otherwise.
    Given LAKE's "Beast Chase" context this is almost certainly
    the beast-vs-lester proximity test.

  Routine B: the consumer.
    `je [0x07], 0x01, LABEL_30E4 / killChannel`. If routine A
    found the beast in range, branches to a follow-up; otherwise
    terminates this scheduler thread.

The address swap:

  | routine | snes (cart) | gba_usa |
  |---|---|---|
  | A — range check | 0x2F9D | 0x2FC1 |
  | B — react-or-kill | 0x2FC4 | 0x2F9D |

Note the GBA reused address 0x2F9D for routine B (not a typo!).

Adding semantic-name entries to both releases' KNOWN_LABELS so
the disasm renders the same name for the same logical routine
across ports:

  CHECK_IF_BEAST_IS_NEAR_LESTER             — routine A
  IF_BEAST_NEAR_THEN_REACT_ELSE_KILL_THREAD — routine B

This unblocks cross-branch unification (the another-world-source-
reconstruction repo's LAKE.asm.in was emitting `;@if`/`;@elif`
blocks for `jmp/call/cond_jump` instructions whose targets used
these now-resolved swapped names).

Discovered while pushing LAKE unification to its floor; user
proposed the names. See research/09 (Phase 3b) and the inline
discussion in the archaeology repo for context.

events.title: gba_usa: extract cinematic.rom + correct over-extracted bytecode_chunks
events.message:
gba_usa: extract cinematic.rom + correct over-extracted bytecode_chunks

The cartridge-format extractor `prepare_cartridge_romset` now also
writes `cinematic.rom` from a per-port `cinematic_chunks` spec
(empty `&[]` by default). Adds the field to `CartridgeSpec`.

`gba_usa`: was extracting both bytecode AND adjacent cinematic-
polygon data into `bytecode.rom`. The previous spec declared each
level's `bytecode_chunks` entry as a full 64 KB
(`(0x6ea74, 0x10000)`), but the actual bytecode is much shorter
(level_0: ~9.9 KB, level_1: ~21 KB) — the rest of each 64 KB
region in the GBA ROM is the level's cinematic-polygon slab. The
disassembler then either tried to decode those data bytes as
instructions (producing nonsense) or emitted them as `db <bytes>`.

Fixed:
  bytecode_chunks: &[(0x6EA74, 0x26B3), (0x813F8, 0x5225)]
  cinematic_chunks: &[(0x71128, 0x10000), (0x86620, 0x10000)]

Verified: at the cinematic-base offsets (0x71128 and 0x86620),
ALL CINEMATIC_xxx labels referenced by the disassembler resolve
to valid polygon-entry bytes (≥ 0xC0 fill, or low-6==0x02
hierarchy):
  level_0: 570 / 570 (100 %)
  level_1: 660 / 660 (100 %)

The new `bytecode.rom` md5 changes (cinematic data no longer
inlined). The level_0 chunk was `c978f22c…`, now `c21c7864…`.
Downstream consumers (e.g., the byte-matching source-
reconstruction at another-world-source-reconstruction) need to
update the expected md5 — but the actual bytecode content is
correct now, and the unified INTRO.asm.in `;@if` count drops as a
result (the trailing-padding divergence becomes a shared
`FILL(N, 0xFF)` instead of bytes-vs-bytes).

`snes`, `snes_eu`, `genesis_europe` keep `cinematic_chunks: &[]`
for now — their cinematic-data offsets in the cartridge ROMs
haven't been mapped yet. SNES-EU's `level_0` cinematic is at
ROM offset 0x486E0 (95 % verified, brute-force scan); follow-up
needed.

GBA stages 3-7 (per `STAGE_TITLES`) also remain unmapped: the
spec only declares `level_0` and `level_1` chunks. The
`(bytecode | sep | cinematic | small palette)` pattern probably
repeats; brute-forcing once their disasm exists would pin them
down.

Discovery thread + verification details: research/10 in the
archaeology repo (`docs/content/research/10-gba-cinematic-data-found.md`).
Tracked as issue #0068 there.

- dump_theme_files() now writes embedded TOML files directly (like

events.title: mac-rsrc-walk: walk Mac resource forks; mac-stuffit-extract: decompress
events.message:
mac-rsrc-walk: walk Mac resource forks; mac-stuffit-extract: decompress

Adds the second stage of the Mac extraction pipeline + fixes a
critical bug in the first stage.

mac-stuffit-extract: SitEntry.data_fork / .resource_fork are stored
in COMPRESSED form by the stuffit crate (default lazy
decompression). The previous version was writing the compressed
bytes verbatim, which is why downstream tools saw random-looking
high-entropy data. Now calls SitEntry::decompressed_forks() so
.data and .rsrc files contain the real (decompressed) fork bytes.
On the AW Mac fixture this changes the v1.0.3 .rsrc from a 555 KB
compressed blob into a 928 KB raw resource fork that parses
cleanly.

mac-rsrc-walk (NEW): takes a raw resource fork file (typically
produced by mac-stuffit-extract) and emits each resource as a
separate file named <TYPE>_<ID>[_<safe_name>].bin. Uses the
upstream macbinary = "0.2.1" crate. Supports --summary-only mode
for surveying which resource types exist in a fork without
extracting.

End-to-end on the v1.0.3 main app (`Out of this World™ 1.0.3`):

  TYPE      count   total_bytes
  Estr        192          6114    (error/event strings — 192 entries
                                    matches no DOS resource count, but
                                    is suspiciously round; under
                                    investigation)
  CODE          7         38250    (68k engine code, 7 segments)
  PICT          9        112205    (Mac graphics)
  snd          97        722689    (75% of fork is sound; same byte
                                    count across all 3 versions)
  OOTW          1            15    (custom 4cc — game-specific
                                    copyright stamp; content varies
                                    per version)
  ... plus standard Mac fluff (ALRT, DITL, DLOG, vers, ...)

mac-stuffit-extract: extract data + resource forks from 1993 Mac .sit

Adds a fifth helper binary alongside adf-extract / opera-list /
valve-pak-extract: parse classic Macintosh StuffIt archives and
write each entry's data fork + resource fork as separate files.

Uses the upstream `stuffit = "0.1.4"` crate (StuffIt 5.0 + SIT! 1.x,
compression methods 0/13/14/15) and pins `macbinary = "0.2.1"` for
the eventual resource-fork walker (which would surface individual
TYPE+ID-keyed Mac resources within each .rsrc — that's the next
step, not in this commit).

Smoke-tested on the 1993 OOTW Mac fixture (out_of_this_world.sit,
3.7 MiB) — yields 141 entries including:

  Out of this World™ 1.0.3       data: 0 bytes      rsrc: 555,039 bytes
  Out of this World™ (1.0.2)     data: 0 bytes      rsrc: 529,036 bytes
  Out of this World 1.0           data: 0 bytes      rsrc: 524,598 bytes
  ... 2 updaters, 50 .rsrc forks total, 141 entries, 4 MB total

The three application builds give us 68k Mac genealogy material
across three close versions (1.0 / 1.0.2 / 1.0.3) — a higher-density
dataset than most of the cross-CPU comparisons we've done so far.

events.title: 3do extractor: fix Opera FS DirEntry layout + dir-block chaining
events.message:
3do extractor: fix Opera FS DirEntry layout + dir-block chaining

Two bugs that were preventing recursion past the first directory
entry:

1. Avatar list is at offset 68 of each DirEntry, not 72 — there is
   no 4-byte reserved field between `last_avatar` and the avatars.
   Total fixed prefix is 68 bytes (flags + id + type + block_size +
   byte_count + block_count + burst + gap + 32-byte name +
   last_avatar) and entry size is 68 + 4*(last_avatar+1).

2. Each dir block's `next_block` field is a *logical* block index
   within the directory (relative to avatar 0's first block), not
   an absolute LBA. Physical LBA of the next block is therefore
   `avatar_start + next_block`. Without this, walking GameData
   tried to follow next_block=1 directly, ending up in the disc
   lead-in.

Verified by extracting the full disc tree from "Out of this World
(USA).bin": 423 files across root + GameData/ + StalData/ +
System/Tasks/ — including the suggestive `GameData/song1..30`,
`GameData/EndShape1/2`, `GameData/FileN`, `StalData/*.AIFF`, plus
the ARM-binary `ootw` at the root.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: extractors: add valve-pak-extract for the Windows XP 1.1c Pak01.pak
events.message:
extractors: add valve-pak-extract for the Windows XP 1.1c Pak01.pak

The Windows XP build of Another World 1.1c (distributed via Eric
Chahi's anotherworld.fr as `AnotherWorld_Demo.exe`) ships its
assets in a single `Data/Pak01.pak` file inside an NSIS installer.

The PAK format is the well-known Valve `PACK` magic + 64-byte
file-table entries (filename + offset + length), trivially
parseable.

awvm/src/valve_pak.rs
  PakReader + extract_to_dir() helper. Pure Rust, no deps.

awvm-tools/src/bin/valve-pak-extract.rs
  CLI: `valve-pak-extract <pak> <out_dir>`. Round-tripped on the
  cached `Pak01.pak` (113 MiB → 448 files, matching the
  directory-entry count).

IMPORTANT FINDING — Win XP 1.1c is a different engine entirely.
The Pak01 contents are: DirectX vertex/pixel shaders, BMP
textures, OGG audio, WAV sounds, JPG documentation. NOT the Eric
Chahi VM bytecode that the rest of awvm-tools targets. The 1.1c
build is a Windows-XP-era graphical remake using DirectX, with a
distinct codebase from the original 1991 Amiga / 1992 MS-DOS / etc
ports. So this extractor:

- produces useful asset extraction for the WinXP build
  (researchers may want to compare its localised text /
   re-rendered cinematic art to the original);
- does NOT feed `awvm-disasm` — there's no VM bytecode in Pak01
  to disassemble.

Three other extractors remain on the project's wishlist:
- snes-eu (different chunk offsets from USA — needs RE)
- atari-st-pasti (Pasti `.stx` reader + Atari ST FAT12 + bank
  format; same engine as Amiga so much should be reusable)
- 3do-cue-bin (3DO Opera filesystem reader)

events.title: adf: pure-Rust OFS reader + adf-extract CLI; amiga validates byte-identical
events.message:
adf: pure-Rust OFS reader + adf-extract CLI; amiga validates byte-identical

Adds an Amiga Disk File reader so the Amiga release can actually be
fed real input. The format covered is the OFS family (DOS\0 / DOS\2
/ DOS\4) — sufficient for the AnotherWorld retro-presskit fixture
and the original Eric Chahi releases. FFS would need a different
file-data layout (no per-block header, header-table-driven
chaining instead of `next_data`); we error out with a clear message
on FFS input rather than silently producing garbage.

awvm/src/adf.rs
  AdfReader exposes:
    AdfReader::from_bytes / ::from_path → builds the reader
    AdfReader::list_root_files → returns (name, data) for every
      ST_FILE entry reachable from the rootblock's hash table
      (skips ST_USERDIR for now)
    extract_to_dir(adf_path, out_dir) → convenience: read +
      list + write each file to out_dir

  Format details follow <https://lclevy.free.fr/adflib/adf_info.html>:
  bootblock magic check, rootblock at sector 880 (or whatever the
  bootblock's offset-8 word says when non-zero), 72-entry hash
  table with collision-chain via SECTOR_SIZE-16, OFS file payload
  walked via first_data + per-block next_data with 488-byte chunks
  at offset 24, file size cross-checked against the header's
  BSIZE-188 word.

awvm-tools/src/bin/adf-extract.rs
  CLI: `adf-extract <adf_path>... <output_dir>`. Multiple ADFs
  extract into the same output dir (later disks overwrite earlier
  ones on filename collisions). Tested against the AnotherWorld
  retro-presskit's two disks: 11 + 9 files extracted (with three
  duplicates between disks) totalling 13 unique files including
  `another` + bank01..bank0D (no bank05 in this presskit).

awvm-tools/Cargo.toml
  Adds the `adf-extract` binary target.

End-to-end amiga validation:
  1. Unzip AnotherWorld-Retro-presskit.zip (twice, per the
     metadata.json note).
  2. adf-extract DiskA.adf DiskB.adf <dir> → produces `another`
     + bank01..bank0D in <dir>.
  3. awvm-disasm <dir> all_levels amiga → all 9 levels disassembled.
  4. diff against Python reference output: BYTE-IDENTICAL on every
     level (totalling ~5.4 MB of disassembly text).

amiga is the third release with full byte-identical parity (after
msdos and genesis_europe).

events.title: phase-f: add symbian_demo dispatch (zlib + LZMA1)
events.message:
phase-f: add symbian_demo dispatch (zlib + LZMA1)

Adds the last remaining release. Port of
`releases/symbian_demo/symbian2romset.py:SymbianDemoROMSet`:

1. Read `<input_dir>/locked_anotherworld.sis`.
2. Slice the zlib payload at `[0xBBA, 0xBBA + 749540)`.
3. zlib-decompress the slice (outer layer) into a `raw` buffer.
4. For each `(start, end)` chunk in the bytecode/cinematic recipes,
   LZMA1-decompress `raw[start..end]` and pad the result to 0x10000
   bytes with `0xFF`. Concatenate slabs into bytecode.rom (8 levels)
   and cinematic.rom (1 slab).
5. Copy the hardcoded text/font ROMs from `hardcoded_data/`.

New dependencies in awvm-tools:
- `flate2 = "1.0"`     for the zlib outer layer (pure-rust backend).
- `lzma-rs = "0.3"`    for raw LZMA1 ("alone" format) decompression.

Both are pure-Rust (no C linkage) so the workspace continues to build
with just `cargo build --release` and no system libs.

Validation: the Symbian-OS .sis fixture is not in the local cache,
so the path is wired up and dispatches correctly but is exercised
only by a smoke test (graceful "No such file or directory" error
when the fixture is absent). The code follows the Python reference
verbatim — chunks, offsets, padding behaviour, hardcoded fallback
for the string ROMs (Python doesn't extract symbian-specific
strings either).

With this commit Phase F is structurally complete: every release
recognised by `releases::by_slug` has a working prep path.
Validation against actual fixtures is gated on availability:
- msdos:           validated, byte-identical
- amiga:           code in place, needs ADF unpacking infrastructure
- snes:            code in place, needs USA ROM (we only have EU)
- genesis_europe:  validated, byte-identical
- gba_usa:         code in place, needs USA prototype ROM
- symbian_demo:    code in place, needs the .sis fixture

phase-f: port genesis_europe text-string extraction → full parity

Adds optional `string_extraction: Option<(start, end)>` to
`CartridgeSpec` that captures the per-cartridge string-table
recipe. When present, the cartridge prep walks the ROM byte range
reading `(BE 16-bit index, null-terminated ASCII string)` records
and writes them to `<release>/romset/str_data.rom` and

for those releases).

`genesis_europe_level-N.asm` are now BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Python
reference, and `str_data.rom` matches byte-for-byte. The text-
opcode `;` comments now read the correct genesis-specific strings
(e.g. "PRESS BUTTON OR RETURN TO CONTINUE" instead of MSDOS's
"PRESS BUTTON TO CONTINUE   PRESS START FOR CODE ENTRY").

Generalises the per-release prep into two paths:

- prepare_cartridge_romset (snes, genesis_europe, gba_usa) —

CartridgeSpec captures the per-release recipe (source filename
+ list of (start, length) chunks). The chunks are transcribed from:
- snes2romset.py:           Out of This World (USA).sfc, 2 chunks
- genesis2romset.py:        Another World (Europe).md,  7 chunks

`msdos_level-N.asm`, now `<release_slug>_level-N.asm` to match
Python.

disassemble cleanly. .asm output is mostly byte-identical to
Python's, with one known divergence: text-opcode comments contain
different strings because Python's genesis2romset extracts a
genesis-specific str_data.rom *from the cartridge* (the strings
are baked into ROM at offset 0x382B..0x46FE), while we still copy
msdos's hardcoded string ROMs. The bytecode bytes themselves are
identical and `;@raw=...` annotations match — so round-trip
correctness is preserved; only the human-readable text comments
differ.
