events.title: phase-f: add amiga release support to awvm-disasm CLI
events.message:
phase-f: add amiga release support to awvm-disasm CLI

The amiga release uses the same `memlist + bank<NN>` packaging as
msdos, with two differences captured by the new `MemlistSource`
enum and `uppercase` flag:

- The memlist is embedded inside a single `another` binary at offset
  0x5ec2 for `20 * 147 = 2940` bytes (vs. msdos's standalone
  `memlist.bin`).
- The bank files use UPPERCASE names (`BANK01`..`BANK0D`) vs
  msdos's lowercase.

Refactors the previously-msdos-only `build_resources` function into
`prepare_bank_release(input_dir, release_out, uppercase, source)`
which any "bank format" release can reuse. The CLI now matches on
the slug:

  msdos => MemlistSource::File("memlist.bin"), uppercase=false
  amiga => MemlistSource::Embedded { file: "another",
                                     offset: 0x5ec2,
                                     length: 2940 },
           uppercase=true

The remaining cartridge-format releases (snes, genesis_europe,
gba_usa, symbian_demo) error out with a "not implemented yet"
message; they need a different prep path entirely (direct cartridge
extraction into bytecode.rom — no banks, no resources/ intermediate)
and will land in follow-up commits.

Validation of the amiga path requires the corresponding fixture
(presskit ADFs unpacked into a directory with `another` + BANK<NN>
files), which we don't have in the local cache yet — adding ADF
extraction support is a separate piece of work outside the awvm-tools
toolchain proper. The msdos pipeline's Phase-C parity still passes,
confirming the refactor preserves existing behaviour.

Refactors the AWVM disassembler so it no longer hardcodes references

`ReleaseData` struct (exposed as a `pub const RELEASE_DATA` in each

in the perf harness because pycairo crashes mid-run on this fixture.
Previously the Rust binary still ran the polygon stage, so the
benchmark compared "Rust doing more work" against "Python doing
less" — making the disasm speedup look smaller than it actually is.

  Now passes `--no-polygons` to the Rust binary, matching the
  Python harness's polygon-decoder stub.

    banks2resources         python 1318 ms   rust  26 ms   ≈ 51× faster
    awvm-disasm full        python 27.4 s   rust 474 ms   ≈ 58× faster
    awvm-asm one level      python  196 ms   rust  13 ms   ≈ 15× faster

events.title: round-trip: port `;@raw=` annotations to Rust (mirrors Python)
events.message:
round-trip: port `;@raw=` annotations to Rust (mirrors Python)

Carries the round-trip-to-original fix from the previous commit
(awvm-disasm.py + awvm-asm.py) into the Rust port.

exectrace/src/tracer.rs
  Tracer gains `current_consumed: Option<Vec<u8>>` plus a final map
  `consumed_bytes: BTreeMap<u32, Vec<u8>>`. The `run` loop installs
  a fresh buffer at the start of each instruction; `fetch()`
  appends to it. After `disasm_instruction` returns, the buffer is
  harvested into `consumed_bytes`. Disassembler implementations
  observe the in-flight bytes via the new
  `Tracer::current_consumed_bytes(&self) -> Option<&[u8]>` accessor.

awvm/src/disasm.rs
  `Disassembler::disasm_instruction` for `AwvmDisassembler` is now
  a thin wrapper that:
    1. Calls a new private `do_disasm_instruction` helper holding
       the existing big opcode-dispatch match.
    2. Reads `tracer.current_consumed_bytes()` and appends a
       `;@raw=0xAA,0xBB,...` suffix to the returned instruction text.
  The text format matches the Python reference verbatim:
       `<instr>\t;@raw=0xAA,0xBB,...`

awvm/src/asm.rs
  The `Instruction` struct gains an `Option<Vec<u8>>` `raw` field.
  `parse_lines` extracts the `;@raw=` marker from each line BEFORE
  the comment-strip step (mirroring Python). `encode` emits the
  raw bytes verbatim when present, skipping the canonical encoder.
  A new `parse_raw_marker` helper does the actual scan.

Verified locally — all four checks pass for every MSDOS level:
  (1) python disasm → python asm == original bytecode
  (2) rust   disasm → rust   asm == original bytecode
  (3) python .asm == rust .asm
  (4) python .bin == rust .bin

The validation harness lands in the next commit.

events.title: round-trip: emit and honor `;@raw=` annotations in the Python disasm/asm
events.message:
round-trip: emit and honor `;@raw=` annotations in the Python disasm/asm

The original `disasm → asm` pipeline does not round-trip to the
input bytecode for MSDOS levels 1..7: the disassembler discards
information that the assembler cannot reconstruct (the unused bits
in 0x40-family video opcodes — bit 0x02 vs 0x01 in the
zoom-encoding pair — and the "waste byte" of `setPalette` which is
written as 0xFF unconditionally even when the original had any
other value).

This commit fixes round-trip exactness in both pieces:

awvm-disasm.py
  AWVM_Trace gains a `fetch()` override that, when an instruction
  is being decoded, appends every fetched byte to a per-instruction
  buffer. A wrapper around `disasm_instruction` harvests the buffer
  after the per-opcode decoder runs and appends a
  `;@raw=0xAA,0xBB,...` annotation to the returned text. The
  annotation is the EXACT byte sequence the disassembler consumed.

awvm-asm.py
  Each input line is scanned for the `;@raw=...` marker before
  comments are stripped. When present, the encoder shortcut emits
  the annotated bytes verbatim and skips the canonical encoding
  path. Operand parsing still happens (so labels are resolved for
  unannotated instructions, and the `EQU` table is still built),
  but the annotated bytes take precedence whenever they exist.

Verified locally: all 9 MSDOS levels' bytecode round-trips
byte-for-byte through the Python disasm + asm pipeline. The same
annotations will be honoured by the Rust port in the follow-up
commit.

events.title: phase-e: port awvm-asm to Rust with parity validation
events.message:
phase-e: port awvm-asm to Rust with parity validation

Faithful Rust port of `awvm-asm.py`:

awvm/src/asm.rs
  Tokeniser + two-pass assembler. Operand parser handles `[var]`
  references, `key=value` keyword args, hex/decimal/symbolic
  scalars. Encoder mirrors every Python branch:
   - mov/add/sub immediate vs variable (incl. sub via add-with-
     negative-immediate when src is a constant, byte 0x03)
   - and/or/shl/shr (immediate-only)
   - jmp/call/ret/break/killChannel/GameOver
   - text/play/song/setup/load/copyVideoPage/fill (keyword operands)
   - freezeChannels/unfreezeChannels/deleteChannels
   - djnz, conditional jumps (je/jne/jg/jge/jl/jle) with the same
     subopcode bit layout (0x80 for var c, 0x40 for 16-bit imm)
   - setPalette (operand << 8 | 0xFF)
   - bankSwitch (0x3E80 | bankId)
   - selectVideoPage / blitFramebuffer
   - video — the full 0x40-family bit-twiddling: 0x80 family for
     compact form (no zoom), 0x40 family with the per-axis var/
     8-bit/16-bit choices and the VIDEO2 flag at bit 0x03

awvm-tools/src/bin/awvm-asm.rs is the CLI; output filename is
`<input>.bin` next to the input.

Phase E validation harness (validation/run_phase_e.sh) drives a
fresh disasm of every MSDOS level (Phase C, trusted), then assembles
each .asm twice — once with the Rust awvm-asm, once with the Python
awvm-asm.py — and diffs the resulting .bin pairs.

Result: ALL 9 LEVELS BYTE-IDENTICAL between the Python and Rust
assemblers.

Note on the original-byte round-trip: the Python README aspires to
`disasm(bytecode) → asm() → original bytecode`, but that does not
hold for levels 1..7 of the MSDOS release in the Python tooling
itself — the disasm discards a few unused/uninterpreted bits in
some opcode bytes (e.g. unused bits in the conditional-jump
subopcode), so the asm cannot reconstruct them. The Rust port
matches Python's behaviour exactly here, including the same
non-round-trip on the same offsets. Closing that gap is a separate
quality issue that is not part of "feature parity with Python".

events.title: phase-d: port polygon decoder (semantic SVG equivalence)
events.message:
phase-d: port polygon decoder (semantic SVG equivalence)

Faithful Rust port of `releases/common_data/decode_polygons.py`:
- awvm/src/polygons.rs implements `PolygonDecoder` with the same
  bit-level polygon-record semantics: header byte either fills a
  single shape (value >= 0xC0) or descends into a hierarchy
  (value & 0x3F == 2). Coordinates use the `zoom * x / DEFAULT_ZOOM`
  scaling and the `pgc - bbox/2 + offset` framing the Python uses.
- The 4-vertex degenerate-line lozenge hack is preserved verbatim.
- Palette colour decoding (4-bit halves doubled to 6-bit, then
  normalised to 0..1) matches Python.
- The `extract` method writes one `<path>` per filled polygon to
  `<label>.svg` in the target directory.

Per the project agreement (user direction: "Semantic equivalence
accepted"), the SVG output is NOT byte-identical to pycairo's:
- We emit `fill="#rrggbb"` instead of pycairo's
  `fill="rgb(N.NNN%, ...)"`. Same colour, different notation.
- Path data is `M x.xxx y.yyy L ... Z` without pycairo's trailing
  redundant `M ...` after `Z`. Same vertices.
- We omit `xmlns:xlink` from the root since we never use xlink.

awvm-disasm CLI now drives the polygon extraction per level and
once at the end for video2 (matching Python's loop ordering).

Validation harness `validation/run_phase_d.sh` runs both
implementations over a single level (default 0; later levels
crash the Python reference with `cairo.IOError` in this fixture)
and asserts SVG file counts and per-file path counts match.

Verified locally on level 0: 80 cinematic SVGs each with matching
path counts. The .asm output (Phase C) remains byte-identical
since that pipeline is unaffected.

events.title: phase-c (3/3): awvm-disasm CLI + parity validation harness
events.message:
phase-c (3/3): awvm-disasm CLI + parity validation harness

Wires the disasm/romset modules into a binary that mirrors the
Python `awvm-disasm.py` CLI (`<input_dir> <level|all_levels> [release]`,
where `release=msdos` is currently the only one supported).

Pipeline per level:
  1. banks2resources (extract resources)
  2. resources2romset (build bytecode.rom et al.)
  3. AwvmDisassembler::run + save_disassembly_listing

`Video2Accumulator` is created once at the binary level and threaded
through every per-level `disassemble_level()` call — preserving the
across-levels accumulation that the Python module-globals provide.

validation/run_phase_c.sh runs the Python reference and the Rust port
side-by-side over an MSDOS-format `aworld/aworld/` directory and
asserts that every level's `.asm` file is byte-identical. The Python
reference's polygon decoder (Phase D, not yet ported) crashes mid-run
with `cairo.IOError`; the harness monkey-patches
`PolygonDecoder.extract_polygon_data` to a no-op so the disasm step
completes for every level. This is purely an observation aid for
parity testing; it does not affect the .asm bytes the disassembler
emits.

Both Phase A and Phase C harnesses also gain a small fix: probe for
the *symbol* `from exectrace import ExecTrace` rather than the bare
`import exectrace`. The bare import spuriously succeeds because the
Rust workspace's own `exectrace/` crate directory is treated as a
Python 3 namespace package — masking the absence of the real
Python `exectrace` package and breaking the wheel-download fallback.

Validated locally: ALL 9 MSDOS LEVELS BYTE-IDENTICAL TO PYTHON.
4.3 MB of disassembly output, every byte matches.

events.title: phase-c (2/3): port resources2romset + AWVM disassembler to Rust
events.message:
phase-c (2/3): port resources2romset + AWVM disassembler to Rust

awvm crate gains two large modules:

awvm/src/romset.rs
  Port of releases/common_data/resources2romset.py — concatenates
  per-level binaries (bytecode, cinematic, palettes, video2) with
  0xFF padding to their fixed engine sizes, and copies the hardcoded
  str_data.rom / str_index.rom / chargen.rom from `hardcoded_data/`.
  ResourceIds is a small struct passed in by the caller; the Rust
  generated tables (msdos::resource_ids::*) are slices borrowed into it.

awvm/src/disasm.rs
  Port of awvm-disasm.py:AWVM_Trace + the 250-line opcode dispatch.
  Implements `exectrace::Disassembler` for `AwvmDisassembler<'v>`;
  the `'v` lifetime threads the cross-level `Video2Accumulator` so
  COMMON_VIDEO_NNN labels accumulate in registration order across
  every level — matching the Python module-globals' behaviour.
  Every opcode (0x00..0x1b plus the two video-draw families at 0x40
  and 0x80) emits text byte-for-byte identical to the Python
  reference.

  Notable subtleties carried over verbatim:
  - register_cinematic_entry assigns labels in registration order
    (CINEMATIC_NNN by counter, or CINEMATIC_<name> when matched in
    LABELED_CINEMATIC_ENTRIES); cinematic_entries resets per level
    while video2_entries accumulates.
  - The opcode 0x19 (load) recognises `bankSwitch <n>` when the
    immediate looks like 0x3E80 | n and emits the same warning the
    Python version does for off-pattern values.
  - The disasm-listing emitter (in exectrace) preserves Python's
    insertion-order dict iteration via VideoEntryMap.

Phase A still passes (banks2resources unchanged); this commit
adds the Rust support library that the awvm-disasm binary will
consume in step 3.

events.title: phase-b: port ExecTrace core to Rust
events.message:
phase-b: port ExecTrace core to Rust

Replaces the placeholder skeleton in the `exectrace` crate with the
real port of `exectrace.__init__.py`:

  exectrace/src/lib.rs        public surface + log levels + hex helpers
  exectrace/src/codeblock.rs  CodeBlock struct
  exectrace/src/tracer.rs     Tracer + Disassembler trait + crawl loop
  exectrace/src/listing.rs    save_disassembly_listing emitter

Design choices vs the Python original
- `Disassembler` is a trait; user types implement it and ExecTrace
  drives the crawl. `disasm_instruction` takes `&mut Tracer` so the
  body can call back via `tracer.fetch()`, `tracer.subroutine()`,
  etc., the way Python's `self.fetch()` did.
- `AddressAlreadyVisited` is no longer an exception. The fetch path
  sets an internal flag that the crawl loop notices instead.
- Maps are `BTreeMap` (ordered iteration). Output order in the
  listing is driven by explicit sorts (matching Python), so this
  does not affect parity.
- `generate_graph()` (pydotplus) is not ported — visualisation is
  out of scope for the byte-identical-output goal.

The listing emitter mirrors Python's exact output format: leading
`\torg <hex>`, mixed code/data sections, 8-bytes-per-line `db <hex>`
runs in data regions, special handling for `Str`, `NMinus1Str`,
`JumpTable`, and `Pointers` variable kinds.

Smoke-tested via two unit tests over a synthetic disassembler:
straight-line-until-ret produces a single code block; an illegal
opcode terminates the crawl. Phase A's MSDOS parity check still
passes (the awvm-tools binary now links exectrace via the workspace
graph).

The Phase C disassembler port will exercise this full surface
end-to-end against the Python reference.

events.message:
phase-a: Cargo workspace + port Unpacker / memlist / bank / banks2resources to Rust

Sets up the rust-port branch with a Cargo workspace and ports the
first slice of the toolchain.

Workspace layout
  Cargo.toml                      workspace root (members: exectrace, awvm, awvm-tools)
  exectrace/                      stub lib crate; full port lands in phase B
  awvm/                           library crate
    src/lib.rs
    src/unpacker.rs               port of releases/common_data/Unpacker.py
    src/memlist.rs                port of memlist parsing in banks2resources.py
    src/bank.rs                   bank lookup + decompression dispatch
  awvm-tools/                     binary crate
    src/bin/banks2resources.rs    port of banks2resources.py (Resources.generate)

Behavioural fidelity
  The Rust unpacker mirrors Python's bit-stream geometry (input
  consumed BACKWARDS in 32-bit big-endian chunks, output written
  backwards from raw_size-1, single shared buffer). The memlist
  end-of-list condition matches the Python reference (sentinel
  bank_offset == 0xFFFFFFFF). The CLI's per-resource stdout log line
  is byte-identical to the Python reference, as is the
  resource-0xNN.bin output filename pattern.

Verified locally against the MSDOS bank set: 146 of 146 resource
binaries hash-identical to Python output, and stdout transcripts
match line-for-line. Permanent regression harness lands in the
follow-up commit (validation/run_phase_a.sh).

events.title: Fix C64 boot screen text alignment
events.message:
Fix C64 boot screen text alignment

Rust's backslash line-continuation strips ALL leading whitespace on the
next line, silently eating the intentional spaces in the header:
- '    **** COMMODORE 64 BASIC V2 ****' lost its 4-space indent
- ' 64K RAM SYSTEM  38911 BASIC BYTES FREE' lost its 1-space indent

is preserved exactly as on the original Commodore 64 screen.

events.title: Improve C64 easter egg: border/screen layout, typing animation, auto-close
events.message:
Improve C64 easter egg: border/screen layout, typing animation, auto-close

a) Render authentic C64 layout: light-blue border fills the popup,
   a darker-blue 'screen' (80 % w x 80 % h) is centered within it,
   matching the real Commodore 64 colour scheme.

b) 'SYS 64738' is typed character-by-character at 120 ms/char.
   A blinking cursor (400 ms period) appears after each new character
   and stays visible for 1 s after typing completes.

c) The dialog now auto-closes exactly 2 s after the last character
   is typed. A background tick thread (80 ms interval) drives re-renders
   so the animation runs smoothly without any user input.
   AppEvent::Tick now sets should_render = true to support this.

Infrastructure changes:
- AboutDialog::new() takes an mpsc::Sender<AppEvent> to spawn the ticker.
- handle_menu_action() receives event_tx and forwards it to AboutDialog.
- handle_global_input() receives event_tx and forwards it to all
  handle_menu_action() call sites.

events.title: Use real label address for external label definition lines
events.message:
Use real label address for external label definition lines

External label definition lines (e.g. 'a58 = $58') previously used
Addr::ZERO as a placeholder address. This caused the cursor to jump
to position 0 after Analyze (Ctrl+A) when the cursor was on an
external label, and the MCP server's get_disassembly_cursor returned
$0000 instead of the actual label address.

Definition lines now carry the real label address in the address
field. Header and separator lines still use Addr::ZERO since they
have no specific address. The Analyze handler is simplified
accordingly, with a saved_cursor_index fallback for header rows.

Refactor FPCEEmu initialization and reset logic: extracted bank creation into CreateBanks(), adjusted ROM bank naming from "ROM_%02d" to "ROM_%03d". Also ensure MPR bank mappings are validated after setup and update window title when no project is loaded.

events.title: Decompose level-1 $1300-$18FF HEX blob into 15 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks
events.message:
Decompose level-1 $1300-$18FF HEX blob into 15 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks

The <<level1 pages 13-18>> raw HEX blob (1536 bytes) was a byte-exact
mirror of drol.bin's $1300-$18FF window but carried no structure.
Split it into 15 labelled sub-chunks matching drol's decomposition:

  L1_BEAM_TARGET_DRAW_TAIL   $1300-$1309 ( 10 bytes)
  L1_BEAM_UPDATE             $130A-$13A3 (154 bytes)
  L1_GAME_START_INIT         $13A4-$13D5 ( 50 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_A_ADVANCE         $13D6-$1422 ( 77 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_A_DRAW            $1423-$1535 (275 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_B_ADVANCE         $1536-$1590 ( 91 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_B_DRAW            $1591-$1645 (181 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_C_ADVANCE         $1646-$16AB (102 bytes)
  L1_ENEMY_C_DRAW            $16AC-$17A5 (250 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_1          $17A6-$17E0 ( 59 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_2          $17E1-$1812 ( 50 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_3          $1813-$1843 ( 49 bytes)
  L1_ATTRACT_ANIM_4          $1844-$1889 ( 70 bytes)
  L1_FLOOR_BASE_ROW_PAD      $188A-$188E (  5 bytes)
  L1_FLOOR_BASE_ROW_HEAD     $188F-$18FF (113 bytes)

Two artifacts of the swappable-page boundary: L1_BEAM_TARGET_DRAW_TAIL
is only the final 10 bytes (routine entry at $1297 is inside the
persistent drol.bin window) and L1_FLOOR_BASE_ROW_HEAD is only the
first 113 of 256 entries (tail 143 bytes $1900-$198E live in
persistent pages 19-1F).

Added a prose subsection with cross-reference table; updated the
level1.asm collection chunk to list the 15 chunks in ORG order.
All 5 targets verify byte-perfect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.message:
Decompose level-1 $7500-$7AFF HEX blob into 10 L1_-prefixed sub-chunks

Split the 1536-byte raw `<<level1 pages 75-7A>>` chunk into:
  L1_SPRITE_POINTER_TABLES_LO/HI   ($7500 / $7600, 256 bytes each)
  L1_PILLAR_SPR_DATA_0..6          ($7700-$7AD3, 7x140 bytes)
  L1_HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_0            ($7AD4-$7AFB, 40 bytes)
  L1_HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_1_HEAD       ($7AFC-$7AFF, 4 bytes)

Bytes are byte-identical to the corresponding drol.bin range (a known
loader invariant), so the L1_ labels mirror drol's SPRITE_POINTER_TABLES
and PILLAR_SPR_DATA / HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA decomposition.  Using the L1_
prefix follows the same pattern established for page 02 seeds and
avoids symbol collisions with the authoritative drol symbols.

HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_1 spans the $7AFF/$7B00 swappable/persistent boundary:
the first 4 bytes live here (in level1.bin) and the remaining 36 bytes
live in drol.bin at $7B00-$7B23.  That boundary is an actual in-game
artifact, not a disassembly mistake --- made explicit via the
L1_HIT_SPR_NEG_DATA_1_HEAD label.

Also adds a prose \subsection to chapter "Level 1 swappable data"
documenting the byte layout and the boundary cut.

All 5 targets (boot1 / loader / rwts / drol / level1) still verify
byte-perfect against the reference binaries.

events.message:
Decompose SPRITE_PIXEL_DATA_RESIDUE_2 into player/hit/grid sub-frames

Split the remaining undecoded 1716-byte HEX blob at $854C-$8BFF into
30 labeled per-frame chunks:

  - PLAYER_SPR_IDLE_DATA_0..8 ($854C..$87F7) --- 9 unique 76-byte
    idle-path player sprites (entries 1 and 3 of the pointer table
    both reference PLAYER_SPR_IDLE_DATA_1).
  - PLAYER_SPR_ACTIVE_DATA_0..8 ($87F8..$8ABF) --- 2 idle-sized
    frames at 76 bytes, 7 at 80 bytes. Entry 1 of the active pointer
    table aliases back to PLAYER_SPR_IDLE_DATA_8 at $87AC.
  - HIT_SPR_POS_DATA_0..6 ($8AC0..$8BD7) --- 7 positive-parallax
    impact-sprite frames, 40 bytes each (W=7 H=5).
  - PLAYER_GRID_SPR_A_DATA_0..4 ($8BD8..$8BFF) --- first 5 of 7
    grid-A frames; the remaining 2 live in the swappable bank.

Key discovery: DRAW_SPRITE runs W+1 = 4 bytes/row for the player,
so many frames have a 4-byte leading or trailing zero row as
alignment pad --- bytes between frames are NOT uniform padding but
part of the frame data. Active frames 0-1 are unused at runtime
(pointer live range is [3..9]), explaining the size mismatch (76 vs
80 bytes) relative to DRAW_PLAYER's fixed H=$14.

The SPRITE_PIXEL_DATA_RESIDUE_2 label is removed from @ %def; three
new \\section{} blocks document the idle+active, hit-pos and grid-A
tail sub-tables. All 5 assembly targets remain byte-perfect.

events.title: Decompose STAGE_RESIDUE_DEAD at $5E00-$5EC4 into disassembled phases
events.message:
Decompose STAGE_RESIDUE_DEAD at $5E00-$5EC4 into disassembled phases

The dead 197-byte fragment between STAGE_VECTORS and RESTART_DISPATCH
was an opaque HEX blob.  It is now fully disassembled with labeled
phases: a nibble sector-reader head, a 7x retry delay into
DEAD_BA00_OVL ($BA00, which is sprite data at run-time -- confirming
the code is dead), a mid-instruction entry into live NIBBLE_READER
via NIBBLE_READER_OVL = $BE5A, and a GAME_START_INIT-style restart
tail with a BIT-abs 3-byte NOP mid-entry on the STA ZP_SCORE_1
operand that lets .restart_skip bypass the third-digit zero while
still seeding HUD_SCORE_COL/HUD_LIVES_COL.

New symbols: DISK_Q6_OFF/Q6_ON/Q7_OFF ($C08A/B/E); STAGE_DISK_DATA/
STAGE_DISK_MOTOR_ON/STAGE_RWTS_RELOAD cross-target re-EQUs;
NIBBLE_READER_OVL/DEAD_BA00_OVL overlay targets; TXT_RETRY_04F8/
05F8/06F8 text-page retry counters; ZP_DEAD_SECHDR/FLAGS/HDR_AUX/
HDR_DST dead-residue ZP aliases.

All five targets still assemble byte-perfect; PDF builds cleanly
(pre-existing \gets-in-[[]] warnings unchanged).  TODO-SYM count:

HEX blob for many rounds.  An absolute-opcode scan of all 5 reference
binaries finds no reference to any byte in this span; comparing
drol.bin vs level1.bin confirms the span is all-zeros in level1.bin
(phase-0 reload target) and only holds the non-zero pattern in the
cold-start drol.bin.  Split into four labeled sub-chunks:
  PAGE2_DEAD_ZEROS    ($0274, 13 bytes of $00)
  PAGE2_DEAD_DITHER   ($0281, 10 bytes D4 82 repeated -- hi-res stripe)
  PAGE2_DEAD_SEP      ($028B, one $2A separator byte)

events.message:
RE GAME_OVER at $BDA0 (level1.bin end-of-game handler)

Break GAME_OVER out of the <<level1 pages 8C-BD>> HEX blob into a
labelled code chunk with symbols.  Routine: MAIN_LOOP's exit path
when ZP_GAME_OVER underflows.  Phases:

  1. Wipe (SCREEN_ROW_COPY) + reload (RWTS_RELOAD).
  2. Reseed score digits, HUD column bounds, ZP_PLAYER_Y, ZP_GAME_OVER
     (same writes as GAME_START_INIT, minus the lives/score-BCD trio
     which the conditional GAME_RESTART reaches below).
  3. 192-row page-2 -> page-1 dissolve via SCREEN_ROW_ADDR_*/MON_WAIT/
     ROW_COPY_CLICK.  The routine uses ZP_HGR_SRC as the page-1 write
     pointer and ZP_HGR_DST as the page-2 read pointer -- opposite
     roles from START_ATTRACT's orientation.

     - == 0 -> JMP LIFE_LOST_RESUME
     - < 0  -> JMP MAIN_LOOP direct (joystick path)
     - > 0  -> JSR GAME_RESTART (resets lives/score/flag -> $FF), JMP MAIN_LOOP

assembly target can reference drol.asm / rwts.asm symbols

events.title: RE cold-start zero-page image at $5700-$57FF
events.message:
RE cold-start zero-page image at $5700-$57FF

Upgrade the ZP_SAVE chunk in loader.bin from a flat 32-line HEX blob
to a labeled, row-annotated table. Each 8-byte HEX row now carries an
inline comment identifying the named ZP symbols that receive non-zero
seeds in that span -- making the cold-start value of every ZP
variable visible at a glance.

Add a new prose section "Empty page and zero-page image" documenting
both UNUSED_PAGE ($5600, dead padding) and ZP_SAVE's dual role: cold-
start ZP image copied byte-by-byte into $00-$FF by FIRST_BOOT just
before JMP (ZP_GAME_ENTRY), AND save/restore backing reused by
SAVE_ZP / SEEK_AND_RESTORE_ZP across level swaps.

Key findings documented inline:
  $4E/$4F = $A3 $72 -> ZP_GAME_ENTRY = $72A3 = START_ATTRACT. This is
    why attract is the first live code to run after boot.
  $36/$37 = $30 $C0 -> ZP_SFX_CLICK low + its implicit high byte.
    The $C0 high byte at ZP $37 has no runtime store anywhere; it
    comes from this cold-start copy (see prior drol-zp-37-assumption
    memory).
  $52/$53 and $54/$55 seed ZP_INPUT_1/2 with C061/C062 (push-button
    soft switches), so default input is joystick-button-polled.
  $5E = $04 seeds ZP_LIVES_BCD = four lives.
  $D4/$DC/$E0 = $01 each -> enemy A/B/C slots initially active.

perfect. PDF builds cleanly (502 pages, same 195 pre-existing LaTeX
errors as before the change -- no new errors introduced by this pass).

events.title: Assignment-form comments: use "<-" and "#\$" for values
events.message:
Assignment-form comments: use "<-" and "#\$" for values

User caught "STA ZP_SPRITE_H ; \$57 = \$1C":
- \$57 is the symbol's own address (should be ZP_SPRITE_H)
- \$1C is the value being stored, not an address (should be #\$1C)
- "=" loses direction information

Correct form: "; ZP_SPRITE_H <- #\$1C". The "<-" makes destination/
source unambiguous; "#\$" mirrors the 6502 immediate-vs-absolute
distinction (LDA #\$1C is a value; LDA \$1C is a ZP read).

Added to CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" as a new bullet under
"Don't restate the instruction". Illustrates the three fixes
together (symbol, direction, immediate marker).

Cleanup this pass: 23 assignment expressions rewritten across the
document. Form "\$XX = \$YY" → "SYMBOL_XX <- #\$YY" (or
"SYMBOL_XX <- SYMBOL_YY" when RHS address has a known symbol and is
high-page). Skipped EQU-definition citations ("SYMBOL = \$ADDR"
describing a symbol's own address — those are documentation, not
assignment).

All 5 targets byte-perfect.

events.title: Strengthen "purpose not mechanics": delete pure restatement comments
events.message:
Strengthen "purpose not mechanics": delete pure restatement comments

User flagged "LDA RESCUE_DIR,Y ; RESCUE_DIR[Y]" — the comment just
echoes the operand in bracket notation. Zero new information. Should
either be an actual explanation of what the row means, or nothing.

New CLAUDE.md bullet in "### Chunk annotation":
  Don't restate the instruction. LDA RESCUE_DIR,Y ; RESCUE_DIR[Y]
  and STA ZP_SPRITE_Y ; ZP_SPRITE_Y both carry zero information.
  Replace with a real explanation or delete.

Cleanup: 42 bare "; SYMBOL[X/Y]" trailing comments deleted. These
were a side-effect of the earlier automated "\$XXXX,Y → SYMBOL[Y]"
conversion: original "; \$XXXX,Y" comments were also pure
restatements but went unnoticed because they looked like they were
adding information (the raw hex). Now that the automated conversion
surfaced them as "; SYMBOL[Y]", they're visibly empty and can be
cleaned up.

CLAUDE.md rule now explicitly names all widths: "The rule applies to

events.title: Rule: compiled branch targets use labels, never assembled addresses
events.message:
Rule: compiled branch targets use labels, never assembled addresses

User flagged comments like:
  ;   delta == \$00           ->  \$629E branch (1-col wide)
  ;   delta == \$01 (via BEQ) ->  \$6296 branch

The numeric PCs are compiled addresses. The programmer never knew them
— the assembler chose them. Such references should use the local
label (.delta_zero, .delta_one, etc.) or be dropped entirely if the
behavioral description suffices.

Rule added to CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" as case (c) of the
numeric-addresses-in-comments rule: compiled branch targets are a
third forbidden case, alongside (a) instruction own-address and (b)
symbol-redundant hex.

Cleanup this pass:
- REFRESH_LEFT_WALL header plate (lines 9799-9808): replaced

  .shared_tail local labels; dropped the shared-tail address range.
- REFRESH_RIGHT_WALL header plate (lines 9645-9652): same treatment
  with .edge_2B/.general/.shared_tail labels, plus upgraded
  "LDY \$4C" reference to "LDY ZP_SPRITE_XREF".

events.title: Upgrade $XXXX → SYMBOL in verb-context code comments
events.message:
Upgrade $XXXX → SYMBOL in verb-context code comments

User caught another miss: "loaded from \$7519/\$7619" where both
addresses have symbols. The prior apposition regex only matched
"SYMBOL at \$X" and "\$X <noun>" forms; it missed prepositional
phrases like "loaded from \$X", "points to \$X", "writes \$X".

This pass broadens the rewrite to any \$X / \$X/\$Y where a context
word within the preceding ~3 words strongly implies a memory
address: from/to/into/at/of/in/via, loaded/stored/points/writes/
reads/jumps/calls, indexed/table/pointer/routine/buffer/page, etc.

Touched 138 comment lines. \$XXXX values without a known symbol or
without a memory-context preceding word are left alone (they're
literal values like comparison thresholds, bit masks, constants).

events.title: Strip symbol-address duplication in code comments
events.message:
Strip symbol-address duplication in code comments

User caught "WALL_L_SPR_LO/HI at \$7519/\$7619" — a symbol name with
its own address as an apposition. Same rule the prose side already
enforces: if a symbol exists for the address, don't also write the
hex.

Cleanup in this pass:
- 300 lines where the pattern "SYMBOL at \$X", "SYMBOL (\$X)", or
  "SYMBOL_LO/HI at \$X/\$Y" had the address duplication stripped.
- 20 phrases like "\$X <noun>" / "\$X/\$Y <noun>" where <noun> is
  table/pointer/entry/routine/etc., rewritten to use the symbol.
- Manual fix for the exemplar line in REFRESH_LEFT_WALL:
    \$4C          -> ZP_SPRITE_XREF
    \$7519/\$7619 -> WALL_L_SPR_LO/HI

The broader sweep caught "SYMBOL ($X)" patterns that my earlier
prose-side script only touched outside code chunks.

events.title: Enforce ASCII-only code comments: no LaTeX commands, no Unicode
events.message:
Enforce ASCII-only code comments: no LaTeX commands, no Unicode

Noweb copies code-chunk content verbatim into the PDF via \Tt{},
so LaTeX commands like \Delta / \to / \S{...} and Unicode chars like
em-dash, →, ≥ render as literal backslash-text or missing glyphs.
The user spotted this in REFRESH_LEFT_WALL where "\Delta == \$00
\to \$629E branch" appeared as garbled text in the rendered PDF.

New rule in CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation": code comments are
ASCII-only. Use ASCII equivalents: delta, ->, >=, <=, <->, *, +/-, --.
Also: no \\$XXXX escapes in code comments; use plain $XXXX (dasm
ignores comments anyway). LaTeX commands are fine in prose chunks.

Cleanup this pass:
- 54 LaTeX commands replaced (\Delta → delta, \to → ->, etc.)
- 125 non-ASCII chars replaced (— → --, → → ->, etc.)
- 3 remaining \S{...} cross-refs cleaned up manually
- 59 \\$XXXX → $XXXX escapes stripped in code comments

All 5 targets remain byte-perfect. Prose (doc chunks) untouched —
LaTeX math and Unicode remain fine there.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Generalize the "addresses in comments" rule
events.message:
Generalize the "addresses in comments" rule

Previous phrasing only forbade \$XXXX as a ":" or end-of-line prefix,
so "\$629E (A was 0)" slipped through — the parenthesized form wasn't
caught and the address is still noise (it's the instruction's own PC).

The underlying principle: an address in a code comment must serve a
purpose beyond identification. Two non-purposes: (a) repeating the
instruction's own PC (.lst has it); (b) repeating a symbol's address
(use the symbol).

Rule in CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" rewritten as a general
principle with both sub-cases explicit, plus examples. Keeps the
"addresses may stay when the reader needs the number" out (unlabeled
address, memory-region span, opcode byte value).

Cleanup this pass:
- 7 instruction-PC prefixes stripped (e.g. "; \$629E (A was 0)" →
  "; (A was 0)").
- 22 symbol-address prefixes rewritten to use the symbol.
- 1 other numeric-prefix comment left alone (serves a purpose).

All 5 targets byte-perfect.
events.author: XekriRedmane

events.title: Use SYMBOL[Y] in comments instead of \$XXXX,Y
events.message:
Use SYMBOL[Y] in comments instead of \$XXXX,Y

Flagged by the user: on a line like
  LDA WALL_L_SPR_LO,Y    ; \$7519,Y -> ZP_BLIT_SRC
the comment repeats the instruction operand in raw-hex asm syntax —
both redundant (the asm is right there) and a hex-where-a-symbol-
exists violation.

New rule in CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation":
- In comments, refer to indexed tables as SYMBOL[Y] (not \$XXXX,Y
  and not SYMBOL,Y). The [Y] bracket form is unambiguously prose, not
  asm, so it reads as annotation rather than duplication.

Mechanical cleanup: 67 comment rewrites where the instruction operand
used a known symbol and the comment used the raw-hex form with the
same index.

All 5 targets remain byte-perfect.

events.title: Tighten style rules: no instruction-address comments, no redundant [[SYM]]([[\$X]])
events.message:
Tighten style rules: no instruction-address comments, no redundant [[SYM]]([[\$X]])

Two rule additions flagged by the user during review:

1. Assembly comments must never prefix the instruction's own address.
   Pattern that was creeping in:
     STA \$3CA8,X  ; \$05B4: row 79
   Correct form:
     STA \$3CA8,X  ; row 79
   The .lst file has instruction addresses; repeating them in source is
   pure noise.
   - CLAUDE.md "### Chunk annotation" gets a new bullet.
   - Cleaned 492 "; \$XXXX:" prefixes in main.nw.
   - Cleaned 341 bare "; \$XXXX" trailing comments (carried no info).

2. Prose apposition [[SYMBOL]] ([[\$XXXX]]) is forbidden — the
   parenthetical hex adds no information over the symbol itself. Only
   range appositions conveying extent ([[SYMBOL]] ([[\$A]]--[[\$B]]))
   remain allowed.

   - reveng.md standing rule principle 2 tightened.

events.title: Enshrine prose address rules as three explicit principles
events.message:
Enshrine prose address rules as three explicit principles

The earlier prose-rule section implied the wrap-in-[[ ]] requirement
but didn't state it crisply. A reader could read "use [[SYMBOL]] when
a symbol exists" and conclude bare \$XXXX is OK when no symbol
exists. That's wrong — the rule is universal: every numeric address
in prose gets wrapped, period.

Restated as three principles:
1. Wrap every address in [[ ]]. Bare \$XXXX in prose is never correct.
2. Prefer [[SYMBOL]] over [[\$XXXX]]. When numeric adds info, write
   [[SYMBOL]] ([[\$XXXX]]).
3. No backslash inside [[ ]]. weave.py strips them as a safety net,
   but the source stays clean.

Exceptions list narrowed and clarified. Added "if unsure, wrap it"
escape valve.

reveng.md's standing-rule section mirrors the three-principle
structure and points at CLAUDE.md for the full policy.

events.title: Add prose rule: use symbolic addresses, flag raw hex with TODO-SYM
events.message:
Add prose rule: use symbolic addresses, flag raw hex with TODO-SYM

Prose in main.nw has been drifting toward raw \$XXXX references in
captions and paragraphs even when a label or EQU exists for the
address. That fails the reader — the rendered PDF shows a hex number
with no way to navigate to the defining chunk. [[SYMBOL]] noweb refs
render as tt-styled hyperlinks to the defining chunk.

New policy in CLAUDE.md "### Prose rules":
- Symbolic [[LABEL]] preferred; [[LABEL]] (\$XXXX) is fine when the
  numeric address adds information.
- Raw [[\$XXXX]] allowed during active RE but must carry a
  % TODO-SYM: needs label comment so a later pass can upgrade.
- When introducing a new label, grep prose for the raw hex and
  propagate in the same commit.
- Lists exceptions: memory-map tables, ORG directives, "why-this-value"
  comments, and code chunks (already covered by code chunk rules).

reveng.md gets a brief standing-rule section pointing at CLAUDE.md for
the full policy, so the reverse-engineer agent sees the rule in the
process doc it reads each session.

events.title: Identify $4713-$47FF as dead sector-image residue (not the DROL logo painter)
events.message:
Identify $4713-$47FF as dead sector-image residue (not the DROL logo painter)

The 237-byte HEX blob previously labelled GAME_INIT_EXTRA and stubbed
as "screen-init routines that paint the DROL title logo" has been
confirmed to be statically unreachable dead code.  Three independent
lines of evidence: (1) zero JSR/JMP/JMP-indirect in any of the five
reference binaries targets $4713-$47FF, and no immediate load of $47
into any pointer appears either; (2) the "code" at $474E is a
truncated copy of STRIPE_COPY_PAGE1's prologue and first 13 iterations,
cut off mid-instruction at $4800 followed by 5120 bytes of $00; (3)
the 237 bytes are a byte-exact copy of $0513-$05FF (CLEAR_PAGE2 tail +
CLEAR_PAGE2_TEXT_ENTRY body + start of STRIPE_COPY_PAGE1), with the
leading $0B at $4713 being the high byte of JSR INTERLACE_FILL_P2's
operand at $0512-$0513 --- mid-instruction residue, not a constant.

Mechanism: PAGE_TABLE maps track 2 sector 15 to page $47 and track 1
sector 3 to page $05; those two disk sectors happen to contain
identical bytes (build artefact).  GAME_INIT's packed stream
terminates at $4712 and nothing else calls in, so the residue has no
runtime effect.  Corroborated by level1.bin (built by replaying the
loader's reload-phase track read which targets different pages): it
has $00 throughout $4700-$47FF.

Changes:
- Renamed chunk <<game init remaining>> to <<sector residue 47xx>>
  with label SECTOR_RESIDUE_47XX (retires the GAME_INIT_EXTRA misnomer).
- Added \section{Sector-image residue at $4713--$47FF} with the
  three evidence lines documented.
- Corrected the HUD-frame prose: the DROL logo is drawn by the
  attract sprite routines ATTRACT_ANIM_1..4 at $17A6/$17E1/$1813/$1844
  compositing sprite pointer tables into hi-res page 2 during the
  animated title sequence --- not by any code at $47xx.
- TODO.md milestone documents the investigation.

No PNG rendered: the bytes are neither executable game logic nor
displayable art.  The existing images/drol_logo.png caption already
correctly identifies its subject as the "(c) 1983 Broderbund"
attribution strip at $BCF1, so no rename is needed.

All five assembly targets remain byte-perfect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: Render all reverse-engineered sprite families to PNG + figures
events.message:
Render all reverse-engineered sprite families to PNG + figures

Implements the standing rule by rendering every sprite pointer table that
has been identified in main.nw.  Adds:

- reference/level1.bin: flat 48640-byte image covering the level-1
  swappable memory pages, extracted from drol.dsk by replaying the
  loader's phase-0 track read (tracks 5-9) using the documented
  PAGE_TABLE_RELOAD and DOS 3.3 skew.  Without this, most sprite data
  is unreachable from drol.bin alone.
- .claude/scripts/extract_level1.py: the extraction driver.
- .claude/scripts/render_sprite_lib.py: shared sprite decoder.  Encodes
  the DRAW_SPRITE quirk that ZP_SPRITE_W is one less than the actual
  bytes per row (the inner loop's BPL on DEC runs W+1 iterations).
- .claude/scripts/render_player_sprites.py: player idle/active body.
- .claude/scripts/render_sprite_tables.py: everything else.

Rendered families: player idle/active, projectiles (L+R), rescue
children (4 tables x 7 frames), enemy-A body/feet/step1/step2, enemy-B
body, enemy-C body, enemy-C auxiliary (tail + puff/peek), companion
(6 poses x 7 frames), special body (4 poses x 7 frames), special drift
puff, SPRITE_TABLE UI (beam + ready prompt), and the $BCF1 "logo"
sprite (which turns out to be the Broderbund credit strip, not the
DROL title).

All figures cross-referenced from the relevant draw-routine sections
in main.nw.  drol.bin still verifies byte-perfect.

Not rendered: the variable-width attract-mode sprites via
ATTRACT_SPR / ATTRACT_SPR2 whose dimensions live in runtime ZP slots
($E5..$ED, $F1..$F6); these would require simulating the attract
animation state.

events.title: Promote image rendering to a standing rule in reveng.md
events.message:
Promote image rendering to a standing rule in reveng.md

The existing "Round 5: Fonts and images" block treated rendering as a
Round-5-specific task. In practice the agent uncovers sprite tables,
font glyphs, and image unpackers constantly — during code RE, not just
when systematically filling in data regions. Deferring the rendering
makes the document noticeably less useful.

New standing rule (before "Chunk hygiene"):
- Render any graphics data found in any session to a PNG.
- Use the existing .venv Pillow install and render_hud_frame.py as a
  template. Don't install packages globally.
- Save under images/ with a descriptive lowercase_underscore filename.
- Embed in main.nw with a figure + caption + \label, scaled to be
  visible for tiny sprites.
- Verify visually — if it renders as noise, the format guess is wrong;
  iterate before committing.
- Commit image + renderer + prose together with the RE that found it.

The Round 5 block now defers to the standing rule and keeps only the
font/sprite-sheet-specific guidance (character grid, ASCII offset,
animation frame labeling).

events.title: RE $0C98 as RESCUE_DRAW: per-frame draw+collision sibling of RESCUE_UPDATE
events.message:
RE $0C98 as RESCUE_DRAW: per-frame draw+collision sibling of RESCUE_UPDATE

The 441-byte $0C98-$0E50 routine previously stubbed as PROJECTILE_HANDLER
is now fully RE'd as RESCUE_DRAW.  The misnaming was historical: the
routine has no relation to general projectile handling --- it is the
draw-side sibling of RESCUE_UPDATE ($6F9C) for the 20-slot rescue-child
entity subsystem.

It iterates Y=$13 down through the same seven parallel slot tables
RESCUE_UPDATE uses, and per slot:

  * pre-computes the perspective screen-X residue $AF (via sub-entry
    RESCUE_DRAW_PERSPECTIVE_CACHE at $0D8C);
  * picks one of four body sprite variants ($75DB/$75E2/$75E9/$75F0
    + $76xx hi pages) based on RESCUE_DIR sign and RESCUE_ANIM phase
    (mid-step h=$1C vs. end-step h=$1A);
  * draws via DRAW_SPRITE, with the SMC_SPRITE_MASK_OP slot patched
    to AND #imm in drift mode for one frame of flicker;
  * runs three independent collision/spawn checks for active slots:
      (1) floor-enemy mutual kill (clear $9B,X, +$0035 BCD);
      (2) player pickup (centre X-band [$40,$50) + Y window around
          ZP_PLAYER_COL; sets ZP_HIT_FLAG=$FF, +$0035 BCD, NO life
          loss);
      (3) hostile projectile-spawn into $C5/$C9/$CD slots when the
          rescue is on the player's floor at an odd row.

The third gate is the surprise of the session: rescue children are
NOT pure friendlies.  When the player joins their floor, every odd
row they emit a hostile projectile that HAZARD_CHECK then animates
on subsequent frames.  The +$0035 BCD pickup reward is for catching
them before they keep firing.

New defines:
  * RESCUE_DRAW_PERSPECTIVE_CACHE ($0D8C) sub-entry
  * ZP_PERSP_OFFSET_LO/HI ($0F/$10) --- the 16-bit pre-compute
    scratch pair (was previously unnamed scratch).
  * RESCUE_SPR_NEG_END/MID + RESCUE_SPR_POS_END/MID label pairs
    for the four sprite tables.
  * RESCUE_DRIFT_PITCH ($0213) --- the 4-entry drift-state pitch
    table.

Plus one prose correction: RESCUE_UPDATE's prose now refers to the
sibling as RESCUE_DRAW rather than "still inside the $03A8 HEX
blob".

drol.bin remains 100% byte-perfect; pre-existing chunk-placement
violations dropped from 10 to 9 (the now-removed PROJECTILE_HANDLER
reference is the one fixed).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: RE $6F9C as RESCUE_UPDATE: 20-slot rescue-child tick; drol.bin now 100%
events.message:
RE $6F9C as RESCUE_UPDATE: 20-slot rescue-child tick; drol.bin now 100%

Final carve of the "game engine B tail" blob (retires the
LEVEL_LOGIC = $6F9C EQU stub and eliminates the last 513-byte
HEX region that was game-engine-B-derived).

RESCUE_UPDATE is the per-frame tick for the 20-slot rescue-child
entity subsystem --- Drol's actual scoring objective.  Iterates
Y=$13..0 through seven parallel tables and runs a five-state
machine per slot:

  $00     -> inactive: PRNG-gated (1/256) spawn combined with a
             $4D-counter-residue-3 phase gate, plus a one-shot
             player-floor override (when RESCUE_FLOOR,Y equals
             ZP_PLAYER_FLOOR_CUR $0C and $1F < $10).  The
             one-shot is implemented by a BIT/JMP opcode patch
             at $705F that fires at most once per pass.  Spawn
             direction alternates by slot parity (+dir at
             world-X $003E, -dir at $035C); row reseats to
             FLOOR_THRESH[RESCUE_FLOOR] - 7.
  $01..$7F -> active walking: step +/- 3 world-X per frame with
              a row bobble from the 7-byte signed RESCUE_BOBBLE
              ($BD) table; 1-in-32 PRNG gate triggers the
              no-hit drift path.  When the player is on the
              slot's floor, a chase AI compares the entity's
              perspective-space X against ZP_PLAYER_Y ($4A) and
              flips direction toward the player.
  $FE     -> exit animation: INC floor-col, deactivate on wrap.
  other - -> drift countdown: DEC RESCUE_COUNTDOWN every 2
             frames (gated on $FD bit 0); on 0, reseat floor-col
             from ZP_DIFF_THRESH_A ($34) and transition to $FE.

Sibling draw + collision at $0C98 (still inside $03A8..$0C97 HEX
blob) awards +$0035 BCD (35 decimal) on player-pickup and sets
ZP_HIT_FLAG $1E=$FF.  No DEC $39 --- pickup is not a life-loss
event.  DRAW_ENTITIES phase 5 at $694E renders the perspective-
grid marker sprite using only the four shared tables.

New labels:

  RESCUE_UPDATE          ($6F9C) routine
  RESCUE_DIR             ($0394) walk direction
  RESCUE_ANIM            ($03BC) step anim counter
  RESCUE_FLOOR           ($03D0) assigned floor index
  RESCUE_COUNTDOWN       ($03E4) drift countdown
  RESCUE_BOBBLE          ($BD)   7-byte signed step-Y delta
  ZP_RESCUE_SPAWN_CTR    ($4D)   free-running slot counter
  ZP_PLAYER_FLOOR_CUR    ($0C)   per-frame player-floor copy
  PERSPECTIVE_XOFF_BYTE  ($B9)   byte-domain perspective offset

drol.bin: 35583/35584 -> 35584/35584 (100.0% documented, zero
gaps).  All four targets byte-perfect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

events.title: RE $6CFE as COMPANION_UPDATE: two-slot hostile-walker tick+draw
events.message:
RE $6CFE as COMPANION_UPDATE: two-slot hostile-walker tick+draw

Carves the 670-byte companion subsystem (tick + 3-pose SMC walk cycle
per direction + drift/climb handler + player-catch hit-box) out of
the head of <<game engine B tail>>, which now starts at $6F9C with
513 bytes remaining (was $6CFE, 1183 bytes).

Retires the ENTITY_PROCESS = $6CFE EQU stub.  The MAIN_LOOP JSR at
$682F now points at the named routine directly.

Key findings:
- The "companion" slots drawn as tiny markers by DRAW_ENTITIES phase 4
  are actually hostile walker-creatures (monsters).  Each slot
  patrols a floor with a 16-bit world-X at $11/$13,X, 5% per-frame
  PRNG direction flip, damages player on contact (sets $1E=$FF in
  $40..$4F x $1A-row catch box).
- Drift trigger: when on same floor as a rescue-entity
  (ENTITY_HIT_ROW $72,X match) AND screen-X in [$40,$47), enter
  drift mode ($B3,X = $FF).  Drift climbs 4 px/row/frame until
  hitting a floor-anchor ($63/$8B/$B3), then re-arms to active on
  a new floor with row = FLOOR_THRESH[player_floor] + $0B.
- 3-pose SMC walk cycle per direction, trampoline JMPs at $6E30/$6EA9,
  operand bytes $6E31/$6E32 and $6EAA/$6EAB rewritten by each pose
  handler.  Per-level sprite pointer tables at $75A2/$75A9/$75B0
  (-dir) and $75B7/$75BE/$75C5 (+dir).
- Gate $33 (ZP_COMPANION_GATE) is set $01 on all non-minimum
  difficulty tiers (DIFFICULTY_UPDATE), so companions activate
  once score >= 4000.  Both slots auto-activate every frame gate
  is open --- nothing externally writes $B3,X.

Introduces ZP EQUs: ZP_COMPANION_STATE ($B3), ZP_COMPANION_DIR ($B1),
ZP_COMPANION_POS_LO/HI ($11/$13, aliases for ZP_COMPANION_COL/OFF),
ZP_PLAYER_FLOOR ($0A), ENTITY_HIT_ROW ($72); SMC labels
SMC_COMPANION_POS_LO/HI ($6E31/$6E32) and
SMC_COMPANION_NEG_LO/HI ($6EAA/$6EAB); sprite-table labels
COMPANION_POS_POSE1..3_LO/HI, COMPANION_NEG_POSE1..3_LO/HI.

All four targets still verify byte-perfect.

events.title: RE $6B39 as SPECIAL_DRAW: special-sprite draw + collision partner
events.message:
RE $6B39 as SPECIAL_DRAW: special-sprite draw + collision partner

Carves 453 bytes out of `<<game engine B tail>>` as three new chunks:
SPECIAL_DRAW ($6B39, 262 bytes), SPECIAL_BODY_STEP1..6 ($6C3F-$6CDA,
six 26-byte SMC-chained handlers), and SPECIAL_INACTIVE_DRAW ($6CDB,
35 bytes).  Retires the `SPECIAL_DRAW = $6B39` EQU stub (formerly
misnamed ANIM_UPDATE; the SMC dispatch is an optimisation for a
single-slot draw, not an animation-state update).

Three-phase draw gated on ZP_SPECIAL_STATE: inactive ($00) tail-jumps
to SPECIAL_INACTIVE_DRAW for a $02x$06 "peek" marker from new
SPECIAL_PEEK_LO/HI ($755B/$765B); active (positive) runs a 4-slot
floor-enemy kill-box ($9B/$9F/$A3) then dispatches through a SMC ring
to draw the body sprite; drift (negative) draws a $04x$0F puff from
new SPECIAL_PUFF_LO/HI ($AFDA/$B05A, Y-indexed) and tests player-catch
for +$0500 BCD.

The six body-step handlers form a palindromic walk cycle (offsets
{0, 7, 14, 21, 14, 7} into four per-level sprite pointers at $7578+).
Each handler rewrites the JMP operand bytes at
SMC_SPECIAL_BODY_LO/HI ($6BE9/$6BEA) to advance the ring, then calls
DRAW_SPRITE (not DRAW_SPRITE_PLAYFIELD).  Correction: prior-session
peek said "7 ladder-step handlers" — there are 6, and they're a walk
cycle, not ladder dispatch (ladder-row semantics live in SPECIAL_TICK).

Uses the inline DRAW_SPRITE transparent-OR blit, patching
SMC_DS_SRC_LO/HI ($65B3/$65B4).  Second sound slot at new
ZP_SPECIAL_SND_CTR_B ($B6) with new SND_PITCH_TBL_SPECIAL_B ($021F)
clicks via SFX_TONE duration $08, armed to 4 on player-catch for a
four-click pickup tone.

New ZP EQUs: ZP_SPECIAL_SND_CTR_B ($B6), ZP_SCREEN_X ($AF),
ZP_SCREEN_X_HI ($B0).  New data EQUs: SND_PITCH_TBL_SPECIAL_B,
SPECIAL_PUFF_LO/HI, SPECIAL_PEEK_LO/HI, SPECIAL_BODY_POSE0..3_LO/HI.
New SMC slot EQUs: SMC_SPECIAL_BODY_LO/HI.

`<<game engine B tail>>` HEX blob now starts at $6CFE (was $6B39,
1636 bytes; now 1183 bytes).

events.title: RE $6ABA as SPECIAL_TICK: special-sprite bonus-creature tick
events.message:
RE $6ABA as SPECIAL_TICK: special-sprite bonus-creature tick

Carves 127 bytes out of the head of <<game engine B tail>>,
retiring the SOUND_UPDATE EQU stub.  $6ABA turns out to be the
per-frame tick for the "special" sprite slot drawn by DRAW_ENTITIES
phase 3 -- a bonus creature that walks the playfield killing
floor-enemies for four hits then falls into a drift animation the
player catches for +$0500 BCD.  Name corrected from SOUND_UPDATE
(misnomer: it is only one of four simultaneous sound channels) to
SPECIAL_TICK, aligning with the three ENEMY_{A,B,C}_ADVANCE tick
routines.

State machine on ZP_SPECIAL_STATE ($AB, aliased with DRAW_ENTITIES'
ZP_SPECIAL_A): $00 inactive (8-bit timer on $AC, wrap rearms);
positive active (advance 16-bit ZP_SPECIAL_POS by $0002 per frame,
rearm when it crosses $035A); negative drift (fall 2 rows per frame
except at four ladder rows $34/$5C/$84/$AC where 94% of frames RTS
early and 6% climb one rung up, gated on ZP_PRNG_A < $0F).  Sound
channel ZP_SPECIAL_SND_CTR ($B5) plays through SND_DELAY_UP with
pitch from new SND_PITCH_TBL_SPECIAL ($0218, 12 entries); only
armed to $06 by SPECIAL_DRAW's defeat edge, silent on normal rearm.
Rearm sub-entry SPECIAL_REARM ($6B14) picks row anchor from
ENEMY_C_ROW_TBL[PRNG & 3] - $0B, arms new ZP_SPECIAL_HP ($08) to 4
(floor-enemy kills before defeat), and sets state to $01.

New EQUs: ZP_SPECIAL_STATE ($AB), ZP_SPECIAL_POS ($AC), ZP_SPECIAL_SND_CTR
($B5), ZP_SPECIAL_HP ($08), SND_PITCH_TBL_SPECIAL ($0218).  ANIM_UPDATE
EQU stub renamed to SPECIAL_DRAW (pairs with SPECIAL_TICK; still
inside the remaining hex blob).  `<<game engine B tail>>` now starts
at $6B39 (1636 bytes HEX remaining, down from 1763).  All four
assembly targets byte-perfect.

events.title: RE state machine: $7208 LIFE_LOST_HANDLER + $6AA7/$7255/$7299/$5EC5
events.message:
RE state machine: $7208 LIFE_LOST_HANDLER + $6AA7/$7255/$7299/$5EC5

Promote the attract/game/restart state machine from partial coverage
to fully-labeled sub-entries, and disambiguate the two MAIN_LOOP
game-over arms.

- $7208 LEVEL_COMPLETE -> LIFE_LOST_HANDLER: fires on ZP_LIVES_BCD
  underflow (BCD $00 - 1 = $99, bit 7 set), not on level completion.
  Add sub-entry LIFE_LOST_RESUME at $720E (skip strobe/transition
  prologue) and RESTART_NEW_GAME at $7255 (tail .no_more_lives
  branch: JSR GAME_START_INIT, silence sound, fall through to
  ATTRACT_LOOP).  Fix MAIN_LOOP's exit-check comment (the $5E
  check was described as "level complete" but is "lives out").
- $7299 START_GAME_FROM_ATTRACT: label the end-of-ATTRACT_LOOP
  "JSR GAME_START_INIT; JMP MAIN_LOOP" tail so the three live
  GAME_START_INIT callers (the others: $6121 INPUT_PROCESS
  Ctrl-R, $7255 RESTART_NEW_GAME) are all named sub-entries.
- $6AA7 RESUME_GAMEPLAY_SMC: promote from EQU stub to module-level
  label inside LEVEL_INTRO_TICK's .activate block.  The 13-byte
  SMC-patch tail at $6AA7-$6AB8 is reached both by fall-through
  from .activate's prefix (on normal intro activation) and by
  GAME_START_INIT's JMP (for game-reset without the intro

events.title: RE $13A4 as GAME_START_INIT + GAME_RESTART; correct five ZP/HUD misnomers
events.message:
RE $13A4 as GAME_START_INIT + GAME_RESTART; correct five ZP/HUD misnomers

GAME_START_INIT ($13A4) is the attract→game and in-game restart reset.
It seeds ZP_PLAYER_Y=$6B, zeros the three on-screen score digits, sets
the playfield column bounds ($65AB=$00 / $65A7=$28) and clear-loop
counter ($2E=$27), calls DIFFICULTY_RESET + INIT_LEVEL_STATE, resets
the BCD lives counter ($5E=$04), clears the BCD score triple
($D1/$D2/$D3), sets the restart flag ($44=$FF), and tail-calls
RESUME_GAMEPLAY_SMC at $6AA7 to re-arm the MAIN_LOOP SMC slots.
Sub-entry GAME_RESTART at $13C2 is used by $5ECB to skip the
player-position + column-bounds reseed.

Five prior labels were wrong and are corrected:

- $6AA7 was stubbed LOAD_LEVEL.  It is actually RESUME_GAMEPLAY_SMC:
  a 13-byte routine that patches SMC_SR_YSRC=$06, SMC_INPUT=JSR,
  SMC_RENDER=JSR, SMC_SR_HEIGHT=$13 --- the exact same SMC-flip
  LEVEL_INTRO_TICK inlines when activating gameplay.  Not a level
  loader.  EQU retired; will get a proper ORG chunk once the $6ABA
  HEX blob is carved.

- $5E was ZP_LEVEL_STATE.  It is ZP_LIVES_BCD: the BCD on-screen
  lives counter drawn as two sprite digits at HUD columns 4/6 every
  frame by POST_FRAME.  BCD-decremented at $6A1E (die) and in
  LEVEL_INTRO_TICK's wait phase.  Initial $04 (four lives).
  Negative means game over (jump to $7208 at $682B), not
  level-complete.  Propagated rename through POST_FRAME and
  LEVEL_INTRO_TICK.

- $65AB/$65A7 were SCORE_DISPLAY_VAL / LIVES_DISPLAY_VAL.  They are
  HUD_SCORE_COL / HUD_LIVES_COL: the left and right playfield column
  bounds gated by BEAM_UPDATE's tracer-draw clip.  Initial 0/$28
  opens the full 40-column strip; the routine at $6200 adjusts both
  (and $2E) as the lives HUD grows.

- $2E was ZP_LIVES.  It is ZP_CLEAR_COL: the playfield clear-loop
  counter used as LDX index in the hi-res clear at $0400/$04A7.
  Initial $27 = col 39 (playfield right edge).

- $44 was ZP_HIGH_SCORE_FLAG.  It is ZP_RESTART_FLAG: a dispatch
  flag only read at $5EC5 selecting among three restart paths
  (0/negative/$FF).  Initial $FF from DEX after X=0.

- $46 is write-only in game code (the one store is here); listed as
  "never read --- likely dead store" in the header plate.

Added prose table listing every memory write with its initial value
and semantics.  Updated the BEAM_UPDATE prose + code to use the new
HUD column labels.  Added agent memory with the corrections.

Build: drol / boot1 / loader / rwts all byte-perfect.

events.title: RE $130A as BEAM_UPDATE: player laser-beam subsystem
events.message:
RE $130A as BEAM_UPDATE: player laser-beam subsystem

Carves out the $130A-$13A3 region from the `<<score game routines>>`
HEX blob as a fully documented chunk and retires the speculative
"PAGE_FLIP_PREP" stub (real page flip is at $6138
DISPLAY_PAGE_FLIP).

BEAM_UPDATE is the main-loop entry for the player's laser-beam
subsystem.  It is unconditionally called each frame but returns
immediately when ZP_PROJ_GATE ($32) is negative --- i.e., at the
minimum/moderate difficulty tiers (see DIFFICULTY_UPDATE).  At
standard/maximum (score >= 10000) it dispatches three sub-handlers
and then walks a 5-slot tracer animation table:

  - BEAM_TARGET_TICK ($1230): beam-target state machine.  $03FF
    (BEAM_STATE) encodes idle / chase-phase / attack-phase with the
    target floor index in its low nibble; $03FE (BEAM_Y) holds the
    current Y scan position, advanced by +-2 each frame toward the
    FLOOR_Y_TABLE target.
  - BEAM_TARGET_DRAW ($1297): draws the beam sprite trail (sprite
    data at $B529, via DRAW_SPRITE) and runs a 4-slot enemy
    collision test against ZP_ENEMY_FLAG/COL/Y ($9B/$9F/$A3); a
    hit deactivates the enemy, clears BEAM_STATE, re-arms the
    post-hit jingle (ZP_BEAM_SND_CTR = $0A), and awards 100 BCD
    via SCORE_ADD.

from Y=4 down to 0, decrementing each active slot's lifetime/X
and writing a single $7F byte directly into hi-res at
screen[TRACER_ROW,Y][new_X] (HUD-clipped against LIVES_DISPLAY_VAL
/ SCORE_DISPLAY_VAL).  Two SMC operand bytes in the inner draw
path (SMC_TRACER_ADDR_LO/HI at $1359/$135A) are patched each
iteration to carry the effective screen row address.  When the
decrement enters the $12/$13 near-player window, a hit test

band) sets ZP_HIT_FLAG ($1E) = $FF.

events.title: RE $719D as DIFFICULTY_UPDATE: score-driven difficulty tier ramp
events.message:
RE $719D as DIFFICULTY_UPDATE: score-driven difficulty tier ramp

The routine at $719D was stubbed as SCROLL_CAMERA but never touches
scroll or camera state.  It is a per-frame difficulty ramp: when the
free-running frame counter ($FD) wraps to zero (every ~256 frames), it
builds a tier index from two BCD score digits and dispatches to one of
four presets that write six shared ZP variables consumed by other
engine routines.

Key reframing:
- $D1/$D2/$D3 are the BCD score (HI/MID/LO), not "entity state".
  Confirmed by SCORE_ADD (BCD add), POST_FRAME (digit display), and
  LEVEL_TRANSITION (BCD compare against high-score $20/$21/$22).
  Renamed ZP_ENTITY_D1/D2/D3 -> ZP_SCORE_HI/MID/LO throughout.
- The tier index is (D1_lo << 4) | (D2_hi >> 4), giving score
  brackets <4000 / 4000-9999 / 10000-17999 / 18000+.
- $71D6 is the minimum preset, renamed INIT_ENTITY_STATE ->
  DIFFICULTY_RESET (still called from GAME_START_INIT to initialize).

New ZP EQUs: ZP_PROJ_GATE ($32), ZP_DIFF_THRESH_A ($34),
ZP_DIFF_THRESH_B ($35), ZP_ADVANCE_RATE ($40), ZP_DIFF_TMP ($5C),
ZP_FRAME_COUNTER ($FD).  ZP_PROJ_MAX ($31) and ZP_COMPANION_GATE ($33)
are now used symbolically here as well.  $32 is read at $130A as an
early-return gate; $40 is read at $13F7 and $1675 as the SBC amount
applied to 16-bit event counters at $DD/$DE and $D5/$D6 --- larger
$40 means events fire more often.

Updated POST_FRAME, SCORE_ADD, LEVEL_TRANSITION and GAME_START_INIT
header-plate comments to reference the new score labels.  All four
assembly targets remain byte-perfect.

events.message:
RE $662C as DRAW_SPRITE_OPAQUE: opaque (STA) HUD tile blitter

Third member of Drol's sprite-blitter triplet --- sibling of
DRAW_SPRITE ($656F, OR-blit) and DRAW_SPRITE_PLAYFIELD ($65D5,
OR-blit with HUD clipping).  Shares the same sprite-parameter
quartet and ZP_PAGE_FLAG row-high-table selection as the other
two, but uses a plain STA (no ORA) and has no source-zero
transparency test: every source byte is written unconditionally.
Column clip is the simple >=$28 offscreen check (same as
DRAW_SPRITE).  Live size 72 bytes, retires the last game-engine-A
HEX blob.

Callers: DISPLAY_UPDATE ($10AB) for the 1x6 timer-animation tile
at col 9 row $16, and DRAW_DIGIT ($115C) for BCD digit tiles ---
POST_FRAME calls the latter seven times per frame for score,
hiscore, and level digits.  Opaque blit is required because the
previous frame's digit pixels must be replaced, not OR'd on top.

Replaces the old TILE_DATA_LO/HI + BLIT_TILE EQU stubs with
SMC_TILE_SRC_LO/HI at $6662/$6663 (source-pointer SMC operand
bytes, set by callers before JSR).

Also marks $6000 INPUT_DISPATCH done in TODO (already RE'd).

RE $65D5 as DRAW_SPRITE_PLAYFIELD: HUD-clipped sprite blitter

Sibling of DRAW_SPRITE ($656F) — identical structure, but its inner

events.title: RE $683C as DRAW_ENTITIES: per-frame draw dispatcher
events.message:
RE $683C as DRAW_ENTITIES: per-frame draw dispatcher

Reverse-engineered the 352-byte HEX blob at $683C--$699B (previously
labelled `PAGE_FLIP`) as `DRAW_ENTITIES`, the final drawing call in
MAIN_LOOP.  The routine is a five-phase restore-and-draw dispatcher,
not a page flip (that is `DISPLAY_PAGE_FLIP` at $6138):

  1. Restore one hit-entity's hi-res background from 12-slot tables at
     `HIT_BG_HI/LO/BYTE0/BYTE1` ($0328/$0334/$034C/$0340), with a $20
     high-byte offset applied when `ZP_PAGE_FLAG` is negative.
  2. Draw player sprite (gated on $0E) using floor-position lookups
     `FLOOR_SPRITE_IDX` ($1E00), `FLOOR_SCREEN_COL` ($1F00),
     `FLOOR_TO_ROW` ($1D40) and frame-counter bit 2 for animation.
  3. Draw a "special" sprite (moon-ball / attract actor, gated on $AB).
  4. Draw two "companion" slots from ZP tables at $11/$13/$15
     (gated on $33).
  5. Iterate the 20-slot `ENTITY_ACTIVE` table at $03A8 with parallel
     `ENTITY_FLOOR_COL` ($0358), `ENTITY_XOFF_IDX` ($036C),
     `ENTITY_FLOOR_POS` ($0380).

Phases 2--5 all end with `JSR DRAW_SPRITE_CLIPPED` ($65D5, still a
stub --- sibling of `DRAW_SPRITE` with narrow column clipping for the
playfield), patching sprite-data source operands at `SMC_PFB_SRC_LO/HI`
($6615/$6616) per call.

Also corrected the earlier speculation that this routine patched the
same SPRITE_RENDER SMC slots (`SMC_SR_HEIGHT` / `SMC_SR_YSRC`) as
`LEVEL_INTRO_TICK`: it does not.  It patches the source-address
operand bytes of the `LDA $9000,Y` at the top of `DRAW_SPRITE_CLIPPED`,
which is a different blitter.  `LEVEL_INTRO_TICK`'s existing
documentation of its own SMC patches is unchanged.

Updates:
  * Renamed `JSR PAGE_FLIP` -> `JSR DRAW_ENTITIES` in MAIN_LOOP.
  * `INIT_LEVEL_STATE` now uses the `ENTITY_ACTIVE` label.
  * `<<game engine B head>>` chunk renamed to `<<draw entities>>`.

All four assembly targets remain byte-perfect.

events.title: RE $67C1 as SFX_TONE; fix stale DRAW_SPRITE flicker-slot docs
events.message:
RE $67C1 as SFX_TONE; fix stale DRAW_SPRITE flicker-slot docs

$67C1 is the game's sole sound-effect generator --- a nested
delay-loop speaker-click tone routine.  A on entry sets the pitch
(inner-loop count), X sets the duration (number of clicks).

The speaker access is done indirectly through ZP pointer $36/$37.
$37 is $C0 (boot ZP state, never written by the game).  $36 encodes
the mute state in the low byte of the pointer itself:
  $36 = $30 → ($36,$37) = $C030 = SW_SPEAKER (click)
  $36 = $20 → ($36,$37) = $C020 = cassette output (silent)
Ctrl-S flips bit 4 of $36 to mute/unmute without any branch on the
hot path.  $38 is a preserved copy across attract/game transitions.

Renames driven by this RE:
  ZP_SOUND_A      ($36) → ZP_SFX_CLICK
  ZP_SOUND_B      ($38) → ZP_SFX_CLICK_SAVED
SOUND_FLAG_MASK kept (it's still the bit that toggles the pointer
between speaker and silent).

Also fix DRAW_SPRITE documentation: the "BIT $00" at $65B7/$65B8 was
described as harmless 2-byte padding, but LEVEL_INTRO_TICK patches it
to "AND #<flicker>" every intro countdown frame to flash the intro
sprite on every other frame.  Prose updated, SMC_SPRITE_MASK_OP/ARG
EQUs replaced by inline `= *` / `= *+1` labels over an explicit
DC.B $24 $00, and the misleading "BIT ZP_PAGE_FLAG" pseudo-instruction
(same bytes, but named for an unrelated ZP alias) removed.

All four assembly targets remain byte-perfect.

events.title: RE $699C as LEVEL_INTRO_TICK: per-frame level-start state machine
events.message:
RE $699C as LEVEL_INTRO_TICK: per-frame level-start state machine

This is the first JSR in MAIN_LOOP each frame. It implements the
state machine that runs between level transitions, controlled by $1E:

  $1E > 0 (gameplay active): return immediately — fast path.
  $1E = $FF (needs init): disable the input / movement / sprite-render
    SMC slots in MAIN_LOOP, clear scratch, save $06 into ZP_INTRO_Y,
    re-point SPRITE_RENDER at ZP_INTRO_Y, seed countdown ($18=$12) and
    auto-start timeout ($19=$40), set $1E=0, fall into tick.
  $1E = 0 (intro running): on odd frames decrement the countdown,
    patch DRAW_SPRITE's BIT slot into "AND #<FD|$80>" for flicker,
    draw via SPRITE_RENDER, restore the BIT opcode, and pulse
    SFX_TONE with the level-data byte at $0200,$18.
  Countdown == 0: wait-for-start phase — a software timer in $06
    BCD-decrements ZP_LEVEL_STATE; if ZP_LEVEL_STATE goes negative
    the main-loop exit check at $7208 takes over. Otherwise clear
    the entity-active table $8D..$8D+$41, poll the keyboard,
    (ZP_INPUT_1)/(ZP_INPUT_2) handler MSBs, and the timeout counter;
    on trigger, activate (restore JSR opcodes + set $1E=1); otherwise
    draw a "ready" prompt sprite (sprite-table id 1) with a late-phase
    two-row bob.

Splits <<game engine B>> ($683C-$719C HEX) into three chunks:
<<game engine B head>> ($683C-$699B), the new <<level intro tick>>
chunk at $699C, and <<game engine B tail>> ($6ABA-$719C).

New symbols (in <<level intro defines>>):
  ZP_INTRO_Y ($17), ZP_INTRO_COUNTDOWN ($18), ZP_INTRO_TIMEOUT ($19)
  LEVEL_DATA_BASE ($0200), SPRITE_TABLE_LO/HI ($B000/$B080)
  SMC_SR_HEIGHT ($64F6), SMC_SR_YSRC ($64FA) — self-mod operands
    inside SPRITE_RENDER
  SMC_SPRITE_MASK_OP/ARG ($65B7/$65B8) — DRAW_SPRITE BIT-slot
    patched into AND #imm for the flicker effect
  SFX_TONE ($67C1) — EQU stub for the nested-delay/tone routine
    (called from 7 sites; not yet RE'd)

Removes the RENDER_SETUP EQU stub; MAIN_LOOP now calls
LEVEL_INTRO_TICK by label. All four assembly targets still match
their reference binaries byte-for-byte.

events.message:
RE DRAW_SPRITE ($656F): transparent OR-blit to hidden hi-res page

Carve the most-referenced subroutine (~40 xrefs) out of the <<game
engine A>> hex blob. DRAW_SPRITE is an OR-blit that writes sprite data
to the currently-hidden hi-res page (page 1 or page 2, chosen by
ZP_PAGE_FLAG bit 7). It takes sprite dimensions and position in the
ZP_SPRITE_W/H/Y/X quartet and source data via the self-modified
SPRITE_PTR_LO/HI operand at $65B3/$65B4.

The routine patches three absolute-address operands: the row-high-byte
table lookup at $6592 alternates between $72C0 (page 1) and $7440
(page 2), and the ORA/STA at $65B9/$65BC are patched every outer-loop
iteration with the current row's base screen address. Zero source
bytes are transparent.

Includes verbatim bytes for a short dead-code tail at $65CC-$65D4 that
is unreachable from live code (the CPX #$00/BCS fall-through at
$65AE-$65B1 is always taken because X is unsigned).

Split the 1321-byte <<game engine A>> hex blob into two chunks
(<<game engine A>> covering $614B-$656E and <<game engine A tail>>
covering $65D5-$6673) so the DRAW_SPRITE chunk can sit at its natural

<<level complete defines>> into the new <<draw sprite defines>>; the

events.title: Fix .fill not emitted when preceded by non-matching bytes in same block
events.message:
Fix .fill not emitted when preceded by non-matching bytes in same block

The fallback byte-grouping loop in handle_data_byte consumed up to
bytes_per_line bytes into a single .byte line without checking whether
any of those bytes started a fill-eligible run. This caused the fill
detection on the next call to see fewer bytes than the threshold,
silently suppressing the .fill directive.

Fix: after accumulating at least one byte in the fallback loop, perform
the same look-ahead used by the fill detector on the next candidate
byte. If it heads a run >= fill_run_threshold, stop and let the next
handle_data_byte call emit the .fill.

events.title: Workaround for WinUAE disassembler stack smashing / crashing
events.message:
Workaround for WinUAE disassembler stack smashing / crashing

Prior to writing to buffer and adding the symbol to it, showea_val()
advances pointer to end of given buffer content. Take also that into
account.

This is workaround instead of a fix, because 80 chars is nowhere near
the space needed to show full C++ symbols within disassembly.
Demangled C++ symbols can be hundreds of chars long...

PS. Upstream code has similar issue(s) in symbol additions, so this
fix will likely need to be adapted to later upstream fixes for the
same issue, after it's been verified that this fixes the user
crashes.

events.message:
Add drag-to-select and Shift+Click in disassembly view

Terminals intercept Shift+Click for their own text selection, so it
never reliably reaches the app. Add click-and-drag (MouseEventKind::Drag)
as the primary mouse range-selection gesture: the first drag event
anchors selection_start at the click-down cursor position and subsequent
drag events extend it, identical to Shift+Arrow behaviour.

Shift+Click is kept as a best-effort bonus for terminals that do forward
modifier keys on mouse events (e.g. kitty, some iTerm2 configs).

events.title: Add .fill directive support for homogeneous byte runs
events.message:
Add .fill directive support for homogeneous byte runs

When fill_run_threshold (default 8, 0 = disabled) consecutive DataByte
cells share the same value with no cross-reference, line-comment, or
side-comment at any interior address, the disassembler emits a single
fill directive instead of individual .byte lines.

Assembler-specific directives:
  - 64tass / KickAssembler: .fill N, $xx
  - ACME:                   !fill N, $xx
  - ca65:                   .res  N, $xx

fill_directive() is now a required method on the Formatter trait so new
assemblers must explicitly declare their syntax.

The threshold is exposed in Document Settings (left/right keys or typed
input, range 0-64; 0 displays as 'off').

Unit tests cover: basic elision, below-threshold fall-through, and run
interruption by cross-reference, line-comment, and side-comment.

events.title: Replace heuristic data region detection with string-based approach
events.message:
Replace heuristic data region detection with string-based approach

The previous approaches (sliding-window ASCII detection, control-flow
tracing, opcode validation) all suffered from false positives — marking
real code as data.  68000 opcodes frequently use bytes in the printable
ASCII range, making heuristic detection fundamentally unreliable.

New approach uses known facts instead of guesses:
- DATA segment boundary from the Atari ST header (text_size/data_size)
- Exact string locations from the string extractor (>= 20 chars,
  passing the _is_meaningful_string quality filter)
- No merging of adjacent regions (prevents swallowing code between
  nearby strings)
- Font bitmaps, lookup tables, and other binary data are left to
  manual DATA_REGIONS entries in annotations.py (Phase 4.6)

Tested against 12 known offsets in BOSS.PET: zero false positives.
events.author: mbackschat

events.title: Disk Copy: Preserve Aux RAM interrupt vectors, prevent crash on IIc
events.message:
Disk Copy: Preserve Aux RAM interrupt vectors, prevent crash on IIc

The memory map permitted use of Aux $FE00-$FFFF as a block buffer
during copies, but this would trash the interrupt vectors that reside
there. Mark those pages as unavailable.

This would be visible on the IIc/IIc+ (which use interrupts for the
mouse even if the software is polling) and a disk copy of sufficient
size overwrote that block. Moving the mouse once the vectors were
trashed would lead to a hang or crash.

Fixes #900
events.author: inexorabletash

events.title: Improve disassembler with two-pass scanning and better data region detection
events.message:
Improve disassembler with two-pass scanning and better data region detection

- Use two-pass approach: first pass discovers code references, then
  identify_data_regions marks non-code areas, second pass re-scans
  with data regions active to eliminate false positives
- Include BRA targets in code reference set for data region identification
- Add visible ASCII threshold (40%) to prevent null-heavy regions from
  being classified as string data
- Post-filter data regions that contain code references or are reached
  by fall-through from preceding code
- Record wrapper TRAPs (func=-1) so detect_indirect_syscalls can find them
- Filter wrapper entries from system call summary counts
events.author: mbackschat

events.title: Add indirect system call detection through wrapper subroutines
events.message:
Add indirect system call detection through wrapper subroutines

Many Atari ST programs route GEMDOS/BIOS/XBIOS calls through a
centralized wrapper. The TRAP scanner only sees the single TRAP
inside the wrapper, missing all actual call sites. This adds
detect_indirect_syscalls() which identifies wrapper subroutines,
scans all BSR/JSR callers, and extracts pushed function codes.

Results are reported in console output, SOURCE.txt header, and
analysis.json (addresses PROBLEMS.md issue #4).
events.author: mbackschat

events.title: Add Borland HLP format analysis and converter tool
events.message:
Add Borland HLP format analysis and converter tool

Reverse-engineered the Borland Help System 2.0 (.HLP) binary format
used by Pure C / Turbo C on the Atari ST (1989-1992). Includes:

- HLP-ANALYSIS.md: complete byte-level format specification covering
  the 136-byte header, nibble-based compression, XOR-encrypted string
  table, cross-reference encoding, and keyword search tables
- hlp_convert.py: Python 3 converter (no dependencies) that decodes
  .HLP files to HTML, Markdown, or plain text (LLM-friendly)

events.title: DeskTop: Prevent possible zero page collision with Disk II format code
events.message:
DeskTop: Prevent possible zero page collision with Disk II format code

The Disk II format code uses some zero page locations that could
conflict with MGTK. We probably got lucky, e.g. by always selecting
a grafport after a call. But better to just run the Disk II code
with the Main bank ZP in place, and let MGTK own the upper half
of the Aux ZP page when calling the format routine from DeskTop.
DeskTop already did this when using the ProDOS driver entry point
for non-Disk II devices.

The previous commit did this for Disk Copy. This commit also aligns
the implementations between the two sites, but doesn't change how
Disk Copy works at all.

events.title: Rudimentary main game loop (experiment) (#2)
events.message:
Rudimentary main game loop (experiment) (#2)

* feat: implement initial game loop and render logic

- Move sprite initialization to `gamedata` package to centralize
  asset loading.
- Introduce `GameLoopScene` to manage player movement, terrain
  rendering, and object placement.
- Refactor `Sprite` struct to decouple from screen bounds.
- Update `main` to bypass terminal scenes for active gameplay
  prototyping.

* feat: implement camera centering and intro sequence

- Centered the camera on the player using `screen` dimensions.
- Refactored `DrawObject` into the `Draw` loop for better coordinate
  handling.
- Enabled the intro splash screen and terminal text.
- Updated initial game level selection.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Camera
    participant Terrain
    participant LevelObjects

    Camera->>Terrain: Offset by screen center
    Camera->>LevelObjects: Translate relative to player
    Note over LevelObjects: Loop draws all active objects
```

* feat: add gravity and tune movement physics

- Add `Gravity` field to `Sprite` struct to enable vertical
  acceleration.
- Adjust `MoveForward` parameters and thrust intensity for
  better control.
- Update default game level to 2.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Sprite
    participant U as Update()
    U->>S: Apply Gravity to Velocity.Y
    U->>S: Add Velocity to Position
```
