events.title: Achieve 100% binary match for drol.asm (35,584 bytes)
events.message:
Achieve 100% binary match for drol.asm (35,584 bytes)

Fill all gaps between documented ORG regions with HEX data chunks,
achieving byte-perfect match across the entire $0100-$8BFF range.

Coverage breakdown:
- Annotated assembly: ~2,177 bytes (6.1%) with labels and comments
- HEX data blocks: ~20,014 bytes (56.2%) as labeled placeholders
- DS zero-fill: ~13,393 bytes (37.6%) for framebuffer/unused regions

New labeled regions include:
- SCREEN_ROW_HELPER ($01B7), game data tables ($02C6),
  main game engine ($03A8), projectile handler ($0C98),
  enemy AI ($0F37/$0F5D), score routines ($1230),
  sprite/player code ($13D6), level logic ($188A),
  lookup tables ($1D47), game engine chunks ($614B/$6683/$683C),
  screen data tables ($72BC)

Resolved 7 EQU stubs with real ORG+label definitions.
The HEX data blocks are placeholders for future RE cycles that
will replace them with properly annotated assembly.

events.title: RE 8 routines: attract anims, display, score, levels, hazards, PRNG
events.message:
RE 8 routines: attract anims, display, score, levels, hazards, PRNG

New routines (8 cycles, ~1000 bytes of new code):

- ATTRACT_ANIM_4 ($1844, 70 bytes): draws attract-mode entities and
  logo sprite from ZP arrays.
- SCREEN_ROW_COPY ($0100, 43 bytes): copies 40-byte buffer to all 192
  hi-res rows with page flip and delay.
- DISPLAY_UPDATE ($10AB, 36 bytes): timer animation display.
- POST_FRAME ($10CF, 157 bytes): BCD score/status digit rendering with
  DRAW_DIGIT_SHORT and DRAW_DIGIT sub-entries.
- LEVEL_TRANSITION ($116C, 76 bytes): high score BCD comparison, calls
  SCREEN_ROW_COPY for transition effect.
- INIT_LEVEL_STATE ($11B8, 98 bytes): level state initialization from
  saved buffers, resets entity arrays.
- SCORE_ADD ($121A, 22 bytes): 3-byte BCD score addition with carry.
- ATTRACT_ANIM_1 ($17A6, 59 bytes) + ATTRACT_ANIM_2 ($17E1, 50 bytes):
  attract entity vertical bounce and draw routines.
- PRNG ($6674, 15 bytes): 8-bit LFSR pseudo-random number generator.
- HAZARD_CHECK ($0E5A, 221 bytes): projectile update, movement, sprite
  draw, and player collision detection for up to 4 projectiles.

Progress: 28 ORG regions, ~3985 bytes documented (~13.7% of game code).

events.title: RE 5 routines: joystick, game start, difficulty, level complete, attract anim
events.message:
RE 5 routines: joystick, game start, difficulty, level complete, attract anim

New routines (5 cycles, 402 bytes of new code):

- JOYSTICK_HANDLER ($012B, 105 bytes): reads game-port buttons and
  paddles, maps vertical zones to ascend/descend and horizontal
  zones to left/right with hysteresis. Shares direction-setting
  entry points with INPUT_DISPATCH.

- GAME_START_INIT ($13A4, 50 bytes): resets player position, zeroes
  score, sets initial lives, initializes entity/level state. Adds
  ZP EQUs for player Y, score digits, lives, level state.

- DIFFICULTY_CONFIG ($719D, 107 bytes): runs every 256 frames,
  computes difficulty from progress, selects entity configuration
  preset. Contains INIT_ENTITY_STATE sub-entry shared with
  GAME_START_INIT. (Renamed from SCROLL_CAMERA stub.)

- LEVEL_COMPLETE ($7208, 91 bytes): extra-life animation loop with
  input polling, falls through to attract on game over. Shares
  input detection labels with ATTRACT_LOOP.

- ATTRACT_ANIM_3 ($1813, 49 bytes): vertical oscillation state
  machine for attract-mode element.

Discovery corrections:
- SCROLL_CAMERA ($719D) renamed to DIFFICULTY_CONFIG — it configures
  entity parameters based on progress, not camera scrolling.
- Added shared entry points INPUT_SET_RIGHT/LEFT, INPUT_DO_ASCEND/
  DESCEND to INPUT_DISPATCH for joystick handler reuse.
- ZP $00 renamed to ZP_PAGE_FLAG, ZP $48 to ZP_INPUT_MODE.

events.title: Add reverse engineering guide (reveng.md)
events.message:
Add reverse engineering guide (reveng.md)

Comprehensive guide for RE'ing Apple II games from .dsk images into
documented, reassemblable literate programming documents. Covers:

- Agent architecture (main agent dispatching sequential skill agents)
- Project setup (interleave detection, reference binary extraction)
- Round-by-round progression (boot → loader → game entry → routines)
- The discovery cycle: disassemble → analyze → name → discover →
  propagate corrections back to earlier work
- Data region documentation including hi-res graphics decoding
- Chunk hygiene rules and naming conventions

Emphasizes the cyclical nature of RE — names evolve, comments get
corrected, data gains structure, and every new routine feeds back
into earlier documentation.

events.title: Add build.py: single-command build pipeline
events.message:
Add build.py: single-command build pipeline

Unified build script that tangles, assembles, and reconstructs the
disk image in one step:
  1. Tangle main.nw -> output/*.asm
  2. Copy support files (splash screen, DOS, font data)
  3. Assemble main.asm, boot1.asm
  4. Generate resident_copy.asm from main.bin ($0500-$07FF)
  5. Assemble ealdr.asm
  6. Build ali_baba.dsk from binaries + scene tracks

With --verify, confirms all outputs match reference binaries
and the original .dsk image byte-for-byte.

events.title: Decode EALDR protection VM bytecodes with macros
events.message:
Decode EALDR protection VM bytecodes with macros

Add PVMXXX macros for the protection VM's opcode table (different
numbering from the main EALDR VM) and decode all three bytecode
regions into readable macro instructions:

- Bytecodes 1 ($A072-$A0FD): integrity checks on data field verifier
  bytes, sector read/verify on two tracks with stepper phase control,
  error threshold with retry logic
- Bytecodes 2 ($A16A-$A180): delay subroutine + stepper phase off
- Bytecodes 3 ($A18C-$A1A5): error handler that fills text screen
  via self-modifying ST target, loops forever

All bytecodes now use symbolic macros. Assembly matches reference
byte-for-byte.

events.title: Replace EALDR_PROT_VM HEX data with proper assembly
events.message:
Replace EALDR_PROT_VM HEX data with proper assembly

Reverse engineer the unused copy-protection VM at $A000-$A2FF into
proper 6502 assembly with labeled subroutines:
- Data field verifier ($A003): D5 AA AD search + 342 nibble verify
- VM execution loop ($A069): context swap + dispatch cycle
- Address field search ($A100): D5 AA 96 prologue + nibble decode
- Read-and-verify wrapper ($A14D): sector find + verify + error accum
- Delay loop ($A181): nested LDX #$20 countdown (VM CALL1 target)
- VM exit OK/error ($A1A6/$A1AB): context swap + carry flag
- VM dispatch ($A1B3): RTS-trick opcode fetch + table dispatch
- Context swap ($A1E0): ZP $50-$5F <-> saved state
- 11 opcode handlers ($A200-$A2DE): GOTO, CALL1, BNE, LDI, LD,
  CALL, RET, ST, SUBI, LDX, INC

VM bytecodes remain as HEX data (3 regions totaling 191 bytes).
Assembly matches reference byte-for-byte.

events.title: Speed up hard disk check again
events.message:
Speed up hard disk check again

Starting with commit 6245942, EmuTOS tries reading the root sector of hard
disks, to better match Atari TOS behavior. If the read fails with 'unknown
device', there is no point in attempting an additional 'inquire' command.

The check is deliberately only for 'unknown device', since, for example, a
removable disk could fail while reading the root sector, but still respond
to the 'inquire' command.

events.title: Fix ACSI2STM GEMDRIVE booting
events.message:
Fix ACSI2STM GEMDRIVE booting

The GEMDRIVE boot code expects A2 to point to writable memory that it
can use as scratch buffer. On Atari TOS this is the case by coincidence.
EmuTOS now uses its disk buffer for this purpose.
events.author: czietz

events.title: Support for booting 3rd party hard disk driver
events.message:
Support for booting 3rd party hard disk driver

By default, on disks where it doesn't find any partitions, EmuTOS will
now try executing the root sector, if the checksum indicates the root
sector is bootable.

Additionally, a new define 'CONF_WITH_EXTERNAL_DISK_DRIVER' is provided
that can be used to disable EmuTOS's internal disk driver entirely. In
that case, EmuTOS will load an external hard disk driver like Atari TOS.
events.author: czietz

events.title: Accept disks that only return a root sector
events.message:
Accept disks that only return a root sector

Atari TOS only reads sector 0 (the root sector) to determine if a disk
is bootable.

In particular, this makes the ACSI2STM GEMDRIVE mode work.
events.author: czietz

events.title: Ignore 'EFI hidden' GPT partitions
events.message:
Ignore 'EFI hidden' GPT partitions

This would give the authors of 3rd-party drivers a way to hide partitions
from EmuTOS's disk driver, ultimately enabling EmuTOS to boot said 3rd-
party disk driver.
